CONCLUSIONS: Intraventricular MSC therapy did not reduce the mortality or VP shunting dependence in premature infants with PVHI. However, 2-year exploratory long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes suggested potential benefits, which warranting confirmation in larger trials. Trial registration The study protocol was registered at Clinical Trials.gov (NCT02890953) on September 6, 2016.

articles.title: Effectiveness of digital self-assessment and support tools for improving maternal and child health in Africa: a protocol of a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal and neonatal mortality remain urgent public health challenges, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, which accounts for around 70% of maternal deaths worldwide. Digital self-assessment and support tools, which let women and caregivers enter health information, assess symptoms or risks, and receive tailored feedback, may improve access to timely care. However, evidence of their effectiveness in African settings is scattered and has not been quantitatively synthesised.
AIM: This systematic review aims to synthesise evidence on the effectiveness of digital self-assessment and support tools in improving maternal and child health outcomes in African settings.
METHODS: This protocol follows the PRISMA-P 2015 statement, and the completed review will be reported according to PRISMA 2020. Eligible studies will include quantitative evaluations of mHealth self-assessment or support interventions targeting women of reproductive age, newborns, or children under five in Africa. A comprehensive search strategy will be applied across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, AJOL, Google Scholar, and grey literature sources. Study quality will be appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist. Data synthesis will combine narrative and, where feasible, meta-analysis.
EXPECTED OUTCOMES: The review will map the range of digital self-assessment and support tools currently deployed in African contexts, assess their effectiveness in improving MCH outcomes (antenatal care utilisation, skilled birth attendance, maternal morbidity and mortality, neonatal mortality; secondary: knowledge, birth preparedness, acceptability, adherence, cost-effectiveness, equity), and identify contextual enablers and barriers to adoption.
CONCLUSION: By consolidating fragmented evidence, this review will inform researchers, policymakers, and practitioners on best practices and context-specific strategies for integrating digital tools into African health systems. Findings will provide insights to advance Sustainable Development Goal 3 and support equitable maternal and child health improvements.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: Our systematic review protocol is registered with the international Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO: CRD420251158174).

articles.title: Morbidity and mortality burden of seasonal influenza in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza poses a significant global health burden, responsible for substantial morbidity and mortality annually, particularly among high-risk populations such as the elderly, young children, pregnant women, and individuals with chronic illnesses. While the burden of influenza is well-documented in high-income countries, limited data exist for sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries, where fragile healthcare systems and underreporting obscure the true impact. Influenza exacerbates prevalent health conditions such as HIV, malaria, and malnutrition, further increasing its toll. The meta-analysis outlined in this protocol aims to systematically assess the morbidity and mortality burden of seasonal influenza in SSA countries, providing policymakers with critical insights to strengthen surveillance, prioritize at-risk populations, and inform vaccination strategies.
METHODS: This is a protocol for a planned systematic review and meta-analysis. This research will follow the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, incorporating observational studies and surveillance reports published between August 2010 and December 2026. We will search major health databases, including MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, as well as regional databases (African Index Medicus and the WHO Global Index Medicus) and grey literature sources (medRxiv and national health reports). Studies reporting laboratory-confirmed seasonal influenza cases from SSA countries will be included. A standardized form will be used for data extraction, capturing morbidity (prevalence, incidence, and hospitalization rates) and mortality (case-fatality rates and excess mortality rates) indicators. Pooled data will be analyzed using meta-analytic techniques, applying random-effects models to account for heterogeneity. Sensitivity analyses will address variations in case definitions, methodologies, and study quality across studies. Publication and language bias will be mitigated by including grey literature and applying no language restrictions.
EXPECTED OUTCOMES: The completed review is expected to provide updated, pooled estimates of seasonal influenza-associated morbidity and mortality across SSA countries, stratified by age group, geographic subregion, and presence of comorbidities. These findings will support evidence-based policy decisions, including the strengthening of influenza surveillance systems and the prioritization of vaccination programs for high-risk populations in SSA countries.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: As this study involves secondary data from published literature, ethical approval is not required. Results will be disseminated via a peer-reviewed publication, conference presentations, and stakeholder meetings. Tailored reports will be shared with policymakers in SSA countries to translate findings into public health strategies, particularly to enhance surveillance and implement targeted vaccination programs.
SYSTEMIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024617707.

articles.title: Changing characteristics, treatment patterns, and risk among children and young people with a first recorded common mental disorder symptom or diagnosis in primary care in England (2001-23): a retrospective, population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Presentations to primary care by children and young people (CYP) for common mental disorders (anxiety and depression) have risen steeply in the past two decades. In this study, we aimed to describe changes in the case mix of CYP with an incident record of a common mental disorder, treatment patterns after the incident record, and whether these trends were accompanied by secular changes in the demographics of those presenting, their treatment patterns, and whether the clinical risk profile of those presenting changed between 2001 and 2023 in England.
METHODS: In this retrospective, population-based cohort study, we used anonymised primary care health records data from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum (2001-23). We identified children and adolescents (aged 10-18 years) registered with English general practices with linked hospital admission and mortality records. We estimated trends in incidence of common mental disorders (using both symptom and diagnosis codes) in primary care and, among CYP with an incident record of a common mental disorder, changes in demographic and comorbidity profiles, referrals to Child And Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS), and antidepressant prescribing. We compared CYP with incident common mental disorders to matched controls on hospital admission for self-harm, alcohol misuse, and drug misuse, and tested for change in these associations using common mental disorder-by-calendar-year interactions. People with lived experience were not involved in the design or conduct of this study.
FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2001, and Dec 31, 2023, 6 220 923 CYP were registered with CPRD-Aurum practices. 379 802 CYP had a first recorded common mental disorder symptom or diagnosis. 250 315 (65·9%) of 379 802 CYP were girls and 129 353 (34·1%) were boys, with a mean age of 15·2 years (range 10-18; SD 2·1), 304 544 (80·2%) were White, and 35 082 (19·2%) were from minoritised ethnic groups. From 2001, the incidence of common mental disorders increased by four times from 57 per 10 000 person-years to 240 in 2019, followed by a decrease to 163 in 2023. The age of CYP with an incident record of a common mental disorder became younger (mean age 15·5 years [SD 2·1] to 15·0 [SD 2·1]), the proportion of White CYP became increasingly overrepresented relative to the general population, and the prevalence of psychiatric or neurodevelopmental comorbidities almost tripled (5·1% in 2001, 13·8% in 2023). After an incident common mental disorder, CAMHS referrals increased from 6·8 to 17·8 per 100 person-years (rate ratio [RR] 2·64 [95% CI 2·48 to 2·79]); antidepressant prescribing halved (38·8 to 17·9 per 100 person-years; RR 0·46 [0·45-0·48]), while prescriptions per treated CYP increased from 4·1 to 6·2 (RR 1·50, 1·48- 1·52). Between 2001 and 2019, the association between common mental disorders and adverse outcomes in the 2 years after the index date remained broadly stable over time (ratio of hazard ratios [HRs] per calendar year 1·01 [95% CI 1·00-1·02] for hospital admission for self-harm; 1·00 [0·99-1·01] for alcohol misuse; 1·01 [0·99-1·02] for drug misuse).
INTERPRETATION: The increase in recorded common mental disorders among CYP was not accompanied by declining clinical risk as would be expected if young people were increasingly being recorded at lower levels of severity, whether through readier presentation to primary care, greater clinical recognition, or more liberal recording. These findings highlight the need for greater consistency, better recording of psychometric measures, and transparency in care pathways.
FUNDING: NIHR, Wellcome Trust, Place2Be.

articles.title: Metabolic perturbations involved in the association of neonicotinoid insecticide exposure with thyroid stimulating hormone in children: A longitudinal panel study.
articles.abstract: Epidemiological evidence regarding the effects of neonicotinoid insecticides (NNIs) exposure on children's thyroid function and the underlying metabolic mechanisms remained scarce. We conducted a longitudinal panel study among children aged 4-12 years to assess associations of 15 urinary NNIs and their metabolites with thyroid function, and to identify potential metabolomics pathways. We found robust positive associations of desnitro-thiamethoxam (DN-THM) and acetamiprid (ACE) with thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and TSH/free thyroxine (FT4), while imidaclothiz was associated with FT4 (False Discovery Rates <0.05). Random forest and linear mixed-effect models revealed that, of the 2067 detected serum metabolites, hundreds were significantly related to DN-THM, ACE, and thyroid function biomarkers. Up to 17 overlapping metabolites related to DN-THM, TSH and TSH/FT4, including 3-hydroxyphenylurea, Phosphatidylcholine(15:0_20:3), glucosaminic acid, γ-glutamylcysteine, Indole 3-Carboxaldehyde and so on, showed significant mediation in DN-THM-associated TSH or TSH/FT4 elevation, with mediated proportions ranging from 10.12% to 15.06%. All significant metabolites were enriched in 5 shared metabolic pathways: sphingolipid metabolism, tyrosine metabolism, glutathione metabolism, pentose phosphate pathway, glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor biosynthesis. Moreover, we found that the significant clinical biomarkers within these overlapping metabolic pathways were significantly related to DN-THM and metabolites. The effects of DN-THM on TSH and TSH/FT4 were more evident in those with high total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and low glutathione reductase levels. Accordingly, higher NNIs exposure was associated with increased TSH and TSH/FT4 ratio in children, partly through disturbances in lipid and glutathione metabolism.

articles.title: Clinical and instrumental phenotyping of gait in subjects with Cri du Chat syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cri du Chat syndrome (CdCS) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by disabling psychomotor and gait impairments. The aim of this study is to assess and characterize CdCS gait through a comprehensive and validated set of trunk acceleration-derived gait indexes by means of inertial gait analysis.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we enrolled 38 CdCS individuals (age 22.6 [18.4-26.0] years, 52.6% females) and 39 healthy subjects (HS) matched for age, sex and speed of gait. Besides the conventional spatio-temporal parameters we calculated: the harmonic ratio (HR, primary outcome), the largest Lyapunov exponent for short time-series (sLLE), the percent determinism in recurrence quantification analysis (RQA).
RESULTS: Compared to HS, CdCS gait was characterized by lower HR (CdCS: 1.6 [1.4-1.7] vs. HS: 2.6 [2.4-2.7], p = 0.001), lower RQA (p = 0.001) and higher sLLE (p = 0.001). In CdCS individuals, we also found a higher stride time, along with a lower cadence and range of pelvic obliquity during gait (p < 0.025 for all comparisons). Logistic regression analysis identified HR and RQA in the antero-posterior plane and the range of pelvic obliquity as the independent and most relevant features able to differentiate gait of CdCS subjects from HS.
CONCLUSIONS: Our study provides a comprehensive description of CdCS gait pattern, predominantly characterized by reduced symmetry, rhythmicity, and stability.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was approved by local Ethical Committee (CE Pavia, Approval Number: 2022-3.11/797) and pre-registered on www.
CLINICALTRIALS: gov (NCT05887739).

articles.title: Risk factors that predict future onset of overvaluation of weight and shape in adolescent girls.
articles.abstract: Given that overvaluation of weight/shape has emerged as a potent transdiagnostic risk factor for a range of eating disorders, we investigated risk factors that predict future onset of this key prodromal symptom to advance understanding of etiologic processes, which has not been examined previously. We used data from a community sample of 496 adolescent female participants (M age = 13.02, SD = 0.73, age range = 11.0-15.0 years) who completed annual diagnostic interviews and surveys assessing putative risk factors over 8-year period. Overvaluation of weight/shape was not significantly correlated with thin-ideal internalization, but was positively correlated with pressure to be thin, body dissatisfaction, dietary restraint, and zBMI at baseline. In univariate logistic regressions, higher baseline perceived pressure to be thin, body dissatisfaction, dietary restraint, negative emotionality, and zBMI, as well as lower parent support and self-esteem, predicted future onset of clinically meaningful overvaluation of weight/shape over 8-year follow-up. Multivariate analyses revealed that only low self-esteem showed a unique effect when statistically controlling for the other risk factors. An exploratory classification tree analysis suggested that low self-esteem was the primary pathway to overvaluation of weight/shape, but that there was also evidence of qualitative distinct risk pathways through elevated dietary restraint and zBMI. Our results suggest that certain risk factors predict future onset of clinically significant overvaluation of weight/shape, and that reducing these risk factors in selective prevention programs may prove effective in reducing a broader range of eating disorders than extent prevention programs.

articles.title: Effectiveness of prevention of mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B virus and its associated factors among children born to HBsAg-positive mothers in China, 2023-2025: a nationwide cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major global public health issue. Despite substantial progress in the prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) of HBV, contemporary nationwide evidence on progress towards elimination of mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT) in China remains limited. In addition, the serological characteristics of children with residual HBV infection after PMTCT failure remain poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate recent progress towards EMTCT in China and investigate anti-HBs positivity and its associated factors among children with PMTCT failure.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional study using data from the National Integrated Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission of HIV, Syphilis and Hepatitis B Programme (iPMTCT Programme) and the linked Establishment of a Pediatric HBV Infection Cohort and Natural History Study (Pediatric HBV study). Children born to HBsAg-positive mothers between Jan 1, 2023, and Dec 31, 2025, were included in this study. HBV infection prevalence and PMTCT success rates were assessed at the population level, and anti-HBs positivity among infected children and its associated factors were evaluated using logistic regression.
FINDINGS: Among 569,730 children born to HBsAg-positive mothers, HBV infection prevalence among children declined from 9.09 per 100,000 live births in 2023 to 2.92 per 100,000 in 2025, while national PMTCT success rates remained consistently high, at 99.73% in 2023, 99.66% in 2024, and 99.68% in 2025. Higher PMTCT success rates persisted in eastern China than in central and western regions. Among 1742 HBV-infected children, 658 (37.77%) were anti-HBs positive. Birth year, maternal HBeAg status, maternal antiviral treatment during pregnancy, timing of antenatal HBV screening, and maternal occupation were independently associated with anti-HBs positivity.
INTERPRETATION: China has made substantial progress towards EMTCT of HBV, with HBV infection prevalence among children remaining at very low levels and consistently high PMTCT effectiveness nationwide. However, persistent regional disparities indicate that further optimisation of PMTCT implementation is needed to achieve equitable elimination. The substantial proportion of anti-HBs-positive children among those with PMTCT failure highlights previously underappreciated serological heterogeneity in residual pediatric HBV infection. As countries move towards achieving and sustaining EMTCT, integrating high-quality PMTCT services with longitudinal follow-up of infected children may become increasingly important for further reducing HBV-related disease burden.
FUNDING: National Key Research and Development Program of China (2023YFC2308101).

articles.title: Navigating the Storm: Understanding the Support Needs of Parents of Children With Autism Amid the Iran-U.S.-Israel Conflict.
articles.abstract: The Iran-U.S.-Israel war has imposed unprecedented stress on Iranian families raising children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This study explored parents' lived experiences, support needs and coping across three provinces with varying war exposure. Convergent mixed-methods design. Semi-structured interviews with 36 parents (34 mothers) of children with ASD from Isfahan (n = 10), Tabriz (n = 16) and Rafsanjan (n = 10). Conventional qualitative content analysis was used. Quantitative data included war exposure and logistic regression predicting willingness to return to autism centres. Six themes emerged: disrupted routines/child regression (91.7%), parental stress/financial collapse (100%), ineffective online therapy (83.3%), demand for safe in-person respite (91.7%), direct trauma exposure (47.2% within 1 km of strike) and ambivalence about returning. High-intensity zones (Isfahan + Tabriz) showed lower return willingness than Rafsanjan (42.3% vs. 80%, p < .01). Logistic regression found Rafsanjan residence increased return likelihood (odds ratio [OR] = 6.5, p = .03), whereas ASD level 3 (OR = 0.18, p = .04) and direct explosion exposure (OR = 0.09, p = .01) reduced it. Lower family decile correlated with greater financial hardship (ρ = -0.54, p < .01). War magnifies existing challenges for parents of children with ASD. Immediate humanitarian responses must prioritise safe in-person respite, sensory emergency kits and low-tech therapy alternatives. Policy reforms should embed autism-specific considerations into war relief.Lay AbstractWhat is already known about this topic?When war disrupts daily routines, children with autism are especially vulnerable to behavioural regression, anxiety and emotional dysregulation. Parents of children with autism already experience high levels of stress, but little is known about how they cope when active military conflict compounds their caregiving responsibilities - particularly in Iran, where sanctions and geographic disparities in autism services create unique challenges.What this paper adds?This study is the first to systematically document the experiences of Iranian parents raising children with autism during active war with the United States and Israel. Through interviews with 36 parents across three cities with different levels of war exposure, we found that nearly all parents reported their child's behaviour worsened after war - driven as much by closure of autism centres as by explosions themselves. Every parent reported elevated anxiety and most experienced significant income loss, making it hard to afford basic needs like diapers and medications. The most urgent request was for safe, in-person autism services to reopen with proper safety measures. Parents described an impossible trade-off: risking their child's physical safety versus accepting their developmental regression.Implications for practice, research or policyWar magnifies existing challenges for families of children with autism. Humanitarian responses must prioritise safe in-person respite care, sensory emergency kits and low-tech therapy alternatives. Policymakers should embed autism-specific considerations into war relief - including subsidised diapers and medications, trauma-informed training for psychologists and accessible emergency alerts. Parents ask for practical help to help their children survive it.

articles.title: Maternal influenza vaccination boosts durable breast milk antibody-mediated protection in infants.
articles.abstract: Influenza contributes to significant disease burden worldwide, and young infants are at an increased risk of severe influenza infection. Maternal antibodies transferred across the placenta and through breast milk confer anti-influenza immunity to the newborn. Placental transfer provides a finite window of protection, but breast milk antibody transfer may provide prolonged immunity across the postnatal period. Yet, how breastmilk antibody profiles are shaped by maternal vaccination, change postnatally, and whether they contribute to protection against influenza remains incompletely defined. Comprehensive systems serological analysis of influenza-specific antibodies across 21 different antigens in a longitudinal birth cohort revealed maternal influenza vaccination was associated with enhanced antibody-dependent complement deposition (ADCD) and FcγR binding in breast milk at two weeks postpartum. This effect was further stratified by trimester of vaccination: first trimester vaccinees exhibited increased ADCD and IgM levels, whereas second or third trimester vaccination was associated with increased FcγR and FcαR binding. Analysis of longitudinal samples revealed that anti-influenza antibody responses in milk shift postpartum toward increased FcγR binding and decreased ADCD activity and IgM levels. Finally, baseline ADCD activity in breast milk and serum IgG1 levels were identified as signatures of resistance to influenza infection during the first six months of life. A multivariate model combining correlates of protection across milk and serum compartments offered greater predictive power compared to either compartment alone, suggesting both routes of antibody transfer bolster anti-influenza immunity in infants. These data collectively suggest that maternal influenza vaccination confers infant protection via breast milk to augment placental antibody transfer, and the functional capacity of these protective antibodies could be enhanced with prolonged breastfeeding.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 RBD fusion ameliorates enhanced disease induced by RSV G CCD mRNA vaccine in BALB/c mice.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a primary pathogen responsible for lower respiratory tract infections in both infants and the elderly. However, vaccine development has been consistently hampered by the risk of vaccine-enhanced disease (VED), while the role of the RSV attachment (G) glycoprotein has long been overlooked. Using an mRNA vaccine platform, this study systematically evaluated the roles of two critical RSV G protein domains-the central conserved domain (CCD) and the mucin-like domains-in mediating immune protection and VED. Results indicate that the mucin-like domains confer no protection and induce marked VED. Surprisingly, although CCD immunization elicits potent humoral immunity and significantly reduces viral load, it also induces Th2-biased responses and exacerbates pulmonary inflammation following RSV challenge. However, fusion of CCD with the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2 in an mRNA vaccine (CCD + RBD) successfully redirected the Th2-biased immune responses toward a balanced Th1/Th2 profile, while significantly attenuating CCD-induced immunopathology. CD8⁺ T-cell depletion and adoptive-transfer experiments further supported a contribution of RBD-responsive CD8⁺ T cells to the reduction in pathology. These findings provide proof of concept that heterologous antigen fusion can reshape CCD-associated immunopathology in a BALB/c RSV challenge model.

articles.title: Maternal PspA antibodies protect neonates and enable serotype-specific immunity.
articles.abstract: Maternal antibodies are essential for protecting fetuses and infants with immature immune systems, and maternal vaccination is a promising strategy to prevent neonatal infections. We previously reported the vaccine efficacy of RBD-PspA, a fusion protein combining the receptor-binding domain of parvovirus B19 (B19V) and pneumococcal surface protein A (PspA). Here, we evaluated the protective efficacy of RBD-PspA-induced maternal immunity and its impact on offspring adaptive immunity development. Offspring of vaccinated mothers exhibited anti-RBD and anti-PspA IgG levels comparable to those of their mothers, with neutralizing activity against B19V. These offspring exhibited significantly improved survival following primary challenge with a pneumococcal strain harboring the same PspA family protein. Surviving offspring demonstrated enhanced survival upon re-challenge with a strain of the same capsule-defined serotype but expressing a different PspA family protein. These findings suggest that maternal pneumococcal vaccination protects offspring and permits the development of protective immunity in pups.

articles.title: Outcomes among Pregnant Women with Measles and Their Infants in the United States - Preliminary Analysis, 2025-2026.
articles.abstract: AbstractMeasles virus infection during pregnancy can result in severe maternal illness, adverse pregnancy and infant outcomes, and neonatal complications, including congenital measles. During multiple large outbreaks from January 1, 2025, to September 28, 2026, a total of 112 cases of confirmed measles during pregnancy and 13 cases of congenital measles were reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; complications included maternal pneumonia, preterm delivery, and neonatal complications. Almost all pregnant women with measles (98%) had not received measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccination before pregnancy or had unknown vaccination status. MMR vaccination before pregnancy and high community MMR vaccination coverage are important to prevent measles and related complications.

articles.title: International Adaptation of NCCN Guidelines for Sub-Saharan Africa: Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia, Version 1.2025.
articles.abstract: The NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) include evidence-based, consensus-driven recommendations from a multidisciplinary panel of experts in the United States with knowledge and experience in the management of patients with pediatric ALL within maximal resource settings, such as those present at NCCN Member Institutions. The International Adaptations of the NCCN Guidelines address the availability of resources, metabolic differences in populations, and regulatory status of health care technologies used in cancer care in a specific country or region. These targeted regional resources are created to combat increasing cancer rates and provide treatment recommendations that are more specific and unique to each region or country. These resources are updated biennially; for the most current version, please go to http://www.nccn.org/global/what-we-do/international-adaptations. This manuscript reviews the recommendations outlined in the International Adaptation of NCCN Guidelines for Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA; referred to as NCCN Guidelines for SSA within this discussion), Version 1.2025, published August 11, 2025, for the optimal diagnosis, workup, and treatment of pediatric ALL within the variable resource settings of SSA while highlighting the modifications required to optimize care when the maximal resource settings provided at comprehensive cancer centers such as NCCN Member Institutions are not available.

articles.title: Corn Syrup Solids in Infant Formula and Child Health Outcomes: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: The potential impact of corn syrup solids (CSSs) in infant formula on long-term child health outcomes is a critical area of investigation, informing nutritional guidelines and parental choices.
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to investigate the effects of CSSs in infant formula on various child health outcomes.
DATA SOURCES: Following PRISMA guidelines, our PROSPERO-registered protocol (CRD420261306977) guided a comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, completed on January 23, 2026.
DATA EXTRACTION: From 150 identified studies, titles and abstracts were screened, followed by full-text review. Data from eligible studies were extracted independently in duplicate, and study quality and risk of bias were assessed.
DATA ANALYSIS: We extracted data from 5 observational and 2 controlled interventional studies. Two studies reported a higher early childhood obesity risk in children fed CSS-containing formula. Other findings included increased food fussiness, decreased food enjoyment, frequent sweet intake, and gut microbiota changes (depleted Bifidobacteriaceae, enriched Lachnospiraceae). Short-term postprandial differences in plasma metabolites and gastric acidity were also noted. Four studies had low risk of bias, 3 had moderate risk.
CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review suggests that CSS-containing formula intake during infancy may be associated with altered eating behaviors, gut microbiota changes, acute metabolic responses, and childhood obesity. Future well-designed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are needed to elucidate these connections. Limitations include a scarcity of robust RCTs, imprecise exposure data, and exclusion of non-English studies.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. [CRD420261306977].

articles.title: Incidence and case fatality of patients hospitalised with leptospirosis, overseas departments, France, 2005 to 2023.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUNDLeptospirosis, a zoonotic disease caused by Leptospira bacteria, is a public health concern in French overseas departments. The tropical climate and frequent heavy rainfalls create favourable conditions for the transmission of the pathogen. While most infections are mild, severe cases occur requiring hospitalisation.AIMWe aimed to investigate epidemiology of patients hospitalised with leptospirosis in the French overseas departments Guadeloupe, Martinique, French Guiana, Réunion and Mayotte between 2005 and 2023.METHODSWe extracted data on hospitalised cases of leptospirosis from the French national hospital discharge database (PMSI) using codes A.27.0, A.27.8 and A.27.9 for leptospirosis of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision (ICD-10), analysed the data descriptively and estimated hospitalisation incidence rates (HIR) and case fatality rates.RESULTSOverall, 4,823 hospitalised cases were identified, most of them were males (n = 4,051; 84%). Guadeloupe (22.2/100,000) and Martinique (14.3/100,000) had the highest HIR. The HIR decreased in Guadeloupe (p = 0.03) while it increased in Réunion and French Guiana (p < 0.001). A total of 1,001 (20.8%) hospitalised cases were admitted to an intensive care unit: the highest proportion in Réunion (452/2,018; 25.8%) and the lowest in Martinique (174/1,119; 16.8%). Case fatality rate was 3.4%; 166 cases died.CONCLUSIONLeptospirosis remains a persistent health threat in the French overseas departments. Strengthened surveillance and clinician awareness are critical for reducing the incidence of leptospirosis, particularly in these regions where the co-circulation of arboviruses likely complicates the diagnosis.

articles.title: Different diameters of particulate matter exposure and health outcomes: An umbrella review.
articles.abstract: Airborne particulate matter (PM) is a pervasive environmental hazard, yet the comparative toxicity of different aerodynamic diameters-particularly sub-micron particles (PM1)-remains insufficiently characterized in environmental health risk assessments. To address this, we conducted an umbrella review systematically synthesizing observational meta-analyses to evaluate the dose-response associations between PM fractions (PM10, PM2.5, and PM1) and diverse health outcomes. By harmonizing effect estimates and assessing evidence quality via the GRADE framework, we observed a potential 'size effect' influencing pollutant toxicity. Our comparative analyses suggested that PM1 may be associated with relatively stronger adverse effects than larger fractions across multiple physiological domains. Notably, PM1 exposure was associated with the highest relative risks for metabolic disorders, including metabolic syndrome (RR=1.30), childhood obesity (RR=1.41), and childhood hypertension (RR=1.61), significantly outpacing the effects of PM2.5 and PM10. Furthermore, moderate-quality evidence highlighted a striking systemic vulnerability, with PM1 demonstrating a robust association with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD, RR=1.59). Similar size-dependent toxicity gradients were observed for neurodevelopmental (autism) and respiratory (asthma) outcomes. The amplified toxicity of PM1 is likely mediated by its higher alveolar deposition efficiency, larger specific surface area for toxicant adsorption, and enhanced capacity to translocate across biological barriers (e.g., air-blood barrier) to induce systemic oxidative stress. These findings highlight that current air quality regulations, which predominantly rely on PM2.5 and PM10 mass concentrations, may not fully capture the systemic and metabolic health burdens of smaller particles. Incorporating size-resolved PM1 monitoring into environmental safety frameworks could be an important step toward better estimating human health risks and developing targeted mitigation strategies.

articles.title: Prenatal atrazine exposure and offspring neurodevelopment: Sex-specific effects, neurochemical pathways, and risk assessment using the TRAEC strategy.
articles.abstract: Atrazine (ATR) is a widely used herbicide detected in various environmental media, raising concerns about its potential neurodevelopmental toxicity. To systematically evaluate this risk, we employed the Targeted Risk Assessment of Environmental Chemicals (TRAEC) framework. However, epidemiological evidence regarding ATR exposure during pregnancy and its impact on offspring neurodevelopment remains limited. Here, we conducted a cohort study of 579 mother‑child pairs with urinary ATR determination in early and late pregnancy and neurodevelopmental assessments at 1-year-old using the Gesell Developmental Scale. Sex-dependent neurodevelopmental effects were identified, characterized by greater vulnerability in adaptive performance among girls and in gross motor among boys. Furthermore, we established a mouse model and exhibited sex‑dependent neurobehavioral deficits in offspring, including male motor impairment and female cognitive dysfunction. Histological and transcriptomic analyses further revealed region‑ and sex‑specific hippocampal neuronal alterations, with dopaminergic neuron loss in the DG region of males and GABAergic neuron elevation in the CA1 region of females. The primary neural stem cell cultures derived from E14.5 fetal mice demonstrated that ATR exposure impaired neurosphere formation and shifted neuronal subtype specification away from the dopaminergic lineage toward glutamatergic and GABAergic fates. By systematically integrating published studies and our results, the TRAEC‑based assessment for ATR yielded a composite evidence score of 8.69, classifying ATR as a high-risk developmental neurotoxicant. Overall, our study establishes a comprehensive framework for evaluating the neurodevelopmental toxicity of ATR exposure during pregnancy, elucidates the sex‑ and region‑specific neuronal mechanisms, and provides robust evidence for the high‑risk classification of ATR as a developmental neurotoxicant.

articles.title: Gestational co-exposure to PM2.5 and heat impaired cardiac development in offspring.
articles.abstract: Air pollution and extreme heat frequently co-occur, yet their combined effects on cardiac development following gestational exposure remain poorly understood. We investigated the effects and potential mechanisms of gestational co-exposure to PM2.5 and heat. Pregnant mice were exposed to filtered air, PM2.5 (10 μg/m3), heat (39 ℃), or both for 2 h/day from embryonic day 6.5 (E6.5) to E18.5, and offspring hearts were evaluated on postnatal day 1 (P1). Gestational co-exposure increased ventricular wall thickness and impaired systolic function, accompanied by inflammatory cell infiltration, oxidative damage, and mitochondrial ultrastructural changes. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that co-exposure altered pathways related to energy metabolism, including inositol phosphate metabolism and pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis. Further analysis of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) revealed that myo-inositol levels and Ucp2 expression were reduced after co-exposure. These changes are noteworthy because myo-inositol has been linked to congenital heart defect risk, while UCP2 contributes to neonatal cardiomyocyte metabolism. Experimental validation further showed that co-exposure decreased ATP content, downregulated cardiac development-related genes, and increased the protein expression of DRP1 and FIS1. Collectively, these findings suggest that mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to impaired cardiac development following gestational co-exposure, with reductions in myo-inositol levels and UCP2 expression potentially involved in this process. These findings provide preliminary mechanistic insights into the developmental cardiotoxicity of combined environmental exposures.

articles.title: Placental microplastic exposure and neonatal cardiovascular biomarkers: Evidence from umbilical cord blood using advanced mixture modeling.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly detected at the maternal-fetal interface, yet human evidence linking placental MP burden with neonatal cardiovascular perturbations remains limited. This study investigated associations between placental MP polymers and cardiovascular, inflammatory, and oxidative-stress biomarkers in umbilical cord blood (UCB). In this cross-sectional study, 198 mother-neonate dyads were evaluated. Six placental MP polymers, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polystyrene (PS), polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polyurethane (PU), were quantified using μ-FTIR and pyrolysis-GC/MS with batch-specific blank correction. Seven UCB biomarkers (NT-proBNP, cTnT, cTnI, CK-MB, IL-6, TNF-α, and hs-CRP) and three oxidative-stress biomarkers (MDA, SOD, and 8-OHdG) were measured. Multivariable regression, weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression, quantile g-computation, Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR), and exploratory mediation analyses were applied. MPs were detected in all placentas, with a median total burden of 11.47 μg/g dry tissue. Higher MP burden was positively correlated with all seven cardiovascular and inflammatory biomarkers (Spearman's ρ=0.41-0.63; all p < 0.001), accompanied by increased MDA and 8-OHdG and decreased SOD activity. PVC showed the strongest individual association with NT-proBNP (β=0.48, 95% CI: 0.31-0.65), while PET was strongly associated with cTnT. WQS, qg-comp, and BKMR consistently demonstrated positive associations between the six-polymer mixture and all seven biomarkers. PVC, PET, and PS were the principal contributors. Exploratory mediation analyses identified statistical indirect associations involving oxidative-stress and inflammatory biomarkers in relation to NT-proBNP and cTnT; however, these findings do not establish temporal or causal mediation. Placental MP burden was associated with an adverse neonatal cardiovascular biomarker profile, accompanied by oxidative and inflammatory alterations. These findings support potential biological perturbation associated with prenatal MP exposure, warranting confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Inhibition of oxytocin neurons during key periods of development has long-term behavioral and body composition effects.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oxytocin (OT) is a key neuromodulator of social behavior in mammals, and accumulating evidence supports the existence of a critical period for OT action during infancy. However, other developmental windows remain poorly explored, and it remains unclear whether OT exerts distinct functions depending on the timing of its activity. In this study, we aimed to determine whether specific developmental stages exist during which OT-expressing neurons play a decisive role with long-term consequences.
METHODS: We used a chemogenetic approach to transiently inhibit OT-expressing neurons during three postnatal developmental periods: infancy, the juvenile period, and young adulthood in male and female mice. Behavioral and metabolic outcomes were then assessed longitudinally. We also examined the effects of inhibiting OT neurons during late fetal stages and at birth.
RESULTS: Social memory was consistently impaired in males, regardless of the timing of neuronal inactivation. The most pronounced behavioral effects were observed following inhibition during infancy in both sexes. Metabolically, adult males from all cohorts exhibited increased body weight, whereas increased fat mass and adipocyte size hypertrophy were specifically observed following inhibition during the juvenile period. Notably, inhibition of OT-expressing neurons around the time of birth resulted in delayed parturition and altered neonatal feeding behavior.
LIMITATIONS: OT-expressing neurons release multiple signaling molecules. However, converging evidence suggests that the observed phenotypes are primarily attributable to OT deficiency. Although this study demonstrates long-term behavioral and metabolic consequences of transient OT neuron inhibition, further experiments are required to elucidate underlying mechanisms and identify additional effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Transient inhibition of OT-expressing neurons during distinct postnatal developmental periods leads to long-lasting effects on social behavior and metabolism, with outcomes depending on both the timing of inhibition and sex. Furthermore, our findings reveal an unexpected role for fetal/neonatal OT neurons in regulating the timing of birth and early feeding behavior.

articles.title: Development of RSV subgroup neutralizing immunity across consecutive seasons with alternating RSV-A and RSV-B predominance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) circulates as two antigenically distinct subgroups, RSV-A and RSV-B, frequently alternating in seasonal predominance. Whether RSV subgroup predominance affects neutralizing immunity and how population immunity shapes subsequent subgroup dynamics, remains unclear. We analyzed multi-season RSV surveillance data and subgroup neutralizing antibody responses to characterize RSV-A/B neutralizing immunity across age groups and successive seasons.
METHODS: We analyzed 41,899 respiratory samples collected through sentinel surveillance to characterize RSV-A and RSV-B circulation across five seasons (2021-2026). Subgroup neutralization was measured by live-virus neutralization assays in post-season serum samples from infants, children and adults.
RESULTS: RSV-A and RSV-B alternated in seasonal predominance, with RSV-A predominating in 2021/22 and 2023/24, RSV-B in 2022/23 and 2025/26, with no clear predominance in 2024/25. In infants, the relative neutralizing activity against RSV-A and RSV-B differed across seasons, whereas adults maintained a balanced neutralizing activity against both subgroups. During the first three years of life, repeated exposure broadened antibody responses toward balanced subgroup neutralization. In the 2021/22, 2022/23, and 2024/25 seasons, lower neutralizing activity in infants was observed against the subgroup that predominated in the subsequent RSV epidemic.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that neutralizing immunity develops from initially subgroup-biased responses after primary RSV infection toward balanced RSV-A/B neutralization with repeated exposure. Subgroup neutralizing activity in infants varied in the context of alternating RSV-A and RSV-B predominance across successive epidemic seasons. These findings provide new insights into age-dependent and seasonally varying patterns of RSV-A/B neutralizing immunity and subgroup circulation.

articles.title: Non-canonical open reading frame-derived antigens as emerging immune targets in cancer immunotherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Cancer immunotherapy predominantly targets mutation-derived neoantigens, thereby limiting its efficacy in low-mutational-burden tumours such as pancreatic and paediatric cancers. Non-canonical open reading frames (ncORFs) generate a diverse repertoire of peptides, the dark immunopeptidome, including upstream ORFs, lncRNA-derived ORFs, and transposable element-derived ORFs, which are efficiently presented by MHC class I molecules.
METHODS: A narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature integrating ribosome profiling, immunopeptidomics, proteogenomics, and functional T-cell assays was conducted across multiple tumour types.
RESULTS: Evidence demonstrates that ncORF-derived peptides are frequently tumour-enriched at the transcript or translation level, and a proportion has been directly identified at the peptide level by HLA-elution immunopeptidomics from primary tumour tissue; a subset can prime antigen-specific CD8+ T-cell responses ex vivo, with cytotoxic activity demonstrated against peptide-pulsed targets in vitro and, in selected cases, against endogenously processed tumour cells. These ncORF-derived antigens may partially evade, and direct human thymic immunopeptidome data are lacking.
CONCLUSIONS: Incorporating ncORF-derived antigens into personalised cancer vaccine strategies could expand therapeutic targets, especially for low-mutational burden and therapy-resistant tumours, but requires further bioinformatic refinement and rigorous safety validation.

articles.title: Higher observed 12-month relapse-free survival with satralizumab than with rituximab in aquaporin-4 immunoglobulin G-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct real-world comparisons of satralizumab and rituximab in aquaporin-4 immunoglobulin G-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder remain uncommon.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study across eight hospitals in Fujian Province, China. Patients aged 12 years or older contributed treatment episodes beginning at the first verifiable administration of satralizumab or rituximab. Patients who changed therapy could contribute one episode to each treatment group, while uncertainty estimates accounted for patient-level clustering. The primary outcome was time to the first clinician-documented NMOSD relapse. Kaplan-Meier methods estimated 12-month relapse-free survival and its absolute between-treatment difference. Restricted mean relapse-free time, recurrent relapses, treatment-period safety events, and exploratory Expanded Disability Status Scale outcomes were also examined. Sensitivity analyses considered treatment switching, episode selection, calendar era, center composition, age restriction, and propensity-score overlap weighting.
RESULTS: The cohort included 103 patients and 115 treatment episodes (50 satralizumab and 65 rituximab). First relapse within 12 months occurred in 1 satralizumab episode and 10 rituximab episodes. Twelve-month relapse-free survival was 98.0% (95% CI, 94.2-100.0%) with satralizumab and 84.6% (95% CI, 76.2-93.8%) with rituximab, an absolute difference of 13.44 percentage points (patient-clustered bootstrap 95% CI, 4.20-23.59). The direction was consistent across the principal unweighted sensitivity analyses. Corrected overlap weighting yielded a 5.28-percentage-point difference (95% CI, -11.69 to 21.21); limited common support, an effective rituximab sample size of 9.38, and appreciable patient influence made this an exploratory estimate. Infection rates were 18.2 and 14.7 events per 100 treatment-episode years, respectively (rate ratio, 1.24; 95% CI, 0.58-2.37), and one serious adverse event occurred in each group. Exploratory EDSS analyses did not identify a clear between-group difference.
CONCLUSIONS: Satralizumab episodes had higher observed 12-month relapse-free survival than rituximab episodes in this cohort. The finding is a clinically relevant real-world comparison signal, while the treatment-specific contribution to the difference remains uncertain because treatment eras were separated, common support was limited, and satralizumab events were sparse.

articles.title: Cell-informed host-response profiling distinguishes neutrophil-like and PLA2G7-associated immunometabolic axes in systemic infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whole-blood host-response signatures can distinguish infection-positive from infection-negative systemic inflammation, but their signal combines changes in leucocyte composition with regulation within cells. We asked whether a retrospectively selected and subsequently fixed blood transcriptomic framework could relate candidate transcripts to granulocyte-associated and monocyte/macrophage-associated expression contexts rather than serve as another stand-alone diagnostic product.
METHODS: A 12-gene framework was retrospectively derived from four contrasts across three studies (444 contrast-level observations; 443 unique arrays) and subsequently fixed for external evaluation using a single-sample transcriptome-rank score. Performance was examined separately across cohorts with different specimens, age groups and comparators. Transcript-score sensitivity analyses, donor-level whole-blood single-cell pseudobulk and cell-line qRT-PCR were used to assess candidate localization and cell-line expression-context concordance. Cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation and colocalisation were included as exploratory genetic context.
RESULTS: In the closest target-context cohort, GSE134347, the fixed score achieved an AUROC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.764-0.889) for sepsis versus non-infectious critical illness. Performance was lower in pediatric day-1 SIRS comparisons, indicating dependence on population and comparator context. Adjustment for alternative neutrophil-associated transcript scores produced a marker-dependent ordering, with SMPDL3A among the most attenuated and PLA2G7 among the least attenuated candidates; no candidate remained FDR-significant in the primary six-gene family. Donor-level single-cell analysis and qRT-PCR supported a monocyte/macrophage context for PLA2G7 and granulocyte-like localization of the diagnostic immune markers. Exploratory Mendelian randomisation did not support a susceptibility effect for the testable immunometabolism-associated candidates, and the HLA-DRB1 regional signal lacked evidence of a shared variant under single-variant colocalisation assumptions.
CONCLUSION: This study provides an auditable, cell-informed framework that relates granulocyte-associated transcription to PLA2G7-associated monocyte/macrophage localization within the whole-blood infection response. The framework is intended for biological prioritisation, and it defines testable candidates for future studies.

articles.title: Necrotizing enterocolitis as a disorder of neonatal mucosal immune ecology: from dysbiosis and barrier failure to regulated cell death and precision prevention.
articles.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) remains one of the most severe gastrointestinal emergencies of prematurity. Although survival of extremely preterm infants has improved, NEC continues to cause substantial mortality, intestinal failure, neurodevelopmental impairment, and prolonged neonatal intensive care. Its pathogenesis has traditionally been described as a convergence of prematurity, enteral feeding, intestinal ischemia, and abnormal bacterial colonization. This model remains useful, but it does not fully explain why only a subset of high-risk infants develop NEC or why single interventions show inconsistent benefit. This narrative review examines classic preterm NEC as a disorder of neonatal mucosal immune ecology, while distinguishing it from spontaneous intestinal perforation and predominantly hemodynamic injury in congenital heart disease. Epithelial immaturity, dysbiosis, altered microbial metabolism, exaggerated pattern-recognition signaling, immune-cell activation, endothelial dysfunction, thromboinflammation, and regulated cell death amplify one another. Particular attention is given to cell-specific signaling, the interaction of vascular and epithelial injury, and the distinction between protective autophagy and destructive stress responses. These mechanisms inform translational opportunities involving mother's own milk, donor human milk, strain-specific probiotics, postbiotics, defined microbial metabolites, extracellular vesicles, organoids, and multi-omics biomarkers. A mucosal immune-ecology model supports precision prevention based on developmental timing, microbial function, immune state, and injury mechanism.

articles.title: Clinical phenotype and diagnostic pathways of 22q11.2 deletion syndrome in a Ukrainian cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) is a common multisystem genomic disorder with marked phenotypic variability and diagnostic delay. Data on diagnostic pathways and specialist involvement in Eastern Europe remain limited. We aimed to characterize diagnostic pathways and clinical triggers, assess specialist involvement and follow-up, and identify factors associated with diagnosis before or after 1 year of age in a Ukrainian cohort.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study of patients with 22q11.2DS registered in the Ukrainian National Registry of Primary Immunodeficiencies. Clinical manifestations, diagnostic triggers, specialists involved in diagnosis and follow-up, immunological findings, and age at diagnosis were analyzed.
RESULTS: The cohort included 126 patients, with a median age of 12 years (range, 0.1-39 years) and median age at diagnosis of 1.0 year (range, 0.1-18 years). Among 120 patients with available diagnostic timing, 63 (52.5%) were diagnosed within the first year, including the two antenatal cases. Congenital heart disease (CHD) was the most frequent major manifestation (74/89, 83.1%), followed by craniofacial dysmorphism (62/74, 83.8%), thymic hypoplasia (54/65, 83.1%), developmental delay (46/62, 74.2%), and recurrent infections (44/65, 67.7%). Among 83 patients with documented diagnostic triggers, CHD was the most frequent (61/83, 73.5%). Developmental delay was more frequent among patients diagnosed after 1 year than within the first year (22.9% vs. 4.4%, p = 0.0135). Immunodeficiency was a diagnostic trigger in 10/83 patients (12.0%), despite T-cell lymphopenia in 31/59 (52.5%). Immunologists and geneticists were most frequently involved in diagnosis. Cardiothoracic surgeons and cardiologists were more frequently involved among patients diagnosed within the first year than after 1 year (27.9% vs. 9.1%, p = 0.0411). Among 13 patients diagnosed after implementation of TREC/KREC newborn screening, two were identified following an abnormal screening result.
CONCLUSIONS: In this Ukrainian cohort, 22q11.2DS diagnosis was predominantly phenotype-driven, with CHD representing the principal diagnostic trigger. Developmental delay was associated with diagnosis after 1 year, whereas immunological abnormalities relatively infrequently initiated diagnostic evaluation. Broader recognition of non-cardiac presentations, standardized referral criteria, coordinated multidisciplinary care, and continued development of newborn and prenatal screening may improve timely diagnosis of 22q11.2DS in Ukraine.

articles.title: Introducing the Open Educational Resource PAVIN: a blended-learning, interprofessional multiplayer virtual reality training in paediatric emergencies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The inherent dynamics of paediatric emergencies create substantial challenges for interprofessional teams and limit the availability of an optimal learning environment for developing emergency‑care competencies. Consequently, there is an increasing demand for educational approaches that replicate the dynamics of paediatric emergencies while offering a safe learning environment. Virtual reality (VR) scenarios deliver realistic, repeatable training experiences that allow novice interprofessional teams to acquire their first exposure in challenging situations. To encounter the demand paediatric-emergency trainings, we aimed to implement a blended-learning course that couples e-learning modules with VR scenarios and incorporates objective feedback systems.
METHODS: We developed the Paediatric virtual reality emergency training (PAVIN), an interprofessional blended-learning course that integrates three complementary components: (1) preparatory e‑learning modules, (2) on-site sessions and (3) multiplayer VR scenarios. The case‑based e‑learning modules supply the theoretical basic medical knowledge and introduce essential non‑technical skills in communication and interprofessional collaboration. Interprofessional tandems - comprising medical, nursing and midwifery students and nursing apprentices - subsequently train in multiplayer VR simulations, offering a safe, reproducible learning environment.
RESULTS: The pilot phase demonstrated that PAVIN could be implemented successfully. Of the ten participants, nine (90% response rate) completed the evaluation questionnaire and awarded the course an overall "very good" rating. They gave positive scores across several self-reported domains: they judged the course highly relevant to their future work, reported heightened interest in interprofessional learning and found the blended-learning framework appropriate. Moreover, participants reported that the immersive VR scenarios helped them internalise paediatric-emergency procedures and that communication and collaboration with their tandem partner improved. We integrated multiple feedback mechanisms throughout the course, encompassing both the e-learning modules and the multiplayer VR scenarios, which participants found useful. They are supplemented with team-performance instruments, such as the virtual Team Performance Observation Tool (vTPOT) and pre- and post-intervention self-assessments.
CONCLUSION: PAVIN is a blended-learning course that offers a safe environment for participants to gain experience in paediatric-emergency care and communication while training in interprofessional teams. Multiple feedback systems are embedded to enable data-driven debriefings. Available as an Open Educational Resource (OER), PAVIN may represent a promising approach for interprofessional medical education, could help meet the ongoing demand for paediatric-emergency training and might has the potential to support medical education in patient safety.

articles.title: Feasibility of a school-based cardiopulmonary resuscitation educational programme incorporating microlearning and gamification in primary school children: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract: Cardiorespiratory arrest (CRA) is a priority public health problem whose survival depends largely on the early action of the community as the first link in the life-saving systems (chain of survival). In this context, international organisations such as the European Resuscitation Council (ERC) promote early training in basic life support (BLS) through initiatives such as Kids Save Lives, integrating cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) education into community-based education strategies.The study, conducted within the framework of the CORE-LIFE research project, evaluated the feasibility of a school-based CPR educational intervention incorporating microlearning and gamification and assessed the delayed performance of selected basic CPR procedural components in a sample of 416 primary school students. The intervention consisted of a short, practical and sequential didactic unit, aligned with the ERC recommendations, followed by a delayed assessment conducted four months after the intervention.The results showed significant differences between grades in the correct execution of the overall CPR sequence (p < 0.001). Four months after training, students demonstrated varying levels of performance across the assessed CPR procedural components. In addition, 95.0% of the 259 available family questionnaires reported positively on the transmission of CPR-related content to the family environment; these exploratory self-reported data suggest perceived intrafamilial dissemination but do not provide evidence of learning or CPR skill acquisition among family members. The intervention was successfully implemented across all six primary school grades, with a high proportion of non-excluded participants completing the four-month assessment. As no pre-specified feasibility criteria were established, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive indicators of implementation rather than as evidence that formal feasibility thresholds were met. However, the absence of a comparison group precludes attributing the observed outcomes to either instructional strategy.

articles.title: Perception and willingness of Greek early career scientists to specialize in infectious diseases: a survey of the Hellenic Society of Chemotherapy Early Career Study Group.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The recent pandemic has highlighted the role of Infectious Diseases (ID) Specialists. In Greece, ID is a two-year subspecialty of internal medicine or pediatrics. We aimed to discover the willingness of early career Greek scientists (ECS) to specialize in ID.
METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among undergraduate 4th -5th -6th -year medical students, residents of internal medicine/pediatrics, and Master (MSc) graduates of the Program "Infectious Diseases" of the University of Athens. Data were collected via an electronic case report form ( https://hsch.gr/erotimatologia/ ) from 17 September to 16 November 2025 and included demographics, level of education/training, satisfaction of ID training, willingness to specialize in ID, reasons if not, and suggestions how ID would attract more scientists. All society members were contacted by email, as well as, members of two panhellenic medical student societies.
RESULTS: In total, 556 ECS responded; 310 students, 192 residents, and 54 MSc graduates; 66.9% were female, aged 27 ± 6 years, and 81.5% were aware that ID is a subspecialty. Among medical students, 274 (88.4%) were exposed very often/often to patients with common infections, whereas 254 (81.9%) never or seldom to infections in special populations. Respectively, 189 (98.4%) residents reported being exposed very often to patients with common infections and 88 (45.8%) to infections in special populations. Among respondents, 22.6% of students declared intention to specialize in ID; 41.1% of residents and 81.5% of MSc holders (p < 0.001). 17.5% of medical students declared that although interested in ID, they do not wish to train in Internal Medicine/Pediatrics. When participants were asked "how ID would be more attractive", 39.8% responded by training for some time in an ID center in Europe/ USA and 24.8% in a special field such as immunocompromised patients.
CONCLUSION: Results imply that it may be the case that independent training with a separate curriculum makes ID more attractive.

articles.title: Telerehabilitation and teleassessment in rare pediatric neurological disorders: an ERN-RND telerehabilitation working group systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Children and adolescents with rare neurological disorders (RNDs) often require long-term rehabilitation, but specialist access is limited by geography, medical fragility, and travel burden. Telerehabilitation and teleassessment may extend care into the home, yet evidence remains fragmented. We evaluated functional outcomes and summarized feasibility, adherence, acceptability, safety, and teleassessment measurement properties.
METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251238931) followed PRISMA and SWiM guidance. PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched through April 20, 2026, supplemented by citation searching. Eligible studies evaluated telerehabilitation or teleassessment in participants aged ≤18 years with Orphanet-classified RNDs and reported child-level functional outcomes. Mixed cohorts required separable data or ≥80% eligible participants. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias and certainty of evidence using design-appropriate tools.
RESULTS: 2,260 unique records were screened and 71 full texts assessed; 16 studies were included. 13 evaluated telerehabilitation (316 participants: 203 intervention, 113 comparator/control) and 3 evaluated teleassessment (94 participants). Most studies involved neuromuscular disorders, mainly Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy; other conditions included Rett syndrome, Fragile X syndrome, Dravet syndrome, Canavan disease, Guillain-Barré syndrome, and rare pediatric ataxias. Technologies included videoconferencing, apps, wearable sensors, and video-based assessment. Telerehabilitation was associated with improvement or stabilization in selected motor, respiratory, cognitive, communication, and daily functional outcomes, whereas global measures often showed limited short-term change. Feasibility, adherence, and acceptability were generally favorable. No major telerehabilitation-related safety concerns were reported when assessed. Teleassessment showed good reliability or agreement with in-person motor assessment.
DISCUSSION: In selected pediatric RNDs, telerehabilitation and teleassessment demonstrate strong feasibility, high acceptability, and meaningful clinical potential as effective complements to in-person care. These approaches offer valuable opportunities to expand access, enhance continuity of care, and support patient-centered rehabilitation. Larger multicenter studies should evaluate long-term outcomes and equitable implementation.

articles.title: Predicting late-pregnancy depression using machine learning: A longitudinal study with external validation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Depressive symptoms in late pregnancy is a serious public health issue with profound effects on maternal well-being and infant development. Developing a data-driven predictive model for depressive symptoms in late pregnancy can facilitate early identification and provide a basis for timely intervention.
METHODS: Six machine learning (ML) models were compared by nested cross-validation (5 × 3 repeats), including Lasso Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Multilayer Perceptrons, Naive Bayes, Random Forests, and Extreme Gradient Boosting. The Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) was used for the assessment of depressive symptoms during pregnancy. The models were evaluated on accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Matthews correlation coefficient, Brier score, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were utilized to improve model interpretability and highlight important predictive features. The development cohort comprised 713 pregnant women at 28-36 weeks of gestation recruited during prenatal visits at the obstetrics clinic of a major hospital in Wuhan, China. For temporal external validation, a separate cohort of 515 pregnant women at 37-40 weeks of gestation was recruited at the same clinic during a later period.
RESULTS: The Lasso Logistic Regression model outperformed the other models in terms of predictive accuracy and generalizability in the temporal external validation. Key predictors of depressive symptoms in late pregnancy included early-pregnancy insomnia symptoms, EPDS score, and fear of pregnancy. The model demonstrated robust performance in temporal external validation, offering an effective tool for predicting depressive symptoms in late pregnancy.
CONCLUSION: This study developed a reliable and interpretable ML model for the early identification of women at high risk of depressive symptoms in late pregnancy. The findings suggest that ML, particularly Lasso Logistic Regression, can be integrated into prenatal care to enhance early screening and facilitate timely intervention for high-risk women, improving maternal mental health outcomes. We further developed a web-based tool to facilitate the clinical application of the model.

articles.title: Automated extraction of seizures and ictal-interictal continuum patterns from EEG reports to enable large-scale neurophysiology and neurocritical care research.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Critical clinical information in EEG reports is often locked in free text, limiting large-scale research. This work develops and validates an automated, cross-institutional pipeline to extract seizures, rhythmic patterns, and ictal-interictal continuum features for population-level neurophysiology studies.
METHODS: We developed a five-stage hybrid pipeline comprising: (1) text normalization, (2) rule-based pattern filtering to focus the analysis on relevant report segments, (3) segment-focused prompt generation, (4) large language model (LLM) inference for structured attribute extraction, and (5) post-processing. This hybrid design combines the consistency of rule-based screening with the flexibility of LLM-based extraction from variable free-text EEG reports. The pipeline was applied to 156,582 EEG reports from three health systems (two adult, one pediatric). Performance was evaluated using a balanced set of 1,500 expert-reviewed samples, which extracted seizure presence, count, burden, and timing, as well as the frequency and prevalence of periodic and rhythmic patterns. Patterns included lateralized periodic discharges (LPD), generalized periodic discharges (GPD), and generalized/lateralized rhythmic delta activity (GRDA/LRDA).
RESULTS: The pipeline achieved high performance across health systems for seizure (average accuracy 0.94) and periodic and rhythmic pattern detection (LPD: 0.97 [95 % CI: 0.94-0.99], GPD: 0.96 [0.92-0.98], GRDA/LRDA: 0.97 [0.94-0.99]). Seizure specificity was 0.72 at two adult institutions (95 % CI: 0.66-0.77) and 0.99 at the other two (one adult and one pediatric). Frequency and prevalence extraction showed strong agreement with mean values 0.94 and 0.93, respectively. High-frequency discharges (≥2 Hz) were associated with higher seizure occurrence within 24 and 48 h in descriptive analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: This study introduces a scalable method for EEG analysis using clinical narratives, linking rhythmic patterns to seizure progression and supporting critical care risk stratification and large-scale EEG outcome prediction research.

articles.title: "Feeding for happiness": Caregiver use of food for emotion regulation and obesity in Thai children with autism spectrum disorder.
articles.abstract: Children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) face an elevated risk of overweight and obesity, yet post-pandemic data from Asian settings remain scarce. Caregiver feeding practices, particularly using food to regulate a child's emotions, represent a potentially modifiable pathway to excess adiposity. This cross-sectional study estimated the prevalence of overweight and obesity among Thai children with ASD and examined associations with caregiver feeding practices. We assessed 136 child-caregiver dyads (aged 5-15 years) at a tertiary psychiatric clinic in Bangkok, Thailand. Child weight and height were measured directly, with BMI-for-age z-scores classified using World Health Organization standards. Caregiver behaviors were evaluated via an interviewer-administered questionnaire adapted from established feeding frameworks. Logistic regression examined associations with overweight or obesity (> +1 SD) as well as overweight (> +1 to ≤ +2 SD) and obesity (> +2 SD) separately, adjusting a priori for child age, sex, and atypical antipsychotic use. Overall, 50.7% of children had overweight (18.4%) or obesity (32.4%). In the adjusted combined model, age > 8 years (AOR 2.385, 95% CI 1.017-5.310) and allowing the child to eat more to promote happiness (AOR 4.956, 95% CI 1.360-18.058) were independently associated with overweight or obesity. In separate adjusted models, allowing the child to eat more to promote happiness remained independently associated with both overweight (AOR 6.666, 95% CI 1.235-35.986) and obesity (AOR 5.099, 95% CI 1.261-20.623). These findings support incorporating culturally sensitive guidance on alternative emotion regulation strategies into ASD management.

articles.title: Indirect pathways linking psychological flexibility with paranoia worries through social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking, and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions among late adolescents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional study examines the association between psychological flexibility and paranoia worries, through indirect pathways of social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking, and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions. This cross-sectional study aimed to examine the direct and indirect pathways linking psychological flexibility and paranoia worries among late adolescents aged 18-20 years.
METHODS: Data were collected from 967 late adolescents aged 18-20 years in eastern China, including sociodemographic characteristics, psychological flexibility, paranoia worries, COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions, social-media-related social anxiety, antisocial rule-breaking, and social-emotional expertise. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to analyze the direct and indirect pathways linking psychological flexibility with paranoia worries through social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions.
RESULTS: Significant indirect associations between psychological flexibility and paranoia worries were observed through social-media-related social anxiety (β = -0.089, p = 0.001). Psychological flexibility was indirectly associated with paranoia worries through COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions (β = 0.023, p = 0.001). Significant indirect associations between psychological flexibility and paranoia worries were observed through a sequential indirect pathway of social-media-related social anxiety and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions (β = -0.021, p = 0.001). These findings highlight indirect pathways linking psychological flexibility with paranoia worries through social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight indirect associations linking psychological flexibility with paranoia worries through social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking, and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions among late adolescents. The findings may provide useful insights for research involving comparable late-adolescent and university student populations. Broader applicability to other sociocultural and upper-and middle-income countries (UMICs) contexts requires further cross-cultural replication.

articles.title: Associations of trimester-specific maternal lipid levels with abnormal foetal birth weights: a cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy triggers substantial increases in maternal lipids, which are essential for foetal growth but are linked to severe adverse outcomes when dysregulated. Despite evidence linking dyslipidaemia to birth weight abnormalities, inconsistent findings and a lack of standardized management criteria persist.
METHODS: A cohort study involving 2,032 participants was conducted in Beijing, China. The associations between maternal lipid profiles across early, middle, and late pregnancy and foetal birth weight outcomes were assessed by multivariate logistic regression, chain mediation models, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis.
RESULTS: Multivariate analysis demonstrated that third-trimester total cholesterol (TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDLC), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDLC) levels were significantly inversely associated with the risk of small for gestational age (SGA) outcomes (all ORs < 1, P < 0.05). Conversely, third-trimester triglyceride (TG) levels were significantly positively associated with large for gestational age (LGA) outcomes (OR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.05-1.47, P < 0.05). Additionally, late-pregnancy HDLC and LDLC levels were protective against LGA outcomes (adjusted OR = 0.44 and 0.64, respectively; P < 0.05). Chain mediation analysis revealed that early and mid-pregnancy lipids were not directly associated with birth weight but were significantly associated with outcomes through indirect pathways mediated by late-pregnancy lipids (TG_1→TG_3→LGA, β = 0.073; TC_1→TC_3 →SGA, β = - 0.122). Furthermore, the RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear relationship between third-trimester TG levels and birth weight with a saturation threshold of 4.88 mmol/L. Below this level, birth weight increased positively with increasing TG concentration.
