CONCLUSION: Late-pregnancy lipid profiles exhibit the strongest direct associations with birth weight deviation. Specifically, elevated TC, HDLC, and LDLC levels in the third trimester are protective against SGA outcomes, whereas TG in the third trimester is nonlinearly associated with birth weight. Crucially, early and mid-pregnancy lipids are indirectly associated with these outcomes, suggesting that trimester-specific monitoring and tailored interventions throughout gestation may be important for optimizing foetal growth.

articles.title: Long-term Risk of Neoplasms After Childhood Growth Hormone Therapy in Patients with Turner Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with Turner syndrome have a distinct pattern of neoplastic events occurrence, although their overall cancer risk does not appear to exceed that of the general population. Recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) therapy is widely used to improve adult height, but concerns remain regarding its long-term safety.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term risk of neoplastic events among patients with Turner syndrome treated with rhGH during childhood and to examine associations between rhGH treatment duration or dose.
DESIGN, SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including all Swedish patients with Turner syndrome treated with rhGH during childhood between 1983 and 2010 (n=583) and matched comparators (n=8745). Follow-up continued until the first neoplastic event, death, emigration or December 31, 2020.
RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 20.2 years (188445 person-years), patients with Turner syndrome had an increased hazard of overall neoplastic events (Hazard Ratio, HR, 2.0, 95% confidence interval, CI: 1.7-2.4), and of benign neoplasms (HR 2.5, 95% CI: 2.1-3.0), but not of malignant neoplasms (HR 0.7, 95% CI: 0.5-1.1). Hazards were increased for malignant neoplasms of the gastrointestinal tract and several benign neoplasms, while female genital malignancies were decreased. Neither rhGH treatment duration nor dose was associated with malignant or overall neoplastic risk.
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Patients with Turner syndrome treated with rhGH in childhood had an increased risk of overall neoplastic events driven primarily by benign neoplasms. No association was observed between rhGH treatment duration or dose and neoplastic risk in early to mid-adulthood, supporting its long-term safety.

articles.title: Predicting Treatment Quality in Children and Adolescents with Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia Using Insulin and Renin.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Monitoring treatment quality in congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) remains challenging. Current approaches rely predominantly on bone age and serum steroid measurements, which are variable and require expert interpretation. Reliable, accessible biochemical indicators are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a predictive score for undertreatment in children and adolescents with CAH using routinely available clinical and non-steroid laboratory parameters.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective, multicenter cohort study including 81 patients with genetically confirmed 21-hydroxylase deficiency across four European pediatric endocrinology centers. Clinical features and laboratory parameters-including fasting insulin, renin, lipid profile, glucose, and growth indices-were assessed at three outpatient visits. Treatment status (optimal, undertreatment, overtreatment) was classified by expert endocrinologists. Logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of undertreatment and to construct a predictive model.
RESULTS: Data from 233 visits were analyzed. Undertreated patients showed significantly higher insulin (p = 0.005), higher renin (p = 0.003), increased height SDS (p = 0.014), and lower HDL cholesterol (p = 0.007) compared with optimally treated patients. The final predictive model retained insulin (coefficient 1.15) and renin (1.038) as independent predictors. At a threshold of ≥30-36, sensitivity was 71%, specificity 84%and overall correct classification 80%. The ROC curve yielded an AUC of 0.785.
CONCLUSION: Serum insulin and renin, two inexpensive and routinely measured parameters, predict undertreatment in children and adolescents with CAH with good accuracy. Their dual relevance for short-term treatment monitoring and long-term cardiometabolic risk underscores their potential as practical tools to complement current strategies.

articles.title: Prevalence and Symptom Network of Co-Occurring Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms and Their Associations with Quality of Life Among Chinese Empty-Nest Older Adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The growing number of empty-nest older adults in China has become a critical public health concern. Living apart from adult children may reduce opportunities for daily family interaction and emotional support and increase feelings of loneliness, potentially increasing vulnerability to anxiety and depressive symptoms. The aim of this study was to investigate the prevalence and network structure of co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms, and explored their association with quality of life (QoL) among Chinese empty-nest older adults.
METHODS: We included 5110 empty-nest older adults aged 65 and above from the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS2018). Anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms, and QoL were respectively assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale-7 (GAD-7), the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale-10 (CESD-10), and the World Health Organization Quality of Life-brief (WHOQOL-Bref). Co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms were defined as concurrent CESD-10 ≥ 10 and GAD-7 ≥ 5. We performed network analyses of co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms to identify central and bridge symptoms, and constructed a flow network to examine their associations with QoL. Multivariable linear regression analyses were conducted to assess the associations between symptom-status groups and QoL after adjustment for potential confounders.
RESULTS: The prevalence of co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms among Chinese empty-nest older adults was 8.67%. Network analysis revealed CESD3 (felt depressed), GAD4 (trouble relaxing) and GAD2 (uncontrollable worry) exhibited relatively high expected influence (EI) values within the anxiety and depressive symptom network. Concurrently, GAD1 (nervousness), GAD4 (trouble relaxing), CESD1 (bothered by things), and CESD6 (felt fearful) were identified as potential bridge symptoms between anxiety and depressive symptom communities. Moreover, CESD10 (sleep disturbances) showed a relatively strong negative association with quality of life (QoL). After adjustment for potential confounders, all three symptom groups had significantly lower QoL scores than the control group (depression-only: β = -0.96; anxiety-only: β = -0.33; co-occurring symptoms: β = -1.28; all p ≤ 0.001). Pairwise comparisons further showed that the co-occurring symptoms group had lower QoL scores than both the depression-only group (mean difference = -0.32, p < 0.001) and the anxiety-only group (mean difference = -0.95, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms are relatively common among Chinese empty-nest older adults and are significantly associated with poorer quality of life. It is important to pay attention to both central and bridge symptoms when assessing mental health in this population. Interventions aimed at addressing sleep disturbances among empty-nest older adults may be beneficial for supporting their mental health and improving their quality of life.

articles.title: The Varying Benefits of Two Years Automated Insulin Delivery System Use on Continuous Glucose Monitoring Profiles in Children and Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems are recommended for youths with type 1 diabetes, but real-world longitudinal data remains limited despite increasing use. This study evaluates the effect of 2 years of AID use on continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) profiles and body mass index (BMI) development.
METHODS: Data from individuals with type 1 diabetes aged <18 years, diabetes duration >3 months, and AID use of >3 months from the Diabetes Prospective Follow-up (DPV) Registry between 2019 and 2025 were analyzed. CGM and HbA1c were required at the last documented time in range (TIR) (±90 days; follow-up) and 2 years earlier (±90 days; baseline). Changes were investigated using adjusted regression models with repeated measurements.
FINDINGS: Data from 2486 participants (baseline: median age: 11.9 years, diabetes duration: 5.0 years, 53% male) were analyzed over ∼23 months. The largest gains occurred in time in tight range (TiTR) (42.4% [95% confidence interval: 41.0-43.7] to 50.1% [48.8-51.4]; P < 0.001) and coefficient of variation (CV) (32.9 [32.0-33.7] to 29.5 [28.7-30.2]; P < 0.001). HbA1c (7.3% [7.2-7.3] to 7.2 [7.1-7.2]; P < 0.001), TIR (64.5% [63.9-65.1] to 66.7% [66.1-67.3]; P < 0.001), and mean sensor glucose (SG) (161.0 mg/dL [158.4-163.5] to 155.5 mg/dL [153.1-157.9]; P = 0.001) improved statistically, but below clinical relevance thresholds. Time below range (TBR) < 70 mg/dL increased (2.7% [2.6-2.9] to 3.2% [3.1-3.4]; P < 0.001), TBR < 54 mg/dL remained stable (1.7%-1.8%; P = 0.516), and severe hypoglycemia decreased (6.4-4.5/100 patient-years; P < 0.001). No changes were seen in children <6 years. In youth 6 to <12 and 12 to <18 years, TiTR and CV improved most, while TBR increased. BMI-standard deviation score (SDS) increased (0.57 [0.53-0.61] to 0.67 [0.63-0.72]; P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: After 2 years of AID use, TiTR and CV showed clinically relevant improvements, while TBR < 70 mg/dL increased with stable TBR < 54 mg/dL and severe hypoglycemia decreased. Changes in TIR, SG, and HbA1c were statistically significant but small, yet noteworthy, as glycemia usually deteriorates during adolescence. The increase in BMI-SDS needs to be further investigated.

articles.title: Potential Central Neuroprotective and Peripheral Intestinal Homeostasis-Regulating Effects of Jiuwei Xifeng Granules in MPTP-Induced Parkinson's Disease Mice.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Jiuwei Xifeng Granules (JXG) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula made from nine herbs, which include: Gastrodiae Rhizoma, Rehmanniae Radix Praeparata, Gentianae Radix Et Rhizoma, etc. The formula is generally used to nourish yin and tonify the kidney, calm the liver and stop wind, resolve phlegm, and soothe the mind. Clinically, it is mainly used to treat pediatric tic disorders caused by kidney yin deficiency and liver wind stirring, but its potential in treating Parkinson's disease remains untapped and is worthy of further exploration.
AIM OF THE STUDY: In a 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced PD mouse model, the neuroprotective effects of JXG and its possible molecular signaling pathways in PD mice were investigated.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An MPTP-induced PD mouse model was used, and a control group, a model group, low- and high-dose JXG groups, and an L-Dopa positive control group were set up. The effects of JXG were evaluated through behavioral studies, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, Western blot, transcriptome sequencing, 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics.
RESULTS: Motor dysfunction in MPTP mice can be improved by JXG, TH-positive neurons in the substantia nigra can be protected, abnormal α-syn aggregation can be reduced, and microglial activation can be inhibited. The dopaminergic synapse was suggested by transcriptome sequencing to be one of the core enriched pathways; after JXG intervention, p-ERK and p-CREB levels rebounded, and the protein expression of VMAT2, DAT, and Drd2 was synchronously upregulated, suggesting a potential association between the ERK-CREB signaling axis and the modulation of dopaminergic synaptic function by JXG. MPTP induced motor dysfunction, as well as colonic damage. At the peripheral level, JXG alleviated colonic barrier damage, inhibited colonic iNOS, TNF-α, and IL-6 mRNA expression, and was associated with alterations in the dysregulated gut microbiota and the recovery of arginine and proline metabolism. Furthermore, JXG improved the oxidative-inflammatory imbalance in both gut and brain tissues by lowering MDA and increasing GSH.
CONCLUSION: The multi-target anti-PD effects of JXG are manifested as concurrent central dopaminergic neuroprotection and peripheral gut homeostasis improvement. Nevertheless, the causal relationship between the ERK-CREB signaling axis and synaptic proteins, as well as the exact gut-brain interaction mechanisms, still need further verification.

articles.title: Regional and national burden and aetiologies of non-COVID lower respiratory infections in Latin America and the Caribbean, 1990-2023: a secondary analysis of the global burden of disease study 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income regions. Reliable, up-to-date burden estimates are needed to inform public health strategies in Latin America and the Caribbean, where prevention and management strategies remain heterogeneous. We aimed to characterise temporal and geographical patterns in LRTI mortality, incidence, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and aetiology across the region from 1990 to 2023.
METHODS: We analysed secondary, modelled estimates of mortality, incidence, and DALYs attributable to LRTIs in Latin America and the Caribbean from 1990 to 2023, extracted from the GBD 2023 Results Tool and produced following the standardised GBD protocol coordinated by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME).
FINDINGS: In Latin America and the Caribbean, LRTI mortality declined in most countries between 1990 and 2023, with the steepest reductions among children younger than five years (e.g., Brazil ARC -6·16, 95% UI -6·61 to -5·71). All-age mortality rose in some countries, but age-standardised rates showed that these increases reflected population ageing rather than rising age-specific risk. Following a sustained pre-pandemic decline, incidence showed and overall upward direction in the post-pandemic period across age groups, although the magnitude and statistical relevance of these changes varied by age and country, with the largest increase observed among children in Suriname (ARC +8·84, 95% UI +2·80 to +14·95). Streptococcus pneumoniae remained the leading cause of LRTI mortality in 2023 (7·68 per 100,000, 95% UI 7·11-8·24; ARC -2·70, 95% UI -2·96 to -2·45).
INTERPRETATION: LRTIs remain a major cause of death in the region, with substantial progress among children but persistent burden among older adults, driven by population ageing, and evidence of a post-pandemic increase in incidence. There is a great importance of combining clinical interventions with broader public health strategies addressing vaccination coverage, antimicrobial-resistance surveillance, nutrition, housing, and access to primary care, particularly in populations that have experienced less favourable trends.
FUNDING: Wellcome Trust (303666/Z/23/Z); UK International Development (301542-403); the Gates Foundation (INV-063472) and Universidad de La Sabana (MED-289-2020).

articles.title: Oropouche virus disease across Latin America during the 2023-2025 epidemic: a multi-country case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2023-2025 epidemic of Oropouche virus (OROV) disease across Latin America raised public health concerns due to its expansion into previously unaffected regions, alongside reports of increased clinical severity and vertical transmission.
METHODS: We conducted a multi-country case series to characterise the clinical presentation, disease course, outcomes, and virological features of OROV disease during the 2023-2025 epidemic. Analyses were descriptive.
FINDINGS: We describe 2716 OROV disease cases reported between January 31st, 2024, and November 4th, 2025, across ten states in Brazil, Panama, and Peru. Median age was 38 years (IQR 25-51); 1379/2716 (51%) were female. Most common symptoms were fever (89%), headache (88%), and myalgia (59%), followed by retro-orbital pain (47%). One-fourth of participants reported symptoms' duration beyond one week. Most cases were mild (2542/2716; 94%), although severe manifestations and one death occurred. Haemorrhagic manifestations were reported in 41/2716 (2%), and 7/2716 (<1%) developed severe disease temporally associated with OROV infection. Among 108 pregnant women, 15 (14%) had adverse pregnancy outcomes, including abortions, preterm births, stillbirths, and symptomatic newborns; no congenital malformations were observed. Older age, comorbidities, warning signs, and laboratory abnormalities were more frequently observed among participants with complications. Prolonged RNA detection beyond seven days was observed in serum and urine.
INTERPRETATION: Although most OROV disease cases were mild, severe disease and adverse pregnancy outcomes occur and may be under-recognised. These findings support the need for improved clinical recognition, risk stratification, and diagnostics, particularly for high-risk groups, and highlight priorities for surveillance and future research.
FUNDING: None.

articles.title: Pediatric intensive care resources in Ibero-Latin America: SPREAD PED Ibero-Latin America, a multinational, multicentre, cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) are a cornerstone of child survival, yet their structure, staffing, and adherence to evidence-based protocols vary widely across regions. Comprehensive and contemporary data from Ibero-Latin America are lacking. We aimed to characterize the organization, human resources, and implementation of standardized care practices in PICUs across this region.
METHODS: We conducted an international, multicentre, cross-sectional study including all PICUs admitting patients during a five-day period (Sept 2024) across 21 countries in Latin America, Spain, and Portugal. Unit-level data were obtained through a standardized electronic survey describing hospital characteristics, workforce distribution, monitoring capabilities, and clinical protocols. The primary objective was to characterize the distribution of structural and organizational features of participating PICUs across the región; secondary outcomes examined multidisciplinary coverage and adherence to standardized care practices.
FINDINGS: Among 339 PICUs (70.6% public; 61.4% university-affiliated), nearly half had fewer than ten beds. Median physician-to-patient ratio was 1:5-6 by day and 1:8-10 overnight. Nursing ratios varied widely, most favourable in the Iberian region (≈1:1-2) and least in the Andean block (≈1:3-4), underscoring inequities in bedside care capacity. Only 68% of units had dedicated physiotherapists, with far lower coverage from nutritionists, psychologists, or pharmacists. Basic monitoring and ventilation were nearly universal (>95%), yet advanced technologies-cardiac output, near-infrared spectroscopy, renal replacement therapy-were available in fewer than 40% of centers. Structured protocols for sepsis, mechanical ventilation, sedation, or antimicrobial stewardship were reported in only 56% of PICUs, with adherence highest in the Iberian and lowest in the Andean and Caribbean regions.
INTERPRETATION: This multinational, multicentre assessment provides the first comprehensive and contemporary map of pediatric critical care capacity across Ibero-Latin America, revealing major disparities in infrastructure, human resources, and protocol implementation. Strengthening human capital, multidisciplinary training, and regionally adapted strategies is essential to achieve equitable, high-quality critical care for children across the region.
FUNDING: This work was supported by institutional funding from the Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo (FAPESP; Grant No. 2017/21052-0), provided to the Latin American Sepsis Institute (ILAS) to support the conduct of the study, including research assistant and statistical support.

articles.title: Drosha in mesangial cells regulates glomerular capillary tufts formation through drosha/ribosome/Gata3 axis.
articles.abstract: Drosha is a critical regulator of kidney development; its loss or mutation, identified in a subset of Wilms tumor (WT), a pediatric kidney cancer, leads to nephric cap mesenchyme developmental defects. Here, we investigated the role of Drosha in mesangial cells and its impact on glomerular capillary tuft formation. Mesangial cells specific deletion of Drosha (Drosha cKO) in mouse model was generated. Deletion of Drosha in mesangial cells disrupted the glomerular capillary tufts formation, leading to dysplastic glomeruli, proteinuria, oliguria, reduced looping of glomerular capillaries and capillary dilation. Drosha knockdown in mesangial cells (SV40 MES 13) leads to decreased cell proliferation and reduced Gata3 protein level. Transcriptome analysis by RNA-seq shows decreased levels of ribosomal protein genes (RPGs) but unaltered mRNA levels of major genes affecting kidney development, including Gata3, Pax2, Atn1, Wt1 etc., in Drosha-KD compared to Control SV40 MES13 cells. Further analysis indicates Drosha regulates the translation of Gata3 in mesangial cells via regulating RPG transcription. Removal of Drosha in adult mesangial cells did not cause significant kidney dysfunction, indicating that Drosha functions primarily during development rather than in homeostasis. Our work reveals that Drosha in mesangial cells orchestrates the formation of glomerular capillary tufts by regulating Gata3 translation. It identifies the critical role of DROSHA in nephric development and proposes DROSHA as a novel potential causal gene for congenital anomalies of the kidney and the urinary tract (CAKUT).

articles.title: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity and functional disability in middle-aged and older adults: a harmonized multicohort study.
articles.abstract: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is highly prevalent in aging populations, yet its association and underlying mechanisms with functional disability (FD) remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate CMM-FD relationship, quantify the influencing mechanisms, and explore heterogeneity across different CMM patterns and population subgroups. A multicohort study was conducted by pooling harmonized longitudinal data from three international aging cohorts. CMM was defined as the co-occurrence of at least two cardiometabolic diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, heart diseases, and stroke. FD was measured through difficulty performing basic or instrumental activities of daily living. Logistic regression models were used to estimate associations and heterogeneities, and Kohler-Holm-Breen decomposition was used to quantify mediating contributions. CMM prevalence was 22.53%, and FD prevalence was 23.01%. CMM was strongly associated with higher odds of FD (OR = 2.940; p < 0.001), with consistent findings across all countries and FD subtypes. Respiratory, neuropsychiatric, and sensory conditions jointly explained 20.44% of the association, with psychological problems contributing the largest share. CMM patterns involving stroke generally showed high odds of FD, while the four-disease combination had the largest overall point estimate. Middle-aged, male, married, childless, non-retired, and smoking older adults exhibited a stronger CMM-associated elevation in odds of FD. Early identification of high-risk CMM patterns, routine screening for functional and psychological, cognitive, respiratory, and sensory symptoms, and targeted follow-up for individuals with stroke-containing or complex CMM patterns may reduce the risk of functional deterioration and support independent living in aging populations.

articles.title: Mentalization-based treatment for eating disorders: a systematic review and narrative synthesis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mentalization-based treatment (MBT) targets difficulties in reflective functioning, emotion regulation and interpersonal relationships, which may contribute to the development and maintenance of eating disorders (EDs). This systematic review synthesised the available quantitative evidence on the outcomes of MBT or MBT-informed interventions for people with EDs.
METHODS: A protocol was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024421136) and the review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Bibliographic databases, trial registries, grey-literature sources and Google Scholar were searched from inception to 1 July 2026. Forward and backward citation chaining was conducted. Eligible studies included quantitative, longitudinal studies reporting outcomes of MBT or MBT-informed treatment in children, adolescents, or adults with a diagnosed ED. Two reviewers independently conducted each stage of study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment. Findings were synthesised narratively because clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Seven reports described 326 reported enrolments of participants with EDs; two reports may have included overlapping clinical samples. The evidence comprised three randomised controlled trials, two quasi-experimental studies, and two prospective observational studies. Samples were small and diagnostically heterogeneous, and interventions varied in format and duration. Although within-group improvements in ED symptoms and broader psychological functioning were frequently reported, comparative studies did not demonstrate consistent superiority of MBT over comparator interventions. All randomised studies raised some concerns about risk of bias, and all non-randomised studies were judged to have a critical risk of bias overall.
CONCLUSIONS: Evidence for MBT and MBT-informed interventions in EDs remains preliminary and is insufficient to establish comparative effectiveness or sustained benefit. Future research should use adequately powered, methodologically rigorous studies to clarify which people are most likely to benefit from MBT, in which clinical contexts, and through which mechanisms.
PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD42024421136.

articles.title: Weight talk and its association with disordered eating in children and adolescents: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Disordered eating has become increasingly prevalent among children and adolescents, with weight talk identified as a potential contributing factor.
METHOD: This meta-analysis examined the strength and nature of this relationship using a three-level model across 460 effect sizes and examined potential moderators related to the characteristics of weight talk, types of disordered eating, and characteristics of sample.
RESULTS: Results indicated a small but significant positive association between weight talk and disordered eating (r = 0.27). Moderation analyses revealed that characteristics of weight talk and types of disordered eating significantly influenced this relationship. In particular, the strongest associations were observed when weight talk was negative, targeted both the listener and oneself, originated from the self, and involved mixed forms of weight talk (i.e., comments, teasing, and encouragement to lose weight). The association was most pronounced for variables related to anorexia and bulimia. In contrast, participant characteristics such as age, gender, ethnicity, and country were not significant moderators. However, the sample was predominantly female and White, limiting the generalisability of the findings.
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the importance of addressing weight talk in prevention and intervention efforts to reduce disordered eating among children and adolescents.

articles.title: The Diabetes Eating Problem Survey-Revised (DEPS-R) in a Finnish adolescent and adult population with insulin-dependent diabetes: a validation study in Finland.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Diabetes Eating Problem Survey-Revised (DEPS-R) has been widely studied in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1D), but fewer studies have validated the DEPS-R in adults. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the factor structure, internal consistency, and criterion validity of the Finnish version of the DEPS-R in adolescents over 16 years of age and adults with insulin dependent diabetes (T1D and T2D).
METHODS: The sample consisted of 201 patients with insulin dependent diabetes, including individuals with T1D (93%) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). Inclusion criteria were age over 16 years. Mean age was 34.5 years (SD 14.7). Both males and females were included (56.7% females). Participants completed DEPS-R and Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire (EDE-Q). Construct validity and factor structure of the DEPS-R questionnaire was to be explored by conducting confirmatory and exploratory factor analyses. The association between DEPS-R and EDE-Q total scores was calculated using Spearman´s correlation coefficient. Criterion validity analysis with the ROC curve analysis was conducted to investigate the ability of the 16-item Finnish version of DEPS-R to identify respondents with a greater risk of eating disorder.
RESULTS: Because of the skewness of item distributions, the results of confirmatory factor analyses and exploratory factor analysis were discarded. DEPS-R scores correlation coefficient to EDE-Q score was positive with Spearman's rho 0.678 (p < .001). The reliability of the full scale was α = 0.860. In ROC curve analysis, the area under the curve was large (AUC = 0.94%, asymptotic 95% confidence interval 0.89-0.99%). According to Youden's index, the optimal DEPS-R cut-off score for detecting heightened risk of eating disorder in this study was ≥ 17 points, with that score sensitivity was 0.94 and specificity was 0.82.
CONCLUSIONS: Based on clinical guidelines, a diabetes-specific screening tool for disordered eating behavior is recommended to be used routinely in the clinical care of adults with insulin-dependent diabetes. According to the present study, the Finnish version of DEPS-R shows good criterion validity, when ROC curve was used. Based on this study cut-off score ≥ 17 points may be more suitable than cut-off score ≥ 20 points, but further studies are needed. It is a promising measure for further studies and, with some caveats, it can be used in a clinical context.

articles.title: Deep learning of brain-behavior dimensions identifies transdiagnostic biotypes in youth with ADHD and anxiety disorders.
articles.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and anxiety disorders are highly prevalent in youth and frequently co-occur, yet substantial within- and cross-disorder heterogeneity limits neurobiological specificity and complicates treatment selection. Here we conducted an observational cohort analysis and developed a deep learning framework that integrates clinically salient functional connectivity with cognitive and behavioral measures to identify interpretable transdiagnostic dimensions and biologically grounded biotypes. In 3,508 children aged 9-11 years from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study, the model revealed two reproducible brain-behavior dimensions reflecting cognitive control and emotion-attention regulation. These dimensions yielded three biotypes (externalizing-disinhibited, internalizing-distressed and mixed dysregulation) with distinct symptom profiles, network organization and brain development. They generalized to 224 age-matched Healthy Brain Network participants and were detectable before symptom onset, indicating preclinical expression. These findings support brain-behavior dimensions for parsing transdiagnostic heterogeneity and motivating early risk stratification and mechanism-informed intervention in youth mental health.

articles.title: Nutrition assistance program participation, healthcare access, and perinatal health among U.S. Latinos in the context of the "public charge" rule: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The "public charge" rule assesses whether an immigrant to the U.S. is likely to become dependent on government assistance, particularly for potential use of cash-benefit programs or long-term institutionalization at government expense. Being deemed a public charge can make an applicant for legal status inadmissible. Although the rule applies to specific immigration determinations, its effects may impact health outcomes. This systematic review synthesized evidence on public charge policy and health-related outcomes among U.S. Latino populations.
METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines and a PROSPERO-registered protocol (CRD42024507861), we searched PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus for peer-reviewed studies published in English or Spanish from January 1996 through February 20, 2026. Eligible studies included U.S.-based Latino populations, examined the public charge rule as exposure, and reported health-related outcomes, health behaviors, healthcare access, or use of health or social programs. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, with disagreements resolved by consensus and, when needed, a third reviewer. Data were extracted using a standardized PECO-based form and narratively synthesized.
RESULTS: Of 157 citations identified, 19 studies met inclusion criteria. Studies examined program utilization and access (n = 13, 68%), maternal health (n = 4, 21%), or both domains (n = 2, 10%). Nearly all used cross-sectional designs (n = 18, 95%); 9 used qualitative and 10 quantitative data. Across studies, fear, misinformation, and concerns about immigration and legal consequences were the most consistent barriers to nutrition assistance programs, healthcare, Medicaid, and government-funded perinatal services. During the policy changes briefly implemented in 2018, Latino children with medical needs had the highest estimated risk of losing Medicaid, CHIP, or nutrition assistance benefits (79.8%; 95% CI, 74.4%-85.1%). Among likely undocumented Latino patients, self-pay emergency department visits increased after the 2018 proposed rule expansion. Maternal health studies documented delayed perinatal care, reduced Medicaid-funded prenatal care initiation, higher odds of preterm birth, and lower birth weights.
CONCLUSIONS: The public charge policy may function as a structural determinant of health for Latino families by discouraging the use of safety-net programs, including among eligible individuals. Additional research is needed to assess downstream health consequences, reduce misinformation, strengthen trusted communication, and protect access to healthcare and social welfare programs.

articles.title: The DR-DQ HLA haplotypes dominant-recessive interplay leads to the heterogeneity of antibody immune response in T1D.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1D) is an autoimmune disorder defined by the presence of islet-specific autoantibodies (AAb). Growing evidence indicates substantial heterogeneity in T1D pathogenesis, reflected in divergent AAb profiles across patient subgroups. We integrated ELISA-based measurements of four major islet autoantibodies-insulin (IAA), glutamic acid decarboxylase (GADA), IA-2 (IA-2A), and zinc transporter 8 (ZnT8A)-with whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 917 individuals diagnosed with T1D or latent autoimmune diabetes in adults (LADA). Analyses were stratified by class II human leukocyte antigen (HLA) haplotypes, age at disease onset (0-55 years old), sex, and disease duration (0-51 years). To investigate seroconversion dynamics during the preclinical phase, we additionally included 72 preclinical participants. HLA haplotype emerged as the primary determinant of AAb specificity, while dominant-recessive interactions between alleles in the heterozygous state have been revealed. In addition to confirming the previously described associations between IA-2A and ZnT8A with DR4-DQ8 and GADA with DR3-DQ2, an increase in ZnT8A levels was detected for heterozygotes of the DR1-DQ5 haplotype. Moreover, even within identical HLA backgrounds, sex, age at onset, and disease duration significantly modulated the autoantibody repertoire. These findings demonstrate that HLA haplotype is a major driver of T1D heterogeneity, while non-HLA factors may modify its effects. The observed immunological heterogeneity underscores the need for multidimensional stratification in T1D research and highlights opportunities for HLA-informed prediction and monitoring during the preclinical window.

articles.title: Construction and immunogenicity evaluation of recombinant Bacillus subtilis expressing VP8 protein of porcine rotavirus.
articles.abstract: Porcine rotavirus (PoRV), an enteric infectious virus, is a major cause of neonatal diarrhea in piglets, resulting in significant economic losses to the global swine industry. In this study, the cholera toxin B subunit (CTB) was utilized as a molecular adjuvant to construct recombinant Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis) strains expressing VP8 proteins and CTB-VP8 fusion proteins derived from the PoRV genotypes P[7], P[13], and P[23]. The recombinant strains expressing PoRV proteins from different genotypes were combined and orally administered to mice, and their immunogenicity and probiotic functions were evaluated. The results demonstrated that the recombinant B. subtilis significantly increased serum-specific IgG and fecal-specific sIgA antibodies levels (P < 0.001), indicating that the recombinant strains induced both humoral and mucosal antibody responses in mice. Notably, the CTB-fused strains elicited higher titers of IgG and sIgA. Furthermore, the recombinant strains significantly elevated the expression levels of cytokines, including IFN-γ, IL-2, and IL-4, in both serum and intestinal mucosa (P < 0.01), suggesting a Th1/Th2-biased immune response at the cytokine level. In addition, administration of recombinant B. subtilis increased villus height and the villus height-to-crypt depth ratio while reducing crypt depth, showing a tendency to improve intestinal morphology. This study addresses the limitations associated with insufficient mucosal immune activation by conventional injectable approaches and the absence of cross-protection among different genotypes of PoRV, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for the development of an oral trivalent live-vector vaccine.

articles.title: Chromosomal Amplification in Pediatric Tumors: Implications and Therapeutic Strategies.
articles.abstract: Pediatric tumors often exhibit relatively low coding mutation burdens, and recurrent chromosomal amplifications are observed in specific tumor entities. These amplifications may contribute to influence tumor initiation, progression, and treatment response. For instance, amplification of the MYCN oncogene is a well-established marker of high-risk neuroblastoma and is associated with aggressive disease and poor outcomes. Advances in genomics and molecular biology have identified numerous chromosomal amplification events in pediatric tumors and provided insights into their underlying mechanisms. In this review, we first examine the molecular mechanisms driving chromosomal amplification. We then discuss the roles of chromosomal amplifications in pediatric tumorigenesis and summarize therapeutic approaches, including targeted inhibition, combination strategies, and experimental approaches to promote oncoprotein degradation. Throughout, we distinguish promising therapeutic concepts and preclinical findings from strategies with demonstrated clinical benefit. Further Integration of mechanistic studies, functional validation and biomarker-guided clinical trails may help advance precision therapy for pediatric tumors.

articles.title: The Swedish Child Health Service-is it a silver bullet?
articles.abstract: The Swedish universal Child Health Service (CHS) has nearly 90 years of history and > 99% population coverage. It serves children from birth to five years of age and is free of charge for families. This overview addresses whether the service has remained fit for purpose in an increasingly diverse society, identifies its minimal scalable unit, and considers whether the Swedish CHS can serve as a blueprint for other countries. We provide a brief history and describe the regulatory and funding framework, the structure, organization, and content of services, along with European comparison data. Using the CHS Quality Register (BHVQ), we present system performance in terms of process indicators, child outcomes, equity, quality, and economic impact. Despite ongoing challenges in achieving fully equitable service provision, the Swedish CHS delivers a universal service for families. The system achieves high rates of vaccination, breastfeeding, developmental screening, and screening for maternal mental health, while non-birthing parent support rates are lower. The minimal scalable unit of the CHS is a well-trained, independently working specialist nurse with access to a physician and referral resources. With relatively low costs and high geographic accessibility, the CHS may serve as a model for other primary care-based health systems.

articles.title: Screen use, lifestyle habits and mental health in preschool children: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excessive screen exposure is associated with sleep disturbances, unhealthy dietary patterns, reduced physical activity, and poorer socio-emotional wellbeing. This study aimed to: (1) assess the association between screen time and lifestyle habits, and (2) examine the associations of screen time and lifestyle habits with emotional and behavioral difficulties in preschool children.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 931 children (2-6 years) from Portugal. Parents completed questionnaires on children's lifestyle habits and emotional and behavioral difficulties using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). Anthropometric measurements were collected. Screen time was classified as low (≤ 60 min/day), moderate (> 60 to < 120 min/day), or high (≥ 120 min/day). Linear and logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and parental education were performed.
RESULTS: Regarding lifestyle habits, high screen time was associated with shorter weekday sleep duration and higher consumption of ultra-processed foods. No significant associations were observed with active play time or participation in extracurricular sports after adjustment. Regarding mental health, children with high screen time had higher odds of abnormal SDQ scores, indicating greater emotional and behavioral difficulties. Longer weekend sleep duration and lower maternal educational level were independently associated with SDQ categories.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher screen time was associated with shorter weekday sleep duration, higher consumption of ultra-processed foods, and greater emotional and behavioral difficulties in preschool children. These findings support current recommendations promoting balanced screen use and healthy lifestyle habits during early childhood while highlighting the importance of family and sociodemographic factors for children's mental health.

articles.title: A qualitative participatory study on adolescent mental health and well-being in Sierra Leone.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescents in Sierra Leone have endured successive crises including civil conflict, the 2014 to 2016 Ebola virus disease outbreak, and the COVID-19 pandemic, each compounding pre-existing vulnerabilities in mental health, education, and family stability. Despite growing global recognition of adolescent mental health as a public health priority, qualitative evidence documenting how young Sierra Leoneans experience distress, coping, and recovery remains limited. This study examined how adolescents in Sierra Leone experience mental health, well-being, coping, schooling, and post-crisis recovery.
METHODS: A qualitative participatory study was conducted across three districts in Sierra Leone between February and July 2024. Purposive sampling recruited 112 participants, including adolescents aged 13 to 19 years, caregivers, teachers, youth leaders, community health workers, counsellors, and child protection actors. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, emotion mapping, personal timelines, and guided storytelling. Reflexive thematic analysis was applied.
RESULTS: We identified four themes: (1) landscapes of distress, encompassing grief, fear, poverty-related shame, and school disruption; (2) gendered and intersecting vulnerabilities, including early marriage, sexual violence, and differential educational access; (3) coping, resilience, and meaning-making through faith, peer solidarity, creative expression, and aspiration; and (4) navigating support, revealing trust barriers, stigma, and the centrality of informal networks.
CONCLUSIONS: Adolescent mental health in Sierra Leone is shaped by layered, intersecting crises that exceed individual-level coping. School-based psychosocial support, community-level stigma reduction, and gender-responsive services are urgently needed.

articles.title: Cybervictimization and psychological burden among internet users aged 15 years and older: online harassment, fraud, and co-victimization.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital victimization is heterogeneous, yet population studies rarely distinguish interpersonal cybervictimization from fraud or determine whether co-occurrence adds psychological burden.
METHODS: We analyzed public-use data from 17,403 Internet users aged ≥15 years in a Canadian population victimization survey. Five-year indicators defined four groups: neither exposure, fraud only, cyberstalking/cyberbullying only, and both; fraud delivery mode was unavailable. The primary outcome was fair/poor self-rated mental health; secondary outcomes were recent medication use to aid sleep, calmness, or depression and current life satisfaction (0-10). Weighted modified Poisson and linear models used all 500 survey bootstrap replicate weights. Core models adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, religious affiliation, and Internet use; extended models also included conventional victimization, offline stalking, and discrimination.
RESULTS: After extended adjustment, fair/poor mental health was more prevalent in the cyber-only group [prevalence ratio (PR) 1.30, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.05-1.62]. The both-exposure estimate was elevated but imprecise (PR 1.38, 95% CI 0.99-1.94), and the fraud-only CI included the null (PR 1.12, 95% CI 0.93-1.36). All exposed groups had lower life satisfaction; medication associations were weaker. Interaction estimates did not establish synergy.
DISCUSSION: The added adversity variables may have multiple temporal roles, so attenuation between models is not a mediation estimate. The released age variable combines ages 15-34, precluding adolescent-specific estimates. Coordinated assessment is a practice implication that requires evaluation.

articles.title: The effects of physical exercise interventions on executive function in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: a three-level meta-analysis and systematic review.
articles.abstract: Physical exercise has been increasingly recognized as a potential non-pharmacological approach for improving executive function in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This study systematically examined the effects of physical exercise on executive function in this population. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were systematically retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, and other electronic databases. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool. Meta-analyses were conducted using the metafor package in R, with three-level and two-level random-effects models applied to account for dependent effect sizes. A total of 19 studies involving 714 participants were included. The three-level model showed that physical exercise significantly improved inhibitory control (g = 0.70, 95% CI [0.09, 1.31], p < 0.05) and cognitive flexibility (g = 0.59, 95% CI [0.29, 0.90], p < 0.001), with these findings supported by the two-level model. The effect on working memory was not statistically significant in the three-level model (g = 0.31, 95% CI [-0.40, 1.01], p > 0.05), although a significant positive effect was observed in the two-level model (g = 0.41, 95% CI [0.01, 0.85], p < 0.05). Subgroup analyses indicated significant improvements across executive function domains following interventions lasting >8 weeks, although between-subgroup differences were not statistically significant. Meta-regression further showed that total intervention duration significantly predicted improvements in cognitive flexibility. The certainty of evidence was rated as moderate according to the GRADE approach. Overall, physical exercise may be a promising adjunctive strategy for supporting executive function in children and adolescents with ASD, particularly inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously given the substantial heterogeneity, wide prediction intervals, and potential small-study effects. Systematic review registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251165448, identifier (CRD420251165448).

articles.title: 24-h movement behavior composition associated with mental health in preschool children: a cross-sectional compositional data analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health problems in preschool children represent an important public health concern. Understanding the associations between 24-h movement behaviors, including moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), light physical activity (LPA), sedentary behavior (SB), and sleep (SLP), and mental health may help identify activity compositions associated with more favorable psychological outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the associations between reallocations of time among 24-h movement behaviors and mental health in preschool children aged 3-6 years and to identify activity compositions associated with more favorable mental health outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 850 Chinese preschool children aged 3-6 years. MVPA, LPA, and SB were objectively measured using ActiGraph GT3X-BT accelerometers, whereas SLP was assessed using structured parent- and teacher-reported questionnaires. Mental health outcomes, including total difficulties, internalizing and externalizing problems, and prosocial behavior, were assessed using the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). Compositional data analysis (CoDA) was performed using isometric log-ratio (ilr) transformations and multiple linear regression models. A one-to-three proportional time-reallocation approach was used to estimate changes in mental health outcomes associated with reallocating 10% of time in one behavior proportionally across the remaining three behaviors. In addition, optimal time-use analysis was conducted to identify 24-h movement compositions associated with more favorable mental health outcomes. Models were adjusted for age, gender, body mass index, residential district, parental education, and parental attitudes toward physical activity.
RESULTS: An increase in MVPA was significantly associated with a reduction in Total Difficulties (β = -1.658, p < 0.001) and Internalizing Problems (β = -0.636, p = 0.027). An increase in SB was associated with an increase in Total Difficulties (β = 1.615, p = 0.032), while an increase in SLP was significantly associated with a reduction in Total Difficulties (β = -1.134, p = 0.034) and an improvement in Externalizing Problems (β = -1.642, p = 0.009). Increases in MVPA or SLP, when proportionally replacing the other three behaviors, as well as the substitution of SB with other behaviors, were all associated with improvements in mental health (p < 0.05). The model-derived 24-h movement behavior composition associated with more favorable mental health profiles in the study sample comprised 71 min of MVPA (55-85 min), 234 min of LPA (190-265 min), 514 min of SB (450-590 min), and 621 min of sleep (515-690 min).
CONCLUSION: Greater relative time spent in MVPA and SLP was associated with more favorable mental health outcomes among preschool children. The model-derived 24-h movement behavior composition identified in this study reflects associations within the observed sample and should not be interpreted as a causal relationship or a prescriptive intervention target. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Efficacy of animal-assisted therapy for the relief of dental anxiety: quantitative synthesis of clinical randomized controlled trial evidence.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The aim of this systematic review was to comprehensively evaluate the efficacy of animal-assisted therapy (AAT) for alleviating dental anxiety based on clinical randomized controlled trials (RCTs), and to explore its potential implications for dental clinical practice. Following the PRISMA guidelines, inclusion criteria were defined according to the PICO framework. Four databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and The Cochrane Library) were systematically searched. Two reviewers independently completed study screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (ROB 2.0). All statistical analyses were performed in Rstudio software. Subgroup meta-analyses, multiple sensitivity analyses (including alternative pre-post correlation assumptions for change-score calculations and Hartung-Knapp adjustment), and post-hoc exploratory meta-regression (limited by small study count and risk of over-fitting) were performed to investigate potential sources of heterogeneity. One crossover RCT was incorporated using only pre-crossover first-period parallel-group data. A total of 10 RCTs involving 524 patients were included. Meta-analysis showed that dog-mediated AAT was associated with reduced dental anxiety relative to control conditions (SMD = -0.95, 95% CI [-1.65; -0.24], p < 0.01), with high heterogeneity observed (I 2 = 92%). Dog-mediated AAT also exerted beneficial effects on patients' behavior responses, pain perception, and physiological indicators. Subgroup analyses indicated more pronounced anxiety-relieving effects among children, while limited improvement in objective anxiety indices was observed in adults despite higher patient satisfaction. Intervention timing and baseline anxiety severity could modulate treatment magnitude. We emphasize that Cohen's SMD thresholds reflect statistical effect size instead of patient-perceivable clinical benefit. No validated minimal clinically important differences (MCID) exist for mainstream dental-anxiety scales, restricting definitive judgments regarding clinical meaningfulness. GRADE assessment yielded very-low-certainty evidence for the primary outcome. Although dog-mediated AAT appears to be a promising complementary option for dental care, especially for children aged 6-12 years without dog phobia or canine allergy, conclusions should be interpreted prudently, given the substantial clinical heterogeneity observed across intervention and comparator protocols. Future well-designed RCTs with larger sample sizes are required to resolve heterogeneity and identify optimal intervention regimens for different patient subgroups.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/view/CRD420261464388, identifier CRD420261464388.

articles.title: "If they're your friends and they want to force you, they're not really your friends": social influence on substance use in school adolescents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescent substance use is a public health problem due to both its short- and long-term consequences. During adolescence, more intimate and complex relationships with peers are developed, making the spaces of daily interaction more relevant. Social influence processes may occur in these interactions through two processes: selection and socialization. The aim of this study was to provide a detailed account of the mechanisms involved in selecting peers and socialization in relation to substance use from the perspective of school adolescents.
METHODS: We analyzed twenty-five group interviews using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants comprised 197 adolescents from 8th grade elementary to 2nd year secondary (55.3% female) from schools in Temuco, Chile.
RESULTS: The following themes were reported: (1) The opportunities my school provides to form friendships; (2) "Ripple effect": Friendships that are a bridge to making new friends; (3) What makes us alike brings us together: homophily in the selection of friends; (4) From offer to disparagement: Continuum of social pressure to use substances; (5) 'To be part of': Conformity with friends' substance use; (6) The social status that substance use confers upon my peers and friends; and (7) "True" friends look out for me and respect my decision to use substances.
CONCLUSION: Adolescents' accounts highlight the critical role of social influences in substance use, which seems to be linked to their need for belonging and validation within peer groups. According to their perspectives, friends often encourage substance use, sometimes through overt peer pressure. Schools may offer a pivotal opportunity to foster positive social networks.

articles.title: Screening-positive subclinical eating disorder symptoms and associated factors among high school students: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclinical eating disorder (SCED) symptoms are common among adolescents and may be associated with adverse psychological and behavioral outcomes. However, evidence on screening-positive SCED symptoms and associated factors among high school students remains limited. Identifying these factors may support early screening and prevention.
METHODS: In December 2023, a stratified random cluster sampling method was used to recruit students from 12 high schools in Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province, China. Data were collected using a self-developed general information questionnaire, the Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire 6.0 (EDE-Q 6.0), the Ma Body Figure Scale, the Children's Depression Inventory-Short Form (CDI-S), the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale-Short Version (SCAS-S), the National Mental Health Literacy Questionnaire, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. BMI was classified using the WHO 2007 age- and sex-specific BMI-for-age reference for participants younger than 19 years, with adult WHO BMI cut-offs used for participants aged 19 years or older. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) with school as the clustering variable were used to examine factors associated with screening-positive SCED symptoms.
RESULTS: A total of 2,681 high school students were included in the analysis, of whom 645 (24.1%) screened positive for SCED symptoms. In the school-clustered GEE model, female sex (OR = 1.351, 95% CI: 1.109-1.645), overweight (OR = 3.418, 95% CI: 2.632-4.439), obesity (OR = 7.740, 95% CI: 5.939-10.089), positive body image misperception (OR = 4.280, 95% CI: 3.533-5.184), higher depressive symptom scores (OR per 1-SD increase = 1.454, 95% CI: 1.297-1.630), higher anxiety symptom scores (OR per 1-SD increase = 1.387, 95% CI: 1.269-1.516), and poor sleep quality (OR = 1.393, 95% CI: 1.121-1.733) were associated with higher odds of screening-positive SCED symptoms. Adequate mental health literacy was associated with lower odds (OR = 0.609, 95% CI: 0.506-0.734).
CONCLUSION: Approximately one-quarter of the participating high school students screened positive for SCED symptoms. Screening-positive SCED symptoms were associated with weight status, body image misperception, depressive and anxiety symptom severity, sleep quality, and mental health literacy. These findings support multidimensional school-based screening and health education while recognizing that the EDE-Q threshold identifies a screening-defined condition rather than a clinical diagnosis.

articles.title: Mediators of the association between physical activity and depressive symptoms in youth: a systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modelling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical activity is consistently associated with fewer depressive symptoms in young people, yet the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. This systematic review and meta-analytic structural equation modelling (MASEM) study aimed to identify potential mediators linking physical activity with depressive symptoms in youth and quantitatively synthesise repeatedly examined mediation pathways.
METHODS: Six electronic databases were searched for observational quantitative studies examining physical activity, potential mediators, and depressive symptoms in children, adolescents, and young adults within a prespecified eligibility range of 6-27 years. Potential mediators were synthesised narratively and categorised into conceptually related domains. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted within the mediation-focused quantitative subset, followed by two-stage random-effects MASEM for mediator constructs with sufficient independent studies and complete correlation data.
RESULTS: Eighty-seven studies were included in the broader systematic review, of which 80 formally examined at least one mediator and 39 contributed to the quantitative evidence base. Within this mediation-focused quantitative subset, physical activity was, on average, inversely associated with depressive symptoms (r = -0.234, 95% CI -0.281 to -0.187), although heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 98.29%) and the 95% prediction interval included zero (-0.499 to 0.070). Narrative synthesis identified potential pathways involving psychological resources and self-related perceptions, social factors, behavioural and lifestyle factors, cognitive-emotional processes, maladaptive behavioural factors, and physical or neurobiological factors. Construct-specific MASEM supported statistical indirect associations through psychological resilience (ab = -0.108, 95% CI -0.172 to -0.061), self-esteem (ab = -0.134, 95% CI -0.239 to -0.062), and social support (ab = -0.127, 95% CI -0.220 to -0.059). Sleep quality showed a significant indirect association in an exploratory model based on three studies.
CONCLUSION: Psychological resilience, self-esteem, and social support emerged as repeatedly examined candidate pathways linking physical activity with depressive symptoms. However, the predominantly cross-sectional and just-identified MASEM models cannot establish temporal ordering, and alternative-direction analyses indicated that at least the resilience correlation structure was also compatible with a reverse indirect pathway. The findings should therefore be interpreted as statistical indirect associations rather than established causal mechanisms.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/recorddashboard, identifier (CRD420261355504).

articles.title: Advancements in Composite Drug Delivery Systems for Osteosarcoma Treatment: Targeting ROS, Cuproptosis, and Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents and remains difficult to treat when metastatic, recurrent, or chemotherapy-resistant. Rather than viewing reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial dysfunction, and cuproptosis as independent therapeutic topics, this review integrates them into a single mechanism-to-material framework for osteosarcoma treatment. Mitochondria are a major source and target of ROS and also determine susceptibility to cuproptosis through mitochondrial respiration and protein lipoylation. Mechanistically, excess intracellular copper can directly bind lipoylated tricarboxylic-acid-cycle proteins, particularly dihydrolipoamide S-acetyltransferase, promoting protein aggregation, loss of iron-sulfur-cluster proteins, proteotoxic stress, and cell death. Composite drug delivery systems may exploit this vulnerability by increasing tumor-selective ROS, depleting antioxidant defenses, delivering copper or copper ionophores, targeting mitochondria, and responding to the osteosarcoma microenvironment. Importantly, copper-containing nanoplatforms should not automatically be classified as cuproptosis-inducing systems, because copper may also trigger chemodynamic oxidative injury through mechanisms that do not satisfy current molecular criteria for cuproptosis. We therefore distinguish osteosarcoma-specific evidence from findings extrapolated from other cancers, critically compare major delivery platforms and experimental models, and discuss immunological effects, toxicity, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, manufacturing, and regulatory barriers. This integrated perspective suggests that the most promising future systems will be those that verify mechanism-specific biomarkers, achieve spatially controlled mitochondrial/copper exposure, and demonstrate efficacy and safety in clinically relevant orthotopic and immunocompetent osteosarcoma models.

articles.title: Effect of critical illness and mechanical ventilation on energy and substrate metabolism in patients with liver cirrhosis: an indirect calorimeter-based cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Energy and substrate metabolism are altered in liver cirrhosis and may worsen with critical illness. Indirect calorimetry provides accurate metabolic assessment. This study compared resting energy expenditure (REE), respiratory quotient (RQ), and substrate oxidation among healthy controls, non-critically ill, and critically ill cirrhosis patients.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This prospective observational study included 63 healthy controls (Group I; age 32.5 years; 46% male), 68 non-critically ill cirrhosis patients (Group II; age 47.5 years; 85.3% male; MELD 15), and 70 critically ill ventilated cirrhosis patients (Group III; age 49.7 years; 75.7% male; MELD 29). Valid indirect calorimetry (Quark RMR) measurements were available for all 63 controls and for 66 and 68 patients in Groups II and III, respectively. Metabolic state was classified using the measured-to-predicted REE ratio (Harris-Benedict): hypometabolic (< 0.9), normometabolic (0.9-1.1), and hypermetabolic (> 1.1). Compared with Group I, RQ declined across Groups II and III (0.86, 0.80, 0.74; p=0.003), carbohydrate oxidation decreased (60.3%, 30.3%, 13.3%; p<0.001), and fat oxidation increased (27%, 59.8%, 72.7%; p<0.001), indicating progressive starvation, while REE remained comparable (1446, 1485, 1415 kcal/day; p=0.32). Hypometabolism was more prevalent in Group III than Groups I and II (45.6% vs. 22.2% and 30.3%; p=0.015). Group III had higher pro-inflammatory markers (IL-6, CRP) and non-esterified fatty acid levels. Across Child-Pugh classes A, B, and C, RQ decreased (0.86, 0.79, 0.75) and fat oxidation increased (36.3%, 69%, 73%), with minimal changes in REE.
CONCLUSION: Liver cirrhosis is characterized by a progressive starvation phenotype without a significant increase in absolute energy expenditure. Critically ill patients with cirrhosis showed further reduction in carbohydrate utilization, without a significant increase in energy expenditure. These findings suggest that altered substrate utilization may be the predominant metabolic abnormality in cirrhosis, particularly during critical illness.

articles.title: Maternal prenatal gut microbiome and domain-specific neurodevelopment in early childhood: associations and exploratory prediction.
articles.abstract: The potential of the maternal prenatal gut microbiome for prediction of domain-specific neurodevelopment in children has not been fully appreciated. We sought to explore the associations and predictive capacity of the maternal prenatal gut microbiome in relation to children's domain-specific neurodevelopment. Leveraging a prospective birth cohort, we performed both 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and shotgun metagenomic sequencing for pregnant women's fecal samples. The domain-specific neurodevelopment in children was evaluated utilizing the Ages and Stages Questionnaire (ASQ). We used the prenatal gut microbiome at the phylum, genus, species, and pathway levels in combination with multiple machine learning models, including random forest, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient-boosting machine (LightGBM), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, and ridge logistic regression, individually and in conjunction with conventional risk factors to predict children's neurodevelopment. We found that the gut microbiome features, individually or integrated with conventional risk factors, improved the predictive performance of machine learning models for children's neurodevelopment across five subdomains, achieving area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROCs) up to 0.88. Compared with AUROCs of 0.70-0.76 for communication, 0.70-0.72 for gross motor, 0.71-0.77 for fine motor, 0.68-0.77 for problem solving, and 0.57-0.62 for personal-social development using conventional risk factors alone, the combined models achieved AUROCs of 0.79-0.83, 0.71-0.80, 0.82-0.84, 0.79-0.88, and 0.59-0.64, respectively. The highest area under the precision-recall curves (AUPRCs) were 0.63, 0.50, 0.63, 0.60, and 0.39 for communication, gross motor, fine motor, problem solving, and personal-social development, respectively, compared with prevalence-matched AUPRC baselines of 0.12, 0.14, 0.12, 0.12, and 0.17. However, performance gains varied across algorithms and feature configurations. Maternal prenatal gut microbial features were associated with domain-specific neurodevelopment and showed exploratory predictive signals in selected internally validated models. Independent external cohorts and age-specific longitudinal validation are required before these features can be considered clinically useful biomarkers or used to inform early-identification or intervention strategies.

articles.title: Validation of the Universal Dietetic Patient Complexity Tool (UDPCT): a multi-centre study of content validity, face validity and inter-rater reliability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Observed changes in patient acuity over the past century and in more recent years due to the COVID-19 pandemic, plus financial constraints, are putting pressure on the healthcare system and those who work in it to become more efficient. This has highlighted the importance of job plans and skill mixing for caseload and staffing management. The Universal Dietetic Patient Complexity Tool (UDPCT) was developed taking into account all aspects of dietetic care, to provide a standardised assessment of caseload acuity and to facilitate timely and cost-effective screening of dietetic patients. This study aimed to evaluate the content validity, face validity and inter-rater reliability of the UDPCT.
METHODS: A multicentre validation study was conducted across National Health Service (NHS) dietetic departments throughout the United Kingdom. Content validity was assessed using structured questionnaires completed by senior dietitians from participating sites. Item-level Content Validity Index (I-CVI) was calculated for each UDPCT domain. Inter-rater reliability was evaluated through independent paired assessments of the same patients using the UDPCT. Agreement between assessors was analysed using Spearman's rank-order correlation coefficient. Face validity was assessed using a five-point Likert questionnaire and qualitative feedback.
RESULTS: Twelve NHS dietetic departments representing all four UK nations participated. Twelve senior dietitians completed content validity assessments and 204 dietitians and dietetic assistants (104 assessor pairs) assessed 417 patients across acute, community, adult, paediatric and mental health services. All 10 UDPCT domains exceeded the predefined threshold for content validity (I-CVI range 0.92-1.00). Consensus regarding complexity categories and associated cut-off scores was achieved by 91.7% of expert respondents. Inter-rater reliability demonstrated a high positive correlation between paired assessors (Spearman's rho = 0.70, p < 0.001). Face validity demonstrated strong acceptability, with median and modal scores of 4/5 across all questionnaire domains.
CONCLUSIONS: The UDPCT demonstrated strong content validity, face validity and inter-rater reliability across diverse dietetic settings. The tool provides a validated approach to assessing dietetic patient complexity and has potential applications in assessing capacity and demand, safe staffing/workforce planning, service development and business case planning.

articles.title: Probiotic supplementation is associated with distinct gut microbiota development in extremely preterm infants: A pre- and post-implementation cohort study.
articles.abstract: Probiotics are used in preterm infants to reduce necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), potentially through modulation of the gut microbiota. We investigated the effects of multi-strain probiotic supplementation (ProPrems®) on microbiota development in extremely preterm infants (<28 weeks). Pre- and post-implementation cohorts from four neonatal intensive care units were included. Fecal samples collected during the first 4 weeks of life were analyzed using IS-pro microbiota profiling and targeted quantitative PCR. 243 infants and 777 fecal samples were studied. NEC incidence was significantly lower in probiotic-exposed infants (2% vs 11%, p = 0.007). Probiotic exposure was the strongest of the tested influencing factors of microbial beta-diversity (adj.R2 4.1%, p = 0.001) and was associated with increased probiotic-associated taxa, reduced potentially pathogenic taxa, and a more connected microbial network. Antibiotic exposure and invasive ventilation reduced quantities of B. longum subsp. infantis. These findings show probiotics alter early gut microbiota development, which provides plausible mechanistic insights into how they may protect against NEC.

articles.title: Risk factors and clinical phenotype stratification of secondary and drug-resistant epilepsy in children with gray matter heterotopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gray matter heterotopia (GMH) is a congenital brain malformation caused by abnormal neuronal migration, and children with GMH are at risk of secondary epilepsy and drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). We aim to investigate risk factors for secondary and DRE in children with GMH for early risk identification and management.
METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled children with GMH diagnosed using magnetic resonance imaging at Chongqing Medical University Children's Hospital (from Sept 2012 to Sept 2025). Kaplan-Meier analysis, Firth-corrected Cox regression, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-Cox (LASSO-Cox) analysis  were used to identify risk factors for secondary epilepsy. Firth-LASSO logistic regression was used to assess risk factors of DRE. K-mode clustering was used to define phenotypic subgroups based on pre-epilepsy baseline variables.
RESULTS: A total of 219 children with GMH were enrolled in this study. Periventricular nodular heterotopia was the most common type of GMH (82.19%). The main clinical manifestations included epileptic seizures (43.38%), intellectual disability (ID) (38.81%), and global developmental delay (GDD) (33.33%). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that ID (P < 0.001), GDD (P < 0.001), multiple brain abnormalities, and patent foramen ovale (PFO) (P = 0.006) were linked to shorter seizure-free survival. Multivariate Firth-corrected Cox regression identified ID [hazard ratio (HR) = 2.606, 95% confidence interval (95% CI) = 1.375-4.864, P = 0.003], GDD (HR = 3.068, 95% CI 1.625-5.912, P < 0.001), lissencephaly-pachygyria spectrum (HR = 1.835, 95% CI 1.046-3.139, P = 0.035), and PFO (HR = 4.002, 95% CI 1.659-8.433, P = 0.003) as being statistically associated with secondary epilepsy. Exploratory mediation analysis demonstrated that multiple structural abnormalities were significantly associated with both ID and epilepsy. Furthermore, subcortical band heterotopia [odds ratio (OR) = 6.229, 95% CI 1.596-25.797, P = 0.008] and moderate-to-severe ID (OR = 6.114, 95% CI 2.136-20.855, P < 0.001) were statistically associated with secondary DRE. Cluster analysis stratified patients into high-risk (n = 78) and low-risk (n = 141) subgroups. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance revealed significant differences in characteristics between the two groups (F = 40.494, R2 = 0.157, P = 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Developmental impairment, lissencephaly-pachygyria spectrum, and SBH were associated with higher risks of epilepsy and DRE. In addition, an exploratory phenotype stratification into high and low risk of secondary epilepsy based on clinical and imaging features is proposed. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings and advance precision care for children with GMH.

articles.title: Data quality assessment of maternal and newborn indicators from District Health Information Software 2 in five African countries for the period 2014-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tracking progress of sustainable development goal (SDG) targets requires robust monitoring systems, yet data quality remains challenging across sub-Saharan Africa. Most countries rely on aggregated data from District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) or surveys to track maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH) indicators. We evaluated MNCH data quality in DHIS2 across Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zimbabwe (2014-2023).
METHODS: We analysed 16 ENAP-aligned indicators and their 29 corresponding data elements captured in DHIS2 across health facility levels. We applied the WHO Data Quality Review framework to assess availability, reporting completeness, internal consistency (ratio-based validation metrics and temporal trends), and external consistency (comparison with UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (UN IGME), Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (MMEIG), and World Health Organization Global Health Observatory data).
RESULTS: Of 29 data elements, Uganda had highest availability (72-76% during 2020-2023), followed by Kenya (62-66%), Tanzania (52%), and Ghana and Zimbabwe (41% each). Reporting completeness varied substantially: Tanzania achieved >95% facility reporting across all levels, while other countries showed disparities between hospitals and lower-level facilities. Internal consistency revealed problematic patterns for mortality-related ratios in Ghana (stillbirth-to-neonatal mortality ratios reaching 5.0-12.5) and Kenya (KMC-to-low birthweight ratios >2.0). After adjusting DHIS2 estimates for facility birth coverage, stillbirth rates generally exceeded or matched UN IGME estimates, whereas maternal mortality ratios showed substantial underreporting relative to MMEIG estimates. Ghana showed the closest MMR alignment and Kenya the largest discrepancy. Neonatal mortality was underreported in Ghana and Uganda but appeared higher than UN IGME estimates in Tanzania, a finding sensitive to aggregation method.
