Despite the launch of the global call to elimination of CC in 2020, only 10% of women in Uganda are screened and studies in Uganda among women of reproductive age group(WRAG) living with Human Immune virus (HIV) [(WRAG-LHIV)] have reported rates of 30.3% to 39.4%. Subsequently 85% patients with CC present with advanced disease leading to poor outcomes. Furthermore, women living with (HIV) have a six-fold higher risk of developing CC compared to their HIV negative counterparts. Alebtong district in Northern Uganda is reported to have a higher HIV prevalence than the national average and CCS uptake among women of reproductive age group living with HIV (WRAG-LHIV) is unknown. Therefore this study aimed to determine the prevalence of CCS uptake and its determinants among WRAG-LHIV in Alebtong district.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted at 7 purposively selected high volume antiretroviral therapy (ART) offering health facilities and their attached 34 community drug distribution points (CDDPs). 381 WRAG-LHIV were recruited by systematic sampling. Researcher administered pretested closed-ended questionnaires were used to collect quantitative data. The data was entered into Microsoft Excel and subsequently imported into Stata version 14 for statistical analysis. Statistical significance was set at a p-value < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 381 women with a mean age of 32.9 years (SD ± 7) participated in the study. The majority, 80.8% (308/381) had had at most primary education, 81.4% were either married/cohabiting and 53.3% (203/381) resided within 5 km of a health facility. Importantly, 53.5%( 204/381) had had early sexual debut and 81.6%( 311/381) were multiparous. The prevalence of cervical cancer screening (CCS) uptake was 49.6% (189/381). The statistically significant factors associated with CCS uptake were encouragement by friends and family members, spouse support, good knowledge about cervical cancer screening, and preference of male healthcare providers, literacy and distance of ≤ 5km.
CONCLUSION: CCS uptake among WRAG-LHIV was suboptimal and below the 70% target set for CC elimination. There is need for more emphasis on male involvement in terms of spouses and clinical team, peer advocacy integration of CCS into chronic care clinics and adopting modalities that would encourage community participation and males in CCS activities.

articles.title: Men's health awareness in focus: knowledge of testicular cancer and awareness of testicular self-examination practices among men in Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Testicular cancer (TC) is the most common malignancy among young men aged 15 to 39 years, with a rising global incidence. Despite its highly treatable nature, early detection remains critical for improving survival and minimizing long-term complications. However, awareness of TC and testicular self-examination (TSE) remains limited, particularly in regions where male-specific cancer education is lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the level of knowledge and awareness of TC among men in Saudi Arabia, identify demographic factors associated with awareness, and evaluate attitudes toward TSE.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study was conducted between October and November 2024 using an online survey disseminated through social media, university platforms, and community networks. The study included Saudi males aged 18 years and older. Individuals with a prior diagnosis of TC and oncology healthcare professionals were excluded.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were TC knowledge and TSE engagement, assessed through a structured questionnaire. Data analyzed using Kruskal-Wallis tests, multiple linear regression for the log-transformed Knowledge Score, and Firth logistic regression for the binary TSE category.
RESULTS: A total of 386 participants were included. The mean TC knowledge score was 9.2/20, and the mean TSE score was 0.32/6. Most participants were aged 18-30 years (76.19%) and college graduates (70.37%). Knowledge scores were significantly higher among individuals with higher education, but no other demographic factors were strongly associated with TC awareness. TSE engagement was low across all groups, with higher education being the strongest predictor. Regression analyses showed no significant predictors of TC knowledge, suggesting a widespread lack of awareness regardless of demographic factors.
CONCLUSIONS: TC awareness remains low among a sample of Saudi men, with minimal engagement in TSE. Higher education attainment was the demographic factor most consistently associated with awareness and self-examination practices. Public health interventions, including structured TC education, digital health campaigns, and healthcare provider engagement, are needed to improve early detection and reduce the burden of TC in Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Post-pandemic SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence and population immunity in Conakry, Guinea, 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Since May 2023, COVID-19 is no longer a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. However, it remains an infection that requires monitoring, especially in the post-emergency context where testing and preventative measures have been abandoned by the population. The objective of this study was therefore to measure the seroprevalence of antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 in Conakry in the post-health emergency period and to identify the associated factors.
METHODS: In January 2024, we conducted a population-based, age-stratified seroprevalence survey in Conakry. We collected demographic and epidemiological information, as well as dried blood spot samples, and tested them for immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 recombinant nucleocapsid and spike proteins using Luminex technology.
RESULTS: Overall, 1018 individuals with a median age of 18 years (IQR: 10-37 years) from 180 households participated in the survey. The overall weighted and age-standardized SARS-CoV-2 IgG seroprevalence against spike and nucleocapsid proteins was 88.9% (95% CI: 80.8-93.9). People with secondary education (AOR = 4.10, 95% CI: 1.46-11.51) and those who had been vaccinated (AOR = 2.53, 95% CI: 1.26-5.10) were significantly more likely to have SARS-CoV-2 antibodies.
CONCLUSIONS: High SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence in Conakry indicates widespread community exposure through infection and/or vaccination. Secondary education and vaccination were associated with antibody positivity. Despite strong population immunity, continued surveillance, improved vaccine access, and strengthened public health communication remain essential to address ongoing viral circulation and potential waning immunity in Guinea.

articles.title: Age-stratified probabilistic cancer and noncancer inhalation risks from volatile organic compounds near a major petrochemical complex in Rayong, Thailand.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Communities residing near petrochemical complexes are chronically exposed to complex volatile organic compound (VOC) mixtures, but routine surveillance is often restricted to limited sentinel panels, which may lead to the underestimation of true health risks. This study assessed age-stratified probabilistic carcinogenic and noncarcinogenic inhalation risks near the Map Ta Phut Industrial Estate, Thailand, the world's eighth-largest petrochemical hub.
METHODS: During 2021-2023, six routinely monitored VOCs, namely, benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, xylene, 1,3-butadiene, and vinyl chloride, were measured at two residential stations and one industrial fence-line station. An expanded 20-VOC panel was additionally analyzed at the fence-line station to capture broader industrial emissions. In this study, Thai-specific anthropometric data and the carcinogenic equivalence quotient framework were integrated into 10,000-iteration Monte Carlo simulations to estimate the excess lifetime cancer risk (ELCR) and hazard index (HI) for preschool children, school-aged children, adolescents, and adults. In addition, the annual number of VOC-attributable excess cancer cases in Rayong Province was also estimated.
RESULTS: The mean ELCRs were low at the community stations (4.10 × 10- 7 to 3.08 × 10- 6) but increased markedly at the fence-line station (3.18 × 10- 5 to 2.32 × 10- 4) and increased further under the expanded 20-VOC panel (5.00 × 10- 5 to 3.61 × 10- 4). While the mean HI remained below 1.0 for the routine panel at all the stations, it exceeded 1.0 for all the age groups under the expanded 20-VOC panel (ranging from 2.04 to 4.83). Preschool children had the greatest noncarcinogenic burden, with a 95th -percentile HI of 10.8. Benzene and ethylbenzene were the main carcinogenic contributors at the two community stations, whereas vinyl chloride dominated both the carcinogenic and noncarcinogenic risks at the industrial fence line. The estimated number of adult VOC-attributable excess cancer cases increased from 2.79 in 2015 to 3.15 in 2023, accounting for 0.36% of the regional cancer burden.
CONCLUSIONS: Limited routine VOC monitoring may substantially underestimate petrochemical-related carcinogenic and noncarcinogenic risks. Age-stratified probabilistic assessment using an expanded VOC panel revealed substantial fence-line risks driven by specialty monomers, highlighting preschool children as a priority population for strengthened surveillance and site-specific risk management.

articles.title: Latent class analysis of sexual behavior and HIV testing profiles among sexually experienced college students in China: a cross-sectional online survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rising human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infections among young people underscore the need to strengthen campus-based prevention. We used latent class analysis (LCA) to summarize sexual behavior and HIV-testing profiles among sexually experienced college students, examine associated factors, and assess whether the selected solution added information beyond an observed-response typology.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed 5,218 students reporting lifetime sexual intercourse in an anonymous online survey in Nanning, China. LCA included sexual exposure/protection status, multiple sexual partnerships and same-sex sexual behavior in the past six months, and HIV testing in the past year. Modal LCA membership was compared with a post hoc rule-based typology using agreement measures. Multinomial logistic regression examined associated factors.
RESULTS: Among 108,552 valid respondents, 5,218 were analyzed. The three-class model balanced fit, class size, parsimony, and interpretability. Class 1 (n = 509, 9.76%) combined multiple partnerships and/or recent same-sex sexual behavior with past-year HIV testing; Class 2 (n = 2,535, 48.58%) comprised participants with 0-1 recent partners, no recent same-sex sexual behavior, and low testing uptake; and Class 3 (n = 2,174, 41.66%) resembled Class 1 in partner patterns but lacked past-year testing. The rule-based typology exactly reproduced modal LCA membership (agreement = 100%; κ = 1.000; adjusted Rand index = 1.000), indicating limited additional person-level classification. Compared with Class 2, Class 1 membership was positively associated with junior college status, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) awareness, and ever PrEP use, and inversely associated with town household registration, heterosexual orientation, and an opposite-sex first sexual partner. Class 3 membership was positively associated with ever PrEP use and inversely associated with male sex, town household registration, comprehensive university attendance, an opposite-sex first sexual partner, and adequate HIV-related knowledge.
CONCLUSIONS: Many participants reporting multiple partnerships and/or recent same-sex sexual behavior had not undergone HIV testing in the past year, indicating a need for confidential and accessible testing. Because LCA mainly summarized strongly separated observed patterns, brief, non-stigmatizing assessment of partner patterns, condom-use consistency, and testing history may support behavior-informed campus prevention and linkage to PrEP/PEP services.

articles.title: Cannabidiol for Severe Behavioral Problems in Youths With Intellectual Disability: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: There is a high level of interest in cannabidiol (CBD) as treatment for severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disabilities. Given the lack of evidence, clinical trials are needed to inform practice.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy of CBD to reduce severe behavioral problems in children and adolescents with intellectual disability.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This parallel design, double-blind placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted between May 11, 2021, and May 8, 2025. Participants were children and adolescents aged 6 to 18 years with an intellectual disability and severe behavioral problems from 3 children's hospitals in Australia: The Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, Monash Children's Hospital in Melbourne, and The Children's Hospital Westmead in Sydney.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive CBD isolate in oil (10 mg/kg/d) or placebo orally for 8 weeks, with a 4-week follow-up period.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURE: The primary outcome was parent-reported score on the Aberrant Behavior Checklist, Irritability (ABC-I) subscale assessed at the end of the 8-week maintenance phase.
RESULTS: Of 131 participants randomized after exclusion of 1 participant randomized in error, 65 were in the CBD group and 66 were in the placebo group. Overall, mean (SD) age was 11.2 (3.1) years, and 98 participants (74.8%) were male. A total of 110 participants (84.0%) had comorbid autism. Primary outcome data were available for 61 participants in the CBD group and 63 in the placebo group. Mean (SD) ABC-I subscale scores at baseline were 32.2 (7.3) and 30.0 (6.3) in the CBD and placebo groups, respectively. Intention-to-treat analysis showed similar mean (SD) ABC-I subscale scores at the end of treatment: 21.7 (11.0) in the CBD group and 19.2 (10.7) in the placebo group (mean difference, 2.4; 95% CI, -1.5 to 6.3). A similar proportion of participants experienced at least 1 adverse event in the CBD group (41 [63.1%]) and the placebo group (40 [60.6%]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, CBD was not effective in treating severe behavioral problems in youths with intellectual disability. The results suggest that CBD should not be used to treat severe behavioral problems in this population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04821856.

articles.title: Genome sequencing based sequential diagnostic strategy improve diagnosed yield of pediatric genetic kidney disease: a national multicenter study.
articles.abstract: Genetic kidney disease (GKD) is a major cause of pediatric chronic kidney disease. Many patients remain genetically unresolved by exome sequencing (ES) and copy number variation (CNV) analysis. Genome sequencing (GS) enables a comprehensive detection of genetic variations. This study evaluates a GS-based sequential strategy to determine the diagnostic yield in pediatric GKD. We recruited families with GKD from a national cohort of 23 centers from 2020 to 2024 through Chinese Children Genetic Kidney Disease Database. This sequential sequencing strategy involved initial trio-ES and Trio-CNV-seq, followed by GS in undiagnosed cases, splicing essays analysis was performed for intronic variants. A total of 735 families were enrolled. Trio-ES and Trio-CNV-seq achieved a diagnostic yield of 39.4% (35.5% from ES and 4.0% from CNV-seq). Subsequent GS identified pathogenic variants in 23 of 445 previously undiagnosed cases (5.2%), including small structural variants (5 cases), intronic variants affecting splicing function (9 cases), and variants in mitochondrion DNA (9 cases). GS showed 14% and 8.8% increase in diagnostic yield in renal tubular disease and CKD of unexplained cause. Syndromic cases exhibited a higher diagnostic yield (10.9%) than isolated cases (4.6%). These findings indicate GS-based sequential strategy improves the diagnostic yield of GKD.

articles.title: Rare variant enrichment analysis in pediatric European Moyamoya Angiopathy patients unveils novel candidate susceptibility genes.
articles.abstract: Moyamoya angiopathy (MMA) is a rare steno-occlusive condition resulting in transient ischemic attacks and strokes in children and adults. Previous studies, mainly in adult patients, suggested RNF213 as the most prevalent susceptibility gene due to an Asian founder variant. Nevertheless, the genetic landscape in early-onset European MMA patients requires further elucidation. Exome-sequencing was performed in 104 pediatric MMA patients, including three with Down syndrome, and 520 healthy controls. Rare-variant enrichment testing was performed using the R-package SKAT on the whole cohort as well as in a 100% European subset, revealing a total of 28 enriched genes. Both tests showed the most common known MMA genes (RNF213 and NF1) among the top three enriched genes, underlining the validity of our approach. Seven of the concordantly enriched genes are novel MMA candidates (ATAD2, COL18A1, NAV1, ALOX12B, KRTAP4-7, KCNJ12, and KBTBD13). De novo variants were found in NF1, RNF213, COL18A1, ECI1, and YIPF1. In summary, our study confirms RNF213 and NF1 as major susceptibility genes and suggests seven novel early-onset MMA susceptibility genes. Of special interest is the novel candidate gene COL18A1, which is involved in angiogenesis and endothelial cell proliferation, due to its potential additional role as a modifier of MMA in trisomy 21.

articles.title: Nutrition-transition and intervention themes in publications explicitly focused on childhood obesity: a systematic computational mapping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutrition transition connects childhood obesity to changing diets, food environments, intervention institutions, and unequal research capacity. We systematically mapped how these issues were represented in indexed publication records.
METHODS: Title-restricted childhood/adolescent obesity searches in the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus supplied 19,858 comparable filtered exports; 6,909 nutrition-explicit original-study records formed the primary corpus. Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) and SPECTER2-based BERTopic were aligned and used to compare 2016-2020 with 2021-2025. Sensitivities varied model, corpus, temporal unit, random seed, BERTopic parameters, and denominator. Author-affiliation countries were fractionally counted. Estimands captured record-level research attention and institutional participation.
RESULTS: Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) yielded 35 topics, and BERTopic yielded 23 topics, with 27.34% of documents assigned to the HDBSCAN noise cluster before reassignment. In the retrieved corpus, diet quality, meal patterns, and food processing had a +0.97-percentage-point LDA contrast (q < 0.001) and a +1.66-point raw-BERTopic contrast (q = 0.077). Double burden, food insecurity, and structural determinants of nutrition had corresponding contrasts of +0.87 (q < 0.001) and +1.13 points (q = 0.061). Adjusted support remained model-specific, with no focal pair supported in both models; year-level tests also fell below adjusted thresholds. The family/community BERTopic estimate was corpus-specification dependent and inconclusive. Of 6,909 records, 6,877 had parsed affiliation countries; high-income fractional affiliation share was 59.27% in 2021-2025 and low-income share was 1.06%.
CONCLUSION: Descriptive findings consistently observed within this title-explicit English-language indexed corpus concerned its thematic structure and institutional geography. Temporal contrasts were corpus-conditional observational patterns whose support depended on model and temporal unit. They motivate a prospective study of how food-system pressures, implementation institutions, and regional institutional participation shape childhood-obesity dietary strategies.

articles.title: Isocaloric substitution of plant-based for animal-based protein and physical fitness in adolescents: a cross-sectional study from the EHDLA study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Plant and animal protein sources have been associated with health outcomes, but evidence on physical fitness within isocaloric substitution frameworks remains limited. This study examined whether modeled isocaloric substitutions between plant- and animal-derived protein sources were associated with physical fitness in adolescents.
METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis included adolescents aged 12-17 years from Spain. Source-specific protein variables were estimated from a 45-item food frequency questionnaire using reported consumption frequencies, standard portion sizes, and food-composition values. Physical fitness was evaluated using the Assessing the Levels of Physical Activity and Fitness (ALPHA-Fit). Using robust linear regression models, the association between a theoretical 5%-energy plant-for-animal protein contrast and physical fitness was estimated, while adjusting for age, sex, socioeconomic status, sleep duration, physical activity, sedentary behavior, body mass index, total energy intake, and energy from other macronutrients.
RESULTS: The analytical sample comprised 790 adolescents (55.1% girls; median age: 14.0 years). Median energy intake was 2,585.9 kcal⋅day-1. No associations were observed between the modeled 5% of total-energy substitution of animal protein by plant protein and physical fitness outcomes (all p > 0.05). In food-level models, the theoretical substitution of egg-derived protein by plant protein was associated with lower standing long jump performance (standardized beta coefficient [β] = -0.55, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -1.06 to -0.06) and slower 4 × 10 m performance (β = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.12 to 1.04). A similar association with slower 4 × 10 m performance was observed for the modeled substitution of oily-fish-derived protein by plant protein (β = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.65). The theoretical substitution of root-vegetable-derived protein by animal protein was inversely associated with overall physical fitness (β = -1.23, 95% CI: -2.17 to -0.29), whereas the modeled substitution of cereal-derived protein by animal protein was associated with faster 4 × 10 m performance (β = -0.53, 95% CI: -0.89 to -0.17).
CONCLUSION: In adolescents, modeled isocaloric substitutions between plant- and animal-derived protein sources were not associated with overall physical fitness, although food-level analyses showed heterogeneous associations, suggesting the relevance of the broader food matrix.

articles.title: Early-stage follicle development regulated by RGD peptide and ovarian fragment size in three-dimensional culture.
articles.abstract: The tripeptide Arg-Gly-Asp (RGD) is a minimal integrin-binding motif found in multiple extracellular matrix (ECM) proteins. We previously determined that immature ovarian fragments cultured in the RGD-immobilized dextran hydrogel significantly promoted antral follicle development compared to those cultured in the dextran hydrogel control. In this study, using neonatal mouse ovaries, we examined the effects of RGD peptide and ovarian fragment size on early-stage follicle development in our 3D culture system. One neonatal ovary was cut into 1/2, 1/4, or 1/8 fragments and cultured in the dextran hydrogel with or without RGD. Follicle development progressively increased as fragment size decreased (intact < 1/2 < 1/4 < 1/8). Notably, RGD treatment further enhanced follicle development in a size-dependent manner. In particular, the RGD-treated 1/8 fragments significantly promoted follicle development compared to all other groups with or without RGD. Previous studies have shown that ovarian fragmentation stimulates early-stage follicle development through disruption of the Hippo pathway. We found that the RGD treatment further increased the Hippo pathway disruption in the 1/8 fragments compared to those cultured without RGD. As a ligand, RGD binds to integrin receptors to induce various cell functions. In the neonatal ovary, ovary-specific RGD-binding integrins αvβ3 and αvβ5 were predominantly localized in the ovarian interstitial/theca cells. To evaluate the role of the RGD-integrin interaction, we blocked integrins αvβ3 and αvβ5 using Cilengitide (Ci). In the presence of Ci, RGD-induced follicle development and the Hippo pathway disruption were completely suppressed in the 1/8 fragments in 3D culture. These results suggest that the RGD-integrin interaction is crucial for promoting early-stage follicle development in 3D culture. Overall, our study demonstrates that ovarian fragment size significantly influences early-stage follicle development in culture. Fragmentation exposes the ovarian stromal compartment expressing RGD-binding integrins to the surrounding hydrogel. Moreover, the effect of RGD treatment on follicle development depends on ovarian fragment size in our 3D culture system, with 1/8 fragments yielding the greatest enhancement.

articles.title: Exploring the relationship between bone mineral density and bone biomarkers with the duration of childhood-onset type 1 diabetes in Kuwait.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The significance of the human skeleton as an endocrine organ has been emphasized in recent literature where it may have the ability to regulate metabolic pathways including insulin signaling and glucose homeostasis. Therefore, the consequences of T1D can significantly impact bone health and structural formation, leading to osteoporosis later in life. This study aimed to evaluate lumbar spine size adjusted bone mineral density (BMD) and bone turnover biomarkers in Kuwaiti youth with childhood-onset T1D, and to examine its association with diabetes duration and glycemic control.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 132 Kuwaiti participants aged 5 to 18 years with T1D were recruited from a pediatric diabetes clinic. Anthropometric measurements, pubertal status, and clinical histories were recorded. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA; Hologic Discovery W, Hologic APEX Software version 5.6.0.5) was used to assess lumbar spine bone mineral apparent density (BMAD). Bone formation (osteocalcin, P1NP, P1CP) and resorption (urine CTX) biomarkers were measured. Multivariable linear regression models adjusted for age at diagnosis, sex, pubertal status, height, and HbA1c were used to assess associations between (i) diabetes duration and BMAD Z-score and (ii) diabetes duration and each bone biomarker.
RESULTS: Median diabetes duration was 3.5 years (LQ-UQ: 1.01-6.98 years). Each additional year of diabetes duration was associated with a non-significant decrease in BMAD Z - score after adjustment for age at diagnosis, sex, Tanner pubertal status, average HbA1c, and height (effect size: -0.11, 95% CI: -0.22 to 0.01). Higher average HbA1c was significantly associated with lower BMAD Z - score (-0.18 per unit increase, p=0.005). Each additional year of diabetes duration was associated with lower osteocalcin levels by 30.6% (95%CI: 37.5-22.9%) amongst females and 14.5% (95% CI: 24.7-2.8%) amongst males, and lower Urine CTX levels by 14.3% amongst females (95% CI: 8.5-19.7%), but not amongst males.
CONCLUSION: Higher mean HbA1c was associated with a lower lumbar-spine BMAD Z-score, whereas diabetes duration was not significantly associated with BMAD Z-score. Sex-specific associations were observed between diabetes duration and selected bone-turnover markers. These cross-sectional findings require confirmation in longitudinal studies incorporating appropriately matched controls and population-appropriate DXA reference data.

articles.title: Continuous glucose monitoring, automated insulin delivery, and remote care in adolescents with type 1 diabetes: advances toward integrated digital management.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes management in adolescents remains challenging due to physiological and behavioral factors. This review summarizes recent advances in three interconnected technologies: continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), automated insulin delivery (AID), and remote care. CGM provides real-time glycemic data with time in range (TIR) as the core metric, improving glycemic outcomes when implemented with structured education. AID systems, particularly hybrid closed-loop devices, consistently increase TIR, reduce glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and lower risks of severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) across randomized trials and real-world studies, with validated efficacy in children as young as 1-year-old. Remote care models leverage continuous data streams to enable individualized follow-up, showing glycemic outcomes approaching those of traditional visits in comparative studies while improving access and psychosocial support. Despite proven benefits, barriers remain, including socioeconomic inequities in technology access, alarm fatigue, and implementation gaps across healthcare systems. Future priorities include fully closed-loop systems, dual-hormone approaches, algorithm optimization for exercise and illness, long-term psychosocial outcomes, and equitable implementation strategies. Clinical practice should integrate these technologies through multidisciplinary teams, early initiation, and patient-centered support to transform adolescent diabetes care from intermittent visits to continuous digital management.

articles.title: Development and internal validation of prediction models for maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes in HELLP syndrome: a retrospective cohort study in China.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: HELLP syndrome is uncommon but can cause serious maternal adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). We investigated whether routinely available clinical and laboratory variables could support outcome-specific risk prediction.
METHODS: We included all women with HELLP syndrome treated at Fujian Maternity and Child Health Hospital from January 2013 to June 2023. Five outcomes were modeled: placental abruption (PAB), posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and a severe maternal composite outcome. The primary analysis used repeated nested cross-validation in the full cohort. Missing-data filtering and imputation, predictor screening, model-family selection, hyperparameter tuning, and threshold estimation were performed within each outer training fold so that the held-out fold evaluated the entire modeling process. Candidate families were ridge logistic regression, elastic-net logistic regression, and random forest. A paired sensitivity analysis using multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) was conducted to assess the effect of replacing mean/mode imputation.
RESULTS: Among 272 women, PAB occurred in 33 (12.13%), PRES in 23 (8.46%), PPH in 19 (6.99%), DIC in 9 (3.31%), and the severe composite outcome in 25 (9.19%). The corresponding AUCs were 0.715, 0.677, 0.833, 0.907, and 0.742. Ridge logistic regression was selected in 62%, 74%, 56%, and 62% of the outer folds for PAB, PRES, PPH, and the severe composite outcome, respectively. For DIC, the single-predictor logistic regression fallback was selected in 85% of the outer folds. In the paired analysis, MICE changed AUC by -0.002 to 0.009 and AUPRC by -0.005 to 0.002. PAB, PRES, and PPH did not meet the prespecified analysis criteria. DIC and the composite outcome met these criteria, although both estimates were limited by sparse events and the lack of external validation.
CONCLUSIONS: Although performance was not uniformly strong and external validation is still needed, routinely available data showed potential for early risk stratification. In particular, the severe composite outcome provided a clinically meaningful way to combine individually rare but serious complications and may help identify women who warrant closer surveillance.

articles.title: Navigating the epigenetic landscape of gestational age.
articles.abstract: Accurate estimation of gestational age is essential for clinical decision-making during pregnancy and is a critical indicator of both fetal development and maternal health. While traditional methods relying on the last menstrual period or ultrasound imaging provide varying levels of precision, emerging evidence suggests that DNA methylation patterns offer a powerful molecular approach for estimating gestational age at birth. Epigenetic gestational age clocks, developed using machine learning models trained on DNA methylation data from neonatal blood samples, have demonstrated high accuracy and are increasingly used in epidemiological research. However, despite the growing interest in these tools, their biological significance is only partially understood. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on the relationship between DNA methylation and gestational age, with a particular focus on the development and interpretation of epigenetic gestational age clocks. We explore potential biological pathways linking DNA methylation to gestational age, discuss key methodological considerations, and compare these clocks with established DNA methylation-based aging clocks. Finally, we outline future research directions to clarify the utility of epigenetic gestational age measures in understanding prenatal development, perinatal health, and early-life risk factors.

articles.title: Relationship between Helicobacter pylori IgG seropositivity and soil-transmitted helminth infections among school-aged children in Fongo-Tongo (Western Cameroon): prevalence, associated factors, and IgG variation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Soil-transmitted helminths (STH) and Helicobacter (H.) pylori exposure are highly prevalent in developing countries, where poor living conditions favor their transmission and persistence. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of STH infections and H. pylori IgG seropositivity, identify associated factors, and explore the relationship between these conditions among school-aged children in Fongo-Tongo, West Region of Cameroon.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted from February to May 2024 among children aged 1-15 years from five public primary schools (EP): EP Fossong Tchuentchue, EP Chefferie Fongo-Tongo, EP Lefang, EP Lithiapang, and EP Melang, in Fongo-Tongo, West Region of Cameroon. Eggs of STH species were morphologically identified in stool samples of participants using Kato-Katz thick smear. For STH species positive slide, egg counts were performed and expressed as number of eggs per gram of stool (EPG). Serum samples were used for the detection of anti-H. pylori IgG antibodies using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) with a commercial kit (ErbaLisa® H. pylori IgG, Calbiotech Inc., USA). Sociodemographic, behavioral, and household data were collected using a structured questionnaire given to participants or their guardians. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 23.
RESULTS: A total of 357 children were enrolled in the study (47.3% girls; mean age: 9.17 ± 2.51 years). The prevalence of STH infections was 32.8%, while H. pylori IgG seropositivity was 66.9%. The most common STH species was hookworm (24.9%), followed by Trichuris trichiura (10.4%) and Ascaris lumbricoides (5.3%). Overall, STH/H. pylori co-occurrence was observed in 20.7% of children. No significant association was observed between H. pylori IgG serostatus and the prevalence of combined STH or species-specific STH infection (p > 0.05). Similarly, median egg counts (EPG) were comparable between anti- H. pylori IgG-seropositive and seronegative children for each STH species. However, analysis according to IgG concentration revealed a significant decrease in hookworm prevalence (p = 0.029) and median egg counts (p = 0.048) with increasing antibody levels. Multivariate analysis identified several factors associated with STH/H. pylori co-occurrence, including specific school catchment areas, poor hand hygiene after toilet use, and irregular footwear use (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: These findings indicate a high coexistence of STH infections and H. pylori IgG seropositivity among school-aged children, likely reflecting shared environmental, behavioral, and hygiene-related risk factors. Although no direct association was observed between STH infections and H. pylori IgG seropositivity overall, the findings highlight the importance of integrated prevention strategies, including hygiene education, preventive chemotherapy, and improvements in water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) infrastructure.

articles.title: Epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Aeromonas from pediatric diarrhea in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China: 2017-2024.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study characterized the epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance of Aeromonas isolates from pediatric patients between 2017 and 2024 to inform improved clinical management and infection control.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 439 Aeromonas isolates from 2017 to 2024 included antimicrobial susceptibility testing of 316 isolates by the Kirby-Bauer method and whole-genome sequencing of 217 isolates for species identification, MLST, and resistance gene profiling.
RESULTS: The prevalence of Aeromonas spp. in feces was 2.36% (439/18,627) between 2017 and 2024, with significant temporal variation and a pronounced summer peak, while no age or sex differences were observed. Among 316 isolates, resistance was highest to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (45.25%) and lowest to amikacin (0.32%). Resistance to third- and fourth-generation cephalosporins ranged from 5.06% (cefepime) to 9.49%. Carbapenem resistance was higher for imipenem (8.23%) than for meropenem (1.58%). Among the 217 sequenced isolates, Aeromonas caviae predominated (86.18%), followed by A. veronii (5.07%), and most isolates (81.57%) belong to the novel sequence type. Several relatively uncommon species, such as A. trota, A. taiwanensis and A. sanarellii were detected in this study and formed a distinct phylogenetic clade separate from the major species. Additionally, a single A. veronii isolate (strain Q212) was found to branch distantly from other A. veronii strains, raising the possibility of unique genetic features. A. caviae and A. veronii exhibited the broadest resistance profiles, with A. veronii showing higher resistance to several antimicrobials. A total of 779 antimicrobial resistance genes were identified. cphA (5.07%) and imiH (0.92%) were detected in A. veronii, A. dhakensis, and A. hydrophila, whereas blaNDM-14 was detected in one A. caviae isolate. mcr-3 (11.06%) was predominantly detected in A. caviae. Genes such as ampH, ampS, and blaOXA-427 also showed species-associated distribution patterns.
CONCLUSIONS: Aeromonas, with A. caviae predominating, shows substantial genetic diversity and clinically relevant antimicrobial resistance, with species-specific resistance genes. Furthermore, the detection of rare species should not be overlooked. These findings provide critical evidence for empirical therapy and resistance surveillance.

articles.title: Epidemiology of Clonorchis sinensis infection in Guangdong, China, 2006-2024: a retrospective analysis of over 0.17 million reported cases from passive surveillance data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonorchiasis, caused by the ingestion of raw freshwater fish containing Clonorchis sinensis metacercariae, lacks national notifiable status in China, resulting in insufficiently characterized epidemiology. However, as an important endemic disease in Guangdong province, it is reported in the National Notifiable Disease Reporting System (NNDRS). We conducted an observational study to characterize clonorchiasis epidemiology using NNDRS data from Guangdong.
METHODS: Cases included in this study were patients diagnosed with clonorchiasis in Guangdong province (2006-2024) and reported via NNDRS. Proportion and reported incidence of cases by gender, ages, and occupations were analyzed and compared, when spatial analysis was employed to identify high clusters at county level.
RESULTS: There were 170,709 cases reported during the study period, of which 166,728 cases lived in Guangdong. A steady increase in reported incidence from 1.77/100,000 in 2006 to 37.27/100,000 in 2024 was observed (average annual percent change (AAPC):17.22%, P<0.001). The median age of patients was 54.0 years (inter-quartile range, 44.0-64.0). Most cases were male (78.30%). House-hold or unemployed personnel (25.86%), retirees (20.43%) and farmers (16.66%) comprised the majority. The reported incidence was notably higher among males and individual aged 65-69 years. Although clonorchiasis was reported in all 21 prefecture-level cities, spatial clustering was observed, particularly in the developed Pearl River Delta region.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings revealed the importance of clonorchiasis as a public health problem in Guangdong province. Precise strategies for prevention and control of clonorchiasis should be employed for targeted populations, with an emphasis on middle-aged and elderly people, male individuals, and people living in Pearl River Delta region.

articles.title: Bridging the gap in multidrug-resistant tuberculosis care: a mixed-methods study of treatment outcomes, enrolment, and caregiver perspectives in Oyo State, Nigeria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, with gaps in treatment enrolment and completion undermining control efforts. This study assessed MDR-TB treatment outcomes and explored caregivers' perspectives on factors influencing treatment enrolment and adherence in Oyo State, Nigeria.
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted in Oyo State, Nigeria. The quantitative component involved retrospective review of 277 MDR-TB patient records from accredited treatment facilities between 2016 and 2022, while the qualitative component comprised in-depth interviews with 10 purposively selected caregivers, including healthcare workers, tuberculosis and leprosy supervisors, and community-based organization representatives involved in MDR-TB care. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests at p < 0.05, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Analysis of MDR-TB case detection and enrolment was restricted to 2020-2022 due to availability of complete surveillance records.
RESULTS: Most patients were aged ≥ 30 years (70.4%) and male (52.3%). Between 2020 and 2022, a total of 716 MDR-TB cases were detected, of which 295 (42.2%) were enrolled in treatment, with enrolment improving to 51.3% in 2022. Among the enrolled patients, 75.8% achieved successful treatment outcomes, including 63.2% who completed treatment and 12.6% who were cured, while 24.2% experienced unfavorable outcomes such as loss to follow-up (11.6%) and death (6.9%). No statistically significant associations were observed between socio-demographic or clinical characteristics and treatment outcomes (p > 0.05). Qualitative findings identified perceived treatment effectiveness, counselling, free treatment services, financial and social support, and strong health system follow-up as major facilitators of treatment enrolment and adherence. Key barriers included poverty, stigma, prolonged treatment duration, poor adherence, and disruption of livelihoods.
CONCLUSION: Although MDR-TB treatment outcomes were relatively successful in Oyo State, significant gaps remain in treatment enrolment and completion. Strengthening patient support systems, addressing socioeconomic barriers, and improving linkage between diagnosis and treatment initiation are essential to improving MDR-TB control. Caregiver perspectives provide important insights for strengthening program implementation and patient retention.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This study was a descriptive cross-sectional mixed-methods study involving retrospective record review and qualitative interviews, and therefore did not require clinical trial registration.

articles.title: Model-informed characterisation of the target therapeutic window for dexamethasone by quantitatively balancing foetal lung maturation and neurotoxicity in pregnant rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Dexamethasone, a first-line treatment for neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS), promotes foetal lung maturation whilst simultaneously inducing neurotoxicity in offspring. We aimed to define the therapeutic window of dexamethasone for the treatment of NRDS.
EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Pregnant rats were given dexamethasone at 0.1 or 0.4 mg·kg-1 to simulate clinically equivalent prenatal dexamethasone exposure. Half of the rats were anaesthetised, and surfactant proteins A and B in foetal lungs quantified. A pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) model was developed to determine the minimum effective concentration. The remaining rats, delivered naturally, and their offspring underwent open-field testing. Messenger RNA sequencing of the foetal hippocampus was performed, and concentration-toxicity assays were conducted using H19-7/IGF-IR cells. Data were integrated with a maternal-foetal physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to determine the maximum tolerated concentration. A clinical PBPK for dexamethasone in pregnant women was used to simulate a potentially optimal dosing regimen.
KEY RESULTS: The PK/PD model adequately characterised dexamethasone-induced foetal lung maturation and indicated a minimal effective concentration of 1.63 ng·ml-1. The offspring of PDE rats exhibited significant behavioural changes. mRNA sequencing analysis suggested that neurotoxicity was mediated via the Wnt pathway and renin-angiotensin system, with BDNF and CMA1 identified as potential biomarkers of neurotoxicity. Cell-based assays suggested a neurotoxic threshold concentration of 17 ng·ml-1. For a therapeutic window of 1.63-17 ng·ml-1, PBPK model simulations indicated that a reduced dose regimen of 2.5 or 3 mg every 8 h for six doses may represent an optimised therapeutic strategy.
CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: This model-informed precision dosing strategy provides a rational approach to optimising clinical dexamethasone dosing regimens.

articles.title: Sex-specific effects of prenatal vitamin D supplementation on repetitive behaviour and neuroimmune mediators in the BTBR mouse model of autism spectrum disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) are prevalent in males compared with females, possibly attributed to male-centric profiles diagnostic criteria. ASD pathogenesis involves neuroinflammation and altered immune signalling. Therefore, maternal vitamin D deficiency may contribute to ASD by impairing fetal neurodevelopment, promoting immune dysregulation and inflammatory conditions. Due to the difficult recruitment of the vulnerable paediatric population, we used BTBR T + tf/J (BTBR) male and female mice, characterized by core ASD-like behaviours, to investigate the effects of prenatal vitamin D supplementation.
EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: On gestational day 9, pregnant BTBR dams received a subcutaneous injection of either vitamin D3 (400 ng·kg-1) or vehicle. At 8-week-old, offspring underwent a battery of behavioural tests, including Hole Board, Marble Burying, Self-grooming, Open Field and Social Interaction tests. mRNA expression and protein levels of tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), transforming growth factor-β2 (TGF-β2), fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) and resistin in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus were then quantified.
KEY RESULTS: Maternal vitamin D supplementation reduced BTBR stereotypies. Moreover, vitamin D decreased cortical and hippocampal protein TNF-α levels only in BTBR males. In addition, vitamin D upregulated hippocampal TGF-β2 gene expression and FABP4 gene expression and protein content in male offspring, whereas a down-regulation of TGF-β2 mRNA and protein levels was reported in females.
CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Our findings indicated that prenatal vitamin D supplementation exerted beneficial effects on BTBR stereotypies, neuroinflammatory and neuroimmune signalling alterations, ultimately suggesting its potential as an early preventive strategy to target ASD sex-tailored biomolecular dysfunctions.

articles.title: What is the association between mode of delivery at birth and childhood adiposity? Findings from the Southampton Women's Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a major public health concern. Caesarean section (CS) delivery has been linked to increased childhood adiposity; however, the literature is inconsistent.
AIMS: To examine the associations between mode of delivery at birth and adiposity in childhood and whether they differ by type of CS (planned versus emergency).
METHODS: The Southampton Women's Survey recruited 12,583 non-pregnant women between 1998 and 2002 in Southampton, UK. From 3153 women who had liveborn singleton infants followed up after birth, mode of delivery was recorded and adiposity measured at age 4, 6-7 and 8-9 years. Outcome measures were child body mass index (BMI) and fat mass and body fat percentage measured by Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry. Associations were investigated using mixed-effects linear regression models after multiple imputation by chained equations, adjusting for maternal (adiposity, age, education, pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, smoking during pregnancy) and child-related confounders (birthweight, sex, gestational age), ascertained using a Directed Acyclic Graph.
RESULTS: 16% of the women had an emergency CS, and 8% a planned CS. Adjusted analyses showed that CS (versus vaginal delivery) was associated with increased offspring adiposity, with the magnitude of association increasing with the age of the child. For example, compared to children born vaginally, those born via CS had an average fat mass percentage 0.09 standard deviations (95% CI 0.00, 0.18, p = 0.04) higher and showed a 0.03 standard deviation (95% CI 0.01, 0.06; p = 0.009) greater increase in body fat percentage per year. Emergency CS was associated with increased adiposity compared to assisted vaginal delivery, particularly for BMI and fat mass outcomes.
CONCLUSION: CS-delivered babies had higher childhood BMI, fat mass and body fat percentage. Emergency CS accounted for most CS deliveries and was associated with increased adiposity. The findings support important effects of maternal and early life factors on long-term health outcomes.

articles.title: Elarekibep, an inhaled Anticalin protein, targets IL-4Rα locally: first-in-human randomized phase 1 trials of a novel potential therapeutic class in asthma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elarekibep (AZD1402/PRS-060) is an Anticalin, a new class of inhaled therapeutic proteins, which has been engineered to inhibit interleukin-4 receptor α-subunit (IL-4Rα) signalling, a key target in asthma.
METHODS: Two phase 1 randomized, first-in-human, dose-escalating, single-blind studies (NCT03384290; NCT03574805) investigated single ascending doses (SADs) or multiple ascending doses (MADs) of elarekibep compared with placebo. In the SAD study, healthy participants received a single inhaled dose of elarekibep 0.1-160 mg, intravenous doses of 1 mg or 2 mg, or matched placebo. In the MAD study, participants with mild asthma and elevated fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) received inhaled doses of elarekibep 0.2-60 mg or placebo twice daily for 10 or 17 days (single dose on day 10 in all but one cohort), continuously or intermittently.
RESULTS: In total, 148 participants were enrolled across both studies. No safety concerns were reported. Treatment-emergent adverse events were experienced by 34.7% (elarekibep, 35.2%; placebo, 33.3%) and 81.6% (elarekibep, 75.9%; placebo, 95.5%) of SAD and MAD study participants, respectively. Elarekibep was absorbed after inhalation, with dose-related increases in systemic exposure detectable with doses greater than or equal to 6 mg. In both studies, systemic exposure resulted in decreased levels of phosphorylated signal transducer and activator of transcription 6, a biomarker for systemic IL-4Rα target engagement. In the MAD study, rapid reductions of FeNO were demonstrated with doses greater than or equal to 2 mg, indicating pulmonary target engagement.
CONCLUSIONS: Elarekibep was well tolerated in both studies and demonstrated pulmonary and systemic target engagement. Elarekibep was investigated further in a phase 2a study (NCT04643158).
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT03384290. Registered 26 November 2017, https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03384290 . NCT03574805. Registered 2 July 2018, https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03574805 .

articles.title: Proliferative control of the saccular-stage developing mouse lung requires the histone methylation activity of KMT2D.
articles.abstract: KMT2D, the histone methyltransferase and core component of the COMPASS/MLL4 complex, has been implicated in developmental diseases such as Kabuki Syndrome, interstitial lung disease, and congenital diaphragmatic hernia, with clear links to pediatric pulmonary disorders. Despite this, the mechanism by which KMT2D governs lung development remains unclear. Knock-in mouse models harboring catalytically inactive KMT2D (KMT2DKI), thereby reducing H3K4 methylation, have demonstrated potential in defining KMT2D's role in pulmonary development. Our post-hoc examination of the E18.5 lungs of KMT2DKI mice revealed increased cellular density and impaired sacculation indicated by reduced airspace chord length, thickening of intersaccular septa, and abnormal alveolar cell differentiation. KMT2DKI mice revealed narrowed Sox2 + conducting airways and epithelial differentiation defects characterized by reduced Cc10 + club cells. Accompanying the alveolar and airway hypoplasia, blood vessel luminal area was reduced. Conversely, KMT2DKI lungs had a significantly higher proportion of proliferating cells accompanied by a dramatic expansion in Pdgfrα + mesenchymal progenitor cells. Our findings therefore suggest that KMT2D-mediated H3K4 methylation is vital to normal lung development, and its impairment results in widespread pulmonary hypoplasia and potentially pulmonary hypertension.

articles.title: Psychological Assets and Cardiovascular Health in Adulthood: A Mixed Methods Investigation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychological risk factors like depression increase risk for poor cardiovascular outcomes but psychological assets like purpose in life are protective and linked to reduced risk of cardiovascular events. However, most assets are investigated individually, and not all have been explored in relation to cardiovascular health (CVH). This study used mixed methods to assess multiple psychological assets and evaluate associations with CVH 12 years later.
METHODS: Data came from 2092 participants in the National Child Development Study. At age 50 years, participants wrote open-ended responses describing their futures. Two trained researchers qualitatively coded each response by rating them for 7 commonly assessed psychological assets (1=not at all; 7=very): optimism, purpose, satisfaction, personal growth, agency, enjoyment, and overall positivity. At age 62, CVH behavioral factors (exercise, smoking status, sleep) were self-reported; CVH clinical factors (blood pressure, lipids, glucose, body weight) were measured during nurse visits. Following Life's Essential 8 guidelines, CVH components were combined into total CVH scores. Linear regressions examined associations between each age 50 asset and age 62 CVH scores, adjusting for age 50 confounders.
RESULTS: All age 50 assets were positively associated with better CVH scores 12 years later, accounting for sociodemographic characteristics and word counts (p≤0.05). Purpose (b=0.81 [95% CI, 0.33-1.29]) and personal growth (b=0.82 [95% CI, 0.34-1.20]) showed the strongest associations with CVH in fully adjusted models.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher levels of most midlife psychological assets were linked with better CVH over time, suggesting multiple paths to health protection. These findings highlight assets that could be prevention targets.

articles.title: Real-World Safety and Effectiveness of Evolocumab in Japanese Patients With Familial Hypercholesterolemia: Postmarketing Survey Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on the real-world use of PCSK9 (proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9) inhibitors in familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) remains limited. This postmarketing surveillance study (NCT02808403) evaluated Japanese patients with FH and the long-term real-world effectiveness of evolocumab.
METHODS: This analysis included patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) and homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH). Diagnostic pathways, patient characteristics, background lipid-lowering therapy, evolocumab use, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction, long-term target achievement, and findings in pediatric HoFH were assessed.
RESULTS: Of 2117 patients in the safety analysis set (HeFH, n=2009; HoFH, n=108), 1380 (HeFH, n=1296; HoFH, n=84) were included in the effectiveness analysis. Compared with patients with HeFH, patients with HoFH had higher genetic testing rates (40.7% versus 9.8%), higher mean baseline LDL-C levels (188.4±107.3 mg/dL versus 139.2±58.3 mg/dL), and higher lipoprotein apheresis use (26.9% versus 2.1%), but fewer total comorbidities (2.2±1.5 versus 2.7±1.5). Statin use was similarly high in patients with HeFH and HoFH (92.2% and 93.5%, respectively) with many patients receiving low- to moderate-intensity statins. Most patients received evolocumab biweekly. LDL-C reductions were evident at 4 weeks and sustained at 104 weeks. At 104 weeks, mean LDL-C changes from baseline were -54.0% in patients with HeFH and -48.9% in patients with HoFH. LDL-C<70 mg/dL was achieved by 63.0% of patients with HeFH and 43.9% of patients with HoFH, and LDL-C<55 mg/dL was achieved by 48.2% and 17.1%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Evolocumab was associated with sustained LDL-C reductions over 104 weeks in Japanese patients with HeFH and HoFH, with higher target achievement in HeFH. Gaps exist in genetic testing and treatment optimization in routine Japanese FH care.

articles.title: Navitoclax and Venetoclax with Chemotherapy for Relapsed/Refractory ALL in Children and Young Adults.
articles.abstract: Despite improving survival rates, a significant number of children, adolescents and young adults (CAYA) with relapsed/refractory acute lymphoblastic leukemia (r/r ALL) still die from disease. This calls for new drugs combination to reinduce complete remissions (CR) and enable consolidation. B-cell lymphoma (BCL) family proteins have a key role in regulating the blast apoptotic response to chemotherapy-induced cell damage and the combination of the BCL-2 and BCL-XL/BCL-2 inhibitors (venetoclax [VEN] and navitoclax [NAV], respectively) with chemotherapy could revert the resistance observed in r/r ALL. We retrospectively collected data of NAV/VEN, combined with chemotherapy, in 30 CAYA with advanced, R/R, either B-ALL (n=17) or T-ALL (n=13), treated under compassionate use, in 5 European centers. NAV and VEN (median number of cycles 1, range 1-3) were administered over 28 days. The most common toxicity was hematologic: overall, 93% of the patients developed grade 3-4 neutropenia, 83% grade 3-4 anemia and 83% grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia. No fatal adverse event was recorded. The overall response rate (CR/CRi/PR) was 71% for the B-ALL (12/17 patients) and 50% (6/12) for the T-ALL cohort, allowing, respectively, 11 and 4 patients to receive further consolidation. Six B-ALL patients and 2 T-ALL patients are alive and maintain response, with a median follow-up of 25 (0,6 - 38) and 8 months (0.5-47), respectively. All patients who did not receive consolidation ultimately relapsed and died. Our experience underlines the strong potential of NAV/VEN plus conventional chemotherapy to reinduce complete remission in heavily pretreated and refractory CAYA with either B- or T-ALL.

articles.title: Low Uptake of Guideline-Recommended MRI Screening for Silent Cerebral Infarcts over the Lifespan in Sickle Cell Anemia.
articles.abstract: Silent cerebral infarcts (SCIs) are common and clinically consequential in individuals with sickle cell anemia (SCA; HbSS or HbSβ⁰-thalassemia). In 2020, the American Society of Hematology recommended magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based screening in childhood (strong recommendation) and adulthood (conditional recommendation); however, real-world implementation remains poorly characterized. We conducted a multicenter sequential mixed-methods study integrating site-level MRI utilization data, clinician surveys, and semi-structured interviews. Eleven academic SCD programs contributed MRI data for patients aged 5-18 years and >18 years. Clinicians completed the Clinician Guideline Determinants Questionnaire (CGDQ), adapted for pediatric and adult SCI screening, and a purposively sampled subset participated in interviews guided by the Tailored Implementation for Chronic Diseases framework. Thirty-eight clinicians completed surveys, and 25 participated in interviews. Clinicians endorsed the evidence supporting SCI screening; however, readiness to implement adult screening was lower than for pediatric screening (mean CGDQ score 117.0 vs. 126.4). Across 6,959 patients with SCA, fewer than 1 in 8 (11.75%) had undergone brain MRI over the study period (2015-2024), with consistently lower utilization in adult-only programs. Qualitative analysis identified 5 modifiable, multilevel determinants influencing implementation: unclear guideline expectations, patient and family readiness, interprofessional workflows and interpretation capacity, clinic resources and staffing infrastructure, and structural and policy barriers. Despite strong clinician support for SCI screening, implementation remains inconsistent, particularly in adult SCA care. Identified determinants highlight actionable targets for multicomponent implementation strategies to improve uptake and sustainability of MRI-based SCI screening across the lifespan.

articles.title: Rethinking obesity metrics: the body roundness index as a screening tool for sarcopenia in young and middle-aged adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is a progressive musculoskeletal syndrome characterized by a generalized and accelerated decline in skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. Primarily associated with aging, it is a key determinant of frailty, mobility impairment, and increased risk of adverse health outcomes. Sarcopenia is often overlooked in young and middle-aged adults. Concurrently, rising obesity rates have exacerbated its societal burden. Although conventional obesity indices such as body mass index (BMI) and waist circumference are associated with sarcopenia, their comparative predictive utility in younger populations remains unclear. To address this gap, the present study examines the association between the Body Roundness Index (BRI)-a shape-based metric incorporating both height and waist circumference-and sarcopenia in young and middle-aged adults (mean age 38 years), with the aim of identifying an obesity indicator that may be useful for early risk stratification in this specific population.
METHODS: This study analyzed data from NHANES 2011-2014, including 6,009 adults aged 18-59 years. In this investigation, we assessed obesity via eight anthropometric indices (all calculated from simple body measurements without requiring laboratory results). Sarcopenia was primarily defined in accordance with the criteria established by the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP). Machine learning was employed to rank the indices based on their relevance to sarcopenia. BRI demonstrated the highest association and was further analyzed using multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and threshold effect analysis. Subgroup analyses (stratified by age, sex, and metabolic factors) were conducted to evaluate consistency.
RESULTS: The study included 6,009 participants (inverse-weighted to represent 133,965,501 individuals; mean age 38.25 ± 12.33 years; male-to-female ratio 13:12), among whom 198 had sarcopenia. All eight obesity-related indices showed significant associations with sarcopenia. Machine learning revealed that BRI had the strongest correlation (Model 3: OR = 1.76, 95% CI: 1.62-1.91, p < 0.001). RCS confirmed a nonlinear relationship, and trend analysis indicated that the highest BRI tertile was associated with a 7.69-fold higher prevalence of sarcopenia compared to the lowest tertile (Model 3: OR = 9.31, 95% CI: 5.28-16.4, p < 0.001; p for trend < 0.001). A threshold effect was identified at BRI = 3.33, beyond which sarcopenia risk increased markedly. Across all subgroups (stratified by gender, age, etc.), a positive association between BRI and the prevalence of sarcopenia was consistently observed, lending further support to the robustness of the results.
CONCLUSION: BRI, a simple anthropometric measure, is independently associated with sarcopenia risk in young and middle-aged adults. These findings suggest that BRI may serve as a potentially useful indicator for early risk stratification in obesity-prone populations, highlighting the importance of myogenic obesity in this age group. Further mechanistic and longitudinal studies are warranted to confirm these associations and explore underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: A key to combating pertussis through maternal immunization in the Eastern Mediterranean Region: recommended action points from the Expert Network Meeting (ENM) on pertussis maternal immunization.
articles.abstract: Pertussis can seriously affect infants who are too young to be fully immunized (< 6 months of age) leading to increased risk of severe and potentially lethal complications. Pertussis control remains fragile in EMR, facing several challenges from the healthcare sector and providers, likewise low awareness, and a lack of clear recommendation of maternal immunization and maternal care services for infectious disease prevention and treatment, particularly against pertussis. The Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (EMPHNET) launched the initiative entitled "The Way Forward for Pertussis Control in EMR: Focus on Maternal Immunization" aims to emphasize that the primary goal is the control of pertussis, initially focusing on the protection of infants under 4 months through maternal vaccination strategies. This initiative aimed to leverage existing epidemiological data and disease burden, as well as the exchange of successful experiences both regionally and globally related to maternal vaccination strategies. The following document presents the key findings of the Expert Network Meeting on Pertussis Control implemented in Amman-Jordan in 4-8 August 2024. It proposes the way forward for Pertussis control strategies in the EMR, with recommendations on bolstering regional efforts towards strengthening maternal Tdap immunization.

articles.title: Specific associations of seven dimensions of sleep quality with suicide behaviours in Chinese adolescents: the partially moderating role of morning chronotype.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To quantify the associations between seven dimensions of sleep quality and suicide behaviours (suicide ideation [SI], suicide plan [SP] and suicide attempt [SA]), and to examine the moderating role of chronotype in these relationships.
METHODS: A total of 20,055 adolescents were recruited through a stratified cluster sampling across 5 representative provinces in mainland China. Confounding variables included demographic characteristics, depression and anxiety.
RESULTS: Among 20,055 adolescents, 2,099 had SI (10.5%), 1,596 had SP (7.9%) and 1,005 had SA (5.0%). In total, 4,276 were classified as morning-type (21.3%). Multinomial logistic regression analysis indicated that sleep duration and sleep disturbances were significantly associated with SI, SP and SA (all p < 0.05), whereas the relationship between subjective sleep quality and suicide behaviours was not significant (p > 0.05). Notably, hypnotic drug use is significantly associated only with SA (p < 0.05). Moreover, among morning-type adolescents, the relationships between the two dimensions of sleep quality (sleep disturbance and hypnotic drug use) and suicide behaviours became non-significant (p > 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: The seven dimensions of sleep quality exhibited unique associations with suicide behaviours in Chinese adolescents. Furthermore, morningness appears to partially moderate the associations between some sleep problems and suicide behaviours.

articles.title: Linguistic subtyping within stages of psychosis: A natural language processing approach.
articles.abstract: As one of the core characteristics of schizophrenia, linguistic impairments show substantial heterogeneity. Dissecting linguistic subgroups in schizophrenia using natural language processing methods may reveal distinct clinical profiles regarding current symptomatology and premorbid abnormalities. We aimed to investigate computational linguistic subgroups in 227 Turkish-speaking individuals, including 61 patients with chronic schizophrenia (SCH), 89 patients with first-episode psychosis (FEP) and 77 individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P). Speech samples were collected through the Thematic Apperception Test. We investigated semantic similarity and syntax, alongside normative thematic and lexical choice in SCH, FEP and CHR-P groups. The exploratory factor analysis of 27 linguistic features derived 7 factors, which revealed 4 classes in latent profile analysis. Cluster 1 demonstrated global linguistic impairments, including higher semantic similarity, more severe syntactic disturbances, and less normative thematic and lexical choice. This cluster was associated with more severe neurodevelopmental abnormalities and poorer premorbid adjustment, alongside more severe negative symptoms and poorer psychosocial functioning, neurocognition and social cognition. Cluster 2, with the largest sample size, used more pronouns than cluster 4 and healthy controls, and was associated with higher levels of childhood trauma. Cluster 3 showed a near-normal computational linguistic profile, while cluster 4 demonstrated moderate linguistic impairments associated with elevated negative symptoms. Importantly, the distribution of SCH, FEP and CHR-P did not significantly differ across the clusters. Overall, these outcomes indicated that computational linguistics can dissect linguistic subgroups associated with distinct current and premorbid characteristics within stages of psychosis.

articles.title: Differential factors associated with adolescent suicide ideation, plans, and attempts in South Korea: a nationwide population-based study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Few studies have examined factors differing between adjacent levels of suicidality or between hospital-treated and non-hospital-treated suicide attempts. We examined factors associated with levels of suicidality among South Korean adolescents.
METHODS: We used data from the 2020 Korea Youth Risk Behavior Web-based Survey (N = 54,809). Suicidality was categorised into mutually exclusive groups (i.e., no suicidality, suicide ideation, plans, and attempts, with attempts classified as non-hospital-treated or hospital-treated). We compared the sex-specific prevalence of seven mental health and well-being factors (e.g., depressive symptoms and anxiety), five risk behaviours (e.g., substance use), and four adverse life circumstances (e.g., experience of violence) across suicidality levels. Multivariable logistic regression was used to compare adjacent levels of suicidality.
RESULTS: Overall, 7.2% of adolescents reported suicide ideation, 2.3% plans, and 2.0% attempts (1.7% non-hospital-treated and 0.3% hospital-treated), with higher prevalence among girls. Most risk factors, particularly depressive symptoms (odds ratio [OR]: 4.08, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.74, 4.46), were associated with suicide ideation compared with no suicidality, whereas few factors (e.g., anxiety) differentiated suicide plans from ideation. Compared with suicide plans, suicide attempts were associated with most risk behaviours, including substance use (OR: 2.06, 95% CI: 1.16, 3.66), and with depressive symptoms (OR: 1.48, 95% CI: 1.16, 1.90), experience of violence (OR: 2.00, 95% CI: 1.32, 3.02), and perceived poor academic performance. Among adolescents reporting suicide attempts, anxiety, substance use, and experience of violence were associated with hospital-treated attempts.
CONCLUSION: Population-level mental health promotion may help reduce suicidality, while risk behaviours and violence may be targets for preventing suicide attempts.

articles.title: Applications of artificial intelligence in cerebral palsy research: A bibliometric analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Research on the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in the diagnosis and treatment of cerebral palsy (CP) has grown steadily. However, the overall research landscape, collaboration patterns, and thematic evolution in this field have not yet been systematically summarized. This study aims to clarify the current research status, shifts in research hotspots, and existing limitations through bibliometric analysis, thereby providing a comprehensive reference for future investigations.
METHODS: A total of 278 English publications concerning AI applications in CP over the past 20 years were included in the analysis. Multiple bibliometric tools, including R-bibliometrix, VOSviewer, Scimago Graphica, and Pajek, were used to systematically analyze publication distribution, collaboration networks, intellectual base, and the temporal evolution of research hotspots in this field.
RESULTS: This field demonstrates rapid growth and interdisciplinary development. Global research output is dominated by European and North American countries, characterized by close intraregional collaboration, whereas in-depth cross-team, interdisciplinary, and transnational joint research remains scarce. Two core research themes have emerged: early screening and risk prediction for CP in high-risk infants, and intelligent motor function assessment for children with confirmed CP. Research hotspots have gradually shifted from traditional machine learning to deep learning-based automatic feature extraction. At present, the field suffers from imbalanced research priorities, insufficient model interpretability, and limited clinical translation. Inconsistent data standards and overreliance on unimodal data greatly restrict the generalizability and clinical applicability of intelligent models.
CONCLUSION: Future research should foster in-depth multi-center, interdisciplinary, and transnational scientific collaborations, build standardized multimodal datasets, and develop interpretable intelligent models. Meanwhile, understudied directions such as rehabilitation response prediction and long-term prognosis tracking should be explored. Strengthening the clinical translation of algorithmic models will further refine the interdisciplinary research system of AI-assisted precision rehabilitation for CP, and promote the high-quality and intelligent development of pediatric rehabilitation.

articles.title: Predicting post-surgical seizure outcomes in drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy using hippocampal radiomics from 18F-FDG hybrid PET/MRI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop multivariate hippocampal radiomics models using multimodal 18F-FDG hybrid PET/MRI and clinical variables to predict post-surgical seizure outcomes in patients with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 117 drug-resistant TLE patients from Xuanwu Hospital (August 2015-March 2023) who underwent preoperative 18F-FDG hybrid PET/MRI, surgical intervention, and one-year postoperative follow-up using Engel classification. Structural (3D-T1 and T2-FLAIR) and metabolic (18F-FDG PET) images were obtained. Hippocampal subfields were automatically segmented using FreeSurfer on 3D T1 images, with 18F-FDG PET and T2-FLAIR images registered accordingly. Radiomics features were extracted from the hippocampal subfields. Feature selection was performed using the minimum redundancy maximum relevance algorithm and the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression methods to calculate radscores. Radiomics-clinical and clinical models was constructed and model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and decision curve analysis. Patients were divided into hippocampal sclerosis (HS) and non-HS groups based on histology and mediation analysis explored relationships among radscore, HS, and Engel classification.
RESULTS: The radiomics model combining all three imaging sequences outperformed models using single or dual modalities. In the training set, the combined 18F-FDG PET/MRI radiomics-clinical model demonstrated higher discrimination than the clinical model alone (AUC = 0.915 vs. 0.716, p = 0.004). In the test set, the combined model showed a numerically higher AUC (0.819 vs. 0.743); however, this difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.661). Decision curve analysis shown that the combined 18F-FDG PET/MRI radiomics-clinical model provides higher clinical benefits in all risk threshold compared with the clinical model. The radscore was significantly higher in the HS group than in the non-HS group (t = 2.308, p = 0.023). Mediation analysis shows that radscore is a significant mediator between HS and Engel classification (proportion of indirect effect = 45.8%, p = 0.028).
CONCLUSION: The combined 18F-FDG PET/MRI radiomics-clinical model enhances the prediction of post-surgical seizure outcomes in drug-resistant TLE patients. Radiomics features may reflect the pathological state of HS, aiding in preoperative prognostication and clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Development and validation of a machine learning nomogram model for differentiating mycoplasma pneumoniae coinfection with other pathogens in children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current diagnostic methods, such as serological tests and polymerase chain reaction (PCR), are limited by slow turnaround time and sample quality, making early diagnosis challenging. Although mNGS offers higher sensitivity, its expense and specialized equipment limit clinical applicability. These limitations underscore the need for more reliable, rapid, and cost-effective diagnostic tools.
METHODS: Between June 2023 and March 2024, 191 consecutive pediatric patients were enrolled. The most recent laboratory test results prior to bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) were included. After LASSO screening, seven machine learning classifiers (LR, SVM, KNN, RF, ET, XGBoost, LightGBM) were tested, and the optimal one was selected for model construction. The nomogram model combined the radiomics (rad) signature and the clinical signature. The ROC curves were drawn to evaluate the diagnostic efficacy of different models. The calibration efficiency of the nomogram was evaluated by drawing calibration curves, and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test was used to evaluate the calibration ability of the models.
