Decision curve analysis (DCA) was utilized to evaluate the clinical utility of the models. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: A total of 1,834 handcrafted radiomics features were extracted, including 360 first-order features, 14 shape features, and texture features. The LR classifier achieved the best AUC, reaching 0.922 and 0.867 for distinguishing Co-MPP from MPP in the training and test cohorts, respectively. For building the clinical signature, LR was selected as the base model. The univariate analysis results of all clinical laboratory and CT imaging features showed that only reticulation and bronchial lumen occlusion were significantly different between MP and Co-MPP patients (p = 0.011 and p < 0.001, respectively). The clinical signature achieved AUC values of 0.729 and 0.706 in the training and test cohorts, respectively. A nomogram based on the LR algorithm was constructed to combine the clinical signature and the Rad signature. The DeLong test showed that the performance of the nomogram and the Rad signature was significantly higher than that of the clinical signature (p < 0.05), whereas no significant difference was observed between the nomogram and the Rad signature. Both the Rad signature and the nomogram demonstrated substantial clinical benefit.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that machine learning can assist clinicians in distinguishing Co-MPP from MPP in children. Furthermore, both the Rad signature and nomogram model showed higher clinical benefit than the clinical signature.

articles.title: From landmark uncertainty to clinical confidence: screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip.
articles.abstract: Clinical image annotation-based assessment methods often rely on anatomical landmarks to derive landmark-based measurements (angle or distance) that underpin screening, diagnosis, and treatment decisions. In screening pathways, landmark-based measurements typically use predefined thresholds to classify patients as healthy or unhealthy. Natural variability exists among clinicians in landmark placement and, consequently, in the derived measurement and screening decisions, reflecting genuine uncertainty in these assessments. We propose a method to estimate uncertainty associated with landmark-based measurements. By defining this measurement uncertainty, we derive a confidence estimate for the clinical screening task to provide context for the measured uncertainty. While the approach is applicable to screening in general, we demonstrate its utility in detecting developmental dysplasia of the hip in neonates using two standard clinical landmark-based measurements: the Graf α angle and the femoral head coverage percentage. We show a strong correlation between multiple clinicians' confidence and model's confidence. This indicates that the model and the clinicians identify the same cases that are difficult or borderline. To our knowledge, this work presents the first method to evaluate a model's confidence when predicting clinically relevant landmark-based measurements. This confidence estimate can establish trust in automated models, facilitating wider clinical adoption, which, in turn, can widen access to screening.

articles.title: Oropouche Fever Outbreak, Havana, Cuba, June-September 2024.
articles.abstract: Oropouche fever emerged nationwide in Cuba in 2024. We investigated the outbreak in Havana; of 549 suspected cases, 189 (34.4%) were confirmed. No cases were severe. Incidence was 8.9/100,000 population and was highest in adults 27-59 years of age (10.2/100,000 population). Three infants tested positive. Dengue cocirculation challenged surveillance.

articles.title: Monkeypox Virus Seroprevalence among Adults Assessed at Roadside Wellness Centers along Major Transportation Corridor, Kenya, 2025.
articles.abstract: Since 2024, Kenya has confirmed >1,000 cases of monkeypox virus (MPXV) infection. We conducted a cross-sectional serosurvey at 8 clinics along a transportation corridor in Kenya to quantify unrecognized MPXV transmission. From September 29-October 28, 2025, adults >18 years completed a questionnaire and provided blood samples tested with a serologic assay that distinguishes likely MPXV infection from orthopoxvirus vaccination. We used a modified Poisson regression to assess associations with likely MPXV infection. We compared participants with serologic evidence of MPXV infection to those self-reporting prior confirmed mpox cases. Of 2,896 participants, 332 (11.5%) were seropositive, including 82 (2.8%) classified as likely MPXV infection. Four participants reported prior confirmed MPXV cases, yielding a 21:1 ratio of participants with serologic evidence of MPXV infection to self-reported confirmed cases. Despite some evidence of undetected transmission, most participants lacked serologic evidence of prior orthopoxvirus exposure, indicating a large susceptible population and supporting additional vaccination and ongoing serosurveillance.

articles.title: Management of Infants Born to Mothers with Q Fever During Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: We conducted a systematic review of published literature from 1953-2021 for cases of infants born to mothers who had Q fever during pregnancy. We describe clinical management characteristics and neonatal outcomes for 11 case reports. No live-born infant had confirmed C. burnetii infection. Placental infection was identified in 4 cases; all infants tested negative. Uncommon adverse obstetric outcomes included preterm birth and low birthweight. There were no cases of transmission through breastmilk. Infection-control precautions ranged from standard to airborne. Evidence indicated that vertical transmission to the fetus or live-born infant is rare. Maternal illness and fetal loss appear related to placental infection. Separation of mother and infant or avoidance of breastfeeding are not supported. Management should prioritize placental handling precautions and structured infant follow-up. No published clinical consensus guidelines exist for management of infants born to mothers with Q fever (Coxiella burnetii) during pregnancy. Global collaboration and evidence gathering can inform evidence-based guidelines.

articles.title: Responsiveness of the CPCHILD Questionnaire to Monitor Changes in HRQoL for Nonambulatory Children With Cerebral Palsy After Hip and Spine Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caregiver Priorities and Child Health Index of Life with Disabilities (CPCHILD) is a health-related quality-of-life questionnaire designed for children with cerebral palsy (CP). It is valid, reliable, and universally adopted; however, studies evaluating its longitudinal validity are lacking. The aim of this study was to evaluate the CPCHILD's responsiveness to change after orthopaedic hip and spine surgery in nonambulatory children with CP.
METHODS: This longitudinal observational responsiveness study used distribution-based methods to evaluate the CPCHILD questionnaire. Caregivers of nonambulatory children with CP completed the questionnaire before and 6-, 12-, 24 months after hip and spine surgery. Responsiveness was quantified using effect size (ES) and standardized response mean with 95% confidence intervals (CI), and measurement precision was assessed using standard error of measurement and minimal detectable change at the 90% confidence level (MDC90).
RESULTS: One hundred forty-one children (mean age 11 years) with CP underwent surgery (95 hip reconstruction surgery/46 spinal fusion surgery). Six months after hip reconstruction, the Personal, Positioning, and Health domains, as well as the Total score demonstrated small or moderate responsiveness (ES, range 0.25-0.57), with up to half of patients exceeding the MDC90 threshold for measurement error. After spinal fusion surgery, the Total score and all domains showed small or moderate responsiveness (ES, range 0.22-0.77), with a larger proportion of patients exceeding the MDC90 compared with hip reconstruction.
CONCLUSIONS: CPCHILD captured meaningful responsiveness in the Personal and Positioning domains, as well as the Total score following hip and spine surgery, while other domains (Comfort and QoL) showed minimal or no detectable change. This suggests that CPCHILD can capture improvements in functional domains, while changes for Comfort and QoL were smaller than expected, and other domains (Communication and Health) not expected to be influenced with surgery, remained stable. Healthcare providers using the CPCHILD to evaluate the effect of surgical procedures on health-related quality of life should be aware of these findings.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

articles.title: In Utero Exposure to Acetazolamide and Pregnancy Outcomes: A Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Data on pregnancy outcomes following acetazolamide exposure remain limited. The main safety issues relate to suspected teratogenic effects, supported by similarities between malformations reported in humans and animals. Other concerns include intrauterine growth restriction, amniotic fluid anomalies, and neonatal electrolyte imbalances. This study aimed to describe pregnancy outcomes and neonatal characteristics following acetazolamide exposure during pregnancy and to assess the association between first-trimester exposure and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study using data from the French national Teratology Information Service (Centre de Référence sur les Agents Tératogènes, CRAT). We included all prospective pregnancies exposed to acetazolamide with a known outcome and an estimated delivery date before 1 January, 2024. The study proceeded in two stages. First, we described pregnancy and neonatal outcomes among all acetazolamide-exposed pregnancies, overall and according to timing of exposure (descriptive analysis). Second, we assessed the association between first-trimester acetazolamide exposure and adverse pregnancy outcomes, using a composite outcome including spontaneous miscarriage, medical termination of pregnancy, stillbirth, and major congenital malformation. We conducted this comparative analysis using a matched unexposed control group (1:4 ratio) randomly selected from the same database after exclusion of known teratogenic exposures and genetic disorders. Conditional logistic regression was used to estimate crude conditional odds ratios.
RESULTS: Between 1988 and 2024, 135 prospective pregnancies were referred to the CRAT: 114 (84.4%) resulted in live births, 8 (5.9%) in miscarriages, 9 (6.7%) in elective terminations, 3 (2.2%) in medical abortions, and 1 (0.7%) in stillbirth. Among 87 first-trimester exposures with documented malformation status, three major congenital malformations unrelated to genetic disorders were identified (3.4%, 95% confidence interval 0.72-9.75). In the comparative analysis, first-trimester acetazolamide exposure was not associated with an adverse pregnancy outcome (crude conditional odds ratio = 1.03, 95% CI 0.51-2.09). Major congenital malformation rates did not differ between exposed (2.6%, 2/78) and unexposed pregnancies (2.8%, 9/327) [crude conditional odds ratio = 1.03, 95% confidence interval 0.21-4.99).
CONCLUSIONS: This study reports the largest cohort of acetazolamide-exposed prospective pregnancies to date and does not identify evidence supporting previous concerns regarding an association with major congenital malformation. However, given the limited sample size, small increases in risk cannot be excluded, and acetazolamide should be used during pregnancy only when no effective alternative exists.

articles.title: Success rate of MRI scanning during natural sleep for younger autistic and typically developing toddlers.
articles.abstract: Toddlerhood represents a critical period of brain development in autism, yet there is limited magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data for children ages 1-3 years. These ages are difficult to scan without sedation because toddlers tend to have difficulty falling asleep in noisy, unfamiliar environments and following instructions to stay still. While some studies have successfully scanned typically-developing toddlers without sedation, fewer have scanned autistic toddlers. The few with high success rates (>90%) are not easily replicated (e.g., flexible scan durations). Recent reviews emphasize a need for gold-standard, feasible scan protocols and detailed reporting of natural-sleep methods. To address these gaps, we examined MRI scan success rates and detailed our scanning procedures. Twenty-two autistic and twenty-three typically-developing toddlers attempted scans during natural, non-sedated sleep in our longitudinal study. Our MRI battery included structural, resting-state functional, and diffusion-weighted scans. The overall scan success rate was 40.3%; autism (36.4%) and non-autism groups (44.1%) did not significantly differ. Among unsuccessful scans, 87.5% resulted from toddlers not falling asleep. Success rates did not significantly differ by factors such as age, timepoint, or developmental functioning. While our success rate aligns with most literature describing difficulty scanning 1-3 year-olds, our rate was lower than the few high-rate, natural-sleep studies of autistic toddlers. We identified differences in procedures and budget as key considerations (e.g., absence of standardized pre-visit measures, inability to scan late in evenings). These differences emphasize the need for standardized procedures to bolster success rates and broaden our understanding of early brain development in autism.

articles.title: Risk factors and substance use consequences from prenatal exposure to early adolescence: A review of findings in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study.
articles.abstract: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study is one of the largest longitudinal studies on adolescent substance use in the United States. To date, publications have focused on antecedents and consequences of early adolescent substance use including factors of mental health, physical health, neurodevelopment, family, environment, and additional factors. In this narrative review, we summarize the 153 publications in ABCD that have focused on or included substance use in analyses up to June 2025. Specifically, we reviewed publications that investigated prenatal substance use exposure, family history of substance use, childhood factors of substance use initiation, and consequences of adolescent substance use exposure within the ABCD study cohort. A summary of findings across all substance use domains are highlighted including brief discussion of limitations and future directions. These publications lay the foundation for the distinct advantage of the ABCD Study dataset in the future. As prevalence and frequency of substance use progresses as the ABCD cohort ages, it is imperative to identify additional predictors of substance use escalation as well as consequences of this heavier use across adolescence.

articles.title: Apixaban reduces hepatic decompensation in patients with cirrhosis (ApiHep): A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evolving data suggest that anticoagulation is safe in cirrhosis and may improve decompensation-free survival in select patients. This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of the direct oral anticoagulant apixaban in patients with cirrhosis.
METHODS: In this open-label randomized controlled trial with blinded endpoint assessment, adult patients (18-60y) with cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B7-C10) without splenoportal axis thrombosis were randomized (1:1) to receive apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) along with standard medical therapy (SMT) or SMT alone for 12 months. The primary outcome was the comparison of the proportion of patients with hepatic decompensation at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included frequency of liver-related events, overall and liver-related mortality, and adverse events (AEs).
RESULTS: One hundred thirty-four patients (mean age 43.4±9.5 y; Child-Pugh B/C:115/19) were randomized (67 Apixaban+SMT and 67 SMT). Patients receiving apixaban experienced significantly lower rates of hepatic decompensation compared with SMT (33.1% vs. 54.3%; absolute risk reduction 21.2% [95% CI: 4.5%-38.2%]; p=0.013). Although rates of ascites (6.4% vs. 17.4%), HE (21.2% vs. 36.0%), and variceal bleeding (7.5% vs. 14.6%) were lower among patients receiving Apixaban+SMT as compared with SMT alone, the differences were not statistically significant. No significant between-group differences in all-cause and liver-related mortality at 1 year were noted. There were no significant between-group differences in AEs (55.2% vs. 53.7%), any bleeding (41.8% vs. 46.3%), and major bleeding (9.0% vs. 11.9%) events.
CONCLUSIONS: Apixaban significantly reduced hepatic decompensation events without increasing hemorrhagic episodes in Child-Pugh B7-C10 cirrhosis (CTRI/2023/09/058018).

articles.title: Understanding the Burden of Influenza in Children and Adolescents in Spain During 9 Seasons (from 2016-2017 to 2024-2025): The INFLUENZE Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Seasonal influenza is a major cause of acute respiratory infections and imposes a significant burden. The Spanish Ministry of Health recommends influenza vaccination for children aged 6-59 months since the 2022/2023 season, although implementation varies across regions. The objective was to describe influenza incidence, complications, and healthcare resource use among < 18 years old in Spain.
METHODS: Observational study using Telotrón® database (> 2.2 million individuals across seven Autonomous Communities in Spain). Population < 18 years with clinical diagnosis of influenza across nine seasons (from 2016-2017 to 2024-2025) were included. Influenza-related complications and healthcare resource utilization were assessed for four seasons (from 2021-2022 to 2024-2025).
RESULTS: Across the study period, the highest influenza incidence was observed among children aged 24-59 months, 5-11 years, and 12-14 years, and 66.7% occurred in children without pre-existing conditions. Around 23% of children with influenza experienced a complication, with the highest burden in those aged 0-23 months and 24-59 months. Antibiotics were prescribed in 14-18% of influenza cases.
CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric influenza represents a substantial public health burden in Spain, suggesting that pediatric influenza vaccination among children and adolescents could contribute to reduce the disease burden.

articles.title: 3D bioprinting of vascularized cardiac constructs reveals improved cardiomyocyte organization and contractile function.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in cardiac tissue engineering, generating constructs that simultaneously achieve vascularization and organized cardiomyocyte function remains a major challenge.
METHODS: In this study, three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting was used to fabricate human umbilical vein endothelial cell (HUVEC)-laden alginate/gelatin constructs with defined architectures designed to mimic myocardial alignment. Constructs were cultured with vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) under static conditions followed by short-term dynamic stimulation in a bioreactor. Cardiomyocytes - H9c2 cells, neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs), or human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) - were subsequently seeded onto the constructs. Vascularization and the distribution of cells were assessed using immunofluorescence, and functional activity of cardiomyocytes was evaluated by calcium transient imaging.
RESULTS: Bioprinted constructs developed interconnected CD31-positive endothelial networks in response to growth factor supplementation and dynamic culture, whereas control constructs cultured without growth factors or bioreactor exposure showed limited vascular organization. Cardiomyocytes seeded onto vascularized constructs exhibited improved structural organization, including increased alignment and integration with endothelial networks. Functional assessment revealed more synchronized and rhythmic calcium transients compared to non-vascularized constructs.
CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that combining 3D bioprinting with controlled architectural design and endothelial network formation enhances cardiomyocyte organization and function. These findings highlight the critical role of vascular-like networks in improving the performance of engineered cardiac tissues.

articles.title: Multidimensional analysis of the pathological mechanisms of infantile hemangioma: metabolic reprogramming, immune remodeling, and programmed cell death.
articles.abstract: Infantile hemangioma (IH) is a common benign vascular tumor of infancy. Its self-limiting course, which progresses from proliferation to involution, involves aberrant angiogenesis, altered cell fate, and remodeling of the lesional microenvironment. Hypoxia/HIF-VEGF, PI3K/AKT, MAPK/ERK, and Notch signaling pathways contribute to vascular formation and cellular differentiation. During the proliferative phase, hemangioma endothelial cells (HemECs) undergo metabolic reprogramming characterized by enhanced glycolysis and altered amino acid metabolism, including pathways involving glutamine, arginine, glycine, and serine. Macrophages, mast cells, T cells, and their associated cytokines also shape a proangiogenic immune microenvironment. During the involuting phase, the transition of hemangioma stem cells (HemSCs) toward an adipogenic fate, together with changes in lesional cell composition, contributes to fibrofatty tissue remodeling. At the same time, the immune microenvironment undergoes stage-dependent remodeling, and processes related to programmed cell death, including apoptosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, and autophagy, change accordingly. However, the strength of evidence supporting these processes in IH varies. Current studies have identified specific links among metabolism, immunity, and cell death, but they have not established a fixed, sequential causal cascade; PANoptosis remains an unverified mechanistic hypothesis in IH. Although propranolol is the first-line treatment, variable treatment responses, rebound growth after treatment withdrawal, and refractory lesions remain clinical challenges. Focusing on the transition from proliferation to involution, this review integrates current evidence and potential mechanistic connections to inform research on spontaneous involution and the development of interventions tailored to specific disease stages and cell types.

articles.title: Sulodexide versus low-molecular-weight heparin in critically ill neonates: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Critically ill neonates are at high risk of thrombosis, inflammation, and antimicrobial exposure in the neonatal intensive care unit, but evidence guiding adjunctive anticoagulant selection remains limited. We compared the clinical, laboratory, and safety outcomes associated with sulodexide (SDX) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH).
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included critically ill neonates treated with sulodexide or low-molecular-weight heparin. Propensity score matching (PSM) yielded 85 matched pairs. The primary outcome was relative percentage change in D-dimer from baseline to treatment end. Secondary outcomes included other coagulation, hematological, blood-gas, and respiratory-support measures. Inflammatory status and antimicrobial defined daily doses (DDDs) were exploratory outcomes. Bleeding events first documented after treatment initiation were assessed as safety outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 234 eligible neonates, 85 matched pairs were analyzed. D-dimer change did not differ significantly between groups [-70.2% (-82.0, -50.5) vs. -72.0% (-87.1, -42.2); between-group effect, 1.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -8.3 to 9.7; P = 0.765], and no other coagulation, hematological, or blood-gas outcomes differed significantly. Among neonates with abnormal baseline inflammatory status, CRP/hs-CRP improvement occurred in 12/12 (100.0%) and 7/11 (63.6%) in the SDX and LMWH groups, respectively (P = 0.037), suggesting a potential difference in inflammatory response. SDX remained associated with lower observed DDDs after multivariable adjustment, although this association was not robust in calendar-period sensitivity analyses. Bleeding was first documented after treatment initiation in 24/85 (28.2%) SDX-treated and 18/85 (21.2%) LMWH-treated neonates, respectively. Among neonates with bleeding, first documentation occurred during active treatment in 9/24 (37.5%) and 14/18 (77.8%), respectively.
CONCLUSION: No significant between-group differences were observed in the primary D-dimer or other coagulation outcomes. A higher proportion of CRP/hs-CRP improvement was observed in the SDX group, although this finding was exploratory and based on a small subgroup. The lower observed DDDs were not robust to calendar-period analyses and should not be attributed to a drug-specific effect. Bleeding was numerically more frequent in the SDX group overall, whereas a greater proportion of bleeding cases in the LMWH group were first documented during active treatment. The observed timing pattern does not establish a causal relationship with treatment. These retrospective findings require cautious interpretation and prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Human amniotic mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes alleviate cerebral Palsy-Associated neuronal damage via TSC1/mTOR/ULK1 autophagy suppression and PINK1/Parkin mitophagy restoration.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral palsy (CP) from perinatal hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury lacks effective therapies. Human amniotic mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (hAMSC-exos) show neuroprotective potential, but their mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the effects and molecular pathways of hAMSC-exos in a neonatal rat CP model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) neuronal model.
METHODS: hAMSC-exos were isolated and characterised. Severe CP was induced in postnatal day 21 rats by carotid ligation and hypoxia; hAMSC-exos or vehicle were given via tail vein 24 h later. Brain histology, ultrastructure, TSC1/mTOR/ULK1 pathway proteins, and apoptosis were assessed. In vitro, cortical neurons underwent OGD/R with or without exosomes; mitochondrial function (ATP, ROS, membrane potential), morphology, dynamics proteins (DRP1, FIS1, MFN1, MFN2), and PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy were evaluated.
RESULTS: hAMSC-exos significantly ameliorated cortical neuronal degeneration, Nissl loss, and mitochondrial ultrastructural damage, and reduced autophagosome accumulation. They reversed CP-induced TSC1 upregulation, restored mTOR phosphorylation, and decreased ULK1 phosphorylation, correlating with fewer apoptotic neurons. In vitro, exosomes restored ATP content, reduced mitochondrial ROS, and normalised membrane potential. OGD/R caused excessive mitochondrial elongation via MFN1 upregulation; exosomes selectively downregulated MFN1 without affecting fission proteins (DRP1, FIS1). Moreover, exosomes restored impaired PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, increasing co-localisation of phospho-PINK1, phospho-Parkin, and LAMP1 with mitochondria, and rescued their phosphorylated protein levels.
CONCLUSION: hAMSC-exos protect against hypoxic-ischaemic injury through coordinated regulation of mitochondrial quality control, involving suppression of excessive TSC1/mTOR/ULK1-mediated autophagy (in vivo) and restoration of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy (in vitro), collectively preserving mitochondrial integrity and reducing neuronal apoptosis. These findings support hAMSC-exos as a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy for CP.

articles.title: Endpoint design in pulmonary arterial hypertension therapeutic trials permitting pediatric enrollment: a ClinicalTrials.gov registry analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric therapeutic development depends not only on age-appropriate dosing but also on endpoints whose administration and interpretation remain coherent across developmental stages.
METHODS: An expanded ClinicalTrials.gov search was performed on 2 October 2026 using pulmonary hypertension terms plus the structured Child age filter (birth-17 years), while restricting eligibility to records first posted on or before 8 August 2026. The combined inventory contained 394 unique records. Seventy-two records formed the main analysis set; 69 were assigned to 57 traceable trial families and three continuation records remained unassigned at family level. Endpoint domains were counted once per family.
RESULTS: Fifty-two families had registered outcomes available for domain analysis (42 first posted before 2017 and 10 in 2017-2026). Biomarker/laboratory measures occurred in 12/42 versus 9/10 families and functional capacity/activity in 38/42 versus 6/10. The study-level registered maximum permitted age was 18 years or younger in 14/42 earlier and 9/10 later families; this was used only for an age-scope sensitivity stratum and was not an eligibility criterion. In this age-scope stratum, several era contrasts attenuated, including PK/PD/dosing (9/14 vs. 7/9; difference +13.5 percentage points, 95% CI -24.4 to +43.6). A core-primary sensitivity analysis excluding four families whose registry records were updated after the eligibility cutoff produced the same qualitative pattern of no recent functional primary entries and wider uncertainty in the smaller later-era group. Five families with completely missing outcome modules were all in the earlier era; extreme-case analyses are reported in the supplement.
CONCLUSION: Endpoint portfolios differed across registration eras, but age-scope composition, differential missingness, and incomplete historical registry reconstruction limit a temporal interpretation. Public endpoint descriptions should specify the clinical construct, measurement method, reporter or data source, capability rule, and handling of children unable to complete an assessment.

articles.title: Real-world pharmacovigilance analysis of adverse events associated with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor antidepressants in children and adolescents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depressive disorders are common in children and adolescents, with major depression affecting 3.7% of youth and subclinical symptoms affecting over one-fifth. Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), including fluoxetine, sertraline, and fluvoxamine, are prescribed for moderate-to-severe pediatric depression. However, real-world safety signals for specific SSRIs remain incompletely characterized because evidence derives mainly from randomized controlled trials with restrictive inclusion criteria, observational studies affected by prescribing bias, and spontaneous reporting systems without reliable exposure denominators.
METHODS: We extracted reports from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System through the second quarter of 2026 for depressed children and adolescents aged 6-18 years receiving fluoxetine, sertraline, or fluvoxamine. Disproportionality analyses used reporting odds ratio, proportional reporting ratio, Bayesian confidence propagation neural network, and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker to detect signals at system organ class and preferred term levels. Weibull models assessed time to onset, and network toxicology approaches explored candidate targets and pathways underlying the shared rhabdomyolysis signal.
RESULTS: A total of 2,614 reports were included: 1,260 for fluoxetine, 1,278 for sertraline, and 76 for fluvoxamine. Psychiatric and nervous system disorders were the most frequently reported system organ classes for all three drugs. Fluoxetine showed prominent signals for serotonin syndrome, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, rhabdomyolysis, blood creatine phosphokinase increase, and acute kidney injury; sertraline showed strong signals for serotonin syndrome, urinary retention, intentional self-injury, rhabdomyolysis, hepatocellular injury, and respiratory failure. Rhabdomyolysis was reported in 39 fluoxetine cases (ROR = 4.26, 95% CI: 2.81-6.45) and 26 sertraline cases (ROR = 2.69, 95% CI: 1.71-4.24). Time-to-onset analyses revealed an early-failure Weibull pattern for both drugs, with median onsets of 24 and 30 days, respectively. Network toxicology analysis identified shared candidate targets including CYP3A4, CYP2D6, SLC6A4, MAOA, DRD1, DRD2, NOS2, and KCNH2, with enrichment in serotonergic synapse, oxidative stress, and hypoxia response pathways.
CONCLUSION: This study provides evidence to prioritize symptoms, organ systems, and high-risk monitoring windows in pediatric SSRI prescribing. It offers the first systematic report of SSRI-associated rhabdomyolysis in children and adolescents and translates real-world pharmacovigilance signals into guidance for baseline risk assessment, early monitoring, family education, and symptom-driven laboratory testing.

articles.title: Early food introduction and skin intervention in the prevention of food allergy in young children (PreventADALL): 7-year follow-up of a factorial, multicentre, cluster-randomised trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In our previous study, early food introduction prevented food allergy, whereas skin intervention alone did not prevent atopic dermatitis at age 3 years. In this follow-up study, we aimed to determine the effect of food and skin interventions on food allergy, allergic sensitisation, atopic dermatitis, food avoidance diets, and BMI at age 7 years.
METHODS: We conducted a 7-year follow-up study of 2394 children from Norway and Sweden antenatally included (between Dec 9, 2014, and Oct 31, 2016) in the ongoing, general-population-based Preventing Atopic Dermatitis and ALLergies in children (PreventADALL) study. Children were randomly assigned at study site hospitals at birth (1:1:1:1) into the 2×2 factorially designed cluster-randomised controlled trial to no intervention (n=597), skin intervention (n=575; oil baths and facial cream from age 2 weeks to 9 months a minimum of four times weekly), food intervention (n=642; tastes of peanut, cow's milk, wheat, and egg a minimum of four times weekly from ages 3-6 months), or both interventions combined (n=583). The primary outcome at the 7-year follow-up was allergy to any of the interventional foods, as diagnosed by an expert panel following international guidelines. Secondary outcomes were allergy to the individual interventional foods, allergy to non-interventional foods, allergic sensitisation by skin prick test and serum-IgE, atopic dermatitis by validated diagnostic criteria, food avoidance diets through interview, and BMI. Study personnel performing clinical assessments and all researchers involved in data analysis were masked to group allocation, except for the data manager for some parts of the analysis. Mixed logistic regression with best case imputation (of no atopic disease) was used to estimate risk differences. The trial is registered on clinicaltrials.gov (NCT02449850) and is closed for recruitment.
FINDINGS: At the 7-year follow-up, the risk of food allergy to interventional foods (38 [1·6%] of 2394) was similar in the no food intervention (21 [1·8%] of 1170) versus food intervention groups (17 [1·4%] of 1224; risk difference -0·4% [95% CI -1·4 to 0·6]). Any food allergy was diagnosed in 76 (3·2%) of 2394 children, similar across the intervention groups. Allergic sensitisation to interventional foods at 7 years was lower in the food intervention (67 [9·9%] of 680) versus no food intervention groups (95 [15·6%] of 610; -5·7% [-9·3 to -2·1]). Atopic dermatitis was less frequent in the combined intervention group (17·3%) than in the controls (25·2%; -7·8% [-12·5 to -3·2]). Food avoidance diets and BMI were similar across the intervention groups.
INTERPRETATION: Early short-term food intervention was insufficient for sustained food allergy prevention by age 7 years, despite reduced allergic sensitisation, suggesting that continued allergen exposure might be needed for long-term prevention. Combined food and skin interventions reduced atopic dermatitis at 7 years.
FUNDING: For a full list of funders, see Acknowledgments.

articles.title: Receptor specificity and glycocalyx accessibility shape bovine P[1] and P[11] rotavirus infection.
articles.abstract: Viruses initiate infection by engaging receptors within the crowded cell-surface glycocalyx; however, how this environment affects receptor accessibility remains poorly understood. Here, we compared two bovine rotavirus field isolates, P[1] C73 and P[11] HM26, which differ markedly in replication efficiency and early disease kinetics, to examine how VP4-mediated receptor use contributes to these phenotypes. Reverse-genetics experiments identified VP4, particularly its VP8* lectin domain, as a major determinant of the replication difference. C73 recognized sialylated gangliosides, whereas HM26 bound type II precursor glycans. Although HM26 VP8* displayed higher intrinsic affinity for its type II glycan ligand, it bound less efficiently to intact cell surfaces and was associated with lower viral attachment. Neuraminidase treatment increased the detectable accessibility of type II glycans, reduced P[1] infection, and enhanced P[11] infection. Structural modeling and mutational analysis further supported a role for VP8* residue 188 in the glycan-binding phenotype. The Y188T substitution reduced detectable glycan binding, impaired replication in the rBLR/C73VP4 background, and attenuated early infection in neonatal mice. Analysis of human P[1] and P[11] VP8* proteins also revealed an association between the Y/T188 polymorphism and glycan preference in the strains examined. Together, these results indicate that intrinsic VP8* glycan-binding affinity alone does not predict effective receptor use at the intact cell surface. Receptor accessibility within the glycocalyx also contributes to bovine rotavirus attachment and infection.IMPORTANCERotavirus infection begins with specific glycan recognition on the host cell surface; however, receptor presence alone is insufficient to guarantee productive viral engagement. Comparing bovine P[1] and P[11] rotaviruses with distinct glycan preferences reveals that receptor accessibility within the glycocalyx critically dictates viral attachment and subsequent infection. Notably, higher affinity for an isolated glycan fails to confer superior binding efficiency on intact cells. These results demonstrate that the glycocalyx acts as a functional barrier and modulator at the virus-cell interface rather than an inert receptor scaffold, underscoring the role of spatial glycan organization in governing viral entry.

articles.title: Japanese encephalitis virus infection reshapes the gut microbiome and induces colonic inflammation in neonatal mice.
articles.abstract: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), a neurotropic flavivirus, predominantly causes severe infection in children, leading to neuropsychiatric complications. Given that the juvenile period is a transitional window for the gut microbiota to develop into a stable community profile, any alterations to the microbiota during infections can result in chronic inflammation. Therefore, we investigated changes in the gut microbiota of neonatal mice during the early and late stages of JEV infection. Postnatal day 10, BALB/c mice challenged with JEV succumbed to acute infection at 6 to 7 days post-infection. This severity was marked by a surge in systemic pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-6, and MCP-1) and reduced food intake. Fecal 16S rRNA V3-V4 sequencing revealed distinct β-diversity between mock and JEV-infected groups, with the dominant phyla being Firmicutes, Bacteroidota, and Proteobacteria. The relative abundance of these phyla shifted, with Firmicutes decreasing from ~63.7% (control) to ~39% (JEV), whereas Proteobacteria remained unchanged in JEV. The Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio decreased in JEV, along with a reduction in Lactobacillus. Simultaneously, altered mucosal secretion, reduced tight-junction protein ZO-1, increased pNF-κB, and cleaved caspase-3 together indicated colonic inflammation. Prediction of microbial pathways using PICRUSt2 suggested a reduction in specific pathways associated with beneficial secondary metabolites and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in JEV. Intragastric administration of the SCFA cocktail prolonged survival and delayed the onset of clinical signs and the inflammatory response. Our findings suggest that systemic inflammation and reduced feeding during an acute infection could result in colonic dysbiosis, reduced beneficial bacteria, and trigger inflammation. SCFAs displayed a transient therapeutic effect in JEV infection, highlighting the potential of gut microbiota modulation to manage acute viral infection.IMPORTANCEJapanese encephalitis remains a leading cause of viral encephalitis in children across the Asia-Pacific region, with new outbreaks driven by evolving demographic factors. The need for targeted therapies beyond existing supportive care underscores the need for new host-directed interventions. Our findings suggest that gut-brain axis interactions may play a role in acute viral infections, potentially amplifying disease severity through infection-driven reduction in feeding, increased cytokine production, and shifts in the gut microbiome. We propose that SCFA supplementation can serve as a microbiota-modulating strategy that offers a safe, translatable approach to managing inflammation and JEV outcomes in pediatric viral encephalitis. This could be utilized as a supplement along with supportive care in other flavivirus infections.

articles.title: Experiences from a structured single-centre transition program for patients with Type 1 diabetes in Italy: a longitudinal sex-stratified analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transition from paediatric to adult care represents a critical phase for individuals with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D), often associated with suboptimal glycaemic control and loss to follow-up. Structured transition programs may mitigate these risks, yet longitudinal data from real-world settings are limited, particularly regarding sex-specific differences. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of a structured, single-centre transition program in Italy.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, longitudinal, observational study on 187 patients (108 males and 79 females) with T1D transitioning from the Paediatric Unit to the Adult Endocrinology and Prevention and Care of Diabetes Unit at IRCCS Sant'Orsola University Hospital, Bologna, between June 2017 and June 2025. The transition protocol included a joint paediatric-adult visit, shared electronic records, and subsequent structured follow-up every 4-6 months. We collected demographic, anthropometric and clinical parameters at the baseline joint visit and during follow-up. We evaluated the HbA1c slope after transition for those who had at least 3 follow-up visits: worsened HbA1c was defined when the slope was > 0.5. A validated satisfaction questionnaire was administered after 12 ± 3 months of follow-up.
RESULTS: Mean age at transition was 20 ± 2 years. Females more frequently used insulin pumps at baseline (53% vs. 30%, P = 0.036) and had higher prevalence of autoimmune diseases. Only 10% (n = 19) were lost to follow-up, without sex-related differences (P = 0.990). Seven of these 19 patients moved to other regions/abroad for personal reasons. Patient-reported satisfaction with the new diabetology team was moderate (31%) to high (61%), but 52% of women vs. 30% of men declared to have been fairly or very worried about transition (P = 0.018) and 28% of women (vs. 11% of men) considered themselves minimally or not at all prepared (P = 0.018). At 12 months (n = 141), we observed a stability of HbA1c levels (58.0 ± 12.2 vs. 58.7 ± 12.5 mmol/mol, P = 0.414), confirmed in both sexes; HbA1c levels remained stable also at the end of follow-up (n = 126; P = 0.122). HbA1c at joint visit was the only significant predictor of HbA1c worsening after transition, with a lower risk for higher baseline levels (OR 0.96 [95% CI 0.93-0.99] for 1 mmol/mol increase; P = 0.021).
CONCLUSION: In a structured transition program, we observed stable glycaemic control, low loss to follow-up, and high patient satisfaction. One third of losses was due to causes unrelated to diabetes. Women expressed more concern about transition and less preparedness but showed comparable glycaemic control over time.

articles.title: Association of adverse perinatal outcomes of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy with maternal serum bile acid profiles.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is associated with increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, yet current monitoring lacks predictive accuracy. This study aimed to explore alterations in serum bile acid profiles and their relationship with adverse perinatal outcomes in ICP.
METHODS: This study enrolled 149 pregnant women, including 77 normal pregnant women and 72 cases with ICP, subdivided into ICP with adverse perinatal outcomes and those without according to the perinatal outcomes. Serum concentrations of 15 bile acids were quantified using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry and compared among the three groups.
RESULTS: ICP patients exhibited significantly lower gestational age at delivery, Apgar scores, and birth weight, alongside higher rates of cesarean delivery, low birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit admission, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and preterm birth (all p < 0.05). Twelve bile acids were significantly elevated in ICP (all p < 0.01); notably, taurolithocholic acid elevation was exclusive to the ICP with adverse perinatal outcomes. Glycocholic acid (GCA), glycochenodeoxycholic acid (GCDCA), taurocholic acid (TCA), taurochenodeoxycholic acid (TCDCA), tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA), and total bile acid levels positively correlated with adverse perinatal outcomes (all p < 0.05). The combined indicator of these six indicators demonstrated superior predictive efficacy for adverse perinatal outcomes with an area under the curve of 0.836, sensitivity of 73.0%, and specificity of 82.9%.
CONCLUSIONS: Distinct serum bile acid metabolic signatures characterize ICP patients with adverse perinatal outcomes. Elevated levels of total bile acids and conjugated bile acids, including GCA, GCDCA, TCA, TCDCA, and TUDCA, were associated with adverse perinatal outcomes and might serve as candidate biomarkers for risk prediction. The multi-bile acid combined indicator demonstrated superior exploratory predictive performance over individual markers, offering a potential tool for identifying high-risk ICP patients, which requires prospective external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Divided oral versus single-dose intravenous etoposide for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with comorbidity: lower early hematologic toxicity with preserved 2-week response.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Etoposide is a backbone of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) treatment. But most adults suffering from HLH have comorbidity that limits the use of intravenous etoposide.
OBJECTIVE: We conducted a retrospective study to compare the efficacy and safety of divided oral versus single-dose intravenous etoposide within the DEP regimen (liposomal doxorubicin, etoposide, methylprednisolone) in HLH.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a cohort of 57 patients (28 oral, 29 intravenous), including 13 patients under 18 years (six oral, seven intravenous). Week-2 overall response was the efficacy endpoint. The safety endpoint was any grade III-IV hematologic event at the worst grade recorded within 14 days after treatment.
RESULTS: Patients with comorbidity were enrolled in both groups: 24/28 (85.7%) in the oral and 20/29 (69.0%) in the IV group. Week-2 overall response was 96.4% vs 89.7%, respectively. Grade III-IV hematologic events occurred in 5/28 (17.9%) oral and 16/29 (55.2%) IV group (p = 0.006). This association persisted after adjustment for lymphoma-associated HLH, age, performance status, comorbidity, LDH, AST, platelet and creatinine (odds ratios 0.13 to 0.19; all p ≤ 0.008). In the 44 patients with comorbidity, grade III-IV hematologic events were far less frequent (16.7% vs 65.0%; odds ratio 0.11; 95% confidence interval 0.03 to 0.44; p = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: Compared to single-dose etoposide, divided oral dosing was associated with fewer grade III-IV hematologic events in comorbid HLH. However, if true absorption is much lower than 50% in critically ill patients, the apparent reduction in hematologic toxicity would in part reflect the lower dose administered rather than the route of administration. Further randomized pharmacokinetic studies are warranted.

articles.title: PDE4B inhibition attenuates intestinal inflammation with reducing glycolysis in macrophages.
articles.abstract: Accumulating evidence underscores that PDE4B expression is significantly upregulated in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). However, its therapeutic potential and the underlying molecular mechanisms in pediatric IBD remain poorly defined. In this study, multiple public datasets were analyzed to characterize PDE4B expression in pediatric IBD. This was followed by therapeutic evaluation in mice colitis models to validate the efficacy of PDE4B inhibition in vivo. Analysis of public datasets revealed a marked elevation of PDE4B in pediatric IBD cohorts. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that a PDE4B inhibitor effectively suppressed LPS-induced inflammatory responses in primary blood samples from pediatric patients. In murine models, pharmacological inhibition of PDE4B significantly attenuated intestinal inflammation in both DSS- and LPS-induced colitis models. Furthermore, treatment with the PDE4B inhibitor successfully alleviated established chronic mucosal injury and preserved goblet cell integrity in spontaneous Il10-/- mice. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene sequencing demonstrated that PDE4B inhibition was associated with a partial restoration of gut microbiota diversity and a reduction in specific bacterial dysbiosis. At the molecular level, the inhibitor promoted the activation of the anti-inflammatory mediator p-CREB while concurrently abrogating pro-inflammatory p-STAT3 signaling. Notably, the suppression of pathological glycolysis by the inhibitor was closely accompanied by the metabolic reprogramming and enhanced anti-inflammatory function. In conclusion, these findings suggest that targeting PDE4B represents a potential therapeutic approach for pediatric IBD by modulating macrophage immunometabolism and restoring intestinal homeostasis.

articles.title: Cross-sectional analysis of the association between exclusive breastfeeding duration and Autism Spectrum Disorder odds in U.S. preschool children: a nationally representative study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between breastfeeding and Autism Spectrum Disorder remains unclear, with existing evidence showing inconsistency. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between breastfeeding patterns and ASD in a national sample of preschool children.
METHODS: Data from the 2018-2023 National Survey of Children's Health (N = 48,158) were analyzed. Breastfeeding was categorized into four mutually exclusive groups based on official NSCH methodology: never breastfed, breastfed < 6 months, breastfed ≥ 6 months non-exclusively, and exclusively breastfed for 6 months. Multivariable weighted logistic regression models examined the association between breastfeeding patterns and ASD, adjusting for confounders. Dose-response was evaluated by modeling breastfeeding category as an ordinal variable (0-3) in fully adjusted models, with polynomial contrasts assessing linearity of trends. Subgroup analyses stratified by age, sex, race/ethnicity, parental education, household size, poverty level, low birth weight, and preterm status tested effect heterogeneity via likelihood ratio tests. Robustness to unmeasured confounding was quantified using E-values for the primary exposure-outcome association.
RESULTS: The weighted prevalence of ASD was 3.0%. Compared to never breastfeeding, exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months was associated with significantly lower ASD odds in fully adjusted models (OR = 0.61, 95% CI:0.44-0.86). A significant linear trend was observed, with ASD odds decreasing by 16% for each increase in breastfeeding category (OR = 0.84, 95% CI: 0.76-0.93). Polynomial contrasts further indicated the steepest reduction in odds occurred at the transition to exclusive breastfeeding. Subgroup analyses revealed significant effect modification (P for interaction < 0.05) and stronger inverse associations with lower ASD odds among 3-year-olds, non-Hispanic White children, children of college-educated parents, and those from single-child households.
CONCLUSION: Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months was associated with lower odds of ASD in U.S. preschool children, with a graded inverse association across increasing breastfeeding exposure categories. This association was modified by sociodemographic and biological factors, underscoring the importance of contextualizing feeding practices within broader family and social environments in neurodevelopmental research.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Breastfeeding outcomes after postpartum haemorrhage: a socio-ecological secondary analysis of the WOMAN trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breastfeeding has been recognised as a significant driver of neonatal and infant outcomes, particularly in Low- and Middle-income Country (LMIC) settings. Postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) is an increasingly common complication of childbirth, with multiple effects on mothers and their babies. This study aimed to explore the association between aspects of PPH care and outcomes, as they relate to the Socio-Ecological Model of Health for breastfeeding, and the rates of breastfeeding among this cohort of women.
METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of data from the WOMAN trial. The WOMAN trial was a randomised, controlled, pharmaceutical trial in 193 hospitals across 21 countries between 2010 and 2016. A binary logistic regression model was developed to examine the associations between the status of clinical and psycho-social factors from the individual and organisational levels of the Socio-Ecological Model of Health for breastfeeding and the rates of any breastfeeding during the study period.
RESULTS: 16,285 mothers of healthy singleton babies were included in the current study. Factors that may result in maternal-infant separation in the immediate postpartum period were associated with lower rates of any breastfeeding in the study period. These included: the mother requiring transfer between hospitals following PPH (Odds Ratio 0.47 [95%CI 0.41-0.54]) and the mother being admitted to ICU postpartum (OR 0.65 [95%CI 0.54-0.78]). Maternal pain (OR 0.65 [95%CI 0.58-0.75]) and maternal anxiety or depression (OR 0.63 [95% CI 0.53-0.75]) were also associated with lower rates of breastfeeding.
CONCLUSIONS: Some women who experience PPH are at increased risk of not initiating breastfeeding, particularly if there is maternal-infant separation. Organisational factors such as hospital transfer and ICU admission were strongly associated with reduced breastfeeding rates. Individual psycho-social and physical challenges, including pain and psychological distress, further compound these difficulties. Identifying women at higher risk of breastfeeding disruption following PPH could allow targeted support and interventions. Within emergency obstetric care there is a need for universal implementation of breastfeeding-friendly practices, informed by multi-disciplinary, evidence-informed guidelines.

articles.title: Understanding and participation in genetics research among Nigerian mothers of children with orofacial cleft: a qualitative study of prior genetic study participants.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study sought to identify strategies to increase the level of participation of orofacial cleft (OFC) caregivers in craniofacial genetics research as well as assess their understanding of genomics research and secondary findings (SF).
METHODS: This was a qualitative study. After obtaining informed consent, we conducted four focus groups with an average of 7 participants per group. The study participants (females) were 28 caregivers of children with non-syndromic OFC attending the multidisciplinary outpatient orofacial cleft clinic of a tertiary health facility in Lagos, Nigeria. Caregivers were purposively recruited, and data were analyzed through thematic analysis.
RESULTS: The key findings in this study are (a) voluntary participation in past genetic studies, (b) ongoing interest in participation in genetics research, (c) request for accessibility and explanation of genetic research results, (d) limited general knowledge of genetics and genetic testing and (f) a relatively low understanding of secondary findings.
CONCLUSION: The participant's responses highlighted the need for use of simple and relatable language in OFC- related study information documents, including the informed consent form. There was a strong desire to have results returned, including SF among interviewees. However, there is need for increased participant education on the concept of SF. Importantly, there is a need to bridge the gap in workforce and health care provider education to provide genetic counseling services in resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: Deep learning-based classification of dental caries from intraoral photographs using ICDAS criteria.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Dental caries remains a major global health burden, yet current artificial intelligence tools are often constrained by limited classification systems or rely on specialized imaging equipment unsuitable for self-examination. This study aims to develop and validate a deep learning-based approach using intraoral photographs to detect and classify dental caries using the full International Caries Detection and Assessment System (ICDAS) alongside modified ICDAS, merged ICDAS, and binary classification schemes.
METHODS: ICDAS scores were assigned through direct clinical examination. Two annotators independently examined each patient and compared their results. Disagreements were first resolved by joint re-examination. If consensus could not be reached, a third senior clinician examined the patient and made the final determination. A dataset of 1606 intraoral photographs was collected from volunteers aged five years and older across multiple clinics in China. The dataset was split into training, validation, and test sets at an 8:1:1 ratio at the patient level. The YOLOv12x and YOLOv8x architectures were trained and tested, with performance evaluated in terms of precision, recall, and mean average precision at 50% IoU (mAP50) with 95% confidence intervals. Gaussian blur was systematically applied to the test set at seven σ levels (0 to 11) to evaluate robustness.
RESULTS: YOLOv12x significantly outperformed YOLOv8x in full ICDAS (mAP50 0.762 [0.755-0.769] vs. 0.736 [0.733-0.740]; F1 0.715 ± 0.013 vs. 0.693 ± 0.007; p < 0.0001), modified ICDAS (mAP50 0.785 [0.780-0.790] vs. 0.764 [0.759-0.770]; F1 0.731 ± 0.011 vs. 0.718 ± 0.011; p < 0.0001), and merged ICDAS (mAP50 0.897 [0.893-0.901] vs. 0.888 [0.885-0.891]; F1 0.835 ± 0.007 vs. 0.821 ± 0.007; p = 0.0012) schemes, but not in the binary task (mAP50 0.938 [0.935-0.941] vs. 0.937 [0.935-0.940]; F1 0.885 ± 0.003 vs. 0.888 ± 0.007; p = 0.7807). Codes 0 and 6 achieved the highest accuracy, whereas codes 2-5 showed frequent adjacent-stage confusion, particularly between codes 3 and 4. Under Gaussian blur, mAP50 declined from 0.776 to 0.498 at σ = 11, with extreme classes proving most resilient. Metallic restorations and implants were often misclassified as advanced caries.
CONCLUSION: The attention mechanism in YOLOv12x improves fine-grained ICDAS classification but does not help in binary detection, where both models approach ceiling performance. Discriminating adjacent early-stage lesions is substantially harder than detecting caries. The model is better suited to screening and triage than to standalone diagnosis. Future work should incorporate data from additional regions and imaging equipment, and validate performance in uncurated clinical settings.

articles.title: Differences in self-reported orofacial pain and daily activities between children surveyed in metropolitan and provincial areas of Japan: a school-based cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orofacial pain (OFP) in children may be associated with daily activities and psychological factors; however, these characteristics may vary across geographical settings. Evidence regarding geographical differences in OFP and related daily activities among Japanese children remains limited. This study aimed to compare self-reported OFP characteristics, daily activities, and trait anxiety between children surveyed in one metropolitan area and one provincial area in Japan.
METHODS: This school-based cross-sectional survey included 923 children aged 11-12 years from selected elementary schools in a metropolitan area (MA; n = 480) and a provincial area (PA; n = 443). Data were collected in 2011-2012. Participants self-reported TMD-related symptoms, headache, neck pain, and toothache. Daily activities were assessed using a 15-item questionnaire and trait anxiety using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory for Children-Trait (STAIC-T). Group differences were examined using t-tests, chi-square or exact tests. Associations with headache and neck pain were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Geographical area × daily-activity interactions were tested in the pooled sample with false discovery rate (FDR) correction.
RESULTS: Age, sex distribution, STAIC-T scores, and the prevalence of self-reported TMD symptoms and toothache did not differ significantly between the geographical samples. Headache and neck pain were reported more frequently in the MA sample than in the PA sample (p = 0.035 and p = 0.002, respectively). Several daily activities were associated with headache and/or neck pain in area-stratified multivariable analyses. In formal interaction analyses, only the association between use of a high pillow and headache differed significantly between the geographical samples after FDR correction; no daily-activity interaction for neck pain remained significant after FDR correction.
CONCLUSIONS: Children surveyed in the metropolitan area reported headache and neck pain more frequently than those surveyed in the provincial area. Several self-reported daily activities were associated with headache and/or neck pain, although these associations should not be interpreted as causal or necessarily specific to either geographical area. Given the cross-sectional design, reliance on self-reported measures, and sampling from selected geographical areas, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in contemporary longitudinal studies.

articles.title: The range of M-shaped zygomatic arch fractures: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The M-shaped zygomatic arch fracture consists of anterior and posterior segments, presenting an M-shaped configuration when viewed from the skull base. However, the extent of involvement of the anterior and posterior fracture segments has not been reported. This study aims to define the range of M-shaped zygomatic arch fractures.
METHODS: Forty-six patients were enrolled in this study. Clinical data along with CT images were collected from the patients. Landmarks were identified on coronal CT sections using the horizontal plane at the zygomatic arch root as the reference plane.
RESULTS: The deepest point of the fracture depression was located at the zygomaticotemporal suture in 91.30% of cases. In 97.83% of patients, the posterior fracture line was situated anterior to the articular eminence of the temporomandibular joint. The superior extent of the anterior fracture line could reach the zygomaticofrontal suture, its inferior extent extended to the zygomaticoalveolar crest, and its anterior limit reached the lateral orbital wall. The anterior fracture line can be classified into five types. When the coronoid process was above the fracture's deepest point, mouth opening (1.58 ± 0.80 cm) was significantly less than when it was below (2.59 ± 0.99 cm) (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In typical M-shaped zygomatic arch fractures, the location of the deepest depression point and the posterior fracture line remains relatively constant while the anterior fracture line varies in its course and position. The spatial relationship between the deepest point and the coronoid process determines the degree of mouth opening.

articles.title: Ingredient composition and toxicological assessment of commercially available pediatric remineralizing dental gels: a cross-sectional market survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remineralizing dental gels are widely used in pediatric dentistry for the management of early enamel lesions and white spot lesions. Considering the increased likelihood of accidental ingestion in children, evaluation of the ingredient composition and potential toxicological concerns of these products is important. This study aimed to analyze the ingredient composition of commercially available pediatric remineralizing dental gels and assess their potential toxicological implications.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional market survey was conducted between September 2025 and January 2026. Pediatric remineralizing dental gels commercially available in Türkiye were identified through major retail supermarkets and online marketplaces. Ingredient lists were obtained from product labels and verified using manufacturers' official websites. A structured literature search was performed using PubMed, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect to identify published evidence regarding the functional roles and toxicological properties of each ingredient. Descriptive statistics were used to calculate ingredient frequencies, and an exploratory hazard classification framework was applied to compare ingredient hazard profiles.
RESULTS: Seven pediatric remineralizing dental gel formulations were analyzed, revealing 29 unique ingredients. The most frequently detected ingredients were water, glycerin, xylitol, and flavoring agents (85.7%). Most ingredients were classified as having low hazard, whereas CPP-ACP, sodium fluoride, propylene glycol, parabens, sodium benzoate, and potassium sorbate were classified as moderate hazard. Titanium dioxide was the only ingredient classified as high hazard. Cumulative hazard scores ranged from 11 to 25.
CONCLUSION: Most ingredients identified in commercially available pediatric remineralizing dental gels exhibited low literature-based hazard profiles; however, certain compounds were associated with reported allergenic or irritative concerns. These findings highlight the importance of considering overall ingredient composition when selecting pediatric remineralizing products and support the need for continued evaluation of their safety profiles.

articles.title: Social Media Insights Into the Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Catch-Up Campaign for Young Adults in the Netherlands, 2023-2024: Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, but its uptake remains suboptimal. In the Netherlands, a catch-up campaign invited individuals aged 18 to 27 years for an additional cost-free opportunity to initiate or complete their HPV vaccination in 2023-2024, which led to 24% of the invited population getting vaccinated. As young adults increasingly seek health information online, understanding online questions, concerns, and misinformation in response to the campaign may help improve future vaccination efforts. In addition to the overall evaluation of the vaccination campaign, we piloted online social listening processes to generate an insight report for the Public Health Service (PHS) Amsterdam.
OBJECTIVE: This study piloted online social listening processes at PHS Amsterdam to identify actionable insights into questions, concerns, and misinformation surrounding the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign among young adults.
METHODS: Following an inventory of potential platforms and data sources, a retrospective online social listening analysis was conducted across Instagram, Facebook, and X (formerly Twitter), using data from PHS Amsterdam, the National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, the Dutch public broadcasting foundation, and LINDA.meiden from January 1, 2023, to June 1, 2024. Publicly available posts, comments, and engagement concerning HPV vaccination were manually collected and inductively coded. Themes were assessed for risk based on expected potential harm and observed reach and were used to develop recommendations.
RESULTS: A total of 821 posts and 5157 comments were collected and analyzed. Ten recurring themes were identified across varying risk levels. Two themes were classified as high risk: an information gap regarding HPV vaccination effectiveness and concerns about the transparency regarding HPV vaccine side effects. Three themes were classified as medium risk: questioning HPV vaccine effectiveness, reduced general vaccine trust following COVID-19, and accessibility issues related to vaccination locations and service times. Two themes were classified as neutral risk: questions regarding campaign eligibility criteria and calls for broader HPV prevention measures. Finally, 3 low-risk themes concerned questions regarding HPV vaccine brand specifics, campaign choices, and scheduling HPV appointments. Comments also referred to subsequent information sources, including reliable sources, false narratives, and misinformation. Recommendations focused on addressing questions and information gaps (ie, improving risk perception and providing more detailed HPV vaccine information), improving communication, and reducing practical barriers to vaccination.
CONCLUSIONS: Manual social listening across selected online sources provided actionable insights into the public discourse during the HPV vaccination catch-up campaign. Results mostly reflected questions, concerns, and information gaps. Although some themes were critical of HPV vaccination, false narratives and misinformation did not dominate the discourse. Recommendations aim to reduce practical barriers and address information needs. This pilot showed that online social listening can be effectively implemented even with limited resources.

articles.title: FcRn beyond IgG recycling in systemic lupus erythematosus.
articles.abstract: In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), in which autoantibody titers alone do not account for disease activity, the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) links their persistence in the circulation to the routing of immune complexes (ICs) and antigen presentation. The recycling of monomeric IgG maintains the pool available to form these complexes, whereas their multivalency engages FcRn in pathways that direct their degradation and the presentation of their autoantigens. It is not the functions themselves, but the cell type in which they operate, that shapes their consequences. This cell dependence results in distinct effects, from the placental transfer of anti-SSA/Ro antibodies to renal clearance or inflammatory functions. Extracellular signals and intracellular mechanisms can locally modulate FcRn expression. Early therapeutic data provide clinical proof of concept in SLE, but the inhibitors evaluated primarily target IgG recycling and transport, without directly elucidating the intracellular handling of ICs. Linking local FcRn expression to IC fate should clarify its contribution to lupus manifestations and the scope of its therapeutic blockade.

articles.title: Trends and projections of the syphilis burden in China: an analysis of GBD 2021 data and global comparison.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: China accounts for a significant proportion of the global burden of syphilis, yet detailed comparisons of long-term epidemiological trends between China and the global population at present remain lacking.
METHODS: Data on syphilis for China and the global population from 1990 to 2021 were extracted from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2021. Joinpoint regression analysis was employed to identify the temporal trend. Age and sex distributions were examined, and mortality and DALY rate attributable to unsafe sex were analyzed. The future syphilis burden from 2022 to 2041 was estimated using the Nordpred model, and alternative model-based scenario analysis was conducted using complementary ARIMA and Holt-Winters models.
RESULTS: Between 1990 and 2021, the number of incident cases and prevalent cases of syphilis increased by 3.64% and 12.87% in China, respectively, whereas deaths and DALYs declined by 55.75% and 55.65%, respectively. China's age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR), age-standardized prevalence rates (ASPR), age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR), and age-standardized disability-adjusted life-year rates (ASDR) remained substantially below global levels over the 32-year period. Joinpoint analysis revealed that China's ASMR and ASDR increased sharply during 2019-2021, with APCs of 20.75% and 20.36%, far exceeding the corresponding global values (4.43% and 4.54%). Across China and globally, ASMR and ASDR reached their highest levels among children under five, while unsafe sex-linked syphilis mortality was greatest among those aged 80 and above. Nordpred projects continued decline in China's ASIR, ASPR, and ASDR for syphilis through 2041. In contrast, both the ARIMA and Holt-Winters models forecast upward trends in ASIR, ASPR, and ASDR.
CONCLUSION: Syphilis-related ASMR and ASDR increased during 2019-2021, a period coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic and the final evaluation year of the National Syphilis Prevention and Control Plan. This observation warrants further investigation into the potential contributions of healthcare disruptions, surveillance artifacts, and changes in reporting practices. Strengthening prenatal syphilis screening and timely, evidence-based treatment is essential to prevent congenital syphilis; concurrently, enhancing clinicians' diagnostic proficiency for complications associated with late-stage syphilis is critically important.

articles.title: Simple and easy to build mechanical ventilator for pandemic health crises in resource-limited areas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical shortages of mechanical ventilators, particularly in low-resource settings. Disruptions in global supply chains and dependence on specialized components highlighted the need for scalable, locally manufacturing alternatives for emergency respiratory support.
AIM: To describe and evaluate a simplified mechanical ventilator with minimal supply-chain dependence, assembled from widely available automotive and simple hardware components, and intended as a last-resort solution.
METHODS: The ventilator is based on a reciprocating air pump driven by an automotive windshield wiper motor coupled to parallel shaft bellows and readily assembled passive membrane valves, only requiring materials available from standard hardware retailers, minimal tools, and basic manual skills. Ventilator performance was assessed through bench testing using a patient model simulating severe lung disease in an adult (R = 20 cmH₂O·s/L, C = 15 mL/cmH₂O) and pediatric (R = 50 cmH₂O·s/L, C = 10 mL/cmH₂O) patients. Realistic proof of concept was performed in four mechanically ventilated 50-kg healthy pigs.
RESULTS: According to the bench test, the device delivered tidal volumes up to 600 mL and respiratory rates up to 45 breaths/min with PEEP up to 10 cmH₂O, covering most pediatric and adult ventilation ranges. The in vivo proof-of-concept showed that the ventilator maintained arterial blood gases within the targeted range. Technical details for ventilator construction are provided in an open-source video tutorial.
DISCUSSION: Notwithstanding its limitations, this low-cost ventilator demonstrated adequate performance as a prototype. Although not a substitute for commercial intensive care ventilators, its simplicity, autonomy, and low dependence from fragile supply chains provides an approach towards life-saving options in resource-constrained emergency scenarios.

articles.title: Diagnostic pathways and unmet healthcare needs in rare diseases: a Romanian survey.
articles.abstract: Rare disease policy in Europe increasingly emphasises not only timely diagnosis but also the integration of specialist expertise into sustainable national care pathways. We analysed a cross-sectional, network-based online survey conducted in Romania within the ECOU project to describe diagnostic trajectories and principal unmet care needs and to consider their relevance within the evolving European rare disease landscape. Of 799 exported records, 768 met the inclusion criteria and were analysed. The individuals represented included 291 children and 473 adults, with age category missing for four individuals. Amongst 763 responses concerning the diagnostic interval, 47.1% reported diagnosis within 6 months of the first medical consultation, while 32.9% reported intervals of at least 1 year. Two to three physicians were consulted most frequently (39.1%). Amongst 729 responses concerning principal unmet healthcare needs, rehabilitation (22.6%), access to available treatment (21.7%), expert-centre follow-up (14.7%) and psychological counselling (11.1%) were most frequently reported. These findings identify unmet needs extending beyond diagnostic assessment, particularly in rehabilitation, treatment access, expert-centre follow-up and psychological support. They highlight priorities for strengthening links between specialist rare disease services and local health and social care in Romania.

articles.title: Prevalence of physical activity, sedentary screen time, and sleep duration among non-Saudi adolescents in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-Saudi residents constitute nearly 44% of Saudi Arabia's population, yet non-Saudi adolescents have been almost entirely absent from national school-health surveillance, including studies using the Global School-based Student Health Survey (GSHS). This study aimed to determine the prevalence of physical activity, sedentary screen time, and sleep duration among non-Saudi adolescents across five Saudi cities, and to examine variation by sex and city of residence.
METHODS: A cross-sectional survey using a modified, Arabic-translated GSHS questionnaire was administered to students in 40 public intermediate schools across Riyadh, Jeddah, Dammam, Khamis Mushait, and Tabuk. This analysis was restricted to non-Saudi students with complete data (n = 1,036).
