Physical activity (linear regression) and three binary outcomes, 7-day activity attainment, high sedentary screen time, and very short sleep (logistic regression) were each modeled with sex, city of residence, and age as simultaneous covariates, using cluster-robust standard errors to account for students nested within 36 schools. Adjusted estimates and 95% confidence intervals are reported, with a Bonferroni-corrected threshold (α = 0.006) applied across eight tests (sex and city for each of four outcomes).
RESULTS: Only 14.0% of participants reported ≥60 min of physical activity on all 7 days, 26.8% reported no active days, 48.9% reported high sedentary screen time, and 37.1% reported very short sleep duration (≤6 h, below the 8-10 h recommended for this age group). After adjustment for city, age, and school clustering, males reported more physical activity days than females (adjusted mean difference = 0.66 days/week, 95% CI 0.23-1.09, p = 0.003) and were less likely to report very short sleep (aOR = 0.59, 95% CI 0.47-0.74, p < 0.001); both associations survived Bonferroni correction. Males were also more likely to report ≥60 min of activity on all 7 days (aOR = 1.55, p = 0.035) and less likely to report high sedentary screen time (aOR = 0.74, p = 0.012), but neither survived correction. City of residence was not significantly associated with physical activity days, high sedentary time, or very short sleep, but showed a nominally significant, non-corrected association with 7-day activity attainment (driven by Dammam vs. Riyadh). Older age was independently associated with fewer physical activity days (adjusted difference = -0.14 days/year, p = 0.036).
CONCLUSION: Physical inactivity, high sedentary screen time, and very short sleep were common among non-Saudi adolescents attending public schools in Saudi Arabia. Sex differences were robust for physical activity days and short sleep, while differences in 7-day activity attainment and sedentary time were smaller and did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. City of residence contributed little to this variation. These findings, among the first population-specific estimates for this substantial and previously understudied group, support further surveillance and consideration of non-Saudi students in school health programming; the effectiveness of sex-specific interventions should be evaluated in future research rather than assumed from these cross-sectional findings.

articles.title: From efficacy verification to precision intervention: a dual-database bibliometric and clinical mapping analysis of therapeutic exercise for adolescent obesity (2016-2025).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically map the research landscape, knowledge structure, collaboration patterns, and evolutionary frontiers of therapeutic exercise for adolescent obesity from 2016 to 2025, and to identify translational gaps between basic research and clinical practice.
METHODS: Publications were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and PubMed. The WoSCC dataset, comprising original articles and reviews, was analyzed using CiteSpace 7.0.1 for co-citation, keyword co-occurrence, thematic clustering, and burst detection, and VOSviewer 1.6.19 for collaboration networks at the country, institution, and author levels. The PubMed dataset, restricted to clinical research, was analyzed using CiteSpace to identify clinical intervention hotspots and evolutionary trends.
RESULTS: A total of 2,953 records from WoSCC and 1,295 clinical studies from PubMed were included. Annual publications showed a fluctuating upward trend, peaking at 349 articles in 2022. The United States and China led publication output, but international cross-regional collaboration remained limited, with high-output countries functioning primarily as production cores rather than collaboration hubs. Ten research clusters were identified in the WoSCC dataset, with insulin resistance, cardiorespiratory fitness, and body mass index as core themes. Research evolved through three distinct phases: basic efficacy evaluation (2016-2018), mechanism and benefit expansion (2019-2021), and precision intervention for special populations (2022-2025). Clinical research in PubMed emphasized intervention efficacy and patient-oriented outcomes, with high-intensity interval training and health-related quality of life emerging as the latest frontiers since 2024. A clear thematic divergence was observed between basic research, which focused on mechanistic targets and population characteristics, and clinical practice, which prioritized intervention protocols and practical outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Therapeutic exercise research for adolescent obesity has developed steadily from 2016 to 2025, with prominent multidisciplinary integration but insufficient international cross-regional collaboration. A potential translational gap, reflected by thematic divergence, persists between basic mechanistic research and clinical practice. Future efforts should prioritize multi-factor synergistic interventions combining exercise with sleep, nutrition, and psychological support; precision exercise prescriptions tailored to special populations such as adolescents with Down syndrome or severe obesity; and high-quality multicenter clinical trials to accelerate the translation of basic findings into standardized clinical protocols.

articles.title: Enhancing psychological wellbeing in STEM education through public health strategies across educational transitions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Student mental health is a growing public health concern in higher education, and small questionnaire datasets are often highly imbalanced and difficult to model reliably.
OBJECTIVES: This study empirically validates a Transition-Aware Public Health Wellbeing Network (TAPHW-Net) using an openly accessible questionnaire dataset and narrows the STEM-transition domain to the available variables.
METHODS: The source dataset contained 843 responses. Respondents aged 18-22 years were retained, and the analytic sample consisted of 777 students, classified based on the original survey label: No Stress (n = 38), Eustress (n = 710), and Distress (n = 29). 24 predictors were grouped into emotional/psychological, physical/somatic, academic pressure, social and environmental, and demographic branches. To prevent leakage of the targets, the direct recent-stress item was omitted. Median imputation, standardization, and SMOTE were applied in the training folds only. Five-fold out-of-fold evaluation was used to assess Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, MLP, ANN, and TAPHW-Net.
RESULTS: Logistic Regression had the highest fold-averaged accuracy (0.968 ± 0.019), macro-F1 (0.884 ± 0.048), and macro-AUC (0.996 ± 0.004). TAPHW-Net's pooled OOF accuracy, macro-F1 score, and macro-AUC were 0.8739, 0.6626, and 0.9523, respectively. It had lower overall accuracy, but it successfully retrieved 78.9% of the No Stress cases and 86.2% of the distress cases, although precision was only 0.385 and 0.397 for these two classes, respectively. Difficulty in the home environment, anxiety, palpitations, work-environment stress, sleep problems, and health problems were important predictors.
CONCLUSION: The attention architecture did not outperform simpler models on this small and highly imbalanced tabular dataset. Its main value lies in domain-structured representations, minority-class recall, and transparent mapping of model importance to a hypothetical decision-support template. The findings are limited to the source dataset and require external validation before institutional use or transfer to STEM-specific and educational-transition settings.

articles.title: Prenatal exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and heating-season air pollution: associations with birth outcomes in a coal-reliant city.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: As air pollutants and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) can enter the human body through multiple routes, prenatal exposure may compromise neonatal development. This study characterizes heating-season air pollution exposure and PAH detection among pregnant women and neonates in Urumqi, a coal-reliant city in northwestern China with severe winter air pollution, and evaluates its association with neonatal birth outcomes.
METHODS: Between June 2019 and January 2020, we enrolled 279 mother-infant pairs in Urumqi. Participants were stratified into long and short heating-season exposure groups based on the duration of gestational overlap with the municipal heating period. Sixteen PAHs were analyzed in paired maternal and umbilical cord plasma samples using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), and detection rates were calculated. We compared neonatal anthropometric outcomes, maternal lifestyle factors, and ambient air pollution levels between groups, and examined correlations between air pollutants and neonatal outcomes. Multivariable linear regression models were established to examine the associations between heating-season exposure (LHPEG vs. SHPEG) and neonatal outcomes after adjusting for potential confounders. In a sensitivity analysis, DGOHP was treated as a continuous variable.
RESULTS: The detection rates of the 16 PAHs ranged from 66.02 to 91.08% in maternal plasma and from 47.68 to 77.64% in cord plasma. Neonates in the long heating-season exposure group (LHPEG) had significantly lower body length, Ponderal Index than those in the short-exposure group (SHPEG) (p = 0.002 for body length). No significant difference was observed for birth weight (p = 0.132). In the sensitivity analysis, each 1-day increase in DGOHP was associated with a 0.011 cm decrease in body length (p = 0.004). Higher gestational exposure to PM2.5 and PM10 was also associated with reduced body length.
CONCLUSION: Prolonged heating-season air pollution exposure in Urumqi is associated with reduced neonatal body length. PAHs were widely detected in maternal and cord plasma, indicating widespread exposure. These findings support the need for public health strategies to reduce air pollution exposure among pregnant women in coal-reliant regions with long heating seasons.

articles.title: Anti-HBc seropositivity among women of childbearing age in Indonesia: a nationally representative cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate the national prevalence of hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc) seropositivity, indicating prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) exposure, among Indonesian women aged 15-49 years. Additionally, the study sought to identify associated sociodemographic factors.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the 2018 Indonesian Basic Health Survey (Riskesdas), a nationally representative survey with a complex sampling design and appropriate sampling weights. Anti-HBc seropositivity was measured at the Sulianti Saroso Laboratory. Of the 19,418 participants, 12,617 women were included in the final analysis. Survey-weighted logistic regression was applied to estimate adjusted odds ratios (ORₐⱼ) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
RESULTS: Anti-HBc seropositivity was significantly more common among women aged >35 years (ORₐⱼ = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.58-1.87), those with lower educational attainment (ORₐⱼ = 1.16; 95% CI: 1.05-1.28), employed women (ORₐⱼ = 1.19; 95% CI: 1.09-1.29), rural residents (ORₐⱼ = 1.28; 95% CI: 1.18-1.40), and women reporting contraceptive use (ORₐⱼ = 1.22; 95% CI: 1.11-1.35).
CONCLUSION: Anti-HBc seropositivity remains a significant public health concern among Indonesian women of childbearing age, particularly those who are older, less educated, employed, living in rural areas, and reporting contraceptive use. Policy recommendations should prioritize maternal screening, timely and universal birth dose vaccination, administration of hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) when indicated, and improved vaccination coverage among unvaccinated adults.

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of non-fasting lipid abnormalities among 9- to 11-year-old students in the Science City area.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to examine the prevalence of and factors associated with non-fasting lipid abnormalities among students aged 9-11 years in the Science City area, thereby establishing a foundation for early, targeted interventions to enhance cardiovascular health in this demographic.
METHODS: In October 2025, we recruited 580 primary school students aged 9-11 years from the Science City area. We measured non-fasting levels of four lipid parameters: total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). In addition, we recorded height, weight, and waist circumference. Data on lifestyle behaviors were gathered through questionnaires. To identify factors associated with lipid abnormalities, we employed binary logistic regression.
RESULTS: Based on the diagnostic criteria for non-fasting lipid abnormalities in children, the prevalence among 9- to 11-year-old students in the Science City area was 29.7% (172/580). There was no significant difference in prevalence between boys and girls (30.5% vs. 28.9%; χ 2 = 0.19, p > 0.05). In addition, LDL, TG, HDL, and TC levels showed no significant gender differences (all p > 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression revealed that a meat-centric diet (OR: 21.84, 95% CI: 10.51-45.37), frequent consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages (OR: 4.49, 95% CI: 2.00-10.06), being overweight or obese (OR: 3.18, 95% CI: 1.85-5.48), frequent intake of fried foods (OR: 3.21, 95% CI: 1.45-7.11), and a family history of metabolic disorders was an independent positive correlates of lipid abnormalities (OR: 2.87, 95% CI: 1.75-4.72). In contrast, moderate single-session exercise duration (OR: 0.17), high-frequency weekly physical activity (OR: 0.29), and parental attention to children's lipid health (OR: 0.51) were independent inverse correlates (all p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Among 9- to 11-year-old students in the Science City area, the prevalence of non-fasting lipid abnormalities is notably high. These lipid alterations are positively associated with overweight or obesity, high-sugar and high-fat dietary patterns, and a family history of metabolic diseases. Encouraging longer exercise sessions, increasing the frequency of physical activity, optimizing household dietary habits, and enhancing parental awareness could help lower the likelihood of lipid abnormalities in children within this age group.

articles.title: The Relational Cascade Model: a Measurement for Change framework for testing caregiver coaching as upstream mental health promotion.
articles.abstract: Early childhood development remains chronically underfunded and marginalized in global health policy, often treated as a downstream education concern because no single sector owns it. We propose that the relational environment of early childhood, mediated through caregiver regulation, attunement, and responsiveness, is a proximal pathway through which adversity may be transmitted across generations and therefore interrupted. The Relational Cascade Model (RCM) is an architecture linking trainer, coach, caregiver, and child in a cascade of regulatory capacity in which each level requires the same relational resources it transmits. The RCM draws on developmental cascade theory, attachment and co-regulation, salutogenesis, differential susceptibility, and neurobiological evidence on hippocampal plasticity, and is operationalized through the Conscious Discipline curriculum, which is distinct from the cascade itself. We describe its implementation in two low- and middle-income country contexts, via the Roving Caregiver Programme in Grenada and Community Health Promoter coaching in Kenya, reaching 5,692 children through 2,828 trained parents and 279 community workers as of June 2026. The model is assessed through a Measurement for Change (M4C) framework capturing caregiver wellbeing, intervention fidelity, child neurodevelopment, and attitudes toward corporal punishment. These are captured within one cross-sectoral architecture, making the caregiving relationship visible across health, education, and child-rights accountability streams. We argue that this measurement framework, rather than additional intervention content, supplies the multilevel data needed to test the cascade rather than assume it, and propose it as a template for moving early childhood, and public health broadly, from siloed accountability to systems-level learning.

articles.title: Factors influencing COVID-19 vaccination among adolescents in Western Mexico: the role of family influence and access barriers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: COVID-19 vaccination remains an important public health strategy. Adolescents represent approximately 16% of the global population (1.3 billion), making their vaccine uptake a critical component of pandemic control. This study aimed to identify the factors and barriers influencing COVID-19 vaccination behaviors among adolescents in western Mexico.
METHODS: A non-experimental, observational, cross-sectional study was conducted in high school students aged 15-17 years. Data were collected through an online Google Forms questionnaire. Statistical analysis included chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and binary logistic regression to evaluate factors associated with vaccination behavior.
RESULTS: A total of 838 adolescents were included, of whom 83% received at least one dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. Sociodemographic characteristics including age, sex, and religion, were not significantly associated with vaccination attitudes. In contrast, parental influence, particularly maternal attitudes and vaccination behaviors, showed a stronger association with adolescent vaccination status than paternal attitudes. Additionally, parental refusal, family dynamics, and structural accessibility barriers had a greater influence on vaccine hesitancy than concerns regarding vaccine safety or effectiveness among adolescents in western Mexico.
CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the need for public health strategies that address access barriers and family-centered approaches when evaluating adolescent vaccination behaviors. Interventions focused solely on correcting misinformation are unlikely to be sufficient without addressing these broader factors.

articles.title: Respiratory virus prevalence among healthcare university students in Ecuador: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses remain a major global public health concern and are among the leading causes of acute respiratory infections worldwide. University students, particularly healthcare students, represent a potentially important group for viral circulation because of frequent social interaction and exposure to clinical environments. Evidence regarding respiratory virus circulation in university populations from Latin America, especially Ecuador, remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence of respiratory viruses among 438 healthcare university students in three Ecuadorian cities and to describe the proportion of infections detected in students without symptoms.
METHODS: A multicenter cross-sectional study based on a convenience sample was conducted between January 4 and February 3, 2026, among healthcare university students from universities located in Quito, Guayaquil, and Cuenca, Ecuador. Nasopharyngeal samples were analyzed on site using a combo rapid antigen test for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), Influenza A, Influenza B, and Adenovirus. Sociodemographic and epidemiological variables were recorded. Exact tests and exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression were used to explore factors associated with positivity.
RESULTS: Fourteen participants tested positive for at least one respiratory virus, corresponding to an overall prevalence of 3.2% (95% CI: 1.8-5.3). Influenza A virus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were the most frequent single detections (n = 4 each), followed by adenovirus (n = 3). Three coinfections were identified. Eight of the 14 positive participants (57.1%) were asymptomatic, whereas six (42.9%) reported respiratory symptoms. A significant association was identified between symptom presence and viral detection (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Respiratory virus detection among healthcare university students in Ecuador was low, and more than half of the positive students reported no symptoms, suggesting that these viruses may circulate unnoticed within university environments. Because rapid antigen tests have limited sensitivity and do not directly measure infectivity, the true prevalence is probably higher, and studies with molecular confirmation, larger samples, and longer sampling periods are needed. Rapid antigen tests were operationally feasible as point-of-care tools for on-site screening in academic environments.

articles.title: School-based scoliosis screening among 73,509 students in Zhangye, Northwest China: epidemiological characteristics, 7-day non-completion in the radiographic diagnostic cascade, and an exploratory case-control analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: School scoliosis screening is effective only when students who screen positive complete diagnostic confirmation. We described a citywide program in Zhangye, Northwest China, quantified 7-day non-completion in the radiographic diagnostic cascade, and explored characteristics associated with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) case status.
METHODS: From September to October 2025, all 66 primary and secondary schools in Zhangye City participated. Students aged 10-18 years underwent postural inspection, the Adams forward bend test, and angle of trunk rotation (ATR) measurement. ATR > =5 degrees defined a screening-positive result. Screening-positive students were advised to undergo standing full-length spine radiography within 7 days. Two experienced spine surgeons, blinded to ATR results, independently measured the maximum Cobb angle; their mean was used. AIS required a mean Cobb angle ≥ 10 degrees and exclusion of known secondary causes. We analyzed the screening population, diagnostic cascade, and an unmatched exploratory case-control sample of 250 AIS cases and 250 screening-negative controls using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 73,509 students, 1,451 screened positive (1.97%, 95% CI 1.88-2.08). The rate was higher in girls than boys (2.59% vs. 1.49%), increased after age 12, and ranged from 1.50 to 3.08% across counties/districts. Only 348 screening-positive students completed radiography within 7 days (23.98%, 95% CI 21.86-26.25); 1,103 had no recorded completion within this window (76.02%, 95% CI 73.75-78.14) reflecting 7-day non-completion rather than permanent non-completion. Among those imaged, 250 had a mean Cobb angle ≥ 10 degrees and were diagnosed with AIS, representing 71.84% (95% CI 66.89-76.31) of those imaged and a minimum confirmed detection proportion of 0.34% (95% CI 0.30-0.38) among all screened students. In the complete-case model (n = 452), female sex, increasing age, sometimes rather than frequently maintaining an upright classroom posture, and left-side rather than supine sleeping were associated with AIS case status; BMI was not independently associated.
CONCLUSION: The principal implementation gap occurred between screening-positive identification and timely radiographic confirmation. The 0.34% proportion is a minimum confirmed detection estimate, not population prevalence. Closed-loop referral pathways are needed, and the exploratory case-control associations should not be interpreted causally.

articles.title: Co-designing maternal mental health interventions and implementation strategies under climate stress in Nigeria: a participatory workshop.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Climate change is a risk multiplier in low- and middle-income countries, threatening maternal mental health and early childhood development. In Nigeria, environmental shocks intensify these risks, yet responses remain fragmented across sectors. Using a participatory implementation-science approach, this study co-designed a psychosocial intervention package and accompanying implementation strategies to protect maternal mental health under climate stress.
METHODS: A full-day co-creation workshop was conducted in Enugu, Nigeria, involving 16 stakeholders (affected mothers, community health workers, community leaders, data collectors, and policymakers). Grounded in prior systematic review, national quantitative, and qualitative evidence, the workshop utilised participatory inquiry to map implementation determinants and the Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change (ERIC) taxonomy to select and categorise implementation strategies. Participants progressed through determinant mapping, appraisal of candidate components from Low-Intensity Psychological Interventions (LIPI) and WHO Problem Management Plus (PM+), delivery framework co-design, and strategy prioritisation via dot-voting.
RESULTS: Stakeholders identified environmental shocks as key drivers of maternal anxiety, distress, and trauma. From eight candidate components, participants retained five for the preliminary Climate Adaptation and Psychosocial Support (CANOPY) candidate package: behavioural activation, cognitive restructuring, managing worries and problems, lifestyle, and strengthening social support. Three PM + components were discarded as duplicative, whereas strengthening social support was added to leverage existing community networks. Participants developed three preliminary delivery frameworks pairing psychosocial support with environmental protection. These frameworks represent proposed delivery channels requiring further operational specification. Voting favoured immediate, actionable implementation strategies and frontline health-system strengthening over slower legislative and structural reforms.
CONCLUSION: Stakeholders pragmatically prioritised feasible, frontline community and health system strategies over structural policies. Prospective implementation of the CANOPY package would likely require addressing workforce shortages and stigma while leveraging informal social safety nets and faith-based structures. Voting outcomes are presented as exploratory participant preferences within the workshop, and prospective implementation of CANOPY is presented as a future step requiring further operationalisation and evaluation.

articles.title: Understanding health behaviors and resilience during pandemics: a systematic review of ethical, cognitive, and existential dimensions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pandemic events such as HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 destabilize not only public health systems but also the philosophical and ethical frameworks through which individuals interpret illness. Health behavior influenced by contagion challenges definitions of identity, perceptions of truth, moral reasoning, and core bioethical principles, including autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice. This study employs a triadic lens, such as ontology, epistemology, and axiology, to examine how pandemic crises transform embodied experience, cognition, ethical response, and value-laden behavioral choices. From there, the consequences for health behavior are analyzed within both phenomenological and bioethical domains.
METHODS: Using a phenomenological framework, the study draws on interdisciplinary data, including clinical case reports, psychosocial literature, and first-person narratives. Philosophical constructs from Husserl, Merleau-Ponty, and Carel inform the mapping of existential vulnerability, cognitive distortion, and value formation. Bioethical principles from Beauchamp and Childress guide the interpretation of moral tensions arising in pandemic behavior, while public health ethics frameworks (e.g., Kass) contextualize collective obligations. Psychiatric presentations during COVID-19 provide illustrative grounding for abstract principles. Motivations and frameworks for pandemic health behaviors are reported as outcomes. A review of 134 articles helped frame the cognitive and ethical terrain of pandemic prevention and dissemination.
RESULTS: Pandemics cause overlapping disruptions across ontological, epistemological, axiological, and bioethical levels. Embodied identity becomes fragmented by diagnostic classification, social distancing, and existential uncertainty, raising tensions between autonomy and relationality. Cognitive processing is hindered by emotional stress, misinformation, and isolation, leading to distorted perceptions of truth and reduced rationality, which complicates beneficent and non-maleficent decision-making. Moral behavior reflects value-based tensions-altruism, denial, concealment, stigma-negotiated within shifting contexts of personal risk, communal obligation, and distributive justice. These patterns illustrate how existential dislocation, epistemic fragmentation, and moral ambiguity shape lived experience and ethical behavior during a pandemic.
CONCLUSION: Phenomenology offers vital insights into the human impact of pandemics by examining how relational, cognitive, and ethical dimensions shape illness experiences and health behaviors. Integrating bioethical principles clarifies why individuals struggle with autonomy, responsibility, and fairness during crises. To support recovery and coherence, public health governance must move beyond biomedical control toward emotionally attuned, ethically grounded care that emphasizes relational responsibility, moral imagination, and justice-oriented policy.

articles.title: Structured physical activity, yoga, and music-based interventions for depressive symptoms in adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depressive symptoms are common in adolescence. Structured physical activity, yoga, and music-based interventions have been proposed as low-intensity options, but randomized evidence is limited and heterogeneous.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effect of structured physical activity, yoga, and music-based interventions on post-intervention depressive symptom severity in adolescents and to rate the certainty of this evidence.
METHODS: The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261429956) and reported according to PRISMA 2020. CENTRAL, CINAHL, Embase, PsycINFO, PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched. Randomized controlled trials in adolescents aged approximately 12-19 years with depressive disorders, elevated depressive symptoms, or clinically relevant risk were eligible. Hedges g was pooled with a restricted maximum likelihood random-effects model; Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) small-sample intervals were also calculated. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE.
RESULTS: Of 11,575 records, 13 studies (16 reports) were included; seven randomized comparisons (N = 345; four exercise, two music-based, one yoga) contributed to the primary meta-analysis. The pooled estimate, an average across heterogeneous interventions, populations, and comparators, favored the interventions (SMD -0.59, 95% CI - 0.97 to -0.20; HKSJ 95% CI - 1.09 to -0.08), with substantial heterogeneity (I 2 = 63%) and a 95% prediction interval that included no effect (-1.75 to 0.58). No trial was at low risk of bias, mainly because participants could not be blinded and most outcomes were self-reported; four were at high risk. Estimates were smaller and imprecise for the three trials not at high risk of bias (SMD -0.38; HKSJ 95% CI - 1.16 to 0.40) and for the four exercise trials (SMD -0.26, 95% CI - 0.58 to 0.07); larger estimates came from three music-based and yoga trials at high risk of bias. The certainty of evidence was very low.
CONCLUSION: Current randomized evidence is insufficient to determine whether structured physical activity, yoga, or music-based interventions reduce depressive symptoms in adolescents. The pooled estimate should be regarded as hypothesis-generating; adequately powered, prospectively registered trials with blinded outcome assessment and appropriate control conditions are needed before these interventions can be recommended.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261429956, identifier CRD420261429956.

articles.title: Leisure-time sedentary behavior and psychosocial distress among intermediate-school adolescents in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leisure-time sedentary behavior is strongly linked to poorer psychosocial wellbeing among adolescents. In Saudi Arabia, however, where adolescents have among the highest reported levels of screen-based media use, this association is notably under-researched. To address this gap in the literature, the current study investigated the association between leisure-time sedentary behavior and psychosocial wellbeing using the metrics of loneliness and anxiety-related sleep disturbance among Saudi intermediate-school adolescents.
METHODS: Adopting a cross-sectional research design, a stratified multi-stage sample of Saudi adolescents (N = 5,895; grades 7-9) was recruited from 40 public intermediate schools across five Saudi cities in 2019 using a modified Global School-based Student Health Survey (GSHS). Leisure-time sedentary behavior (a single self-report sitting/screen-time item) was dichotomized at ≥3 h/day ("high"). Loneliness and anxiety-related sleep disturbance were assessed individually and as a composite distress score (two items, 0-3 each, summed; distress = score ≥3). Logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, nationality, city, physical activity, and sleep duration, estimated adjusted odds ratios (aOR), with standard errors clustered by school (N = 40) to account for students being sampled within, rather than independently of, schools.
RESULTS: Just over half (52.2%) reported high sedentary behavior (≥3 h/day), which was significantly associated with composite psychological distress (aOR 1.55, 95% CI 1.33-1.80), loneliness (aOR 1.37, 95% CI 1.19-1.58), and anxiety-related sleep disturbance (aOR 1.64, 95% CI 1.38-1.94); crude and adjusted estimates were similar. An exploratory dose-response analysis showed a pattern visually consistent with a threshold, with odds rising significantly only beyond 6-7 h/day; the significant ≥3 h/day association was likely driven by this highest-exposure subgroup. Distress similarly increased with age from 14 onwards, and girls were approximately twice as likely to report distress as boys (aOR 2.09).
CONCLUSION: High leisure-time sedentary behavior was independently associated with loneliness and anxiety-related sleep disturbance among the sampled Saudi intermediate-school adolescents, particularly at the highest exposure levels. As the design was cross-sectional, these findings describe an association, not causation; longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to establish direction and to test whether reducing sedentary behavior improves psychosocial outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Pediatric palliative care research participation: do adolescent and adult patients and caregivers find it acceptable?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Palliative care has matured as a life-span field with an increasing research base. Advancing the field means understanding why patients and caregivers participate in palliative care research, and participation's benefits and burdens. This study extended previous work to include greater diversity of clinical sampling and study design.
METHODS: Prospective, multi-methods study examined reported benefits, burdens, and motivations associated with participation in pediatric palliative care research. Study pParticipants included patients, caregivers, and family members who enrolled in pediatric palliative care research, as well as individuals declining participation, within a single quaternary pediatric hospital system. Structured questionnaires were administered at enrollment and study completion; qualitative responses were analyzed thematically.
RESULTS: 57 participants completed the questionnaires. Altruism and personal benefit were the most frequently cited motivations for enrollment at baseline and study completion. Emotional expression and the opportunity to help others were commonly identified as positive aspects of participation. The majority reported no discomfort and indicated willingness to participate in future research. The most frequent reasons given for declining participation were feeling overwhelmed, lack of interest, or study-specific aversion, rather than distress associated with palliative care research iPPC involvement.
DISCUSSION: Participants consistently reported greater benefit than burden, suggesting that pediatric palliative care research participation is acceptable and often meaningful. Given the pre/post design, the findings suggest eligible participants are able to determine if actual study participation is likely beneficial for them or not. Supporting families as they consider research participation promotes ethical, sensitive, and inclusive research design. Identified patterns may guide research design for future investigators to continue to advance the science of pediatric palliative care across the lifespanresearch.

articles.title: Constructing the Self Data Atlas ontology: a crisp-fuzzy ontology for quality of life representation in children with neurodevelopmental and learning disabilities.
articles.abstract: The lived experiences of children with neurodevelopmental and learning disabilities are documented through diverse forms of personal data, including identity, medical, mental health, accomplishments, social relationships, financial resources, and personal ecology. However, these records rarely integrate quality of life (QoL) information represented through validated multidimensional frameworks. Building on the gap identified in a companion narrative review, this paper presents a reproducible ontology engineering methodology for representing QoL in children with neurodevelopmental and learning disabilities. The paper presents a design-science methodology for constructing an ontology from the Self Research Institute's Self Data Atlas (SDA), a seven-category taxonomy for organizing longitudinal personal data. Derived from Wieringa's design-science framework, the methodology follows a seven-step protocol comprising: (1) competency-question-based requirements specification; (2) ontology reuse and re-engineering; (3) conceptualization; (4) crisp formalization in OWL 2 DL; (5) fuzzy formalization in Fuzzy OWL 2; (6) alignment with the Common Core Ontology (CCO) as a Basic Formal Ontology (BFO)-conformant mid-level scaffold; and (7) iterative evaluation and refinement. The methodology incorporates two complementary design features. First, it separates factual and classificatory information, including demographics, SNOMED CT diagnostic codes, and clinical observations, represented in classical description logic, from graded and context-dependent QoL concepts, including social inclusion, severity, intensity, and wellbeing, represented using fuzzy datatypes, fuzzy linguistic variables, and graded class membership. Second, it embeds tritemporal reasoning by assigning three temporal qualifiers to each SDA event, state, or information artifact: (1) absolute time, representing when the fact existed in reality; (2) ingestion time, representing when the record entered the system; and (3) assignment time, representing when an interpretative classification was applied. These temporal qualifiers are represented as ontology entities rather than opaque metadata. This tritemporal structure supports longitudinal queries, retrospective recording, and event-history replay. Each stage is illustrated using examples from the seven SDA categories. The paper illustrates how CCO classes provide stable upper-level abstractions for SDA components and interoperability with ICF, SNOMED CT, HL7 FHIR, and the Schalock-Verdugo QoL model. This paper makes a methodological rather than an empirical contribution. It provides a reproducible ontology engineering methodology for future SDA ontology development and related personal-data ontologies.

articles.title: Network analysis of hope, medical coping, and self-deficiency in patients with port-wine stain.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Port-wine stain (PWS) is a chronic congenital vascular malformation that often causes substantial psychosocial burden due to visible skin lesions. However, the complex interrelationships among hope, medical coping, and self-deficiency in patients with PWS remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the network structure of hope, medical coping styles, and self-deficiency in patients with PWS, identify core and bridge psychological nodes, and examine subgroup differences by socioeconomic status (SES), gender, and treatment experience.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 227 patients with PWS. Hope was assessed using the Herth Hope Index (HHI), coping styles using the Medical Coping Modes Questionnaire (MCMQ), and self-deficiency using the Feeling of Inadequacy Scale (FIS). Network analysis was performed to estimate the psychological interaction structure, evaluate centrality and bridge centrality, identify community structures, and assess network stability. Subgroup network comparisons were further conducted based on gender, SES, and treatment experience.
RESULTS: The network analysis identified learning ability as the most central node and the most important bridge node. Confrontation and appearance also showed high centrality. The strongest edge was observed between learning ability and confrontation, suggesting a close interaction between perceived competence and active coping. Bridge centrality analysis further highlighted social confidence as an important connector across psychological domains. Community detection identified three interconnected psychological subsystems. Subgroup analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity: males showed stronger associations between hope and self-deficiency, females demonstrated tighter connections among self-esteem, appearance, and social confidence, and patients without treatment experience exhibited denser psychological networks. In addition, low-SES patients had significantly higher network density than high-SES patients, indicating stronger mutual reinforcement among psychological factors.
CONCLUSION: The psychological adaptation of patients with PWS exhibits a complex network structure, with learning ability, confrontation, and social confidence serving as key intervention targets. Patients with lower SES may be more psychologically vulnerable due to denser network connectivity. These findings provide a theoretical basis for precision psychological interventions in PWS from a network perspective. Notably, patients with low SES exhibited denser network connectivity, suggesting heightened psychological vulnerability, so future public health strategies should prioritize both node-specific interventions and resources for disadvantaged populations.

articles.title: Associations of insomnia symptoms and physical activity with life satisfaction and psychological well-being among secondary school students in Spain: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Insomnia symptoms and physical inactivity are common during adolescence and may be associated with poorer well-being. However, their independent associations with different well-being indicators remain insufficiently examined in Spanish secondary school students.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the independent associations of insomnia symptoms and physical activity with life satisfaction and psychological well-being among adolescents, after adjusting for sociodemographic factors.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 462 secondary school students from six schools in Zaragoza, Spain. Participants completed self-report measures of insomnia symptoms, physical activity, life satisfaction, psychological well-being, and subjective social status. Hierarchical multiple linear regression models with bootstrap confidence intervals were used to examine the contribution of insomnia symptoms and physical activity beyond age, gender, geographical area, and subjective social status.
RESULTS: The mean Insomnia Severity Index score was 9.08 (SD = 4.58), and 59.1% of students presented subthreshold, moderate clinical, or severe clinical insomnia symptoms. The mean PAQ-A score was 2.67 (SD = 0.77), with 57.1% of students classified as physically inactive. Insomnia symptoms were negatively associated with both life satisfaction and psychological well-being, whereas physical activity was positively associated with both outcomes. The addition of insomnia symptoms and physical activity increased the explained variance in life satisfaction and psychological well-being beyond sociodemographic covariates. Insomnia symptoms showed larger standardised associations than physical activity in both models.
DISCUSSION: Insomnia symptoms and physical activity were independently associated with well-being indicators among Spanish adolescents. School-based strategies addressing both sleep health and physical activity may contribute to adolescent well-being, although longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to clarify the directionality of these relationships.

articles.title: First-trimester maternal exposures and offspring congenital heart defects: a Hungarian population-based case-control study, 1980-2009.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are a major cause of infant morbidity and mortality. Identifying modifiable maternal exposures during early pregnancy is important for CHD prevention and maternal and child health.
OBJECTIVES: To examine associations between first-trimester maternal active smoking and alcohol consumption and offspring CHDs, and to explore associations of selected maternal diseases and related treatments with CHD outcomes.
METHODS: This population-based case-control study used data from the Hungarian Case-Control Surveillance of Congenital Abnormalities (1980-2009), including 7,362 CHD cases and 56,894 controls. Overall CHDs were the primary outcome, with ventricular septal defect (VSD) and atrial septal defect (ASD) examined as secondary outcomes. Complete-case multivariable logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for smoking and alcohol consumption, with mutual adjustment and additional adjustment for maternal age, socioeconomic status, and offspring sex. Multiple imputation was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Maternal disease and treatment analyses were crude and exploratory.
RESULTS: First-trimester maternal smoking was associated with higher odds of overall CHDs (adjusted OR 1.50, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.30-1.71), VSD (1.36, 1.11-1.66) and ASD (1.62, 1.35-1.93). Multiple-imputation estimates were similar to the complete-case estimates. No statistically significant associations were observed between maternal alcohol consumption and CHD outcomes in either the adjusted complete-case analysis or the multiple-imputation analysis. Maternal epilepsy, migraine, anxiety disorder and anemia showed positive crude associations with one or more CHD outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Maternal smoking reported during the first trimester was associated with higher odds of overall CHDs, VSD, and ASD, supporting smoking cessation before conception and during pregnancy as a prevention priority. Exploratory associations involving maternal diseases and treatments require further investigation and should not be used to infer treatment effects or guide treatment decisions.

articles.title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes and associated maternal and infection-related factors in a rural malaria-endemic setting in Western Kenya.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Maternal health during pregnancy is critical for favorable birth outcomes and long-term wellbeing of both mothers and infants. Women in rural, malaria-endemic regions face unique biological and socioeconomic challenges that may increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). This study investigated the proportions and determinants of APOs among pregnant women attending antenatal care at Webuye sub-County Hospital in Western Kenya, a rural malaria-endemic setting.
METHODS: A secondary data analysis was conducted utilizing previously collected data of 302 women enrolled at different gestational ages and followed through delivery in a prospective cohort study. Maternal demographic, clinical, and infection-related factors were assessed, and associations with APOs were evaluated using chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Maternal age and gestational age at enrollment were significantly associated with malaria history (P-value <0.001). Maternal anemia (9.9%), abortion (6.3%), preterm birth (4.4%), miscarriage (1.7%), low birth weight (3.4%), stillbirth (7.6 per 1,000 births), neonatal death (3.8 per 1,000 live births) occurred at varying frequencies, indicating a range of adverse outcomes in the study cohort. Younger mothers (<20 years) and older mothers (>35 years) had a higher proportion of anemia (P-value = 0.026) than those aged 21-35 years, and reported malaria history was significantly associated with maternal anemia at enrolment (p-value = 0.02). An additional analysis using microscopy-confirmed malaria status showed a similar difference in hemoglobin levels between microscopy-positive and microscopy-negative participants (p-value < .001). Abnormal urinalysis findings suggestive of urinary tract infection were significantly associated with low birth weight (p-value = 0.031). No significant associations were found between APOs and infant sex, parity, gravidity, or maternal ABO blood type.
DISCUSSION: These findings describe the proportions of the occurrence of adverse outcomes in this rural population and identify maternal age, malaria exposure and abnormal urinalysis results as factors associated with selected outcomes. Strengthening malaria prevention, urinary infection screening, and encouraging early antenatal care attendance are critical to improving maternal and neonatal outcomes. Targeted interventions for adolescent and older mothers, along with enhanced point-of-care diagnostics, may reduce preventable complications in similar resource-limited, malaria-endemic settings.

articles.title: Profiles of attentional, emotional, and digital functioning and their association with substance use in adolescents.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify exploratory profiles of attentional, emotional, and digital functioning in adolescents and examine differences in anxiety and depressive symptoms and associations with cannabis, alcohol, conventional cigarettes or nicotine-containing e-cigarettes, and energy drink consumption.
METHOD: A cross-sectional study of 597 Spanish adolescents aged 12-19 years. Profiles were identified by clustering ADHD-compatible symptoms, emotion dysregulation, Internet use in response to negative emotional states, and problematic Internet use. Their psychological characteristics and consumption behaviors were compared, and 12 logistic regression models were fitted adjusting for age, sex, and other concurrent consumption behaviors.
RESULTS: Five exploratory profiles were identified: low vulnerability (40.2%), attentional vulnerability (13.7%), emotional vulnerability (14.4%), high global vulnerability (15.1%), and specific problematic Internet use (16.6%). Profiles differed substantially in anxiety (η² = .332) and depression (η² = .451), especially the high global vulnerability profile. Associations with substance use were small (Cramér's V = .069-.179) and varied by behavior and assessment period. After adjustment for other consumption behaviors and multiple testing, only combined cigarette or nicotine-containing e-cigarette use in the past 30 days retained a significant incremental global association with profiles (Δχ²[4] = 16.77; p = .002; q = .026).
CONCLUSIONS: The profiles primarily differentiated concurrent anxiety-depression distress, whereas associations with substance use were limited and heterogeneous. Their utility is exploratory and descriptive, although they may help guide the development of preventive or clinical interventions.

articles.title: Maternal and paternal adverse childhood experiences and parent-child disconnectedness in later life.
articles.abstract: Childhood is a sensitive life stage during which significant adversity can set in motion chains of disadvantage in social relationships across the life course. Thus, older parents' adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) may shape the quality of their relationships with adult children. Although rates of disconnectedness tend to be higher for fathers, prior research primarily focused on mothers, overlooking potential gender differences. Using data from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE; N = 38,900), we run logistic regressions to examine how both mothers' and fathers' ACEs (physical abuse, emotional neglect, parental absence, poverty, and peer isolation) relate to parent-child disconnectedness, defined as having no contact with at least one child. Each of the five parental ACEs is associated with a higher likelihood of parent-child disconnectedness in later life, with cumulative effects across ACEs. Patterns are highly similar for mothers and fathers, suggesting that the mechanisms linking parental ACEs to adult intergenerational relationship quality are largely gender neutral. Our findings highlight how early adversity reverberates across generations, shaping the parent-child bond well into later life in similar ways for mothers and fathers. This underscores the need for policies that protect children from ACEs and mitigate their long-term consequences.

articles.title: Early Continuous Glucose Monitoring to Lower the Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in Women With Pre-Pregnancy Obesity: Protocol for the Multicentre Randomised Controlled Trial (GLOW).
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pre-pregnancy obesity substantially increases the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet preventive strategies before routine GDM screening remain limited. The Glucose monitoring to Lower risk of GDM in Obese pregnant Women (GLOW) trial aims to determine whether continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) initiated in early pregnancy reduces the incidence of GDM in women with pre-pregnancy obesity.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: GLOW is a national, multicentre, open-label, parallel-group randomised controlled trial enrolling 1034 women with pre-pregnancy body mass index ≥ 28 kg/m2, a singleton pregnancy and gestational age ≤ 14+6 weeks at eight hospitals in China. Participants will be randomised 1:1 to routine antenatal care alone or routine antenatal care plus CGM. In the CGM group, five consecutive 14-day sensors will be used from 14+0-14+6 to 24+0-24+6 weeks of gestation (70 days in total), with access to glucose values and standardised CGM education. The primary endpoint is the incidence of GDM diagnosed by a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24+0-24+6 weeks. Secondary outcomes include gestational weight gain, maternal metabolic and anthropometric measures, lifestyle behaviours and maternal and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: GLOW will determine whether early CGM introduced before routine GDM screening can reduce GDM incidence and favourably influence maternal metabolic and pregnancy outcomes in women with pre-pregnancy obesity. The findings may inform the role of early CGM as a preventive strategy in this high-risk population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2600130043.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of a Cluster Randomised Whole of Systems Trial of Prevention Strategies for Childhood Obesity (WHO STOPS).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To report a cost-effectiveness analysis of the Whole of Systems Trial of Prevention Strategies for Childhood Obesity (WHO STOPS) intervention, which was a cluster randomised trial aiming to prevent obesity in primary school children from Victoria, Australia.
METHODS: Ten communities were randomly allocated (1:1) to the intervention and control communities in 2015. A cost-effectiveness analysis and the resources generated from the project investment were conducted from the government and societal perspectives. Costs (AUD, 2026) were estimated from project team records, organisation records, staff interviews and questionnaires. Outcomes were measured as body mass index (BMI)z (estimated using students' height and weight measured in 2015, 2017 and 2019) and children's health-related quality of life (HRQoL) (measured using the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory 4.0).
RESULTS: Over the 2-year period, the average cost per community was $382,905 for government ($314 per student) and $398,964 for society ($328 per student). No effect was found for BMIz. It costs $138 per student (government) or $144 (society) to achieve a change of one point in children's HRQoL from 2017 to 2015. For every dollar of project funding, an additional $0.02-0.58 of community resources was generated.
CONCLUSIONS: WHO STOPS was not cost-effective in changing BMIz but had the potential to change children's HRQoL and build community capacity to generate investment over and above the initial funding. Further studies should explore the long-term cost-benefit of such system interventions.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR): ACTRN12616000980437.

articles.title: Prenatal alcohol exposure and adolescent sleep in clinical pathways: a commentary on Devine et al.
articles.abstract: Devine et al. provide timely evidence that parent-reported adolescent sleep disturbances are associated with prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development cohort, even when most exposure was low to moderate. This commentary argues that the central contribution of the study is not only the replication of a sleep signal after PAE, but the identification of a clinically recognisable phenotype: sleep-wake transition problems, excessive somnolence, and possible sleep breathing symptoms. We highlight three implications: sleep should be treated as a developmental mediator and modifiable target, future studies should triangulate retrospective PAE and parent-reported sleep with objective measures, and prevention messages about alcohol in pregnancy should be paired with non-stigmatising family support. Building clinical pathways from screening to intervention may transform small epidemiologic effects into meaningful benefits for affected adolescents.

articles.title: Not all food avoidance is the same: a latent profile analysis informed by the Appetite Self-Regulation model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Food avoidance is a common problem for some children and negatively affects their dietary quality. The Appetite Self-Regulation (ASR) model proposes that food avoidance phenotypes arise in children due to interactions between bottom-up and top-down processes. However, it is unknown how these factors combine within children to produce distinct food avoidant profiles. This study aimed to better understand different types of food avoidance by identifying food avoidant profiles in middle childhood and examining their neurodevelopmental correlates.
METHODS: Participants were 517 parents of children aged 5-12 years. Latent profile analysis was conducted using multiple ASR domains, including appetitive traits (satiety responsiveness, slowness in eating, food responsiveness, enjoyment of food and food fussiness), temperament traits (fear, shyness, inhibitory control, impulsivity), food avoidance behaviours (food avoidance, texture sensitivity and cognitive rigidity) and liking of low- and high-energy-density foods (vegetable and snack liking). Multinomial logistic regression examined associations between profile membership and neurodevelopmental disorders.
RESULTS: Five profiles were identified, including two food avoidant profiles. Multi-Domain Food Avoidant profile (n = 114, 22%) was characterised by a multi-domain form of avoidance, particularly showing higher levels of fear and shyness, suggesting greater bottom-up emotional reactivity to foods. The Rigid Texture-Sensitive Avoidant profile (n = 66, 13%) showed the highest texture sensitivity and cognitive rigidity, indicating a sensory-driven pathway to food avoidance. The Rigid Texture-Sensitive Avoidant profile was also characterised by the lowest inhibitory control, reflecting reduced top-down regulatory capacity. Children with neurodevelopmental disorders were disproportionately represented in the food avoidant profiles.
CONCLUSIONS: Food avoidance in middle childhood reflects heterogeneous behavioural patterns shaped by different combinations of bottom-up avoidance processes and top-down regulatory control. Identifying distinct avoidant profiles may improve understanding of the processes underlying children's food avoidance and inform more targeted approaches to supporting children with persistent avoidant eating behaviours.

articles.title: Psychotropic medication use in early pregnancy: impacts on child socio-emotional and behavioral development.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical symptoms of distress (anxiety or depression) affect around 10%-25% of women during the perinatal period, which, if left untreated, can adversely affect both maternal health and child development. Psychotropic medications are often first-line treatments for maternal distress in pregnancy, but their effects on child socio-emotional development remain underexplored. This study aims to compare socio-emotional and behavioral development of children at 18 and 36 months according to early pregnancy exposure to treated or untreated maternal distress.
METHODS: This project is based on the Montreal Antenatal Well-Being Study, a prospective cohort study of 1,130 pregnant individuals from Quebec, Canada. Women self-reported their medication use and were categorized as: (1) Untreated maternal distress, (2) Psychotropic medication use, (3) Control group (no maternal distress, no psychotropic medication). Analyses of covariance were used to examine the associations between exposure groups and indices of child socio-emotional and behavioral development, assessed using the Early Childhood Behavior Questionnaire and the Child Behavior Checklist. To better account for baseline symptom severity and treatment indication, propensity score weighting was used to create comparable groups with balanced covariates such as socioeconomic status and health care access.
RESULTS: Approximately 9.4% of women reported psychotropic medication use in early pregnancy. Analyses of covariance showed that maternal psychotropic medication use was associated with child inhibited temperament at 18 months and greater social withdrawal at 36 months. Propensity weighting revealed that these associations were largely driven by unmeasured confounding, showing no lasting associations with medication. In contrast, children born to mothers with untreated distress had poorer socio-emotional development.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings underscore the critical importance of appropriate statistical control of confounding in observational studies of maternal medication use and child outcomes. They also emphasize the impact of maternal distress on child development and the need for access to effective perinatal treatments.

articles.title: Prospective associations between prolonged sleep onset latency and the co-development of sleep disturbances and mental health problems among preschoolers: a population-based longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbances and mental health problems frequently co-occur in childhood, but their symptom-level dynamics during early development remain unclear. Prolonged sleep onset latency (SOL) may be sensitive to changes in both domains during the preschool years, when expanding psychosocial demands and structured routines may challenge sleep initiation. We examined longitudinal symptom-level associations between sleep disturbances and mental health problems to identify potential symptoms with prominent prospective links, particularly prolonged SOL, that may inform symptom-specific early prevention strategies.
METHODS: Data came from a three-wave cohort of children aged 3-6 years recruited from 191 preschools in Shanghai, China. Parent-reported sleep disturbances and mental health problems were assessed using the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) and the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ). Cross-lagged panel network models examined longitudinal symptom-level associations. Prolonged SOL was assessed using frequency-based and duration-based measures from the CSHQ sleep onset delay item and parent-reported SOL duration (>20 min), and examined in relation to subsequent mental health problems using logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 16,575 children (mean [SD] age, 3.73 [.29] years; 51.9% boys), co-occurring sleep disturbances and mental health problems were 9.6%, 7.0%, and 6.1% from wave1 to wave3. Sleep-onset-delay showed high out-expected influence in both adjacent-wave networks (.30 and .34), indicating prominent prospective associations with subsequent symptoms of sleep disturbances and mental health problems. Frequency-based prolonged SOL was associated with overall mental health problems at both subsequent waves (AORs = 1.32-1.33, both ps < .001), while duration-based prolonged SOL (>20 min) was consistently associated with subsequent hyperactivity (AORs = 1.26-1.28, both ps < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged SOL showed prominent prospective associations within the co-development of sleep disturbances and mental health problems and may serve as an early signal and potential intervention target for promoting sleep and mental health in preschool children.

articles.title: Tailored Dosing Recommendations for Amikacin in Severely Ill Children: A Population Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Evaluation using Cmax/MIC and AUC/MIC-based Indices.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Optimal amikacin dosing in severely ill patients remains challenging due to maturational and pathophysiological alterations affecting the pharmacokinetics (PK). This study aimed to develop a population PK model for amikacin, evaluate pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) indices, and propose personalised dosing recommendations for this patient population.
METHODS: A prospective PK study was conducted in 38 severely ill children receiving intravenous 20 mg/kg amikacin every 24h. PK parameters were determined using nonlinear mixed-effects modelling (Monolix 2024R1). Probability of target attainment (PTA) was simulated for the minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 2 mg/L and 8 mg/L for Enterobacterales. Evaluated PK/PD targets were a peak concentration (Cmax)/MIC ≥ 8 and a 24h area under the concentration-time curve (AUC0-24h)/MIC ≥ 62.5h, in combination with a trough concentration (Ctrough) ≤ 5 mg/L toxicity threshold.
RESULTS: A two-compartment model with a priori allometric weight scaling on the PK parameters best described the data. Clearance was predicted using the Bouvet estimated glomerular filtration (eGFR) formula, combining creatinine and cystatin C. The central volume of distribution was 41% lower in oncology patients compared with intensive care patients. The population parameters for clearance and the total volume of distribution were 7.4 L/h/70 kg and 39.0 L/70 kg, respectively. AUC0-24h/MIC, as PK/PD index, was less frequently attained than the Cmax/MIC index. For a MIC of 2 mg/L, a dose of 20 mg/kg every 18h achieved a 100% PTA for the targets Cmax/MIC ≥ 8, AUC0-24h/MIC ≥ 62.5h, and Ctrough ≤ 5 mg/L in typical patients with a 120-150 mL/min/1.73 m2 eGFR, compared with ≤76% for the current regimen. For a MIC of 8 mg/L, ≥80% PTA could not be achieved.
CONCLUSIONS: Current amikacin dosing regimens may result in subtherapeutic exposure, particularly in intensive care patients with high eGFR or when targeting higher MIC values or AUC/MIC targets. Optimised dosing regimens were proposed.

articles.title: Multicenter observational cohort study of clinical and viral features of human metapneumovirus infection in hospitalized children, Taiwan, 2023-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of respiratory tract infections (RTIs) in children. This study examined the circulation, seasonality, and clinical characteristics of pediatric hMPV infection in Taiwan during the three years following the COVID-19 pandemic.
METHODS: We enrolled children hospitalized with molecularly confirmed hMPV infection at three hospitals in Taiwan between January 2023 and December 2025. The study comprised two periods: Period 1 (January 2023 to June 2024), a retrospective review of medical records, and Period 2 (July 2024 to December 2025), a prospective enrollment with written informed consent and collection of nasopharyngeal specimens. Genotyping was performed on a subset of respiratory samples collected during Period 2.
RESULTS: Of 3310 hospitalized children tested for RTIs, 390 (11.8%) were confirmed to have hMPV infection, of whom 342 were enrolled and analyzed. hMPV peaked from February to April. The median patient age was 2.77 years. Most patients presented with lower RTIs (93.6%); 41.5% had underlying conditions, 66.4% had antibiotic use, 43.9% had viral co-infection, 17.1% required intensive care, and 39.8% required respiratory support. The median hospital stay was 6 days. Four sublineages co-circulated, with A2.2.2 (51.6%) and B2 (24.2%) predominating. Clinical presentations did not differ significantly between hMPV subgroups A and B. A significant temporal shift toward younger patients was observed, driven mainly by an increase in infants aged 0-1 year (p for trend = 0.004).
CONCLUSIONS: hMPV contributes substantially to pediatric RTIs in Taiwan and shows distinct spring seasonality. Sublineage A2.2.2 predominated, whereas B2 increased during the 2024-2025 season. The shift toward younger affected children during the three-year observation period may suggest changing patterns of pediatric susceptibility but requires confirmation in large-scale, well-designed prospective studies.

articles.title: Increased incidence of group A streptococcal infections requiring hospitalization following the COVID-19 pandemic, with no change in the proportion of invasive disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess changes in group A Streptococcus (GAS) infections in hospitalized children and adults between pre-pandemic and post-pandemic periods in Alicante, Spain.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study including all patients hospitalized with GAS infection between January 2015 and December 2025. Incidence rates were calculated per 10,000 hospital admissions and per 100,000 population. Temporal trends were analyzed using Poisson regression models and expressed as incidence rate ratios (IRR).
RESULTS: 456 hospitalized GAS infections were identified, 75 (16.4%) pediatric and 381 (83.6%) adult cases; 298 (65.4%) non-invasive and 158 (34.6%) invasives. The annual number of cases increased from 13 in 2015-84 in 2023. Overall incidence doubled in the post-pandemic compared with the pre-pandemic period (hospital-based IRR 2.53, 95% CI 2.05-3.12; population-based IRR 2.40, 95% CI 1.94-2.96). The increase was greater in adults (IRR 1.17; 95% CI 1.13-1.21) than in children (IRR 1.08; 95% CI 0.98-1.19). The proportion of invasive infections remained stable before and after the pandemic (35.0% vs 36.6%; RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.79-1.39). Patients with invasive GAS infection were older and had a higher burden of comorbidity.
CONCLUSIONS: GAS infections increased markedly after the COVID-19 pandemic. It was not accompanied by an increase in the proportion of invasive infections.

articles.title: Age-Related Tibetan-Han Differences in Continuity of Care Among Insured Populations in High-Altitude Western China: Retrospective Longitudinal Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuity of Care (CoC) is an important dimension of health system performance and health equity, reflecting whether individuals can maintain stable and coordinated care relationships over time, rather than merely gaining access to services. Although ethnic differences in CoC have been documented, most existing studies have examined average group differences and have paid limited attention to whether such differences vary across the life course. Claims-based analyses can provide a population-level approach to monitoring CoC and identifying age-specific equity gaps in routine health service use.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine whether Tibetan-Han differences in CoC vary by age among insured populations in high-altitude western China and to assess whether these age-related patterns differ across outpatient, inpatient, chronic disease, and nonchronic disease care settings.
METHODS: We used deidentified health insurance claims data from 3 major cities in high-altitude western China between January 1, 2021, and December 1, 2024. After data cleaning, we constructed a person-year dataset and restricted analyses to individuals with at least 3 annual health care encounters, yielding 850,469 person-years. The Bice-Boxerman CoC index was the primary outcome. Fixed-effects models with year and insurance-region fixed effects included ethnicity, age, age squared, and their interaction terms, adjusting for covariates derived from the Andersen behavioral model. SEs were clustered at the individual level. Subgroup analyses were conducted for outpatient, inpatient, chronic disease, and nonchronic disease samples.
RESULTS: Mean CoC in the overall sample was 0.52 (SD 0.33). A significant nonlinear interaction between ethnicity and age was observed. Fixed-effects models showed a positive Tibetan coefficient (β=0.0582, P<.001), a negative ethnicity × age interaction (β=-0.0035, P<.001), and a significant ethnicity × age² interaction (P<.001). Outpatient results were similar. Inpatient analyses showed an overall disadvantage for Tibetans (β=-0.0795, P<.001) and a different age pattern. No significant age interaction was found in the chronic disease sample, whereas significant age heterogeneity remained in the nonchronic disease sample. Age-group analyses showed the largest Tibetan advantage at ages 20 to 25 and significantly lower continuity in most groups aged 35 to 75.
CONCLUSIONS: Ethnic differences in CoC were age-dependent and nonlinear rather than constant across age groups. Because the study covers 4 calendar years, these age-related associations may also reflect birth-cohort differences and should not be interpreted as within-person aging effects. Policies should pay greater attention to continuity barriers faced by middle-aged and older Tibetan populations.

articles.title: Machine learning-integrated full-length 16S rRNA gene profiling reveals early-life gut microbial signatures associated with subsequent infantile colic in Thai infants.
articles.abstract: Infantile colic develops after the neonatal period, but neonatal gut microbial patterns preceding symptom onset remain unclear. We examined early-life gut microbiome associations with subsequent infantile colic and internally evaluated microbiome-only prediction alongside retrospective metadata-containing comparisons. Stool samples collected 0-4 days after birth from 209 Thai infants (119 healthy and 90 who later met Rome IV diagnostic criteria for infantile colic) were profiled by Oxford Nanopore full-length 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing. Analyses included diversity and composition assessments, covariate-adjusted MaAsLin3 models, repeated nested cross-validation, and exploratory conditional association networks. Infants who subsequently developed infantile colic had lower Chao1 richness than healthy infants (q = 8.7 × 10-5), although delivery mode and collection day explained more community variation than outcome status. After covariate adjustment, Enterococcus faecium presence was associated with subsequent colic (odds ratio, 4.23; q = 0.021). The fully nested model-development procedure yielded participant-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) values of 0.773 and 0.740. In a secondary fixed-model comparison including feeding summarized through one month, a species-presence radial basis function support vector machine outperformed metadata alone (mean outer-fold AUROC/AUPRC, 0.780/0.764 vs. 0.539/0.484), while adding metadata produced only a small, uncertain improvement. Exploratory network analysis contextualized candidate taxa within group-specific conditional association modules. These findings support a focused early-life species-level pattern associated with subsequent infantile colic and prioritize candidate microbial features for external validation.

articles.title: Genotype-phenotype investigation of evolving mutations associated with antimalarial resistance among Senegalese Plasmodium falciparum malaria parasites.
articles.abstract: Drug resistance in Plasmodium falciparum threatens malaria control and elimination efforts, particularly where sustained chemoprevention and treatment have driven parasite evolution. Senegal has implemented antimalarial strategies for two decades, including sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy and SP plus amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in children. We analyzed whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 2,805 monogenomic P. falciparum infections collected from febrile, treatment-seeking patients across Senegal between 2006 and 2022. Wild-type (WT), drug-sensitive alleles at four major resistance loci (Pfcrt, Pfmdr1, Pfdhfr, and Pfdhps) were rare, while resistance-associated variants, including Pfcrt K76T, the canonical Pfdhfr triple mutant (N51I, C59R, S108N), and Pfdhps A437G, predominated. To define how these genotypes shape drug response and parasite fitness, we cultured 33 clinical isolates representing 26 common combined haplotypes, which together accounted for 63.9% of infections in the WGS dataset. Multivariable mixed-effects models revealed drug- and background-dependent effects. Relative to the Pfcrt WT, the CVIET background increased monodesethyl-amodiaquine EC50 approximately 1.4-fold; adding N326S or I356T produced cumulative increases of approximately 2.6-fold and 3.2-fold, respectively. The Pfdhfr triple mutant increased pyrimethamine EC50 approximately 2,196-fold relative to Pfdhfr WT. For sulfadoxine, Pfdhps A437G was associated with an approximately 463,000-fold increase in EC50 relative to WT, while Pfdhps S436A had little effect. Pairwise competitive growth outcomes analyzed with a Bradley-Terry model showed reduced competitive ability for Pfcrt CVIET, partially rescued by Pfmdr1 Y184F; Pfdhps S436A increased whereas A613S reduced competitive ability. These findings reveal resistance-fitness trade-offs that may shape P. falciparum evolution as antimalarial policies change across Africa.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States.
