Strengthening access, continuity of treatment, and adherence support should remain clinical and public health priorities, while prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm causality.

articles.title: Health worker perspectives on the screening and management of hypertensive disorders and diabetes in pregnancy in Uganda: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) and diabetes in pregnancy (DIP) are leading contributors to maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, yet effective management depends on health workers having the knowledge, attitudes, and practices to screen, diagnose, and treat these conditions. Evidence on these provider-level factors remains limited in Uganda.
METHODS: We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional survey among health workers in Uganda (November-December 2025), disseminating a structured questionnaire on HDP and DIP knowledge, attitudes, practices, prescribing, and task shifting via WhatsApp-based Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) networks and professional association platforms, hosted on REDCap. We analysed data in STATA 17 using descriptive statistics and comparisons across health worker groups.
RESULTS: Of the 690 eligible health workers, 577 completed the survey (83.5%). Midwives comprised the largest group (341, 59.1%) and most worked in public facilities (425, 73.7%). Knowledge and protocol integration were substantially stronger for HDP than DIP: CPD attendance was 70.9% for HDP versus 36.4% for DIP, self-reported protocol familiarity was 90.1% versus 38.6%, and routine BP screening was near-universal (538, 93.2%) while only 122 (21.1%) always screened for diabetes in pregnancy. Correct oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) thresholds were identified by only 186 (32.2%). Attitudes reflected strong support for patient involvement in treatment decisions and consistent treatment targets, with moderate confidence in guideline-based adjustments (279, 48.4%). Prescribing prioritised affordability (438, 75.9%) and reliable drug supply (473, 82.0%). Task shifting was widely accepted for basic functions including BP measurement (538, 93.2%) and lifestyle counselling (514, 89.1%), but less so for algorithm-based prescribing (170, 29.5%). Cadre differences were consistent across domains: for HDP, correct identification of severe preeclampsia features and use of advanced diagnostics were significantly lower among midwives than specialist cadres (p < 0.001); for DIP, gaps were most pronounced among midwives, with the lowest DIP CPD attendance (105, 30.8%) and OGTT endorsement (186, 54.5%) of all cadres (p < 0.001). Advanced diagnostic use and OGTT endorsement also increased progressively with facility level (p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Health workers in Uganda demonstrate substantially stronger knowledge, attitudes, and practices for HDP than for DIP, with consistent cadre-related differences. Under-recognition of DIP likely contributes to missed opportunities for timely intervention. Targeted CPD on DIP, wider protocol dissemination, and system-level support for diabetes screening are urgently needed. Leveraging existing RMNCAH networks offers a practical pathway for integrating DIP into routine antenatal care.

articles.title: Gamma-delta T cells in neuroblastoma: Exploiting MHC-independent recognition to overcome the barriers of high-risk disease.
articles.abstract: Neuroblastoma is the most frequent extracranial solid tumor in children and the main cause of early childhood cancer deaths. Relapse occurs in more than half of high-risk patients despite rigorous multimodal therapy, and four-year overall survival in relapsed disease is approximately 20%. Anti-GD2 monoclonal antibodies and GD2-directed CAR T cell treatment have advanced the field, although neither has eliminated neuroblastoma's immune resistance. Current immunotherapy has three interrelated challenges. GD2 heterogeneity lets antigen-negative subclones escape and cause recurrence. Inhibitory cytokines, regulatory T cells, and myeloid-derived suppressor cells dominate the TME. MHC class I downregulation frequently renders traditional αβ T cell methods ineffective, even with the target antigen present. Gamma-delta (γδ) T cells offer a distinct mechanism. They recognize tumor targets without antigen presentation by sensing stress-induced ligands through NKG2D and DNAM-1 and phosphoantigens through butyrophilin proteins BTN3A1 and BTN2A1. This recognition holds regardless of MHC class I status. In conjunction with anti-GD2 antibodies, CD16 expression boosts antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. In neuroblastoma lesions, γδ T cells are the primary antitumoral fraction in tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte products, indicating compatibility with the disease's immune system. This study examines neuroblastoma immunotherapy failure mechanisms and innovative γδ T cell platforms, such as non-engineered allogeneic products, composite γδ T plus NK cell techniques, and CAR- and AbTCR-modified designs. A biomarker-driven patient selection paradigm and product standardization, in vivo persistence, and TME suppression are examined. NCT05400603, the first trial of adoptive transfer of ex vivo-expanded allogeneic γδ T cells in a population that includes pediatric neuroblastoma patients, is crucial for proving the mechanism.

articles.title: Culture-independent identification and serotyping of Streptococcus pneumoniae by targeted metagenomics in pleural fluid samples.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the leading cause of empyema and pneumonia in children and monitoring of effectiveness of polyvalent pneumococcal vaccines has been essential for controlling invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) in children and elderly adults. Conventional serotyping of pneumococci has relied on Quellung reaction following laboratory culture; however, more recently whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has been implemented in many reference laboratories to enhance traditional typing. Pleural fluid samples from cases with empyema are often culture negative, limiting the utility of WGS and requiring PCR or 16S rRNA sequencing to detect S. pneumoniae. These molecular methods have limited sensitivity and capacity to characterize pneumococcus in clinical samples, especially in specimens with a low pathogen abundance. This study applied capture-based enrichment [(targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS)] to identify and characterize S. pneumoniae directly from pleural fluid samples. A total of 50 pleural fluid samples were subjected to tNGS with a custom probe panel, including 39 known positive fluids collected from IPD cases between 2018 and 2025 in New South Wales, Australia. tNGS results were benchmarked against molecular-based serotyping. Our tNGS achieved 100% sensitivity and specificity in detecting S. pneumoniae. Serotyping results were concordant with PCR, and 95% (37/39) of S. pneumoniae PCR-positive pleural fluid cases could be serotyped using tNGS. Standard molecular methods, however, could only determine serotype in 56% (22/39) of samples. This tNGS enabled 39% improvement in ability to directly identify and serotype IPD-associated serotypes of S. pneumoniae in difficult-to-culture pleural fluids, which can significantly enhance laboratory surveillance of IPD as well as our understanding of vaccine effectiveness.

articles.title: The hidden burden of insomnia in late pregnancy: prevalence and risk factors among Egyptian women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep condition that has a harmful impact on one's quality of life and presents considerable health hazards, especially for pregnant women in their third trimester. It can lead to stress, postpartum depression and negative fetal outcomes. The prevalence and contributing variables of insomnia among pregnant women in Egypt have not been adequately studied. This study evaluated the prevalence of insomnia among third trimester pregnant women in Egypt and analyzed the associated risk factors.
SUBJECTS AND METHODS: This is a cross-sectional study of pregnant women in the third trimester at Menoufia University Hospital. The study included 390 participants. The study employed a pre-structured questionnaire that includes questions about sociodemographic and lifestyle attributes, accompanied by the ISI questionnaire used to diagnose and assess insomnia severity.
RESULTS: A total of 390 pregnant women in the third trimester completed the questionnaire. The prevalence of insomnia was 75.4% (n = 294), with 33.1% categorized as sub-threshold, 26.2% as moderate, and 16.2% as severe. Multivariate logistic regression identified maternal age 25-35 years (AOR = 4.57, 95% CI: 2.50-8.36) and age > 35 years (AOR = 3.27, 95% CI: 1.01-9.70) as significant risk factors. Conversely, university education (AOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.11-0.61), overweight BMI (AOR = 0.32, 95% CI: 0.16-0.62), and rural residence (AOR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.30-0.95) were significant protective factors. Linear regression further confirmed that higher insomnia severity scores were predicted by increased maternal age, while overweight BMI (B = -3.10), rural residence (B = -1.98), and nulliparity (B = -3.69) were significant negative predictors of severity (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Insomnia is highly prevalent among pregnant women, particularly in the third trimester. Advanced maternal age and urban residence were associated with a higher risk and severity of insomnia, while higher education and nulliparity appear protective. Further research is needed to develop strategies to improve maternal well-being and reduce adverse outcomes for mothers and infants.

articles.title: U.S. preterm birth rates reduced nationwide, particularly among medically-induced deliveries, during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown period.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: During the early months of the COVID-19 pandemic, many studies-particularly from wealthy nations-reported a drop in preterm birth rates. Our goal was to examine nationwide changes in U.S. preterm births in relation to a range of sociodemographic, perinatal conditions, and obstetric care factors.
METHODS: Using data from the publicly available natality files from the National Center for Health Statistics, we examined 25,767,850 observations of all U.S. registered singleton births during the months of April to June (i.e. early pandemic lockdown months) for the years 2015 to 2021. To control for seasonal shifts and focus on the early onset of the pandemic, we calculated average annual preterm birth rates (< 37 weeks gestation) between the months of April to June. We used these observed rates to generate predicted rates for 2020 and 2021, and stratified by sociodemographic and medical characteristics of interest.
RESULTS: The nationwide preterm birth rate has been increasing since 2015, but this trend was temporarily interrupted by a significant decrease in the early months of the pandemic. Preterm birth rates dropped for nearly everyone regardless of their sociodemographic characteristics. Additionally, there was a significant and steeper drop for late compared to early preterm births, for preterm home births compared to preterm hospital births, and significantly lower rates of preterm birth among those with induced births (c-section or vaginal). The average number of prenatal visits decreased in these months, and preterm birth rates significantly decreased among those with low (0-10) and average (11-15) number of prenatal visits. The decrease in preterm birth rates during this period was also accompanied by a decrease in fetal death rates, and decreases in neonatal and maternal intensive care admissions.
CONCLUSION: Our analyses indicate a potentially unintended interim health benefit of the pandemic across nearly all sociodemographic groups, with significant decreases particularly among induced preterm births. These findings, paired with reduced rates of fetal deaths and maternal and neonatal ICU admissions, suggest that in some cases, less intervention may have served as a benefit to reproductive outcomes. These results support the reduction in prenatal visits recommended by the 2025 national obstetric guidelines.

articles.title: "I do not want to do that alone": couples' experiences navigating hybrid perinatal care during a public health crisis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic challenged healthcare systems to balance infection prevention with equitable, patient-centered perinatal care. Risk-mitigation policies including restricted visitor access and rapid adoption of telehealth were intended to protect maternal and infant health. While many studies focus on the birthing individual, few studies have examined the perspectives of both members of a couple or how hybrid models of care may address gaps exposed during a public health crisis.
METHODS: We conducted a qualitative study of couples early in the pandemic to examine perinatal care experiences among pregnant/postpartum women and their partners. Participants were drawn from a prior pilot study focused on reducing anxiety and depression; eligible pregnant women screened positive for elevated symptoms (GAD-7 or PHQ-9 ≥ 10) and were cohabiting with a consenting partner. All trial participants were invited to an interview; data were collected from all who accepted. Semi-structured interviews were conducted individually via Zoom and explored experiences of healthcare engagement, perceptions of pandemic-related policy, and the role of perinatal support people. Forty-two interviews with 20 women and 9 partners were audio-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis supported by team-based coding and a consensus-driven analytic process.
FINDINGS: Three major themes emerged with virtual care functioning as a crosscutting element across themes: (1) Inclusion of Support People, including isolating experiences, fear of receiving traumatic news, partner perspectives, and the role of doulas; (2) Virtual Care: Necessity and Promise, highlighting both the benefits and limitations of telehealth; and (3) Navigating Perinatal Care, encompassing perceptions of care quality, policy inconsistencies, and adaptations to safety measures.
CONCLUSIONS: Emergency perinatal policies must be clear, consistent, and adaptable to meet patient needs while preserving the presence of essential support people. In this study we found hybrid prenatal care models that combine telehealth and in-person support were valued for clear communication, and support presence. However, their effects on experience, satisfaction, and preparedness cannot be assumed from these data and require further study among perinatal couples.

articles.title: The association between intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy and risk of small for gestational age in China: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify the relationship of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) with the occurrence risk of small for gestational age (SGA) in China.
METHODS: The Chinese National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Medline and Web of Science databases were searched for available studies. Relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were combined and subgroup analysis based on the specific comorbidity was conducted.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies with 24712 cases were included. The incidence rates of SGA among the ICP and non-ICP patients were 14.04% (294/2094) and 4.66% (1053/22618), respectively. Pooled results demonstrated that ICP was significantly related to the occurrence of SGA (RR=3.12, 95% CI: 1.99-4.88, P＜0.001) in Chinese pregnant women. Subgroup analysis based on specific comorbidity also showed the relationship between ICP and SGA among patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (RR=6.09, 95% CI: 2.96-12.55, P＜0.001) and hepatitis B virus infection (RR=3.22, 95% CI: 1.69-6.12, P＜0.001).
CONCLUSION: In China, ICP was associated with the occurrence of SGA in China and pregnant patients with ICP experienced a significantly higher risk of SGA.

articles.title: PROTECT: PRegnancy Outcomes using continuous glucose monitoring TEChnology in pregnant women with early-onset Type 2 diabetes: a multicentre randomised controlled trial - study protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-onset type 2 diabetes (EOT2D), meaning type 2 diabetes diagnosed before the age of 40 disproportionately affects women from socially deprived and minority ethnic groups. EOT2D is now the most common form of pre-existing diabetes complicating pregnancy. These pregnancies carry high risks of congenital anomalies, stillbirth, neonatal death, and of both maternal and neonatal morbidity. Maternal glycaemia is the key modifiable risk factor yet remains suboptimal and is often accompanied by limited self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG). Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) offers continuous real-time glucose profiles, potentially enabling better dietary, lifestyle and therapy adjustments.
METHODS / DESIGN: The PROTECT trial is a multicentre, randomised controlled trial designed to evaluate whether CGM improves maternal glucose and neonatal outcomes in women with EOT2D. The trial will recruit 422 pregnant participants (≤ 16 weeks 0 days' gestation, HbA1c ≥ 43 mmol/mol) from around 20 UK NHS antenatal diabetes clinics. After a run-in phase with masked CGM, participants will be randomised to either real-time CGM (FreeStyle Libre 3) or standard SMBG. The primary maternal outcome is percentage of time in pregnancy-specific glucose target range (3.5-7.8 mmol/L). The primary neonatal outcome is a composite of neonatal care unit admission or death. Secondary outcomes include maternal HbA1c, glycaemic variability, insulin use, obstetric complications, neonatal morbidity, psychosocial measures, and cost-effectiveness. An internal pilot will assess recruitment feasibility, before proceeding to the full trial. Qualitative interviews with women and healthcare professionals will explore barriers and facilitators to CGM use. Statistical analyses will follow intention-to-treat principles.
DISCUSSION: This is the largest trial to date investigating CGM in EOT2D pregnancy, aiming to generate robust evidence on clinical efficacy, lived experiences, and economic impact, informing future NHS policy and practice.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN12804317 Registration Date: 23/10/2023.

articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Lisdexamfetamine Dimesylate in Paediatric Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Assessed by Physicians and School Teachers: A Post-marketing Surveillance Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lisdexamfetamine dimesylate (LDX) is a long-acting prodrug approved for the treatment of paediatric attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in Japan. This multicentre, prospective, post-marketing surveillance study evaluated real-world safety and effectiveness of LDX in children and adolescents with ADHD in Japan.
METHODS: Patients aged 6 to < 18 years initiating LDX between April 2021 and September 2023 were enrolled across 24 medical institutions in Japan. Safety was assessed over 24 weeks by monitoring adverse drug reactions (ADRs), including dependence/abuse events. Effectiveness was evaluated by physicians and school teachers at baseline, and weeks 12 and 24 using the Japanese ADHD rating scale IV (ADHD-RS-IV) questionnaire.
RESULTS: Of the 88 enrolled patients, 73 were included in the safety analysis and 57 in the effectiveness analysis. The mean (standard deviation [SD]) age was 10.4 (2.6) years; 79.5% were male and 20.5% were female. Most patients (90.4%) had received prior ADHD treatment. LDX was initiated at a mean (SD) dose of 26.8 (4.7) mg, with 72.6% continuing treatment at week 24. ADRs occurred in 30.14% of patients; the most common (in ≥ 2 patients) were decreased appetite (17.81%), weight decrease (4.11%), and aggression, insomnia, irritability, middle insomnia, and abdominal pain (each 2.74%). One serious ADR (suicide attempt with methylphenidate overdose, also considered a dependence/abuse event) was reported; LDX was discontinued and the patient recovered the following day. No other dependence/abuse events were reported. Physician- and teacher-rated ADHD-RS-IV total scores improved significantly from baseline: mean (SD) changes were - 10.1 (8.0; p < 0.0001) at week 12 and - 9.7 (8.5; p < 0.0001) at week 24 for physician-rated scores, and - 4.9 (8.5; p < 0.001) at week 12 and - 5.1 (9.7; p < 0.01) at week 24 for teacher-rated scores.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings from this post-marketing surveillance study of LDX in paediatric patients with ADHD in Japan were consistent with its established safety profile. Patients' ADHD symptoms improved according to both physician and teacher assessments.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN) Clinical Trials Registry (identifier UMIN000046038).

articles.title: The Societal Burden of Sickle Cell Disease: A Life Course Perspective.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sickle cell disease (SCD) places a lifelong burden on patients and family members. Our objective was to review the available evidence to understand the impact of SCD across the life course, including childhood development, education, employment, quality of life, and life expectancy.
METHODS: This targeted literature review examined empirical studies from 2001 to 2026 that assessed the burden of SCD among patients and family caregivers across different life stages, including childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood. Outcomes included early childhood development, education, labor market outcomes, life expectancy, and impact on family caregivers.
RESULTS: Overall, 23 unique studies were included. Studies consistently demonstrated that SCD places a large burden on patients and family caregivers across all life stages, especially for those with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises. Many children with SCD experience significant developmental delays in cognition, while adolescents often experience greater school absenteeism, worse academic performance, and a higher likelihood of school dropout. Caregivers for children with SCD experience lost labor market opportunities and diminished mental health. Adults with SCD are less likely to work (unemployment), and when they do, they often have greater work absenteeism and presenteeism, worse job opportunities, and less income. Ultimately, people with SCD experience both lower overall life expectancy and lower quality of life.
CONCLUSION: Patients with SCD experience a burden associated with the disease across the life course. These outcomes should inform future evaluations of treatment and supportive services for SCD, which have the potential to generate substantial societal value.

articles.title: Vamorolone for DMD: Clinical Pharmacology of a Novel Dissociative Corticosteroid, A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Vamorolone is a dissociative corticosteroid approved for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). This review presents the clinical pharmacology program in support of its development, including dose rationale, pharmacokinetics-pharmacodynamics (PK-PD) modeling, and regulatory alignment. Key findings from early-phase studies, food effect evaluation, special population modeling, bioequivalence assessments, and comparative pharmacology evaluation are summarized. This narrative review synthesized 15 studies/investigations from peer-reviewed publications, regulatory documents, and unpublished sponsor data. Particular attention is given to the evaluation of PK in the target pediatric population across age groups, using population modeling to support individualized dosing. Vamorolone demonstrated dose-proportional PK (i.e., exposure increased in proportion to dose) in the therapeutic range, increased bioavailability with food intake, and a favorable safety profile at doses up to 6 mg/kg/day. PK-PD modeling supported individualized dosing in pediatric patients. In clinical trials and indirect treatment comparisons, vamorolone efficacy was broadly comparable to standard corticosteroids with a differentiated safety profile in which some corticosteroid-class adverse effects (notably effects on bone and growth) appeared attenuated. Clinically relevant, dose-dependent corticosteroid-class-related effects, including hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal-axis suppression, Cushingoid features, increased weight and appetite, behavioral/mood disturbances, headache, and gastrointestinal disorders remain at therapeutic doses. The vamorolone clinical pharmacology program demonstrates how mechanistic innovation related to dissociative glucocorticoid‑receptor signaling, modeling, and strategic regulatory alignment can inform corticosteroid therapy in DMD. The differentiated mechanism of action, efficacy, individualized dosing approach, and differentiated safety profile of vamorolone make it a promising option in DMD care.

articles.title: Gender bias in stereotypes of autism: Assessing the non-prototypicality of autistic women within the autistic group.
articles.abstract: Autistic women face specific challenges and feel they do not fit the autistic prototype. This paper examines the gendered nature of stereotypes towards autistic individuals as a possible underlying mechanism, owing to the apparent incompatibility between stereotypes on autistic individuals and stereotypes on women. In four studies, stereotypes about autistic individuals were analysed through a gendered (Studies 1 and 2) or intersectional lens (Studies 3 and 4). The first two studies used a trait nomination task (Study 1) or ecological traits (Study 2). Contrary to expectations, in these studies, stereotypes towards autistic individuals were represented by traits that are more predominantly perceived as feminine. However, more detailed analysis suggests that this varies according to facets of social evaluation. To deepen these results, two other studies focused on perceptions within the intersectional space. Study 3 underlined that core characteristics associated with autistic individuals are perceived as more representative of autistic men than of autistic women. Finally, a fourth study suggests that autistic women are being perceived differently than the average of autistic individuals and autistic men. These findings suggest that core facets of the stereotypes of autism are more masculine, suggesting a non-prototypicality of autistic women within the autistic community.

articles.title: Study of 34 prospective pregnancies in women receiving IL-1 inhibitors for autoinflammatory diseases and comparison to unexposed pregnancies (GR2 study).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interleukin-1 (IL-1) inhibitors are widely used in autoinflammatory diseases (AID) such as Still’s disease and monogenic inflammasomopathies, including cryopyrinopathies (CAPS) and familial Mediterranean fever. As these conditions frequently affect women of reproductive age and data are limited, concerns remain regarding anti-IL-1 therapy safety during pregnancy. We aimed to evaluate maternal and neonatal outcomes in women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception and pregnancy.
METHODS: This prospective observational study included pregnant women from the Groupe de recherche sur la Grossesse et les Maladies Rares (GR2) prospective cohort, spanning 76 French centres before September 2024. Women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception or pregnancy were selected. Maternal and obstetrical outcomes were compared with a 1:1 matched control group of unexposed women with similar conditions and with the nationwide 2021 French National Perinatal Survey.
RESULTS: Thirty-four pregnancies (three twin pregnancies) in 31 women were exposed to anakinra (n=30) and/or canakinumab (n=5) for Still’s disease (n=15), familial Mediterranean fever (n=15), CAPS (n=3), undifferentiated systemic AID (n=2), tumour necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome and recurrent pericarditis (n=1 each). Reported outcomes included infections (n=6), intrahepatic cholestasis (n=3), gestational diabetes (n=2), gestational hypertension (n=1) and intrauterine growth restriction (n=1). Median gestational age was 39 weeks with five preterm births between 32 and 37. One baby was diagnosed with laryngomalacia but did not require surgery. Paediatric follow-up (33 babies to 6 months, 30 thereafter for a median of 14.5 months (13–24)) confirmed normal infant development. Maternal and obstetrical outcomes did not differ between treated with anti-IL-1 and untreated with anti-IL-1 patients with AID.
CONCLUSION: Anti-IL-1 therapy, particularly anakinra, appears safe during pregnancy in women with systemic AID.

articles.title: Individual differences in blood-brain barrier permeability are associated with childhood trauma and circulating immune markers in major depressive disorder: Preliminary findings.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a major public health challenge, and childhood trauma is an important risk factor for its development. The blood-brain barrier (BBB) regulates communication between the peripheral immune system and the brain, but how childhood trauma and circulating immune alterations relate to BBB permeability in MDD remains unclear. We studied 39 participants with MDD and 22 healthy controls (HC). Childhood trauma was assessed using the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ), BBB permeability was measured using dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, and circulating leukocyte subtypes and immune-related proteins were quantified in blood. Covariate-adjusted linear models accounted for age, gender, body mass index, race, ethnicity, and current psychiatric medication where applicable. Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability did not differ significantly between participants with MDD and HC. Within the MDD group, higher whole-brain BBB permeability was associated with greater childhood trauma, specifically higher CTQ total, emotional abuse, and physical abuse scores, as well as higher circulating monocyte and neutrophil counts. In a hypothesis-driven analysis based on our prior work, higher plasma matrix metalloproteinase 8 (MMP8) was associated with higher BBB permeability. In an exploratory Olink screen, fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) was the only protein associated with whole-brain BBB permeability after correction for multiple testing, with higher FGF21 related to lower permeability. The corresponding whole-brain associations were not significant in HC. Our preliminary findings identify dimensional associations of BBB permeability with childhood trauma and circulating immune measures within MDD, without evidence of a disorder-level increase in BBB permeability. They support further investigation of the BBB as a potential interface linking childhood adversity and peripheral immune processes in depression, while requiring replication in larger longitudinal samples.

articles.title: Inferring population-level physiologically based model parameters for sleep in infancy and young childhood.
articles.abstract: The sleep patterns of infants and young children differ from adult sleep patterns, with longer duration and multiple bouts per 24 hours. There is also considerable heterogeneity in infant sleep, both between individuals and within individuals across development. While mathematical models have been used to understand the mechanisms that regulate adult sleep, the development of sleep from infancy through early childhood has remained largely unexplored. Here we used an established mathematical model for adult sleep regulation to investigate how the underlying mechanisms of sleep mature from ages 1 month to 5 years, and identify a basis for inter-individual differences at each age. Using a Bayesian approach to estimate joint distributions of model parameters at different ages, we found that: (i) decreases in the rate of accumulation of sleep homeostatic pressure captured the reduction in sleep duration across development; while (ii) increases in the time scale of the sleep homeostatic drive captured the consolidation of sleep into fewer sleep bouts per day across development. In terms of inter-individual differences, we found larger spread in the parameters within the earlier stages of infancy (<1 year). The center and boundaries of the joint distributions evolved with age through the parameter space, converging towards previously described adult parameter values. A bifurcation analysis of the homeostatic time scale parameter revealed that progressive consolidation of sleep occurs through abrupt loss of bouts one at a time, punctuated by narrow intervals of non-entrained (>24-h) cycles. These results establish plausible, population-level trajectories in physiological parameters underpinning maturation of sleep regulation through infancy and early childhood.

articles.title: Cost effectiveness of residential care for mental health and substance use disorders: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the cost effectiveness of residential care for mental and substance use disorders.
METHODS: The review follows the PRISMA guidelines with the protocol registered on PROSPERO (ID: CRD42021287480). Embase, Medline, CINAHL, PsychINFO, and EconLit databases were searched until 31 March 2025. This review included studies that conducted a full economic evaluation or a return-on-investment (ROI) analysis of residential care or supported housing for mental and/or substance use disorders across all age spectrums. A narrative synthesis was conducted to summarise the findings of the included studies. The 10-point Drummond checklist was used to evaluate study quality.
RESULTS: Total 33 studies were included that consisted of 25 full economic evaluations and seven ROI studies. More than 93% of eligible studies focused on adults, and only two targeted children and adolescents. Most studies showed that residential care for mental or substance use disorders was dominant (i.e., cost-saving and more effective) compared to inpatient care from a healthcare sector perspective. Residential care for substance use disorders was found to be dominant or cost-effective based on a pre-defined threshold compared to outpatient care from a societal perspective.
CONCLUSION: Residential care and supported housing programs offer cost effective services for adults with mental and/or substance use disorders. However, long-term cost effective evidence of such services is required. Future economic evaluations focusing on residential care for children and adolescents, residential care in low- and middle-income countries, or using floating outreach or day programs as comparators are encouraged.

articles.title: Variation in educational outcomes following ADHD: A population register-study on individual, family, school and area level modifiers.
articles.abstract: Globally, 5-8% of children and adolescents are estimated to have ADHD, which has consistently been linked to impaired educational outcomes. These average associations may, however, obscure substantial heterogeneity. To better understand variation in the educational outcomes of diagnosed children, we examined 33 potential moderating characteristics at the individual, parental, household, school, and area levels. Using total population register data, we identified 4355 children born in Finland in 1998-2000 and diagnosed with ADHD (identified from data on healthcare visits and medication purchases) at age 6-16 and matched them to 41,861 non-diagnosed controls on birth year, sex, parental migrant background, maternal and paternal education, and region. The children were followed for grade point average (GPA) at the end of compulsory education (∼age 16) and probabilities of completing any upper secondary degree, academic secondary degree, and enrolment in tertiary education at age 20. Using causal forests, we estimated that ADHD is associated with lower GPA and large reductions in the probabilities of completing any upper secondary degree, an academic degree, and tertiary enrolment, but all these associations are substantially heterogenous. For GPA, academic secondary completion, and tertiary enrolment, the strongest negative associations of ADHD were concentrated among children from advantaged families, schools, and areas. However, the opposite was true for completion of any upper secondary degree, for which family, school- and area-level socioeconomic advantage played a mitigating role. These findings suggest that social advantage at different levels of the child's social environment may benefit early educational transitions but not suffice for later progression.

articles.title: Health behaviors as a pathway between early life adversity and cardiometabolic risk for previously institutionalized youth.
articles.abstract: Early life adversity including caregiving stress and neglect has been linked to elevated cardiometabolic risk. Children adopted from institutional care represent a well-characterized model of this exposure limited to the first few years of life, with elevated cardiometabolic risk documented as early as adolescence, even in the absence of overweight or obesity. The present study examines whether health behaviors such as diet, sleep quality measured as daytime drowsiness, and physical activity serve as pathways through which early life adversity shapes cardiometabolic risk during adolescence. Ninety-five previously institutionalized youth (MeanAdoptionAge = 16.2, SD = 12 months, 63% female) and 95 birth-reared youth (MeanAge = 15.8, SD = 2.4 years, 52% female) reported on diet, daytime drowsiness, and physical activity. Two years later, they visited the lab for cardiometabolic health assessment via SphygmoCor, Dual X-ray absorptiometry scan, and blood draws. Cardiometabolic risk was indexed by insulin resistance, cholesterol, arterial stiffness (aortic augmentation index and pulse wave velocity), and android fat percentage. Eating an inflammatory diet and greater drowsiness, but not physical activity, emerged as significant indirect pathways linking early adversity and cardiometabolic risk. Specifically, previously institutionalized youth ate more inflammatory diets and were drowsier during the day than birth-reared youth, which in turn, was associated with higher cardiometabolic risk. These findings raise questions about the mechanisms linking early life adversity to later eating and sleep behaviors and suggest that these behaviors may be modifiable targets for reducing cardiometabolic risk in adolescents with histories of early adversity.

articles.title: From legalisation to implementation of mitochondrial donation in the UK: How new technology attains social legitimacy.
articles.abstract: In 2015, the UK became the first country to legalise the clinical use of mitochondrial donation (MD), a new in vitro fertilization-based innovation that offers women with mitochondrial diseases the potential to have a genetically related child with a reduced risk of transmission. MD legalisation provoked intense ethical, social, and legal debates internationally. This study explored how this technology receives social legitimacy during the legalisation process and how that legitimacy is retained, or challenged, during its early clinical implementation. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine key informants who were involved in the development, legalisation, and implementation of MD in the UK. The interview guide and analysis were informed by four dimensions of social legitimacy: pragmatic, moral, regulative, and cultural-cognitive legitimacy. Findings show that pragmatic and moral legitimacy were established by framing MD as a necessary intervention to meet the reproductive needs of affected women who desire to have a genetically related child, potentially free of mitochondrial diseases. Regulatory legitimacy was reinforced through a rigorous legislative and oversight process. Cultural-cognitive legitimacy was supported through public engagement in ethical and regulatory debates. Key challenges that continue to impact the social legitimacy of MD include transparency in the implementation procedures and ongoing concerns regarding equitable access to MD for all eligible patients. MD continues to negotiate social legitimisation in ways that are neither settled nor guaranteed. Retaining social legitimacy beyond legalisation is essential for the responsible, equitable, and sustainable implementation of MD in clinical practice.

articles.title: Percutaneous Electrical Nerve Field Stimulation: Revitalizing the Management of Neurogastrointestinal Motility Disorders.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Neurogastrointestinal motility disorders and disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) are difficult to treat, particularly with pharmacotherapy alone. This review examines percutaneous electrical nerve field stimulation (PENFS) as a non-invasive neuromodulation therapy, addressing its potential mechanistic rationale, clinical evidence, patient selection, practical implementation, and future directions of research.
RECENT FINDINGS: PENFS appears to act through several pathways: limbic modulation via the central nucleus of the amygdala, altered vagal afferent signaling at the nucleus tractus solitarius, and effects on an enteric nervous system that continues to mature through adolescence. Randomized sham-controlled trials and a multicenter registry show improvement in pain, nausea, and disability alongside a favorable safety profile. Auricular allodynia and impaired cardiac vagal efficiency are emerging as markers of treatment response. PENFS is a safe, effective, non-pharmacologic option across the DGBI spectrum. Formal dose- and duration-response work, adult trials, and long-term durability data remain the principal gaps, though work is ongoing.

articles.title: Nutrition in the Era of Incretin-Based Therapies: Clinical Strategies for Optimizing Care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To review current evidence and practical nutrition strategies for patients receiving incretin-based therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists, with a focus on nutritional adequacy, body composition, gastrointestinal tolerance, and long-term adherence.
RECENT FINDINGS: Incretin-based therapies have transformed obesity treatment by producing substantial weight loss and cardiometabolic improvement. However, these therapies are also associated with reduced oral intake, gastrointestinal adverse effects, lean mass loss, and potential micronutrient inadequacy, highlighting the need for comprehensive nutritional management. Emerging evidence supports individualized dietary strategies to improve tolerance and maintain nutritional status, including targeted approaches for constipation, diarrhea, nausea, and reflux, as well as considerations for special populations such as pati​ents with inflammatory bowel disease, short bowel syndrome, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and pediatric obesity. Nutrition care is a critical component of treatment with incretin-based therapies. Individualized dietary strategies may help preserve lean body mass, optimize nutrient intake, reduce gastrointestinal side effects, and support long-term adherence and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: A systematic review of the existing parent-led interventions to promote the psychosocial development of neurodivergent children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review takes a transdiagnostic approach to understanding the active components commonly used across evidence-based interventions, to inform the development of a novel psychosocial intervention for children with Developmental Language Disorder (DLD).
METHODS: Searches were conducted in December 2020, August 2022 and July 2026 of 11 databases, including: PsycINFO, PsycEXTRA, Embase, PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL and MEDLINE. Inclusion criteria was: trials must have compared interventions to a control group, or have an 8-week follow-up, include parent-led components and measures of child psychosocial outcomes, must be published in English after 2000, with participants aged 2-13 years old, who met diagnostic criteria for seven categories of neurodivergence (that share psychosocial difficulties to children with DLD). Synthesis was conducted by coding intervention content using a taxonomy and calculating effect sizes using baseline and follow-up data on psychosocial outcomes. Quality appraisal was assessed using the National Institute of Health's quality assessment measures.
RESULTS: A total of 11,583 studies were selected for abstract screening; 52 studies met the pre-specified inclusion criteria after full-text screening. All interventions analysed were designed for autistic children (n = 26) and/or attention deficit hyperactive disorder (ADHD; n = 23). Across studies, 870 children with ADHD and 832 autistic children received interventions; 730 children with ADHD and 701 autistic children received a control. Four intervention components were most used across effective interventions: parent-child interaction training, parenting behaviours, and emotion management for both parent and child. An association between parent wellbeing and improved child psychosocial outcomes is suggested, however limited by the lack of data. Therapeutic and researcher contact appears to impact intervention engagement. Accessibility is discussed.
CONCLUSION: Evidence-based psychosocial interventions are required for neurodivergent children other than children with autism and ADHD. Psychosocial interventions for children with DLD should consider addressing parent-child communication, wellbeing of both parent and child, and involve therapeutic support.

articles.title: Sleep in school-age children at elevated familial likelihood of autism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinically significant sleep problems are common in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and can have negative impacts on child cognition, behavior, and health. However, few studies have evaluated sleep in school-aged children with elevated familial likelihood of autism using objective and subjective sleep measures in the home environment.
METHODS: We obtained objective measures of sleep using actigraphy and parent-report of sleep problems using daily sleep diaries and the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire. Direct assessment established ASD diagnosis in 7-14-year-old children at higher familial likelihood (HL-ASD n = 39; HL-noASD n = 83) and lower familial likelihood of ASD (LL n = 64).
RESULTS: Child sleep problems reported by parents, controlling for age, differed across groups following an endophenotypic pattern (HL-ASD > HL-noASD > LL) and HL-ASD females demonstrated increased sleep problems. Actigraphy and daily sleep diaries did not demonstrate significant group differences. There were significant group differences in psychotropic medication and melatonin use.
CONCLUSION: In one of the first studies to evaluate sleep in school-age children at higher familial likelihood of ASD, parent-report of sleep problems was increased in HL-ASD versus HL-noASD versus LL children. This suggests shared familial influences between ASD and parent-reported sleep problems which could include genetic factors or shared aspects of the home environment. However, sleep characteristics measured objectively by actigraphy and daily sleep diaries revealed a different pattern. Multimodal sleep data can reveal less understood dimensions of sleep patterns in naturalistic home environments and may lead to improved sleep interventions for autistic youth and their siblings.

articles.title: 10 tips to integrate genetic testing into nephrology practice.
articles.abstract: A substantial subset of chronic kidney disease has an underlying monogenic cause, in both children and adults. Modern sequencing technologies provide the means for broad genetic testing, and approaches to therapy and patient care become increasingly aetiology based. Thus, unravelling the genetic cause is getting clinically more and more important. Today, genetic testing represents a valuable diagnostic tool that offers clinical value in various aspects, starting from validation, refinement or correction of the diagnosis (so-called reverse phenotyping). This often leads to optimized evaluation of risks and prognosis, improved clinical management and potentially targeted treatment options. Interpreting genetic results and test reports is often regarded as challenging. The following 10 tips aim to provide clinicians with helpful background information on genetic tests, address frequent uncertainties and unanswered questions, and aid in the use of genetic testing in routine diagnostics.

articles.title: Health state utility values in children with peanut allergy and their caregivers: a UK vignette study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peanut allergy is a common allergy in children, affecting the health-related quality of life (HRQoL) of the child and other members of the family. Demonstrating health state utility values (HSUVs) for children with peanut allergy is a requirement for reimbursement of treatments in health technology assessment, yet evidence is scarce relative to eliciting dose (ED, in mg peanut protein). We aimed to estimate utility values of children with peanut allergy and their caregivers, for four distinct health states defined by ED and guided by survey results: <150mg; ≥150-<300mg; ≥300mg peanut-only allergy; and ≥300mg poly-nut allergy (300mg corresponding to roughly one large Virginia peanut).
METHODS: An online survey investigating the impacts of peanut allergy was conducted, and 604 participants completed the survey across two waves between 2019 and 2020. Health-state vignettes (descriptions) were generated based on survey outcomes and validated via six semi-structured interviews with caregivers of children with peanut allergy, members of patient organizations, and two clinical experts. The resulting eight vignettes were valued by 100 members of the UK general public using the time trade-off (TTO) method to derive HSUVs.
RESULTS: The estimated HSUVs (standard deviation) generated using TTO for the <150mg, ≥150-<300mg, ≥300mg peanut-only allergy, and ≥300mg poly-nut allergy ED categories were: 0.80 (0.24), 0.86 (0.21), 0.92 (0.18) and 0.88 (0.19), respectively, for children; and 0.82 (0.27), 0.89 (0.18), 0.93 (0.16) and 0.91 (0.17), for caregivers.
CONCLUSION: We successfully generated HSUVs for children with peanut allergy and their caregivers for different ED categories, which may be used to inform economic modelling and reimbursement decisions. Our study provides supportive evidence of a potential association between ED and utility, highlighting the importance of treatments focused on desensitizing children with peanut allergy and providing long-term solutions to living with peanut allergy.

articles.title: Intrarater reliability of expert electroencephalographic interpretation of 100 full-length recordings.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The value of electroencephalography (EEG) relies on accurate and reliable interpretation. Prior research has demonstrated imperfect interrater reliability, but intrarater reliability remains poorly characterized. We performed a "noise audit" primarily to measure intrarater variability in EEG interpretation by epileptologists.
METHODS: Experts independently rated the same 100 full-length EEGs on two separate occasions ≥60 days apart, unaware the EEGs were the same. EEGs were recorded from adult (56%) and pediatric patients in outpatient (78%) and non-critical care inpatient settings. There were 20 studies in each of five categories: normal, focal epileptiform (FE), generalized epileptiform (GE), focal nonepileptiform (FNE), and generalized nonepileptiform (GNE) abnormalities. EEGs were presented using our online platform (EEGHub) without clinical information except for age and sex. Experts rated each recording and indicated their level of confidence (LOC) for each EEG and overall. We analyzed percent as well as chance-corrected intra- and interrater agreement.
RESULTS: Fourteen experts (mean of 19 years EEG reading experience, range = 4-52 years) were included in the study. Percent self-agreement was 96% for GE, 90% for FE, 88% for FNE, and 87% for GNE abnormalities; 90% for any epileptiform abnormality; and 82% for any nonepileptiform abnormality. Self-agreement was strongly correlated with interrater agreement (mean κML), which was almost perfect for GE (.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .87-.94) and FE (.82, 95% CI = .77-.87) and substantial for GNE (.75, 95% CI = .69-.81) and FNE (.74, 95% CI = .68-.80) abnormalities. LOC correlated with self-agreement on the presence of nonepileptiform but not epileptiform abnormalities.
SIGNIFICANCE: We found generally strong within-expert agreement in EEG interpretation, especially in the identification of epileptiform abnormalities. Nevertheless, the number of flipped decisions was high enough to be clinically consequential. This undesired variability ("occasion noise") may be addressed by interventions to (1) decrease this noise directly and (2) reduce case ambiguity with longer recordings and better EEG data whenever feasible.

articles.title: Antiseizure medication use in self-limited epilepsies of childhood: A scoping review by the ILAE Pediatric Medical Therapies Task Force.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Self-limited focal epilepsies (SeLFEs) of childhood, including self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), self-limited epilepsy with autonomic seizures (SeLEAS), childhood occipital visual epilepsy (COVE), and photosensitive occipital lobe epilepsy (POLE), are common pediatric epilepsy syndromes with heterogeneous clinical management. We performed a scoping review to synthesize evidence regarding the use, effectiveness, safety, and discontinuation of antiseizure medications (ASMs) in children with SeLFEs.
METHODS: Nine databases were searched from inception to January 2026. Eligible studies included original research reporting ASM-related outcomes in children with SeLFEs. PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses, extension for scoping reviews) guidance was followed.
RESULTS: Sixty-two studies met eligibility criteria, including 11 randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Most studies evaluated SeLECTS (6171 participants), whereas substantially fewer investigated SeLEAS (n = 348), COVE (n = 91), or POLE (n = 26). Evidence was highly heterogeneous and consisted predominantly of retrospective observational studies. In SeLECTS, reported 12-month seizure freedom rates after ASM treatment were approximately 72% across studies, although estimates varied considerably. Evidence for SeLEAS, COVE, and POLE was limited and derived mainly from small retrospective cohorts with heterogeneous methodologies and outcome definitions. Failure of first-line ASM therapy occurred in approximately 30% of patients. Adverse events were reported in approximately 22% of treated children and infrequently led to treatment discontinuation. RCTs generally reported similar seizure outcomes across multiple ASMs, although many trials were limited by small sample sizes and open-label designs.
SIGNIFICANCE: Current evidence suggests that children with SeLFEs often achieve seizure control with ASM treatment and that adverse effects are generally manageable. However, the overall certainty of evidence remains limited because of methodological heterogeneity, predominance of retrospective studies, and limited randomized data. Important evidence gaps remain regarding the need for ASM treatment, optimal treatment duration, and timing of medication withdrawal.

articles.title: Ferroptosis in Pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae Pneumonia: An Emerging Mechanistic Framework, Candidate Biomarkers and Their Limitations, and Translational Priorities.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) is among the most common causes of community-acquired pneumonia in children. Against a background of widespread macrolide-resistant M. pneumoniae (MRMP) in East Asia, severe (SMPP) and refractory (RMPP) MP pneumonia have become pressing clinical problems, and a subset of children develop long-term sequelae including bronchiolitis obliterans, bronchiectasis, and organizing pneumonia. The mechanisms driving MPP severity remain incompletely understood, and tools for the early identification of high-risk children are limited. Ferroptosis-an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by uncontrolled accumulation of lipid peroxides-contributes to several forms of infectious lung injury; extrapolating from this cross-pathogen evidence, we propose here that it may also participate in MP-related alveolar epithelial damage and inflammatory amplification, a hypothesis that has not previously been articulated specifically for pediatric MPP. In this narrative review of an emerging area, we summarize the molecular regulation of ferroptosis, appraise the current-and still limited-evidence linking it to pediatric MPP (explicitly separating direct MP data from cross-pathogen extrapolation), and critically evaluate the clinical applicability of ferroptosis-related biomarkers. Because direct evidence in pediatric MPP is sparse, the mechanistic model presented here is explicitly hypothesis-generating rather than a claim of established causation. We give particular attention to serum ferritin, whose pragmatic value for SMPP/RMPP risk stratification is well supported but is better understood as reflecting combined iron metabolism and systemic inflammation than as evidence of ferroptosis specifically; markedly elevated values should prompt evaluation for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis/macrophage activation syndrome. We argue that ferroptosis offers a biologically plausible, complementary framework to the cytokine-storm paradigm for understanding MPP severity, and we outline priority research directions for a field that remains in its infancy.

articles.title: The efficacy of adding leg wrapping to prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of post-spinal hypotension in elective cesarean section: a prospective double-blinded randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Various pharmacological and non-pharmacological methods have been studied in the literature to reduce the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of adding bilateral lower-limb wrapping to a prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of hypotension in parturients receiving intrathecal anesthesia for cesarean delivery.
METHODS: This prospective randomized trial included parturients undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. Parturients were divided into the following: norepinephrine group (N) (n = 84), and norepinephrine and leg wrapping group (NW) (n = 84). The 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion continued until 5 min after fetal delivery. The primary outcome was the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of maternal severe hypotension, bradycardia, tachycardia, hypertension, nausea, vomiting, post-delivery hypotension, and neonatal outcomes.
RESULTS: The final analysis included 168 patients. The incidence of hypotension in the NW group was lower than in the N group (7/84 [8.3%], 18/84 [21.4%], respectively) with P = 0.017, RR = 0.39, and CI: (0.17-0.88). According to the Kaplan-Meier curve with the log-rank test, the time to post-spinal maternal hypotension differed significantly (P = 0.016), with a restricted mean time of 21.1 min in the NW group and 19.7 min in the N group (hazard ratio = 2.82 for the N group vs. NW, 95%CI: (1.18-6.76). Furthermore, a repeated-measures analysis revealed significant group-by-time interactions for both heart rate (P = 0.003) and systolic blood pressure (P = 0.028), demonstrating superior longitudinal hemodynamic stability in the NW group. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected for secondary maternal and neonatal outcomes.
CONCLUSION: When added to a prophylactic 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion, leg wrapping decreased the incidence of postspinal maternal hypotension and enhanced hemodynamic stability over time during elective cesarean delivery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06496061; principal investigator: Mohamed Ahmed Hamed; date of registration: 11/07/2024; no protocol amendments or study changes after trial start).

articles.title: Clinical features and comparative outcomes of antiviral treatment in children with influenza A and B: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Comparative evidence on antiviral treatment in pediatric influenza remains limited. We compared the clinical features of influenza A and B and assessed the comparative outcomes of oseltamivir, baloxavir marboxil, and peramivir in children.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included 3,718 children with nucleic acid-confirmed influenza A or B who presented to a tertiary pediatric emergency department between November 2023 and April 2024 and initiated antiviral treatment within 48 h of fever onset. Primary endpoints were time to fever resolution and time to full symptom resolution. Propensity score matching was performed separately within the influenza A and influenza B cohorts for prespecified pairwise comparisons, followed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: Among 3,718 children, 1,717 had influenza A and 2,001 had influenza B. Influenza A was more often associated with higher fever and neurologic complications, whereas influenza B more commonly presented with gastrointestinal symptoms. After propensity score matching, baloxavir and peramivir were associated with shorter times to fever resolution than oseltamivir in both cohorts (influenza A: baloxavir 1.57 days vs. oseltamivir 2.11 days, peramivir 1.72 days vs. oseltamivir 2.23 days; influenza B: baloxavir 1.50 days vs. oseltamivir 2.29 days, peramivir 1.71 days vs. oseltamivir 2.25 days). Differences in time to full symptom resolution were smaller and less consistent across comparisons. Overall adverse events were documented in 16.5% of children receiving oseltamivir, compared with 5.0% receiving peramivir and 3.6% receiving baloxavir; notably, no serious adverse events were observed across the cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Influenza A and B showed distinct clinical phenotypes in this pediatric cohort. In propensity score-matched analyses, baloxavir and peramivir were associated with modestly faster fever resolution and lower recorded rates of adverse events than oseltamivir. Given the retrospective, non-randomized design and the modest absolute differences observed, these findings should be interpreted as associative and hypothesis-generating rather than as evidence of causal superiority. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized outcome assessment are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Glucose-based fluid creep or maintenance fluids in critically ill adult patients: a scoping review of the available evidence related to blood glucose control.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluid therapy is a fundamental aspect of intensive care unit treatment, encompassing resuscitation, maintenance, nutrition, and hidden fluid "creep" to keep lines open or dilute drugs. While most research has focused on resuscitation fluids, maintenance and fluid creep are major contributors to overall fluid and electrolyte intake. Normal saline is commonly used as fluid creep, but concerns about electrolyte imbalances have led to interest in alternatives like Dextrose 5% in Water.
METHODS: In this scoping review we aimed to map the available evidence of glucose-based vs non-glucose-based maintenance fluids/ fluid creep with regard to blood glucose levels, insulin need and further related outcomes (urinary output, length of stay in ICU) in adult ICU patients. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Library. We aimed to include prospective and retrospective clinical cohort studies and controlled trials in adult ICU patients reporting blood sugar levels or insulin use and excluded trials on resuscitation fluids or patient populations with specific requirements regarding fluid therapy (e.g., burn patients, children). We analysed risk of bias using the standardized Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies-of Interventions tool.
RESULTS: Six observational, single-center cohort studies (n = 6343 patients) met inclusion criteria. Overall, evidence was limited and heterogeneous, with no non-randomized controlled trials identified meeting our inclusion criteria. Findings on blood glucose levels were heterogeneous and inconclusive across studies. Findings for urinary output and ICU length of stay were inconsistent but trials were not powered to report these endpoints. The included studies were subject to confounding, incomplete outcome reporting, and variability in fluid regimens.
CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence on glucose-containing maintenance fluids as well as on fluid creep or combined strategies on glycemic control in critically ill adults is limited and observational. Maintenance fluids, drug diluents/fluid creep, and combined strategies are distinct exposures with different glucose loads; evidence is sparse and should not be generalized across categories. Adequately powered randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify effects on blood glucose and insulin-related outcomes as well as on patient-centered outcomes for each category.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024542262.

articles.title: Neonatal umbilical cord treatment: a prospective study on detachment time and complications with different topical approaches.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Umbilical cord care plays a crucial role in neonatal health, influencing cord detachment time and the occurrence of complications such as bleeding, discharge, infection, and umbilical granuloma. While dry care is widely recommended, increasing attention has been directed toward alternative topical approaches aimed at optimizing healing and reducing complications. This study compares different umbilical cord care regimens-Dry Care, Connettivina Silver Plus Spray®, Cliaxin Spray®, and Cicaben Powder®-focusing on cord detachment time and associated outcomes.
METHODS: A prospective study was conducted from November 2020 to February 2022 at the Neonatology Department of the Regional General Hospital "F. Miulli," enrolling 1,699 neonates. Participants were assigned to one of four umbilical care regimens: Dry Care, Connettivina Silver Plus Spray, Cliaxin Spray, or Cicaben Powder. Treatment was administered in the hospital, and post-discharge follow-up on cord detachment time, bleeding, discharge, and umbilical granuloma (UG) formation was conducted on postnatal day 30. Statistical analyses included ANOVA and chi-square tests, with significance set at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: The shortest detachment time was observed in the Cliaxin Spray group (6.5 ± 2.2 days, p < 0.05), while Dry Care had the longest (8.0 ± 2.8 days). UG incidence ranged from 4.7% to 7.8%, with no statistically significant differences between groups. Bleeding and umbilical discharge rates were significantly lower in the Cicaben Powder group (9.1% and 5.5%, respectively) compared to other regimens (p < 0.05). No cases of omphalitis or sepsis occurred in any group.
CONCLUSION: In this large prospective cohort, topical dermatological formulations were associated with improved outcomes in specific aspects of cord care. Cliaxin Spray was linked to faster cord detachment, while Cicaben Powder reduced bleeding and discharge. Although Dry Care remains widely used, it was associated with a higher rate of minor complications. These findings support the need to reconsider current approaches to umbilical cord care and explore more tailored strategies. Further controlled studies are warranted.

articles.title: A hub-and-spoke network organizational model in Liguria (Italy) for managing anaphylaxis in pediatric age: a retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anaphylaxis is a severe, potentially life-threatening systemic hypersensitivity reaction for which intramuscular epinephrine is the sole non-deferrable first-line treatment. Despite well-established international guidelines, real-world adherence remains critically suboptimal, particularly in peripheral emergency settings. This study examines anaphylaxis management in children aged 0-16 years presenting to the emergency department within the Gaslini Diffuso initiative, a structured Hub-and-Spoke pediatric network in Liguria, Italy, to evaluate inter-institutional variability in clinical practice.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective observational study spanning 10 years at the Hub Center (IRCCS Istituto Giannina Gaslini, Genoa; January 2013 - December 2023) and 2 years across all network centers (January 2022 - December 2023). Anaphylaxis was defined according to the NIAID/FAAN 2006 criteria.
RESULTS: The cohort comprised 168 patients aged 0-16 years, distributed across the Hub Center and four Spoke Centers. Epinephrine was administered in only 34.9% of patients overall (rising to 52.8% in the 2022-2023 period), with marked inter-institutional variability across the network (Hub 52.8% vs. La Spezia 6.7%). Antihistamines (89.2%) and corticosteroids (87.3%) dominated clinical practice despite lacking proven efficacy in preventing anaphylaxis progression. Tryptase measurement was performed in 43.4% (acute) and 21.1% (baseline) of Hub patients. Autoinjector prescription was documented in only 26.5% of newly eligible patients, and as low as 5.3% at Savona-Pietra Ligure.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest significant gaps that may contribute to suboptimal outcomes, underscoring the urgent need for network-wide epinephrine-first protocols and structured training programs.

articles.title: Transition of care from pediatric to adult age in persons with Down Syndrome: a comprehensive evaluation via the InterRAI suite of mental health instruments.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The transition from pediatric to adult healthcare is a critical phase for persons with Down syndrome (DS). The InterRAI Child and Youth Mental Health - Developmental Disabilities (ChYMH-DD) and the InterRAI Intellectual Disability (ID) are validated tools for pediatric and adult populations, respectively.
AIM: this study aimed to facilitate more coordinated care planning and a consistent understanding of functioning across developmental stages of persons with Down syndrome.
METHODS: This study included 186 participants (aged 5-35 years) with a DS diagnosis. Each participant was assessed using the age-appropriate InterRAI instrument for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
RESULTS: The transition to adulthood is associated with an increased complexity of mood, behaviour and symptom burden, as well as a decline in engagement with preventive healthcare after childhood.
CONCLUSION: This proof-of-concept study demonstrated the feasibility of applying InterRAI multidimensional assessment instruments across the transition from pediatric to adult care in individuals with DS. The observed patterns-gains in autonomy and communication alongside increasing behavioral, emotional, and medical challenges-underscore the need for structured, lifespan-oriented approaches to care.

articles.title: Diagnostic value of systemic immune-inflammation index versus lactate dehydrogenase in early prediction of severe mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children: a retrospective matched case-control study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to investigate the diagnostic utility of the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), as well as their combined models, for the early prediction of severe mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (SMPP) in children.
METHODS: This retrospective matched case-control study analyzed data from 100 hospitalized children (50 SMPP cases and 50 non-SMPP controls, 1:1 matched) at Xi'an Children's Hospital between June 2023 and June 2024. Laboratory indicators, including SII, LDH, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and procalcitonin (PCT), were collected at admission. Independent risk factors were identified through logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, DeLong test, and Youden index were used to evaluate predictive efficacy.
RESULTS: The SMPP group showed significantly prolonged fever duration, higher peak temperature, elevated CRP and PCT levels, increased rates of glucocorticoid and bronchoscopy use, and longer hospitalization (all P < 0.05). SII, NLR, PLR, and LDH were significantly higher in the SMPP group, with SII showing the largest effect size (r = 0.720). After adjusting for age and duration of fever before admission, multivariate analysis confirmed SII (aOR = 1.013, 95% CI: 1.006-1.019, P < 0.001) and LDH (aOR = 1.029, 95% CI: 1.009-1.050, P = 0.005) as independent risk factors. SII alone demonstrated superior predictive performance (AUC = 0.918, 95% CI: 0.863-0.972; sensitivity 78.0%, specificity 94.0%) compared with LDH (AUC = 0.797, 95% CI: 0.708-0.886; P = 0.025). The SII-LDH combined model achieved an AUC of 0.950 (95% CI: 0.910-0.990; sensitivity 82.0%, specificity 98.0%), showing no significant difference versus SII alone (P = 0.083) but significantly outperforming LDH alone (P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: The study showed superior discriminatory capability of SII compared to LDH in identifying SMPP within this cohort. These results imply that SII could serve as a valuable biomarker for early risk assessment, pending prospective multicenter validation prior to standard clinical adoption.

articles.title: Skin safety during umbilical venous catheter insertion using 2% chlorhexidine gluconate in 70% isopropyl alcohol: a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Umbilical venous catheter (UVC) placement in NICU requires effective antisepsis to minimize catheter-related bloodstream infections. Chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) in isopropyl alcohol (IPA) is commonly used, but its safety in preterm infants is debated. This study evaluates the skin safety of 2% CHG in 70% IPA during UVC placement in neonates.
METHODS: A prospective analysis of neonates admitted to a tertiary NICU from January 2021 to December 2024 was conducted. Skin reactions were assessed at 30 min, 24 h, and 48 h post-procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of skin lesions categorized according to a dermatitis severity score.
RESULTS: Among 506 neonates, 48.4% had a gestational age ≤ 32 weeks. No severe lesions were observed. Erythema and discoloration were common but resolved within 48 h. The incidence of erythema decreased with increasing gestational age. Only two catheters were removed as a result of catheter-related bloodstream infections (0.89 per 1000 catheter days).
CONCLUSIONS: 2% CHG in 70% IPA showed a favorable safety profile in neonates undergoing UVC placement when appropriate precautions were observed.

articles.title: Predicting severity and long-term respiratory health in pediatric adenovirus pneumonia: A retrospective cohort study integrating risk modeling and atopic status.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To identify risk factors for severe adenovirus pneumonia (SAP) in children, develop and validate a predictive nomogram, and investigate the impact of atopy on both acute severity and long-term pulmonary sequelae.
METHODS: The retrospective cohort study involved 416 children diagnosed with adenovirus pneumonia at Shandong Provincial Hospital between January 2019 and February 2025. Patients were stratified into SAP and non-SAP groups based on disease progression. Independent predictors were identified using multivariate logistic regression to construct a nomogram, validated by 1,000 Bootstrap resamples. 89 survivors of SAP were followed up longitudinally to compare pulmonary function and respiratory complications between patients with and without atopic predisposition.
RESULTS: In this study, 189 enrolled children (45.43%) progressed to SAP. Multivariate analysis revealed that atopic predisposition (odds ratio [OR] = 1.933, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.102-3.392), pulse oxygen saturation< 95% (OR = 4.963, 95% CI: 2.702-9.117), serum amyloid A (OR = 1.002, 95% CI: 1.000-1.004), hypoalbuminemia (OR = 0.914, 95% CI: 0.888-0.941), and clinical pulmonary infection score ≥ 1 (score 1: OR = 3.899, 95% CI: 1.533-9.915; score 2: OR = 15.825, 95% CI: 6.663-37.587) were independent predictors of SAP. The constructed nomogram demonstrated robust discrimination (area under the curve = 0.854, 95% CI: 0.818-0.890) and excellent calibration (Spiegelhalter Z-test p = 0.941). In the follow-up cohort, atopic predisposition was associated with adverse long-term outcomes: it was present in 69.23% (18/26)of children who developed bronchial asthma and 100% (10/10) of those diagnosed with bronchiolitis obliterans respectively.
CONCLUSION: This study developed a reliable risk prediction model integrating clinical, laboratory, and imaging markers to facilitate early identification of children at high risk for SAP. Atopic predisposition is associated with acute disease severity and may increase the risk of long-term pulmonary impairment (particularly bronchiolitis obliterans and asthma) , highlighting host-virus interplay rather than viral infection alone. These findings support systematic long-term pulmonary function monitoring and personalized respiratory rehabilitation strategies for children post-adenovirus infection to optimize respiratory health.

articles.title: Advancing complement inhibition for the treatment of malarial anemia: a translational roadmap.
articles.abstract: Severe anemia is responsible for hundreds of thousands of deaths in children with malaria. For every Plasmodium-infected erythrocyte that is lysed, considerably more than 10 uninfected erythrocytes are cleared by extravascular hemolysis, thus leading to anemia. Compelling evidence indicates that breakdown products released from infected erythrocytes in the bloodstream activate complement and promote "innocent bystander" deposition of C3 activation fragments on the uninfected erythrocytes, thereby sensitizing them for elimination. We propose a series of in vitro experiments with blood cultures of malaria parasites to test the hypothesis that use of inhibitors that block complement at the C3 activation step can preserve and protect uninfected erythrocytes from C3 deposition. Successful demonstration of in vitro protection will set the stage for clinical trials based on the limited and focused use of complement inhibitors to prevent severe anemia in malaria.

articles.title: Factors associated with malaria parasitemia in hospitalized children under five years of age with severe acute malnutrition in Burundi: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malaria and severe acute malnutrition (SAM) are among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in children under 5 years of age in sub-Saharan Africa. When these conditions occur, they interact synergistically, exacerbating disease severity and compromising child survival.
