OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of malaria parasitemia and identify factors associated with malaria parasitemia among children under five years of age with severe acute malnutrition admitted to Butezi District Hospital, Burundi, between 2023 and 2024.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using the medical records of children under 5 years of age diagnosed with SAM at Butezi District Hospital, Burundi. Malaria parasitemia was diagnosed using either microscopy or rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs), according to routine hospital practice. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the study population. Associations between SAM and malaria parasitemia were examined via chi-square tests and logistic regression models. Statistical significance was established at p < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 481 children under five years of age with SAM were included in the study. Malaria parasitemia was detected in 150 (31.2%) children. Among all participants, 275 (57.2%) were diagnosed using microscopy and 206 (42.8%) using RDTs. Girls had higher odds of malaria parasitemia than boys (OR = 1.52, p = 0.042), while children who did not use mosquito nets had nearly twice the odds of malaria parasitemia (OR = 1.97, p = 0.002). Compared with children whose fathers were farmers, those whose fathers were civil servants (OR = 0.18, p < 0.001) or merchants (OR = 0.21, p < 0.001) had significantly lower odds of malaria parasitemia. In sex-stratified analyses, edema (aOR = 2.00, p = 0.037) and lack of mosquito net use were significantly associated with malaria parasitemia among boys, whereas age younger than 6 months (aOR = 3.21, p = 0.034) was significantly associated with malaria parasitemia among girls.
CONCLUSION: Integrated interventions addressing both malnutrition and malaria, alongside targeted prevention strategies, are essential to reduce child morbidity and mortality in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Epigenetic dysregulation in H3K27M diffuse midline glioma: therapeutic vulnerabilities and emerging insights into viral mimicry.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pediatric diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a near-lethal childhood brain tumor. The lysine-to-methionine substitution at histone H3 lysine (K) 27 disrupts normal histone post-translational modification, driving global loss of H3K27 trimethylation and widespread reprogramming of chromatin accessibility and transcription that sustain oncogenic cell states.
AREAS COVERED: In this review, we synthesize current knowledge on how histone modifications, DNA methylation, and chromatin-remodeling machinery are altered in H3K27M DMG, and summarize therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting each affected epigenetic regulator. We also highlight an emerging therapeutic paradigm in which epigenetic disruption of repetitive-element silencing may create a viral-mimicry vulnerability that can be therapeutically exploited.
EXPERT OPINION: In our view, viral mimicry represents a promising and potentially powerful therapeutic strategy in H3K27M DMG that exploits an epigenetic vulnerability. Loss of H3K27me3 may weaken repetitive element silencing, likely leaving tumor cells dependent on alternative repressive mechanisms. Disrupting these silencing pathways with epigenetic drug combinations may derepress retrotransposons and activate antiviral sensing, potentially reducing tumor fitness through cell-intrinsic stress and antitumor immune responses. However, clinical translation will require ongoing rigorous preclinical validation, CNS-penetrant agents, biomarkers of epigenetic vulnerability, and resistance monitoring. Future studies must also thoughtfully balance antitumor immunity against neuroinflammatory toxicity.

articles.title: Latent profile analysis of sleep quality and associated factors in Chinese adolescents with major depressive disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbances are pervasive among adolescent patients with major depressive disorder (MDD), yet the heterogeneity of sleep phenotypes within this population remains underexplored. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of sleep quality in Chinese adolescent patients with MDD and to examine their associations with sociodemographic, clinical, and psychosocial factors.
METHODS: A total of 1,467 adolescent patients with MDD were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), the Borderline Personality Features Scale for Children (BPFS-C), and a self-designed sociodemographic and clinical inventory. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was conducted using the seven PSQI component scores as profile indicators. Multinomial logistic regression was subsequently performed to determine factors associated with profile membership.
RESULTS: A five-profile solution was identified: Normal Sleep Group (13%), Mild Disturbance-Low Hypnotic Use (36%), Mild Disturbance-High Hypnotic Use (22%), Severe Disturbance-Low Hypnotic Use (16%), and Severe Disturbance-High Hypnotic Use (13%). Logistic regression revealed that the presence of non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) and exposure to negative life events significantly increased the odds of belonging to more severe sleep disturbance profiles (OR = 2.92-8.37 and 2.33-2.60, respectively; all p < 0.05). Notably, patients without left-behind experiences exhibited higher odds of being classified into the Severe Disturbance-High Hypnotic Use profile compared to those with such histories (OR = 0.46, p < 0.001). Furthermore, profiles characterized by poorer sleep quality and profiles characterized by more frequent self-reported sleep medication use were cross-sectionally associated with greater anxiety and borderline features in this study.
CONCLUSION: Sleep quality among adolescent patients with MDD exhibits distinct typological heterogeneity, characterized primarily by severity and hypnotic use patterns. These findings provide preliminary exploratory evidence for the development of personalized, profile-informed clinical interventions for this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Mental health outcomes following COVID-19- associated caregiver loss in children and adolescents: a six-year evidence gap.
articles.abstract: By May 2022, an estimated 10.5 million children worldwide had lost a parent or caregiver to COVID-19. We found only two cohorts with quantitative mental-health data: one in Iran and the South African Orphanhood and Caregiver Loss Among Adolescents and Youth study. Both reported more psychiatric and psychosocial difficulties among bereaved children than controls. In Iran, internalizing symptoms, post-traumatic stress, and suicidal ideation increased during follow-up, and no participant received mental-health care. In South Africa, likely mental disorder declined in both groups but remained more common among bereaved participants; suicidal ideation or attempts rose slightly in the bereaved group while falling among controls. Social support, food insecurity, and domestic violence were associated with outcomes. These children were bereaved during school closures, social isolation, disrupted mourning, and financial strain, when usual sources of support were often reduced. Yet few were identified and followed over time. Research funding priorities and fragmented health, education, mortality, and child-protection systems may have contributed to this gap. Many children bereaved in the first pandemic waves are now adolescents or young adults, but their longer-term mental-health course remains largely unknown. They should be identified, followed, and offered support according to clinical and family need.

articles.title: Symptom interactions of insomnia, anxiety, and depression in early pregnancy: a network analysis perspective.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy is a unique phase involving significant physical, social, and psychological changes, increasing vulnerability to anxiety, depression, and insomnia. These conditions are interrelated and often overlap, yet their symptom-symptom relationships during early pregnancy remain underexplored.
METHODS: A total of 1,830 women in early pregnancy (≤12 weeks) who attended the Children's Hospital of Shanxi Province /Shanxi Maternal and Child Health Hospital, China, between 2021 and 2024 were included. Anxiety and depression were assessed with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and insomnia with the Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS). Regularized partial correlation networks (EBICglasso applied to polychoric correlations) were estimated to examine the connections among symptoms of anxiety, depression, and insomnia; node centrality and bridge symptoms connecting the three symptom clusters were examined, and the accuracy and stability of the estimates were assessed with bootstrapping.
RESULTS: In total, 148 women (8.09%) screened positive for depression, 115 (6.28%) for anxiety, and 316 (17.27%) for insomnia. In the symptom network, the symptoms with the highest point estimates of strength centrality were 'I feel as if I am slowed down' (depression), a reduced sense of well-being during the day (insomnia), and 'I feel cheerful' (depression, reverse-scored); these symptoms did not differ reliably from one another or from several other symptoms in bootstrapped difference tests. The same symptoms, together with 'worrying thoughts go through my mind' (anxiety) and 'I can sit at ease and feel relaxed' (anxiety, reverse-scored), showed the highest bridge strength, and this set of five bridge symptoms was identical across all four correlation and estimation methods examined. Bridge expected influence, which retains the direction of the associations, identified the slowed-down item and the worry item as the strongest bridge symptoms.
CONCLUSION: Anxiety, depression, and insomnia are common, interconnected concerns in early pregnancy. Targeting the core and bridge symptoms identified here may enhance intervention effectiveness; however, causal inferences require longitudinal or experimental validation.

articles.title: Experiences of suicidal behaviour and perceived triggers among young people and caregivers at a tertiary healthcare facility in Kenya.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suicidal behavior among adolescents and young adults remains a major public health concern. In sub-Saharan Africa, however, qualitative work that captures both youth and caregiver perspectives is still limited. This study explored the experiences of suicidal behavior, perceived triggers and responses to it among young people and their caregivers attending a tertiary facility in Nairobi, Kenya.
METHODS: This qualitative study was conducted at the outpatient youth mental health clinic of a tertiary facility in Kenya, which receives both walk-in clients and referrals. It included 42 young people aged 13-24 years with personal experience of suicidal behavior and 11 caregivers. Participants were recruited purposively, and semi-structured interviews were conducted separately with young people and caregivers. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed thematically using NVivo.
FINDINGS: Young people described suicidal behavior as developing gradually through cumulative and interacting stressors. Perceived triggers included academic and work-related pressure, family conflict, relationship difficulties, harmful social media experiences, socioeconomic hardship, and psychological or health-related challenges, including depression, substance use, trauma, and abuse. Caregivers expressed concern and willingness to help but frequently reported uncertainty about recognizing distress and responding appropriately.
CONCLUSION: Suicidal behavior in this setting reflected the interaction of personal and structural disadvantage rather than a single precipitating event. Prevention should combine youth-friendly mental health care, caregiver psychoeducation, family involvement, school-based support, and community-level action on poverty, stigma, and service access.

articles.title: Perinatal bereavement care skills, training needs, and workplace support in an Italian descriptive study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Perinatal bereavement is a complex clinical and emotional experience that affects not only parents but also healthcare professionals working in maternal and child healthcare. Despite growing international attention to bereavement care, many healthcare professionals report inadequate preparation, limited organizational support, and insufficient confidence in caring for families following a perinatal death.
OBJECTIVE: To describe self-reported bereavement-care skills, attitudes toward training, awareness of learning needs, and workplace support among healthcare professionals and near-graduation students.
METHODS: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted in Italy between January and April 2026 among healthcare professionals and near-graduation students in maternal and child healthcare. The sample comprised 126 participants. Participants completed an Italian adaptation of the Perinatal Bereavement Care Confidence Scale (PBCCS). Descriptive statistics, internal consistency analysis, and non-parametric inferential tests were performed. Open-ended responses were examined using exploratory thematic content analysis with T-LAB Plus.
RESULTS: The descriptive mean of the 44 adapted questionnaire items was 2.23 (SD = 0.263; possible range 1-3; α = 0.86). Block means were 2.51 for knowledge, 2.22 for skills, 2.55 for self-awareness, and 1.68 for organizational support. These summaries do not constitute validated measures of overall professional confidence. Exploratory omnibus comparisons were significant across professional groups (p = 0.009); the years-of-service comparison was not statistically significant (p = 0.210). The principal reported needs concerned organizational support, training, and emotional coping.
CONCLUSION: The item and block descriptions highlight needs for structured training, reflective and emotional support, and multidisciplinary protocols. The 44-item mean is a descriptive summary of heterogeneous questionnaire content, not a validated measure of overall professional confidence. The cross-sectional study does not establish effects on confidence, quality of care, or staff well-being.

articles.title: Influenza A-Associated Encephalitis and Encephalopathy in Adults: An Exploratory Criteria-Based Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Influenza A can cause encephalopathy or encephalitis, yet adult data are scarce and the two entities are seldom distinguished systematically. This small retrospective study of five adults explored the feasibility and limitations of classifying these complications with the International Encephalitis Consortium (IEC) 2013 criteria and describes their clinical, radiological, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and treatment characteristics.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed five consecutive adults admitted to a tertiary center with polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed influenza A and acute neurological symptoms, all evaluated with brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), lumbar puncture, and electroencephalography (EEG). Encephalitis was defined by the IEC 2013 criteria (altered mental status > 24 h plus ≥ 2 minor criteria of central nervous system (CNS) inflammation). Data were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Three patients met criteria for encephalitis and two for encephalopathy (four women; age 44-68 years). Respiratory influenza A PCR was positive and CSF PCR negative in all. CSF pleocytosis occurred in two patients, bilateral thalamic and subcortical white matter MRI hyperintensities in two, generalized EEG slowing in four, and focal status epilepticus in one. All received oseltamivir; three received high-dose methylprednisolone, two of whom also required intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange. The categories overlapped substantially: EEG slowing and negative CSF PCR occurred in both, and treatment escalation followed clinical course rather than category, with the most intensive regimen required by one patient in each. At 3 months, three patients were asymptomatic and two, both with encephalitis and structural MRI lesions, had persistent deficits.
CONCLUSION: In this small, hypothesis-generating study, IEC-based classification was feasible, but encephalitis and encephalopathy overlapped substantially and the distinction did not determine treatment. The main contribution lies in illustrating both the feasibility and limitations of criteria-based classification in adults with influenza A, rather than in establishing its clinical utility.

articles.title: Metabolic dysfunction associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and obesity.
articles.abstract: Rising global trends in obesity have led to increased prevalence of fatty liver disease known as nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). The previously used, stigma-associated term has been replaced by updated nomenclature-first, metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and subsequently metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This modification reflects a more accurate understanding of disease pathophysiology and removes the emphasis from severe alcohol consumption, while introducing diagnostic criteria centered on metabolic dysfunction. This review also describes related clinical entities like metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and steatotic liver disease (SLD). Global trends in obesity indicate a continuous rise in prevalence, accompanied by an increasing burden of SLD in both adults and pediatric population. Projections suggest that by 2040, more than half of the global population may be affected by both obesity and SLD, highlighting the need for non-invasive diagnostics, effective targeted therapy and structured follow up strategies. Drugs for obesity management like semaglutide and tirzepatide demonstrated clinical improvement primarily through beneficial metabolic effect, highlighting common basis of treatment of obesity and SLD. Although several liver-targeted therapies are currently under investigation, resmetirom represents the first approved pharmacologic agent available on the market. However, lifestyle modification remains significant part of treatment. Looking ahead, field of greatest potential is pharmacotherapy with certain molecules currently under phase 2 and phase 3 clinical trials. Importantly, shared pathophysiologic mechanisms linking obesity, metabolic syndrome and MASLD must not be overlooked in suspicion, diagnosis and treatment of liver diseases.

articles.title: Heritability estimation of subcortical volumes in a multi-ancestry multi-site cohort study.
articles.abstract: Heritability of regional subcortical brain volumes (rSBVs) quantifies the contribution of genetic variation to individual differences in subcortical brain morphology during neurodevelopment. rSBVs are highly heritable in adults but are not well characterized in adolescents. The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study (ABCD), collected across 21 US sites, provides data to characterize the heritability of subcortical structures in adolescence. However, in a multi-site multi-ancestry study, such as ABCD, site-specific effects may co-occur with genetic effects, which can bias heritability estimates. Existing methods that adjust for site effects require additional steps and can lead to inconsistent estimates. We propose a random-effect model-based MOM approach to estimate heritability that is a single-step asymptotically consistent estimator even when ancestries are differentially distributed across sites. Our approach performed well under a wide range of simulations. The proposed approach yielded heritability estimates similar to previous results derived from single-site studies and studies on different age groups, with the cerebellar cortex and hippocampus showing the highest estimated heritability (>50%).

articles.title: Sample size critically shapes the reliability of EEG case-control findings in psychiatry.
articles.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) studies in psychiatry have produced highly inconsistent findings, particularly in case-control designs. Small sample sizes are widely assumed to contribute to this variability, yet their impact on the reliability of EEG group comparisons has not been systematically quantified at scale. Here, we address this key gap using a large multisite resting-state EEG dataset comprising 2,874 participants aged 5-18 years, including individuals with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, autism spectrum disorder, anxiety, learning disorders, and healthy controls. We extracted a comprehensive set of spectral, temporal, and complexity EEG features and performed repeated case-control comparisons across a wide range of sample sizes using extensive random subsampling. Results from small samples were unstable, with inflated and highly variable effect sizes across iterations. In contrast, larger samples produced consistent and reproducible findings, converging on uniformly small but robust effects. Statistical power rose steeply with sample size, whereas false positive rates remained relatively stable. These results demonstrate the central role of sample size in shaping EEG study outcomes and challenge the utility of conventional case-control approaches for biomarker discovery in psychiatry.

articles.title: Processing strategies for improving cortical thickness correspondence between low-field and high-field MRI in young people.
articles.abstract: Portable low-field MRI systems are a promising complement to conventional high-field systems, enabling broader access to MRI. However, correspondence in cortical thickness estimates between low- and high-field MRI in young people remains limited despite its importance for neurodevelopment and psychopathology. To evaluate how multiple low-field image processing approaches improve cortical thickness correspondence with high-field MRI in a large sample of young individuals, we collected T1-weighted (T1w) and T2-weighted (T2w) data using both low-field (64 mT) and high-field (3T) MRI within 1 week of each other from a community sample of young people. We applied deep learning-based super-resolution methods (SynthSR v1 and SynthSR v2) followed by recon-all, or other reconstruction methods (recon-all-clinical and recon-any), to low-field data acquired across multiple sequences (T1w and T2w) and orientations (axial, coronal, sagittal, and multi-orientation average), with and without resampling and/or co-registration. We assessed global, lobar, and regional cortical thickness correspondence with 3T MRI measures based on the Desikan-Killiany atlas using Pearson and intraclass correlations. We compared pipelines using Steiger's Z-tests and Fisher's Z-tests. A total of 150 individuals (mean age, 18.63 ± 5.07 years; 80 female) were included. We observed the highest global correspondence with recon-all-clinical applied to coronal T1w images (r = 0.40, p FDR = 3.02e-05), which significantly exceeded the best global correspondence in our previous study (Fisher's Z = 1.99, p = 0.047). At the lobar and regional levels, multi-orientation T2w images processed with recon-all-clinical showed the highest correspondence across the greatest number of regions (4/12 lobes; 13/68 regions). This pipeline showed the highest correspondence and largest improvements relative to recon-all alone in frontal, cingulate, and temporal regions, including the right pars triangularis (r = 0.52, p FDR = 4.78e-11; Steiger's Z = 4.78, p FDR = 4.25e-06), right caudal anterior cingulate (r = 0.47, p FDR = 3.83e-09; Steiger's Z = 5.46, p FDR = 1.32e-07), and left parahippocampal regions (r = 0.58, p FDR = 2.98e-14; Steiger's Z = 5.17, p FDR = 6.01e-07). We observed significantly improved cortical thickness correspondence in low-field MRI in young people relative to recon-all alone and our prior work. The recon-all-clinical pipeline yielded moderate correspondence, particularly in frontal, cingulate, and temporal regions. Our results demonstrate a methodological improvement in the use of low-field MRI for assessing cortical thickness in young people, providing a quantitative benchmark for current tools in this area.

articles.title: Discriminative value of serum adiponectin as a potential adjunctive marker for HOMA-IR-defined insulin resistance in women with unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insulin resistance (IR) is increasingly recognized as a modifiable contributor to unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion (uRSA), yet its routine surrogate, the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), requires fasting glucose and insulin measurement and therefore an overnight fast, which is inconvenient in routine reproductive-clinic workflows. HOMA-IR is itself a surrogate index rather than the gold standard for insulin sensitivity (the hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp), and any downstream marker must be interpreted accordingly. Adiponectin is an insulin-sensitizing adipokine with low biological variability and limited post-prandial fluctuation. We evaluated whether serum adiponectin, measured in this study from fasting oral-glucose-tolerance-test samples, could serve as an adjunctive marker for HOMA-IR-defined IR in women with uRSA.
METHODS: We performed a single-centre retrospective observational study of women managed for uRSA at a tertiary maternal and child health hospital in Dongguan, southern China. All participants were of Chinese Han ethnicity. Serum total adiponectin was quantified by latex-enhanced immunoturbidimetry (Sekisui Medical Co., Tokyo, Japan; catalogue No. 17083) on a Hitachi 7180 automated analyser, with an intra-assay coefficient of variation (CV) of 3.2% and an inter-assay CV of 5.1%. Adiponectin was measured from the fasting blood sample obtained for the oral glucose tolerance test, and IR was defined as HOMA-IR ≥ 2.41. The primary analysis was conducted in the non-pregnant subgroup (n = 346), with the full cohort (n = 404, including 58 early-pregnant women) analysed secondarily. The relationship between adiponectin and HOMA-IR was assessed by Spearman correlation; adiponectin was compared between IR and non-IR groups using the Mann-Whitney U test. Discriminative performance was quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the optimal cut-off identified by the Youden index. Incremental discrimination of adiponectin beyond age and body mass index (BMI) was evaluated by nested-model AUC comparison using the DeLong test. Sensitivity analyses were conducted with alternative HOMA-IR thresholds (2.0, 2.5 and 3.0). Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for age, BMI and sampling status.
RESULTS: Among 404 women (346 non-pregnant, 58 early-pregnant; all Chinese Han), 203 (50.2%) met the criterion for HOMA-IR-defined IR. Serum adiponectin was significantly lower in the IR group than in the non-IR group (median 6.40 [interquartile range 5.20-8.70] versus 8.50 [6.90-11.10] µg/mL; P < 0.001) and was inversely correlated with HOMA-IR (Spearman ρ = -0.455, 95% confidence interval [CI] - 0.529 to - 0.374; P < 0.001), with a graded decline across ascending HOMA-IR quartiles (P for trend < 0.001). In the primary non-pregnant analysis, adiponectin yielded an AUC of 0.733 (95% CI 0.680-0.786); in the full cohort the AUC was 0.711 (95% CI 0.661-0.761). Adding adiponectin to a model containing age and BMI increased the AUC from 0.759 to 0.788 (DeLong P = 0.038). In the primary non-pregnant analysis, the optimal cut-off of ≤ 6.60 µg/mL provided a sensitivity of 58.3%, a specificity of 78.7%, a positive predictive value of 72.1% and a negative predictive value of 66.7%, with a positive likelihood ratio of 2.73. Sensitivity analyses with HOMA-IR thresholds of 2.0, 2.5 and 3.0 yielded consistent AUCs (0.697-0.724). Each 1 µg/mL decrease in adiponectin was independently associated with IR (adjusted odds ratio 1.17, 95% CI 1.06-1.29; P = 0.002).
CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-centre observational study, serum adiponectin measured from fasting samples showed a consistent inverse association with HOMA-IR-defined IR and moderate, specificity-weighted discrimination in women with uRSA. Adiponectin provided modest incremental discrimination beyond age and BMI. Although insufficiently sensitive to replace fasting indices, a low adiponectin concentration may increase clinical suspicion for IR and help triage women for confirmatory fasting assessment. These findings require prospective validation in independent cohorts before adiponectin can be recommended as a clinical triage marker; the study does not demonstrate that adiponectin predicts pregnancy prognosis or that adiponectin-guided management improves reproductive outcomes.

articles.title: Beyond clinical outcomes: exploring the relationship between healthy lifestyle adherence and metabolic-hepatic biomarkers in obese individuals with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a major driver of metabolic dysfunction and is strongly associated with the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, early identification of individuals at increased metabolic and hepatic risk remains challenging. Composite lifestyle scoring provides a practical and integrative approach to capturing multiple modifiable health behaviors simultaneously. This study aimed to examine the association between a Composite Healthy Lifestyle Score (CHLS) and metabolic and hepatic biomarkers among obese adults with MASLD.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 340 obese adults aged 18-65 years with MASLD who were recruited from gastroenterology and obesity outpatient clinics. The CHLS was constructed based on four modifiable lifestyle factors: diet quality (Healthy Eating Index-2020), physical activity, smoking status, and body weight status. Participants were categorized into four CHLS quartiles. Anthropometric measurements, biochemical markers (fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, insulin concentrations, and liver enzymes), and blood pressure were assessed. Associations between CHLS and metabolic outcomes were evaluated using multivariable-adjusted models.
RESULTS: Higher CHLS was significantly associated with lower fasting blood glucose (adjusted P = 0.039). HbA1c levels also differed significantly across CHLS quartiles after multivariable adjustment (adjusted P = 0.012), although the pattern was non-linear, with the lowest mean HbA1c observed in the second CHLS quartile rather than the highest. Significant inverse associations were also observed between CHLS and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) concentrations, indicating a more favorable hepatic biomarker profile among participants with greater adherence to healthy lifestyle behaviors. After adjustment for potential confounders, no significant differences were observed in lipid profile parameters or blood pressure across CHLS quartiles. Binary logistic regression analysis demonstrated a significant overall association between CHLS and metabolic syndrome (overall P = 0.013). Compared with the lowest CHLS category, participants in the second and third CHLS categories had significantly lower odds of metabolic syndrome, whereas the association for the highest CHLS category was not statistically significant.
CONCLUSION: Greater adherence to healthy lifestyle behaviors, as reflected by a higher CHLS, was associated with lower fasting blood glucose levels and a more favorable hepatic biomarker profile among obese adults with MASLD. Although HbA1c differed significantly across CHLS categories, its relationship with CHLS was non-linear. No significant associations were observed for lipid profile parameters or blood pressure. Overall, CHLS may represent a practical tool for identifying individuals with less favorable metabolic and hepatic profiles and may support targeted preventive strategies in clinical practice and public health.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Reduced circulating osteopontin levels are associated with elevated blood pressure and vascular endothelial-related alterations in children with obesity.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Childhood obesity is associated with metabolic abnormalities and elevated blood pressure, increasing the risk of early cardiovascular complications. Osteopontin (OPN), a multifunctional protein involved in inflammation and vascular homeostasis, has been implicated in cardiometabolic disorders. However, its association with blood pressure alterations in children with obesity remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the associations of serum OPN levels with metabolic parameters, vascular endothelial-related markers, and elevated blood pressure in children with obesity.
METHODS: A total of 106 children were enrolled, including 61 children with obesity and 45 non-obese controls. Anthropometric parameters, metabolic profiles, blood pressure, circulating OPN and adiponectin (ADPN) levels, as well as vascular endothelial-related markers were assessed. Correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between OPN and clinical variables. Multivariable linear regression analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between OPN and systolic blood pressure (SBP) in children with obesity. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to assess the performance of OPN-containing models for identifying elevated blood pressure.
RESULTS: Children with obesity showed higher BMI, blood pressure, triglycerides, total cholesterol, and vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), whereas circulating OPN, adiponectin (ADPN), Wnt family member 5 A (WNT5A), and endothelial cell-specific molecule 1 (ESM1) levels were lower compared with controls (all p < 0.05). In addition, OPN levels were inversely correlated with BMI (r = 0.704, p < 0.001), SBP (r = -0.557, p < 0.001), DBP (r = -0.279, p = 0.013), and VCAM-1 (r = -0.355, p = 0.001), but positively correlated with WNT5A and ESM1 (all p < 0.05). After adjustment for age, sex, and pubertal status, OPN was associated with lower SBP (β = -0.452, 95% CI: -4.30 to -0.74, p = 0.007). The addition of OPN to the basic clinical model improved its ability to identify elevated blood pressure, with the AUC increasing from 0.756 to 0.806.
CONCLUSION: Circulating OPN levels are inversely associated with obesity, blood pressure, and are correlated with vascular endothelial-related markers in children. The findings suggest that serum OPN may serve as a potential biomarker of cardiometabolic risk in children with obesity.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and mid-to-long-term hip joint function in children with non-traumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head: a comparative study of steroid-related, sickle cell disease, and idiopathic etiologies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-traumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) in children is a heterogeneous condition with variable etiologies and prognoses. Few studies have compared mid-to-long-term functional outcomes across etiologic categories in the pediatric population. This study compared clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and 5-year hip joint function among pediatric patients with steroid-related, sickle cell disease (SCD)-associated, and idiopathic ONFH.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 372 pediatric patients (127 steroid-related, 89 SCD-associated, 156 idiopathic) diagnosed with ONFH between 2012 and 2020; the idiopathic group comprised children who fulfilled diagnostic criteria for Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (LCPD), and the terms idiopathic ONFH and LCPD are used synonymously throughout. The patient was the unit of analysis. Primary outcomes were the Harris Hip Score (HHS) at 5-year follow-up (assessed for native, non-replaced hips) and conversion to total hip arthroplasty (THA). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with the log-rank test, competing-risk cumulative incidence analysis accounting for death, a linear mixed-effects model for HHS trajectories, and univariate and multivariable logistic regression were performed.
RESULTS: The SCD group had the worst outcomes, with a THA conversion rate of 53.9% (48/89) and a mean 5-year HHS of 65.6 +/- 19.6, compared with 33.9% (43/127) and 78.4 +/- 14.8 for the steroid-related group, and 9.6% (15/156) and 89.8 +/- 9.2 for the idiopathic (LCPD) group (all p < 0.001). In the multivariable model, SCD etiology (adjusted OR = 5.86, 95% CI: 2.60-13.24), Ficat stage III-IV (adjusted OR = 3.74, 95% CI: 1.93-7.25), and bilateral involvement (adjusted OR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.02-3.80) were independently associated with THA conversion.
CONCLUSIONS: Etiology significantly influences the clinical course and prognosis of pediatric ONFH. SCD-associated ONFH carries the worst prognosis, whereas idiopathic (LCPD) cases show the most favorable outcomes. These findings support etiology-specific management protocols.

articles.title: Machine learning prediction of cyclosporine nephrotoxicity in pediatric patients using therapeutic drug monitoring and clinical data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cyclosporine A (CsA) nephrotoxicity is a dose-limiting toxicity in pediatric immunosuppression, and early identification of children at risk of CsA-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) remains an unmet clinical need.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In retrospective cohorts of CsA-treated inpatients undergoing therapeutic drug monitoring (352 children; 342 adults), a regularized logistic-regression model was compared with six machine-learning classifiers under five feature-selection schemes, three small-sample strategies were evaluated, and adult-child transferability was assessed on 95 aligned features. A 14-variable model was externally validated in an independent pediatric cohort (n = 257).
RESULTS: Regularized logistic regression achieved the best discrimination in children (hold-out AUC 0.800) and adults (hold-out AUC 0.956), with complex models overfitting. Adult and pediatric risk architectures differed fundamentally, with transfer AUCs near chance (≈0.6). The 14-variable model retained discrimination on external validation (AUC 0.784, 95% CI 0.656-0.912).
CONCLUSIONS: On small clinical datasets, regularization rather than complexity determines predictive performance. We provide an interpretable, TDM-integrated pediatric CsA-AKI model, deployed as an online calculator, supporting early risk stratification in pediatric CsA therapy.

articles.title: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and blood pressure in childhood: A systematic review of prospective observational studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) may affect early-life cardiovascular programming, but epidemiological findings regarding blood pressure outcomes in children remain inconsistent. This systematic review synthesized evidence on associations between prenatal PFAS exposure and blood pressure or hypertension in children and adolescents.
METHODS: Following Cochrane recommendations and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, MEDLINE (EBSCO), and Embase were searched through 02 November 2026. The search strategy was developed with an information specialist. Prospective studies reporting prenatal PFAS exposure and offspring blood pressure outcomes were included. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E. Due to substantial methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis.
RESULTS: Thirteen prospective cohort studies from North America, Europe, and Asia were included. Associations between individual PFAS and systolic or diastolic blood pressure were generally small and inconsistent across compounds, exposure windows, and ages at outcome assessment. Evidence regarding PFAS mixtures was similarly heterogeneous, with some studies reporting associations with systolic blood pressure or cardiometabolic outcomes, while others observed null or inverse associations. Heterogeneity in exposure assessment, mixture modeling approaches, and outcome definitions precluded quantitative synthesis.
LIMITATIONS OF EVIDENCE: The evidence was limited by heterogeneity across studies, potential residual confounding, differences in exposure assessment and outcome definitions, and varying risk of bias.
INTERPRETATION: Current evidence suggests that prenatal PFAS exposure may influence offspring BP, but findings remain inconsistent. Harmonized longitudinal studies with standardized exposure assessment and robust mixture methodologies are needed to clarify the role of early-life PFAS exposure in pediatric cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Multiomics Approach to Regionally Profile Zinc-Driven Host-Gut Microbiome Interactions in the Intestinal Tract.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Zinc (Zn) deficiency (ZnD) is a major risk factor for metabolic and inflammatory diseases associated with gut microbial alterations, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, and inflammatory bowel disease. Despite its importance, there are no established dietary recommendations for Zn supplementation in individuals with these conditions, except in cases of severe diarrhea in children. This gap stems from inconsistent outcomes in Zn supplementation trials, suggesting an incomplete understanding of Zn-mediated spatial regulation within the host-microbiome interface.
METHODS: Here, we employed a multi-omics approach to investigate Zn-driven host-gut microbial interactions along the intestinal tract of mice fed Zn-adequate (ZnA) or ZnD diets.
RESULTS: Radiotracing and metallomics analyses revealed region-specific Zn gradients across intestinal tissues and demonstrated reduced mucosal Zn levels in conventionalized compared with germ-free mice, highlighting an influence of microbial colonization on mucosal Zn availability. Transcriptomic analyses identified shared interferon-dominant immune activation in both the small intestine (SI) and the colon under ZnD conditions, accompanied by region-specific epithelial remodeling programs. In the SI, ZnD suppressed apical surface gene networks while inducing Paneth cell-associated antimicrobial responses. In contrast, ZnD colon exhibited suppression of apical junction and extracellular matrix (ECM) structural gene programs. Metagenomic profiling revealed reduced microbial diversity in the SI under ZnD, while the colon displayed enrichment of glycan-degrading taxa, including Hungatella hathewayi and Bacteroides ovatus, along with Clostridioides difficile, a glycan-responsive pathogen that benefits from microbial glycan degradation. Integrated host-microbe correlation and network analyses in the colon identified coordinated associations between ECM/cytoskeletal gene expression and glycosaminoglycan (GAG)-utilizing bacterial taxa. Functional annotation demonstrated enrichment of GAG-catabolic enzymes under ZnD conditions, with the strongest homology mapping to B. ovatus and H. hathewayi, and qPCR confirmed increased tissue-associated abundance of bacterial GAG-utilizing gene sequences alongside reduced host ECM gene expression.
CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Zn deficiency induces region-specific host epithelial and microbial adaptations, revealing a coordinated ECM-GAG-microbe axis in the colon and distinct epithelial remodeling programs along the intestinal tract.

articles.title: Monitoring of asymptomatic AIP mutated PituitarY patients (MAAPY): An ENEA study.
articles.abstract: The penetrance of pathogenic-likely pathogenic (PV-LPV) AIP variants is incomplete, as only 15%-30% of carriers develop a pituitary adenoma. There is no clear consensus on the optimal follow-up for relatives carrying an AIP pathogenic variant. The Monitoring of Asymptomatic AIP mutated PituitarY patients (MAAPY) study, initiated by the European NeuroEndocrine Association, aims to recruit family members of patients with a pathogenic AIP variant to assess the risk of asymptomatic AIP mutation carriers developing pituitary adenomas and to suggest the optimal follow-up for these individuals. This retrospective study invited endocrinologists worldwide to contribute. Index cases with AIP variants who developed a pituitary adenoma were included, as well as their relatives, whether affected or asymptomatic. Each variant was reclassified according to the ACMG-AMP guidelines to assess pathogenicity. A total of 19 centers from 5 countries contributed data and included 209 subjects with 55 different AIP variants. Of these, 39 were classified as PV-LPV variants and involved 167 individuals: 62 index cases and 105 relatives from 38 different kindreds. No relatives were tested for 24 index cases. Among relatives carrying PV-LPV, 23 were affected and 82 were asymptomatic. Index cases were significantly younger at PitNET diagnosis compared to affected relatives (median 20.0 ± 9.1 vs. 30.2 ± 10.1 years, respectively; p < .0002), while index cases presented more frequently with macroadenomas compared with affected relatives (96.6% vs. 75.0%). In all but one of the affected relatives, the PitNET was already known at the time of the molecular diagnosis or was diagnosed during the initial assessment following genetic testing. One asymptomatic patient diagnosed genetically at age 18 subsequently developed a somatotroph microadenoma at the age of 27. The maximum estimated cumulative incidence among relatives carrying PV-LPV was 28% by age 49. The median age at molecular diagnosis in asymptomatic relatives was 38 years, with limited follow-up after genetic testing. This retrospective study shows a penetrance of AIP PV-LPV of 28% after variant reclassification. When genetic screening is performed after the age of 30, the PitNET is already known or diagnosed during the initial assessment following genetic testing. Our data suggest that long-term follow-up has a low yield and may be unnecessary thereafter.

articles.title: Happy Homework 2.0: effects on 24-hour movement behaviours in children-findings from a pilot cluster randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children's 24-h movement behaviours-physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and sleep-are critical to health and wellbeing, yet many fail to meet recommended daily guidelines. School-based health interventions offer a scalable approach to improve movement behaviours, though their impact may be limited by competing academic demands. Homework presents an opportunity to extend the reach of school-based health interventions into the home environment. Happy Homework (HH 2.0) was developed as a digital intervention to integrate movement-based activities into home routines. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and usability of HH 2.0 among primary school children.
METHODS: An 8-week pilot cluster randomised controlled trial was conducted across four primary schools in the West of Scotland, with classes randomly allocated to intervention or control. Feasibility, usability, and acceptability were assessed using basic app-usage analytics and questionnaires completed by children, parents and teachers. Secondary outcomes included physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep measured via activPAL devices, which provided multiple posture- and movement-based metrics. Self-report sleep questionnaires were included, with children's motivation measured through basic psychological need satisfaction questionnaires. Linear mixed-effects models examined group by time interactions, accounting for clustering by school and repeated measures.
RESULTS: A total of 82 children aged 8-12 years were recruited (60% of those invited), with 87% retained at follow up, indicating good feasibility. App-use analytics indicated repeated engagement, although overall use was modest, defined by declining frequency and duration of interactions over time. Secondary outcome data from activPAL devices demonstrated a significant group x time difference in sedentary behaviour, with greater increases in the intervention group compared to the control (B = 66.2 min/day, p < .05). Self-reported sleep also showed a significant group × time interaction, with smaller increases in reported sleep duration in the intervention group relative to control (p < .01). No other significant group × time interactions were found for other secondary outcomes.
CONCLUSION: HH 2.0 was feasible and acceptable as a homework-based health intervention however, engagement levels likely limited its effectiveness. Findings outline the potential and challenges of digital school-based health interventions and emphasises the need to strengthen implementation strategies, sustain engagement, and enhance parent and teacher involvement.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT07631754 (retrospectively registered).

articles.title: Evolution of Newborn Screening Technology for Cystic Fibrosis: From Biochemical Assay to Next Generation Sequencing.
articles.abstract: Newborn screening (NBS) for cystic fibrosis (CF) (OMIM: 219700) became possible in 1979 with the description of elevation of immunoreactive trypsinogen (IRT) levels in the blood of affected babies, and this analyte can be measured from dried blood spot filter paper cards. NBS for CF was initially a measurement of this biomarker, but the methodology evolved to a two-tier test with DNA testing for cystic fibrosis transmembrane regulator (CFTR) variants. Currently, all NBS programs utilize measurement of IRT as the initial step, and if the IRT is elevated, assay for CFTR variants. The number of variants identified has evolved from NC_000007.14:g.117559592_117559594del (GRCh38) (NM_000492.4:c.1521_1523del p.Phe508del; legacy:F508del) only (the most common variant in the White population) to the 23 variants originally recommended by the American College of Medical Genetics for population screening, to panels of variants ranging in size from 39 to 70 variants, and to greatly expanded CFTR panels through gene sequencing. In order to equitably diagnose all infants regardless of race/ethnicity, CFTR gene sequencing is mandatory. Sanger sequencing has been a methodology utilized, but next generation sequencing (NGS) is more efficient and cost effective. In 2025, the United States Cystic Fibrosis Foundation recommended CFTR sequencing for CF NBS and with this recommendation, there is rapid growth of the adoption of NGS in states' CF NBS programs.

articles.title: RDX-Associated Hearing Loss: Expanded Variant Spectrum, Founder Effect, and Mechanistic Insights from Functional Assays.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Bi-allelic RDX variants are responsible for DFNB24, a type of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss. Due to its rarity, the mutational spectrum, genotype-phenotype correlations, and population genetics of this condition are not yet fully understood.
METHODS: We performed exome or targeted panel sequencing, along with segregation analysis, and evaluated clinical data. We conducted minigene assays on three intronic variants, with canonical splice-site variants included as positive controls, and used molecular dynamics simulations to explore the predicted conformational effects of missense and in-frame deletion alleles. Additionally, we compiled a systematic review of all previously reported DFNB24 families.
RESULTS: We identified 12 distinct bi-allelic RDX variants in 16 families, six of which were novel. Those affected experienced bilateral, prelingual, or early childhood onset of sensorineural hearing loss, with varying degrees of severity. Minigene assays demonstrated variant-specific activation of cryptic splice sites for all three intronic variants, generating frameshift transcripts predicted to result in loss of function. Exome-derived haplotype and founder-dating analyses identified two distinct shared ancestral haplotypes among the Iranian families. Probands homozygous for c.1076_1079del, an allele found in four unrelated families, shared a 2.44-Mb haplotype with a most recent common ancestor approximately 386 years ago (95% CI, 83.7-677.7 years), whereas the two probands homozygous for c.1729A>T (Families 14 and 16) shared a 7.88-Mb haplotype dating to approximately 99.9 years ago (95% CI, 24.3-521.1 years), indicating a single ancestral event rather than two independent observations. The systematic review showed that reported DFNB24 families were concentrated in Middle Eastern and South Asian populations.
CONCLUSIONS: This work significantly broadens the RDX mutational spectrum, improves genotype-phenotype correlations, and identifies a founder allele together with a second, more recently shared ancestral haplotype. These data represent the largest single cohort of people with RDX-associated hearing loss compiled to date.

articles.title: Genome sequencing and clinical diagnosis in 186 pediatric and adult patients with genetic skeletal disorders.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize the clinical and genetic landscape of genetic skeletal disorders in a patient cohort and evaluate the diagnostic yield of genome sequencing.
METHODS: A cohort of 186 patients in 182 unrelated families with clinical and radiographic features of genetic skeletal disorders was investigated between 2015 and 2022 using short-read genome sequencing. Clinical data and skeletal radiographs were reviewed according to the 2023 International Nosology of Genetic Skeletal Disorders. Patients without a molecular diagnosis underwent clinical reassessment and additional analyses, including updated gene panels and family-based sequencing.
RESULTS: A molecular diagnosis was established in 134/182 families (73.6%), based on pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants. Genome sequencing identified 125 diagnoses at initial analysis (68.7%), and nine additional diagnoses after reanalysis or family-based investigations (4.9%). Autosomal dominant disorders accounted for 69%, autosomal recessive for 24%, and X-linked for 7%. Variants of uncertain significance in phenotype-consistent genes were found in nine families, including biallelic variants in genes associated with autosomal dominant disease (COL10A1 and UFSP2). A likely non-genetic cause was identified in five families.
CONCLUSION: Genome sequencing is an effective diagnostic approach for identifying a broad range of disease-causing variants, particularly when combined with detailed clinical and radiographic assessment and reanalysis.

articles.title: Vosoritide Treatment in Children with Hypochondroplasia: Three-Year Results from a Phase 2 Extension Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Vosoritide is a C-type natriuretic peptide analog approved for achondroplasia and under investigation for selected genetic causes of short stature. We previously reported the 12-months results of a phase 2 trial in children with hypochondroplasia (NCT04219007). Here, we report safety and efficacy outcomes from the three-year extension phase.
METHODS: After completing a 6-month observation period followed by 12 months of daily subcutaneous vosoritide (15 μg/kg/day), participants with an increase in annualized growth velocity (AGV) >1.6 cm/year compared to baseline were eligible to continue in an open-label extension phase.
RESULTS: Thirteen participants entered the extension phase and completed three years of treatment. Mean height SDS increased by 0.72 SD from Day 1 to Year 3, reaching -2.64±0.79 SD on the CDC growth charts. A similar increase was observed on the hypochondroplasia-specific charts (0.83 SD). Mean AGV increased from 4.27±0.70 cm/year at baseline to 7.24±0.80 cm/year at Year 1 and remained above baseline at Year 3 (6.13±1.27 cm/year). No new safety concerns were identified.
CONCLUSION: Vosoritide was associated with sustained improvements in growth in a selected cohort of initial good responders with hypochondroplasia. The treatment was well tolerated. Limitations of the extension study include selection bias and a small sample size.

articles.title: A Single-Center Retrospective Analysis of Artificial Intelligence-Based Emotion Recognition Systems for Attention-Regulation Training in Children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often experience attention instability and emotion dysregulation. Existing interventions typically lack real-time responsiveness and ecological validity. This study retrospectively examined historical training records from an AI-assisted closed-loop system integrating emotion recognition and behavioral feedback for attention regulation in children with ADHD.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective analysis included historical training records from 60 children with ADHD who had completed either AI-assisted attention training or conventional attention training between 2021 and 2024. The AI-assisted training-record group comprised children whose archived records included 12 sessions of integrated cognitive training involving Go/No-Go, CPT, and Flanker tasks with real-time AI-generated feedback based on task performance and facial-emotion monitoring. The conventional training-record group completed the same attention tasks without AI-based feedback. Assessments included task performance, Conners Continuous Performance Test, 3rd Edition (CPT-3), teacher ratings, and emotion metrics, analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, linear growth modeling, and structural equation modeling (SEM).
RESULTS: Compared with conventional training records, AI-assisted training records showed greater pre-post changes in reaction time (RT), RT variability, and task accuracy, together with fewer commission errors in CPT-3. Post-feedback behavioral recovery was observed in 78.3% of feedback events. Teacher ratings showed consistent pre-post improvements across attention maintenance, emotional regulation, and task execution. Negative emotion labels decreased from 42.3% to 24.6% (p = 0.003). SEM supported an associative pathway linking emotion recognition frequency, feedback frequency, and RT reduction (95% CI: 0.15-0.38).
CONCLUSIONS: The retrospective findings suggest that AI-assisted closed-loop training records were associated with favorable changes in attention and emotional-state indicators in children with ADHD. These exploratory results support further prospective, externally validated studies before broader clinical or educational implementation.

articles.title: Lao PDR's achievements in family planning: a mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The use of modern contraceptives and family planning (FP) services has increased globally; however, progress varies across countries and regions. The current research aims to examine the key socioecological determinants driving the demand for and utilisation of modern contraceptive methods in the Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), providing insights into the factors that facilitate contraceptive uptake.
METHODOLOGY: We employed a mixed-methods analytical approach including: (1) a systematic literature review to synthesise existing evidence, (2) quantitative analysis of secondary data to identify demographic and behavioural trends, (3) a desk review of relevant policies and programmes to evaluate the policy landscape and (4) community-based qualitative design to explore sociocultural and contextual factors supporting FP uptake.
RESULTS: Modern contraceptive prevalence rate (mCPR) rose steadily from 38.6% in 2005 to 56.3% in 2017, associated with education, household wealth, contraceptive knowledge and age at first sex, alongside marked geographic and ethnic disparities that persisted throughout. Policy analysis identified three programmatic phases: foundation-building (1988–2005), scale-up aligned with the Millennium Development Goals (2005–2015) and an equity-focused phase emphasising adolescent health (2015–present). Qualitative findings revealed five interconnected themes driving FP progress in Lao PDR: political commitment, financing sustainability, health systems strengthening, community-driven demand generation and women’s reproductive agency. While strong policy commitment and expanded service delivery have improved access, donor dependency, geographic barriers for rural and ethnic minority populations and persistent gender-based decision-making constraints continue to limit equitable contraceptive use.
CONCLUSION: Lao PDR’s FP success reflects the simultaneous alignment of political will, financing structures, service delivery and shifting social norms. Sustaining and extending these gains will require a structured domestic financing transition, strengthened commodity supply and workforce systems, expansion of youth-friendly services into rural and ethnic minority areas and continued investment in gender-transformative community engagement to translate increased spousal communication into genuine shared decision-making.

articles.title: How Bolivia became a positive outlier in family planning: an in-depth mixed-methods case study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bolivia made remarkable progress in increasing modern contraceptive use among all women of reproductive age, achieving an exponential annual growth rate exceeding 5% between 1989 and 2016—from 8% to 32.4%. Based on a systematic, criteria-based country selection process implemented by the Exemplars in Global Health coalition, Bolivia was identified as a case for in-depth analysis of progress in family planning. In this study, we aimed to identify the socioeconomic, demographic, political, programmatic and health system factors that have contributed to Bolivia’s success in family planning.
METHODS: We employed a mixed-methods analytical approach, incorporating results from: (1) a systematic literature review, (2) quantitative analysis of secondary data, (3) a desk review of policies and programmes and (4) qualitative analysis of primary data. This study summarises the findings from these four analyses.
RESULTS: Bolivia’s progress in family planning outcomes is the result of a multifaceted approach emphasising political commitment, community engagement, health system strengthening and innovative service delivery mechanisms. Key initiatives such as the Universal Maternal and Child Health Insurance and the Revolving Fund for Contraceptives were instrumental in improving the accessibility of family planning services. These efforts ensured a steady supply of contraceptives and reduced financial barriers for marginalised populations particularly in rural and underserved areas.
CONCLUSION: Bolivia’s success in family planning since 1989 has been driven by strong political commitment and policy reforms that created a supportive sexual and reproductive health policy landscape. This, combined with the contributions of non-governmental organisations, has improved access to family planning services. Despite these advancements, service gaps persist for adolescents and marginalised groups, highlighting the need for continued investment in education and healthcare. This study provides valuable insights for enhancing contraceptive use and meeting family planning needs in similar global contexts.

articles.title: Knowledge about prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV among reproductive-age women in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) remains one of the most serious global public health challenges. While several studies have demonstrated that women's knowledge is crucial for preventing mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT), consolidated evidence from Africa is still insufficient. This combined evidence informs policymakers and health professionals in designing and implementing effective strategies to fill knowledge gaps about PMTCT. Therefore, this review aimed to determine the overall estimate of knowledge about prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV among reproductive-age women in Africa.
METHODS: This study followed the Preferred Reporting Item Review and Meta-analysis (PRISMA) guidelines. The study protocol for this review was registered on PROSPERO (reference number CRD420251077063). A comprehensive and systematic literature search was conducted across multiple databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and HINARI, to identify relevant and eligible studies. In addition, relevant articles were identified through searches on Google Scholar. Extracted data from the included studies were analyzed using STATA version 17. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) appraisal tool was employed to assess the methodological rigor of the eligible studies. A random-effects model with the Der Simonian-Laird method was applied to determine the pooled prevalence of women's comprehensive knowledge about PMTCT of HIV. A funnel plot and Egger's test were utilized to evaluate the presence of publication bias. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic and Cochrane's Q test.
RESULTS: A total of 37 eligible studies, involving 466,995 reproductive-aged women, were included in the quantitative meta-analysis. The pooled estimate of women's knowledge on prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV (PMTCT) was 56.97% (95% CI: 52.37%, 61.56%), indicating nearly half of reproductive-age women in Africa lacked adequate knowledge of PMTCT. Significant factors associated with higher knowledge of PMTCT included urban residence (AOR = 1.20; 95% CI: 1.12, 1.28), attainment of primary education (AOR = 1.32; 95% CI: 1.20, 1.44), secondary education (AOR = 1.66; 95% CI: 1.38, 2.01), tertiary or higher education (AOR = 1.98; 95% CI: 1.59, 2.46), being aged 25-34 (AOR = 1.36; 95% CI: 1.32, 1.41) or 35-49 (AOR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.15, 3.36), exposure to mass media (AOR = 1.32; 95% CI: 1.20, 1.44), having adequate knowledge of HIV (AOR = 1.964; 95% CI: 1.45, 2.66), history of maternal HIV infection and HIV-infected child (AOR = 2.19; 95% CI: 1.04, 4.60), and higher women's wealth index categories: poorer (AOR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.05-1.62), middle-income (AOR = 1.29; 95% CI: 1.11, 1.50), and richer groups (AOR = 1.93; 95% CI: 1.32, 2.81).
CONCLUSIONS: Despite substantial progress in HIV prevention efforts, knowledge of PMTCT among reproductive-age women in Africa remains suboptimal, with considerable disparities across settings. The findings highlight persistent inequalities related to education, socioeconomic status, age category, geographical location, and access to health information. Thus, strengthening PMTCT knowledge requires tailored, integrated, and context-specific strategies that expand women's educational opportunities, improve access to reliable HIV-related information through media and comprehensive maternal health services, and prioritize underserved rural and socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. These proactive efforts are crucial to encouraging women for primary prevention of HIV, empowering women to make informed decisions, improving engagement with PMTCT services, and accelerating progress toward the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV in Africa.

articles.title: The social production of silence and vulnerability after child sexual abuse: A qualitative study of young women from the Romanian child protection system.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Child sexual abuse (CSA) is often embedded in broader contexts of cumulative victimization, while opportunities for disclosure and protection are shaped by familial, relational, and institutional conditions. These processes remain insufficiently understood among young people with histories of placement in child protection systems.
OBJECTIVE: This study explored young women's retrospective accounts of CSA and how they understood the conditions shaping silence, vulnerability, disclosure, and recovery in the context of their histories of placement in the Romanian child protection system.
PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Seven women aged 19-27 participated in semi-structured telephone interviews. The interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed in Romanian using a hybrid inductive and theoretically informed thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Participants situated CSA within broader experiences of physical and emotional abuse, neglect, family violence, parental alcohol misuse, and the absence of protective adults. They described silence as shaped by threats, fear, shame, self-blame, dependency, the normalization of violence, uncertainty about institutional responses, and experiences of invalidation. Their accounts presented vulnerability as relationally and structurally conditioned, including through limited or uneven access to protection and support. Trusted adults, educators, psychologists, supportive partners, and educational opportunities were described by participants as supportive resources in relation to disclosure, emotional well-being, autonomy, and the reinterpretation of traumatic experiences.
CONCLUSIONS: Participants' retrospective accounts suggest that silence and vulnerability following CSA cannot be understood solely as individual responses to trauma. They were experienced as shaped by relationships of dependency, normalized violence, responses to disclosure, and access to protective and supportive resources within and beyond the child protection system.

articles.title: Psychotherapy in routine clinical practice in Chile with children who have been sexually abused: Factors associated with initial symptoms and trajectory of symptomatic change.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The efficacy of child sexual abuse treatment has been demonstrated. Nonetheless, a gap persists in understanding how different factors are associated with treatment outcomes. Furthermore, evidence in non-high-income countries and in routine clinical practice is scarce.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the children's symptoms trajectories over the course of treatment for child sexual abuse, and whether child and caregiver characteristics, the nature of the abusive experience, and caregiver session attendance are associated with initial symptom severity and symptomatic change.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The sample comprised 78 children aged 4 to 9 (x̄ 6.6; SD 1.6) who were referred to specialized treatment centres for sexual abuse in Santiago, Chile.
METHODS: Children's primary caregivers and professionals leading their treatment completed questionnaires at the beginning, middle and end of treatment. Multilevel models were utilized to analyse changes in the child's symptomatology.
RESULTS: Internalizing, externalizing and post-traumatic stress symptoms decreased during treatment (p < .001). Children whose caregiver reported a history of child sexual abuse had higher initial scores across all three types of assessed symptoms (p < .05 or less), and those whose caregiver reported higher post-traumatic stress had higher initial internalizing and post-traumatic stress scores (p < .001). Caregiver session attendance was the only factor linked to change, with more sessions associated with a steeper reduction in post-traumatic symptoms (p < .01).
CONCLUSIONS: Children receiving treatment as usual in Chile showed symptom reduction over the course of the intervention, although the observational design precludes attributing this change to treatment. Caregiver-related factors were consistently associated with children's symptoms, with potential implications for clinical practice and for research using an intergenerational approach.

articles.title: Configurations of family and socioeconomic circumstances and registered outcomes among children investigated by child welfare services in Sweden: A latent class analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children investigated by child welfare services (CWS) are often exposed to multiple, co-occurring family and socioeconomic difficulties. Less is known about how such circumstances cluster within this population and whether different configurations are associated with different outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: To identify profiles of family and socioeconomic circumstances among children investigated by CWS and examine their associations with criminal justice involvement, mental health-related medication use, and school performance.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The source cohort comprised 1764 children aged 7-12 years investigated by CWS in Stockholm, Sweden, in 2019 following concerns of maltreatment. The latent class analytic sample included 1660 children with complete data on six class indicators.
METHODS: Latent class analysis was conducted using indicators of foreign background, single-parent household, large household size, low income, persistent parental unemployment, and parental criminal conviction. Associations with distal outcomes were estimated using two-step maximum-likelihood models that retained uncertainty in latent class membership and adjusted for age or birth cohort and sex, as appropriate. Confidence intervals were obtained using 600 nonparametric bootstrap replications.
RESULTS: Three partly overlapping profiles were identified: Multiple adversity (38.3%), Low income and foreign background (21.1%), and Lower adversity (40.6%). In outcome-specific analyses, the Multiple adversity profile had higher odds of antidepressant medication use (OR = 1.79, 95% CI [1.27, 2.69]) and ADHD medication use (OR = 1.53, 95% CI [1.07, 2.45]) than the Lower adversity profile. The Low income and foreign background profile had higher odds of low school performance (OR = 1.96, 95% CI [1.09, 3.12]) than the Lower adversity profile. Associations with criminal justice outcomes were imprecise. None of the 15 pairwise outcome-profile contrasts remained statistically significant after Holm correction for multiple testing.
CONCLUSIONS: Children investigated by CWS showed heterogeneous and partly overlapping configurations of family and socioeconomic circumstances. Outcome-specific patterns suggest that different configurations may be associated with different domains of functioning, but the findings should be considered exploratory given the multiple-testing results. Replication with longer follow-up and richer measures of family processes and child functioning is needed.

articles.title: Extreme temperatures and child neglect: A nationwide case-crossover study of Brazilian children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neglect is the most frequently reported but least studied form of child maltreatment. Because it arises in part from the conditions under which care is provided, neglect may be sensitive to environmental stressors associated with a warming climate. As an act of omission, it may also respond to heat through pathways distinct from those implicated in abusive behavior. However, population-level evidence on this association remains limited.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between heat and child neglect in a middle-income setting and examine heterogeneity across child and case characteristics.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: 150,163 notifications of neglect or abandonment involving children aged 0 to 9, recorded in Brazil's national violence notification system across 3428 municipalities, 2012 to 2019.
METHODS: Time-stratified case-crossover analysis with conditional logistic regression. Each child served as their own control, matched on municipality, calendar month, year, and day of week. Exposure was municipal daily maximum temperature, categorized with 27 to 30 °C as reference.
RESULTS: Odds of child neglect increase with temperature. On days of 33 °C or above, odds were 6.0% higher than at 27 to 30 °C (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.09). Below 24 °C, they were 6.0% lower (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.96). Findings were robust to alternative event dates, reference categories, and municipality exclusions. No variation appeared by sex or race. Exploratory age comparison suggested a larger association among children aged 5 to 9 than among those aged 0 to 4 (ratio of odds ratios 1.10, 95% CI 1.02-1.18, p = 0.017), although the difference did not meet the Bonferroni-adjusted threshold.
CONCLUSIONS: Heat is measurably associated with child neglect. Exploratory analyses suggest that these associations are larger in older children, though this effect does not persist after correction for multiple comparisons. Child welfare research and practice should consider environmental conditions as a potentially relevant and modifiable context.

articles.title: "It is worth seeing this, and it is never too late": Survivors' expectations of significant others during intrafamilial child sexual abuse.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Research on child sexual abuse has largely examined children's needs and expectations after disclosure. Less is known about how survivors retrospectively understand their expectations of significant others who were present during intrafamilial child sexual abuse (IFCSA), before disclosure became possible.
OBJECTIVE: This study examined what adult survivors of IFCSA expected from significant others during and after the abuse, and how these expectations were shaped by others' relational roles, authority, and capacity to intervene.
PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: The study included 18 adult survivors of intrafamilial child sexual abuse (IFCSA) who reported the presence of significant others during abusive incidents. Participants were recruited through online support groups for adults with histories of childhood abuse.
METHODS: Guided by Denzin's interpretive paradigm and reflexive thematic analysis, the study draws on semi-structured, in-depth interviews to examine survivors' expectations of significant others and the meanings attributed to their presence.
RESULTS: Participants' expectations clustered around three relational demands: to be witnessed, to be protected, and to be stood with. Expectations differed according to relational role and capacity, with mothers, adults, siblings, and professionals each assigned distinct forms of responsibility.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings show that the presence of others may shape survivors' traumatic meaning-making before, during, and long after the disclosure. Practice and policy should support earlier recognition, protective action, and long-term acknowledgment.

articles.title: Pancreatic surgery in children: nationwide retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paediatric patients differ in various ways from adult populations, but comprehensive multicentre or population-based data are missing for paediatric pancreatic surgery. This study evaluated indications, procedures, complications, and mortality in paediatric patients undergoing pancreatic surgery.
METHODS: This retrospective observational population-based cohort study queried the German Diagnosis-Related Group database for all patients aged < 19 years who underwent pancreatic surgical procedures between 2010 and 2023. The primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and complication rates. Sex- and age-based differences in surgical indications and procedures were explored as secondary outcomes. Descriptive statistics and multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify risk factors for mortality and perioperative complications.
RESULTS: Among the 761 patients identified, indications for pancreatic surgery encompassed chronic pancreatitis (284 patients, 37.3%), pancreatic tumours (221, 29.0%), trauma (127, 16.7%), extrapancreatic tumours (70, 9.2%), and other diseases (59, 7.8%), with significant sex- and age-based differences (P < 0.001).
