For researchers, results highlighted a need for the use of a consistent outcome measure to support comparison between interventions, describe participants in further detail and prioritize systematic reviews of interventions that are sufficiently similar in format and goals.

articles.title: An In Silico-In Vitro Framework for Model-Informed Precision Dosing in Oncology: Proof-of-Principle for Doxorubicin in Patient-Derived Sarcoma Spheroids.
articles.abstract: Drug dose and drug exposure time are important factors influencing the tumor-specific response to pharmacological agents. These parameters are only minimally reflected, if at all, in current functional precision medicine platforms and general prediction algorithms. In this study, we combined individualized pharmacokinetic modeling with functional long-term in vitro testing in patient-derived tumor spheroids to allow design of effective dosing regimens for solid tumors. Doxorubicin (DOX), which is used as a standard of care in the treatment of solid tumors such as soft tissue and bone sarcomas, served as a model drug. Based on an individualized physiologically-based pharmacokinetic DOX model for a 16-year-old woman, a series of study conditions were defined using the computationally modeled human area under the curve (AUC) for in vitro testing design. The different conditions spanned a range of treatment conditions from long-term exposure at low concentrations to short-term exposure at high concentrations, using patient-derived soft-tissue rhabdoid myosarcoma tumor spheroids derived from a 16-year-old cancer patient. Consistent with clinical observations, our results indicate that the outcome depended mainly on DOX concentration, while the exposure time was almost insignificant. Moreover, our study showed that the inhibitory DOX effect reaches saturation despite the AUC being linearly dependent on the administered dose such that lower DOX doses with similar antitumoral efficacy, yet lower systemic toxicity, can be achieved. The concept presented here is intended to serve as a foundation for in silico-in vitro research, with the aim of enhancing precision dosing in oncology.

articles.title: L-Asparaginase exposure and immune fitness in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia: A critical evidence appraisal for immunotherapy integration.
articles.abstract: L-asparaginase (L-ASP) is indispensable in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but circulating and marrow-resident immune cells encounter the same systemic amino-acid perturbation as leukemic blasts. Whether this exposure modifies the fitness of cells required for immunotherapy remains unresolved. This critical narrative review evaluates L-ASP and amino-acid-restriction evidence across T cells, natural killer cells, B cells, macrophages, and the bone-marrow niche, and relates it to blinatumomab, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, and checkpoint blockade. We assess intervention directness, clinical relevance, and study quality separately. T-cell studies show that asparagine supports early activation, whereas selected activated CD8⁺ states can mount an activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4)-dependent nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) response under defined restriction conditions. Direct in-vitro asparaginase studies report differing effects on human natural killer-cell killing and should be distinguished from glutamine withdrawal or intracellular glutaminase inhibition; direct enzyme-exposure studies also identify B-cell and macrophage effects in non-pediatric-ALL models, while local marrow effects remain uncertain. Clinical regimens establish that L-ASP and immunotherapies can be used within the same treatment program, but they do not define a metabolic washout interval. We therefore distinguish serum enzyme activity, biochemical substrate recovery, and functional immune recovery. Prospective studies should link these measures to partner-specific cellular, manufacturing, and clinical endpoints. Current evidence supports testable compatibility hypotheses, not fixed scheduling rules.

articles.title: Correlation between maternal serum pgRNA levels during pregnancy and neonatal virological characteristics at birth in HBV-infected pregnant women.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between serum pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) in pregnant women with chronic HBV (CHB) infection during pregnancy and maternal clinical characteristics, virological characteristics of newborns at birth, and mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) outcomes.
METHODS: 312 pregnant women with CHB and their newborns were followed up for 12 months, and their clinical data were collected. Spearman correlation analysis was used to evaluate associations between maternal indicators and neonatal outcomes, and logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with neonatal HBeAg positivity.
RESULTS: Maternal HBV DNA, HBsAg, and HBeAg levels were significantly higher in the pgRNA-positive group. All infants followed up to 12 months were negative for both HBsAg and HBV DNA, yielding a 100% success rate of MTCT prevention. Neonatal HBeAg levels at birth were associated with maternal pgRNA levels. Maternal pgRNA levels were significantly higher in mothers of HBeAg-positive newborns than in those of HBeAg-negative newborns, whereas no significant association was found between maternal pgRNA levels and neonatal HBsAg or HBV DNA status. Neonatal HBeAg level was weakly positively correlated with maternal pgRNA levels (r = 0.17, P < 0.01) and maternal HBeAg levels (r = 0.12, P < 0.05). Maternal pgRNA, HBeAg, HBsAg, HBV DNA, age, and treatment were identified as factors associated with neonatal HBeAg status, whereas multivariate analysis showed that only maternal HBeAg remained an independent associated factor.
CONCLUSION: Maternal serum pgRNA is associated with neonatal HBeAg status at birth. However, under standardized combined immunoprophylaxis, maternal pgRNA was not associated with MTCT failure.

articles.title: HHV-7 positivity in hospitalized children with acute respiratory tract infections: co-detection patterns and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To analyze the epidemiology, co-detection patterns, and clinical features associated with Human Herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7) positivity in children with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 9,521 pediatric inpatients with ARTIs using targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) to detect HHV-7 and co-detected microbes. False discovery rate (FDR) correction (Benjamini-Hochberg procedure), age-matched sensitivity analysis, and multivariable logistic regression were applied to control for multiple testing and confounding.
RESULTS: The overall HHV-7 detection rate was 3.3% (315/9,521; median age: 5 years) with an extremely high co-detection rate (99.0%), predominantly Streptococcus pneumoniae (32.1%), rhinovirus (30.8%), EBV (30.5%), and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (30.2%). Bronchial wall thickening (81.1%) and ground-glass opacities (74.8%) were main CT findings. Notably, a subset of patients exhibited substantial clinical severity, with 16.8% (53/315) requiring respiratory support and 4.8% (15/315) admitted to the ICU. Regarding discharge outcomes, in-hospital mortality was zero, with 96.8% (305/315) achieving clinical recovery, while 3.2% (10/315) underwent voluntary discharge prior to full recovery. Although HHV-7-positive children (without CMV co-detection) initially presented with lower unadjusted respiratory support rates than CMV-positive children without HHV-7 co-detection (16.5% vs. 38.7%; FDR-adjusted q < 0.001), this difference lost significance in age-matched sensitivity analysis (q > 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that HHV-7 positivity was not independently associated with respiratory support (aOR = 0.57, P = 0.081). Younger age (aOR = 0.98, P < 0.001), elevated procalcitonin (aOR = 1.26, P = 0.047), and non-respiratory specimens (aOR = 5.19, P = 0.026) were identified as independent risk factors, whereas autumn admission was protective (aOR = 0.60, P = 0.045).
CONCLUSIONS: HHV-7 exhibits a low detection rate (3.3%) in pediatric ARTIs. The high co-detection rate (99.0%) suggests that HHV-7 positivity commonly occurs within polymicrobial respiratory infection contexts; its independent clinical contribution remains uncertain. Baseline clinical severity disparities between HHV-7 and CMV cohorts are primarily driven by host age rather than intrinsic viral pathogenicity.

articles.title: Risk of exposure to heavy metals and hepatic renal profile in children from a rural Peruvian community.
articles.abstract: Children living in rural communities may be particularly vulnerable to chronic exposure to heavy metals through drinking water. This study evaluated the non-carcinogenic health risk associated with arsenic, lead, and mercury exposure and assessed renal and hepatic function biomarkers in children from a rural Peruvian community. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among 50 children younger than 5 years from Rica Playa, northern Peru. Arsenic, lead, and mercury concentrations were measured in treated drinking water and untreated river water. Chronic daily intake and target hazard quotient (THQ) were estimated using deterministic methods and Monte Carlo simulation. Renal function was assessed by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and hepatic function by serum transaminases. Arsenic concentrations exceeded regulatory limits in untreated water and generated THQ values above 1 in both treated and untreated water, with 100% of deterministic and probabilistic estimates exceeding the non-carcinogenic risk threshold. Lead exceeded the risk threshold only in a proportion of children consuming untreated water, particularly among those younger than 1 year. Reduced eGFR was identified in 72.7% (24/33) of evaluated children and elevated transaminases in 9.1%, although neither outcome was significantly associated with drinking water source. Arsenic was identified as the principal contributor to the estimated non-carcinogenic risk under the evaluated drinking water exposure scenarios. These findings support strengthening drinking water quality surveillance and implementing longitudinal biomonitoring in vulnerable pediatric populations.

articles.title: An engineered Zika virus recombinant adenovirus vaccine induces protective immune response in mice.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Zika virus (ZIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and dengue virus (DENV) co-circulate in many countries/territories. Our previous publication reported that the antibodies (Abs) induced by ZIKV infection could exacerbate the mortality of JEV-infected mice, bringing challenges to the development of traditional Zika vaccines. Here, we developed two recombinant adenoviruses (Ad5-ZIKV-EWT and Ad5-ZIKV-Emut) encoding the ZIKV wild-type E protein and an E protein mutant carrying five amino acid substitutions (replaced by alanine) in the bc loop and fusion loop regions of the E protein, respectively. The levels of JEV-cross-reactive or DENV-cross-reactive Ab responses induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut immunization in mice are lower than those induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The level of ZIKV-neutralizing Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut is comparable to that elicited by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The ability of Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut to enhance JEV or DENV infections in vitro is attenuated as compared with that induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The in vivo protective role of Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut is similar to that induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. Mice receiving Ad5-ZIKV-EWT-immune mouse sera exhibited antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) post-DENV challenge, whereas passively transferred Ad5-ZIKV-Emut-immune mouse sera did not lead to obvious ADE of DENV infection in recipient mice. Notably, maternally acquired Abs did not enhance the mortality of 2-day-old neonates born to Ad5-ZIKV-Emut-immunized mice post-JEV challenge. These results suggest that optimizing the E protein amino acid sequence of ZIKV could significantly reduce the level of cross-reactive Abs to JEV and DENV, and abrogate the ADE of JEV and DENV infections, providing a promising strategy to develop an effective and safe ZIKV vaccine.
IMPORTANCE: Zika virus (ZIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and dengue virus (DENV) co-circulate in some countries or territories. The results of preliminary animal experiments and clinical cohort studies support that antibodies induced by ZIKV infection can enhance JEV or DENV infection in vitro and in vivo. Therefore, the ZIKV vaccine encoding the wild-type E protein constructed by conventional methods has the antibody-dependent enhancement risk against JEV and DENV infections. In this study, we obtained an E protein mutant by mutating key amino acids in the bc loop and FL sequences of the ZIKV wild-type E protein to alanine. The recombinant adenovirus vaccine based on this E protein mutant is not only effective but also safer in preventing ZIKV infection in the future.

articles.title: Elucidating mechanisms associated with endoplasmic reticulum stress at the placental and fetal brain axis in response to oxycodone exposure.
articles.abstract: Prenatal oxycodone (Oxy) exposure has been associated with several neurodevelopmental outcomes in newborns. However, the molecular mechanisms involved in Oxy-induced placental and fetal brain damage during gestation remain unknown. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress is a cellular stress response triggered by the accumulation of unfolded proteins, which activates the unfolded protein response. Here, we hypothesized that Oxy exposure induces ER stress in the fetal brain-placental axis. To test this hypothesis, we used three model systems: in vitro primary neurons, primary mixed neuroglial cells, and an in vivo model of maternal Oxy exposure. Quantitative Reverse Transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) was employed to detect mRNA expression of ER stress mediators, such as Binding Immunoglobulin Protein (Bip), activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), spliced X-box binding protein 1 (sXBP1), and C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP). Immunoblot analysis was also used to detect protein expression of ER stress mediators, such as Bip; phosphorylated and total forms of inositol-requiring transmembrane kinase/endoribonuclease 1α (p-IRE1α and t-IRE1α) and protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase α (p-PERKα and t-PERKα); phosphorylated eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2α (p-eIF2α); and sXBP1. Further, we detected pro-apoptotic markers such as Bcl-2 interacting mediator of cell death (Bim), p53 upregulated modulator of apoptosis (PUMA), and cleaved poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP). Exposure of Oxy to rat primary fetal neuronal cells increased mRNA expression of Bip and ATF4. sXBP1 and CHOP mRNA levels were upregulated in both rat primary fetal neuronal cells and mixed neuroglial cells. Prenatal Oxy exposure resulted in increased mRNA expression of all ER stress markers tested in both the placenta and fetal brain. We also observed that Oxy exposure increased protein levels of ER stress markers (Bip, p-IRE1α, t-IRE1α, p-PERKα, t-PERKα, p-eIF2α, and sXBP1), as well as pro-apoptotic and apoptotic markers (Bim, PUMA, and cleaved PARP). In conclusion, Oxy exposure increases ER stress mediators in both the placental and fetal brain compartments, which could further lead to apoptosis.

articles.title: The importance of RSV vaccination for at-risk adults aged 18-59: An expert opinion with an Italian perspective.
articles.abstract: This expert opinion reviews the burden of RSV in at-risk adults aged 18-59 years and summarizes available evidence to provide expert considerations that may inform prevention strategies. Adults with comorbidities or immunocompromise frequently experience severe RSV infection, with annual and seasonal rates of 37.6 per 1000 persons/year and 28.4 per 1000 persons/season, respectively. Clinical presentation ranges from being asymptomatic through to acute respiratory distress, with 6.5-32.8% at-risk adults requiring hospitalization for RSV disease. Three preventative vaccines (RSVpreF, mRNA-1345, RSVPreF3) are currently approved in Europe for adults ≥18 years and in the United States for adults ≥60 years and 18-59 years at increased risk. The panel supports RSV vaccination in adults 18-59 years with severe forms of immunocompromise, respiratory disease, cardiovascular disease, neurological/neuromuscular disease, or renal disease. Higher vaccination rates in this population can be achieved by enhancing awareness, empowering health-care professionals, developing consistent policies, and improving access.

articles.title: Adverse Effects of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors in Pediatric Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Proportions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have become a foundational therapy for adult heart failure across the entire spectrum of ejection fraction, but their safety profile in children with heart failure has not been quantitatively synthesized. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions to summarize the incidence of adverse events associated with SGLT2 inhibitors in pediatric heart failure.
STUDY DESIGN: In this systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions (PROSPERO CRD420261355711; PRISMA 2020), five databases were searched through June 2026 for studies of any design reporting adverse events among pediatric patients receiving an SGLT2 inhibitor for heart failure. Random-effects incidence estimates were pooled using logit-transformed proportions with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals; risk of bias and GRADE certainty were assessed.
RESULTS: Ten studies (573 unique children; 2023-2026) were included; eight studies (572 patients; maximum pooled denominator 474) were meta-analyzed, and one case report was summarized narratively. Dapagliflozin accounted for 94.1% of exposures. Study-level dapagliflozin doses ranged from 0.11 to 0.23 mg/kg/day, while the single cohort reporting empagliflozin used a median dose of 0.13 mg/kg/day. No regimen was derived from pediatric heart-failure pharmacokinetic data, and in the only cohort reporting a comparison, infants received a higher weight-normalized dose than older children (0.18 versus 0.16 mg/kg/day). Pooled incidences were: any adverse event 21.2% (95% CI 10.7-37.8%), acute kidney injury 10.7% (3.5-28.1%), urinary tract infection 7.8% (4.8-12.4%), treatment discontinuation 7.0% (4.5-10.6%), all-cause mortality 5.6% (2.4-12.5%), hypoglycemia 2.9% (0.9-9.3%), genital mycotic infection 2.7% (0.9-8.2%), and diabetic ketoacidosis 1.3% (0.4-3.9%). No deaths were attributed to therapy, and no cases of euglycemic ketoacidosis or Fournier gangrene occurred. Directional efficacy signals were consistently favorable, with left ventricular ejection fraction improving in five of six cohorts and natriuretic peptide levels declining across all seven in which they were assessed.
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitors had a tolerable safety profile in pediatric heart failure, mirroring the adult experience. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized adverse-event grading are needed.
REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier no. CRD420261355711.

articles.title: Efficacy of a nurse-facilitated mindfulness-based management program on severity of childhood cancer symptom cluster-leukemia in adolescents with leukemia receiving chemotherapy: A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the efficacy of a mindfulness-based symptom cluster management program on CCSC-L severity and HRQoL.
METHODS: A two-arm multicenter randomized controlled trial with repeated outcome measurements was conducted among 60 adolescents receiving induction chemotherapy at three tertiary hospitals in Thailand. Participants were stratified by hospital and randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either the program based on the Individual and Family Self-Management Theory plus usual care or usual care alone. The symptom cluster severity was assessed immediately after completion of the four-week structured intervention and at Weeks 4 and 8, and HRQoL at Week 12. Linear mixed-effects models and between-group comparisons were performed.
RESULTS: Linear mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant group × time interaction for overall symptom cluster severity (p < .001). Compared with usual care, adolescents receiving the intervention demonstrated significantly lower overall symptom cluster severity at Week 4 (model-estimated mean difference = -0.90) and Week 8 (model-estimated mean difference = -1.63). Significant between-group differences favoring the intervention were observed across all five symptoms at both assessments (all unadjusted p ≤ .001). At Week 12, the complete-case analysis (intervention, n = 30; control, n = 28) showed higher overall HRQoL in the intervention group (mean difference = 11.59, 95% CI [8.56,14.62], unadjusted p < .001).
CONCLUSIONS: The program reduced symptom cluster severity and improved HRQoL. These findings suggest that the intervention could be considered for integration into routine pediatric oncology nursing practice in similar clinical settings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR20250608004); prospectively registered on 8 June 2025, before the first participant was enrolled on 20 June 2025.

articles.title: A completely unpredictable life - parents' lived experiences of transitioning between hospital and home in paediatric oncology.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hospital-to-home transitions are critical for continuity and safety in childhood cancer care, but little is known about how parents experience them in the context of everyday family life. This study explored parents' lived experiences of the transition between a paediatric oncology centre and home during their child's cancer treatment.
METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with twelve parents of children receiving active treatment at a single Danish paediatric oncology centre. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using a phenomenological-hermeneutic approach inspired by Paul Ricoeur, comprising naïve understanding, structural analysis, and comprehensive interpretation. Data management was supported by NVivo QSR.
RESULTS: Three themes described parents' experiences of transitions. First, everyday rhythms were disrupted, producing instability and unpredictability in family life. Second, responsibility shifted from professionals to parents, who undertook complex care tasks while questioning their competence. Third, parents experienced emotional vulnerability and strain, balancing exhaustion, uncertainty, and guilt with the need to remain strong. These findings demonstrate that transitions extend beyond logistical movement and encompass temporal, practical, and existential challenges.
CONCLUSION: Hospital-to-home transitions, embedded in the ongoing lives of families during childhood cancer treatment, require parents to sustain care and family life across changing settings and conditions. Transitional care should incorporate structured follow-up, assessment of family readiness, and support that is more responsive to families' needs throughout treatment.

articles.title: Do You See Me How I See Myself-and Does It Matter? Parent-Child Agreement on Symptom Ratings after Mild Traumatic Brain Injury and Its Association with Recovery: An A-CAP Study.
articles.abstract: Current methods for diagnosing and monitoring recovery of pediatric mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) rely heavily on both self-report and parent-proxy symptom inventories. Yet little is known about parent-child agreement and the clinical relevance of (dis)agreement on symptom inventories commonly used in pediatric mTBI. The current study thus aimed to (1) quantify parent-child agreement on an mTBI symptom inventory; (2) investigate which sociodemographic, clinical, psychosocial, and study-related factors are associated with agreement; and (3) finally explore whether early parent-child difference in symptom report is associated with symptom reporting over time. We conducted a secondary analysis of data collected from the Advancing Concussion Assessment in Pediatrics (A-CAP) study, a large-scale prospective longitudinal cohort study. Participants were children between ages 8 and 16.99 years with mTBI (n = 633) or orthopedic injury (OI; n = 334). Parent-child dyads completed symptom ratings using the Health and Behavior Inventory (HBI; cognitive and somatic symptom subscales) weekly or biweekly over the first 6 months post-injury and completed a series of questionnaires assessing sociodemographic, clinical, and psychosocial variables. Parent-child agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman (BA) plots. Two ordinary least squares linear regression models were used to assess factors associated with parent-child directional differences (i.e., parent minus child rating scores) on cognitive and somatic ratings. To investigate whether parent-child directional differences were associated with symptom trajectories, four generalized least squares models were used, with parent-reported cognitive and somatic and child-reported cognitive and somatic symptoms as the outcomes. Parent-child agreement was moderate for both cognitive (ICC = 0.67) and somatic (ICC = 0.65) symptoms. Visual inspection of BA plots showed somewhat better agreement for somatic symptoms. Number of days post-injury, sex, race, and parent-reported pre-injury report of symptoms, but not group (mTBI vs OI), were associated with cognitive and somatic parent-child difference scores. Parent-child differences early after injury were associated with both parent (χ2(3) = 38.11, p < 0.001) and child (χ2(3) = 27.16, p < 0.001) cognitive and parent (χ2(3) = 11.11, p = 0.011) and child (χ2(3) = 42.36, p < 0.001) somatic symptom trajectories. Parent-child agreement on the HBI is consistent with the broader psychopathology and health literature. Factors such as time since injury, sex, race, and pre-injury symptoms may be particularly important for understanding parent-child agreement on the HBI. Early disagreement, especially for cognitive symptoms, was relevant to later recovery trajectories, with dyads "coming together" over time. Findings highlight the importance of multi-informant assessment after mTBI.

articles.title: A computational report on Fibrocystin structure via AlphaFold2: considerations and limitations for ARPKD research.
articles.abstract: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD) is a rare, genetic disease that often occurs during early childhood and can be lethal at its most severe presentation. ARPKD is caused by biallelic variants in PKHD1 which encodes Fibrocystin, a large receptor protein. The disease presentation and progression of ARPKD is highly variable, the reason for this is currently unknown. To address this, AlphaFold2 was employed to generate a model of Fibrocystin which was used to establish spatial relationships between compound heterozygous pairs in ARPKD patients. AlphaFold2 was used to generate a model of full-length human Fibrocystin which was assessed for structural similarities to known protein structures. Compound heterozygous variant pairs and disease outcomes were acquired from previously published work and annotated onto the three-dimensional Fibrocystin model to identify spatial relationships. AlphaFold2 predicted the full-length of Fibrocystin with varying confidence. Globally, average modelling confidence was low, with more confident modelling around the G8 and PBH1 domains. Confidence was lowest around the transmembrane region and intracellular tail, which modelled poorly. FoldSeek identified structural similarities to other proteins; however, these had similar structures to those already predicted present in Fibrocystin. No new structural elements were detected. Spatial relationships between compound heterozygous variants did not correlate with disease outcomes. There are limitations to AlphaFold2 which limits its ability to accurately model a protein like Fibrocystin. These limitations may hinder the tools application in determining genotype-phenotype relationships in ARPKD. Currently, Fibrocystin models produced by AlphaFold2 are unable to identify genotype-phenotype relationships.

articles.title: Neonatal oxytocin administration restores impaired ultrasonic vocalizations in a mouse model of 3q29 deletion syndrome.
articles.abstract: The 3q29 microdeletion is a highly penetrant genetic risk factor for neuropsychiatric disorders, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia. Although adult mouse models (Df/+) with this deletion exhibit robust social deficits, their early developmental trajectories are unknown. Here, we investigated neonatal communicative behaviors and the underlying oxytocin (OXT) system in Df/+ pups. On postnatal day 7, Df/+ pups emitted significantly fewer isolation-induced ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) than did their wild-type littermates. This behavioral deficit was accompanied by a significant reduction in the number of oxytocinergic neurons within the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus, as identified by Neurophysin 1 and OXT immunoreactivities. Notably, acute exogenous OXT restored the impaired USVs to normal levels, whereas arginine vasopressin did not. Furthermore, the baseline OXT receptor expression remained unaltered. These findings suggest that a deficiency in endogenous OXT, rather than receptor dysfunction, may drive impaired USVs in this model. As the early OXT system is essential for the maturation of social circuits, our results suggest that the neonatal period is a critical developmental window. Deficient OXT signaling during this specific stage may fundamentally alter the developmental trajectory of patients with ASD.

articles.title: Neuroimmune-endocrine interactions in perinatal asphyxia: from brain injury to neuroprotection.
articles.abstract: Perinatal asphyxia (PA) remains a major cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental disability worldwide. Although hypoxic-ischemic brain injury has traditionally been attributed to oxygen deprivation, excitotoxicity, and oxidative stress, accumulating evidence indicates that neurological outcomes are determined by complex interactions among metabolic, mitochondrial, neuroimmune, and neuroendocrine mechanisms. Following hypoxic-ischemic injury, primary energy failure rapidly triggers excitotoxicity, mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium dysregulation, and oxidative damage, leading to activation of microglia and astrocytes, release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, disruption of blood-brain barrier integrity, and recruitment of peripheral immune cells. These events contribute to the development of secondary energy failure and persistent neuroinflammation. Simultaneously, activation of hypoxia-responsive pathways, including hypoxia-inducible factor-1 (HIF-1), heat shock protein 70 (HSP70), glutathione-dependent antioxidant defenses, and neuroendocrine stress responses involving the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, promote endogenous adaptation and neuroprotection. Nitric oxide signaling further links mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrosative stress, inflammatory activation, and neuronal injury. Together, these mechanisms form an integrated neuroimmune-endocrine network that influences both injury progression and tissue repair. In this review, we propose Brain Energy Failure as a unifying conceptual framework linking mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrosative stress, neuroinflammation, endocrine adaptation, and endogenous neuroprotective responses following perinatal hypoxia. We further discuss the role of biomarkers associated with neuro-immuno-endocrine dysfunction, including inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress markers, endocrine factors, and indicators of neuronal and glial injury. Recent evidence has highlighted the therapeutic potential of multimodal neuroprotective approaches, including endogenous lipid mediators such as palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), which exert anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and mitoprotective effects. We also review current and emerging neuroprotective strategies targeting mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and bioenergetic instability, and discuss their translational implications. Understanding the interactions among these interconnected pathways may facilitate biomarker-guided diagnosis, personalized neuroprotection, and the development of more effective therapies aimed at improving long-term neurological outcomes following perinatal asphyxia.

articles.title: Fertility Treatment with Ovulation Induction or Intrauterine Insemination and the Risk of Cerebral Palsy in Offspring.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination and cerebral palsy in offspring, and to examine the potential mechanisms underlying an association, including specific treatment regimens, mediation by preterm birth, confounding by indication, and the association with specific subtypes of cerebral palsy.
METHODS: This nationwide cohort study included all liveborn, singleton children in Denmark conceived from July 1995 and born before January 2017. The children were followed until March 2022. Children conceived after ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination were identified from redeemed prescriptions for the specific hormones used for these treatments, recorded in the Danish National Prescription Registry. Children with cerebral palsy were identified from the Danish Cerebral Palsy Registry and the Danish Cerebral Palsy Follow-up Program.
RESULTS: The study included 1,231,058 singleton children; 47,017 children were conceived after ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination, and 2,104 children were diagnosed with cerebral palsy. Children conceived after ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination had an increased risk of cerebral palsy compared to spontaneously conceived children (adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 1.36; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.11-1.66). The point estimate remained similar in a sibling analysis. The risk was primarily related to the use of clomiphene citrate (aOR: 1.44; 95% CI: 1.16-1.80). A mediation analysis showed that most of the increased risk was statistically mediated by prematurity and antecedent factors (proportion eliminated: 87%; 95% CI: 36-137%). In line with this, the risk was highest for spastic bilateral cerebral palsy (aOR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.33-2.34), severe motor impairment (aOR: 1.66; 95% CI: 1.17-2.35), and for cerebral white matter lesions (aOR: 1.70; 95% CI: 1.24-2.33).
CONCLUSION: Ovulation induction or intrauterine insemination was associated with an increased risk of cerebral palsy in offspring. The risk was related to treatment with clomiphene citrate, and most of the increased risk was statistically mediated by prematurity and antecedent factors.

articles.title: Neuro-adaptive predictive control for upper-limb rehabilitation using EMG and intention-aware assistance.
articles.abstract: Upper-limb motor impairments associated with neurological disorders such as cerebral palsy (CP) are characterized by abnormal muscle coordination, spasticity, fatigue, and highly variable electromyographic (EMG) patterns, posing significant challenges for rehabilitation exoskeleton control. While EMG-driven and adaptive controllers have shown promise, existing approaches often rely on fixed gains or address physiological state estimation, prediction, and decision-making in isolation, limiting robustness and clinical relevance-particularly in pediatric populations. This paper proposes a unified neuro-adaptive predictive control framework for upper-limb rehabilitation exoskeletons that integrates physiologically interpretable state estimation, task-aware assistance, predictive intelligence, and intention-aware supervisory control within a closed-loop architecture. The framework combines a Neuro-Motor Index (NMI) that fuses muscle co-contraction and joint tracking error, fuzzy EMG-based load estimation for task context awareness, hybrid support vector regression-long short-term memory (SVR-LSTM) trajectory prediction, and robust kernel-based motor intention decoding. NMI and task context are used to adapt admittance parameters at each simulation step, enabling assistance modulation that reflects the user's evolving neuromechanical condition. The learning-based modules were trained and evaluated using EMG recordings from pediatric populations, whereas closed-loop controller evaluation was performed exclusively in OpenSim using simulation-derived muscle excitation and activation variables, joint kinematics, and joint-level assistive torques. Clinically inspired perturbations, including fatigue-like degradation, spasticity-inspired activation bursts, EMG-like noise, and variable external loads, were introduced to assess controller robustness. Compared with no assistance and fixed-admittance control, the proposed controller reduced simulated muscular effort by 45-60% and co-contraction by up to 50%, while improving trajectory-tracking accuracy, movement smoothness, and robustness across the evaluated disturbance conditions. These results support the numerical feasibility of the integrated controller under the evaluated CP-inspired simulation conditions. They do not establish physiological benefit or clinical effectiveness in children with CP. Experimental validation and complete documentation of the clinical-data provenance and evaluation procedures are required before translation to rehabilitation exoskeletons.

articles.title: Primary Care Continuity During the Transition to Adulthood and Its Association With Acute Healthcare Utilization Among Youth With Eating Disorders.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The transition from pediatric to adult care is a high-risk period for youth with eating disorders (EDs), often characterized by care disruptions and disengagement from adult services. This study examined whether patterns of primary care continuity during this transition are associated with acute healthcare utilization post-transition.
METHOD: A retrospective cohort study of 1106 youth discharged from a tertiary pediatric ED program in Ontario, Canada. Primary care continuity was categorized into five groups based on dominant general practitioner (GP) patterns before and after age 18. Outcomes included emergency department visits (EDVs) and hospitalizations within 2 years post-transition. Multivariate logistic regression models estimated associations, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors, and corresponding pre-transition acute healthcare utilization.
RESULTS: Compared with maintaining the same dominant GP before and after age 18 (Group 1), no dominant GP in either period (Group 5) was associated with lower odds of any EDV (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.32-0.73), any hospitalization (OR: 0.37, 95% CI: 0.16-0.76), and MH-related hospitalization (OR: 0.30, 95% CI: 0.08-0.81). A dominant GP before but not after 18 (Group 4) was associated with lower odds of MH-related EDVs (OR: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.29-0.95). Sensitivity analyses generally supported these findings.
DISCUSSION: Primary care continuity was not associated with acute healthcare utilization among youth with EDs, highlighting a complex relationship between GP continuity, healthcare needs, and healthcare use. Lower utilization among those without a dominant GP may not indicate lower need or better outcomes. Future research should clarify these patterns, while transition planning should continue to support timely and sustained primary care involvement for youth with EDs.

articles.title: Macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection: Epidemiology, potential pathogenic mechanisms and novel therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) stands as one of the primary pathogens responsible for community-acquired pneumonia in children worldwide. Its macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MRMP) strains have become a serious clinical challenge. Resistance rates are unevenly distributed globally, reaching 70-100% among children in China, which substantially increases treatment difficulty and disease burden. MRMP is associated with prolonged fever and cough, higher treatment failure rates, and an elevated risk of both pulmonary and extrapulmonary complications. Resistance primarily results from point mutations in domain V of the 23S rRNA gene. Multiple studies have documented associations between MRMP infection, increased bacterial burden, virulence-associated factors, and dysregulated hyperinflammatory host responses. However, whether macrolide resistance mutations directly enhance virulence remains unresolved, as the observed associations could alternatively be confounded by delayed effective therapy, bacterial genetic background, and host factors. Currently, clinical treatment faces a dilemma: the efficacy of first-line macrolide antibiotics is declining, while alternative drugs such as tetracyclines and fluoroquinolones are restricted in children. To address this challenge, current research directions mainly include: developing new inhibitors targeting adhesion proteins and virulence factors; researching new antibiotics targeting resistance mechanisms; exploring immunomodulatory adjuvant therapies; and applying rapid molecular diagnostics to precise medication. Future priorities include strengthened global surveillance, optimized antibiotic stewardship, accelerated development of pediatric-appropriate drugs, and broader implementation of rapid diagnostic tests. Future research should focus on integrating pathogen characteristics with host response profiles to guide individualized therapy and improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Natural environments and sleep during pregnancy: Associations of green and blue spaces with prenatal sleep outcomes in a Canadian cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Sleep quality during pregnancy is critical for maternal and child health, yet environmental determinants of prenatal sleep remain understudied. Green and blue spaces have demonstrated positive effects on mental health, which is robustly associated with sleep, but direct impacts of green and blue spaces on sleep among pregnant individuals are unclear. This study examined associations between green and blue spaces and sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment during pregnancy.
METHODS: Data from the pan-Canadian Pregnancy during the Covid-19 Pandemic (PdP, n = 8583) were linked with green (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), tree canopy) and blue space (distance from the nearest water body) data from Canadian Urban Environmental Health Research Consortium (CANUE). Sleep outcomes included self-reported sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment. Multiple linear regression models adjusted for age, ethnicity, neighborhood deprivation, socioeconomic status, population density, COVID-19 restriction severity, season, physical activity, and trimester.
RESULTS: Greater tree canopy cover and NDVI were significantly associated with longer sleep duration. Contrary to our hypothesis, greater distance from water bodies was also associated with longer sleep duration and lower sleep disturbance. After additional adjustments, only the associations with sleep duration remained significant. No associations were observed for sleep-related impairment.
CONCLUSIONS: Green spaces, particularly tree canopy, may positively influence prenatal sleep duration, whereas the effects of blue spaces may depend more on the type of interaction with these environments and additional contextual factors. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating environmental factors, particularly tree-rich environment, into maternal health strategies and urban planning to support perinatal well-being.

articles.title: A Digital Intervention Reduces Childhood Obesity Risk Behaviors: Analysis of Secondary Outcomes of the Greenlight Plus RCT.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined key behavioral outcomes from the Greenlight Plus RCT.
METHODS: Greenlight Plus was a comparative effectiveness trial from birth to 2 years of life that enrolled 900 dyads from October 2019 through January 2022 across six US medical centers. The clinic-only group received counseling at visits, and the clinic + digital group received tailored, responsive text messages. We assessed 14 parent-reported behaviors selected a priori. We tested overall effects, then estimated individual outcome intervention effects with logistic regression and proportional odds logistic regression models.
RESULTS: We analyzed 857 dyads (424 in the clinic + digital group and 433 in the clinic-only group) and found a significant effect on behaviors overall (Χ2 = 40.54, df = 14, p = 0.0002), including greater breastfeeding at 6 months (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.46, 95% CI: 1.02, 2.10), lower sugar-sweetened beverage consumption at 9 (aOR 0.60, 95% CI: 0.40, 0.90) and 12 months (aOR 0.58, 95% CI: 0.40, 0.86), lower screen time at 9 (aOR 0.59, 95% CI: 0.45, 0.79) and 15 months (aOR 0.61, 95% CI: 0.45, 0.82), and more "tummy time" at 4 months (aOR 1.46, 95% CI: 1.12, 1.92).
CONCLUSIONS: The Greenlight Plus intervention led to significant improvements in breastfeeding, sugar-sweetened beverage consumption, screen time, and tummy time.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04042467.

articles.title: Stable In-Hospital Mortality Despite Increasing Thrombectomy Use in Young Adults With Ischemic Stroke: A Nationwide Study in Spain (2016-2022).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) in young adults is increasing in incidence and carries a disproportionate socioeconomic burden. The adoption of reperfusion therapies, particularly mechanical thrombectomy, has transformed stroke care; however, their impact on mortality in this low-risk population remains uncertain.
METHODS: We performed a nationwide, population-based retrospective study using the Spanish Minimum Basic Data Set (MBDS), including all hospital admissions for IS in patients aged 18-50 years from 2016 to 2022. Temporal trends in admissions, reperfusion therapies, and in-hospital mortality were assessed. Independent predictors of mortality were identified using multivariable logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 20,533 admissions, the number of hospitalizations increased over time, accompanied by a rise in reperfusion therapies. Mechanical thrombectomy rates nearly doubled from 6.3% in 2016 to 12.1% in 2022 (p < 0.001). Despite this expansion, in-hospital mortality remained low and stable throughout the study period (2.8%). Mortality was independently associated with malignant neoplasm (OR 8.45), followed by orotracheal intubation (OR 4.85), coma (OR 3.73), cerebral edema (OR 2.16), acute kidney injury (OR 1.85), acute respiratory failure (OR 1.38), posterior circulation stroke (OR 1.42), and All Patient Refined Diagnosis Related Groups (APR-DRG) mortality risk level (all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In young adults with IS, the expansion of reperfusion therapies was not associated with reduced in-hospital mortality, which remained low over time. Malignant neoplasm was the strongest independent predictor of death, followed by acute neurological complications and organ dysfunction. These findings highlight the need for further multicentre clinical research to better understand the causes of death in young adults with IS.

articles.title: Comparison of the efficacy and safety of intra-aortic balloon occlusion and uterine artery embolization in types IIb-III cesarean scar pregnancy: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Managing cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is clinically challenging because of the substantial risk of hemorrhage, which necessitates appropriate preoperative strategies. Uterine artery embolization (UAE) is widely used to reduce perioperative bleeding, whereas intra-aortic balloon occlusion (IABO) offers temporary vascular control without permanent embolization. This retrospective cohort study compared perioperative, economic, menstrual, and subsequent reproductive outcomes between IABO and UAE in patients with types IIb-III CSP.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 73 patients with types IIb-III CSP admitted to Jiangxi Provincial Maternal and Child Health Hospital between June 2020 and June 2025. Patients were managed with IABO-assisted surgery (n = 40) or UAE-assisted surgery (n = 33) according to the pretreatment strategy used in routine clinical practice. Baseline characteristics, perioperative outcomes, hospitalization indicators, menstrual recovery, and subsequent reproductive outcomes were compared between groups. Because treatment allocation was nonrandomized, between-group findings were interpreted as observational associations.
RESULTS: The groups differed in baseline fetal cardiac activity and ultrasonographic hypervascularity. Intraoperative blood loss, operative time, treatment conversion, treatment success, and readmission did not differ significantly between groups. Massive hemorrhage, defined as intraoperative blood loss ≥500 mL, occurred in 3 of 40 patients (7.5%) in the IABO group and 3 of 33 patients (9.1%) in the UAE group. The IABO group had a shorter hospital stay and lower hospitalization costs. Postoperative hypomenorrhea within 1 year was less frequent in the IABO group than in the UAE group. Subsequent pregnancy outcomes were described descriptively because of the small number of patients with follow-up pregnancies.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, IABO and UAE showed broadly comparable perioperative hemostatic outcomes, while IABO was associated with shorter hospitalization, lower costs, and a lower frequency of postoperative hypomenorrhea. However, treatment allocation was nonrandomized and baseline differences indicated potential confounding by indication. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory associations rather than evidence of comparative superiority.

articles.title: Development of a machine learning-based treatment-response prediction model for levetiracetam in pediatric epilepsy: integrating ABCB1 polymorphism and therapeutic drug monitoring.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Empirical dosing of levetiracetam (LEV) in pediatric epilepsy often yields variable outcomes. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-based treatment-response prediction model integrating therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and ABCB1 C3435 T polymorphism.
METHODS: Clinical, TDM, and genetic data from 346 pediatric patients were retrospectively analyzed. Four machine learning algorithms were evaluated. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was utilized to interpret feature associations.
RESULTS: The XGBoost model demonstrated the highest predictive performance (AUC=0.893). SHAP analysis indicated that LEV trough concentration (Cmin) and ABCB1 genotype were the strongest associative factors for clinical outcomes. The homozygous TT mutation was associated with treatment resistance despite adequate peripheral Cmin. SHAP interaction patterns generated an exploratory hypothesis that ABCB1 genotype may modify the associative relationship between systemic exposure and treatment response.
CONCLUSION: Integrating ABCB1 genotyping and TDM via the XGBoost model may provides an interpretable approach for predicting LEV treatment response in pediatric epilepsy. Rather than directly generating individualized dosing regimens, these associative findings offer a hypothesis-generating reference for identifying patients at risk of therapeutic failure, warranting further prospective exposure-response validation.

articles.title: Increased rate of C-section in women with rheumatic diseases-indications under the magnifying glass: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and inflammatory joint diseases (IJD) show higher obstetric risk and cesarean delivery (CD) rates than healthy women. CD is associated with increased maternal and neonatal morbidity and healthcare costs; however, data on indications for CD in women with rheumatic diseases are limited. This study aimed to investigate the reasons for increased CD rates in women with SLE and IJD using the Robson classification and a detailed analysis of CD indications.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, CD rates and indications in women with SLE and IJD were compared with healthy controls (HC) as part of the RhePro Study, which prospectively collected data from patients with rheumatic diseases before, during, and after pregnancy to investigate reproductive health in this specific cohort. The study population was classified according to the Robson system, the mode of delivery was assessed, and CD indications were categorized as absolute obstetric, relative composite, or rheumatic disease-related.
RESULTS: A total of 185 women were included (119 HC, 40 SLE, 26 IJD). Women with IJD had significantly fewer vaginal deliveries (23.1% vs. 54.6% in HC, p = 0.009) and higher CD rates (65.4% vs. 37.8% in HC, p = 0.038) compared with healthy controls. CD and vaginal delivery rates did not differ significantly between IJD and SLE. SLE patients had the highest proportion of absolute obstetric CD indications (78.95%), compared with HC (55.56%) and IJD (23.53%). In contrast, 64.7% of CDs in IJD patients were performed for composite indications. The most common indication for CD was one previous CD (25.93%).
CONCLUSION: High CD rates in IJD patients, despite few absolute obstetric indications, suggest potentially modifiable clinical decision-making. In IJD, CDs were largely driven by composite indications. Neither SLE nor IJD alone necessitate cesarean delivery, and cesarean deliveries should be reduced in rheumatic patients without absolute indications, in line with WHO recommendations.

articles.title: The burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance in the South Asia and high-income Asia-Pacific region over three decades: a systematic analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an escalating global public health crisis, yet regional disparities remain poorly characterized. This study systematically assessed AMR burden in South Asia and High-income Asia-Pacific (1990-2021) to inform targeted control strategies.
METHODS: We analyzed data from the Global Burden of Antimicrobial Resistance Study 2021, which serves as the most advanced and current database for assessing the burden of AMR. The study covered 22 pathogens, 84 pathogen-drug combinations, and 11 infectious syndromes in countries and territories across South Asia and High-income Asia-Pacific regions. We quantified the deaths burden under two counterfactual scenarios: deaths associated with AMR and deaths attributable to AMR. In addition, based on these data, we calculated the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) to evaluate the temporal trends in AMR death rate.
RESULTS: In 2021, South Asia recorded approximately 1.26 million (95% UI: 1.11 to 1.42 million) AMR-associated deaths and 334,671 (95% UI: 282,451 to 386,890) AMR-attributable deaths, while the High-income Asia-Pacific region reported 108,668 (95% UI: 92,005 to 125,331) and 23,717 (95% UI: 20,074 to 27,360). AMR-associated death rate declined in South Asia(EAPC: -1.88) but increased in High-income Asia-Pacific (EAPC: 0.74). Over three decades, marked variations emerged across regions and age groups. AMR-associated deaths among children under 5 years declined substantially-by 70% in South Asia and 90% in High-income Asia-Pacific. In contrast, adults 70 + years increased by 155% and 70%, respectively. In 2021, India (69.8 per 100,000) and Japan (65.66 per 100,000) exhibited the highest regional AMR-associated death rates. Aminopenicillin-resistant Escherichia coli predominated in South Asia, whereas methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) was most prevalent in AMR-associated deaths in the High-income Asia-Pacific.
CONCLUSION: This evaluation reveals divergent AMR burden trends between regions, highlighting the critical need for tailored interventions, particularly targeting the growing vulnerable aging population.

articles.title: Independent associations of gluteofemoral fat depots with hepatocellular carcinoma and the mediating role of the plasma lipidome: a mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: As metabolic etiologies become increasingly important in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the causal roles of specific adipose depots independent of overall body size remain unclear. This study used Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate the associations of MRI-derived fat-depot phenotypes with HCC and to explore potential mediation by plasma lipids. GWAS summary statistics for BMI- and height-adjusted fat-depot phenotypes were obtained from the UK Biobank, and HCC summary statistics were obtained from FinnGen, with replication in the Million Veteran Program. Univariable and multivariable MR were used to estimate total and independent effects, including analyses adjusted for smoking, alcohol consumption, type 2 diabetes, and childhood BMI. A two-step MR framework was applied to assess mediation by 179 plasma lipid species. Genetically predicted gluteofemoral adipose tissue adjusted for BMI and height (GFATadj) was associated with a lower risk of HCC (OR = 0.444, P = 1.00 × 10-4). This association remained robust after adjustment for other risk factors, and it was replicated in the Million Veteran Program (OR = 0.766). Mediation analysis identified six lipid species as potential partial mediators, each accounting for an estimated 7.0%-15.4% of the protective total effect, and colocalization provided only limited support for shared causal variants. Our results provide insight into depot-specific adiposity and lipid metabolic pathways in hepatocarcinogenesis, although further validation is needed to confirm the underlying causal mechanisms.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics, energy intake patterns, and factors associated with severity of refeeding syndrome in pediatric patients: a single-center retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Refeeding syndrome (RFS) is a critical condition marked by metabolic and electrolyte imbalances during nutritional rehabilitation, particularly in malnourished patients. Data on pediatric RFS remains scarce. This study examined clinical characteristics, energy intake patterns, and factors linked to RFS severity.
METHODS: A retrospective study included patients aged 1 month to 18 years diagnosed with RFS at Srinagarind Hospital, Thailand, between January 2018 and December 2019. Patients were categorized as high-risk or low-risk based on ASPEN consensus criteria. Data on demographics, clinical features, energy intake, and outcomes were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression examined factors linked to severe RFS.
RESULTS: Of 1,677 hospitalized pediatric patients, 135 (8.1%) were diagnosed with RFS, of whom 22.2% were classified as high-risk for RFS. Among patients with RFS, high-risk patients had significantly higher rates of severe malnutrition (BMIZ <-2: 73.3% vs. 15.2%, p < 0.001), prolonged fasting, and ICU admission (30.0% vs. 12.4%, p = 0.046) compared to low-risk patients. Clinical signs of RFS were identified in 16.3% of patients with RFS, with abnormal electrocardiograms (4.4%), heart failure (3.7%), and seizures (2.9%) being the most common. Median energy intake as a percentage of target was slightly higher in high-risk patients (21.0% vs. 14.6%, p = 0.133). High-risk patients more frequently received parenteral or combined nutritional support (24.0% vs. 10.0%, p = 0.019). High-risk RFS status was associated with prolonged fasting and surgical interventions, with a higher prevalence of severe disease (86.7% vs. 62.9%, p = 0.014). Multivariable analysis identified autoimmune diseases, surgical interventions, and hepatobiliary and pancreatic diseases were independently associated with severe RFS.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight the importance of systematic RFS risk stratification in hospitalized children, particularly for those undergoing surgery or with autoimmune diseases. Proactive identification, close electrolyte monitoring, and timely thiamine supplementation are key to preventing severe complications. Future prospective studies and pediatric-specific risk assessment tools are needed to validate and translate these findings into clinical practice.

articles.title: Holding it together: how mothers' work becomes knowledge in childhood spinal cord injury.
articles.journal: Int J Qual Stud Health Well-being
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Parents of children with spinal cord injury navigate support and care across services and everyday life, yet their experiences remain underexplored. This study examined mothers' experiences across these contexts as work and as a source of experiential knowledge.
METHODS: The qualitative study incorporated participatory elements and included five interviews, one workshop, and two follow-up sessions with five mothers. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Four themes were developed: (1) Facing services that do not connect; (2) Carrying what services leave disconnected; (3) Walking a tightrope in uneven relationships; and (4) Making connection and belonging possible in everyday life. Gaps between services became visible as ongoing work carried into family life. Through this work, mothers developed experiential knowledge of what it takes for support and care to function around the child.
CONCLUSIONS: This knowledge comes from a position across services and everyday life that no single service or professional role can occupy. Coordination responsibilities must be clearly assigned within services, and mothers' experiential knowledge should inform how these responsibilities are fulfilled. Involvement in research, practice, and policy should enable mothers to contribute on their own terms, without adding to their workload, and address unequal relationships with services and professionals.

articles.title: Essential Paediatric Life Support Skills: A Set of Rolling Cart-Based Simulations in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Frequent high occupancy combined with increased rates of nursing turnover in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) has led to a limited ability to perform in-room high-fidelity simulations and an increased need for focused life support training for PICU personnel.
METHODS: A multidisciplinary team of physicians, nurses, respiratory therapists, and undergraduate students implemented various simulations in the PICU August through December 2022. Simulations were conducted via a rolling-cart model to capture the largest audience and included, but were not limited to, chest compressions, defibrillation, bag-mask ventilation, push-pull fluid bolus administration, emergency cart utilization, and intraosseous access.
RESULTS: Twelve simulation sessions were performed. Twenty-four participants supplied feedback, with the majority of responses being overwhelmingly positive. In answer to the question 'The content of the simulation was relevant to my current role in the PICU', over 83% of the respondents said that they 'strongly agree'. 100% of respondents would recommend the simulation they performed to colleagues. Additionally, the participation rate was high, with a median of 10 participants per session. For comparison, the PICU in-room simulations had a median of six participants per session.
DISCUSSION: Conducting rolling cart-based simulations involving life support practices is a well-received method of education and garners high participation from PICU health care workers. This model can be beneficial in times when resources are limited.
RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Maintaining life support competency for staff in the PICU can be well supported by brief, low-fidelity rolling cart-based simulations.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients and general public were not involved in the study. Staff from the paediatric intensive care unit were involved by participating in the bedside simulations.

articles.title: The undiagnosed rare disease clinic program of Indiana University School of Medicine: lessons learned from the first 100 cases enrolled (Phase-I pilot).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Undiagnosed Rare Disease Clinic (URDC) of Indiana University, established in January 2020, is a multidisciplinary collaborative clinic that focuses on providing genetic diagnoses for patients and families dealing with the uncertainty of an undiagnosed rare disease and/or diagnostic odyssey.
METHODS: To identify rare disease-causing variants underlying the suspected undiagnosed genetic conditions in our patient cohort, the URDC team implemented the following procedure. After sequencing, each case was evaluated by a small multidisciplinary team using an individualized, multi-modal pipeline, incorporating a customized AI-based variant-prioritization system. Candidate genes and variants identified through this process were further assessed through targeted functional studies, including 3D structural modeling, RNA-seq and additional in vivo and in vitro assays.
RESULTS: The patients enrolled in URDC were referred from both urban (80%) and rural (20%) communities, through various specialty services within Indiana University Health. Multi-site collaborations with research and clinical groups were established to inform the differential and to study the functional effects of gene/variant candidates. Cases were solved in a variety of ways, including exome reanalysis and RNA-seq, novel gene discovery and GeneMatcher collaborations, variant reclassification, periodic genome sequencing reanalysis, and phenotypic expansion. Of the initial 100 cases, 19 received a diagnosis and are considered "solved" and 6 cases are "possibly solved," i.e., the result has a high likelihood of explaining the symptoms; 74 cases remain unsolved, and 1 case was withdrawn. Medical management changes positively impacted care in 7 patients with newly identified diagnoses.
CONCLUSION: The impact of the URDC on the resolution of rare disease diagnostic odysseys for people in Indiana, a state that has faced significant gaps in access to genetic services, is substantial. The URDC successfully resolved approximately 20% of the first 100 cases and presents a model that can be integrated in other institutions across the country. The remaining undiagnosed patients, and those who will be enrolled in the future, present a unique opportunity for further research and novel gene discovery.

articles.title: Invisible impairments? A study of emotional and social functioning in children with inborn errors of metabolism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inborn errors of metabolism (IEM) can affect the cognitive and socio-emotional development of children, even when a stable metabolic state is maintained and treatment is initiated early. Increasing evidence suggests that certain groups of patients with IEM may experience difficulties in emotion recognition, affect regulation, and social functioning, regardless of their intellectual level. The aim of this study was to compare socio-emotional competencies in children with selected inborn errors of metabolism with those observed in healthy children. The study group comprised children with phenylketonuria (PKU), classical galactosaemia (CG), and a heterogeneous group of rare inborn errors of metabolism associated with a high risk of acute metabolic decompensation, including organic acidurias and fatty acid oxidation disorders (hereafter referred to as the non-PKU group).
METHODS: The study involved 127 children aged 5-10 years: 34 children with CG, 34 with PKU, 25 with non-PKU, and 34 healthy children. All children with IEM were in a state of metabolic stability. To measure socio-emotional competencies, four subscales of the Intelligence and Developmental Scales were used: emotion recognition, emotion regulation, social understanding, and social strategies. Intellectual functioning was assessed using the Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scales, Fifth Edition.
RESULTS: Significant differences were found in selected emotional and social competencies between children with IEM and healthy controls, while overall intellectual functioning was generally within the expected range. Children with CG and children with non-PKU disorders showed lower scores in emotion recognition, emotion regulation and social understanding than healthy controls.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings indicate the need for systematic monitoring of socio-emotional development in children with IEM, even when intellectual functioning is not globally impaired. They also highlight the importance of psychological care and interventions tailored to the individual patient and the specific type of IEM.

articles.title: Clinical spectrum of intracellular cobalamin metabolism disorders: a single-center retrospective study from the United Arab Emirates.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cobalamin is essential for DNA synthesis and for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and methionine synthase activity. Inherited disorders of intracellular cobalamin (Cbl) metabolism are single-gene defects affecting absorption, transport, or intracellular processing, with variable phenotypes depending on the severity and location of the defect. Data from high consanguinity populations, such as the UAE, are limited.
AIM: To describe the clinical, biochemical, and molecular characteristics of patients with intracellular Cbl metabolism disorders at Tawam Hospital, UAE.
METHODS: Retrospective review of patients followed between January 2010 and December 2025. Data included demographics, clinical features, laboratory and radiological findings, molecular results, treatment, and outcomes.
RESULTS: Twelve patients were identified: 8 CblC, 1 CblE, 1 CblG, and 2 unclassified. Consanguinity was present in 75%. The earliest diagnosis was at 8 days; 91.6% were symptomatic. Presentations included seizures (58%), apparent life-threatening events (33%), hydrocephalus and cytopenia (25% each), global developmental delay, osteoporosis, hypothyroidism, hypogonadism, multicystic kidney, and psychiatric symptoms. Homocysteine was elevated in all. The MMACHC c.271dupA variant was common; a novel variant in the MTRR gene was identified. All received parenteral hydroxocobalamin, betaine, and carnitine with partial biochemical improvement. The newborn-screened patient had a favorable outcome.
CONCLUSION: This cohort broadens the phenotypic spectrum to endocrine, renal, and psychiatric manifestations. Early diagnosis and hydroxocobalamin treatment improve outcomes, though neurocognitive and ophthalmologic complications persist.

articles.title: Caregiver perspectives on meaningful change in the vineland adaptive behavior scales, second edition (VABS-II), in children with neuronopathic MPS II: an interview-based study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuronopathic mucopolysaccharidosis type II (MPS II; Hunter syndrome) is characterized by progressive multisystemic impacts, including cognitive impairment and behavioral problems. The Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, second edition (VABS-II) is recommended for assessing adaptive behavior in MPS II clinical studies; recently, an increase in VABS-II age-equivalent scores of 3 months (3AEq) has been defined as a threshold for improvement. The aim of the present study was to gain caregiver insights on what constitutes meaningful change on the VABS-II in response to treatment for children with neuronopathic MPS II. Ten semi-structured interviews were conducted with 11 caregivers of 11 children with neuronopathic MPS II aged 3-6 years old in the UK and USA. Caregivers were presented with hypothetical vignettes detailing changes in adaptive behavior and VABS-II scores in response to treatment over 1 year and were asked to select which one(s) represented a minimal meaningful change. The scores for the selected meaningful changes were then compared with those equivalent to an increase of 3AEq to assess the adequacy of this threshold. Caregivers discussed the rationale for their choices.
RESULTS: For all nine VABS-II categories (feeding, drinking, undressing, dressing, brushing teeth and toileting [Personal Subdomain]; sharing skills [Interpersonal Relationships Subdomain]; Play and Leisure Subdomain; and Maladaptive Behavior Domain), the hypothetical vignette most commonly selected by caregivers as representing a minimal meaningful change was associated with the smallest change. The significant impact of small increases in independence and cognitive and physical abilities to perform daily activities were highlighted. For each functional activity within the Personal Subdomain, the majority of caregivers selected vignettes associated with changes in raw scores that were below the total Personal Subdomain raw score equivalent to a change of 3AEq. For sharing skills (Interpersonal Subdomain) and for the Play and Leisure Subdomain, the majority of caregivers chose vignettes associated with raw score changes that were below or equal, respectively, to raw scores associated with a change of 3AEq.
CONCLUSIONS: These insights from caregivers support the use of VABS-II for assessing adaptive behavior in children with neuronopathic MPS II and the use of 3AEq as a threshold for meaningful change.

articles.title: Systemic metabolic remodeling in mucopolysaccharidosis revealed by untargeted urinary metabolomics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mucopolysaccharidoses (MPS) are lysosomal storage disorders characterized by glycosaminoglycan (GAG) accumulation and progressive multi-organ dysfunction. However, the systemic metabolic consequences of lysosomal dysfunction remain incompletely defined.
METHODS: Untargeted urinary metabolomics was performed using LC-MS in 27 patients with MPS and 26 age-matched healthy controls. Multivariate analyses, including principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), were applied to characterize metabolic differences. Differential metabolites were identified using variable importance in projection (VIP) > 1, |log₂ fold change (log₂FC)| ≥ 0.58, and false discovery rate (FDR)-adjusted P < 0.05. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was conducted to evaluate discriminative performance.
RESULTS: A total of 32 differential metabolites were identified, with the majority showing decreased abundance in MPS. These metabolites were primarily involved in microbial-host co-metabolism, lipid and mitochondrial energy metabolism, nucleotide turnover, and amino sugar metabolism. Several metabolites demonstrated good to excellent discriminative performance, with area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.722 to 0.909, including guanine, phenylacetaldehyde, pyrocatechol, and trimethylamine N-oxide. Integrated pathway analysis indicated coordinated metabolic network remodeling associated with lysosomal dysfunction.
CONCLUSIONS: Urinary metabolomics reveals a distinct metabolic signature in MPS characterized by multi-pathway metabolic remodeling beyond primary substrate accumulation. These findings provide insight into the systemic metabolic consequences of lysosomal dysfunction and support the potential of metabolomics for disease characterization in lysosomal storage disorders.

articles.title: Reduced intensity hematopoietic cell transplant using best available donor and post-transplant cyclophosphamide is safe and curative for transfusion-dependent thalassemia.
articles.abstract: Over 300,000 live births annually are affected by hemoglobinopathies worldwide. Of these, transfusion-dependent thalassemias (TDTs) result in severe phenotypes that significantly impact quality of life, shorten life expectancy, and incur high lifetime healthcare costs driven by recurrent transfusions and chelation therapy. Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) is curative but limited by donor availability, regimen toxicity, graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), and transplant-related mortality. We present our single-center experience of TDT patients who underwent allo-HCT using a reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC) regimen (anti-thymocyte globulin, fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, total body irradiation) and posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy)-based GVHD prophylaxis. Twenty-five consecutive children and young adults (ages 2-23 years, median 9) with TDT (beta-thalassemia major n=21, hemoglobin E-beta thalassemia n=3, hemoglobin D-beta thalassemia n=1) underwent HCT from July 2013 to November 2024. Bone marrow was the most common graft source (n=23, 92% of all patients), and haploidentical donors were the most common donor type (n=19, 76% of all patients). Neutrophil and platelet recovery occurred at median 21 days (range 13-38) and 26 days (range 16-88), respectively. Five patients (20%) developed grade I-II acute GVHD; none developed grade III-IV acute GVHD. Two (8%) developed mild chronic GVHD. At a median follow-up of 5.6 years (range 0.7-10), 5-year overall survival was 100%, transfusion-free survival 96%, and thalassemia-free-GVHD-free survival 96% - one patient experienced near-complete loss of donor chimerism with return of the TDT phenotype. Our RIC platform with best-available donor and PTCy-based GVHD prophylaxis significantly reduces post-HCT complications while providing durable transfusion independence, offering a proven, accessible, curative option for TDT.

articles.title: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation after CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in children and adults with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia: a GoCART coalition study on behalf of the PDWP, ALWP, and CTIWP of the EBMT.
articles.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) can rescue B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) recurring after CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR19 T cells). However, in patients at high risk of relapse, the indication for and timing of consolidative HSCT are controversial. We retrieved data on 112 patients who received an HSCT at a median of 6.1 months after CAR19 T-cell infusion. Indication for subsequent HSCT were: (I) Rescue in 72 (64%) patients for disease recurrence; (II) Pre-emptive in 21 (19%) for loss of B-cell aplasia; (III) Consolidative in 19 patients (17%). The 2-year post-transplant Leukemia-Free Survival (LFS) was 54% and the 2-year cumulative incidence of relapse was 32%. Children had better LFS than adults (63% vs 38%). Older age was associated with inferior LFS (HR per 10-year increase 1.30; p= 0.01) and patients receiving a rescue HSCT had a significantly lower 2-year LFS (41%), compared to pre-emptive (74%) and consolidative HSCT (78%), respectively (p=0.002). Haploidentical donor was also associated with inferior LFS (HR: 2.21 95%CI: 1.15-4.25, p=0.02). This "real-world" study corroborates the need to identify patients at higher risk of relapse and optimization of strategies to improve outcome in patients with R/R B-ALL receiving CD19-directed CAR T cells.
