articles.title: Child abuse and mental health outcomes in Canada: A population-based study with a focus on sex at birth and sexual identity: Violence faite aux enfants et résultats en matière de santé mentale au Canada : étude fondée sur la population axée sur le sexe à la naissance et l'identité sexuelle.
articles.abstract: BackgroundContemporary nationally representative Canadian statistics on child abuse and mental health outcomes with a focus on sex at birth and sexual identity are essential in determining approaches to prevention and the need for services. The objectives of the current study were to examine the relationship between experiences of abuse during childhood (physical, sexual, exposure to intimate partner violence, and any) and past-year mental health conditions (depression, generalized anxiety disorder, bipolar disorder, social phobia, and suicidal ideation) among adult Canadians, and whether these relationships are moderated by sex at birth and sexual identity.MethodsData were obtained from the cross-sectional 2022 Statistics Canada Mental Health and Access to Care Survey (2022; n = 9,409; 18+ years).FindingsAny child abuse history and each individual child abuse type were associated with an increased likelihood of all poor mental health indicators in the sample after adjusting for sociodemographic covariates (Adjusted Odds Ratio ranging from 1.66 to 4.67). Generally, an increasing dose-response trend was noted for increasing counts of child abuse types (multitype abuse) experienced and increased odds of poor mental health indicators. Sex at birth and sexual identity moderated models for both child abuse and depression and child abuse and social phobia, with stronger associations for females compared to males and for some sexual identities other than heterosexual.InterpretationThe current study provides updated nationally representative data on child abuse history and mental health indicators among adults in Canada. The development and evaluation of child abuse prevention strategies must remain a priority in reducing violence against children and mental health problems among Canadians. Sex at birth and sexual identity differences highlight the need for policies and practices to address the unique needs of women and individuals identifying as lesbian/gay, bisexual, and other nonheterosexual identities.

articles.title: Non-pharmacological interventions for ADHD in children and adolescents from low- and middle-income countries: A scoping review: Interventions non pharmacologiques chez les enfants et les adolescents atteints de TDAH dans les pays à revenu faible ou intermédiaire: un examen de la portée.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAttention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is common among children and adolescents globally, yet evidence on non-pharmacological interventions remains disproportionately concentrated in high-income settings. This scoping review aimed to identify and synthesize evidence for the benefit of such interventions for this population with ADHD in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).MethodsSystematic searches were conducted for clinical trials evaluating non-pharmacological interventions for youth aged 4-18 years with ADHD in LMICs. Interventions included behavioural and psychosocial therapies, cognitive training, psychoeducation, neurofeedback (NF), and complementary and alternative medicine (CAM). Of 4030 records identified, 16 studies met inclusion criteria. Findings were synthesized descriptively, and risk of bias was assessed using validated risk-of-bias tools.ResultsMost studies reported improvements across ADHD symptoms and selected cognitive, behavioural, or functional outcomes. The effects were moderate-to-large in several domains where standardized effect sizes were available. Studies of behavioural and parent-focused interventions reported relatively consistent improvements, while studies of cognitive training reported benefits across selected attentional, working-memory, and academic outcomes. Evidence for NF was limited, and findings across CAM interventions were mixed and highly heterogeneous. Overall, the evidence base was limited by the small number of studies, generally modest sample sizes, substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, and risk-of-bias concerns, limiting conclusions regarding the relative efficacy of individual interventions.ConclusionsNon-pharmacological interventions may contribute to ADHD management in LMICs as part of multimodal care. Larger, methodologically rigorous studies are needed to better establish their efficacy and support culturally appropriate and accessible implementation.

articles.title: Gitelman syndrome complicated by pregnancy: clinical management and maternal-fetal outcomes - a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gitelman syndrome (GS), an autosomal recessive tubulopathy caused by SLC12A3 mutations, presents with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypocalciuria and hypomagnesemia. Pregnancy can exacerbate these imbalances, increasing maternal-fetal risks, yet standardized management remains lacking. This review summarizes complications, management strategies, and outcomes to guide evidence-based care.
METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CNKI were searched from inception to December 31, 2025, using 'Gitelman Syndrome' AND ('pregnancy' OR 'gestation'). Two reviewers independently performed literature screening, data extraction, and quality assessment. Core data were analyzed descriptively, categorical variables as frequencies (%), continuous as mean ± SD or median (range).
RESULTS: Fifty-six studies (96 pregnancies, 81 women) from 19 countries were included. Among pregnancies with available outcome data, reported maternal complications included gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) (11.5%), oligohydramnios (9.4%), and preeclampsia/hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets (HELLP) syndrome (3.1%); fetal/neonatal complications included preterm birth (16.7%), growth restriction (5.2%), and death (4.2%). Preconception diagnosis showed lower GDM (6.3% vs 18.4%) and fetal/neonatal death (0% vs 8.2%); these comparisons were descriptive and exploratory only. Oral potassium and magnesium were the main treatments. Potassium-sparing diuretics were used in 16 pregnancies (18 exposures); no malformations were reported, but safety is unestablished. Vaginal delivery occurred in 51.2% and Cesarean in 48.8%.
CONCLUSIONS: Preconception counseling and multidisciplinary care with close electrolyte monitoring and individualized supplementation may benefit GS-complicated pregnancies, but evidence is limited by case-report data, publication bias, and heterogeneity. Larger prospective studies with standardized outcome reporting are needed to clarify risk factors and guide clinical management.

articles.title: Treatment outcomes and safety of oral β-blockers and sirolimus in children with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe outcomes and safety of oral β-blockers and sirolimus in children with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma (KHE).
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children with KHE receiving oral β-blockers or sirolimus at Beijing Children's Hospital from January 2016 to April 2026. Lesion regression at fixed time points, treatment duration, treatment discontinuation, recurrence, and safety were assessed.
RESULTS: Thirteen patients received β-blockers and 11 sirolimus, including three with prior therapy. Baseline lesion measurements did not differ significantly, but the β-blocker group was younger [median 4.0 (IQR, 3.0-4.0) vs. 19.0 (10.5-29.5) months; p < 0.001] and had lower frequencies of pain (23.1% vs. 72.7%; p = 0.038) and hyperhidrosis (0% vs. 54.5%; p = 0.003). Cumulative lesion-regression thresholds did not differ significantly through 9 months. At 9 months, >25%, >50%, and >75% regression occurred in 76.9%, 46.2%, and 23.1% with β-blockers versus 100.0%, 72.7%, and 18.2% with sirolimus, respectively. Treatment was discontinued in 9/13 and 3/11 patients (median durations, 40.0 and 18.0 months, respectively). No recurrence was observed after cessation. Safety events were reversible and manageable.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, both treatments were associated with improvement, but baseline imbalances limit direct comparison. β-blocker responses in predominantly younger, less symptomatic patients require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and indicators associated with poor in-hospital prognosis among children with severe pertussis in Shandong Province, China (2022-2024).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pertussis is a life-threatening respiratory infection among young infants. This retrospective study enrolled only children already diagnosed with severe pertussis. We aimed to describe clinical characteristics and identify indicators associated with poor in‑hospital prognosis within this severe cohort, rather than exploring predictors for progression from mild to severe pertussis.
METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted among 80 children diagnosed with severe pertussis who were hospitalized between January 2022 and December 2024. Clinical data, laboratory results, treatment, and outcomes were collected. Multivariate logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were applied to screen indicators associated with composite poor in-hospital prognosis and evaluate their prognostic performance.Composite poor in-hospital prognosis was defined as new in-hospital adverse events including invasive mechanical ventilation, pertussis encephalopathy with persistent neurological sequelae, or all-cause in-hospital death; 6 out of 80 participants met this composite endpoint. White blood cell count was included as a continuous variable in multivariate regression. The optimal cutoff of > 30 × 10⁹/L was derived from ROC analysis for descriptive and potential bedside reference only and was not used for regression modelling.
RESULTS: The median age was 4 months and 19 days (range, 1 month 14 days to 5 years); 65.0% (52/80) of patients were infants ≤ 3 months who could not receive routine diphtheria, pertussis, and tetanus (DPT) vaccine. All patients presented paroxysmal cough, and 95% had inspiratory whoop. Leukocytosis (WBC > 20 × 10⁹/L) was observed in 45.0% of children; 75.0% had patent foramen ovale (PFO), and 18.80% developed secondary cardiac abnormalities. Erythromycin combination therapy carried a significantly higher risk of liver dysfunction than monotherapy (36.40% vs. 8.60%, P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified three independent correlates of composite poor prognosis: unvaccinated status (OR = 4.2, 95%CI 1.8-9.6, P = 0.001), mixed bacterial-viral co-infection (OR = 3.5, 95%CI 1.2-10.1, P = 0.023), and elevated continuous white blood cell count (OR = 5.1, 95%CI 2.3-11.4, P < 0.001). Given the limited number of poor-prognosis events (n = 6), these adjusted associations should be interpreted cautiously as exploratory findings.ROC analysis using continuous WBC count yielded an AUC of 0.678, whereas the combined prognostic model derived from multivariable logistic regression achieved an AUC of 0.689.
CONCLUSIONS: Infants aged ≤ 3 months constituted the majority of children hospitalized with severe pertussis. After adjusting for age-related vaccination eligibility, unvaccinated status, mixed bacterial-viral co-infection, and higher white blood cell count were independently associated with poor in-hospital prognosis. ROC analysis demonstrated only modest discriminative performance of these indicators; at present, they serve merely as potential references and require external validation before any clinical application.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Factors associated with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis among people living with HIV in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: a case-control study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, particularly in developing countries. Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB), defined as resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin, poses a serious public health challenge. People living with HIV (PLWHIV) are 16 times more likely to develop TB than HIV-negative individuals, and TB is the leading cause of death in this population. Despite this, evidence on the specific factors associated with MDR-TB among PLWHIV in Addis Ababa remains limited. This study aimed to identify factors associated with MDR-TB among PLWHIV in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
METHODS: A facility-based unmatched case control study was conducted from June 15 to July 15, 2024, in three MDR-TB treatment hospitals in Addis Ababa. Cases were HIV-positive patients with GeneXpert/culture-confirmed MDR-TB, while controls were HIV-positive patients who were declared cured or had successfully completed first-line anti-TB treatment. Participants were selected using simple random sampling, with a 1:1 case-to-control ratio (117 cases and 117 controls). Data were analyzed using binary and multivariable logistic regression; adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were used to measure associations.
RESULTS: A total of 234 respondents (117 cases and 117 controls) participated in this study. Four factors were independently associated with MDR-TB development: Residence in Addis Ababa (AOR: 4.17, 95% CI: 1.96-8.77), contact history with a known MDR-TB patient (AOR: 9.09, 95% CI: 3.70-22.37), prior TB treatment (AOR: 5.56, 95% CI: 2.33-13.3), and living in rooms without windows (AOR: 6.10, 95% CI: 2.12-17.53).
CONCLUSION: Contact with known MDR-TB patients, prior TB treatment, urban residence in Addis Ababa, and poor home ventilation were significantly associated with MDR-TB among PLWHIV. Targeted interventions including strengthened contact tracing, strict adherence support during first-line treatment, and housing improvement are essential to curb MDR-TB transmission in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Estimation of serial intervals and time-varying reproduction numbers across SARS-CoV-2 variants in childcare clusters: symptom onset vs. reporting dates.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory virus transmission in childcare centers is facilitated by dense contact patterns, making accurate estimation of serial intervals (SI) and time-varying reproduction numbers (Rt) essential for outbreak management. Although symptom onset dates are epidemiologically preferred, reporting dates are frequently used in routine surveillance due to operational constraints. Reliance on reporting dates may introduce systematic bias in transmission parameter estimates. This study aimed to evaluate differences in SI and Rt estimates based on symptom onset versus reporting dates in COVID-19 childcare clusters across SARS-CoV-2 variant periods.
METHODS: Nationwide data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (January 2020-February 2022) were analyzed. Four genotype-confirmed clusters meeting the predefined eligibility criteria were included: one Before Delta, two Delta, and one Omicron cluster, each comprising at least 50 epidemiologically linked cases. Serial intervals were fitted using gamma distributions. Time-varying Rt values were estimated using the EpiEstim package separately based on symptom onset and reporting dates.
RESULTS: Onset-based mean SI declined from 9.85 days (95% CI: 1.97-23.95) in the Before Delta period to 5.34 days (95% CI: 2.00-10.28) during Omicron. In contrast, reporting-based SI estimates were generally longer, reaching 8.87 days (95% CI: 0.71-27.08) during Omicron. Across all variant periods, reporting-based Rt estimates were consistently lower than onset-based estimates. For example, during the Delta period, mean Rt was 1.90 (95% CI: 0.79-3.76) using onset dates compared with 1.08 (95% CI: 0.41-2.39) using reporting dates.
CONCLUSION: The choice of temporal reference substantially affects SI and Rt estimation in childcare clusters. Reliance on reporting dates may underestimate real-time transmission intensity and distort epidemic risk assessment. Prioritizing symptom onset data in surveillance systems may improve the accuracy and timeliness of public health responses in high-risk settings.

articles.title: Healthcare-associated infections in five annual point prevalence surveys at a Chinese tertiary hospital: annual patterns, associated factors, and cumulative healthcare resource use.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Repeated point prevalence surveys (PPSs) can characterize healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and inform infection prevention priorities. This study examined annual HAI patterns, associated factors, antimicrobial use, and cumulative healthcare resource use at the survey date in a Chinese tertiary hospital.
METHODS: Five annual PPSs were conducted from 2020 to 2024 using a repeated cross-sectional design. Patient-level trends were assessed using an exact Cochran-Armitage test and episode-level trends using Poisson regression. Factors associated with prevalent HAI were examined using multivariable logistic regression. Cumulative hospital stay and consumer price index-adjusted hospitalization costs were analyzed using generalized linear models with a gamma distribution and log link.
RESULTS: Among 4,245 surveyed inpatients, 72 patients had 81 HAI episodes, corresponding to patient-level and episode-level prevalence estimates of 1.70% and 1.91%, respectively. Patient-level prevalence decreased from 2.99% in 2020 to 0.93% in 2024 (exact P = 0.001), and episode-level prevalence also declined (rate ratio per one-year increase, 0.735; 95% CI, 0.624-0.867; P < 0.001). Lower respiratory tract and urinary tract infections each accounted for 34.57% of episodes. Antimicrobial use decreased from 38.86% to 30.02% (P for trend = 0.006). Indwelling urinary catheterization (OR, 12.827; 95% CI, 6.545-25.137) and central venous access device placement (CVAD) (OR, 2.223; 95% CI, 1.154-4.284) were associated with prevalent HAI, whereas surgery showed an inverse adjusted association (OR, 0.462; 95% CI, 0.241-0.883). HAI status was associated with adjusted mean ratios of 1.970 (95% CI, 1.616-2.402) for cumulative hospital stay and 2.013 (95% CI, 1.673-2.423) for hospitalization costs at the PPS date (both P < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Patient-level and episode-level HAI prevalence and antimicrobial use showed overall downward trends across the five annual PPSs. Indwelling urinary catheterization and CVAD placement were associated with prevalent HAI. These findings support continued surveillance of priority infection sites and strengthened management of invasive devices.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of a clinical score with a rapid diagnostic test for enteric fever in Nepal, Bangladesh and Cambodia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distinguishing enteric (typhoid and paratyphoid) fever from other causes of fever is challenging. The diagnostic accuracy of Typhoid Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDT) are suboptimal but might improve if combined with a clinical score. We aimed to develop a clinical score, incorporating a point of care C-reactive protein (CRP) and Typhoid RDT, that could be used for febrile patients attending a health facility with limited laboratory capability, to identify those suitable for further investigations such as a blood culture, an empirical antimicrobial choice that covers enteric fever, or to rule out enteric fever as a likely diagnosis.
METHODS: Overall, 1168 Bangladeshi, Cambodian and Nepali children and adults attending hospital with fever were randomly split (80:20) into derivation and validation cohorts. There were 208/1168 (18%) with blood-culture-confirmed enteric fever. In the derivation cohort we studied the association of symptoms, signs, CRP, laboratory results, and the Test-it™ typhoid IgM RDT with blood culture confirmed enteric fever using logistic regression and developed several clinical scores. We determined the diagnostic accuracy of the clinical scores in the validation cohort.
RESULTS: The Typhoid RDT had a sensitivity of 63% and specificity 73% in the validation cohort. A basic clinical score including fever ≥ 3 days, headache, abdominal pain, diarrhoea, absence of cough, and CRP ≥ 10 mg/L had a sensitivity of 80% and specificity 56%. Adding the Typhoid RDT result to the clinical score resulted in a sensitivity of 87%, a specificity of 58%, a PPV of 34%, and a NPV of 95%.
CONCLUSIONS: The diagnostic accuracy of a Typhoid RDT was only marginally improved by combining with a clinical score. Enteric fever was very unlikely with a negative clinical score.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics, etiology, and treatment strategies for renal and perinephric abscesses in adults: a single-center, descriptive, 10-year retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics, etiology, and antimicrobial resistance patterns of renal abscesses (RAs) and perinephric abscesses (PNAs) in adults and to analyze the associated treatment outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 40 adults who were diagnosed with RAs or PNAs at our institution between October 2014 and December 2024. The data collected included demographics, risk factors, clinical presentations, laboratory/imaging findings, microbiology, treatment modalities, and outcomes.
RESULTS: The median age of the patients was 51 years (IQR: 38-63 years; range, 18-84 years), with a male-to-female ratio of 1:2.1. Diabetes mellitus (50%) and urinary tract calculi (35%) were the most common risk factors. The predominant clinical manifestations included fever (72.5%), chills (37.5%), and flank pain (35%). Laboratory findings frequently revealed leukocytosis (87.5%), markedly elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) (median, 174 mg/L; IQR: 124.5-214.5 mg/L), and elevated procalcitonin (67.5%). Escherichia coli (E. coli) was the predominant pathogen, identified in 28 out of 39 positive cultures (71.8%), with a high proportion (53.57%) being extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) producers.Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) was the most frequently used and clinically most useful diagnostic tool, establishing or strongly supporting the diagnosis in 62.5% of patients. Treatment included antibiotics alone (55%), antibiotics combined with drainage (42.5%), and nephrectomy (2.5%). All patients showed clinical improvement at discharge after a median hospital stay of 12 days (IQR: 8-16 days). During follow-up among the 30 patients who had regular outpatient visits, 83.33% (25/30) experienced resolved infections, whereas 16.67% (5/30) experienced recurrence. The outcomes for the remaining 10 patients who did not complete regular follow-up were not captured.
CONCLUSIONS: RAs and PNAs often present with nonspecific symptoms, underscoring the importance of early diagnosis and management. Diabetes is a major risk factor, and infections are predominantly caused by highly resistant E. coli. Contrast-enhanced CT is essential for diagnosis, but combination antibiotic and drainage therapy effectively improves patient prognosis. Optimizing antibiotic selection and intervention timing should be future priorities.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Assessing the association between compliance to intensive adherence counselling and viral suppression among children and adolescents living with HIV in Karamoja sub region, Uganda.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Viral load suppression (VLS) among children and adolescents living with HIV (CALHIV) remains below the 95% target in many settings; in Uganda, only about 60% of CALHIV on antiretroviral therapy (ART) are suppressed. Intensive adherence counselling (IAC) is recommended for non-suppressed patients, but evidence on its effectiveness in pastoralist, resource-limited settings such as Karamoja is limited.
OBJECTIVE: This study had two complementary objectives. The quantitative objective was to assess the association between compliance to IAC and viral load suppression among CALHIV at ART-accredited health facilities in Karamoja sub region, Uganda. The qualitative objective was to explore the perceived barriers and facilitators to completing IAC in the same setting.
METHODS: This mixed-methods cohort study combined retrospective chart review with key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs), conducted across 36 ART-accredited Karamoja facilities (January-December 2023; data abstracted January-March 2024). All eligible CALHIV aged 0-19 years with a documented high viral load (> 200 copies/mL plasma; >400 copies/mL dried blood spot, DBS) who were initiated on IAC were enrolled. Compliance to IAC was defined, using session-attendance records, as receipt of three or more consecutive monthly sessions. Modified Poisson regression was used to estimate the association between IAC compliance and viral load suppression, reported as crude and adjusted prevalence risk ratios (PRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Thematic analysis of the KIIs and FGDs was used to explore perceived barriers and facilitators to completing IAC.
RESULTS: Of the CALHIV assessed for eligibility, 154 met the inclusion criteria and were analysed. Participants' mean age was 12.0 years (SD 4.2); 53.2% were female; mean ART duration was 12.3 months. Most (83.8%, n = 129) received three or more sessions. Suppression reached 41.1% (n = 53) among compliant versus 8.0% (n = 2) of non-compliant participants (crude PRR 5.14, 95% CI 1.34-19.72, p = 0.0016). After adjustment for facility level, age, ART duration, and HIV disclosure status, compliance to IAC remained independently associated with suppression (adjusted PRR 4.78, 95% CI 1.26-18.10, p = 0.021); the hospital-level association attenuated and was no longer significant (adjusted PRR 3.30, 95% CI 0.91-12.04, p = 0.071). Both confidence intervals were wide, reflecting the small non-compliant group, so the magnitude of the effect should be interpreted with caution. Qualitative analysis identified perceived barriers (food insecurity, caregiver alcohol use, boarding-school attendance) and facilitators (caregiver meetings, peer support) to completing IAC, alongside perceptions of IAC effectiveness, health-system readiness for delivery, and improved quality of life.
CONCLUSIONS: Compliant CALHIV were more likely to achieve suppression than non-compliant CALHIV, although the wide confidence interval means the size of this association is uncertain; 58.9% of compliant participants nonetheless remained non-suppressed. IAC is necessary but insufficient; complementary interventions addressing structural barriers and clinical factors including drug resistance screening are required.

articles.title: Development and validation of a decision tree model to distinguish bacterial meningitis from viral meningitis and/or encephalitis in children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early differentiation between bacterial meningitis (BM) and viral meningitis and/or encephalitis (VM/E) in children remains challenging due to overlapping clinical features and limited availability of rapid aetiological diagnosis. We aimed to develop and internally validate an interpretable decision tree model based on routinely available variables for early discrimination between BM and VM/E.
METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study in which paediatric patients were classified as BM or VM/E according to predefined criteria. Candidate variables were first identified through univariate analysis and subsequently incorporated into a decision tree model. Model performance was evaluated in both the training and test sets.
RESULTS: A total of 149 children were included, comprising 94 (63.09%) BM and 55 (36.91%) VM/E cases. The decision-tree model included three predictors, with procalcitonin (PCT) as the primary splitting variable, followed by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) protein and C-reactive protein (CRP). In the training set, the model demonstrated excellent performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.979 (95% CI: 0.912-0.994), sensitivity of 96.97%, and specificity of 97.44%. In the test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.753 (95% CI: 0.622-0.885), with sensitivity of 82.14% and specificity of 68.75%. Empirical antimicrobial therapy was frequently initiated prior to definitive diagnosis, with a substantial proportion of patients with VM/E receiving antibacterial treatment and some patients with BM receiving antiviral therapy.
CONCLUSION: We developed an interpretable and parsimonious decision-tree model based on routinely available clinical variables for early differentiation between BM and VM/E in children. This model may serve as a practical tool for early clinical assessment before microbiological confirmation.

articles.title: Sustained Improvement in Time in Range After Automated Insulin Delivery Initiation in Adolescents and Adults With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A 12-Month Prospective Observational Study From Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated insulin delivery (AID) improves glycemic outcomes in trials, but long-term real-world data on comprehensive continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics remain limited in the Middle East.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) initiating Control-IQ (CIQ) or MiniMed 780G (MMG) at King Fahad Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between December 2023 and November 2025. Participants were followed for 12 months. Continuous glucose monitoring outcomes included time in range (TIR: 70-180 mg/dL), time above range (TAR), time below range (TBR), glycemic management indicator (GMI), mean sensor glucose, and coefficient of variation (CV) and assessed at baseline and 6 post-initiation time points. Glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) was assessed using paired pre- and post-AID values.
RESULTS: A total of 132 adults were included: 76 using CIQ and 56 using MMG. Mean age was 27.2 ± 7.7 years, 68.9% were female, and mean diabetes duration was 14.5 ± 7.9 years. Time in range increased from 59.0 ± 15.4% at baseline to 72.3 ± 10.2% at 2 weeks and remained sustained at 12 months (73.5 ± 11.5%; +15.1 percentage points; P < .001). Time below range <70 mg/dL decreased from 5.3 ± 5.3 to 1.4 ± 1.2%. Glycated hemoglobin A1c decreased from 7.42 ± 1.13 to 6.52 ± 0.73% (P < .001; n = 106). Time in range ≥70% increased from 29.0% to 71.0%, and HbA1c <7% increased from 30.3% to 74.5%. Severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis rates were significantly reduced.
CONCLUSION: In a Saudi tertiary diabetes center, AID initiation was associated with rapid and sustained 12-month improvements in TIR, HbA1c, hypoglycemia exposure, and acute diabetes-related events.

articles.title: Reduced Hippocampal Subfield Volumes in Neonates with Low 1-Minute Apgar Scores Correlate with Umbilical Artery Blood Gas Parameters.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Perinatal asphyxia may induce brain injury, while the effects of transient hypoxia on hippocampal subregions remain unclear. Using the 1-minute Apgar score, this study examined its effects on hippocampal volumes and correlations with umbilical artery blood gas parameters (UABG), providing imaging evidence to evaluate hypoxia-related brain injury.
METHODS: Neonates were assigned to the low Apgar score (LAS) group and the normal Apgar score (NAS) group. All subjects underwent 3D T1-weighted brain MRI for hippocampal volumetry. UABG indices, including pH, lactate (LAC), and base excess (BE), were collected. We performed an analysis of covariance with sex, postmenstrual age at MRI, and total brain volume as covariates, followed by correlation analysis.
RESULTS: Multiple hippocampal subfields exhibited significantly smaller volumes in the LAS group (all FDR-corrected q < 0.05). Within-group analyses identified correlations between hippocampal volumes and UABG parameters. In the LAS group, left parasubiculum volume was correlated with pH and base excess, and in the NAS group, left parasubiculum volume correlated with the two indicators, while right tail volume correlated with pH.
CONCLUSION: Neonates with lower 1-minute Apgar scores exhibit reduced volume of specific hippocampal subregions, correlating with umbilical artery blood gas parameters. These findings link transiently low 1-minute Apgar scores with hippocampal subregional morphology during the neonatal period.
ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: We investigated neonates with low 1-minute Apgar scores that normalized at 5 minutes and found their hippocampal subregional structural changes correlated with umbilical artery blood gas parameters.

articles.title: Detailed Memory and the Self: Examining the Development of the Self-Referential Effect in Autism.
articles.abstract: The self-referential effect (SRE), better memory for self-related information, strengthens with age and includes certain source details. In autism, altered self-referential processing may reduce the SRE, though findings remain mixed. Further, the effect of self-referencing on source details is understudied in autism. We studied 37 (10 female) autistic and 64 (35 female) nonautistic children between the ages of 7 and 17 years using a self- vs. other-referential encoding paradigm and a recognition task. Both groups showed stronger memory for self-encoded words, but nonautistic children had higher average SRE. The SRE emerged for inherent (referent type) but not peripheral (word location) source memory in both groups. In nonautistic children, the SRE increased with age. Findings suggest self-referential encoding can support memory and social learning in both autistic and nonautistic children.

articles.title: Multimodal Communication in Early Autism: A Microanalytic Investigation of Gesture, Speech, and Temporal Synchrony During Parent-Child Interaction.
articles.abstract: Early communication is inherently multimodal, relying on the coordination of gestures, speech, and gaze in time. While differences in gesture and speech production have been widely documented in autism, far less is known about how these communicative modalities are integrated and temporally organized during early interactions, especially in very young children with a confirmed diagnosis. The present study investigated multimodal communication in 30 autistic and 26 neurotypical toddlers and young children during naturalistic parent-child play interactions, using a fine-grained microanalytic coding approach. We examined gesture and speech production, their integration with gaze and with each other, and critically, the temporal synchrony between gesture and speech. Relative to neurotypical peers, autistic children produced fewer gestures and less spoken language, while relying more heavily on non-word vocalizations. Beyond these modality-specific differences, autistic children displayed lower rates of gesture-gaze and gesture-speech integration. Most notably, they exhibited a reduced temporal alignment between gesture and speech, indicating diminished gesture-speech synchrony during spontaneous interaction. These findings suggest that early autistic communication differs not only in the frequency and distribution of communicative behaviors, but also in how and when these behaviors are coordinated in time. By suggesting that temporal organization may be an important dimension of early multimodal communication, this study extends current work on early social communication in autism and underscores the value of temporally sensitive, interaction-focused approaches.

articles.title: Association of Antenatal Corticosteroid Administration-to-Birth Intervals With Mortality and Morbidity Among Extremely Preterm Infants: Multicenter Data from Shenzhen, China.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The optimal interval between antenatal corticosteroid (ACS) administration and birth remains uncertain, and Chinese multicentre data are scarce.
METHODS: In this multicentre retrospective cohort, 1,328 infants born before 32 weeks were classified by ACS-to-birth interval: none, <24 hours, 24 hours-7 days or >7 days. The primary outcome was survival without major morbidity (SWMM).
RESULTS: Only the 24 hours-7 days interval was associated with lower pre-discharge death, treated patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and severe brain injury, and higher SWMM. Intervals <24 hours reduced death and severe retinopathy of prematurity (sROP) only; intervals >7 days improved SWMM, severe brain injury and sROP without survival benefit. Severe intraventricular hemorrhage risk rose nonlinearly at short intervals. A single complete course conferred the broadest protection, with graded reductions in treated PDA.
CONCLUSION: ACS benefits are interval- and outcome-specific; 24 hours-7 days provided the broadest protection, supporting individualized regimens.

articles.title: Subfield-specific hippocampal enlargement in high-functioning autism spectrum disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although previous studies have reported abnormal hippocampal volumes in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), the specific alterations in hippocampal subfields and their relationships with clinical symptoms in high-functioning ASD (HF-ASD) remain unclear.
METHODS: In this study, we analyzed T1-weighted structural MRI data from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE-I), including 182 children and adolescents with HF-ASD and 213 age- and sex-matched typically developing controls (TDC). Using a linear mixed-effects model, we compared hippocampal volumes between groups, and examined associations between volumes and clinical measurements.
RESULTS: Compared to TDC, the children and adolescents with HF-ASD exhibited significantly increased volumes in the right entire hippocampus, presubiculum, subiculum, and granule cell layer of the dentate gyrus (GC-DG). No significant volumetric differences were observed within the child or adolescent subgroups, nor between these age groups. Notably, presubiculum volume showed a positive correlation with verbal scores and a negative correlation with social scores in the HF-ASD group.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate subfield-specific hippocampal overgrowth in children and adolescents with HF-ASD and presubiculum volume alteration may be a potential neuroanatomical correlate underlying verbal and social dysfunctions.

articles.title: Associations of autism spectrum disorder and male sex with violent suicide attempt methods among medically critically ill adolescents: Findings from a tertiary intensive care setting.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify key clinical and demographic factors associated with violent suicide attempt methods among medically critically ill adolescents admitted to a tertiary intensive care setting, with a particular focus on autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and sex differences.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive adolescents aged 10-19 years admitted to a tertiary emergency intensive care center following suicide attempts between February 2012 and April 2023 (N = 113). Violent methods were defined as physical modalities associated with high somatic lethality, distinct from standard pharmaceutical drug overdoses. Psychiatric diagnoses were evaluated post-resuscitation by dedicated on-site psychiatrists and clinical psychologists using DSM criteria and standardized clinical assessments when indicated.
RESULTS: Among 113 participants (33 violent attempts), an ASD diagnosis and male sex were significantly and independently associated with violent suicide attempt methods. Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that adolescents with ASD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 6.96, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.48-19.50, p = .002) and male patients (aOR = 4.31, 95% CI: 1.38-13.50, p = .012) had significantly elevated odds of employing violent attempt methods. Jumping from heights was the predominant violent modality (66.7%), while rare fatal methods, such as lethal substance ingestion and self-immolation, were descriptively observed only in the ASD subgroup. Exploratory sensitivity analyses supported the empirical consistency of these main associations.
CONCLUSIONS: An ASD diagnosis and male sex are independently associated with violent suicide attempt methods among medically critically ill adolescents in tertiary intensive care. Clinical management should integrate acute-phase behavioral safety planning and emotion-regulation support for neurodivergent youth with proactive outreach for adolescent males. In addition, environmental lethal means restriction remains vital to mitigating severe, life-threatening suicide attempts across clinical, educational, and community systems.

articles.title: Perinatal risk factors associated with autism spectrum disorder.
articles.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition with multifactorial etiology, resulting from complex interactions between genetic susceptibility and environmental exposures. Although numerous studies have identified individual perinatal risk factors for ASD, most have examined these exposures in isolation, limiting understanding of how perinatal complications cluster and jointly influence neurodevelopment. Evidence from Latin America also remains scarce. This study aimed to identify multivariate perinatal risk patterns associated with ASD in a Chilean population, addressing gaps in regional representation and methodological approaches. We conducted a population-based analysis of mothers of children with and without ASD in Chile. A broad set of medical and psychosocial perinatal variables was jointly analyzed using multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) to characterize interrelated risk structures. MCA revealed a clear separation between ASD and non-ASD groups along the first dimension, suggesting that ASD diagnosis is embedded within structured perinatal patterns rather than isolated exposures. MCA-derived, stepwise, and LASSO-penalized logistic regression models were then compared. The most parsimonious model identified maternal vaginal bleeding during pregnancy, prenatal maternal stress or anxiety, and negative pregnancy intention or perception as the strongest factors jointly associated with increased odds of ASD, with a dose-response pattern observed for maternal stress. An unexpected inverse association with neonatal cyanosis may reflect enhanced medical surveillance and warrants cautious interpretation. These findings underscore the importance of integrated perinatal care addressing both obstetric and maternal mental health, and demonstrate the value of multivariate approaches for elucidating complex developmental risk pathways.

articles.title: Effects of SMOFlipid-based versus soybean oil-based high-protein parenteral nutrition on hematologic, biochemical, and clinical outcomes after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in children with acute leukemia: a randomized double-blind controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal parenteral nutrition (PN) strategies, especially the parenteral lipid composition, for children undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remain uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a randomized double-blind trial comparing high-protein PN containing SMOFlipid with soybean oil-based PN (Intralipid) in pediatric patients undergoing allo-HSCT for acute leukemia. Forty-six participants completed the study (SMOFlipid, n = 22; Intralipid, n =24). Primary outcomes were neutrophil and platelet engraftment; secondary outcomes included anthropometric, biochemical, inflammatory, and clinical parameters.
RESULTS: Neutrophil engraftment was similar between groups, whereas platelet engraftment occurred later in the SMOFlipid group. Both groups experienced nutritional deterioration during the early post-transplant period; however, SMOFlipid was associated with better preservation of anthropometric measures and more favorable metabolic trajectories, including lower triglyceride excursion and improved glycemic patterns. Adjusted interleukin-6 concentrations were higher in the SMOFlipid group. Although infection rates were similar, adjusted analyses suggested lower hazards of acute graft-versus-host disease and 100-day mortality with SMOFlipid. Kaplan-Meier analysis also demonstrated improved in-hospital survival.
CONCLUSION: SMOFlipid-based PN was associated with favorable metabolic and body-composition outcomes during early recovery after pediatric allo-HSCT, although platelet engraftment was modestly delayed and inflammatory markers were higher. Larger multicenter studies are required to confirm these findings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06625372.

articles.title: Preliminary findings of high-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation on depressive symptoms and cognitive function in adolescents with mood disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mood disorders in adolescents significantly impair their educational attainment and daily functioning. Nevertheless, there is a paucity of Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved pharmacological interventions specifically for adolescents, and pharmacological interventions often require a considerable duration to achieve therapeutic efficacy. High-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation (Hi-tACS), a non-invasive and safe neuromodulation technique, has demonstrated promising outcomes in the treatment of depressive symptoms in adults. Given its favorable efficacy and safety profile, Hi-tACS warrants investigation as a potential therapeutic strategy for adolescent mood disorders.
METHODS: A total of 27 adolescents (aged 14-18 years) diagnosed with a depressive episode of a mood disorder were enrolled and assigned to either a Hi-tACS intervention group (tACS group) or a medication treatment management group (MTM group). The tACS group received ongoing pharmacotherapy concomitant with 20 sessions of Hi-tACS intervention, administered twice daily over 10 days. The MTM group received ongoing pharmacotherapy alone. Baseline data were collected at enrollment, and follow-up assessments were conducted at 10- and 30-day post-baseline, encompassing measures of clinical symptoms (e.g., depression, anxiety, sleep quality) and cognitive function.
RESULTS: The tACS group demonstrated significantly greater and more rapid reductions in both Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D) scores (P = 0.001) and Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAM-A) scores (P = 0.002) compared to the MTM group. Regarding cognitive function, although the time × group interaction effect for the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS) total score (P = 0.113) did not reach statistical significance, the tACS group exhibited a notable but non-significant trend toward superior cognitive improvement relative to the MTM group.
CONCLUSION: As a novel, safe, and efficient neuromodulation technique, Hi-tACS may offer enhanced efficacy in ameliorating symptoms of depression and anxiety among adolescents compared to medication alone. Furthermore, it demonstrates a potential trend toward superior cognitive enhancement, particularly in memory function.

articles.title: Working memory and BMIz in preschool children: an indirect association involving insufficient healthy food intake.
articles.abstract: Executive function and health behaviors may be relevant to obesity in preschool children, a critical period for obesity prevention, but their associations remain unclear. Our cross-sectional study investigated these associations in 1,557 preschool children from Wuhan, China. The primary adiposity outcome was body mass index z-score (BMIz). Executive function was assessed using seven tasks, from which standardized task scores were averaged to derive working memory and inhibitory control composite scores. Dietary intake was assessed using a Food Frequency Questionnaire. The insufficient healthy food intake and excessive unhealthy food intake scores were summed to derive an overall dietary risk score. Linear mixed-effects models with a random intercept for kindergarten showed that working memory composite score was inversely associated with BMIz. This association was not observed in inhibitory control composite score. Both insufficient healthy food intake score and overall dietary risk score were positively associated with BMIz. The indirect association analysis indicated that insufficient healthy food intake accounted for 4.94% of the total association between working memory composite score and BMIz. These findings indicate an inverse association between working memory and BMIz in preschool children and suggest a potential indirect association through insufficient healthy food intake. Given the cross-sectional design, prospective studies are needed to clarify the temporal ordering and directionality of these associations.

articles.title: Effects of L-Carnitine Supplementation on Clinical Outcomes, Metabolic Profile, and Organ Function in Critically Ill Children: A Triple-Blinded Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Critically ill children often develop relative l-carnitine deficiency due to hypermetabolism, which can impair mitochondrial energy production and exacerbate organ dysfunction. While adult data suggest that l-carnitine supplementation improves metabolic and clinical outcomes, robust randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in the pediatric intensive care population are lacking.
METHODS: This double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). Critically ill children aged 1 month to 12 years were randomly assigned to receive enteral l-carnitine (50-100 mg/kg/day, maximum 2000 mg/day) or placebo for seven consecutive days. The primary outcome was change in serum total protein. Secondary and exploratory outcomes included changes in glycemic profile, lipid profile, liver function tests, renal function tests, coagulation parameters, blood gas parameters, and clinical outcomes including 28-day mortality and Glasgow Coma Scale.
RESULTS: The l-carnitine group showed between-group improvements in liver and tissue injury markers compared to placebo, with reductions in ALT (p = 0.01) and LDH (p = 0.002). While serum albumin improved in both groups, between-group differences were non-significant. Within-group increases were observed for HDL (p < 0.001) and TG (p = 0.03) in the l-carnitine arm. No significant between-group differences were observed for blood sugar, renal function, or coagulation parameters. Notably, the l-carnitine group showed less favorable median shifts in PCO2 and pH (p = 0.01 and p = 0.03, respectively). 28-day mortality was numerically lower in the l-carnitine group than in the placebo group; however, this difference did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSIONS: Enteral l-carnitine supplementation for 7 days was associated with exploratory reductions in biomarkers of tissue and hepatocellular injury (LDH and ALT). However, it did not improve lipid profiles, clinical outcomes, or mortality, and was associated with less favorable acid-base alterations. Larger randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these exploratory findings and clarify the clinical relevance of these effects in critically ill children.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT: IRCT20221206056734N3).

articles.title: Measuring school wellbeing in neurodivergent children: Exploring the suitability of a self-report measure with primary school children with Down syndrome.
articles.abstract: The current study examines the suitability of a self-report measure of school wellbeing for primary school-aged children with Down syndrome. The sample comprised 48 children with Down syndrome aged between 6 and 10.75 years (M = 8.4 years, SD = 1), of whom 43 had both parent-reported school wellbeing and teacher-reported classroom behaviour measures. Children and parents completed parallel versions of the How I Feel About My School (HIFAMS; Allen et al., 2018) measure of school wellbeing; classroom teachers completed the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (Goodman, 2001) and the Brief Early Skills and Support Index (Hughes et al., 2015). Properties of the child-reported HIFMAS were broadly similar to those for neurotypical children. Notably, however, both parent-reported school wellbeing and teacher-reported classroom behaviour showed limited association with child-reported school wellbeing, highlighting the need for further research to evaluate this measure's sensitivity to variation in the school experiences of children with Down Syndrome.

articles.title: Coping with developmental coordination disorder: A comparative study of adults and parents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD/Dyspraxia) is a common, yet under-recognised lifelong neurodevelopmental condition characterised by motor coordination difficulties affecting daily functioning and psychosocial wellbeing. Coping plays an important role in wellbeing, yet little is known about how adults with DCD manage ongoing challenges or how their coping compares with that of parents of individuals with DCD.
METHODS: One hundred and fourteen participants (90 adults with DCD; 24 parents who raised a child with DCD for at least 16 years) completed an online survey assessing coping, acceptance, optimism, resilience, condition perceptions and life satisfaction. Group differences were examined using MANCOVA and t-tests.
RESULTS: Parents reported greater use of adaptive coping, particularly acceptance, and planning, alongside higher optimism, resilience, and life satisfaction. Adults with DCD relied more on maladaptive coping, notably mental disengagement, which was associated with poorer wellbeing. Acceptance-based coping was a protective factor in both groups. Social support and humour showed no clear association with wellbeing. Greater motor coordination difficulties were associated with increased disengagement and reduced humour use.
CONCLUSIONS: Adults with DCD and parents show distinct coping and wellbeing profiles. Findings highlight the need for tailored interventions that promote adaptive coping and acceptance in adults with DCD overall.

articles.title: The effect of multi-site repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on executive functions and reading abilities in adolescents with comorbid attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and developmental dyslexia: A randomised controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) frequently co-occurs with developmental dyslexia (DD), and this comorbidity in children and adolescents is associated with pronounced cognitive and academic impairments. Current treatment approaches for ADHD + DD remain suboptimal, particularly in addressing the combined deficits. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has emerged as a promising neuromodulatory intervention, yet its therapeutic potential in this comorbid population has not been systematically evaluated.
METHODS: In a randomized controlled trial, 60 children diagnosed with ADHD + DD were assigned to either the rTMS group (receiving 40 high-frequency sessions over 8 weeks) or the sham rTMS group. Primary outcomes included executive function measures (n-back task, Go/No-go task) and reading-related tasks (phonological, morphological, and orthographic awareness). Safety and tolerability were closely monitored throughout the intervention.
RESULTS: Using mixed-design repeated measures ANOVA, compared with the sham group, the rTMS group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in verbal working memory accuracy (p < 0.05), response inhibition accuracy (p < 0.001), and processing speed across multiple tasks (p < 0.05). Reading performance also improved, with enhanced phonological awareness accuracy (p < 0.05) and faster morphological processing (p = 0.028). Correlation analyses indicated that improvements in executive function were significantly associated with gains in reading ability. Both interventions were well tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported.
CONCLUSION: Multi-site high-frequency rTMS significantly enhances executive function and reading skills in children and adolescents with ADHD + DD, with a favorable safety profile. These findings provide novel evidence supporting rTMS as a neuromodulation-based intervention for this comorbid condition and highlight the therapeutic relevance of targeting the prefrontal-parietal network within an integrative treatment framework.

articles.title: Diagnostic outcomes of adolescents and adults presenting for an autism evaluation who do not meet criteria for autism: A retrospective chart review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Increased autism awareness and evolving diagnostic criteria have led more adolescents and adults to seek formal autism evaluations. This study examined the characteristics and diagnostic outcomes of adolescents and adults presenting for an autism evaluation at an academic autism center who did not receive an autism diagnosis.
METHODS: Electronic health records of patients meeting eligibility criteria (age ≥16 years, evaluation between January 2017 and November 2022, no prior center visits, no known genetic conditions, and not meeting Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders [DSM-5] criteria for autism) were reviewed for demographic and clinical characteristics and DSM-5 diagnostic outcomes. Diagnoses were coded into DSM-5 categories. Diagnostic outcomes were compared across evaluation type, sex, and age groups using Fisher's exact tests.
RESULTS: A total of 121 patients met eligibility criteria (Mage = 28.1 [12.3] years, 57.0% male, 82.1% White). Most patients received multiple DSM-5 diagnoses (M = 2.2 [1.2]). The most common DSM-5 categories were other neurodevelopmental disorders (53.7%), anxiety disorders (47.1%), depressive disorders (28.9%), and trauma- and stressor-related disorders (13.2%). Females were more likely than males to receive an anxiety disorder diagnosis, and males were more likely to receive substance-related diagnoses. There were no differences in diagnostic outcomes across age groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Adolescents and adults presenting for a first-time autism evaluation who did not meet DSM-5 criteria for autism demonstrated diverse psychiatric and neurodevelopmental presentations and frequently received alternative DSM-5 diagnoses.

articles.title: Early intervention in children with fragile X syndrome: Prevalence, timing, and family perception.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is a genetic disorder that commonly leads to intellectual and developmental delays and disabilities. Early intervention (EI) services and therapies provided to children under 3 years of age aim to improve developmental outcomes. This analysis examines the prevalence of EI receipt among children with FXS, enrollment timing, services used, and parental satisfaction with EI services.
METHODS: Data were obtained from the Fragile X Online Registry With Accessible Research Database (FORWARD), collected from 2011 to 2021. Participants aged 3-21 years during at least one clinic visit were included. EI receipt and enrollment age were assessed overall and by demographic characteristics; services used and satisfaction with services were assessed in relation to EI enrollment age. All analyses were stratified by sex.
RESULTS: Among 1114 participants, 86.0% of males and 59.6% of females received EI, with over 80% of parents reporting some level of satisfaction with services. EI receipt varied by household income, parental education, race/ethnicity, household language, and insurance. Among participants diagnosed with FXS at < 3 years, only 8.6% of males and 13.3% of females had a diagnosis before starting EI. Most EI participants received speech and language therapy (93.5% males, 90.3% females), occupational therapy (89.2% males, 72.4% females), and physical therapy (72.5% males, 50.3% females).
CONCLUSION: Most children began early intervention before FXS diagnosis, showing that EI receipt may depend more on recognition of developmental delays than genetic diagnosis. Parental satisfaction with EI was high, though receipt varied substantially by demographic factors, identifying opportunities for targeted outreach.

articles.title: Myocardial Work Analysis: A Novel Echocardiographic Approach for Early Detection of Myocardial Fibrosis in Pediatric Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy With Preserved LVEF-A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While myocardial work (MW) indices have shown diagnostic and prognostic value in various cardiovascular diseases, their role in detecting myocardial fibrosis in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) remains unexplored. This prospective study investigates MW's potential for early identification of fibrosis in pediatric DMD patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction.
METHODS: In this large prospective cohort, we enrolled 242 genetically confirmed DMD males (aged 6-18 years) with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% by cardiac magnetic resonance and 54 age-matched controls. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment included global work index, global constructive work, global wasted work, and global work efficiency analysis. Myocardial fibrosis was assessed via late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance at baseline at 1-year follow-up.
RESULTS: Patients with DMD demonstrated significantly impaired MW indices versus controls (global work index, 1371.4±225.84 versus 1598.04±207.01 mm Hg%; global work efficiency, median 94.67% [Q1-Q3, 93.00-96.00] versus 95.33% [94.30-96.33]; global constructive work, 1630.34±246.37 versus 1900.22±195.84 mm Hg%; global wasted work, median 67.67 [Q1-Q3, 50.17-86.25] versus 59.00 [48.00-73.00] mm Hg%; all P<0.01). Notably, MW abnormalities preceded global longitudinal strain reduction, with significant differences even in patients with DMD with normal global longitudinal strain (≥18%). Global work efficiency showed moderate diagnostic accuracy for baseline late gadolinium enhancement (area under the curve, 0.618) and was associated with subsequent late gadolinium enhancement development in exploratory longitudinal analysis (area under the curve, 0.798; cutoff of 95.85%), providing complementary information beyond conventional echocardiographic parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: This large-scale prospective study suggests that MW analysis, particularly global work efficiency, might be useful for early detection of cardiac dysfunction and might be associated with short-term fibrosis in patients with DMD and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. However, given the limited number of progression events, this finding should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Combined Associations of Maternal Sleep Quality and Prenatal Negative Life Events with Childhood Parasomnias.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Parasomnias are common in early childhood and are increasingly linked to later behavioral and neurodevelopmental vulnerability. Although prenatal determinants of childhood parasomnias are recognized as an emerging research focus, evidence remains limited. Maternal sleep disturbances and psychological stress frequently co-occur during pregnancy and may have long-term implications for offspring health. This study examined the combined associations of maternal prenatal sleep quality and stress exposure with childhood parasomnias.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 6236 preschool-aged children, with maternal prenatal negative life events (NLEs) and sleep quality retrospectively assessed across three gestational periods. Childhood parasomnias were assessed using the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied to reduce group differences across exposure groups. Associations were examined using logistic regressions, and path analysis was performed to estimate direct and indirect effects.
RESULTS: Overall, 25.7% of children had parasomnias, with the highest prevalence in the co-exposure group (37.3%), followed by the poor-sleep-only (29.6%), NLEs-only (23.1%), and no-exposure groups (22.8%). After IPTW, maternal poor sleep quality during pregnancy was associated with increased odds of childhood parasomnias (aOR = 1.402, 95% CI: 1.231-1.596). While NLEs alone were not independently associated with parasomnias, co-exposure to poor sleep quality showed an even stronger risk (aOR = 1.778, 95% CI: 1.122-2.816). Associations appeared stronger among children whose mothers reported lower perceived family support. Path analysis revealed a direct association between maternal sleep quality and childhood parasomnias (β = 0.127, 95% CI: 0.083-0.172).
CONCLUSION: Poor maternal sleep quality during pregnancy was directly associated with increased risk of childhood parasomnias, and co-occurring NLEs further amplified this risk. These findings highlight the importance of jointly assessing maternal sleep quality and psychosocial stress during pregnancy to identify children who are susceptible to developing parasomnias.

articles.title: The Association Between Parent-Reported ADHD-Related Symptoms and English Word Reading in Syrian Refugee Children.
articles.abstract: The purpose of the present study was to examine child-level and family-level factors associated with English word reading in a sample of 133 Syrian refugee children aged 6-13 years resettled in Canada, 35% of whom had resided in refugee camps before resettlement. Using multilevel modeling to account for children nested within families, we examined whether parent-reported ADHD-related symptoms were associated with English word reading after accounting for age, nonverbal reasoning, receptive vocabulary, and phonological awareness, and whether time spent in refugee camps was associated with word reading at the family level. Parent-reported ADHD-related symptoms were assessed using the Hyperactivity/Inattention subscale of the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), a behavioral screening instrument rather than a diagnostic assessment of ADHD. Findings indicated that older age and stronger phonological awareness were associated with higher English word reading scores, while parent-reported ADHD-related symptom scores were associated with lower word reading performance after accounting for the other predictors. In contrast, time spent in refugee camps was not significantly associated with English word reading. These findings highlight the importance of considering attentional and behavioral functioning alongside established cognitive and linguistic correlates when examining English literacy development among Syrian refugee children following resettlement.

articles.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus in women from northern provinces of Lao People's Democratic Republic, 2018-2019.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer is a frequent cause of morbidity and mortality in women worldwide and strongly linked to the presence of high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes. The present study aimed to determine HPV prevalence and genotypes and their relationship with cytology results in Lao women.
METHODS: Between October 2018 and February 2019, a total of 1302 asymptomatic women (mean age 37.4 years, range 18-76) from Xiengkhouang, Luangprabang, Oudomxay and Huaphan provinces were invited to answer a questionnaire, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and a swab for PCR and AnyplexTM II HPV-HR detection.
RESULTS: Overall, 114 of 1268 women with evaluable samples (9.0%) had abnormal cytology and three (0.2%) had cervical cancer. AnyplexTM II HPV-HR kit detected 256 positives among 1184 participants (21.6%), with types 52, 58 and 16 being the most prevalent HR genotypes (20.4%, 12.8% and 11.7%, respectively). Multivariable analysis showed that participants aged ≥ 40 years (OR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.1-2.4, p = 0.015) and those living in Luangprabang province (OR: 1.9; 95% CI: 1.1-3.2, p = 0.02) had a higher likelihood of abnormal cytology compared to younger women and those residing in Huaphan. Single/divorced/widow women had a higher probability of HPV detection compared to married women (OR: 2.3; 95% CI: 1.5-3.7, p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: HPV 52, 58 and 16 were the most prevalent high-risk genotypes, clearly advocating for the introduction of the nonavalent vaccine. Periodic screening of women too old to benefit from the recently introduced vaccine should be considered.

articles.title: Prevalence and factors associated with post-tuberculosis lung disease among children and adolescents in Kenya: A multi-centre study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most patients survive tuberculosis (TB) with treatment. However, emerging evidence reveals occurrence of a post-TB sequelae termed post TB lung disease (PTLD) that affects survivor's long term lung health. Evidence on PTLD in children and adolescents is limited. We evaluated the prevalence and factors associated with PTLD in children and adolescents completing treatment for intrathoracic TB in Nairobi, Kenya.
METHODS: A cross-sectional study done on participants<20 years at the end of treatment for intrathoracic TB in Nairobi. After obtaining informed consent and assent, we interviewed and examined participants, reviewed their medical records, and conducted a six-minute walk test (6MWT) for children >5 years. Post-TB sequelae was defined as persistent respiratory symptoms and/or abnormal respiratory signs after TB treatment. Descriptive statistics were computed for prevalence of post-TB symptoms and signs, and logistic regression analysis performed to evaluate factors associated with post-TB sequelae.
RESULTS: We enrolled 107 participants, of median age 6.3 years; 59% were female and 12% had Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection. Persistent respiratory symptoms were present in 29%; commonest being cough (21.5%). Abnormal respiratory signs were present in 51%; commonest being tachypnea (27%). Of 56 participants who did the 6MWT, 58% walked <70% of their expected distance. Overall, 57.0% (95% CI 47.1-66.5) had at least one while 33.6% (95% CI 23.8-41.6%) had two or more persistent symptoms and/or abnormal respiratory signs. Hospitalization at diagnosis (aOR 10.26 (1.76-59.79) and older age (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26) were independent predictors of PTLD.
CONCLUSION: A significant number of children and adolescents have persisting respiratory disease post-TB and it is more common among older children, and those with severe disease at TB diagnosis. There is need to institute routine assessment of children and adolescents at the end of TB treatment to identify those with sequelae, and provide post-TB care.

articles.title: High blood pressure among children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus in Uganda: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The coexistence of diabetes mellitus (DM) and hypertension (HTN) worsens the clinical outcomes of children with diabetes concerning both microvascular and macrovascular disease. It increases mortality risk by 5 times, with a higher risk of death in developing countries. Therefore, comprehensive care for patients with diabetes, including hypertension screening, must be provided.
METHODS: This multicenter health facility-based cross-sectional study included 150 children and adolescents aged from 6 months to 18 years with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) who were treated at Jinja Regional Referral Hospital (JRRH), Mbale Regional Referral Hospital (MRRH) and Lira Regional Referral Hospital (LRRH). Interviewer-administered questionnaires were used to obtain data, which were then analyzed according to the study objectives using STATA® version 18. High blood pressure diagnosis was based on blood pressure (BP) above or equal to the 90th percentile for <13 years and either systolic BP ≥ 120 mmHg or Diastolic BP ≥ 80mmhg for 13 years and older for age, sex and height. The prevalence of high BP was determined as a percentage, whereas associated factors were analyzed at both bivariate and multivariable logistic regression. The significance of associations was set at a p-value <0.05 and a 95% confidence interval.
RESULTS: Of the 150 participants, 115 (76.7%) were above 12 years of age, and the median age was 15 years (IQR 13-17). There were more females [81/150 (54%)] than males. The majority were attending school [130/150 (86.7%)], with a few attending boarding school [26/130 (20%)]. Sixty-one participants (40.7%, 95% C.I 33%-49%) had high BP, and 53 (86.9%) of these patients had poor glycemic control. The factors associated with high BP among T1DM participants included having diabetes for 4-8 years (aOR= 2.23 [95% CI: 1.05-4.75]; p = 0.037), and 9-12 years (aOR= 4.545 [95% CI: 1.075-19.221]; p = 0.040) respectively compared to those less than 4 years. Additionally, having Poor glycemic control (HBA1C ≥ 7%) increased odds for high BP by 2.905 [95% CI: 1.149-7.342]; p = 0.024) times compared to their counterparts with good glycemic control.
CONCLUSION: There was a high prevalence of high blood pressure among children with type 1 diabetes. Factors associated with high blood pressure included disease duration of more than 4 years and poor glycemic control.

articles.title: Co-developing a women-centered HIV prevention intervention to reduce stigma, increase HIV self-testing, and improve pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake in Ghana (WISE WOMAN): A study protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Young women in Ghana (18-35 years) remain disproportionately affected by HIV due to intersecting structural and social challenges, including stigma, gendered power dynamics, and limited access to women-centered prevention services. Although HIV self-testing (HIVST) and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) are effective biomedical prevention strategies, uptake among young Ghanaian women remains low. Barriers include limited awareness, persistent stigma, and a lack of culturally relevant, youth-responsive prevention approaches. The WISE WOMAN study aims to address these gaps by developing and piloting a women-centered HIV prevention intervention co-created with young women in Ghana.
METHODS: This protocol describes a pilot implementation study of a women-centered HIV prevention intervention that will be delivered via WhatsApp. The intervention is informed by community-based participatory research and human-centered design approaches to enhance cultural relevance and responsiveness to young women's lived experiences. The study will enroll 50 young women aged 18-35 years who will participate in a four-week WhatsApp-based intervention designed to increase HIV prevention knowledge, reduce stigma, and support engagement with HIVST and PrEP. Implementation outcomes, including feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness, will be assessed using mixed methods. Quantitative data will be collected through baseline and post-intervention surveys, including the PIERS-22 engagement scale, and will be analyzed using descriptive statistics and paired comparisons. Qualitative data from group interactions and post-intervention interviews will be analyzed using thematic analysis. The study has received ethical approval from the University at Buffalo Institutional Review Board (STUDY00009328) and the Ensign Global College Ethics Committee (IRB/EL/AF-02/2025) and is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07003789).
DISCUSSION: This protocol outlines the design and methods for a digitally delivered, women-centered HIV prevention intervention grounded in participatory approaches. The planned pilot study will generate critical implementation evidence on the feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness of a WhatsApp-based, co-designed intervention, informing future adaptation, scale-up, and integration of culturally grounded HIV prevention strategies for young women in Ghana and similar settings.

articles.title: Visuo-spatial perception deficit in ophthalmological disorders: Visual field extent matters.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Persons with Visual Impairment (VI) are more at risk to be without academic qualification. This is classically attributed to limited access to visual information, considered difficult due to reduced visual acuity. However, in some cases, visual acuity is preserved but visual field is reduced. Given the importance of visuo-spatial skills in learning, we assessed the accuracy of perceptual visuo-spatial judgements relative to visual field extent and visual acuity to question their respective contribution to the functional repercussions in VI.
METHODS: 97 patients were administered the elementary visuo-spatial perception (EVSP) test during their clinical assessment. We put a focus on two diseases of our sample: Retinitis Pigmentosa (N = 19) and Albinism (N = 18), with mainly restriction of visual field extent in the former, and visual acuity loss in the latter. In addition, we investigated the correlation between the visuo-spatial performance and these two distinctive factors of VI in the whole sample.
RESULTS: The results indicated higher prevalence of visuo-spatial perception deficit in the whole sample of VI compared to typically developing individuals. Even if most pathologies affect both peripheral and central vision, which makes it complicated to fully disentangle between these two factors, the focus on the Retinitis Pigmentosa and the Albinism groups suggested that visuo-spatial perception is less impacted by a low visual acuity than by peripheral visual field restriction. Additionally, we found that visuospatial perception performance was significantly correlated with visual field extent and not with visual acuity in the whole sample.
CONCLUSIONS: Visual field extent matters for visuo-spatial processing and probably for academic achievement. Further investigations are needed to understand how impaired visuo-spatial perceptual skills may explain academic difficulties in VI.

articles.title: Regional variation in adolescent births and associations with adverse perinatal outcomes in Georgia: A birth registry-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Georgia, approximately 2,700 (5.8%) adolescents give birth every year. Adolescent births are a public health concern due to an increased risk of various adverse maternal and newborn outcomes. We aimed to evaluate the regional variation of adolescent births and also the associations between maternal age and preterm birth (PB), neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission, and perinatal death (PD) in Georgia.
METHODS: The study population included all childbirths in women aged <30 years between 2017 and 2022, comprising 173,238 women and their 175,213 newborns. We used three age groups: adolescents aged <18, and 18-19 years, and adults aged 20-29 years (reference group). Logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the associations between maternal age and PB, NICU admission, and PD. Population attributable fractions and absolute numbers of the selected adverse outcomes attributable to adolescent births were estimated.
RESULTS: The adolescent birth rate (ABR) was 22.2 per 1000 adolescents in Georgia in 2022. Most of the adolescents aged <20 years lived in the regions of Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti, and Imereti with an ABR of 70.3 per 1000, 35.3 per 1000, and 26.4 per 1000, respectively.
