Hyperpigmentation and scarring were common sequelae of acne, while treatment adherence and antibiotic resistance, particularly to erythromycin and azithromycin, were noted as key challenges. Procedural interventions, including chemical peels, lasers, and comedone extraction, were increasingly used in early acne management, especially in patients prone to post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation and relapse. Low-dose isotretinoin and hormonal therapies were commonly used in acne management, while dermocosmetics were utilized as monotherapy in mild cases and as maintenance therapy following treatment in more severe cases. Lifestyle factors such as high glycaemic diets, whey protein, multivitamins, and steroid-like drugs were identified as potential contributors to acne exacerbation.
LIMITATIONS: Findings are based on a small expert panel convened with industry support and reflect clinical opinion rather than primary patient data.
CONCLUSION: Procedural interventions are becoming more popular, thereby providing an opportunity to incorporate dermocosmetics into acne treatment regimens.

articles.title: Managing environmental enteropathy among Egyptian infants and children with growth faltering.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Environmental enteropathy (EE) is an acquired subclinical inflammation of the small bowel mucosa, leading to reduced nutrient absorption and increased intestinal permeability. There are currently no universally accepted protocols for the diagnosis and treatment of EE.
OBJECTIVE: The primary aim of this clinical trial was to assess the prevalence of EE among children with faltering growth (FG). Determination of the dietary requirements in pediatric FG with EE and highlighting the histopathologic changes in the small intestine in such conditions were the secondary objectives.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: The current study recruited 200 patients (their age range was 6-58 months) diagnosed as GF at the Pediatric Clinical Nutrition Clinic, Children`s Hospital, Faculty of Medicine, Ain Shams University (Cairo, Egypt), during the period from April 2022 till June 2023. The first phase of the study was a cross sectional interventional one where all patients underwent nutritional rehabilitation using diet regimen including polymeric milk formula. Patients whose weight z score was still below - 2 SD for age and sex after 12 weeks were considered as non-responders and were enrolled in the second phase, when esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) and mucosal biopsies were done. In the latter phase, patients with EE received nutritional rehabilitation regimen using peptide-based milk formula with assessment of anthropometric measurements after 8 weeks of follow up.
RESULTS: Out of the studied cases, 170 were responders, and 30 were non-responders, 24 of the non-responders underwent EGD with biopsies and all were diagnosed as EE with prevalence of 12% among the studied patients with GF as the least possible prevalence. Total histology scores of the EE fell between those of the controls and celiac disease reference samples with cut off values > 3 and ≤ 14 for EE, ≤ 3 for controls and > 14 for celiac disease. There was a significant increase in weight and height z scores among patients of EE on peptide-based formula compared to polymeric formula.
CONCLUSION: EE isn`t uncommon and should be suspected when provision of catch-up nutrients can`t correct FG. Peptide-based formula has a possible beneficial effect on growth of patients with EE.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The clinical trial was registered at Protocol Registration and Results System with number NCT06497907 (12/07/2024).

articles.title: Transabdominal ultrasound as a radiation-free tool for objective assessment of faecal burden in children with constipation and colorectal disorders.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the utility of transabdominal ultrasound in children with colorectal pathology (anorectal malformation, functional constipation and Hirschsprung's disease) to assess the outcome of bowel management. Collect data to calculate age-dependent cut-offs of the transrectal diameter (TRD) in children with faecal load.
METHODS: Prospective cohort study with subgrouping for a-/symptomatic patients and a healthy control group. Derived control group for adjusting sex-ratio in patients with Hirschsprung's disease (4:1 ratio for male to female). 380 patients during a 31-month period were included. The transrectal diameter was measured routinely during the bowel management program after 1/3/6 months. Treatment options were oral laxatives, transanal irrigation or combination of both. For calculation of an age-dependent TRD cut-off, receiver operating characteristic, linear regression and locally estimated scatterplot smoothing were determined. The cut-off value was chosen based on a positive likelihood ratio > 10. Diagnostic accuracy was evaluated by the area under the curve, sensitivity and specificity.
RESULTS: In the symptomatic subgroups of all cohorts the median values of TRD were significantly elevated compared to asymptomatic subgroups or control groups (p < 0.001). Successful bowel management had a large to very large effect on the TRD (Cohen's d = 1.05 - 1.81) and mean values were significantly lower (p = 0.015 - 0.001). TRD and age showed a minor association with a non-linear positive trend without significant influence after age stratification. Receiver operating characteristics determined a collective cut-off for all cohorts of 2.985 cm in children ≥ 1 year old (positive likelihood ratio = 36.09; sensitivity = 81.92 %; specificity = 97.73 %; area under the curve = 0.91 (95%-CI 0.87 - 0.94); accuracy = 88.67 %).
CONCLUSIONS: Measuring the TRD is a radiation-free alternative method to assess faecal loading and monitoring response to bowel management in patients with colorectal pathology. TRD was consistently increased in symptomatic patients and decreased following successful treatment. Diagnostic thresholds were close to 3 cm across all cohorts, with good diagnostic performance. This study extends patient cohorts for transabdominal ultrasound and supports further multicentre validation of a standardized ultrasound protocol.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: The Utility of systemic immune-inflammation index and Systemic inflammation response index in differentiating acute appendicitis from other causes of pediatric abdominal pain.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of our study is to evaluate the diagnostic value of newly identified inflammatory markers in differentiating acute appendicitis from other abdominal pain causes in pediatric patients.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included pediatric patients under 18 presenting to the emergency department with abdominal pain between January 2020 and August 2024. Patients were categorized into two groups: acute appendicitis (Group 2) and non-appendicitis-related abdominal pain (Group 1). Demographic data, clinical presentation, and inflammatory markers such as neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), pan-immune inflammation value (PIV), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), were recorded for analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 135 patients were included in this study (group 1: 100, group 2: 35). Group 2 had a significantly higher mean age (10.5 ± 4.5 vs. 7.6 ± 3.6 years, p < 0.001). Inflammatory indices were significantly elevated in Group 2 compared to Group 1, including median NLR (5.18 vs. 1.78, p < 0.001), PIV (1232 vs. 353, p = 0.001), SII (1743 vs. 528, p < 0.001), and SIRI (4.41 vs. 1.09, p < 0.001). For diagnosis, SIRI (cut-off > 2.56) demonstrated 80% sensitivity, 71% specificity, and an AUC of 0.772, while NLR (> 4) showed 69% sensitivity and 79% specificity. In multivariate logistic regression analysis, only Age > 11 years (OR = 5.45, 95% CI: 1.9-15.5, p = 0.001) and SIRI > 2.56 (OR = 10.8, 95% CI: 1.5-76.5, p = 0.017) remained as significant independent predictors for acute appendicitis.
CONCLUSIONS: These markers, combined with clinical findings, can significantly enhance early diagnostic triage in the emergency department. Specifically, the high negative predictive value of SIRI suggests a strong rule-out utility, supporting safe and effective clinical decision-making regardless of whether the subsequent treatment pathway is operative or non-operative.

articles.title: Analysis of adverse reactions to low-dose dexamethasone in bronchopulmonary dysplasia of extremely premature infants: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) represents a prevalent complication among extremely premature infants. Nonetheless, the optimal dosage, treatment duration, and safety profile of dexamethasone require further validation through clinical research. This study investigates the efficacy and safety of low-dose dexamethasone intervention for BPD in extremely preterm infants and establishes an evidence-based foundation for monitoring adverse drug reactions within this population.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 68 cases of extremely preterm infants between March 2016 and January 2024. Among them, 41 cases received dexamethasone treatment (dexamethasone group) while 27 cases did not (control group). The control group received standard respiratory support, nutritional support, anti-infection measures, and other conventional treatments, whereas the dexamethasone group received low-dose dexamethasone in addition to standard care. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint of severe BPD or in-hospital death. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed adjusting for gestational age, birth weight, and respiratory severity score (RSS). The study compared the extubation success rate, severe BPD incidence, and adverse reactions between the two groups.
RESULTS: After adjustment for gestational age, birth weight, and RSS, dexamethasone was associated with lower odds of the composite endpoint of severe BPD or death (adjusted OR = 0.26, 95%CI 0.09-0.55, P = 0.003) and severe BPD among survivors (adjusted OR = 0.27, 95%CI 0.10-0.59, P = 0.005), and higher odds of extubation success (adjusted OR = 2.88, 95%CI 1.20-7.57, P = 0.024). Hyperglycaemia occurred more frequently in the dexamethasone group (41.5% vs. 18.5%, adjusted OR = 2.04, 95%CI 0.82-4.97, P = 0.121), although the difference did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, low-dose dexamethasone was associated with lower odds of severe BPD or death and higher odds of extubation success after adjustment for gestational age, birth weight, and respiratory severity. Clinically relevant increases in adverse events, particularly hyperglycaemia, cannot be excluded given the limited sample size. Long-term growth was not assessed. These findings require validation in larger multicenter prospective studies.

articles.title: Population-specific genetic variants and related health outcomes in a cohort of Inuit children in Nunavut.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Like all populations, Inuit children experience rare genetic conditions. Awareness of the unique Inuit genetic architecture allows the identification of specific variants associated with autosomal recessive conditions affecting child health across the Arctic. As a priority, the impact of the IFNAR2 c.157T>C variant causing IFNAR2 Deficiency, DNAH11 c.4095+2C>A causing Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia, and SI c.273_274delAG causing Congenital Sucrase-Isomaltase Deficiency (CSID), along with other disease-causing variants were assessed to determine the potential health outcomes on infant and child health in Nunavut.
METHODS: With the direction of Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated and the Government of Nunavut Department of Health a research group was established utilizing local and national expertise. Newborn dried screening blood spots of a 4-year cohort of infants born to residents of Nunavut between January 1st, 2010, and December 31st, 2013, were genotyped (n=2947) followed by linkage of a subset of the cohort to a database with demographic and health information collected from records spanning from birth to 5 years (n=2206 Inuit children). Live birth prevalence (LBP) of cases and carrier frequencies were first estimated for the full cohort and recalculated for the subset with linked data. Health visit information was reviewed for phenotype features consistent with the conditions of interest. In addition, baseline characteristics, and health visits for CSID cases were compared to those without the variant.
RESULTS: LBP of cases due to homozygosity of the DNAH11, IFNAR2 and SI variants were 1/1474, 1/737 and 1/28; carrier frequency was 1/13, 1/18 and 1/4, respectively. Four children with IFNAR2, one with DNAH11, and 83 with SI homozygosity were linked to health data, confirming phenotypes consistent with the conditions. CSID was associated with significant increased health care utilization for gastrointestinal illness visits before age two (OR=1.9, 95% CI 1.2-3.0). However, breastfeeding for up to six months was found to be protective, with a reduced number of health care visits (OR=0.80, 95% CI 0.63-1.0).
CONCLUSION: We describe the presence and health impact of three autosomal recessive conditions in a Canadian Inuit population. Genetic testing, practitioner education, and Inuit-informed management strategies are urgently needed to address these conditions and improve outcomes.

articles.title: Analysis of the current quality of life and influencing factors among primary caregivers of children with cerebral palsy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the current quality of life among primary caregivers of children with cerebral palsy (CP) and analyze its influencing factors, providing reference for developing relevant clinical interventions.
METHODS: Using convenience sampling, 116 pairs of children with CP and their primary caregivers who visited the Pediatric Rehabilitation Department of Zunyi First People's Hospital between February 2024 and February 2025 were enrolled. Data collection involved questionnaires on general information, the SF-36 Health Survey, Zarit Burden of Care Inventory (ZBI), and Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS). Univariate analysis and multiple linear regression were used to identify factors influencing caregivers' quality of life.
RESULTS: The primary caregivers' physical health subscale score was 239.22 ± 68.54, and the mental health subscale score was 247.29 ± 63.06. The child's impact of motor impairment, number of hospitalizations, family monthly income, proportion of out-of-pocket medical expenses relative to total household income, caregiving burden, and social support were factors influencing the physical health of primary caregivers. The child's gender, impact of motor impairment, and number of hospitalizations; the primary caregiver's gender, age, employment status, level of knowledge about the condition, monthly household income, proportion of out-of-pocket medical expenses relative to total household income, caregiving burden, and social support were factors influencing the mental health of primary caregivers of children with CP (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: The quality of life among primary caregivers of children with CP was not optimistic, generally falling at a low-to-moderate level. The caregiving burden was moderate, and the level of social support was low. Healthcare professionals and relevant social departments should implement measures to prioritize the physical and mental health of primary caregivers. Further research is needed to evaluate the effectiveness of comprehensive interventions-including education about CP, psychological support, financial assistance, caregiving skills training, and social support services-in alleviating caregiving burdens, enhancing quality of life, and ultimately improving rehabilitation outcomes for children with CP and overall family well-being.

articles.title: The potential of microRNA-1180-3p as a biomarker for severe childhood pneumonia and its targeting of KANSL1.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe pneumonia in children is a serious threat to life and health, and there is an urgent need to explore efficient biomarkers. MicroRNA-1180-3p (miR-1180-3p) has been reported to be upregulated in community-acquired pneumonia and is involved in inflammatory and immune regulation. Therefore, this study selected this molecule to investigate its diagnostic value and underlying mechanism.
METHODS: The study consisted of clinical investigations and in vitro mechanistic studies. In the clinical part, the study included 83 children with mild pneumonia and 53 children with severe pneumonia. The expression level of miR-1180-3p in serum was detected by quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR). The diagnostic efficacy and associated factors were analyzed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and logistic regression analysis. In the mechanistic part, the regulation of cell viability and inflammatory factors (TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β) was verified using a lipopolysaccharide (LPS) induced A549 cell model. The target gene, KANSL1, was verified using a luciferase reporter assay.
RESULTS: The serum expression of miR-1180-3p in the severe pneumonia group was significantly increased, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.862, a sensitivity of 75.47%, and a specificity of 84.34%. Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that miR-1180-3p (OR = 4.323, 95% CI: 1.594-11.729) was independently associated with severe pneumonia, with a positive correlation observed with inflammatory markers such as white blood cell (WBC), neutrophils, procalcitonin (PCT), and C-reactive protein (CRP). In cellular models, inhibiting miR-1180-3p reversed the decrease in cell viability and elevation of inflammatory factors induced by LPS, and these effects were partially mediated through the downregulation of KANSL1.
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that miR-1180-3p represents a promising candidate biomarker for severe pneumonia in children; however, validation in larger prospective cohorts is required. In vitro experiments suggest that miR-1180-3p may modulate inflammatory responses through KANSL1 in LPS-induced cell model. Further research is needed to elucidate the downstream signaling pathways involved and to confirm the in vivo relevance of these findings.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of intrapleural alteplase in pediatric empyema: real-world data from a tertiary center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric empyema remains an important complication of pneumonia and is associated with considerable morbidity. Although intrapleural fibrinolytic therapy is increasingly used, the optimal management approach remains controversial.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical outcomes and treatment success of intrapleural alteplase in children with empyema in a real-world clinical setting.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 84 children diagnosed with empyema between November 2022 and December 2024. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, microbiological, and radiological data were collected. Patients were managed either conservatively with antibiotics alone or with invasive interventions, including pleural drainage with or without intrapleural fibrinolytic therapy.
RESULTS: The median age was 5.6 years (IQR: 3.85-9.39 years), and 58.3% of patients were male. Fever (86.9%), cough (78.6%), and dyspnea (50%) were the most common presenting symptoms. Intrapleural alteplase was administered to 61 patients (92.4% of those requiring drainage), with a clinical success rate of 95% [61/64 invasive patients]. Surgical intervention was required in only three patients. No major complications were observed. The median hospital stay was 15 days (IQR: 12.25-20; range: 5-33 days), and 15.4% of patients required pediatric intensive care.
CONCLUSIONS: Chest drainage combined with intrapleural alteplase appeared to be a safe and feasible treatment approach for pediatric empyema in our real-world cohort. However, prospective multicenter studies are needed to further clarify its role in relation to alternative treatment strategies.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of initial and serial C-reactive protein in late preterm infants with suspected late-onset sepsis in a tertiary NICU in Pakistan.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: C-reactive protein (CRP) is widely used as adjunct biomarker in neonatal sepsis evaluations. Its reported diagnostic performance varies considerably across settings, and performance in infants born preterm remains inconsistent.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of the Aga Khan University Hospital. Medical records of preterm neonates with clinical suspicion of bacterial late-onset sepsis (LOS) who underwent blood culture and CRP testing were reviewed. Only records with blood culture results and initial CRP measurements (obtained at presentation to the NICU during evaluation for suspected LOS) and serial CRP measurements (taken at 24-48 h of admission) were considered for this analysis. Sensitivity, specificity, positive/negative predictive values (PPV/NPV), likelihood ratios, and area under the curve (AUC) for CRP ≥ 10 mg/L at both timepoints were calculated.
RESULTS: Of the 300 preterm infant records screened between January 2020 and December 2022 with clinical suspicion of LOS, 293 had blood culture, initial CRP and serial CRP recordings. Two blood culture results were positive for fungal organisms and were excluded from the analysis set. Out of 291, 105 (36.1%) infants had bacterial culture-proven sepsis. Initial CRP showed sensitivity of 97.1%(91.9%-99.4%), specificity 10.2% (6.3%-15.5%), PPV 37.9% (32.1%-44%) and NPV 86.4% (65.1%-97.1%). Serial CRP showed sensitivity 94.3% (88.0%-97.9%), specificity 23.1% (17.3%-29.8%), PPV 40.9% (34.7%-47.4%) and NPV 87.8% (75.2%-95.4%). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.68 (0.61-0.74) for initial CRP and 0.67 (0.61-0.73) for serial CRP measurements.
CONCLUSION: Initial and serial CRP demonstrated high sensitivity but poor specificity for bacterial culture-confirmed LOS. CRP should therefore be interpreted as an adjunct to, rather than a substitute for, clinical assessment and microbiological investigations in late preterm infants with suspected bacterial LOS.

articles.title: Clinicopathological characteristics and short-term follow-up outcomes of IgA vasculitis nephritis in pediatric and adult patients: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare the clinical manifestations, laboratory findings, renal pathological features, immune complex deposition patterns, and short-term follow-up outcomes between pediatric and adult patients with IgA vasculitis nephritis (IgAVN).
METHODS: A retrospective review of 441 biopsy-confirmed IgAVN patients was conducted. Patients were divided into pediatric (age < 18 years, n = 305) and adult (age ≥ 18 years, n = 136) groups. General demographic data, clinical classification, laboratory parameters, pathological grades (glomerular and tubulointerstitial), immune complex deposition patterns, and short-term follow-up outcomes were collected and compared between the two groups.
RESULTS: Significant differences were found in sex distribution, time from IgAVN to kidney biopsy, and clinical classification. The adult group had higher levels of urea (BUN), creatinine (Cr), uric acid (UA), fibrinogen (FIB), IgG, IgA, C3, and C4, whereas the pediatric group had higher prothrombin time (PT), thrombin time (TT), D-dimer (DD), and fibrin degradation product (FDPs) levels. The degree of glomerular pathological injury and chronic tubulointerstitial injury were significantly more severe in the adult group than in the pediatric group, whereas no statistically significant difference was observed in the overall distribution of acute tubulointerstitial injury or immune complex deposition patterns. Prognosis was worse in the adult group.
CONCLUSION: Adult patients showed a greater burden of chronic histopathological lesions and a less favorable distribution of short-term outcome categories than pediatric patients. These differences were associated with age group but may also reflect differences in biopsy timing, baseline kidney function, and treatment exposure.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Asthma-like respiratory phenotype and acute complications among hospitalized children with sickle cell disease: a multicenter matched case-control study in French Guiana.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with sickle cell disease (SCD) are at high risk of acute complications, particularly acute chest syndrome (ACS) and stroke. Asthma and asthma-like respiratory phenotypes are frequently reported in this population and may contribute to increased morbidity. However, available data remain heterogeneous, especially in tropical settings where diagnostic approaches and healthcare access differ.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective matched case-control analysis within a multicenter hospital-based cohort between 2012 and 2022 in the three public hospitals of French Guiana. Children aged 6 months to 17 years with SCD who had been hospitalized for at least one acute complication were included. Cases were defined by a clinically diagnosed asthma-like respiratory phenotype documented during routine pediatric follow-up. Each case was matched with four controls without this phenotype by age and sex. Associations with selected clinical complications and healthcare-utilization markers were assessed using classical logistic regression and complementary Bayesian logistic regression models to account for small sample sizes and complete separation.
RESULTS: Among 390 hospitalized children with major SCD, 35 had an asthma-like respiratory phenotype, corresponding to a prevalence of 9.0% (95% CI 6.1-11.8). In univariate analyses, this phenotype was associated with increased hospitalizations, higher ferritin levels, irregular follow-up, stroke, and was strongly associated with ACS. In Bayesian multivariable analysis, the strongest associations were observed with ACS and the frequency of hospitalizations. No independent association with stroke was detected after adjustment.
CONCLUSION: In this hospital-based multicenter cohort of children with sickle cell disease, the asthma-like respiratory phenotype was relatively uncommon. Rather than indicating a causal relationship, this phenotype appeared to identify a subgroup of hospitalized children with greater acute morbidity and healthcare needs. Pragmatic respiratory screening may help clinicians detect children requiring closer respiratory and hematological follow-up, particularly in geographically dispersed and resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Sleep problem profiles, hyperactivity-inattention, and psychosocial health among high-altitude preschool children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep is closely related to children's behavioral regulation and psychosocial functioning, yet preschool sleep is multidimensional and may vary substantially between children. High-altitude residence provides a distinctive ecological context for studying sleep. However, little is known about heterogeneity in measured sleep characteristics among preschool children living at high altitude, or how such heterogeneity relates to behavioral and psychosocial adjustment. This study identified sleep-problem profiles among high-altitude preschool children and examined their associations with hyperactivity-inattention, psychosocial health, and other adjustment outcomes.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 244 preschool children from Lhasa, Xizang, China (approximately 3,650 m). Caregiver-reported sleep indicators included six sleep-problem dimensions and weekday and weekend sleep duration. Latent profile analysis identified sleep-problem profiles. Multivariable logistic regression examined correlates of profile membership. Profile differences in behavioral difficulties, health-related quality of life, and academic achievement were examined. Hierarchical regression was further used to examine whether hyperactivity-inattention was associated with psychosocial health after accounting for sleep-profile membership and covariates.
FINDINGS: Two sleep-problem profiles were identified: a lower sleep-problem profile and a higher sleep-problem profile. Being an only child was associated with higher odds of membership in the higher sleep-problem profile, whereas daily screen time was not significantly associated with profile membership. Compared with children in the lower sleep-problem profile, those in the higher sleep-problem profile showed higher hyperactivity-inattention and lower psychosocial health. No significant profile differences were found for physical health or academic achievement. In hierarchical regression, hyperactivity-inattention was negatively associated with psychosocial health, and the association between sleep-profile membership and psychosocial health was attenuated but remained significant after hyperactivity-inattention was included.
CONCLUSION: Two profiles differing primarily in overall sleep-problem severity were identified among high-altitude preschool children. The higher sleep-problem profile was associated with poorer behavioral and psychosocial adjustment but not with concurrent academic achievement. Hyperactivity-inattention may be an important behavioral correlate of poorer psychosocial functioning among children with higher sleep problems.

articles.title: Validation of neonatal early warning score in medical and surgically critically ill newborns in tertiary care center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal Early Warning Scores (NEWS) are widely used to identify children at risk of clinical deterioration, but their performance may vary across clinical settings and patient populations.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort from a tertiary university hospital, we evaluated the discriminative ability of an institutional NEWS at admission to predict need for intensive care treatment, intubation, and tiered outcomes (ward care, ongoing intensive care requirement, death) in medical and surgical patients. ROC ( Receiver operating characteristic) analyses were performed for the full cohort and for medical and surgical subgroups. AUCs ( Area under the curve) were calculated, and optimal cut-offs determined via the Youden index. Subgroup comparisons used a bootstrap-based DeLong test and Mann-Whitney U test.
RESULTS: The study included 229 patients (158 medical, 71 surgical). In the full cohort, NEWS showed acceptable to good discrimination for intubation (AUC 0.75) and for higher-acuity clinical outcomes (intensive treatment vs. death, AUC 0.80; ward care vs. death, AUC 0.85) at an optimal cut-off near 8 points. In medical patients, AUCs ranged 0.72-0.77 depending on the outcome. In surgical patients, AUCs for intubation and mortality-related contrasts ranged from 0.80 to 0.94. Score distributions differed significantly between cohorts (p = 0.027).
CONCLUSIONS: Admission NEWS demonstrated acceptable to excellent performance for predicting intubation and higher-acuity clinical outcomes, especially mortality in surgical patients. Its utility for predicting hospitalisation or non-fatal escalation was limited. NEWS should be integrated into structured early-warning pathways and calibrated to local case mix and workflows, with cohort-specific thresholds.

articles.title: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia in Sub-Saharan Africa: a scoping review of presentation, management strategies, and outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is a developmental defect of the diaphragm that allows abdominal organs to herniate into the thorax, resulting in pulmonary hypoplasia and pulmonary hypertension. Despite morbidity and mortality associated with CDH, the available evidence has not been comprehensively synthesized in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). This scoping review mapped the clinical presentation, management, and outcomes of CDH in SSA.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, African Journals Online, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2011 and March 2026. Eligible studies reported the clinical presentation, management, or outcomes of CDH in SSA and were in English or French. Findings were synthesized narratively, and study quality was appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklists for case reports and case series.
RESULTS: Sixteen studies comprising 55 children from nine SSA countries were included. No patients were reported to have received a prenatal diagnosis. Age at presentation ranged from birth to 8 years. Bochdalek hernia was the predominant type (44/55); 35 (63.6%) defects were left-sided, 12 (21.8%) were right-sided, 2 (3.6%) were midline or central, and laterality was unspecified for the remainder (6, 10.9%). Respiratory symptoms were the most frequently reported presenting features, although gastrointestinal symptoms were also described. Plain chest or thoracoabdominal radiography was the most commonly reported initial imaging modality. Surgical repair was reported in 14 studies, most commonly by open abdominal repair; thoracotomy was used for an intrapericardial hernia, and one South African series reported laparoscopic repair of Morgagni hernia. Mortality was reported in four studies, with deaths concentrated in severe neonatal presentations. Postoperative outcomes were favourable, but follow-up beyond discharge was inconsistently reported and, where available, ranged from 2 weeks to 3 years.
CONCLUSION: Although the evidence base is small and fragmented, this review suggests favorable outcomes for CDH in SSA. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the likelihood of under-reporting. Future multicenter studies with longer follow-up are needed to better characterize CDH in the region.

articles.title: Comparison of YASHMA and Thompson scores for predicting short-term outcomes in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perinatal asphyxia occurs as a result of disruption in placental blood flow or gas exchange immediately before, during, or shortly after birth. Consequently, several scoring systems have been developed to to assess disease severity and predict prognosis in affected infants. The aim of this study was to compare the Thompson score and the Yieldly and Scorable Holistic Measuring of Asphyxia (YASHMA) score in predicting short-term prognosis in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE).
METHODOLOGY: This retrospective observational study included 80 infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) with a diagnosis of HIE between January 1, 2024, and December 31, 2025. Infants were classified according to the Sarnat&Sarnat classification. The study population was divided into the groups-mild-HIE and moderate-to-severe HIE-and the data were compared between groups.
RESULTS: A total of 80 neonates with HIE were evaluated, including 37 with mild and 43 with moderate-to-severe HIE. Gestational age was similar between groups, whereas birth weight was significantly lower in the moderate-to-severe group. These infants also had significantly lower Apgar scores, higher cesarean delivery rates, more abnormal aEEG patterns, and longer hospital stays. Thompson and YASHMA scores were significantly higher and strongly correlated. Metabolic markers indicated more severe acidosis and higher lactate, LDH, and troponin levels in moderate-to-severe HIE. Both scores demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance in identifying disease severity and predicting short-term clinical outcomes. Although the Thompson score showed numerically higher diagnostic accuracy, the overall performance of the two scoring systems was comparable.
CONCLUSION: Both the Thompson and YASHMA scoring systems are effective tools for assessing disease severity and predicting short-term outcomes in newborns with HIE. While both the Thompson and YASHMA scores demonstrated comparable overall diagnostic and prognostic performance, the Thompson score showed numerically higher diagnostic accuracy, whereas the YASHMA score provided a more balanced sensitivity-specificity profile and may serve as a complementary tool in clinical practice.

articles.title: Environmental risk factors in Juvenile dermatomyositis: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) is a rare autoimmune vasculopathy of childhood. Alongside genetic predisposition, environmental exposures are thought to influence when the disease begins and how it progresses. Despite many reports, the evidence base is fragmented, with few studies able to draw firm conclusions.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review according to PRISMA 2020 standards, searching six major databases and conference proceedings (2005-2025). Eligible studies investigated environmental, infectious, chemical, physical, lifestyle, or psychosocial exposures in children with JDM. Two reviewers independently screened articles, extracted data, and assessed study quality using NIH and ROBINS-E tools. Results were summarized by exposure type.
RESULTS: One hundred forty-eight studies were included. Ultraviolet (UV) radiation was the most consistently reported factor, with recent sun exposure often preceding onset or chronic disease, particularly in defined autoantibody subgroups. Infections, especially viral and respiratory, were frequently described as triggers of onset or relapse. Air pollutants and maternal exposures during pregnancy also emerged as significant risks. Psychosocial stress, including early adversity and pandemic-related distress, was linked to flares. By contrast, structured exercise, particularly aquatic therapy, improved fitness and fatigue without worsening disease.
CONCLUSIONS: Multiple modifiable environmental influences appear relevant in JDM. Strategies such as UV protection, minimizing pollutant exposure, and tailored exercise may benefit patients. Well-designed, prospective studies are urgently needed to clarify causal pathways and inform prevention.
PROSPERO: Registration number: CRD42024595442PROSPERO.

articles.title: Expression and mechanism exploration of miR-483-5p in children with IgA vasculitis with nephritis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: IgA vasculitis with nephritis (IgAVN) represents the most serious renal complication in pediatric patients with IgA vasculitis (IgAV).
AIMS: To characterize miR‑483‑5p expression in pediatric IgAVN patients, evaluate its potential as a diagnostic biomarker, and elucidate underlying molecular mechanisms.
METHODS: A total of 150 children with IgAV (55 with IgAVN, 95 with non‑IgAVN) and 60 age‑ and gender‑matched healthy controls were enrolled in this retrospective clinical study. RT-qPCR was used to detect miR-483-5p and HDAC4 mRNA expression. ROC curve analysis was conducted to assess its tentative auxiliary screening capacity for IgAV-associated renal injury. Pearson correlation analysis was used to analyze the correlation between miR-483-5p expression and clinical indicators. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify factors independently associated IgAVN. Human glomerular mesangial cells (HGMCs) were treated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to construct cell model.
RESULTS: miR-483-5p was markedly downregulated in the serum and renal tissues of children with IgAVN, and serum miR-483-5p exhibited significant discriminative capacity to distinguish children with concurrent IgAVN from IgAV patients without renal involvement in this retrospective cohort. MiR-483-5p expression was negatively correlated with renal function indicators, serum IgA and inflammatory factors, and its low expression was an independently associated factor for IgAVN. In vitro, LPS downregulated miR-483-5p, promoted HGMC proliferation and inflammatory response. MiR-483-5p directly targeted and negatively regulated HDAC4. Overexpression of miR-483-5p inhibited LPS-induced HGMC proliferation and inflammatory factor secretion, while HDAC4 overexpression reversed these effects.
CONCLUSIONS: miR‑483‑5p is downregulated in children with IgAVN and may serve as a potential non‑invasive auxiliary indicator for pediatric IgAVN. miR‑483‑5p attenuates LPS‑induced HGMC proliferation and inflammation by targeting HDAC4 in vitro; however, the in vivo mechanistic relevance and clinical utility remain preliminary and require further validation.

articles.title: Analysis of early-onset sepsis and antibiotic exposure among very preterm infants: a multicenter retrospective study (2022-2024).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-onset sepsis (EOS) is a major threat to very preterm infants (VPIs) (< 32 weeks gestation), with high incidence and mortality rates. Atypical clinical symptoms lead to widespread empiric antibiotic administration and subsequent excessive antimicrobial exposure. Real-world data on antibiotic consumption and inter-hospital variation among these infants are limited. Based on multicenter retrospective data, this study aimed to describe the current profile of EOS-associated antibiotic use and explore practice discrepancies across hospitals in a regional Chinese cohort.
METHODS: A multicenter retrospective observational study was performed using data from the Shenzhen Neonatal Network spanning 2022 to 2024, enrolling VPIs admitted to six NICUs. Collected variables included demographic information, EOS incidence, antibiotic utilization indicators (initiation rate, treatment duration, standardized antibiotic exposure), and clinical outcomes. Descriptive statistics were applied for data summarization, and Spearman's rank correlation was calculated at the hospital level to preliminarily explore the association between antibiotic exposure and EOS incidence. Given the limited number of participating centers, correlation findings were interpreted descriptively only.
RESULTS: A total of 1202 VPIs were enrolled, of whom 91.9% received early antibiotics within 3 postnatal days with a median antibiotic course of 7 days. The overall EOS incidence was 15.5% (95% CI: 13.5-17.6), and the ratio of early antibiotic recipients to confirmed EOS cases was 5.9:1, varying markedly across hospitals (range: 4.2-12.9). Considerable inter-hospital heterogeneity was observed across key indicators: early antibiotic initiation rate (83.5% - 100%), antibiotic continuation rate (54.9% - 100%), and standardized antibiotic exposure (5374-11738 antibiotic-days per 1000 VPIs). Hospital-level Spearman's correlation revealed no statistically significant association between antibiotic exposure and EOS incidence (r s = 0.058, P = 0.913).
CONCLUSIONS: Findings from this regional cohort show relatively high early antibiotic exposure among VPIs that appears mismatched to the actual EOS burden, with substantial inter-hospital heterogeneity in prescribing. This pattern may align with inconsistent, non-standardized antibiotic management for EOS across centres. Our descriptive data characterise real-world antimicrobial use and offer preliminary evidence and testable hypotheses to inform future prospective research and the design of risk-stratified, individualized antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) strategies.

articles.title: The effect of educational intervention using a multimedia package in the prevention of sexual abuse in preschool children on knowledge and attitude of mothers: a quasi-experimental study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preschool children are particularly vulnerable to child sexual abuse. Mothers, as primary caregivers, play a key role in protecting children from sexual abuse through appropriate knowledge and preventive practices. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a multimedia educational intervention on mothers' knowledge and attitudes regarding the prevention of CSA among preschool children.
METHODS: This quasi-experimental educational study included 84 mothers of preschool children who were recruited through multistage cluster sampling from five comprehensive health service centers in Rasht, Iran. Participants were allocated to intervention and control groups. Data were collected at baseline, two weeks after the intervention, and four weeks after the intervention. Mothers in the intervention group received a six-week multimedia educational program delivered via DVD and reinforced through weekly educational reminders sent via social media, whereas the control group received routine care only during the study period. Mothers completed researcher-developed knowledge and attitude questionnaires at all three assessment points.
RESULTS: At baseline, there were no significant differences between the intervention and control groups in knowledge (P = 0.157) or attitude (P = 0.444). Following the intervention, the mean knowledge score in the intervention group increased from 26.19 ± 3.47 at baseline to 32.07 ± 2.18 at two weeks and remained significantly higher (30.83 ± 2.58) at four weeks. The mean attitude score also increased from 125.62 ± 10.81 at baseline to 135.88 ± 10.20 at two weeks and 132.45 ± 10.75 at four weeks. Compared with the control group, knowledge scores were significantly higher at two weeks (P < 0.001) and four weeks (P < 0.001). Likewise, attitude scores were significantly higher at two weeks (P < 0.001) and four weeks (P = 0.013).
CONCLUSION: The multimedia educational intervention significantly improved mothers' knowledge and attitudes regarding the prevention of child sexual abuse among preschool children. These findings suggest that culturally adapted multimedia education may provide an effective and accessible approach for strengthening parental education and supporting community-based child sexual abuse prevention programs.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a home-based nutritional intervention program on anthropometric indices of preschool children with overweight and obesity: a cluster randomized controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a critical global health concern. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a home-based nutritional intervention informed by behavioral theory on anthropometric indices of overweight and obese preschool children in Urmia, Iran.
METHODS: In this cluster randomized controlled trial, 260 children (aged 2-5 years, body mass index (BMI) z-score ≥ + 2) and their mothers from 10 health centers were allocated to either an intervention or a control group. The intervention group received a six-month, multi-component program featuring nutritional education, locally adapted low-calorie recipes, and behavioral counseling informed by the Health Belief Model (HBM) delivered during bi-monthly home visits. The primary outcomes were changes in body weight, BMI, BMI z-score, and waist circumference. Dietary changes were assessed using the Modified Youth Healthy Eating Index (MYHEI). Intervention effects were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models accounting for the clustered study design.
RESULTS: Adjusted intention-to-treat analyses using linear mixed-effects models demonstrated significantly greater improvements in the intervention group for weight (p = 0.006), BMI (p = 0.002), BMI z-score (p = 0.004), and waist circumference (p < 0.001) compared with the control group. The total MYHEI score and several key component scores also improved significantly in the intervention group compared with controls (p < 0.05 for all).
CONCLUSION: A home-based, multi-component nutritional intervention informed by behavioral theory and cultural adaptation was effective in improving anthropometric measures and diet quality in overweight and obese preschool children.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered on 2023-11-08 with registration number IRCT20090124001580N8.

articles.title: Epidemiology and economic burden of diagnosed congenital cytomegalovirus disease in France during the first 2 years of life: a retrospective data analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) is the leading infectious cause of birth defects. Recent estimates on cCMV prevalence and burden in France have been scarce. This study assessed the epidemiology, healthcare resource utilization (HRU), direct costs, and cCMV-related clinical outcomes among infants with diagnosed cCMV in France.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis used data from the French National Health Data System (2015-2023). Birth prevalence of diagnosed cCMV was estimated from 2015 to 2023. To assess cCMV burden, infants with a first diagnosis (index date) of cCMV/CMV within 1 month of birth (cases) were matched 1:1 to non-cCMV controls (index date selected randomly among all claims within 1 month of birth) on birth year, sex, region of residence, and index year. All-cause HRU, direct costs (2023 euro [€]), and clinical outcomes were summarized over the first 2 years of life (observation period).
RESULTS: The prevalence of diagnosed cCMV within 1 month of birth peaked in 2020 and 2023, at 35.04 and 34.77 per 100,000, respectively. The cCMV burden analysis included 1,434 matched pairs of diagnosed cCMV cases and non-cCMV controls. At birth admission, cases had significantly longer hospital stay (mean: 24.6 vs. 6.4 days) and higher costs (mean [median]: €18,759 [€3,804] vs. €3,529 [€1,136]) than controls (both p < 0.001). During the observation period, diagnosed cCMV cases had higher mean number of medical visits than controls (Year 1: 33.7 vs. 18.9; Year 2: 22.6 vs. 12.5), and more cases than controls had ≥ 1 inpatient admission (Year 1: 47.4% vs. 20.3%; Year 2: 25.9% vs. 14.6%) (all p < 0.001). Diagnosed cCMV cases incurred significantly higher direct costs (mean [median] in Year 1: €3,726 [€1,301] vs. €1,870 [€473]; Year 2: €1,759 [€453] vs. €1,019 [€254]) and experienced more potentially cCMV-related sequelae (45.7% vs. 8.4%) than controls (all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: In France, birth prevalence of diagnosed cCMV trended upward from 2015 to 2023. Infants diagnosed with cCMV had higher HRU and costs, driven by inpatient care, and experienced worse clinical outcomes during the first 2 years of life compared with non-cCMV controls. These results underscore the need for increased early screening of cCMV to mitigate its associated burden.

articles.title: Trends and patterns of low birth weight and fetal macrosomia in a tertiary hospital, Northern Ethiopia, 2012-2021: multinomial modeling approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low birth weight (LBW) and fetal macrosomia represent critical extremes of the birth weight spectrum, posing substantial public health challenges in low- and middle-income countries. Although traditionally studied in isolation, these outcomes share underlying systemic factors that warrant simultaneous evaluation. Evidence examining their joint distribution, temporal trends, and shared determinants within the same population remains sparse. To address this gap, this study investigated the in-hospital prevalence, trends, and associated factors of both conditions using a multinomial modeling approach at a tertiary hospital in Northern Ethiopia.
METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted using delivery register data from Ayder Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, encompassing 24,709 live births with complete birth weight records between January 2012 and August 2021. Temporal trends were visualized using line graphs, while a multinomial logistic regression model was employed to identify factors correlated with LBW and fetal macrosomia, with results reported as Relative Risk Ratios (RRR) and corresponding 95% Confidence Intervals (CI).
RESULTS: The in-hospital prevalence was 12.55% (95% CI: 12.14%-12.97%) for LBW and 6.82% (95% CI: 6.51%-7.14%) for fetal macrosomia. LBW was significantly associated with female infant sex (RRR = 1.16; 95% CI: 1.06-1.27), instrumental delivery (RRR = 0.80; 95% CI: 0.69-0.92), obstetric complications (RRR = 2.90; 95% CI: 2.49-3.37), higher parity (RRR = 13.27; 95% CI: 11.51-15.29), and low APGAR scores (RRR = 4.54; 95% CI: 3.89-5.31). Conversely, fetal macrosomia was linked to high-risk maternal age (RRR = 1.34; 95% CI: 1.12-1.61), female infant sex (RRR = 0.64; 95% CI: 0.57-0.72), spontaneous vaginal delivery (RRR = 0.47; 95% CI: 0.42-0.52), instrumental delivery (RRR = 0.23; 95% CI: 0.19-0.28), higher parity (RRR = 0.04; 95% CI: 0.01-0.17), low APGAR scores (RRR = 0.63; 95% CI: 0.44-0.91), and maternal HIV positivity (RRR = 0.40; 95% CI: 0.25-0.64).
CONCLUSION: The study demonstrates a notable burden of both LBW and fetal macrosomia over the decade. These findings emphasize the necessity for targeted clinical interventions, enhanced intrapartum monitoring, and specialized care for high-risk cohorts-such as mothers with obstetric complications and HIV-positive women-to mitigate adverse birth outcomes.

articles.title: A machine-learning-derived online prediction model for coronary artery aneurysm risk in children with kawasaki disease: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery aneurysm (CAA) is the most serious complication of Kawasaki disease (KD) and is associated with long-term cardiovascular morbidity. Early identification of children at high risk of CAA remains challenging. We aimed to develop and temporally validate a machine learning-based prediction model for individualized CAA risk assessment in children with KD.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 1,930 children diagnosed with KD at The Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University between January 2018 and March 2025 were included. Among them, 1,378 patients diagnosed between January 2018 and December 2023 constituted the development cohort and were randomly divided into a training set and an internal test set. A further 552 patients diagnosed between January 2024 and March 2025 were used as an independent temporal validation cohort. Forty-two demographic, clinical, laboratory, and composite biomarker variables were initially considered. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection after preprocessing. Ten machine-learning algorithms were developed and compared. The model was designed to be applied after the initial IVIG response had been determined. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Model interpretability was assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP).
RESULTS: 12 predictors were retained in the final model, including age, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) resistance, IVIG administration time, oral mucosal changes, albumin, hematocrit, platelet count, prothrombin time, D-dimer, NT-proBNP, prognostic nutritional index, and C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio. Among the ten algorithms, the Random Forest model showed the best overall performance, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.899 (95% CI, 0.870-0.928) in the internal test set and 0.847 (95% CI, 0.812-0.882) in the temporal validation cohort. Calibration and decision curve analyses indicated good agreement and clinical utility.
CONCLUSION: We developed and temporally validated a machine-learning model for predicting CAA risk in children with KD. The model has been deployed as an online tool to support early risk stratification. Further prospective multicenter validation is needed before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes of Kielland's rotational forceps-assisted vaginal births in a tertiary care center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rates of second-stage Cesarean section (CS) have increased substantially, contributing to higher maternal morbidity and long-term risks in future pregnancies, including repeat CS and placenta accreta spectrum. Reducing unnecessary second-stage CS is therefore an important goal in modern obstetric care. Fetal malposition, particularly occiput transverse and posterior positions, is a key cause of labor dystocia and operative delivery. While several interventions exist, their success is variable. Kielland's rotational forceps can facilitate vaginal birth and potentially avoid CS, but their use has declined due to safety concerns and limited training, leaving a gap in contemporary evidence comparing outcomes with other delivery methods.
OBJECTIVE: To compare maternal and neonatal outcomes between rotational and nonrotational forceps use in a tertiary care setting.
STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of all forceps-assisted births at a tertiary care hospital in Toronto, between January 2014 and December 2021. Maternal outcomes included postpartum hemorrhage defined as estimated blood loss of 500 mL or more, and significant obstetric anal sphincter injuries defined as 3B, 3C and fourth degree perineal lacerations. Neonatal outcomes included Apgar scores, cord blood gases, need for resuscitation, and neonatal head trauma.
RESULTS: Among 1606 forceps-assisted births, 26 (1.6%) required Kielland's rotational forceps. Episiotomy was universal in the rotational group (n=26/26, 100%) compared with 90.1% (n=1423/1580) in the nonrotational group. Significant OASIS occurred less frequently with rotational forceps (7.6%, n=2/26 vs 10.8%, n=172/1580), while rates of PPH were comparable (26.9%, n=7/26 vs 28.8%, n=456/1580). No major PPH (≥1000 mL) or shoulder dystocia occurred in the rotational group. Low 1-minute Apgar scores (<7) were more common in the rotational group (26.9%, n=7/26 vs 14%, n=227/1580), but all infants achieved scores ≥7 at 5 minutes. No cases of cephalohematoma, subgaleal hematoma, or intracranial hemorrhage occurred in the rotational group.
CONCLUSION: Kielland's rotational forceps are a safe alternative to second-stage CS when performed by experienced operators. Their use was not associated with excess major maternal morbidity or significant neonatal trauma, in comparison to nonrotational forceps. Our data support efforts to transfer these skills to trainees and larger studies are needed to confirm these single institution findings.

articles.title: Improved nutritional status but frequently elevated serum vitamin A in children with cystic fibrosis following elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor: a prospective single-centre study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with cystic fibrosis (CF) have historically required high-energy diets and nutritional supplementation because of malabsorption and elevated energy demands. Although elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) improves these parameters, it may also increase the risk of nutritional excess. Prospective data integrating dietary intake and pancreatic function are scarce. We evaluated the impact of ETI on these parameters in children with CF.
METHODS: This prospective single-centre study assessed 29 children with CF (median age 12.0 years, IQR 8.1-14.0) before and after ETI initiation. Outcomes included body mass index (BMI) Z-scores, dietitian-assessed total energy intake (TEI) and macronutrient intake, fat-soluble vitamins, pancreatic function, and adherence to unchanged vitamin supplementation (medication possession ratio, MPR).
RESULTS: BMI Z-scores increased (median -0.73 to -0.19; p = 0.002) despite declining TEI (79.1 ± 25.9 to 66.8 ± 22.2 kcal/kg; p = 0.036). Vitamin A rose from 1.15 (IQR 0.99-1.48) to 1.48 μmol/L (IQR 1.25-1.90; p < 0.001), while 25-hydroxyvitamin D and vitamin E were unchanged. Vitamin A exceeded the age-specific reference range in 9/29 children (31%) after ETI, versus none before (p = 0.004); these children tended to be younger (median 9.3 vs 12.1 years; p = 0.077). MPR was unchanged (median 0.59 vs 0.67; p = 0.864). All children remained pancreatic insufficient, with unchanged enzyme dose.
CONCLUSIONS: ETI improved nutritional status and increased vitamin A levels despite reduced relative energy intake and persistent pancreatic insufficiency, suggesting it may reduce the elevated energy requirements characteristic of CF. With supplementation and adherence unchanged, nearly one-third of children, particularly younger ones, developed elevated serum vitamin A, supporting routine monitoring as ETI is prescribed at younger ages.

articles.title: Dietary inflammatory index and continuous glucose monitoring metrics in children with cystic fibrosis: An exploratory cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with cystic fibrosis (CF) experience chronic inflammation and early glucose abnormalities. Whether dietary inflammatory potential is associated with glycemic outcomes in pediatric CF remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To examine associations of the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) with continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics and systemic inflammatory markers in children with CF.
METHODS: This exploratory cross-sectional study included 24 clinically stable children with CF aged 6-18 years who were not receiving CFTR modulator therapy. DII scores were calculated from three non-consecutive 24-h dietary recalls. CGM-derived outcomes included mean glucose, time in range (TIR), time above range (TAR), glucose variability, and glucose management indicator (GMI). Inflammatory markers were measured using ELISA. Associations were examined using multivariable regression adjusted for age and sex.
RESULTS: After adjustment for age and sex, higher DII scores were associated with higher mean glucose (β = 0.512, p = 0.021), GMI (β = 0.583, p = 0.011), and TAR (β = 0.466, p = 0.044). The inverse association with TIR was not statistically significant (β = -0.421, p = 0.070). DII was also positively associated with log-CRP (β = 0.528, p = 0.037), whereas other inflammatory markers were not significantly associated with DII.
CONCLUSION: Higher dietary inflammatory potential was associated with greater glycemic exposure and CRP in children with CF. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in larger longitudinal studies, including CFTR modulator-treated cohorts.

articles.title: Pediatric Sleep Disorders: Early Identification and Management Strategies.
articles.abstract: This review highlights pediatric sleep disorders that can be identified early and treated effectively, emphasizing their impact on child health and quality of life. Key conditions discussed include obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), restless legs syndrome (RLS), sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy (SHE), and narcolepsy. This article discusses epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentations, diagnostic approaches, complications and evidence-based treatments for each disorder. OSA is associated with neurocgnitive abd cardiovascular consequences, while RLS is strongly linked to low iron stores (ferritin). SHE requires prompt recognition to reduce seizure burden, and narcolepsy often presents atypically in children, causing diagnostic delays and significant psychosocial impact..

articles.title: Genetics and pathophysiology of syndromic versus nonsyndromic primary vesicoureteral reflux: an update.
articles.abstract: Vesicoureteral reflux (VUR), among the most common urinary tract anomalies in children, can lead to long-term sequelae. The hereditary nature of VUR has long been known. Syndromic VUR is one of numerous congenital syndromes associated with specific disrupted genes and related anomalies extending beyond kidney manifestations. However, its occurrence is rare, and isolated nonsyndromic primary VUR is much more common. Recent improvements in genetic testing have enabled the identification of possible causative genes in the development of VUR. However, mild nondilating VUR can be a normal developmental variant that resolves spontaneously in most cases as a child grows and his/her bladder wall develops. In isolated cases of nonsyndromic VUR, genetic variants are usually subtle and difficult to identify as pathogenic, making this field of research vague and uncertain. This review aims to provide a comprehensive update on the genetics of VUR, including genes associated with syndromic and isolated VUR development that have emerged in recent studies, and encourage further research by associating specific genetic variations with VUR development, kidney parenchymal damage, and longterm sequelae.

articles.title: Persistent left ventricular systolic dysfunction at ≥6 months after SARS-CoV-2-associated MIS-C: a systematic review and rare-event meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with SARS-CoV-2 frequently involves acute myocardial dysfunction. However, the prevalence of persistent left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction at longer-term follow-up remains uncertain. We therefore performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the prevalence of persistent LV systolic dysfunction at ≥6 months after MIS-C.
METHODS: We included observational cohort studies reporting longitudinal echocardiographic follow-up in children and adolescents aged <21 years with SARS-CoV-2-associated MIS-C. The prespecified primary outcome was persistent LV systolic dysfunction, defined as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 55% at ≥6 months. Study-level events and denominators were extracted and harmonized using the number of children who underwent ≥6-month echocardiography as the endpoint-specific denominator. Pooled prevalence was estimated using an intercept-only binomial logistic-normal generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) fitted directly to study-level event counts and denominators without continuity correction. The originally prespecified random-effects logit model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals, together with alternative continuity corrections and transformation-based approaches, was retained as sensitivity analysis under sparse-event conditions.
RESULTS: Ten cohorts met the inclusion criteria and contributed to quantitative synthesis, comprising 432 children with echocardiography at ≥6 months. Persistent LV systolic dysfunction occurred in 3 children, corresponding to a crude observed proportion of 0.69% (3/432). In the revised primary continuity-correction-free binomial logistic-normal GLMM, the pooled prevalence was 0.69% (95% CI, 0.22%-2.13%). Given that only three events were observed, this model-based estimate should not be interpreted as a precise estimate of the underlying population prevalence. Continuity-corrected sensitivity models yielded pooled estimates from 1.62% to 2.23%, further demonstrating numerical sensitivity to the treatment of zero-event cohorts.
CONCLUSION: Persistent LV systolic dysfunction was infrequently observed among children with MIS-C reassessed by echocardiography at ≥6 months. However, only three events were identified, so the available evidence is insufficient to determine the exact population prevalence with precision. Inference is further limited by heterogeneous follow-up and potential selection bias from nonuniform late imaging. Larger prospective cohorts with standardized long-term surveillance are needed.

articles.title: Restrictive lung function defined by body plethysmography is common in children with Fontan palliation and functionally relevant.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary dysfunction is common in single ventricle (SV) patients with Fontan circulation, yet the prevalence and clinical relevance of true restrictive lung disease remain poorly characterized as most studies relied on spirometry alone. This study comprehensively assessed lung function using spirometry and body plethysmography, examined its relationship with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived lung volumes, evaluated its impact on exercise capacity, and identified clinical correlates of restrictive physiology.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-centre study, 31 children and adolescents with Fontan circulation underwent spirometry, body plethysmography, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET), and CMR. Restrictive lung function was defined by reduced (<LLN) total lung capacity (TLC). Lung function, CMR findings, exercise performance, and clinical characteristics were compared between patients with and without restrictive physiology.
RESULTS: Restrictive lung function was identified in n = 8 (26%) participants. TLC correlated strongly with CMR-derived total lung volume (r = 0.889, p < 0.001). Patients with restrictive physiology demonstrated significantly reduced exercise capacity, including lower peak oxygen uptake, tidal volume, and minute ventilation, with reduced breathing reserve and higher peak respiratory rate, indicating clinically relevant ventilatory limitation. Restrictive physiology was associated with lower ventricular ejection fraction and impaired global circumferential strain. In multivariable analysis, TLC was the strongest predictor of peak oxygen uptake.
CONCLUSIONS: Restrictive lung physiology confirmed by body plethysmography is common in children and adolescents with Fontan circulation and associates with impaired exercise performance and reduced ventricular function. Comprehensive pulmonary function testing including body plethysmography may be considered in routine follow-up to identify patients at increased risk of adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Exercise Test Findings in the Long-Term Outcomes After Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MUSIC) Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) commonly presents with cardiovascular involvement, but the frequency of exercise-related arrhythmias and exercise capacity are poorly defined.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to describe exercise stress testing (EST) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) after MIS-C.
METHODS: We summarized EST and CPET results from the MUSIC (Long-terM OUtcomes after the Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome In Children) study (1,204 participants, 32 North American sites). Demographics and details of hospitalization from participants undergoing clinical EST were compared to participants ≥5 years who did not undergo EST. Site reported results of EST and CPET were described.
RESULTS: EST was performed in 22% (208/932) at a mean of 150 ± 110 days after hospitalization. Compared with those who did not undergo EST (n = 724), the EST cohort was older (12.2 vs 10.5 years) and had higher rates of intensive care unit admission (77.4% vs 63.8%), vasoactive infusions (57.2% vs 46.1%), troponin elevation (64.4% vs 51.0%), and coronary artery aneurysm (22.7% vs 0.4%) (all P ≤ 0.01). During EST, only 1% (2/208; 95% CI: 0.1%-3.4%) exhibited premature ventricular contractions and no sustained ectopy. Among 160 participants undergoing CPET, 75.6% (121/160; 95% CI: 68.2%-82.1%) achieved oxygen consumption/kg ≥ 80% predicted, and 83.8% (134/160; 95% CI: 77.1%-89.1%) achieved an oxygen pulse ≥80% predicted.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing exercise testing after MIS-C, most had normal exercise capacity, no sustained arrhythmias occurred, and premature ventricular contractions were rare.

articles.title: Evidence-based expert consensus on long-acting injectable antipsychotics for bipolar disorder: Recommendations from the TSBPN.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop evidence-based expert consensus recommendations from the Taiwanese Society of Biological Psychiatry and Neuropsychopharmacology (TSBPN) on the use of long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics in bipolar disorder.
METHODS: An eight-member working group and 12-member scientific committee formed a 20-member expert panel. A narrative review of MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and EMBASE from inception through February 2026 prioritized bipolar-specific evidence and incorporated relevant indirect evidence when necessary. Fourteen statements were graded using the World Federation of Societies of Biological Psychiatry framework for level of evidence (LoE) and acceptability. After expert review and revision, 18 panelists completed anonymous voting to determine the Taiwan recommendation grade (RG-T) and level of agreement.
RESULTS: The 14 statements covered LAI selection, clinical role, timing of initiation, special populations, and safety monitoring. Strong RG-T 1 recommendations supported prioritizing locally approved agents, individualized shared decision-making, use during mania as part of an acute-to-maintenance strategy, maintenance monotherapy or combination treatment, management of suspected nonadherence, earlier use in recurrent illness, use in patients with frequent manic episodes or comorbid substance use disorder, prevention of manic-spectrum recurrence, and combination with established bipolar-depression treatments when clinically indicated. RG-T 2 recommendations addressed older adults, children and adolescents, pregnancy, breastfeeding, and metabolic monitoring. Agreement ranged from 72.2% to 100%. Evidence was strongest for maintenance and manic-spectrum recurrence, but more limited for bipolar depression and several special populations.
CONCLUSION: This TSBPN consensus integrates available evidence with expert judgment to support individualized LAI use across bipolar-disorder treatment settings while highlighting areas requiring further research.

articles.title: Personal and environmental factors associated with allergic disorders among adolescents in Lusaka, Zambia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between wheezing, allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema and selected environmental, lifestyle and personal factors among school-going adolescents aged 13–14 years.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional study.
SETTING: Participants were enrolled from schools in Lusaka, Zambia.
PARTICIPANTS: Adolescents aged 13–14 years attending urban schools.
PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOMES: Three primary outcomes including symptoms of asthma (wheeze), rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema were determined using the International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood–Global Asthma Network questionnaire. Multivariate mixed effect logistic regression models were used to assess the association between selected exposure variables and each outcome. The study was reviewed and approved by the Levy Mwanawasa Medical University Research Ethics Committee (ref: LMMU-REC 00003/21) and the Zambian National Health Research Authority (ref: NHRA 0000001/23/03/2022). The Ministry of Education, headquarters in Lusaka, gave permission to access the schools (ref: MOE/101/1/45). All participants assented while their guardians consented.
RESULTS: The prevalence of symptoms of asthma (current wheeze), allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema was 13.6%, 11.8% and 6.5%, respectively. In mixed-effect multivariable analysis, exposure to environmental pollutants including smoke from cigarettes, vehicle emissions, use of charcoal and pet exposure as well as lifestyle factors such as physical activity and frequent paracetamol intake were significantly associated with all the outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: This study indicates a significant burden of allergic diseases among adolescents in this population. Additionally, the study reveals an association between these symptoms and modifiable environmental, lifestyle and personal factors. Although further studies are needed to elucidate the observed associations, the findings highlight the potential benefit of reduced exposure to indoor and outdoor air pollutants, promotion of healthier lifestyle choices among adolescents and encouraging cautious use of paracetamol

articles.title: An observational study protocol characterising pain trajectories, opioid use and predictors of chronic postsurgical pain in children with cerebral palsy undergoing orthopaedic surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Children with cerebral palsy (CP) are likely at greater risk for developing chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) due to their high prevalence of pre-existing pain and frequency of orthopaedic procedures. However, little is known about the prevalence, trajectories and risk factors of CPSP or persistent opioid use among children with CP undergoing orthopaedic surgery. Understanding CPSP and patterns of postoperative opioid use in this population is crucial to optimise perioperative pain management, inform opioid stewardship practices, improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare use and costs.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This multi-site, prospective, longitudinal study aims to recruit 450 children aged 5–17 years with CP undergoing orthopaedic surgery. Participants will complete study assessments from 1 month before surgery to 12 months postoperatively. Study measures include preoperative quantitative sensory testing; caregiver-reported and child-reported (for participants ≥8 years who are cognitively able) assessments of pain and psychosocial factors at five time points; real-time postoperative text message assessments of pain and opioid use; and postoperative gait laboratory measures of functional outcomes. Demographic and surgical, and clinical data, including medical history, inpatient postoperative pain scores and analgesic medication use, will be extracted from the electronic medical record. Analysis will (1) characterise the postoperative pain and opioid use trajectories, (2) identify predictors of CPSP and persistent opioid use and (3) examine relationships between perioperative pain severity and the functional mobility outcomes achieved via orthopaedic surgery.
ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Central and local Institutional Review Boards at each site have approved the study. Study results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journal publications and presentations at scientific conferences.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05764681.

articles.title: Efficacy of the consumption of traditional rice compared with that of normal rice in reducing obesity among children aged 10-14 years attending the paediatric endocrine clinic at Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children, Sri Lanka: a study protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Childhood obesity is an emerging global public health concern, with a growing prevalence in Sri Lanka. Dietary management and physical activities play a vital role in the management and prevention of childhood obesity, as effective treatments for this metabolic risk are scarce. Sri Lankan traditional rice varieties, which are known for their low glycaemic index (GI) contributed by high amylose and resistant starch (RS), may offer potential benefits in reducing obesity. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of the consumption of traditional low-GI rice in reducing obesity among children.
METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a single-centre, parallel-group, superiority design, single-blinded, randomised controlled trial. The study population will include children aged between 10 and 14 years who are diagnosed with obesity (body mass index (BMI) over the 95th centile for age and sex (BMI between +2 SD and +3 SD)) and who are registered in the paediatric endocrine unit at the Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children, Colombo, Sri Lanka. Eighty children will be randomised into either the intervention group (consuming traditional rice as one main meal for 5 days per week for 6 months) or the control group (continuing their usual diet with normal rice) via covariate adaptive randomisation balanced for age and sex.
