Demographic and clinical data including maternal age, gestational week, height, weight, body mass index, basal body temperature, intra-labor temperature, number of cervical examinations, duration of the first and second stages of labor, neonatal 1-minute and 5-minute Apgar scores, cesarean section rate, instrumental delivery rate, neonatal transfer, and mechanical ventilation were recorded. The overall incidence of intrapartum fever was higher in the elevated IL-6 group, and mean maternal temperature was also higher at 3 and 9 hours after analgesia (P < .05). No significant differences were observed in other indices (P > .05). Elevated baseline IL-6 was associated with a higher unadjusted incidence of intrapartum fever among women receiving epidural labor analgesia.

articles.title: The trends and hotspots of research on polycystic ovary syndrome in adolescents over the past three decades: A bibliometric analysis from 1995 to 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine and metabolic disorder affecting women, with increasing research attention directed toward adolescent populations. However, no comprehensive bibliometric analysis has systematically mapped the research landscape in this subspecialty. This study aimed to evaluate global research trends and hotspots in adolescent PCOS over the past 3 decades using bibliometric methods.
METHODS: Publications on adolescent PCOS from 1995 to 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer and Citespace were employed for data analysis and visualization, while key bibliometric indicators were computed and presented in tabular form.
RESULTS: A total of 1070 publications were included. Research output steadily increased over time, with the United States (n = 384, 35.89%), Turkey (n = 105, 9.81%), and India (n = 82, 7.66%) being the most productive countries. The most prominent institutions included the University of Pittsburgh, the University of Barcelona, and Monash University. Ibanez, Lourdes (n = 34) was the most prolific author, while the Journal of Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology (n = 84) and the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism (highest citations, n = 6921) were the leading publication platforms. Core research areas encompassed mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment, metabolism, and clinical outcomes. Keyword burst detection identified "diagnosis" (strength = 14.12) and "luteinizing hormone" (strength = 13.6) as the most intense hotspots. Notably, "quality of life" (2020-2024) and "depression" (2015-2024) emerged as the most recent and ongoing research frontiers.
CONCLUSION: This first bibliometric analysis of adolescent PCOS reveals growing global interest and active international collaborations in this field. Future research is expected to focus on refining diagnostic approaches and improving long-term quality of life for adolescent PCOS.

articles.title: Global research trends in asthma during pregnancy: A multidisciplinary bibliometric analysis utilizing multiple databases (2008-2024).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a common chronic disease that poses a double threat to both pregnant women and the health of their fetuses. This study introduces the method of bibliometric analysis to systematically review the current research status of asthma during pregnancy worldwide, aiming to comprehensively analyze its knowledge structure, evolution trends, and emerging research frontiers.
METHODS: The data are derived from the Web of Science Core Collection and the PubMed database, covering relevant literature on asthma during pregnancy. The time range is from 2008 to 2024. The search strategy combined asthma-related terms ("asthma" OR "bronchial asthma") with pregnancy-related terms ("pregnancy" OR "gestation" OR "gestational"). After screening, 4088 eligible publications were included in the bibliometric analysis. A separate search of PubMed identified 28 clinical trials for the supplementary analysis of clinical research progress. Bibliometric analyses and visualization were performed using the bibliometrix R package (developed by Massimo Aria and Corrado Cuccurullo, Department of Economics and Statistics, University of Naples Federico II [with an academic spin-off, K-Synth Srl, associated with its dissemination]), CiteSpace (developed by Chaomei Chen, College of Computing and Informatics, Drexel University), and VOSviewer (developed by Nees Jan van Eck and Ludo Waltman, Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Leiden University).
RESULTS: This study comprised 4088 publications focusing on asthma during pregnancy. Annual publication counts demonstrated a gradual increase with intermittent fluctuations. The United States dominated both in publication output and international collaboration. Litonjua AA, Bisgaard H, and Weiss ST demonstrated high centrality and citation influence among authors. The core contributing journals included Pediatric Allergy and Immunology and Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology. Major research focuses encompassed mechanistic exploration, influencing factors, and fetal and child health. Research hotspots were primarily concentrated on "air pollution," "birth cohort," "pregnancy complications," and "maternal diet." In recent years, emerging research frontiers have included "inflammation," "impact," "gut microbiota," "climate change," and "survivors." Clinical trial analysis highlighted nutritional interventions (particularly vitamin D) and precision management using biomarkers like fractional exhaled nitric oxide as current research priorities.
CONCLUSION: This work examined the evolving trends and trajectories within pregnancy asthma research, offering a systematic roadmap for subsequent studies. The article highlighted the main contributors, research hotspots, emerging frontier topics, and key directions for future research. This study can serve as a crucial reference for researchers in this field and relevant stakeholders.

articles.title: Rehabilitation outcomes in children with physical and intellectual disabilities: a 50-year cohort study in Brazil.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Worldwide, an estimated 240-million children live with disabilities ‒ representing one-third of all people with disabilities and 1 in 10 children overall. Children with physical or intellectual disabilities experience diverse functional impairments and health complications that require appropriate rehabilitation. The objective of our study was to analyze rehabilitation outcomes for children with disabilities over 50-years.
METHODS: This cohort is based on medical records of patients aged 0 to 18-years with physical or intellectual disabilities who received outpatient rehabilitation at one outpatient rehabilitation center in Brazil from the 1970s to the 2020s.
RESULTS: Childhood disabilities (physical, intellectual, and multiple) have decreased over time, with boys showing a greater predisposition to all types. The primary cause was congenital, often related to events during the perinatal or neonatal developmental phase. Cerebral palsy with tetraplegia was the most common physical disability, while Down syndrome was the most prevalent intellectual disability. Both Rehabilitation Onset Age and Length of Stay in Rehabilitation have decreased over time. Furthermore, this study demonstrates that the age at which rehabilitation began also decreased.
DISCUSSION: The probability of dying by age five is ten times lower than the probability of living with a disability. Improvements in prenatal and neonatal care have played a significant role in reducing the incidence of childhood disabilities over time and have decreased the coexisting disabilities. The incidence of disabilities has decreased, but at the same time, their prevalence has increased, leading to a greater demand for rehabilitation services.
CONCLUSION: Providing access to rehabilitation and early referral are key to achieving the goals of stakeholders (health professionals, families, and patients), regardless of disability (physical or intellectual).

articles.title: Childhood Immunization Schedule for National Immunization Program Vaccines, China (Version 2026).
articles.abstract: In June 2026, the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration and the National Health Commission issued the Childhood Immunization Schedule for National Immunization Program Vaccines (Version 2026). Compared with the 2021 version, the key updates include optimization of the five-dose Diphtheria-Tetanus-acellular Pertussis vaccine schedule (with the first dose advanced to 2 months of age and the fifth dose administered at 6 years of age); inclusion of the bivalent human papillomavirus vaccine in the National Immunization Program as a two-dose series for girls aged 13 years (Table 1); and expanded and refined vaccination guidance for children with medical conditions, including preterm and low-birthweight infants, children with allergies, children born to mothers living with human immunodeficiency virus, children with immune function abnormalities, jaundice, common congenital diseases, or common neurological diseases, and children receiving blood products. This English translation provides a reference for public health professionals.

articles.title: Five-year outcomes after brace-free versus brace-based rehabilitation following isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft: long-term follow-up of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Postoperative knee bracing following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) remains common practice despite growing evidence questioning its clinical benefit. Previous studies demonstrated that brace-free rehabilitation was noninferior to brace-based rehabilitation one year after isolated ACLR using hamstring tendon autograft; however, its long-term effects remain unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate long-term effects five years after surgery.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients enrolled in a prospective randomized controlled trial conducted between 2016 and 2019 were recontacted approximately five years after isolated primary ACLR with hamstring tendon autograft for a long-term follow-up. In the original trial, 139 patients had been randomized to postoperative rehabilitation without a brace (n = 71) or with a functional knee brace (n = 68). Participants completed several patient-reported outcome measures. Furthermore, a standardized telephone interview was performed. Changes between the one-year and five-year follow-up were analyzed.
RESULTS: Ninety-seven patients participated in the long-term follow-up (n = 45 brace-free group, n = 52 brace group). Mean follow-up was 5.2 ± 1.0 years. No significant differences were observed between groups regarding subjective knee function, activity level, quality of life, rerupture rate, revision surgery, or persistent knee-related complaints at final follow-up. However, there was a significant interaction between treatment group and time for the subjective IKDC score. Patients treated without postoperative bracing showed stable or slightly improved subjective knee function, whereas patients treated with a brace demonstrated a significant decline between one and five years.
DISCUSSION: Brace-free rehabilitation after isolated ACL reconstruction with hamstring tendon autograft remains safe and effective more than five years after surgery. Postoperative bracing did not reduce rerupture rates, revision surgery, or long-term functional impairment. Instead, brace-free rehabilitation demonstrated a more favorable longitudinal development of subjective knee function. These findings further question the routine postoperative prescription of rehabilitative knee braces following isolated ACL reconstruction.

articles.title: Student perceptions of the School eHealth Education Program Pakistan (eSHEPP): a qualitative study of acceptability, feasibility, and awareness of non-communicable diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noncommunicable diseases are a leading cause of premature morbidity and mortality, and many associated risk behaviors emerge during adolescence. In Pakistan, school health education remains limited and largely lecture-based, leaving adolescents insufficiently equipped to adopt healthy behaviors. To address this gap, the School eHealth Education Program Pakistan, a multimedia and mobile application-supported intervention, was developed. This study explored secondary and higher secondary students' perceptions of the program's acceptability, feasibility, and perceived usefulness in improving awareness of noncommunicable diseases following implementation in school settings.
METHODS: A qualitative explanatory study was conducted in four schools in Karachi (two secondary and two higher secondary; two all-girls and two all-boys schools). The program was delivered over 8 weeks through six classroom sessions. Each 20-30-min session included a short dramatized video, followed by guided discussion and interactive quizzes facilitated by a trained facilitator and teacher representative. Twenty-seven students were purposively sampled to ensure variation by school type and gender. Data were collected through four focus group discussions conducted after the intervention using semi-structured guides in Urdu. Thematic analysis was performed using NVivo through a hybrid deductive-inductive approach.
RESULTS: Students described the program as acceptable and easy to understand, highlighting the engaging dramatized videos, clear language, and supportive subtitles. Participants reported increased awareness of noncommunicable diseases and related risk factors. Some students expressed intentions to make healthier dietary choices, increase physical activity, and discourage smoking among peers. The program was considered feasible within existing school schedules and required minimal technological or personnel resources. Students suggested expanding health topics, slightly extending session duration, and incorporating additional interactive features to enhance engagement.
CONCLUSIONS: The program showed strong acceptability, feasibility, and perceived educational value in under-resourced school settings. With improvements in interactivity and integration into school curricula supported by teachers and parents, it may provide a promising model for adolescent health education in similar contexts.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes After Dupilumab Initiation for Pediatric Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether dupilumab initiation is associated with reduced short-term flare burden, healthcare utilization, and surgical escalation in pediatric patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP).
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: TriNetX United States Collaborative Network.
METHODS: Patients aged ≤18 years with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps were identified between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Dupilumab-treated patients were indexed at treatment initiation and propensity score-matched 1:1 to nondupilumab controls indexed at a systemic corticosteroid burst based on asthma, atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, and prior endoscopic sinus surgery. Outcomes within 12 months were compared using risk ratios.
RESULTS: In 442 matched patients (221 per cohort), dupilumab-treated patients had lower rates of acute sinusitis (12/221 [5.4%] vs 31/221 [14.0%]; risk ratio [RR] 0.39; 95% CI: 0.20-0.73; P = .002), systemic corticosteroid bursts (80/221 [36.2%] vs 101/221 [45.7%]; RR 0.79; 95% CI: 0.63-0.99; P = .042), and functional endoscopic sinus surgery (19/221 [8.6%] vs 38/221 [17.2%]; RR 0.50; 95% CI: 0.30-0.84; P = .007). Nasal polyp diagnoses were more frequently documented in the dupilumab-treated cohort (148/221 [67.0%] vs 95/221 [43.0%]; P < .0001), while emergency department visits (16/221 [7.2%] vs 27/221 [12.2%]; P = .078) and inpatient admissions (12/221 [5.4%] vs 16/221 [7.2%]; P = .435) were similar between cohorts.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that dupilumab may be a steroid-sparing and surgery-sparing option in pediatric CRSwNP.

articles.title: Clinical and biochemical profile of c.703G>T p.(Glu235*): A novel pathogenic CYP27A1 variant of cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis.
articles.abstract: Cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis (CTX) is a rare autosomal recessive inherited disease of cholesterol metabolism caused by variants in the CYP27A1 gene, encoding the enzyme sterol-27-hydroxylase of the cytochrome P450 oxidase system. The resulting deficient conversion of cholesterol to bile acids leads to accumulation of intermediate products such as 5α-cholestane-3-β-ol (cholestanol) in body tissues. Patients exhibit prominent multisystemic involvement with phenotypic variability. Early diagnosis is essential for treatment response. Achilles tendon xanthomas are a hallmark of CTX but may present late in the disease course or, in rare cases, not at all. We report a 24-year-old man who was investigated for progressive gait disorder and profound muscle wasting since adolescence. The patient had a history of neonatal-onset chronic diarrhea, childhood osteoporosis and bone fractures, juvenile bilateral cataracts, recurrent nephrolithiasis, progressive cognitive decline, and major psychiatric disorder. Despite the absence of lipid accumulation in tendons and joints, the sequence of symptom presentation was highly suggestive of CTX. The serum levels of 27-hydroxycholesterol were below the limit of detection, whereas 7α-hydroxycholesterol and cholestanol levels were extremely elevated. We documented homozygous presence of the novel CYP27A1 c.703G>T p.(Glu235*) loss-of-function variant. Chenodeoxycholic acid initiation led to overall clinical improvement, including domains associated with significant resistance to treatment such as cognitive function and fine motor skills, along with normalization of cholestanol and intense suppression of 7α-hydroxycholesterol levels.

articles.title: Perspectives of healthcare workers and policy makers on severe neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia and kernicterus spectrum disorders in Northern Nigeria: A multicenter qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the perspectives of healthcare workers(HCWs) and institutional policymakers regarding severe neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia (SHB) and kernicterus spectrum disorder (KSD).
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a multicenter qualitative descriptive study across five tertiary referral hospitals in Nigeria. We conducted 20 key informant interviews with healthcare workers (HCWs) and institutional policymakers. Semi-structured interviews explored knowledge, clinical practices, barriers and facilitators, health system factors, and policy priorities related to neonatal jaundice/hyperbilirubinaemia and KSD prevention. We used a hybrid inductive-deductive thematic analysis approach and triangulated findings against the World Health Organization (WHO) health system building blocks framework.
RESULTS: Seven major themes were identified: (1) disease burden and recognition of SHB/KSD; (2) delayed presentation largely due to poor awareness and harmful cultural practices; (3) health system limitations in prompt management (staffing shortages, delayed bilirubin testing, blood product shortages, equipment failures); (4) ethical and sociocultural barriers to treatment; (5) hearing impairment as an under-recognized consequence; (6) long-term disability and rehabilitation gaps; and (7) prevention opportunities across the continuum of care. Participants described SHB as a common neonatal emergency and an important cause of neuro-disability, and also identified significant systemic failures and delayed care-seeking perceived to stem from cultural practices, poor referral pathways, inadequate rehabilitation services, and weak policy prioritization for newborn health.
CONCLUSION: Key stakeholders perceived neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia and KSD as preventable causes of neuro-disability in Northern Nigeria, highlighting several end-user and systemic factors perpetuating the high burden. We therefore recommend a coordinated health system strengthening approach, community education, reliable diagnostic/treatment infrastructure, and dedicated leadership engagement across the health system to impact the disease burden.

articles.title: Serum Serotonin and Noninvasive Portal Hypertension Indices in Relation to Esophageal Variceal Severity in Cirrhosis: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Esophageal varices are a life-threatening consequence of portal hypertension in liver cirrhosis, and upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, the reference standard for detecting them, is invasive and resource-intensive. Serum serotonin, over 90% of which is stored in circulating platelets, has been proposed as a candidate biochemical correlate of portal hypertensive and fibrotic change, but its relationship to variceal severity alongside established noninvasive indices has not been well characterized. This study aimed to determine the association of serum serotonin, Child-Pugh class, portal vein diameter, and platelet count to spleen diameter ratio (PSR) with endoscopically graded esophageal variceal severity in patients with liver cirrhosis, and to explore the diagnostic performance of these markers for identifying high-grade varices.
METHODS: In this exploratory cross-sectional study, 140 participants were enrolled into five prespecified groups of fixed size: non-hepatic controls (n = 40), cirrhosis without varices (n = 40), and grade 1 (n = 20), grade 2 (n = 20), and grade 3 (n = 20) esophageal varices confirmed endoscopically. Serum serotonin was measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Group comparisons used one-way ANOVA or the Kruskal-Wallis test according to the normality of model residuals, and the chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test for categorical variables. Spearman correlation and multivariable ordinal logistic regression identified independent predictors of variceal grade among the 60 participants with varices, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis assessed diagnostic performance for grade 2/3 varices among the 99 cirrhotic participants with complete data, with bootstrap correction of cutoff-based estimates for optimism and pairwise DeLong comparison of AUCs; a Firth-penalized model was fitted as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Serum serotonin rose progressively across groups, from 30.0 ± 5.6 ng/mL in controls to 106.5 ± 5.2 ng/mL in grade 3 varices (F = 347.575, P < 0.001), and was, together with portal vein diameter, an independent predictor of variceal grade after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio (OR) of 7.48 per 10 ng/mL, P = 0.0009; portal vein diameter adjusted OR of 1.70 per 0.1 mm, P = 0.0002; exploratory model, n = 59). Apparent areas under the curve (AUCs) for grade 2/3 varices were 0.944 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.895-0.980) for serotonin, 0.923 (0.864-0.974) for portal vein diameter, 0.764 for PSR, and 0.746 for Child-Pugh class; serotonin and portal vein diameter did not differ significantly (DeLong P = 0.553), whereas each exceeded PSR and Child-Pugh class (all P ≤ 0.004). Both associations persisted in the penalized model, and optimism correction changed the accuracy estimates only slightly.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, serum serotonin tracked with esophageal variceal severity and, alongside portal vein diameter, was independently associated with variceal grade, with discrimination comparable to that of portal vein diameter. Because the sample was enriched by design and cutoffs were derived and tested in the same cohort, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in unselected surveillance cohorts before clinical use.

articles.title: Epidemiology and Associated Risk Factors of Malaria Infection in Loka Abaya District, Sidama Region, Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite continuous efforts to manage malaria, it remains a deadly disease, particularly common in low-lying areas of Ethiopia. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to assess the prevalence, trends, and risk factors associated with malaria infection in Loka Abaya district, Sidama region, Ethiopia.
METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study was carried out using house-to-house visits from April to June 2023. A total of 186 febrile patients were chosen using systematic random sampling. Those above the age of 18 were included in the study. Five health facilities and one primary hospital in the district provided retrospective data. A systematic questionnaire and microscopic analysis of blood films were used to gather data. The blood samples were evaluated in Hantate primary hospital. Univariate and multivariate binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify the associated factors of malaria infection. Variables with p value less than 5% were considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Of 34,613 suspected patients tested for malaria over the previous 5 years, 26.2% were positive. The lowest rate recorded at 20.3% in 2018, whereas 2020 was the highest rate at 30.1%. Among them, 47.4% and 52.6% were females and males, respectively. Age groups from 5 to 14 covered up 21.6%, adults aged over 15 take up to 57.2%, and children under age 5 were 21.2%. The infection distribution was 58.8% for Plasmodium falciparum, 38.8% for Plasmodium vivax, and 2.4% mixed infections. The highest rate of infection was recorded during September to November. Cross-sectional parasitological survey showed that 18.3% of individuals were infected. The identified risk of contracting malaria was significant for individuals who were closer to mosquito breeding sites (AOR, 13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), did not use a mosquito net while sleeping (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), did not use indoor residual spraying in the previous 12 months (AOR,13.3, 95% CI, 8.23-26.96, p < 0.001), used a window without a screen (AOR, 2.78.3, 95% CI, 1.03-13.86, p < 0.02), used a thatched roof (AOR, 18.4, 95% CI, 2.82-32.85, p < 0.02), and did not know how malaria is transmitted (AOR, 4.3, 95% CI, 2.36-22.6, p < 0.04).
CONCLUSION: The study indicated that malaria remains a health issue in the Loko Abaya district. Several factors, including low income, wall openings, proximity to mosquito breeding sites, lack of indoor residual spraying, and lack of bed net use, were important predictors of malaria.

articles.title: Uveitic glaucoma in a multi-ethnic Malaysian cohort: demography, risk factors and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between uveitis and secondary glaucoma has been established, but the specific factors associated with progression to uveitic glaucoma remain poorly defined. This study aims to identify the prevalence and factors associated with uveitic glaucoma, and their clinical outcomes in a Malaysian cohort.
METHODS: Retrospective cohort study reviewing the clinical records of patients who attended the uveitis clinics at tertiary eye centres in Kuala Lumpur and Sarawak, Malaysia.
RESULTS: A total of 257 eyes from 163 patients were included. Mean age at uveitis onset was 37.3 ± 16.2 years with a slight female predominance. The prevalence of uveitic ocular hypertension and uveitic glaucoma was 26.1% and 30.0% respectively. Multiple logistic regression identified age of onset (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.023; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.003-1.044, p = 0.023), male gender (aOR 1.970; 95% CI 1.046-3.709, p = 0.036), presence of posterior synechiae (PS) (aOR 3.326; 95% CI 1.092-10.133, p = 0.034), peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS) (aOR 4.606; 95% CI 2.065-10.272, p < 0.001) and intraocular pressure (IOP) at presentation (aOR 1.077; 95% CI 1.039-1.117, p < 0.001) as significant factors for uveitic glaucoma. Steroid responsiveness occurred in 74 (29.2%) corticosteroid-treated eyes. Fifty-three eyes (36.80%) required at least one glaucoma incisional surgery. Chronic uveitis (p = 0.004) and PAS (p < 0.001) were associated with a higher percentage of glaucoma surgery.
CONCLUSIONS: Older age of onset, male gender, presence of PS or PAS, and elevated presenting IOP were significant factors associated with uveitic glaucoma. Additionally, chronic uveitis and PAS were factors associated with a higher percentage of glaucoma surgery. Early identification of these factors can prevent onset of uveitic glaucoma, which is a potential blinding complication of uveitis.

articles.title: Increased choriocapillaris non-perfusion in pediatric hypertension assessed by optical coherence tomography angiography(OCTA).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate retinal microvascular changes in pediatric patients with systemic hypertension compared with healthy controls using optical coherence tomography (OCT) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA).
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 94 pediatric patients (94 eyes; age 6-18 years) with systemic hypertension followed for at least one year and 60 age- and sex-comparable healthy controls. All participants underwent comprehensive ophthalmologic examination. OCT was used to measure foveal thickness (FT) and subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT). OCTA assessed vascular density (VD) in the superficial and deep capillary plexuses (SCP, DCP), optic nerve head (ONH), foveal avascular zone (FAZ), and choriocapillaris non-perfused area (NPCA) ratio. Body mass index (BMI) and microalbuminuria status were recorded.
RESULTS: FT, SFCT, SCP, DCP, FAZ, and ONH VD did not differ significantly between hypertensive patients and controls (p > 0.05). In contrast, NPCA ratios were significantly higher in the hypertensive group across all measured regions (0.5 mm, 0.5-1.5 mm, and 1.5-3 mm; p < 0.001). Within the hypertensive group, microalbuminuria-negative patients showed higher NPCA ratios in the 0.5 mm and 0.5-1.5 mm regions compared with microalbuminuria-positive patients (p < 0.05), although post hoc power was low. BMI demonstrated a weak negative correlation with DCP vessel density (p < 0.05). In multivariable regression analysis, systemic hypertension remained independently associated with increased NPCA values after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric patients with systemic hypertension without clinical retinopathy show increased choriocapillaris non-perfusion on OCTA, suggesting early subclinical microvascular involvement. OCTA-derived NPCA measurements may reflect early subclinical microvascular alterations associated with pediatric hypertension in children before conventional funduscopic findings become apparent.

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of keratoconus in Kilimanjaro region: a population-based evaluation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF THE STUDY: The study aimed to determine the distribution and determinants of keratoconus (KC) among individuals aged 12-45 years in the Kilimanjaro region, where epidemiological data are currently lacking.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional population-based screening was conducted between July 2024 and January 2025 among secondary schools, college and community members. Screening involved six steps: registration and visual acuity assessment, autokerato-refractometry, the Keratoconus Risk Investigative Survey (KRIS), retinoscopy, corneal topography, and counselling or referral. KC diagnosis and classification was based on a total weighted score ≥ 6-10 (scissor reflex, myopia >-5D, astigmatism ≤ 2.5D, Kmax > 46.5D, I-S > 1.4, steep K > 47D) and KC-suspect if score 2-5 including presence of scissor reflex and/or irregular astigmatism; and no KC if score < 2. Data were analyzed. using Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 26 and Stata version 14.
RESULTS: A total of 2,354 participants (49.7% female, 50.3% male), the majority of whom were Black African adolescents, aged 12-19 years, were screened. The prevalence of KC was 1.2% (95% CI: 0.8-1.7), with a mean age of 20.7 ± 7.2 years. Univariate analysis showed associations between KC and male gender (OR = 2.6, p = 0.016), age 12-24 years (OR = 4.0, p = 0.001), eczema (OR = 33.7, p < 0.001), and asthma (OR = 5.5, p = 0.011). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that only eczema is significantly associated with KC.
CONCLUSION: Overall, the findings indicate that KC is present at a clinically important level in the Kilimanjaro Region, particularly among adolescents and young adults, with eczema representing the strongest independent risk factor. The results support the implementation of targeted screening programs and strengthened referral pathways to facilitate early diagnosis and management of KC.

articles.title: Long-term workload, changing injury patterns, and spring festival-related case mix among patients hospitalized with open globe injury at a Chinese tertiary referral centre, 2013-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Open globe injury (OGI) is vision-threatening, but long-term changes in hospitalized workload and injury patterns remain poorly characterized. We assessed temporal changes in OGI workload and relative inpatient burden and whether the Spring Festival was associated with excess admissions or short-window differences in injury composition.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,096 unique patients, each contributing one index hospitalization for traumatic OGI requiring inpatient management at a tertiary referral centre in China from 2013 to 2025. Poisson models assessed monthly OGI workload and relative inpatient burden, with monthly ophthalmic admissions included as an offset. Spring Festival analyses compared Lunar New Year ± 7 days with nonwindow days within the same ± 30-day envelope. Firework-related composition was assessed among patients hospitalized within 24 h after injury, and injury-setting trends were evaluated using multinomial logistic regression.
RESULTS: Among 1,096 patients, 1,070 (97.6%) underwent surgery at the study hospital. Monthly OGI workload increased over time (IRR per year, 1.06; 95% CI, 1.04-1.08; P < 0.001), whereas relative inpatient burden declined (IRR per year, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.95-0.99; P = 0.003). The Spring Festival window was not associated with clear excess daily admissions (IRR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.43-1.02; P = 0.062). Firework-related injury was more frequent during the festival window (31.8% [7/22] vs. 3.4% [3/87]; OR, 13.07; 95% CI, 3.04-56.25; P < 0.001), although based on only 10 events. Agricultural injury increased relative to industrial injury in the primary model (RRR per year, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.03-1.25; P = 0.009), but the estimate was attenuated after adjustment for age and sex, with little further change after adding direct-admission status.
CONCLUSIONS: Hospitalized OGI workload increased while relative inpatient burden declined, but these hospital-level trends do not establish regional incidence. The Spring Festival was associated with a higher proportion of firework-related cases without clear excess admission volume. Injury-setting changes were modest, and industrial injury remained dominant. These findings may inform local ocular trauma prevention and ophthalmic emergency service planning.

articles.title: Internal mammary vessels as recipient vessels in supercharged ileocolon interposition for esophageal reconstruction: a single-center early technical experience.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Esophageal reconstruction remains challenging when conventional conduits are unavailable or unsuitable. Supercharged colon interposition may improve graft perfusion; however, optimal recipient vessels remain debated, particularly when cervical vessels cannot be used because of previous surgery, radiation therapy, or scarring. This single-center study describes a technical modification of the supercharged ileocolon technique, using the internal mammary vessels as recipient vessels via a minimally invasive, sternotomy-free intercostal approach.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Between 1995 and October 2024, nearly 1,000 esophageal resections were performed at our institution. Microsurgical reconstruction was required in 49 cases (38 free jejunal grafts, 11 supercharged colon interpositions); among the latter, 7 patients underwent supercharged ileocolon interposition using the internal mammary vessels as recipient vessels. Data were extracted retrospectively from a prospectively maintained institutional database. Given the small sample size, no formal statistical analysis was performed; results are reported descriptively as absolute numbers, with percentages given as supplementary information only.
RESULTS: Among 7 patients (mean age 42 years; range 18-76), 2 delayed primary and 5 secondary reconstructions were performed. Five of 7 patients (71.4%) had an uneventful postoperative course with satisfactory swallowing function. One patient (14.3%) developed an anastomotic leak that progressed to sepsis and death, and one patient (14.3%) developed graft thrombosis requiring graft removal. The internal mammary vessels were accessed through a left second-intercostal-space approach, in most cases without rib resection.
DISCUSSION: This study describes a technical modification of the previously established supercharged colon interposition technique - the use of internal mammary vessels as recipient vessels via a sternotomy-free intercostal route - rather than a fundamentally new reconstructive principle. It provides structured early clinical data supporting the technical feasibility of this approach in patients with unsuitable cervical vessels, while confirming that this remains a high-risk salvage procedure.
CONCLUSION: Supercharged ileocolon reconstruction using internal mammary vessels accessed via an intercostal approach is technically feasible and represents a useful addition to the reconstructive armamentarium when cervical recipient vessels are unavailable. The small sample size and retrospective design preclude conclusions regarding efficacy or superiority; larger series with long-term follow-up are required.

articles.title: T​he use of biosynthetic mesh in complex abdominal wall reconstruction - a single‑center experience.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Abdominal wall reconstruction in patients presenting with enteric fistulas and mesh infection is challenging. Synthetic mesh should be avoided in contaminated fields and to be used in selected cases. Alternative strategies include primary fascial closure with or without component separation, biologic mesh, and resorbable biosynthetic mesh. Our study aims to evaluate the use of long-term absorbable mesh in a single-stage procedure, focusing on postoperative complications and hernia recurrence rates.
METHODS: A retrospective single-arm study was conducted following Institutional Review Board approval. All incisional hernia repairs using bio-absorbable Poly-4-Hydroxybutyrate mesh were performed at our medical center between January 2017 and March 2025 were included. Adult and pediatric patients with Ventral Hernia Working Group (VHWG) grade III and IV wounds were eligible.
RESULTS: Thirty-four patients met the inclusion criteria. The mean age was 58.7 ± 17.1 years, and the mean body mass index was 30.4 ± 7.6 kg/m². Comorbidity burden was high: 52.9% had a Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and 35.3% had an ASA score ≥ 3. Most patients (82.3%) presented with infected mesh. Mean operative time was 188.5 ± 75 min, and bowel resection was required in 18 cases. Postoperative wound infection occurred in 10 patients. Follow‑up data were available for 28 of the 34 patients with median follow-up duration of 20.5 months. A single death occurred, hernia recurrence was observed in four cases (16%), all managed with reoperation. Quality-of-life assessments demonstrated a clear postoperative improvement.
CONCLUSIONS: In this high-risk, contaminated and infected cohort, P4HB mesh demonstrated acceptable recurrence and complication rates. Its long-term resorbable properties provides a feasible alternative to use in incisional hernia repair with infected meshes.

articles.title: Optimizing motor functions in incomplete spinal cord injury with simultaneous application of transcranial direct current stimulation and virtual reality assisted treadmill training: a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial {1a}.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incomplete spinal cord injury (iSCI) leads to significant motor impairments, affecting mobility and quality of life. Emerging rehabilitation strategies, including neuromodulation and virtual reality-assisted treadmill training, have shown potential in enhancing motor recovery among individuals with neurological conditions. However, the synergistic effects of their simultaneous application remain underexplored. This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to investigate the synergistic effects of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) and virtual reality-assisted treadmill training (VRTT) on motor functions, functional independence, and quality of life of individuals with iSCI.
METHODS: This study is a single-blind, randomized controlled superiority trial. 52 individuals with incomplete spinal cord injury will be recruited based on inclusion criteria. They will be randomly allocated to the transcranial direct current stimulation anodal or sham group. Both groups will simultaneously receive virtual reality-assisted treadmill training and conventional therapy. The intervention will consist of 15 sessions (20 min per session) delivered over a period of 3 weeks. Participants who are unable to complete all sessions within this duration will be permitted to extend the training period by an additional week, in accordance with the intention-to-treat principle. The primary outcome measures will include muscle strength (Lower Extremity Motor Score), balance (Berg Balance Scale and Functional Reach Test), walking speed (10-m walk test), walking ability (Walking Index for Spinal Cord Injury II), and gait parameters, including step length, hip and knee joint range of motion, and vertical displacement of the center of gravity. Secondary outcome measures will include functional independence (Spinal Cord Independence Measure III) and quality of life (World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF).
DISCUSSION: The trial will provide new knowledge about the effectiveness of combined transcranial direct current stimulation with VRTT training on motor functions, functional independence, and the quality of life of individuals with iSCI.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry-India, CTRI/2024/11/076226, Registered on 04/11/2024.

articles.title: Outpatient Referral After Adolescent Sexual Health Emergency Department Visits Improves Follow-Up.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate which methods of outpatient referral during pediatric emergency department (ED) visits for sexual health are associated with increased follow-up among adolescents otherwise at risk of being lost to care.
METHODS: A single-institution retrospective cohort study was conducted among patients 14-20 years-old who underwent testing for any sexually transmitted infection during ED visits between 1/1/2018 and 12/31/2018 and were discharged home, excluding pregnant patients or those presenting following sexual assault. The primary outcome was any follow-up within 6 months of the index ED visit. The primary independent variable was referral at discharge. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations.
RESULTS: Among 1,152 patients (median age 17 years; 76% female), 73% received a referral, and 36.5% were seen in follow-up within 6 months of the index visit. Referrals specifying time frame for follow-up were associated with increased follow-up (odds ratio [OR] 5.9, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.2-8.4), whereas "as needed" referrals were not. In multivariable modeling, attending a follow-up visit was associated with referral (adjusted OR [AOR] 3.6, 95% CI 2.5-5.2), female sex (2.74, 95% CI: 1.90-3.95), and prior preventive care (4.42, 95% CI: 3.36-5.81). Although associated with having follow-up visits, referrals were not associated with contraception initiation or decreased return to the ED within 6 months of the index visit.
DISCUSSION: Referral to outpatient care was associated with increased follow-up among adolescents with sexual health needs, particularly when referrals specified a follow-up time frame. Pediatric EDs should standardize discharge processes to include specific and consistent outpatient referrals.

articles.title: Engaging Boys, Transforming Systems: Multisectoral Approaches to Advancing Gender Equality and Adolescent Health.
articles.abstract: Engaging boys in gender equality efforts is crucial for achieving sustainable societal change; however, incorporating these interventions into existing structures and systems presents a significant challenge. Through an analysis of international case studies, we have identified best practices and valuable lessons to offer actionable recommendations for practitioners and policymakers. These recommendations emphasize: (1) codesigning gender-transformative health promotion interventions with adolescent boys, (2) employing a multisectoral approach to enhance the widespread and in-depth integration of gender-transformative interventions to promote the health of both adolescent boys and girls, and (3) utilizing digital interventions to reach adolescents across multiple sectors effectively. By shifting the focus from specific health subthemes to cross-cutting approaches and settings where boys can be engaged, such as education systems, local government structures, community-led initiatives, and households, this paper presents solutions for scalable and sustainable programming. We call for the systemic integration of gender-transformative interventions to foster adolescent boys' health and promote equitable, caring, and connected masculinities to improve health across generations.

articles.title: Gender Attitudes and the Effects on Adolescent Boys' Mental Health in the Context of Forced Displacement.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adolescent boys and young men (ABYM) in humanitarian settings face unique mental health challenges, yet limited research examines how gender norms shape their psychosocial wellbeing. Understanding the relationship between masculinity norms and mental health outcomes is critical for developing effective interventions for displaced ABYM. This paper examines the association between gender attitudes and mental health outcomes among ABYM in displacement settings, comparing patterns between refugee and host community ABYM among Syrian refugees in Jordan and Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh.
METHODS: We employed a convergent parallel mixed-methods design using midline survey data from Syrian (n = 737) and Jordanian (n = 138) males aged 13-19 years, and Rohingya (n = 281) and Bangladeshi (n = 343) males aged 12-19 years. We complemented quantitative analyses with qualitative interviews exploring how displacement shapes gender attitudes and mental health.
RESULTS: Refugee ABYM reported significantly more gender equitable attitudes compared to host community peers in both contexts. More gender equitable attitudes were significantly associated with lower psychological distress, higher resilience, and reduced substance use among refugee ABYM. Having a trusted adult strengthened the protective effect of gender equitable attitudes on mental health outcomes in both Jordan and Bangladesh, while having a trusted friend showed similar effects in Jordan.
DISCUSSION: Conservative masculinity norms among refugee ABYM are associated with poorer mental health outcomes, indicating an urgent need for gender-transformative psychosocial interventions in humanitarian settings that address traditional masculinities while strengthening supportive relationships with adults and peers.

articles.title: Depression, but Not Anxiety, Is Associated With Poorer Working Memory in Adolescent Psychiatric Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The present study aimed to examine the associations between depression/anxiety and cognitive functioning in adolescent psychiatric patients to understand the progress of symptoms and build effective intervention plans.
METHODS: Data from 82 adolescents who received psychiatric treatment and psychological assessment at a university hospital were analyzed based on Wechsler Intelligence Scale and the Depression (DEP) and Anxiety (ANX) scales of the Personality Assessment Inventory (PAI).
RESULTS: The mean full-scale intelligent quotient was 88.55, which was lower than the normative mean. The mean PAI DEP score was 65.45, and the mean ANX score was 60.10. In the correlation analyses, only DEP and the Working Memory Index (WMI) showed a significant negative correlation(r=-0.24, p=0.005). In a multiple regression analysis in which the three DEP subscales (cognitive, affective, and physiological DEP [DEP-P]) were entered as independent variables and WMI as the dependent variable. Only DEP-P, which assesses symptoms such as sleep problems, reduced activity, and low energy, significantly predicted WMI (β=-0.37, t=-2.90, p=0.005).
CONCLUSION: Adolescent psychiatric patients presenting with a wide range of clinical problems reported more depressive symptoms and showed lower intellectual functioning than normative samples. In addition, the unique association observed between physiological symptoms of depression and working memory is consistent with previous evidence linking these symptoms to circadian rhythm disruption, dysfunction of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex/frontoparietal network, and white matter deficits. These findings suggest that therapeutic interventions targeting physiological depressive symptoms may contribute to improving working memory and academic achievement in adolescents.

articles.title: Pregnancy Risk Information Systems for Psychotropic Medications: A Practical Review for Clinical Decision-Making.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to summarize pregnancy risk information systems for psychotropic medications and recent evidence on reproductive safety, with the goal of improving clinicians' awareness of drug-specific risk information relevant to individualized clinical decision- making in women with psychiatric disorders of reproductive age.
METHODS: We narratively reviewed official reproductive safety information resources from Australia, Europe, Korea, the United Kingdom, and the United States, together with recent umbrella-review evidence on psychotropic medication safety during pregnancy. Information on selected agents was organized by drug class.
RESULTS: National systems differed in structure and clinical utility. Australia and Korea retain category-based elements, whereas sources from Europe, the United Kingdom, and the United States provide more descriptive, context-based information. Antipsychotics were mainly associated with neonatal extrapyramidal or withdrawal symptoms and metabolic risk signals for selected agents. Mood stabilizers and anticonvulsants were more strongly associated with congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental disorders. Benzodiazepines and hypnotics were mainly associated with neonatal sedation, respiratory depression, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, and withdrawal symptoms after late-pregnancy or labor exposure. Antidepressants were associated with neonatal adaptation symptoms, persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn, and postpartum hemorrhage. Recent umbrella-review evidence showed that most reported associations remained at suggestive or weak levels of evidence.
CONCLUSION: Psychotropic medication use during pregnancy should be guided by individualized risk-benefit assessment, integrating drug-specific safety signals, evidence quality, exposure timing, lactation and fertility considerations, and the risks of untreated psychiatric illness.

articles.title: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery Protocols in Laparoscopic GI Surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Protocols known as enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) have transformed perioperative care by integrating multidisciplinary, evidence-based measures that aim to reduce surgical stress and promote faster recovery.
OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the influence of ERAS pathways on perioperative outcomes among patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrointestinal operations.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 170 adult patients (18-80 years) who underwent laparoscopic procedures between February 2023 and August 2025. Patients treated according to ERAS principles were compared with those receiving conventional perioperative care. Outcomes of interest included opioid consumption, readmission rates, complication profiles, hospitalization duration, and overall costs.
RESULTS: Among 170 patients (mean age 42.0 ± 15.9 years; 59.4% female), cholecystectomy was the most common procedure (64.1%). ERAS implementation was associated with a shorter duration of opioid therapy (median 3 days, discontinued by day 5), low readmission frequency (3.5%), and brief hospitalization (median 27 hours). Postoperative complications occurred in 5.3% of patients, most often wound seroma (2.4%). Multivariable analysis showed younger age predicted earlier recovery, while sex, nationality, comorbidities, and procedure type had no significant effect.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective single-center cohort of 170 patients undergoing a range of laparoscopic gastrointestinal procedures, ERAS-based perioperative care was associated with favorable recovery outcomes. Because procedure complexity and expected recovery varied across the cohort, these findings should be interpreted as associative and should not be taken to imply an identical ERAS effect across all procedure types.

articles.title: Adolescent loneliness and health-compromising behaviors: Relations with dieting, substance use, and sleep disturbances.
articles.abstract: Loneliness is a major public health risk, and understanding its impacts on physical health is crucial for preventative healthcare strategies. This study examined whether adolescent loneliness predicted health-compromising behaviors (i.e. sleep disturbances, weight control, substance use) 1 year later and whether gender moderated these associations. Data were drawn from a longitudinal study of adolescents in the Southwestern United States (N = 751). Greater loneliness in ninth grade was associated with more frequent sleep disturbances 1 year later (an association that was significantly stronger among girls than boys) and with larger increases in sleep disturbances over the same period. Loneliness was not associated with dieting or substance use. Findings highlight loneliness as a contributor to adolescent sleep disturbances, particularly among girls, and a potential target for intervention.

articles.title: Prevalence and Multilevel Determinants of Ever Having Been Tested for HIV Among Women Aged 15-49 Years in Ethiopia: Evidence From the 2024 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey.
articles.journal: J Int Assoc Provid AIDS Care
articles.abstract: BackgroundHIV testing is the gateway to HIV prevention, treatment, and care. This study assessed the prevalence and determinants of HIV testing among Ethiopian women aged 15-49 years using nationally representative data.MethodsA secondary analysis of the 2024 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey was conducted among 21,394 women. Sampling weights and multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression were applied.ResultsThe weighted prevalence of ever having been tested for HIV was 52.3% (95% CI: 50.2%-54.5%). In the final model, testing was significantly associated with age, education, marital status, wealth, employment, media exposure, community factors, and region. The odds HIV testing were higher among women aged 25-34 years (AOR=2.44), those with higher education (AOR=7.30), married women (AOR=15.41), and women from the richest households (AOR=2.51). Higher community-level media exposure was associated with higher odds of HIV testing (AOR = 1.59).ConclusionsHIV testing uptakes remains suboptimal among Ethiopian women.

articles.title: Frequency of On-Scene Goal-Directed Field Interventions for Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in a Regional System of Care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Early on-scene resuscitation improves outcomes from pediatric non-traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); however, for pediatric patients, the early evacuation strategy remains commonplace. We sought to determine the frequency of goal-directed interventions initiated by paramedics prior to transport for pediatric patients with OHCA in a regional emergency medical services (EMS) system.
METHODS: In this retrospective observational study and cross-sectional analysis, we analyzed the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES) and linked electronic patient care reports (ePCR) data for patients aged <15 years treated by EMS for nontraumatic OHCA in Los Angeles (LA) County from January 2021 to December 2022. The primary outcome was the frequency of goal-directed therapies administered on scene prior to transport, which we defined as defibrillation for shockable rhythms and administration of epinephrine and fluid resuscitation for non-shockable rhythms. We also tabulated descriptive statistics regarding arrest characteristics, scene times, frequency of other prehospital treatments, and patient outcomes.
RESULTS: Among 176 eligible pediatric OHCA cases analyzed in CARES, 112 (64%) were male, the median age was 10 months (IQR 3-51), and 162 (92%) had an initial non-shockable rhythm. Of these, 156 patients were successfully linked to electronic patient care report (ePCR) records for analyses of prehospital interventions. Among 143 patients with non-shockable rhythms, EMS administered epinephrine before transport in 58 (41%) and fluids in 12 (8%). Among 13 patients with shockable rhythms, EMS delivered defibrillation before transport in 11 (85%). Bag-valve-mask (BVM) use was documented in 80 (51%) patients, although its timing relative to scene departure could not be determined. Median on-scene time was 10 minutes (IQR 5-18). Ten patients (6%) survived to hospital discharge, including 6 (3%) with a favorable neurologic outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: In this regional EMS system, fewer than half of patients with non-shockable rhythms received a dose of epinephrine and fewer than one in ten received intravenous fluids prior to transport, whereas most patients with shockable rhythms were defibrillated on scene. Further work is needed to identify barriers to timely delivery of on-scene resuscitative interventions.

articles.title: Prehospital Trauma Compendium: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP, ACS-COT, ACEP, and AAP.
articles.abstract: In 2014 the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP), American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS-COT), American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) published the first joint position statement discussing withholding and discontinuing resuscitation attempts for pediatric traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest (TOHCA). Since then, the body of literature addressing pediatric TOHCA has evolved and evidence has grown that demonstrates the nearly uniformly poor prognosis of children who suffer circulatory arrest in the prehospital setting as a result of trauma. To support emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians in their approach to these high-acuity, low-frequency, and challenging cases, this project aimed to update guidance regarding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts for pediatric traumatic circulatory arrest. NAEMSP, ACEP, ACS-COT, and AAP recommend:EMS resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA should:Prioritize prompt identification of patients who may benefit from transport to definitive care at trauma centers when safe and appropriate. On-scene resuscitation should be balanced against the potential benefit of transfer to a proximate trauma center.Emphasize the identification of reversible causes of traumatic circulatory arrest and timely use of clinically indicated life-saving interventions (LSIs) within the EMS clinician's scope of practice. These include:External hemorrhage control with direct pressure, wound packing, and tourniquetsAirway management using the least-invasive airway interventions required to achieve and maintain airway patency, oxygenation, and adequate ventilation.Chest decompression if clinical concern for tension pneumothorax. Empiric bilateral decompression is not recommended in the absence of suspected thoracic trauma.External chest compressions and ventilations have a larger role in pediatric TOHCA resuscitation than in adult TOHCA resuscitation, with children frequently having TOHCA secondary to head injury, hypoxia and other non-hemorrhagic mechanisms. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be provided when the cause of circulatory arrest is unclear.Epinephrine is of lower priority than other LSIs.Consider point of care ultrasound (POCUS) to guide decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts.Resuscitation attempts may be withheld in pediatric TOHCA patients with:Injuries that are incompatible with life (e.g., decapitation, hemi-corpectomy, incineration).Evidence of prolonged circulatory arrest (e.g., rigor mortis, dependent lividity, decomposition).Advanced care planning documents that indicate Do Not Resuscitate (DNR)/ Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR)/Allow Natural Death medical orders.Resuscitation attempts may be discontinued in pediatric TOHCA patients who:Have no return of spontaneous circulation after provision of at least 15 minutes of high-quality CPR in addition to performance of other lifesaving interventions directed at treating potentially reversible causes of pediatric TOHCA. Longer durations of CPR, up to 30 minutes, may be considered for patients with positive predictors of survival such as organized rhythm, witnessed arrest, bystander CPR, or with proximate access to a trauma center.Have known predictors of very low probability of survival such as penetrating trauma without proximate access to a trauma center, asystole, unwitnessed arrest, or lack of bystander CPR.Protocols guiding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA benefit from oversight by EMS physicians in collaboration with pediatric experts and local or regional trauma system stakeholders. Implementation of such protocols for pediatric patients benefits from involvement of community stakeholders including family representatives, law enforcement, medical examiner, and child fatality review committees.Considerations for protocol implementation include local resource availability, EMS clinician and public safety, psychosocial support to surviving family members and emergency responders, and dignified handling of the deceased patient.Training needs for EMS clinicians include techniques to communicate with family members regarding the death of a child and understanding the clinician's own response to this low-frequency, high-emotion experience.

articles.title: Presenting Complaints for Children in US Emergency Departments: An Analysis of a Nationally Representative Sample.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the presenting complaints for children in the emergency department (ED), both overall and within subgroups of age, acuity and pediatric ED status, and to evaluate changes in complaint patterns over time.
STUDY DESIGN: We performed a serial, cross-sectional study using the 2014-2022 National Hospital Ambulatory Medical Care Survey, including ED encounters for children (<18 years). Our variable of interest was patient complaint, evaluated as (a) the chief complaint and (b) all reported complaints. We described the distribution of patient complaints using the Pediatric Emergency Reason for Visit Clusters (PERC) rubric and examined distributions across subgroups. We evaluated changes in complaints over time using survey-weighted logistic regression.
RESULTS: Of the 277,624,292 ED encounters, the most common chief complaints were fever (37,330,480; 13.4%), extremity injury or pain (30,546,932; 11.0%), cough (22,479,119; 8.1%), abdominal pain (16,867,178; 6.1%), and rash (14,181,775; 5.1%). Fever predominated from infancy through early childhood, whereas extremity injury or pain and abdominal pain became more prominent with increasing age; psychiatric/behavioral complaints emerged notably in adolescence. Fever was most common among immediate and urgent visits, psychiatric/behavioral concerns among emergent visits, extremity injury or pain among semi-urgent visits, and rash among nonurgent visits. Complaint patterns were similar between pediatric and general EDs. Overall findings were similar when considering all reported complaints.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the distribution of complaints was similar over time and between pediatric and general EDs, there were differences based on age and acuity. These findings provide a national characterization of patient complaints that inform pediatric readiness and resource planning.

articles.title: Kawasaki Disease Linked to Age-Dependent Temporal, Seasonal, Temporal Clustering, and Atmospheric Circulation Patterns in San Diego County, 2002-2025.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate age-stratified temporal, seasonal, temporal clustering, and atmospheric circulation patterns of Kawasaki disease (KD) incidence in a large US cohort over a 24-year period in San Diego County and to determine whether these patterns support age-dependent environmental influences.
STUDY DESIGN: We performed a retrospective cohort study of 1,707 children with KD hospitalized at Rady Children's Hospital San Diego (RCHSD) from 2002-2025. Patients were stratified into 6 age groups (<6 months, 6-<15 months, 15-<24 months, 24-<36 months, 36-<60 months, ≥60 months). Temporal and seasonal patterns were evaluated using normalized running means with bootstrap resampling. Temporal clustering used onset dates. Atmospheric circulation patterns during low- and high-incidence years were compared using 700-mb geopotential height anomalies.
RESULTS: ll age groups demonstrated shared interannual variability, including a nadir in February-March 2018 and peaks in late 2016 and spring 2019. Older children showed a twofold increase in incidence until 2010, followed by a plateau, and no age group demonstrated a significant increasing temporal trend thereafter. Seasonal patterns differed by age: infants and young children (<15 months) showed significant variation, with a peak in late January and nadir in late February. Older children (≥36 months) showed more stability, with increased incidence in February-March and decreased incidence in August-October. Temporal clustering identified 56 clusters involving 375 cases (22%), of which 42 (75%) occurred during the November-April high-incidence season. Comparison of geopotential height anomaly composites revealed distinct circulation patterns between low- and high-incidence years.
CONCLUSIONS: Age-dependent temporal and seasonal variation, together with temporal clustering and atmospheric circulation patterns, support a role for environmental influences in KD onset. Shared interannual fluctuations suggest common environmental influences across childhood, whereas age-specific seasonal differences indicate developmental variation in environmental exposures or susceptibility. These data support an age-dependent framework for investigating environmental influences on KD etiology.

articles.title: Vitamin C Status in Children and Young Adults with Epidermolysis Bullosa.
articles.abstract: Recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (RDEB) predisposes to malnutrition and micronutrient deficiencies. In a retrospective cohort from a multidisciplinary EB clinic, 7 of 24 (29.2%) patients with RDEB had ascorbic acid concentrations consistent with deficiency. We recommend empiric vitamin C for all patients 4 years and older with RDEB.

articles.title: Stress Fracture Recovery and Return to Sports in Youth with Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare stress fracture recovery times in children with and without juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), and to evaluate JIA-related factors associated with recovery.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective case-control study included children with JIA <19 years old with a first stress fracture treated at a single center from 2004-2024. Cases were matched 1:3 to children without JIA by age, gender, and fracture location. Recovery time was defined from imaging confirmation of a stress fracture to medical clearance to return to sports. We used a generalized estimating equations method to compare recovery times and evaluate associations with JIA-related factors, including JIA subtype, glucocorticoid and arthritis-directed therapy exposure, and proximity of arthritis to fracture location.
RESULTS: The cohort included 260 children (65 cases, 195 controls; 53.8% female; median age 14.3 years [IQR 12.6, 16.2]). Pars interarticularis fractures accounted for 30.8% of injuries, followed by metatarsal (23.1%), and tibial fractures (14.2%). Among children with JIA who sustained pars fractures, 75.0% had an enthesitis-related arthritis (ERA) phenotype. Median recovery times were 10.6 (IQR 7.0, 19.4) weeks for children with JIA and 10.6 (IQR 7.1, 14.6) weeks for controls (P=0.197), with no significant differences for lower-extremity fractures. In contrast, children with JIA who sustained pars fractures had longer recovery times than controls (ratio of geometric means: 1.44, 95% CI 1.01, 2.05; P=0.045). Among children with active sacroiliitis, fractures occurred more frequently in the proximate pars or pelvis than at non-proximate sites (P<0.001). Recovery time was not associated with JIA subtype (all p>0.150), glucocorticoid exposure (P=0.365), or biologic therapy (P=0.625).
CONCLUSIONS: Overall recovery times did not differ significantly between children with and without JIA. However, children with JIA and pars fractures had longer recovery times, and associations with ERA and sacroiliitis warrant further investigation. Additional research on spondylolysis recovery in young athletes with JIA may help inform individualized return-to-sports recommendations.

articles.title: Association between youth sexuality and gender identity and outcomes after hospitalization for suicide attempt.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the prevalence of sexual minority (SM) and gender minority (GM) identities among youth hospitalized for suicide attempt (SA) relative to the state youth population (27.8% sexual and gender minority [SGM] in 2021), and to characterize differences in SA outcomes among SGM vs non-SGM youth.
STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of youth 9-24 years medically hospitalized for SA between 2010-2022 at 2 tertiary pediatric centers. Encounters were manually reviewed to extract outcomes and SGM identities. We performed Poisson regression adjusted for age, race and ethnicity, and area deprivation index to evaluate associations between SGM identity with intensive care unit (ICU) admission, in-hospital mortality, and SA readmission.
RESULTS: Of 1,537 included youth, 21.2% (n=326) identified as SM and 11.7% (n=180) as GM. SGM identity rose from 5.0% in 2010 to 47.1% in 2022. Readmission for subsequent SA was higher among both SM (15.6% vs 7.9%; aRR 1.99 [1.30-3.06]) and GM youth (20.0% vs 5.3%; aRR 2.71 [1.76-4.17]). SGM identities were not associated with a difference in ICU admission for SA and were associated with lower in-hospital mortality. However, GM identity was associated with higher risk of mortality following intentional ingestion relative to non-GM youth (1.2% vs 0.4%; RR 3.06 [1.99-4.70]).
CONCLUSIONS: A higher proportion of youth hospitalized for SA identified as SGM compared with the general youth population, and this proportion rose between 2010-2022. SGM youth are particularly vulnerable to suicide by ingestion and to readmission for SA, warranting targeted prevention efforts.

articles.title: Investigating Age Group Differences and the Effect of Arousal on the Evoked Pupil Dilation Response to Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation.
articles.abstract: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is hypothesized to prevent cognitive ageing by increasing phasic locus coeruleus (LC) activity. Short taVNS bursts have been shown to increase phasic LC activity as measured by evoked pupil dilation in young adults. Little is known about their effects in ageing. taVNS-evoked pupil dilation may be smaller in older adults due to age-related increases in tonic LC activity. This study will test age group differences in taVNS-evoked pupil dilation and evaluate whether administering taVNS bursts after slow-paced breathing-an arousal-reducing technique-increases pupil responses in older adults. Thirty-three cognitively unimpaired older adults (55-75) and 33 young adults (18-35) will receive taVNS bursts at the cymba concha (left ear) after blocks of slow-paced breathing at 0.1 Hz and spontaneous breathing on the same day in counterbalanced order. In each breathing condition, a 2.5-min breathing block will precede a 2.5-min stimulation block, three times. Pupil size will be measured during each stimulation block. We hypothesize that taVNS-evoked pupil dilation is smaller in older adults compared with young adults, and it is larger following slow-paced breathing exercises compared with spontaneous breathing in older adults. The breathing manipulation will be considered successful if the slow-paced breathing condition (vs. spontaneous breathing) is associated with decreases in arousal ratings, respiratory rate, and prestimulus baseline pupil size (tonic LC activity index) and with an increase in vagally mediated heart rate variability from baseline. This project represents an important first step toward examining conditions that might increase the impact of taVNS in older adults.

articles.title: Tailoring practices identified in pediatric serious illness communication tools: A scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serious illness communication tools have been designed to ensure safe and standardized care. Effective person-centered communication requires clinicians not only to identify each patient's needs, but also to adapt their communication approach and interaction behaviors accordingly. Tailoring is a responsive and adaptive communication approach that has been defined in adult healthcare literature but not in pediatric literature.
OBJECTIVE: This scoping review sought to identify tools used to guide serious illness communication in pediatric settings and map tool constructs against the communication approach 'tailoring' to consider the potential transferability of this approach to the pediatric healthcare context.
METHODS: This scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews. Articles were eligible for inclusion if they were English-language, peer-reviewed publications that proposed or synthesized an original communication tool for health professionals conducting serious illness conversations in pediatric healthcare. The Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) was used to guide reporting.
RESULTS: A total of 3788 articles were identified for screening and 19 were retained for data extraction. Variation existed in the derivation of pediatric serious illness communication tools with most being informed by expert opinion. Tailoring practices were identified in all pediatric serious illness communication tools, but to varying extents. They could be utilized both prior to and during serious illness conversations and the majority of tailoring practices focused on what to discuss as opposed to how to communicate. Practices that could guide clinicians to address key pediatric considerations such as neurodevelopment and language abilities were underrepresented.
CONCLUSION: Pediatric serious illness communication tools incorporated tailoring practices, albeit to varying degrees. Further empirical research is needed to examine how tailoring practices could be integrated into these tools, particularly to support clinicians in monitoring children's non-verbal cues, emotions, and neurodevelopmental capacities during serious illness conversations.

articles.title: Reliability and validity of the Greek Version of the Sitting Assessment Scale in children with cerebral palsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Sitting Assessment Scale (SAS) is a clinical observational instrument used to evaluate sitting posture and postural control in children with cerebral palsy (CP). However, a culturally adapted and psychometrically evaluated Greek version is currently unavailable. This study aimed to translate and culturally adapt the SAS into Greek and to evaluate its reliability and concurrent validity in children with CP.
METHODS: The SAS was translated and culturally adapted into Greek using a forward-backward translation procedure, expert review, and pilot testing. Thirty children and adolescents with spastic CP, aged 4-18 years and classified across Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) Levels IV, participated in the psychometric evaluation. The SAS was administered in two sitting positions: neutral sitting (SAS-A) and sitting with the seat surface tilted 45° backward (SASB). Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha, and intra-rater reliability was evaluated using a two-way random-effects, absolute-agreement, single-measure intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC (2,1)]. Measurement error was quantified using the standard error of measurement (SEM) and minimal detectable change at the 95% confidence level (MDC95). Agreement between repeated measurements was further examined using Bland-Altman analysis. Concurrent validity was examined by correlating SAS-A and SAS-B scores with the Trunk Control Measurement Scale (TCMS) total score using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient. Floor and ceiling effects were also examined.
RESULTS: The Greek SAS demonstrated excellent internal consistency for both SAS-A (Cronbach's α = 0.940) and SAS-B (α = 0.941). Intra-rater reliability was excellent for SAS-A [ICC (2,1) = 0.985, 95% CI 0.968-0.993, p < 0.001] and SAS-B [ICC (2,1) = 0.997, 95% CI 0.993-0.998, p < 0.001]. Measurement error was low, with SEM values of 0.54 and 0.26 and MDC95 values of 1.49 and 0.72 for SAS-A and SASB, respectively. Bland-Altman analysis indicated minimal systematic bias between repeated assessments in both sitting positions. Strong positive correlations were observed between the SAS and TCMS total scores (SAS-A: ρ = 0.847; SASB: ρ = 0.874; both p < 0.001), supporting concurrent validity. No floor effects were observed in either position, whereas a ceiling effect was identified for SASB, with 20% of participants achieving the maximum score.
CONCLUSIONS: The Greek version of the SAS demonstrated excellent internal consistency and intra-rater reliability, low measurement error, and strong concurrent validity with the TCMS in children with CP. These findings support the Greek SAS as a reliable and valid clinical instrument for assessing sitting posture and postural control in Greek-speaking children with CP.
