Further studies involving larger and more diverse samples are warranted to confirm these preliminary psychometric findings and to investigate inter-rater reliability and responsiveness.

articles.title: Gross motor development of infants with Down syndrome in the first year: Longitudinal comparison with reference curves.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe gross motor development during the first year of life in infants with Down syndrome (DS), compare it with published reference data, and examine its associations with maternal age, congenital heart disease, and home affordances.
METHODS: In this longitudinal observational study, 25 infants with DS, all receiving weekly physical therapy at an early intervention center since early infancy, were assessed at 6, 9, and 12 months (corrected age) with the Gross Motor Function Measure (GMFM-88). The age of attainment of six World Health Organization motor milestones was recorded prospectively. Home affordances were assessed with the Affordances in the Home Environment for Motor Development-Infant Scale. A pre-specified linear mixed model examined associated factors.
RESULTS: By 12 months, 92% of infants sat without support, 52% stood with assistance, and 36% crawled; none stood or walked independently. Crawling was more frequent and standing alone less frequent than reference probabilities. Mean GMFM-88 scores rose from 17.3% to 48.5%, exceeding reference curves at 12 months. Older maternal age was associated with lower scores across assessments (β = -0.75 per year, p = 0.028), but not with the rate of gain. Infants with congenital heart disease (32%) scored lower at 12 months, although not significantly (adjusted difference - 6.7 points, p = 0.116). Home affordances were not associated with motor trajectories.
CONCLUSIONS: Early horizontal milestones were within or above reference expectations, whereas upright skills lagged behind. These longitudinal first-year data support monitoring against DS-specific references to identify infants at risk of delayed upright skills.

articles.title: Burden of diabetes and related chronic kidney diseases in adolescents and young adults aged 10-24 years in China from 1990 to 2021, with projections to 2050: a secondary analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is an important public health concern among adolescents and young adults in China. We assessed the burden of Type 1 DM (T1DM), Type 2 DM (T2DM), chronic kidney disease caused by T1DM (CKD-T1DM), and chronic kidney disease caused by T2DM (CKD-T2DM) among adolescents and young adults aged 10-24 years in China from 1990 to 2021, stratified by age and sex. Data were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2021. We estimated the incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-year (DALY) rates, with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), and percentage changes from 1990 to 2021. Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) modeling was used to project trends from 2022 to 2050. In 2021, the prevalence rates per 100,000 population were 66.70 (95% UI: 46.42-94.55) for T1DM, 1,547.76 (1,252.46-1,877.46) for T2DM, 20.64 (14.80-29.19) for CKD-T1DM, and 124.55 (92.40-173.88) for CKD-T2DM. By sex, the prevalence rate of T1DM and the incidence rate of CKD-T1DM increased in males, whereas no significant changes were observed in females. By age, a relatively greater increase in the incidence rate of T2DM was observed among those aged 15-19 years. BAPC projections suggested that the age-standardized incidence and prevalence rates of T1DM and T2DM among males may continue to increase through to 2050. The burden of DM and its related chronic kidney disease showed age- and sex-related differences, with males having a relatively heavier burden of T1DM and CKD-T1DM. These findings may inform age- and sex-sensitive prevention strategies.

articles.title: Identifying children and adolescents with preclinical type 1 diabetes among first-degree relatives of type 1 diabetes patients: a Polish pilot study (pre-d1abetes study).
articles.abstract: Clinical type 1 diabetes (T1D) is often preceded by preclinical stages with the presence of islet autoantibodies (IAb). The aim of the study was to conduct an early screening programme for preclinical T1D in children and adolescents with a family history of T1D. In total, 1,275 first-degree relatives of T1D patients from 14 clinical centers across Poland participated in the study. Serum samples were tested via the 3-Screen ICATM enzyme-linked immunnosorbent assay (ELISA) for combined detection of autoantibodies to glutamic acid decarboxylase (GADAb), islet antigen IA-2 (IA-2Ab), and zinc transporter 8 (ZnT8Ab). All positive samples (104 subjects, 8.1%) were assayed for the individual autoantibodies (via ELISAs) and insulin antibodies (IAAs) (via radioimmunoassay), all using equipment from RSR Ltd, Cardiff, UK. The presence of two or more antibodies identified 69 subjects (5.4%) with preclinical T1D. Among IAb-positive participants, GADAb antibodies were the most frequent, whereas IAAs were the least frequent. Metabolic staging with an oral glucose tolerance test and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) was carried out in the consenting subjects. T1D was diagnosed in 10 patients with multiple antibody positivity, of whom none presented with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). The results of our study highlight the importance of IAb screening in individuals with already increased risk of T1D developing. Early detection of IAb identifies preclinical T1D prior to the onset of dysglycemia, with subsequent follow-up allowing for timely intervention preventing the development of DKA and its severe manifestations. Implementation of screening programs in routine clinical practice may open up opportunities for innovative therapeutic interventions in individuals at a high risk of T1D.

articles.title: Deep learning-based blood glucose prediction in pediatric type 1 diabetes patients exercising in free-living conditions.
articles.abstract: This paper evaluates deep learning models for blood glucose prediction in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes using insulin pumps and investigates whether transfer learning from adult data improves prediction accuracy and safety. Models were trained using data from the Type 1 Diabetes Exercise Initiative Pediatric study (84 pediatric insulin pump users) and its adult counterpart (380 adult insulin pump users). Two transfer learning strategies were compared: one using pediatric data only and another pre-training the model on adult data before fine-tuning it on the pediatric cohort and each target patient. Prediction accuracy and clinical safety were assessed using root mean square error (RMSE) and the Clarke Error Grid (CEG) at 10-, 20-, and 30-min prediction horizons, with results analyzed separately for open-loop and closed-loop users. Pre-training on adult data yielded the best performance. At 30 min, mean RMSE was 19.61 mg/dL (1.09 mmol/L), with at least 92.64% of predictions falling within zone A of the CEG for 75% of patients. No predictions fell within the unsafe zone E. Delayed hypoglycemia detection occurred only in a small subset of patients and was mainly associated with missing contextual information or atypical clinical events. An additional evaluation on pediatric patients treated with multiple daily injections (MDI) demonstrated clinically acceptable prediction accuracy and safety, supporting the applicability of the proposed transfer learning approach to MDI users. These findings demonstrate that transfer learning from adult data effectively mitigates pediatric data scarcity and enables accurate, clinically safe blood glucose prediction under free-living conditions.

articles.title: Short-term outcomes and follow-up of NICU graduates in selected NICUs in Galle, Sri Lanka: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal health during the post-discharge period is critical, especially for infants discharged from the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), who are at higher risk of complications and long-term developmental issues. In Sri Lanka, there are limited data on post-NICU follow-up, highlighting the need for research. This study aimed to evaluate the post-discharge follow-up status of neonates admitted to selected NICUs in Galle, Sri Lanka.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted between January 2025 and June 2025 in the NICUs of National Hospital Galle (NHG) and German-Sri Lanka Friendship Hospital for Women (GSLFHW). Neonates admitted within 28 days of birth who were discharged home or transferred to other wards were included; those who died before discharge or were transferred to another NICU or another hospital were excluded. A purposive sampling method was used. Follow-up assessments were conducted one week and one month after discharge. Data were collected using a structured guide on feeding status, feeding issues, medical problems, pharmacological management, follow-up visits, and developmental milestones. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26, and descriptive statistics were presented as numbers and percentages.
RESULTS: Respiratory distress was the most common reason for NICU admission (74.4%, n = 96). At discharge, 97.7% were breastfed, and most achieved age-appropriate developmental milestones: cognitive (92.2%, n = 119), motor (96.1%, n = 124), psychosocial (95.3%, n = 123), and communication (93.0%, n = 120). One week post-discharge, 94.4% were breastfed; feeding issues included poor sucking (12.7%, n = 16) and vomiting (6.3%, n = 8). Most infants met developmental milestones. One month post-discharge, 81.8% were breastfed, 10.9% were readmitted for complications, including infections, and the mean weight increased to 3.26 kg. Nearly all (99.1%) achieved age-appropriate developmental milestones by one month.
CONCLUSION: Most neonates showed favorable early post‑discharge status at one week and one month, with high rates of breastfeeding and attainment of age‑expected developmental milestones at these time points. While breastfeeding remained predominant, some experienced feeding difficulties and a small proportion required readmission or died. These findings describe very early outcomes only; continued and longer‑term follow‑up is essential to manage complications and support health outcomes beyond the first month.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Lanadelumab treatment helps prevent swelling attacks in children aged 2 to 11 years with hereditary angioedema (HAE): a plain language summary of the SPRING Study.
articles.abstract: What is this summary about? This is a summary of a clinical trial called the SPRING Study. The study looked at a treatment for children aged 2 to 11 years with a disease called hereditary angioedema, or HAE for short. The treatment is called lanadelumab. It is used to prevent swelling attacks of the skin or other tissues in people with HAE. What happened in the SPRING Study? The SPRING Study included 21 children who had HAE. Before starting lanadelumab treatment, the children's symptoms were tracked for 4 to 12 weeks. This was to help understand how HAE was affecting each child. The researchers used data from completed studies of lanadelumab in adults to help select the doses for children. The study had 2 parts (Part A and Part B) that lasted for 26 weeks each. In Part A, children aged 2 to 5 years had lanadelumab injections every 4 weeks and children aged 6 to 11 years had lanadelumab injections every 2 weeks. In Part B, some children aged 6 to 11 years who did not have any attacks in the first part of the study changed to receiving lanadelumab injections every 4 weeks instead of every 2 weeks. This helped researchers understand if these children could still be protected if they had lanadelumab treatment less often. What are the results of the SPRING Study? Lanadelumab prevented HAE attacks in the children during the study. Before starting lanadelumab treatment, all 21 children had at least 1 HAE attack in the previous 3 months, and each child had an average of 24 attacks each year. While they were receiving treatment, 16 of 21 children did not have any HAE attacks. After 1 year of lanadelumab treatment, each child had on average about 1 attack each year. The average duration of an HAE attack in the children receiving lanadelumab was also half as long as before they started lanadelumab treatment. The most common side effect was mild pain at the site of the lanadelumab injection. This happened in 6 of the 21 children. Most of the children had a better quality of life after starting lanadelumab treatment. What do the results of the SPRING Study mean? These results suggest that lanadelumab treatment is safe and works well to help prevent HAE attacks in children aged 2 to 11 years. Children in this age group are likely to benefit from taking lanadelumab treatment when their doctor thinks it is the most suitable medicine for them. After seeing the results of the SPRING Study, many medical agencies around the world agreed that lanadelumab could be used in children as young as 2 years of age. Where can I find the original article on which this summary is based? The original article is called "Lanadelumab in patients 2 to less than 12 years old with hereditary angioedema: results from the phase 3 SPRING Study." You can read the article that was published in the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology: In Practice in 2024 for free here: https://www.jaci-inpractice.org/article/S2213-2198(23)01019-X/fulltext Who is this article for? The aim of this plain language summary is to help people without specialist knowledge of HAE to understand the findings of the SPRING Study. Who sponsored the study? The SPRING Study was sponsored by Takeda Pharmaceuticals.

articles.title: Omalizumab Efficacy, Drug Survival and Clinical and Serological Biomarkers in Chronic Inducible Urticaria.
articles.abstract: Chronic inducible urticaria is treated with offlabel omalizumab in antihistamine-refractory cases, although real-world evidence on its long-term efficacy, drug survival and predictive biomarkers is limited. The aim was to evaluate the real-world efficacy and long-term drug survival of omalizumab in chronic inducible urticaria and to identify clinical and serological predictors of response and persistence. This retrospective, multicentre study included 144 patients with isolated chronic inducible urticaria treated with omalizumab. At 6 months, 73% of patients achieved complete or good disease control. Solar urticaria showed a higher rate of complete control (69%), with a significantly higher rate than symptomatic dermographism (32%; p=0.0246). Most patients were fast responders (83%) and 26% required updosing. Higher body mass index was associated with lower complete control [odds ratio (OR) 0.92; p=0.049] and a greater likelihood of dose escalation (OR 1.11; p=0.019). Overall drug survival was 95%, 87.5% and 72.4% at 1, 2 and 5 years, respectively. Discontinuation occurred in 33% of patients, primarily due to remission (50%). Exploratory analyses did not identify robust predictors of cause-specific discontinuation. In conclusion, omalizumab is effective and well tolerated in chronic inducible urticaria, providing sustained control and long-term drug survival; however, baseline clinical and serum biomarkers did not predict treatment response or drug survival.

articles.title: Liver and spleen stiffness by 2D shear-wave elastography for identifying high-risk varices in cirrhosis: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the performance of liver and spleen stiffness measurement (LSM and SSM) by two-dimensional shear-wave elastography (2D-SWE) in ruling out high-risk esophageal varices (HRVs) and their utility in predicting other portal hypertension-related gastroduodenal lesions and liver-related events (LREs) in patients with cirrhosis.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled consecutive adult patients with cirrhosis undergoing screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) between 2023 and 2025 at Chulalongkorn University Hospital, Thailand. LSM and SSM were acquired using 2D-SWE (Supersonic Mach 30) within 2 days of EGD by a single blinded operator. HRVs were defined endoscopically as medium-to-large varices or small varices with red wale markings.
RESULTS: 169 consecutive patients with cirrhosis were enrolled. Of these, 77 (45.6%) and 40 (23.7%) patients had esophageal varices (EVs) and HRVs, respectively. Leading cirrhosis causes were hepatitis B and C virus (n = 66, 39.1%). At thresholds to maximize specificity while maintaining sensitivity ≥ 90%, LSM < 13.7 kPa and SSM < 37.6 kPa by 2D-SWE could spare EGD in 36.7% and 44.4%, respectively, with corresponding missed HRV rates of 4.8% and 4%. Moreover, 2D-SWE-derived LSM and SSM yielded AUCs of 0.778 and 0.844 for HRVs, 0.742 and 0.785 for EVs, and 0.766 and 0.724 for portal hypertensive gastropathy (all p < 0.001). In multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis, Child-Pugh score and LSM by 2D-SWE were independently associated with the development of LREs within 1 year.
CONCLUSION: LSM and SSM using 2D-SWE may help reduce the need for screening EGD in patients with cirrhosis, with observed missed-HRV rates of 4.8% and 4.0%, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of 2D-SWE for variceal risk stratification, particularly where vibration-controlled transient elastography is unavailable. The proposed cutoffs require external validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Schwannomas Visible on the Skin: Clinicopathological Characteristics and Treatment.
articles.abstract: Clinical information on schwannomas that are visible on the skin as (sub)cutaneous lesions is very limited. In this article, we provide clinicopathological information about cutaneous schwannomas and (deeper located) visible noncutaneous schwannomas including diagnostic methods, treatments, surgical complications and follow-up. This retrospective observational study includes data from 191 cases obtained from electronic healthcare records within a large teaching hospital with regional neurosurgical expertise. We show that 114 cutaneous and 77 visible noncutaneous schwannomas were painful (83%), slow-growing (68%), skin-coloured (48%) nodules (83%) on the head/neck and upper extremities (58%). Common features included pain after local pressure (72%), radiating pain (45%), tingling after percussion (63%) and mobility (88%). Imaging was performed in 63% (mainly ultrasound and MRI); pretreatment histologic examination in 9%. Excision was performed in 64%, intracapsular microenucleation in 31%. Complications occurred in 15% (8% in cutaneous schwannomas and 23% in visible noncutaenous schwannomas), most commonly sensory nerve deficits (12%). In conclusion, this study shows that visible schwannomas primarily present as painful, skin-coloured, mobile nodules on the head/neck and arms. Invasive treatment by excision and intracapsular microenucleation resulted in complications in 15% of patients, most commonly sensory nerve deficits. These occurred more often in deeply located visible noncutaneous schwannomas.

articles.title: Two international Delphi surveys on labels and descriptors to inform the new classification criteria for juvenile idiopathic arthritides.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Developing an evidence-based classification of the group of juvenile idiopathic arthritides (JIA) is a topic of high relevance. A two-round international Delphi survey was conducted among paediatric rheumatologists to identify the most appropriate names (labels) and the most relevant descriptors used by physicians to define JIA categories.
METHODS: In Delphi 1, participants reported with open-ended responses the descriptors they used to identify JIA categories, and whether and how, these categories should be re-labelled. In Delphi 2, respondents ranked the top three disease labels and the top 10 disease descriptors that emerged from Delphi 1 from best to worst for each JIA category; a weighted score was calculated multiplying the sum of ranks for the selection frequency.
RESULTS: Overall, 330 and 470 physicians responded to Delphi 1 and Delphi 2, respectively. The highest-ranking labels and descriptors were: 'juvenile-onset Still's disease' and response to IL-1 inhibitors for systemic arthritis, 'RF or ACPAs positive JIA' and RF/ACPA positivity for RF-positive polyarthritis; 'polyarticular JIA' and age at onset <18 years for RF-negative polyarthritis; 'juvenile PsA' and dactylitis for psoriatic arthritis (PsA); 'early-onset spondyloarthritis' and HLA-B27 positivity for enthesitis-related arthritis, 'oligoarticular JIA' and ANA positivity for oligoarthritis, 'early-onset ANA-positive arthritis' and ANA positivity with RF negativity for early-onset ANA-positive arthritis; and 'undifferentiated JIA' and arthritis fitting more than one category for undifferentiated arthritis.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies the category labels and descriptors to be prioritized in the future development of the new JIA classification criteria.

articles.title: DiaMEETes: A Collective Narrative and Play-Based Group Intervention for Children Aged 8-10 Living With Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Children aged 8-10 living with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) may experience emotional distress, isolation, and difficulties adjusting to diabetes management. While collective narrative practice groups have been adapted successfully for older children with T1D, a developmentally appropriate intervention for younger children was needed. This paper describes DiaMEETes, a multidisciplinary group intervention combining collective narrative practices, play, and peer support. DiaMEETes was co-developed with young people with lived experience of T1D and delivered within a paediatric psychology service. Activities aimed to externalise diabetes, strengthen identity beyond illness, foster peer connection, and build hope. Thirty children aged 8-11 attended between 2021 and 2025. Quantitative and qualitative feedback was collected from children and parents/carers and analysed using thematic analysis. Seventy-two percent of attendees rated the group 10/10 and 89% would recommend it to others. Five themes were identified: connection and shared experiences, enjoyment of activities, finding hope and strength, valuing peer trainers, and ideas for future groups. Parents reported increased confidence, pride, and acceptance in their children. DiaMEETes highlights the value of developmentally tailored collective narrative interventions within paediatric diabetes services.

articles.title: Concurrent Oximetry and Transcutaneous Carbon Dioxide Monitoring to Screen for Paediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnoea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) diagnosis requires polysomnography (PSG) which can be difficult to access due to wait times. Concurrent oximetry and transcutaneous carbon dioxide (TcCO2) monitoring is used in our sleep unit to triage patients, but its diagnostic utility has not been formally evaluated. The objective of the study was to assess whether adding TcCO2 to overnight oximetry improves screening accuracy for paediatric OSA when compared to a full PSG scored according to the American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) guidelines.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of 172 consecutive overnight PSGs performed at the Children's Hospital at Westmead. Three independent sleep consultants scored deidentified oximetry traces (Phase 1), then the same traces with concurrent TcCO2 (Phase 2). Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) with 95% Wilson confidence intervals were calculated for the senior clinician's impression against the PSG-based AASM diagnosis. Univariate logistic regression identified individual predictors of OSA.
RESULTS: The diagnosis of OSA within the study cohort was 77.3% (133/172). Oximetry alone yielded sensitivity 0.865 (95% CI 0.796-0.913) and NPV 0.514 (0.359-0.666). Adding TcCO2 without a structured scoring framework reduced sensitivity to 0.629 (0.544-0.706) and NPV to 0.310 (0.214-0.425), with non-overlapping confidence intervals. The strongest predictor of OSA was concurrent carbon dioxide (CO2) retention with oxygen (O2) desaturation (OR 9.83, 95% CI 2.88-33.54). Overall inter-rater agreement was poor (weighted κ = 0.13), which reflects lack of clearly defined diagnostic criteria. Concurrent CO2 and O2 events, CO2 rise above baseline of 5-9 mmHg, and episodic CO2 retention are the strongest identifiable predictors of OSA.
CONCLUSIONS: TcCO2 adds extra information to oximetry traces. However, without an established scoring system, adding CO2 traces reduces sensitivity of diagnosing OSA. Further research needs to be conducted in developing and validating a scoring system to interpret CO2 traces.

articles.title: Metabolic Acidosis in Children with Glomerular Disease: Nephrotic Syndrome Study Network (NEPTUNE) and Cure Glomerulonephropathy (CureGN).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic acidosis is linked to faster kidney function decline in children with CKD, especially in those with glomerular CKD who are more likely to have untreated acidosis. Unlike prior cohorts limited to children with established CKD, our cohort consisted of 786 children with glomerular disease and largely preserved kidney function at enrollment. We studied the prevalence, factors associated with acidosis, and the impact of unresolved acidosis on eGFR decline.
METHODS: Children aged 1-17 years from NEPTUNE or CureGN were included. Acidosis was defined as serum bicarbonate <22 mEq/L. Unresolved acidosis was defined as acidosis at baseline that remained <22 mEq/L, and resolved acidosis was defined as baseline acidosis that reached ≥22 mEq/L on follow-up. Associations of acidosis with demographic and clinical characteristics were assessed. The primary outcome eGFR slope (ml/min/1.73m2/year) was analyzed using an adjusted linear mixed-effects model. Secondary analysis examined associations of acidosis with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA).
RESULTS: Mean baseline serum bicarbonate was 24.8±3.2 mEq/L and median eGFR was 97 ml/min/1.73m2 (IQR: 81, 117). The prevalence of acidosis was 12% (n=96), and only 4% of children with acidosis were receiving alkali therapy at baseline. Children with unresolved acidosis had a greater decline in eGFR compared to those with resolved acidosis, with a difference in eGFR slope of -4.05 ml/min/1.73m2/year (95%CI: -5.62, -2.47), independent of disease diagnosis and proteinuria. The degree of IFTA was not significantly associated with categories of serum bicarbonate (P = 0.61).
CONCLUSIONS: Unresolved metabolic acidosis was associated with a faster eGFR decline in children with glomerular disease. Acidosis was not associated with baseline IFTA, suggesting it may not simply reflect pre-existing fibrosis. Further studies are needed to clarify mechanisms linking metabolic acidosis with kidney disease progression and to identify patients who may benefit from targeted interventions.

articles.title: Developmental dynamics of strength and gait asymmetries in hemiparetic cerebral palsy: Findings from a 2-year cohort with biannual assessments.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize the longitudinal relationship between lower limb strength asymmetry and gait asymmetry in children with hemiparetic cerebral palsy (CP) over a 2-year period using biannual assessments.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 29 children with hemiparetic CP (mean age, 13.45 ± 3.15 years; Gross Motor Function Classification System levels I-II). Participants were assessed biannually for lower limb strength asymmetry indices (SAI) and Spatial/Temporal Gait Asymmetry Indices (GAI). Data were analyzed using Linear Mixed-Effects (LME) models, Repeated Measures Correlations, two-wave Cross-Lagged Panel Models (CLPM) (baseline to 24 months), and trajectory analysis.
RESULTS: LME models revealed significant positive associations between baseline SAIs and Spatial GAI for hip flexors (β = 0.625, p < .001), hip abductors (β = 0.470, p < .001), knee extensors (β = 0.216, p = .023), ankle dorsiflexors (β = 0.557, p < .001), and plantarflexors (β = 0.203, p = .016). Similar associations were found for Temporal GAI (β = 0.347-0.544, all p < .001). Repeated measures correlations showed strong associations for all muscle groups (r = 0.579-0.769, all p < .001), with the strongest for ankle plantarflexors (Spatial: r = 0.769; Temporal: r = 0.734). CLPMs demonstrated that baseline SAI significantly predicted future GAI for hip flexors (Spatial: β = 0.347; Temporal: β = 0.312), knee extensors (Spatial: β = 0.435; Temporal: β = 0.391), and ankle plantarflexors (Spatial: β = 0.408; Temporal: β = 0.382) (all p < .001), while reverse pathways were generally non-significant. Trajectory analysis confirmed a progressive decline in all asymmetry scores over 24 months.
CONCLUSIONS: Strength asymmetry significantly predicts the longitudinal course of gait asymmetry in children with hemiparetic CP, with muscle-specific temporal precedence. Targeted interventions addressing hip flexor, knee extensor, and ankle plantarflexor strength asymmetries may optimize gait outcomes.

articles.title: Preliminary postural responses to an immersive VR exergame in children with unilateral cerebral palsy: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Game-based VR interventions have been proposed as a promising tool to enhance motivation and engagement in pediatric rehabilitation. However, there remains insufficient knowledge regarding the therapeutic use of immersive VR systems in this population. This study aimed to evaluate the preliminary postural responses to an immersive virtual reality (VR) exergame‑based intervention on postural control in children with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Fifteen participants with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP) (6 female and 9 male) were included in this pilot study. Static postural stability and foot contact area measurements were recorded before and after 15-minute sessions performed in both the real-game (RG) and immersive virtual reality (VR) environments.
RESULTS: Linear mixed model analyses indicated that none of the pedobarographic contact area variables or center of pressure (CoP)-based postural stability measures showed significant effects of time (before vs. after), environment (immersive virtual reality [VR] vs. real-game [RG]), or their interaction (all p > .05). Although 64.3% of participants reported greater discomfort during the virtual reality condition, 86.7% expressed a preference for it.
CONCLUSION: A single session of immersive virtual reality (VR) gameplay did not result in significant immediate changes in postural control measures in children with unilateral cerebral palsy (UCP). Despite reporting some discomfort, most participants preferred the immersive VR experience, supporting its feasibility and acceptability for further investigation in pediatric rehabilitation.

articles.title: Effects of Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including Lower Extremities (HABIT-ILE) on activity and participation outcomes in children with cerebral palsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of Hand-Arm Bimanual Intensive Therapy Including Lower Extremities (HABIT-ILE) on activity and participation outcomes in children with cerebral palsy, within the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health framework and assess the certainty of evidence.
DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE, PubMed, Cochrane Library, Scopus, OTseeker, Web of Science, and grey literature sources were searched from January 2014 to June 23, 2026.
REVIEW METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines. Experimental studies evaluating HABIT-ILE in participants aged 0-18 years with cerebral palsy were included. Outcomes were mapped to ICF domains; activity outcomes included bimanual hand performance, gross motor function and mobility, daily activity performance, and occupational performance, whereas participation outcomes reflected involvement in life situations. Random-effects meta-analyses included peer-reviewed RCTs when at least three provided comparable immediate post-intervention data for the same construct and outcome measure/domain. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, ROBINS-I, and NHLBI tools, and certainty using GRADE.
RESULTS: Nineteen studies involving 704 participant records were included, comprising 18 peer-reviewed studies and one preprint. Meta-analysis of randomized trials showed significant improvements in activity-level occupational performance measured using the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM-Performance) (MD 3.83, 95% CI 3.00 to 4.66; I2 = 78%) and daily activity performance measured using the Pediatric Evaluation of Disability Inventory-Computer Adaptive Test (PEDI-CAT) Daily Activities domain (MD 1.66, 95% CI 0.09 to 3.24; I2 = 51%). No statistically significant pooled effect was found for the Gross Motor Function Measure-66 (GMFM-66) or PEDI-CAT Mobility. Bimanual hand performance assessed using the Assisting Hand Assessment (AHA) or Mini-AHA was synthesized narratively because the measures were not directly interchangeable and subgroup-specific data were unavailable. Certainty of evidence ranged from low to moderate. Participation outcomes assessed primarily using the Young Children's Participation and Environment Measure (YC-PEM) and Life-H were synthesized narratively.
CONCLUSION: HABIT-ILE may improve occupational and daily activity performance. Narrative evidence suggests potential improvements in bimanual hand performance, whereas effects on gross motor function and mobility remain inconclusive. Evidence for participation outcomes remains limited and heterogeneous.

articles.title: Correlation between albumin and protein excretion in first morning, random spot, and 24-h urine specimens in children with glomerular diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quantifying proteinuria and albuminuria is essential for managing glomerular diseases. Although 24-h urine collection is ideal, spot specimens are more practical in children. Pediatric and adult guidelines recommend spot urine protein-to-creatinine ratios (PCR) and 24-h urine albumin-to-creatinine ratios (ACR), respectively. Correlations between these measures require validation in pediatric glomerular diseases.
METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study examined the correlations of first morning and random spot urine ACR and PCR with 24-h proteinuria and albuminuria. Consecutive patients, 3-18 years old with glomerular diseases, estimated GFR > 30 ml/min/1.73 m2 and dipstick protein trace or more, were enrolled. ACR, PCR, and dipstick were measured on the first morning spot, random spot, and 24-h samples. Pairwise correlations and limits of agreement were examined across proteinuria categories using log-transformed variables. Receiver operating characteristic curves determined optimal ACR thresholds for clinical decision-making.
RESULTS: From September 2023 to March 2025, 169 patients (66.9% boys) were enrolled. First morning spot ACR and PCR correlated strongly with 24-h proteinuria (respective r = 0.85 and 0.92) and 24-h ACR (respective r = 0.95 and 0.91); random ACR and PCR correlated similarly (all P < 0.0001). Bland-Altman analysis found variable agreement between measures across the proteinuria range. ACR thresholds of 1540 and 77 mg/g corresponded best to PCR of 2 mg/mg and 0.2 mg/mg, respectively. Semi-quantitative dipsticks categorized proteinuria and/or albuminuria imprecisely.
CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric glomerular diseases, first-morning and random spot urine PCR and ACR correlate strongly with their respective 24-h measurements. Since agreement varied across the range of proteinuria, the measures should not be considered interchangeable without further validation.

articles.title: Sensory-Perceptual impairments and adaptive functioning in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral palsy (CP) is traditionally conceptualized as a disorder of movement and posture resulting from early brain injury. However, increasing evidence highlights that sensory-perceptual impairments may play a fundamental role in adaptive functioning and social participation. Despite this, explanatory models of CP continue to focus primarily on motor dysfunction.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the relative contribution of neuromotor and sensory-perceptual impairments to adaptive functioning in children and adolescents with CP and related neurodevelopmental conditions.
METHODS: A cross-sectional retrospective observational study was conducted with 131 children and adolescents (48.9% females), aged 6-17 years (M = 11.18, SD = 3.59). Following their established medical diagnoses, participants were classified into CP and related conditions groups and were assessed using the Gross Motor Function Classification System and the Bobath Foundation Scale. Hierarchical regression analyses were performed to determine whether perceptual-motor functioning accounted for additional variance in functional autonomy, communication and language, and cognitive competence beyond neuromotor impairment.
RESULTS: In the CP group, neuromotor impairment was the strongest predictor of functional autonomy (β = .624, p < .001), whereas perceptual-motor functioning made a smaller but significant additional contribution (β = .347, p < .001; ΔR2 = .058). In the related conditions group, perceptual-motor functioning showed a stronger association with functional autonomy (β = .597, p < .001) than neuromotor impairment (β = .287, p = .017; ΔR2 = .188). For communication and language, perceptual-motor functioning emerged as the only significant predictor in both groups (CP: β = .872, p < .001, ΔR2 = .367; related conditions: β = .984, p < .001, ΔR2 = .511), whereas neuromotor impairment was no longer significant after its inclusion in the model. A similar pattern was observed for cognitive competence, with perceptual-motor functioning accounting for substantial additional variance beyond neuromotor impairment (CP: β = .947, p < .001, ΔR2 = .433; related conditions: β = 1.041, p < .001, ΔR2 = .573).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that adaptive functioning in CP is associated not only with motor impairment but also with sensory-perceptual functioning. Assessment and rehabilitation approaches should therefore address perceptual-motor processes alongside traditional motor-focused interventions.

articles.title: Kidney phenotype and clinical course in children with AMN-related Imerslund-Gräsbeck syndrome: a multicenter cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney manifestations of Imerslund-Gräsbeck syndrome (IGS) caused by pathogenic AMN variants remain poorly characterized. We aimed to describe the kidney phenotype and clinical course in children with AMN-related IGS presenting with proteinuria.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort included nine children with homozygous pathogenic AMN variants followed at six pediatric nephrology centers in Turkey. Initial presentations occurred between 2009 and 2024; clinical, laboratory, genetic, and follow-up data were reviewed.
RESULTS: Median age at diagnosis was 41 months (range, 4-97), and median follow-up was 30 months (range, 12-171). Five patients presented with vitamin B12 deficiency-related manifestations, three with isolated urinary abnormalities, and one through family screening. Persistent subnephrotic-range proteinuria was present in all patients; median uPCR was 1.2 mg/mg at admission and 0.88 mg/mg at last follow-up. One patient had a 25% eGFR decline from 144 to 108 mL/min/1.73 m², but final eGFR remained >90 mL/min/1.73 m² in all patients. No patient developed stage 2 or more advanced CKD, nephrotic syndrome, or required kidney replacement therapy. Six patients received RAS inhibitors; changes in uPCR were heterogeneous, and treatment efficacy could not be determined. Eight patients carried homozygous c.208-2 A > G, whereas one harbored the novel c.354 G > A (p.Trp118*) variant.
CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter cohort of children with AMN-related IGS presenting with proteinuria, persistent subnephrotic-range proteinuria was accompanied by generally preserved kidney function during the observed follow-up. Early genetic diagnosis may help avoid unnecessary kidney biopsy and inappropriate immunosuppressive treatment.

articles.title: Effects of pelvic kinesiology taping on functional mobility, muscle strength, and postural balance in children with spastic cerebral palsy: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pelvic dysfunction in spastic cerebral palsy, particularly excessive anterior pelvic tilt and hip abductor weakness, has been associated with gait disturbance. Although kinesiology taping has been applied to various body regions in this population, evidence regarding the effects of pelvic kinesiology taping on functional mobility, hip abductor strength, and postural balance remains limited.
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the short-term effects of pelvic kinesiology taping combined with neurodevelopmental treatment on functional mobility, muscle strength, and postural balance in children with spastic cerebral palsy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-blind (assessor-blinded) randomized controlled trial was conducted with 30 children with cerebral palsy (Gross Motor Function Classification System levels I-II, aged 6-12 years). This study was registered at the Clinical Research Information Service (registration number: KCT0010852). Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to an experimental group (neurodevelopmental treatment + pelvic taping) or a control group (neurodevelopmental treatment only). Both groups received treatment twice weekly for four weeks. The final analysis included 29 participants (experimental group, n = 15; control group, n = 14). Functional mobility was assessed with the Timed Up and Go test (TUG), hip abductor strength was measured using a hand-held dynamometer, and postural balance was evaluated using the Pediatric Balance Scale.
RESULTS: Significant group × time interactions were observed for functional mobility (p = .035, η2p = 0.179) and hip abductor muscle strength (p = .016, η2p = .212). The between-group differences in change were 1.43 seconds for TUG (95% CI, 0.12 to 2.74) and 0.16 N/kg for hip abductor strength (95% CI, 0.03 to 0.28). No significant group × time interaction was found for postural balance (p = .088, η2p = 0.104).
CONCLUSION: This study found that adding pelvic kinesiology taping to neurodevelopmental treatment may be associated with additional short-term improvements in functional mobility and hip abductor strength in children with spastic cerebral palsy classified as GMFCS levels I-II, whereas no additional balance effect was detected. Its ease of application and potential for continued support during daily activities may offer practical advantages in pediatric rehabilitation settings.
STUDY REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service (registration number: KCT0010852).

articles.title: Impact of donor size on short- and long-term outcomes in pediatric kidney transplant recipients: where is the mismatch limit? Analysis of the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: The impact of kidney size mismatch on outcomes after pediatric kidney transplantation remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of donor-recipient height mismatch on short- and long-term outcomes in pediatric kidney transplant recipients.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR), including pediatric kidney transplant recipients between 2010 and 2020. The primary endpoint was graft loss; secondary endpoints were overall survival, acute rejection, and kidney function. Hazard ratios were calculated using Fine and Gray's proportional subdistribution hazards models.
RESULTS: A total of 5321 patients were included (mean age 10.4 ± 5.2 years). A higher donor to recipient height ratio was associated with an increased risk of graft loss (HR 1.90; 95% CI 1.09-3.30; p = 0.023). However, this adverse effect decreased with increasing recipient age (interaction age × HD/Rr: HR 0.93; 95% CI 0.88-0.99; p = 0.016). No significant differences were observed regarding acute rejection or overall survival.
CONCLUSION: Donor-recipient height mismatch increases the risk of graft loss in children; but this adverse effect diminished with recipient age. While height matching should be prioritized in early childhood, flexible allocation, including the use of larger adult living donor organs, remains a sound clinical strategy in children with chronic kidney disease stage 5, as the benefits of transplantation outweigh the risk of size mismatch.

articles.title: Residential altitude and early childhood obesity: a nationwide ecological study from Colombia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is an emerging public health challenge shaped by environmental and socioeconomic factors. Although high-altitude hypoxia has been associated with metabolic adaptations in adults, its relationship with early childhood obesity at a population level remains unclear.
METHODS: We conducted a nationwide ecological study including 1123 municipalities in Colombia. Childhood obesity data for children aged 0-5 years were obtained from the national nutrition surveillance system, population denominators from official census projections and altitude data from national geographical registries. Municipal obesity prevalence was modelled using generalised linear models with binomial distribution and logit link, incorporating altitude as a continuous variable with a quadratic term and adjusting for socioeconomic indicators.
RESULTS: Obesity prevalence was highest in municipalities below 1000 m above sea level and lowest at intermediate-to-high altitudes (2000-3000 m). In multivariable models, altitude showed a significant non-linear association with childhood obesity. Higher unmet basic needs were associated with greater obesity prevalence, whereas extreme poverty was inversely associated. Similar patterns were observed in departmental capitals and in municipalities with smaller child populations.
CONCLUSIONS: Residential altitude was inversely associated with early childhood obesity prevalence at the municipal level. Although causal inference at the individual level is not possible, these findings suggest that environmental and structural contexts may contribute to geographical differences in early-life obesity patterns and support the development of geographically responsive public health strategies.

articles.title: Adolescent Substance Use and All-Cause Mortality Through Midlife in the US Nationally Representative Monitoring the Future Longitudinal Panel Study.
articles.abstract: Objectives. To examine whether adolescent substance use was associated with mortality. Methods. Mortality data on US nationally representative cohorts of high school classes surveyed in 1976 to 2019 were collected through 2026 in the Monitoring the Future Longitudinal Panel Study (n = 107 346). We estimated associations between age-18-years substance use (cigarettes, binge drinking, cannabis, other drugs) and all-cause mortality and time to death using logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models. Results. About 3.5% (n = 3773) were deceased by March 2026. Adolescent cigarette use, binge drinking, cannabis use, and other drug use were associated with likelihood of death and earlier age of death. With age-18-years covariates including sociodemographics and other substance use, use of cigarettes, cannabis, and other drugs remained statistically significantly associated with mortality; binge drinking was not statistically significantly associated with mortality when other substances were included. Conclusions. In a national study with data spanning 5 decades, substance use reported at age 18 years was associated with premature mortality. Public Health Implications. Adolescent substance use predicted mortality across decades of the life course. (Am J Public Health. Published online ahead of print November 19, 2026:e1-e5. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308838).

articles.title: Employing Implementation Science to Move from Paper to Practice.
articles.abstract: Implementation Science studies evidence practice gap separating innovation from clinical practice and designs interventions to close this gap. Process, determinant and evaluation frameworks provide a systematic way to ensure Implementation Science efforts are planned in a comprehensive and standardized format maintaining core components of the intervention but allowing for context-specific adaptations necessary for sustainment. Logic models provide a blueprint to allow for the operationalization of these models and frameworks. Otherwise, I would add one more sentence. Evaluation is a critical piece of all implementation science work from pre- to post-implementation and can be accomplished through evaluation frameworks. Future efforts are needed to close evidence to practice gaps that exist in the field of allergy-immunology, including crucial technological advancements proven to improve health outcomes.

articles.title: Associations Between Frequency of Smokeless Tobacco and Oral Nicotine Product Use and Suicidality Among High School Students in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Limited research has examined associations between adolescent smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use and suicidality. Even less is known about how these associations vary by frequency of use.
OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between frequency of smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use and suicidality among a nationally representative sample of high school students in the United States.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional study.
METHODS: Data from the 2023 Youth Risk Behavior Survey (n = 17,807) were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations between frequency of smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use (0 days, 1-5 days, 6-19 days, 20-30 days) and four outcomes: persistent sadness or hopelessness, suicidal ideation, suicide planning, and suicide attempt. Models adjusted for sex, race, ethnicity, grade, and alcohol use. Linear trends across frequency categories were tested. Sensitivity analyses adjusted for other tobacco product use.
RESULTS: Approximately 2% of students reported past 30-day smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use. Compared to no use, heavy use was associated with higher odds of all four outcomes (aORs = 2.11-9.64); moderate use was associated with higher odds of sadness or hopelessness, suicide planning, and suicide attempt (aORs = 2.14-4.91); and light use was associated with higher odds of suicide attempt (aORs = 2.92, 95% CI: 1.74-4.88). Positive linear trends were observed for all four outcomes (p <0.001). Sensitivity analyses showed that compared to no use, heavy use was associated with higher odds of suicide planning (aOR = 2.02, 95% CI: 1.23-3.30) and suicide attempt (aOR = 5.63, 95% CI: 2.67-11.88) and light use was associated with higher odds of suicide attempt (aOR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.03-2.77).
CONCLUSION: Frequency of smokeless tobacco and oral nicotine product use was associated with persistent sadness or hopelessness and suicidality. These associations were attenuated after adjusting for other tobacco product use. Longitudinal research is needed to establish temporal ordering.

articles.title: Association of Parenting Styles and Parental Involvement with the Mental Health of Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize quantitative evidence on associations among parenting styles, parental involvement, and mental health outcomes among adolescents with Type 1 diabetes.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) Extension for Scoping Reviews (ScR) guidelines. Literature published between January 1993 and May 2025 was searched across four databases (PubMed, CINAHL, Embase, and the Cochrane Library). Search terms included Medical Subject Headings (MeSH), title/abstract (ti/ab), and text words (tw). This review included only original quantitative studies examining relationships among parenting styles, parental involvement, mental health outcomes, and glycemic control in adolescents aged 10-19 years with Type 1 diabetes. Qualitative studies, mixed-methods studies, and review articles were excluded.
RESULTS: Out of 486 identified studies, 10 met the inclusion criteria, seven focusing on parent-child dyads and three on adolescents only. Across the included studies, supportive and collaborative parenting was consistently linked to fewer depressive symptoms, higher quality of life (QOL), greater self-efficacy, better adherence, and improved HbA1c levels. Conversely, controlling, overinvolved, or uninvolved parenting tended to be associated with increased depressive symptoms, lower QOL, and poorer glycemic control.
CONCLUSIONS: Parenting styles and parental involvement appear to be important factors associated with both psychological adjustment and glycemic control among adolescents with Type 1 diabetes. Although this review did not test a specific theoretical model, the findings can be interpreted through the lens of self-determination theory, underscoring the importance of autonomy support. Future research requires greater conceptual clarity and international standardization of autonomy support measures.

articles.title: Early Life Interventions in IgE-mediated Food Allergy Prevention and Management.
articles.abstract: Food allergy has become a major public health concern. Over the past decade, advances in understanding early immune development have transformed approaches to both prevention and treatment of IgE-mediated food allergy. Landmark trials demonstrated that early and sustained introduction of allergenic foods, particularly peanut and egg, significantly reduces the risk of food allergy. This lead to a paradigm shift from allergen avoidance to proactive early introduction. For children who develop food allergy, emerging evidence indicates that early intervention may offer unique advantages, possibly due to heightened immune plasticity. Oral, epicutaneous, and sublingual immunotherapy have shown efficacy in increasing allergen tolerance, with studies suggesting improved outcomes and greater likelihood of remission when initiated in early childhood. Mechanistic studies indicate that these therapies modify allergic immune responses through suppression of effector cells, induction of regulatory pathways, and increased production of protective allergen-specific antibodies. In addition, omalizumab has become the first biologic approved in the United States for food allergy in individuals aged ≥1 year. Despite substantial progress, important knowledge gaps remain. Continued integration of mechanistic discoveries, clinical trials, and real-world evidence will be essential to refine precision approaches that maximize prevention, improve treatment outcomes, and reduce the lifelong burden of food allergy.

articles.title: Earlier and More Criteria-Based Return to Sport After Pediatric Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction in North America Compared With the Asia-Pacific Region: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the management and rehabilitation strategies for pediatric anterior cruciate ligament injuries between North America and the Asia-Pacific region.
METHODS: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, a comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library was performed for studies published between January 2020 and August 2025. Articles were included if they described pediatric anterior cruciate ligament rehabilitation protocols for patients 18 years and younger. Included studies consisted primarily of retrospective studies, cohort studies, case series, technical notes, and cross-sectional studies (Levels II-IV). Data were extracted on bracing use and duration, weight-bearing status, range-of-motion restrictions, sports progression, and return-to-sport criteria.
RESULTS: Forty studies were included (27 North America, 13 Asia-Pacific). Bracing was used frequently in both North America (86%) and Asia-Pacific (72%), with North American protocols often specifying duration (2-6 weeks) or criteria-based discontinuation, whereas Asia-Pacific protocols frequently omitted details. Early range-of-motion restoration was advocated in both regions (North America 85%, Asia-Pacific 91%), although restrictions were applied when meniscal repair was performed. Both regions supported early weight-bearing regardless of surgical technique. Both regions shared similar timelines for running and jogging restrictions; however, North American centers (60%) introduced sport-specific drills earlier between 3 and 6 months. Return-to-sport clearance was delayed beyond 9 months in most protocols (North America 46%, Asia-Pacific 62%). North American center, however, showed more flexibility with 46% allowing return-to-sport clearance before 9 months. North American centers more often incorporated functional criteria (50%) alongside time-based measures, whereas Asia-Pacific centers relied primarily on time-based thresholds.
CONCLUSIONS: Early rehabilitation protocols after pediatric anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction were similar between North America and the Asia-Pacific region with respect to bracing, weight-bearing, and range-of-motion practices. However, return-to-sport progression differed because North American centers more frequently introduced sport-specific activities earlier and more commonly incorporated functional criteria in addition to time-based thresholds, whereas Asia-Pacific centers more often relied on time-based clearance and delayed sport-specific progression.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, systematic review of Level II to IV evidence.

articles.title: Maternal Substance Use During Pregnancy and Congenital Syphilis Among Hospitalized Neonates.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: US congenital syphilis (CS) cases have increased 10-fold in the past decade, exceeding 3700 cases in 2022. This study evaluated the association between maternal substance use during pregnancy and CS among hospitalized neonates by region and year.
METHODS: We analyzed hospitalized neonates (postnatal age ≤28 days) in the Kids' Inpatient Database from 2016, 2019, and 2022. We identified CS using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes and categorized maternal substance use as no substance use, single substance use, or polysubstance use. Using survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression, we tested effect modification by region and year.
RESULTS: Among 4 531 346 hospitalized neonates, 217 220 (weighted prevalence = 2.5%) had maternal substance use during pregnancy. CS prevalence among substance-exposed neonates increased 467% from 2.5 to 14.5 per 1000 neonates between 2016 and 2022, compared with 0.2 to 0.8 per 1000 neonates among unexposed neonates. After adjusting for demographic charateristics, health insurance status, median household income, housing insecurity, year, and region, single substance use and polysubstance use were associated with higher odds of CS (single substance use: adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 9.68; 95% CI, 8.88-10.55; and polysubstance use: AOR = 17.18; 95% CI, 15.21-19.40). We observed a significant effect modification: the association was much stronger in the West region of the United States (interaction OR = 4.80; 95% CI, 3.10-7.44) than in the Northeast, and the polysubstance use association was significantly elevated in 2022 relative to 2016 (interaction OR = 3.10; 95% CI, 1.81-5.30).
CONCLUSIONS: Maternal substance use was strongly associated with CS. These findings underscore the need to address structural barriers to prenatal care through the expansion and integration of syphilis screening within substance use treatment and harm-reduction contexts, especially in regions with a high burden of CS.

articles.title: Empathic Versus Informational Messaging and Expertise Cues in Search Ads for Suicide Prevention.
articles.abstract: Background: Search-based advertising is used as a digital outreach method to reach users searching for suicide-related terms. However, it remains unclear which ad message elements promote access to support information among users searching for terms related to life issues associated with suicide risk. Aims: We compared empathic and informational headlines and descriptions with and without expertise cues to examine ad message elements that promote access to support information among users searching for life issues. Method: Search-based advertising was displayed in Tokyo, Japan, to users searching for life-issue-related terms across six areas (perinatal women, domestic violence, addiction, depression, sexual minorities, and child abuse). Four ad types were created by combining headline type (empathic vs. informational) and description type (with vs. without an expertise cue). Outcomes were click rate and conversion rates for the three landing page actions (self-check, self-care, and consultation services). We fit mixed-effects binomial logistic regression models. Results: Empathic headlines were associated with higher odds of ad clicks and self-checks, while informational headlines were associated with higher odds of consultation services. Descriptions with expertise cues were associated with lower odds of self-care and consultation services. A headline × description interaction was observed for self-care with higher odds when an expertise cue was paired with an empathic headline. Limitations: As this study examined a limited set of ad elements in Tokyo and used Japanese-language ads and landing pages, conversion outcomes may have been influenced by the structure of the multifunctional landing page. Conclusion: Empathic headlines may promote ad clicks and self-check, whereas informational headlines may support access to consultation services. Expertise cues were not uniformly associated with greater engagement, and their associations varied by outcome and accompanying headline. These findings highlight the importance of tailoring ad messages to the behaviors they are intended to promote.

articles.title: Parent-Child Bonding Strengthens the Influence of Perceived Parental Approval or Disapproval of Adolescent Substance Use: Longitudinal Evidence Across Adolescence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perceived parental approval or disapproval of substance use and parent-child bonding are important family influences on adolescent substance use, yet the developmental mechanisms linking these factors to adolescent behavior remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study examined whether perceived parental approval or disapproval of substance use influences adolescent substance use through adolescents' substance use attitudes and whether this indirect association is moderated by parent-child bonding. Developmental differences were also examined.
DESIGN: Prospective longitudinal survey data were collected annually between 2004 and 2011 from 4,407 adolescents in 24 U.S. communities followed from Grades 6 to 12.
METHODS: Moderated mediation models with 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals and cluster-robust standard errors examined whether parent-child bonding moderated the indirect association between perceived parental approval or disapproval and adolescent past-month substance use through adolescents' substance use attitudes across early (Grades 6, 7, and 8) and later (Grades 9, 10, and 12) adolescence. Models adjusted for covariates and prior substance use.
RESULTS: Across both developmental periods, perceived parental approval was associated with more favorable adolescent substance use attitudes, which in turn were associated with more frequent subsequent substance use. Conversely, perceived parental disapproval was associated with less favorable attitudes and less frequent subsequent substance use. Closer parent-child bonds strengthened the association between perceived parental approval or disapproval and adolescents' attitudes. This moderating effect was stronger during early adolescence, although the mediated pathway was evident across both developmental periods.
CONCLUSION: Adolescents' substance use attitudes emerged as a key developmental mechanism linking family socialization processes to subsequent substance use across adolescence. Stronger parent-child bonds can amplify both the protective influence of perceived parental disapproval and the risk associated with perceived parental approval of substance use. Effective prevention and intervention efforts should therefore address both parental substance use norms and parent-child relationships.

articles.title: Magnitude and Burden of Substance Use Disorders Among Adolescents in Eastern Sub-Saharan Africa: Regional Analysis From Global Burden of Diseases 1990 to 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Substance use disorders are chronic conditions characterized by compulsive substance use despite adverse health consequences. However, low-resource settings have limited epidemiological data to inform policies. This study estimated the extent and impact of substance use disorders among adolescents in the Eastern Sub-Saharan African region from 1990 to 2023.
METHODS: The Global Burden of Diseases 2023 estimates, computational techniques, and tools were applied. Disease modelling with a Bayesian meta-regression (DisMod-MR 2.1) was used to estimate non-fatal health outcomes, while the cause of death ensemble model (CODEm) was employed to estimate the fatal health outcomes. Estimates were smoothed by applying the spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression (ST-GPR).
RESULTS: In 2023, there were an estimated 1135 prevalent cases per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 821-1510), 514 incident cases per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 360-697), 100 years lived with disability per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 62-147), 4 years of life lost per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 3-5), and 104 disability-adjusted life years per 100,000 adolescents (95% UI: 66-150). Males had higher rates than females in most countries. Except for an increase in disability-adjusted life years, the other rates remained stable between 1990 and 2023. Most rates increased in Eritrea and Ethiopia.
CONCLUSION: This study indicated that substance use disorders caused substantial morbidity and disability among adolescents in the Eastern Sub-Saharan African region over the past three decades. Moreover, males consistently experienced a greater health burden than females. Thus, gender-responsive interventions, integration of early detection, treatment, and rehabilitation services into primary healthcare, coordination of region-wide surveillance systems, and cross-border substance control can be recommended.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Predictors of Severe Anaphylaxis in Infants and Toddlers: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anaphylaxis in infants and toddlers is increasingly recognized, yet knowledge on its clinical characteristics and predictors of severe disease remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the demographic, clinical, and immunological characteristics of anaphylaxis in children aged 0-36 months and to identify factors associated with severe anaphylaxis.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 68 children aged 0-36 months diagnosed with anaphylaxis at a tertiary pediatric allergy center. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, and outcome data were analyzed, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with severe anaphylaxis.
RESULTS: The median age at presentation was 13.0 months (interquartile range [IQR], 7.0-23.0), and 58.8% of patients were male. Food was the leading trigger (80.9%), with tree nuts, hen's egg, and cow's milk being the most common allergens. Skin involvement was the predominant manifestation (94.1%), followed by respiratory and gastrointestinal involvement (both 57.4%). Respiratory involvement was more frequent in females, whereas gastrointestinal manifestations predominated in males. Non-atopic children had significantly higher rates of severe anaphylaxis, cardiovascular involvement, and multisystem reactions than atopic children. Non-food triggers were associated with a more severe clinical course. In univariate analysis, atopy was associated with lower odds of severe anaphylaxis, whereas drug-induced reactions had higher odds of severe disease than food-induced reactions. Neither atopy nor trigger category remained independently associated with severity after multivariable adjustment. All patients received intramuscular epinephrine under protocolized emergency care, and no biphasic reactions or fatalities occurred.
CONCLUSION: Anaphylaxis in children aged 0-36 months has distinct clinical characteristics. Although food remained the predominant trigger, non-food triggers and the absence of atopy were associated with a more severe clinical phenotype. However, no baseline atopic or trigger-related factor independently predicted severe anaphylaxis after multivariable adjustment, highlighting the challenges of risk stratification in this age group.

articles.title: Quality of Life During Oral Peanut Immunotherapy in the OPIA Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) findings have varied between peanut oral immunotherapy (OIT) trials. The objective of this study was to compare changes in the HRQoL between the OIT and standard (control) treatment groups during the OPIA peanut OIT double-blind randomised controlled trial and at long-term follow-up.
METHODS: OPIA was a single-centre, 3-arm, double-blind placebo-controlled trial of peanut OIT in children aged 10-16 years. Standardised questionnaires (FAQLQ, FAIM, FAQLQ-Parent Burden, PSS) and bespoke surveys were administered at 0, 6, 12 and 13.5 months, with 3-year follow-up. Changes in scores at different time points were analysed descriptively and using 2-tailed T tests. A GEE model investigated the interaction between change in HRQoL score, treatment (OIT vs. standard care) and time. 3 year follow-up surveys were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative analysis.
RESULTS: Sixty-five subjects were randomised and 61 participants completed the study. There was no evidence of difference in HRQoL score changes between the OIT and standard treatment groups from baseline to 12 months or 13.5 months. Furthermore, achieving OPIA's primary efficacy endpoint (tolerance of ≥ 1000 mg of peanut protein (cumulative dose 1449 mg) at month 13.5 double blind placebo-controlled food challenge was not associated with a more favourable change in FAQLQ from baseline to end of study. Changes in global FAQLQ-Parent proxy (FAQLQ-PF) scores from baseline to 12 months were less favourable for carers of children who had experienced treatment-related serious adverse events compared to those without such events (mean change 0.10 vs. -0.97, 0.0063).
CONCLUSIONS: OIT did not confer a HRQoL benefit over standard care in this cohort, based upon the tools used to assess HRQoL. Treatment-related serious adverse effects negatively impacted FAQLQ-Parent proxy scores.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Pregnant Women and Health Care Workers Regarding Antenatal Testing for HIV, Hepatitis B Virus, and Syphilis in Vietnam: Protocol for a Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis remains a preventable cause of fetal loss, neonatal morbidity, and long-term disability. In Vietnam (Viet Nam), although antenatal care coverage is high, gaps persist in the timing, uptake, and completion of screening and follow-up services for these infections.
OBJECTIVE: This study has 2 parallel population-specific objectives. Among women who recently gave birth, we will estimate completion of antenatal testing for HIV, hepatitis B virus, and syphilis and its associated factors with study-defined optimal testing (completion of all 3 tests during the first trimester). Among health care workers (HCWs), we will assess knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices and identify professional factors associated with good practice regarding antenatal screening and MTCT prevention.
METHODS: This multicenter, hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from June to September 2026 in 4 provincial hospitals in northern Vietnam. Women completed an interviewer-administered questionnaire after delivery, once clinically stable and before discharge. Antenatal testing was verified from maternal records, laboratory reports, or electronic records whenever available. HCWs completed a separate anonymous self-administered questionnaire during the same study period. The 2 participant groups were not matched. The primary outcome for women is completion of all 3 antenatal tests during the first trimester (study-defined optimal testing). The primary outcome for HCWs is good practice regarding the prevention of MTCT. The minimum target sample sizes were 601 women and 601 HCWs. Data will be analyzed separately for each group. Descriptive analyses will summarize knowledge, attitudes, and practices indicators and service uptake. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance will be used to identify factors independently associated with the primary outcomes.
RESULTS: The protocol received ethics approval on February 9, 2026. The study is funded by Thai Binh University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Hung Yen, Vietnam. Recruitment was conducted from June to September 2026. As of manuscript submission, 601 patients and 601 health care workers had been recruited. Data cleaning is planned for October 2026, followed by statistical analysis from November to December 2026. Dissemination of the first study results is planned for the first quarter of 2027.
CONCLUSIONS: The study will provide hospital-based evidence on completion of antenatal triple screening and provider practices. By prespecifying distinct outcomes for women and HCWs, the study is designed to identify actionable gaps while avoiding causal interpretation of cross-sectional associations.

articles.title: Lion Tracks: Protocol for a Microlongitudinal Feasibility Study of Health Behaviors and Emotional Dynamics in Mother-Child Dyads.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical activity, sleep, digital-media engagement, cognition, and emotional health become increasingly interconnected. However, reliance on retrospective self-report and low-frequency longitudinal designs limits understanding of how these domains relate within individuals and families in daily life. Few studies have integrated ecological momentary assessment (EMA), passive sensing, and wearable monitoring within mother-child dyads.
OBJECTIVE: Lion Tracks aims to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an integrated ambulatory monitoring protocol. Secondary exploratory aims are to characterize within-person, between-person, and dyadic temporal associations among health behaviors, physiological measures, cognition, and momentary anxiety.
METHODS: Lion Tracks is a prospective, observational, microlongitudinal feasibility study targeting 25 mother-child dyads (50 participants), with children aged 11-14 years. Participants complete baseline assessments, 4 weeks of ambulatory monitoring, and poststudy assessments. Garmin wearables monitor physical activity, sleep, heart rate, and heart rate variability. MetricWire (MetricWire, Inc) collects passive smartphone screen-on duration and timing and delivers repeated EMA of momentary affect, anxiety, context, and behaviors. Digital-media engagement characteristics are self-reported through EMA. Brief mobile cognitive testing assesses cognitive performance. A hybrid EMA design combines fixed, pseudorandom, and behavior-contingent assessments to capture daily experiences while limiting participant burden. Primary outcomes include recruitment, retention, acceptability, participant burden, wearable compliance, EMA completion, and data completeness. Descriptive statistics and CIs will summarize feasibility outcomes. Exploratory multilevel mixed-effects models will examine within-person and between-person associations, while time-lagged and cross-lagged analyses will explore temporal relationships and behavioral synchrony within dyads.
RESULTS: The study received approval from The Pennsylvania State University Institutional Review Board (STUDY00027664). Recruitment is ongoing, with 7 mother-child dyads enrolled as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by June 1, 2027. Analyses will follow completion of data collection.
CONCLUSIONS: Lion Tracks represents Phase 1 of a larger research program designed to progressively optimize ambulatory monitoring and subsequently incorporate mobile electroencephalography to examine neural correlates of daily behaviors, cognition, and emotional functioning. Findings will inform protocol refinement and assess the feasibility of a scalable, multimodal platform for future family-centered behavioral health research.
INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/107879.

articles.title: Examining the Effectiveness of a Dual Executive Function Training Package: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Executive function (EF) refers to the cognitive processes that enable goal-directed regulation of thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. Two interrelated domains are commonly distinguished: "cool" EF, which involves abstract cognitive processes, and "hot" EF, which involves regulation in emotionally or motivationally charged contexts. Children with special educational needs (SEN) frequently show difficulties across both domains, yet most interventions target one in isolation.
OBJECTIVE: The present study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a dual EF training package for 3 of the most prevalent SEN groups: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), specific learning difficulties (SpLD), and autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
METHODS: A total of 288 primary school students aged 6 to 12 years with a diagnosis of ADHD, ASD, or SpLD will be recruited. Participants will be randomly assigned to either an intervention or a waitlist control group, stratified by diagnosis. Each intervention group (n=48) will receive the dual EF training program. Participants in the waitlist control group will continue to receive usual educational and clinical support (standard care) during the study period and will be offered the dual EF program upon completion of the study. Preintervention and postintervention assessments will include neuropsychological tests of EF, teacher- and parent-reported behavioral ratings, and measures of disability impact, school satisfaction, and social participation.
