Changes in outcome measures will be examined using a mixed-design analysis, with diagnosis (ADHD, ASD, and SpLD) and group (experimental vs waitlist control) as between-participant factors and time (pretest vs posttest) as the within-participant factor. Baseline scores will be included as covariates where appropriate. The analysis will assess overall intervention effects and whether changes over time differ by intervention condition and diagnosis, with significant interactions followed by appropriate post hoc comparisons.
RESULTS: The study was funded by Advance Children Medical and Education Foundation Limited from September 2025 to December 2026 and received ethical approval. Recruitment commenced in early 2026, and 30 participants with ADHD, 30 with ASD, and 45 with SpLD had been enrolled by June 2026. Baseline assessments were completed for all participants. Further data collection and data analysis are scheduled for completion by early 2027, with the results to be submitted for publication thereafter.
CONCLUSIONS: This study will evaluate the effectiveness of a theme-based dual EF program that integrates hot and cool EF within a structured curriculum. Findings will provide evidence of the potential of this approach to support EF and related outcomes in children with SEN and may inform future research and inclusive educational practices.

articles.title: 'I Had Been Told I Couldn't [Become a Parent]': Variations of Sex Characteristics and Intersex Family-Building Between Bodily and Reproductive Autonomy.
articles.abstract: Family building is widely understood as a socially meaningful aspiration and a dimension of human rights. For intersex people, or people born with variations of sex characteristics (VSC), pathways to parenthood may be impacted by sociomedical factors that extend beyond those experienced by endosex individuals with infertility. This article explores family-building experiences among adults with VSC by analysing how participants re-imagine reproductive futures in the context of medical power, informational gaps and restrictive reproductive citizenship regimes. Drawing on 64 qualitative interviews with people with VSC, partners and clinicians, alongside a review of reproductive policy frameworks, we examine how biomedical infrastructures, legal regulations and childhood medical experiences overlap with family-building experiences. By foregrounding themes of hermeneutical injustice, embodied agency and reproductive citizenship, this article investigates how participants navigate reproductive futures while mobilising peer expertise and family-building strategies. Ultimately, this paper argues for healthcare and policy frameworks that affirm bodily autonomy and ensure equitable family-building support for people with VSC.

articles.title: Current practice in paediatric occupational therapy in Australia: A descriptive study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Australian paediatric occupational therapy has seen significant changes in the last 15 years, yet there have been no published studies in that time that explore current practice. This study aimed to examine and create a profile of current practices of Australian paediatric occupational therapists regarding application of theories and models, goal setting, assessment, intervention, professional development, and use of evidence.
METHODS: In this descriptive study, a purpose-designed online survey was distributed via social media, occupational therapy organisations, and researcher contacts. The survey was open between March and September 2023. The survey was approximately 25 minutes long and included fixed choice and open-ended questions. Descriptive and content analysis were conducted.
CONSUMER AND COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT: An advisory group of paediatric occupational therapists was involved in survey design and testing.
RESULTS: One-hundred and fifty-six surveys were fully completed. Participants predominantly worked in private practice (56.41%) and utilised National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS)/Early Childhood Intervention funding (71.15%). The most common diagnosis seen was autism spectrum disorder (84.62%). The most common theory used was developmental theory (80.00%). The most frequently used model was the Person, Environment, Occupation model (66.67%). The goal setting tool most used was the Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (81.15%). The most frequently used assessment was Sensory Profile 2 (71.23%). Participants identified that they most commonly focussed on fine motor training (77.93%), parent/caregiver education (69.66%), and goal directed training (68.28%) for intervention. Less than half (41.67%) reported being 'somewhat satisfied' with their access to professional development, but the majority reported being supported by their workplace in using evidence-based practice (90.38%).
CONCLUSION: Changes in current paediatric occupational therapy practice were identified, which were reflective of the change to funding via the NDIS and evidence supporting top-down interventions. An emphasis on measuring at the level of impairment remains a barrier to supporting and evaluating occupational performance and participation outcomes.

articles.title: Nonverbal reasoning in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy: associations with gross motor function, MRI, and EEG findings.
articles.abstract: To examine the association between gross motor function level and Raven's Colored Progressive Matrices (CPM) performance in children and adolescents with cerebral palsy (CP), compare CPM performance with typically developing participants, and explore associations with MRI and EEG findings. This multicenter cross-sectional study included 40 participants with CP and 20 comparison participants aged 10-17 years. CPM totals were converted to center-derived age-referenced scores; the upper available normative age band was applied above age 11.5 years. Gross motor function was classified with the GMFCS. Clinically indicated MRI and EEG findings were categorized using prespecified systems. Median CPM score was 72 (IQR 64-81) in the CP group and 98 (IQR 92-104) in the comparison group (adjusted difference -26.4, 95% CI -31.2 to -21.6). GMFCS level was inversely associated with CPM score (Spearman rho = -.78, 95% CI -.85 to -.68). Predominant white matter injury was associated with lower CPM scores. The adjusted association with epileptiform EEG abnormalities was inconclusive. CPM performance was associated with GMFCS level and MRI pattern, but the cross-sectional findings do not establish causality. Gross motor classification must not substitute for accessible neuropsychological assessment.

articles.title: Learning and memory profile in pediatric craniopharyngioma with and without associated sleep disturbance.
articles.abstract: Children and adolescents with craniopharyngioma are at increased risk for visual field cuts, endocrinopathies, associated sleep disturbances, and cognitive challenges. While general intellectual functioning tends to remain intact within this population, the sellar/suprasellar location of craniopharyngiomas can disrupt important neural pathways essential for learning and memory. This study examines rote verbal learning and memory profiles - including nuances in learning approaches and slopes - in a clinical sample of pediatric patients treated for craniopharyngioma. Furthermore, the role of sleep disturbance on these outcomes is also explored. Retrospective data were collected for 17 pediatric patients with craniopharyngioma and associated endocrinopathies who underwent neurosurgical resection and irradiation (for all but one). As hypothesized, specific deficits related to rote verbal learning and memory were noted for the sample despite average estimated intellectual and adaptive functioning, while more pronounced learning and memory deficits were observed in the subset with reported sleep disturbances. Learning slope stagnation and/or decline across trials was observed in 75% of the patients, while post-hoc analyses revealed heightened susceptibility to recency effects (with poorer recall from the middle of the list) and a non-statistically significant trend toward increased intrusion errors, despite preserved semantic clustering. Findings underscore the importance of targeted memory assessment and multidisciplinary sleep management in this population.

articles.title: Mid-term outcomes of medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction using suture tape in paediatric and adolescent population: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suture tape medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) reconstruction avoids tendon graft harvest, but outcomes in children are poorly reported. This study evaluated functional outcomes and complications in children and adolescents with recurrent patellar instability.
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 56 patients (77 knees; 40 female; mean age 14.3 years, range 8.2-17.7) underwent isolated suture tape MPFL reconstruction for recurrent instability at a tertiary centre between 2020 and 2025. Minimum follow-up was 6 months. The primary outcome was the Paediatric International Knee Documentation Committee (Pedi-IKDC) score at ≥6 months (available for 58 knees). Secondary outcomes were recurrent instability, extensor lag and other complications.
RESULTS: The mean Pedi-IKDC score improved from 49.6 (SD 13.9) to 79.6 (SD 16.9), a mean gain of 30.0 points (p < 0.001). Recurrent instability occurred in 5 of 77 knees (6.5%), one following trauma, despite trochlear dysplasia (Dejour B-D) in 79% of knees. An extensor lag was recorded in 17 of 65 knees (26.2%): 16 of these were 5-10° and resolved with physiotherapy within 3-6 months; one of approximately 25° is awaiting revision. Steroid injection for medial patellar pain was required in four knees (5.2%). No physeal complications were observed.
CONCLUSION: Suture tape MPFL reconstruction improved the Pedi-IKDC score by 30.0 points, more than three times the minimal clinically important difference, with recurrent instability (6.5%) comparable to tendon graft reconstruction in children and no physeal complications. Extensor lag (26.2%) was common but resolved with physiotherapy in all but one knee. Suture tape is a reasonable graft-free option; comparative studies are needed.

articles.title: Burn Management in Disasters.
articles.abstract: Burn disasters are uncommon but uniquely resource-intensive mass casualty events, requiring prolonged multidisciplinary care that can rapidly exhaust the limited number of verified burn centers and beds. This article reviews the epidemiology and injury patterns of burn disasters, burn-specific triage and transport principles, and system-level planning built on regional burn networks. It examines the American Burn Association's role in center verification, regional response plans, and national burn bed capacity monitoring, alongside federal support mechanisms. Acute resuscitation, damage-control operative strategies, temporary wound coverage, workforce augmentation, and pediatric considerations are addressed, together with ethical decision-making, long-term recovery, and emerging technologies.

articles.title: Care of Special Populations in Disasters.
articles.abstract: Disasters and mass casualty incidents disproportionately harm elderly, pediatric, and pregnant patients, yet most triage algorithms and preparedness plans are built around the healthy adult. This review examines the physiologic, anatomic, and social characteristics that make each population vulnerable, drawing on experience from Hurricane Katrina and contemporary armed conflict. For older adults, frailty, rather than chronologic age, drives outcomes, and polypharmacy complicates resuscitation. Children require age-adjusted triage, weight-based dosing, and protection from family separation. Pregnant patients require simultaneous maternal and fetal assessment, as the physiologic adaptations of pregnancy mask hemorrhage. Systems-level preparedness remains the strongest determinant of outcome.

articles.title: A diagnostic model for central precocious puberty in girls based on ultrasonic bone age and clinical indicators.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central precocious puberty is a common pediatric endocrine disorder in girls. The diagnostic gold standard, the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test, is invasive, limiting its widespread use. Ultrasound-based bone age assessment is radiation-free, but its diagnostic value within an integrated model remains unvalidated.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a diagnostic model integrating ultrasound bone age advancement (ΔBA_OA) with clinical and biochemical markers for the differential diagnosis of central precocious puberty in girls.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: 269 girls initially diagnosed with precocious puberty were enrolled. Based on GnRH stimulation test results, they were divided into central precocious puberty (n=66) and non-central precocious puberty (n=203) groups. Clinical data, pelvic ultrasound parameters, hormone levels, and ultrasound bone age parameters were collected. Independent predictors were identified using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by area under the curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA).
RESULTS: ΔBA_OA (odds ratio (OR)=61.05), basal luteinizing hormone (LH) (OR=8.76), and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) (OR=1.02) were independent predictors (all P<0.001). Standardized coefficients confirmed comparable contributions from ΔBA_OA (β=0.675) and LH (β=0.637). The model demonstrated good apparent discriminative ability (AUC=0.972, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.950-0.993). Bootstrap internal validation with 200 resampling iterations yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.968 (95% CI: 0.953-0.992), with a calibration slope of 0.906 and intercept of -0.015, indicating minimal overfitting and satisfactory calibration. The calibration curve showed good agreement (mean absolute error (MAE)=0.016), and DCA indicated positive net benefit. Discrimination remained high across subgroups (AUC 0.959-0.994), though subgroup estimates were exploratory and based on limited event numbers.
CONCLUSION: The proposed model incorporating ultrasound bone age parameter ΔBA_OA with clinical and biochemical markers showed preliminary evidence of apparent discriminative ability. The model is intended as an auxiliary screening tool that may help reduce unnecessary GnRH stimulation testing, but this requires prospective validation. External validation in multicenter, large-sample studies is warranted before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications after severe blunt liver trauma in children: a single-center retrospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-operative management is standard for hemodynamically stable pediatric blunt liver trauma, but the incidence and optimal surveillance for late intra-hepatic arterial complications remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To analyze late intra-hepatic arterial complications and their management in a cohort of children with severe blunt liver injury, to confirm a clinical protocol.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients younger than 18 years referred to a quaternary liver center for grade ≥3 blunt liver injury (American Pediatric Surgical Association grading). Demographic and clinical data, imaging findings, active arterial bleeding or pseudoaneurysm not suspected at presentation and/or not detected on initial computerized tomography, and surgical and interventional radiology procedures were collected.
RESULTS: Thirty-two patients (median age 14.9 years) with grade III (n=10), IV (n=5), and V (n=17) liver injuries were included. A total of 37 procedures were performed in 19 patients (59%), including peri-hepatic packing, early and delayed surgical explorations, angiography, and 12 embolizations in 11 patients. Overall survival was 100%. In 5 patients (16% of the cohort; all grade IV-V injuries), late intra-hepatic arterial complications were documented on elective follow-up computerized tomography at a median of 10 days after trauma (when patients were asymptomatic), and all were managed successfully by selective interventional radiology, without procedure-related complications. No deaths occurred in this series.
CONCLUSIONS: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications were not rare in children with grade IV-V liver injuries. These findings support considering computerized tomography in children with very severe hepatic trauma, around days 10-15 after trauma, to allow pre-emptive interventional radiology management.

articles.title: Abbreviated brain magnetic resonance imaging protocol using fluid-attenuated inversion recovery and diffusion-weighted imaging in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) protocols may reduce radiation exposure and sedation requirements in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and clinical adequacy of an abbreviated brain MRI (abMRI) protocol featuring fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included pediatric emergency department patients who underwent abMRI between July 2023 and July 2025. The protocol consisted of axial diffusion-weighted imaging and axial fluid-attenuated inversion recovery obtained with motion-resistant radial filling, with an acquisition time of approximately 220 s. Technical success and clinical adequacy were evaluated using image quality, emergency observation, pediatric neurology follow-up, and full-protocol MRI when clinically indicated.
RESULTS: Among 971 attempted examinations, diagnostic-quality images were obtained in 951, yielding a technical success rate of 97.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 96.8-98.7%). The mean age was 7.61±5.46 years, and 480 patients (50.5%) were boys. Of the 951 diagnostic examinations, 649 underwent no further neuroimaging. Full-protocol MRI was performed in 302 patients. Eight false-negative cases were identified. The overall clinical adequacy rate was 99.2% (943/951; 95% CI 98.4-99.6%). Clinically inadequate examinations were more frequent in patients with suspected intracranial hypertension (P<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Diffusion-weighted imaging- and motion-resistant radial FLAIR-based abMRI appears feasible and clinically adequate as an initial imaging approach for selected pediatric emergency neuroimaging indications. Full-protocol MRI remains preferable when intracranial hypertension is suspected.

articles.title: Association between latitude, temperature, sunshine hours, and sunshine rate and the incidence of type 1 diabetes in Hokkaido, Japan: an ecological study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the relationships between latitude, temperature, sunshine hours, and sunshine rate and the incidence of type 1 diabetes (T1D) in Hokkaido, Japan.
RESULTS: We analysed data from the Childhood IDDM Hokkaido Registry, including 458 paediatric T1D cases diagnosed before age 15 between 1959 and 1996. Regional incidence rates were calculated using census data, and meteorological variables were obtained from the Japan Meteorological Agency. Linear regression models examined correlations between T1D incidence and latitude, mean temperature, sunshine hours, and sunshine rate. T1D incidence exhibited regional variation, with the highest rate in Ishikari (1.32 per 100,000 person-years) and the lowest in Hiyama/Oshima (0.53 per 100,000 person-years). A positive association was observed between latitude and T1D incidence. Additionally, mean temperature correlated positively with incidence, suggesting a complex interplay between climatic factors. Lower annual sunshine hours and reduced sunshine rates were associated with increased T1D incidence, supporting the hypothesis that diminished sun exposure contributes to disease risk. Higher latitude and reduced sunshine exposure were associated with increased T1D incidence, highlighting the potential influence of sunlight availability and vitamin D status. Promoting adequate vitamin D levels and safe sun exposure may help mitigate T1D risk in high-latitude populations.

articles.title: Early Life Adversity and Adolescent Sleep: A Longitudinal Study Examining Associations Between Dimensions of Early Adversity and Adolescent Sleep Metrics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: A dimensional approach was utilized to examine associations between early environmental adversity (deprivation, unpredictability) and adolescent sleep metrics (average and night-to-night variability in bedtime, wake time, and sleep duration). We predict that greater deprivation and unpredictability are uniquely associated with worse adolescent sleep.
METHODS: In this study (N = 337), preschool unpredictability and deprivation were measured via home observation and parent report; adolescent sleep was measured by actigraphy. Multilevel structural equation modeling examined longitudinal associations between early adversity dimensions and adolescent sleep, controlling for sex, adolescent age, maternal education, preschool family income, and adolescent family income.
RESULTS: In independent models, greater deprivation was associated with more sleep duration variability (β = .18 [.01, .34]), greater bedtime variability (β = .30 [.14, .45]), and shorter average sleep duration (β = -.20 [-.35, -.03]); greater unpredictability was associated with shorter average sleep duration (β = -.21 [-.39, -.02]) and greater bedtime variability (β = .23 [.04, .40]). In the combined model, only greater deprivation (β = .26 [.09, .42]) was associated with greater bedtime variability, controlling for unpredictability.
CONCLUSIONS: While deprivation and unpredictability predict sleep independently, only deprivation played a unique role in adolescents' bedtime variability, beyond other aspects of early childhood adversity. Results inform early intervention and prevention efforts to promote healthy adolescent sleep.

articles.title: Robust Bayesian Variable Selection and Inference Under Misspecified Nonparametric Mixed Models in Longitudinal Studies.
articles.abstract: In high-dimensional longitudinal interaction studies, it is challenging to perform variable selection and statistical inference when the assumed interaction model is misspecified under heterogeneous disease phenotypes. Partially motivated by analyzing a subset of the Childhood Asthma Management Program (CAMP) data with high-dimensional single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) measurements, we develop a novel sparse robust Bayesian mixed model to capture nonlinear longitudinal interactions. In terms of both parameter estimation and statistical inference, the proposed mixed model is robust not only to outliers and heavy-tailed distributions in the response variable but also to misspecification of nonlinear interaction effects. We have developed a Gibbs sampler incorporating spike-and-slab priors to promote exact sparsity in the identification of appropriate forms of main and interaction effects. Simulation results reveal superior performance of the proposed fully robust Bayesian analysis in identification, estimation, and statistical inference compared with alternative methods. In particular, the proposed analysis enables exact statistical inference in misspecified interaction models by yielding Bayesian credible intervals with nominal coverage probabilities on finite samples. Application of the proposed and alternative methods to the CAMP study sheds novel insight into asthma etiology.

articles.title: Common household foods fail to mitigate button battery esophageal injury in infants: an ex vivo dynamic model study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Button battery (BB) ingestion is a life-threatening pediatric emergency, particularly in infants at high risk of severe esophageal injury. This study evaluated whether readily available household food could mitigate BB-induced esophageal injury in infants.
METHODS: A dynamic ex vivo porcine esophageal model simulating peristalsis, salivary flow, and body temperature was used. After insertion of a CR2032 lithium BB, 5 mL of agave syrup, soy drink, orange juice, ketchup, or honey was administered at 5, 15, and 25 min, then every 30 min for 2, 4, or 6 hours. Outcomes included macroscopic ulcer grade, histologic injury depth, esophageal pH, and residual battery voltage.
RESULTS: In this dynamic model, agave syrup, soy drink, and orange juice did not reduce ulcer severity or histologic injury compared with untreated controls (p>0.05). Ketchup markedly worsened injury, increasing ulcer grades and voltage loss at all time points (p<0.05). Protective effects suggested in static models for agave syrup and soy drink were not reproduced under dynamic conditions.
CONCLUSIONS: Common household foods do not protect against BB-induced esophageal injury in a ex vivo experimental model. Dynamic testing is essential before recommending food-based prehospital therapies.

articles.title: Patient and Caregiver Education in Inborn Errors of Immunity: Short-Term Changes After a Structured Booklet-Based Intervention.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess baseline disease-related knowledge among patients with IEI and caregivers and to explore short-term changes 2 months after the distribution of a structured educational booklet.
METHODS: This exploratory, uncontrolled, single-center, pilot pre-post survey study was conducted at a tertiary pediatric immunology center. Eligible respondents were adult patients with IEI, literate adolescents aged 14-17 years, and caregivers of pediatric patients. Respondents completed a researcher-developed 30-item questionnaire covering general knowledge, warning signs/manifestations, treatment awareness, and protective/preventive measures at baseline and 2 months after booklet distribution. Paired scores were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.
RESULTS: Fifty-one respondents completed both assessments: 33 patients with IEI and 18 caregivers. Mean respondent age was 34.55 ± 12.83 years, and 32 respondents were female. The median total score increased from 23 (interquartile range [IQR]: 19-25) to 25 (IQR: 20-27), with a median paired change of 1 point (IQR: 0-5, P <.001). Treatment awareness increased from 6 (IQR: 4-8) to 8 (IQR: 6-9, P <.001), and protective/preventive measures increased from 8 (IQR: 6-9) to 9 (IQR: 7-9, P = 0.009).
CONCLUSION: Questionnaire scores were higher 2 months after booklet distribution, mainly in treatment and prevention domains. These findings suggest that written educational materials may help identify and address selected knowledge gaps, particularly regarding immunoglobulin replacement therapy, home-based treatment, and preventive measures.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Cytomegalovirus Infection in a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to describe the clinical characteristics, epidemiology, and outcomes of children with active cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in a pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and to identify risk factors associated with mortality.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, medical records of patients admitted to a tertiary-level PICU between January 2015 and January 2023 were reviewed. Patients aged 1 month to 18 years with laboratory-confirmed CMV infection during PICU stay were included. Demographic, clinical, and outcome data were collected. Disease severity was assessed using pediatric risk of mortality (PRISM) and pediatric logistic organ dysfunction (PELOD) scores. Risk factors for mortality were analyzed using regression models, and the predictive value of CMV viral load was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.
RESULTS: During the study period, a total of 3320 patients were admitted to the PICU, of whom 79 (2.38%; 95% CI, 1.9-2.9) had laboratory-confirmed CMV infection. Nearly half of the patients (n = 36, 45.6%) were immunocompromised. Overall mortality was 25.3% (n = 20). The main cause of death was septic shock (85%, n = 17). In most non-survivors (80%, n = 16), CMV polymerase chain reaction remained positive prior to death. A PELOD score ≥ 3 independently predicted mortality (crude RR 3.42; 95% CI, 2.98-7.78). Each 1-point increase in PRISM score was independently associated with mortality (crude RR 1.12; 95% CI, 1.05-1.20). Cytomegalovirus viral load demonstrated poor discriminative performance for mortality prediction ( Area Under the Curve-AUC 0.57; 95% CI, 0.47-0.63).
CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of CMV infection in critically ill children was low but associated with high mortality. Organ dysfunction severity, particularly elevated PELOD scores, was a significant predictor of mortality. Pediatric risk of mortality score was statistically associated with mortality despite limited discriminative performance, whereas CMV viral load was not associated with mortality. These findings suggest that CMV infection in PICU patients likely reflects disease severity rather than being a direct determinant of outcome.

articles.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Surgical and Advanced Interventional Treatments for Pediatric Refractory Constipation: A Systematic Review with Domain-Specific Meta-analyses of Proportions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize clinical outcomes and safety of surgical and advanced interventional treatments for pediatric refractory constipation using a phenotype-directed, domain-specific approach.
METHODS: This systematic review with domain-specific meta-analyses of proportions followed PRISMA 2020 and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261378728). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CENTRAL, the Cochrane Library, LILACS, trial registries, Google Scholar, and reference lists were searched through April 29, 2026. Eligible interventions included antegrade continence enema (ACE) procedures, botulinum toxin injection, transanal irrigation (TAI), diversion, and selected resective or motility-guided procedures. Random-effects single-arm proportions were pooled only within clinically coherent domains; safety outcomes were synthesized structurally when definitions and denominators were not sufficiently comparable for pooling.
RESULTS: Thirty-two primary interventional studies met final eligibility criteria, of which 22 contributed to quantitative synthesis. Descriptive pooled study-defined clinical success or response was 85% (95% CI: 81%-88%) for ACE procedures, 81% (95% CI: 72%-89%) for botulinum toxin injection, 81% (95% CI: 64%-94%) for TAI, and 91% (95% CI: 76%-100%) for resective or advanced surgery. The surgical estimate was exploratory because procedures and indications were heterogeneous. These proportions are not comparative treatment-effect estimates. Certainty of evidence was low or very low, and safety reporting was inconsistent across studies.
CONCLUSION: Advanced interventions may be associated with favorable outcomes in carefully selected children with refractory constipation, but indications and risks are phenotype specific. The evidence does not support direct effectiveness comparisons between therapeutic domains.

articles.title: Behavioral Manifestations and Diagnostic Challenges of Restless Legs Syndrome in Infants and Toddlers.
articles.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a sensory-motor neurological disorder, increasingly recognized in children, yet diagnosis in infants and toddlers remains challenging due to the reliance on verbal symptom reporting. This scoping review aims to synthesize the limited literature on probable RLS in infants and toddlers. A structured literature search was conducted using PubMed and Embase from inception through March 2026. Original studies, case reports, case series, and pediatric cohorts reporting probable RLS with onset or evaluation at ≤3 years were included. Reviews, editorials, and studies focusing exclusively on older populations were excluded. Thirteen studies were identified, of which 7 met inclusion criteria. Of the 7 publications, some focused on infants or toddlers, whereas others provided extractable data for children aged ≤3 years. Across studies, symptom onset was reported as early as 7.5 months in 1 cohort. Probable RLS in infants and toddlers presents as a behavioral sleep disorder characterized by nocturnal motor restlessness, accompanied by sleep fragmentation and distress. A characteristic pattern of awakening after 1-3 hours of sleep with motor agitation was frequently described. Periodic limb movements and low ferritin levels provide supportive evidence. Iron supplementation has been associated with improvement in symptoms in select cohorts. Probable RLS can manifest as early as infancy, presenting as a behavioral phenotype. Increased awareness of early behavioral manifestations and consideration of iron status may facilitate earlier identification and management. Future studies are needed to develop diagnostic frameworks and to better define the natural history of early-onset probable RLS.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Once-Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide in Adolescents With Obesity: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Background Childhood and adolescent obesity are increasing public health concerns in India and are associated with cardiometabolic complications. However, real-world evidence on the safety and effectiveness of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide among adolescents with overweight or obesity in routine clinical practice remains limited. Objectives This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (r-DNA) among Indian adolescents aged 12-18 years with overweight or obesity. Methods This retrospective, observational study (IAH-BMR/072/06-26) involved 40 adolescents on once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (0.25-2.4 mg) over 32 weeks. Anthropometric measures (body weight (BW), body mass index (BMI), BMI standard deviation score (BMI-SDS), waist circumference (WC), and blood pressure (BP)) were tracked over time. Biochemical outcomes included fasting blood sugar (FBS), postprandial blood sugar (PPBS), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting insulin, lipid profile, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), and liver enzymes. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) and paired comparisons were used to assess changes. Results The study population comprised 24 female (60.0%) and 16 male (40.0%) adolescents, with a mean age of 14.82 ± 1.78 years. After 32 weeks, semaglutide demonstrated significant mean reductions in BW (-15.20 kg; 17.2%), BMI (-6.70 kg/m²; 19.4%), BMI-SDS (-1.08), WC (-10.71 cm; 10.82%), systolic BP (-8.30 mmHg), and diastolic BP (-4.50 mmHg) (all p < 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed in FBS, PPBS, HbA1c, fasting insulin, total cholesterol, triglycerides, TSH, serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase, and serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase (all p < 0.001). Improvements were consistent across sexes. No adverse events (AEs) were documented. Conclusions Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (r-DNA) was associated with improvements in anthropometric and metabolic parameters among Indian adolescents with overweight or obesity. These real-world findings are broadly consistent with the reductions in BMI and improvements in selected cardiometabolic risk factors reported in the STEP TEENS trial. Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted to further evaluate its long-term effectiveness and safety.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Automated Insulin Delivery Systems in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems integrate continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with algorithm-driven insulin delivery and are increasingly used in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1D). However, the magnitude and consistency of glycemic benefit across pediatric age groups, together with the safety profile of these systems, warrant focused evaluation. We conducted a systematic review of randomized controlled trials evaluating AID systems in children and adolescents with T1D. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through August 2026. Eligible studies compared AID with conventional insulin therapy or non-automated pump/CGM-based management and reported glycemic or safety outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Findings were synthesized narratively without quantitative meta-analysis. Of 2,363 records identified, 11 randomized controlled trials met the eligibility criteria. Trials evaluated multiple AID platforms in participants aged 2-18 years, with intervention durations ranging from 12 to 104 weeks. AID consistently improved time in range ([TIR] 70-180 mg/dL). Individual trials reported TIR improvements ranging from approximately 7 to 12 percentage points. In one pediatric trial, TIR increased by 11 percentage points (95% CI, 7-14; P<0.001), while another demonstrated an 8.7-percentage-point increase (95% CI, 7.4-9.9; P<0.001) accompanied by a 0.4-percentage-point reduction in glycated hemoglobin. A six-month trial demonstrated a 6.7-percentage-point increase in TIR (95% CI, 2.7-10.8; P=0.002), with a concurrent 1.9-percentage-point reduction in time below range. Improvements were particularly pronounced during nighttime in several studies. Hyperglycemic exposure generally decreased, whereas hypoglycemia did not consistently increase. Severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis were uncommon, although the relatively small trial populations limited assessment of rare adverse events. Two trials were judged to have low overall risk of bias, while nine had some concerns; none was judged to have high risk of bias. AID systems consistently improve CGM-derived glycemic outcomes in children and adolescents with T1D, with the most reproducible benefit being increased TIR and reduced hyperglycemic exposure. Improvements in glycated hemoglobin were comparatively modest. Current randomized evidence does not demonstrate a consistent increase in hypoglycemia or diabetic ketoacidosis, although longer and larger studies are needed to characterize rare safety outcomes. AID should be regarded as an effective strategy for reducing glycemic burden rather than a fully autonomous treatment. Future research should emphasize long-term clinical and psychosocial outcomes, treatment burden, technology-related complications, and representation of diverse pediatric populations.

articles.title: Transitional Fetal Circulation: A Comprehensive Review of Physiological Adaptation, Failure, and Neonatal Outcomes.
articles.abstract: The change from fetal to neonatal circulation is one of the most rapid and consequential physiological reorganizations in human life, and it is more accurately described as an integrated cardiopulmonary and placental sequence than as simple closure of fetal shunts. Before birth, the placenta is the organ of gas exchange, pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) is high, and the ductus venosus, foramen ovale, and ductus arteriosus sustain a parallel circulation that preferentially directs relatively oxygenated umbilical venous blood to the myocardium and brain. At birth, lung aeration, clearance of fetal lung liquid, a rise in alveolar and arterial oxygen tension, and mechanical recruitment of the pulmonary microvasculature produce a steep fall in PVR and a several-fold increase in pulmonary blood flow. Pulmonary venous return then replaces umbilical venous return as the dominant source of left ventricular preload, while interruption of the low-resistance placental circuit raises systemic vascular resistance (SVR) and left ventricular afterload. These pressure and flow changes, rather than any intrinsic anatomical event, drive functional closure of the foramen ovale and progressive constriction of the ductus arteriosus. Failure or delay of this coordinated sequence produces a spectrum of hemodynamic disorders: persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN), myocardial dysfunction, inadequate preload, hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in the preterm infant, and decompensation of previously unrecognized duct-dependent congenital heart disease. The mechanisms include incomplete alveolar recruitment, hypoxemia, acidosis, inflammation, impaired nitric oxide (NO)-soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC)-cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) signaling, excess endothelin-1 and Rho-kinase activity, oxidative stress, ventricular maladaptation, and adverse ventriculo-ventricular interaction. Because hypoxemia, hypotension, acidosis, and poor perfusion are shared surface features of mechanistically distinct states, assessment based on blood pressure or oxygen saturation alone is inadequate. This review synthesizes fetal circulatory physiology, the molecular and mechanical basis of normal transition, the principal failed-transition phenotypes, and contemporary physiology-guided monitoring and management. It integrates recent evidence on deferred and physiology-based cord clamping, including the 2023 individual participant data meta-analysis of preterm cord management and the 2024 ABC3 randomized trial; the 2024 American Society of Echocardiography update on targeted neonatal echocardiography; the 2025 American Heart Association and American Academy of Pediatrics neonatal resuscitation guidelines; randomized and network meta-analytic evidence on PPHN pharmacotherapy; and the shift from routine early PDA closure to selective, phenotype-based management. A mechanistic understanding of transitional circulation allows earlier recognition of neonatal cardiovascular compromise and discourages the indiscriminate treatment of numerical hypoxemia or hypotension.

articles.title: Clinical Insights and Social Vulnerability in Infantile Hemangiomas: A 10-Year Retrospective Cohort in Puerto Rico.
articles.abstract: Infantile hemangiomas (IHs) are the most common benign vascular tumors in childhood. While most occurrences regress spontaneously, some require treatment due to ulceration, functional impairment, or cosmetic concerns. In Puerto Rico, social determinants of health potentially affect both access to healthcare and clinical outcomes. The Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), a composite metric encompassing socioeconomic status, household composition, transportation, and other social factors, is commonly used to evaluate community-level vulnerability. This study sought to describe lesion location and treatment modalities, and evaluate whether the SVI is associated with treatment outcomes in IH patients in Puerto Rico as measured by lesion size at presentation, follow-up, and change in lesion size following treatment. Records of pediatric patients diagnosed with hemangiomas between 2015 and 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. A total of 30 patients were identified, and extracted data included patient demographics, treatment modality, lesion location, and lesion size, as measured via a flexible measuring tape, before and after treatment. SVI was calculated and assigned according to patients' residential Zone Improvement Plan (ZIP) code and matched to the corresponding SVI values obtained from the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR) database at the time of presentation. Most patients (43.3%) were treated with propranolol, followed by surgical resection or embolization (20%). The most affected areas were the limbs (50%) and the head and neck (30%) region. Using Spearman's rank correlation, the study found that a higher SVI was associated with a larger hemangioma lesion size at presentation (Spearman's rho = 0.681, p = 0.005) and remained correlated with a larger post-treatment lesion size (Spearman's rho = 0.634, p = 0.011). However, the SVI was not associated with the magnitude of size reduction following treatment (Spearman's rho = 0.09, p = 0.742), meaning that the disparities in lesion size are likely due to differences in disease severity at the time of diagnosis rather than differences due to treatment response. Meanwhile, results also suggest that since more than half of patients were managed with pharmacologic therapy, treatment compliance may play an important role in influencing outcomes. Ultimately, SVIs could be used to flag patients who may present later or with larger lesions in order to enable earlier monitoring and management.

articles.title: Effects of Intravenous Dexamethasone on IL-6 Levels in Children Undergoing Cardiac Surgery With Cardiopulmonary Bypass.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiopulmonary bypass provokes a systemic inflammatory response in children, with interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels rising rapidly after bypass. Corticosteroids are frequently used to blunt this response, but paediatric evidence remains inconsistent.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether a single intravenous dose of dexamethasone reduces the post-bypass increase in plasma IL-6 and improves early postoperative outcomes in children undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
METHODS: This single-centre quasi-experimental study enrolled 46 children aged one month to 12 years undergoing elective repair of congenital heart disease between January 2025 and August 2025. Participants were purposively recruited and alternately allocated to intravenous dexamethasone (1 mg/kg, maximum 10 mg; n=23, 50.0%) or 2 mL normal saline (n=23, 50.0%) after induction of anaesthesia. Plasma IL-6 was measured before drug administration, two hours after cardiopulmonary bypass, and 24 hours after bypass. Haemodynamic variables, oxygen saturation, extubation time, and intensive care unit stay were recorded.
RESULTS: The median IL-6 increase from baseline to two hours was lower with dexamethasone than with saline (261.90 pg/mL, interquartile range: 195.0-824.0, versus 447.0 pg/mL, interquartile range: 261.70-1,230.20), but the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.177). At 24 hours, the median change from baseline was 8.20 pg/mL in the dexamethasone group and 13.0 pg/mL in the saline group (p=0.350). Blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and extubation time were comparable. First-postoperative-day heart rate was higher with dexamethasone (143.63 ± 18.93 versus 117.76 ± 19.57 beats/min; p=0.001), and median intensive care unit stay was longer (120 versus 95.5 hours; p=0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: A single dose of intravenous dexamethasone at 1 mg/kg, capped at 10 mg, did not significantly attenuate the IL-6 response after paediatric cardiopulmonary bypass. The higher heart rate and longer intensive care stay observed in the dexamethasone group should be treated as exploratory because allocation was nonrandom and perioperative complexity was not adjusted for.

articles.title: Conventional Therapy in Pediatric Hypophosphatemic Rickets: Growth Outcomes and Nephrocalcinosis Risk.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypophosphatemic rickets (HR) is characterized by renal phosphate wasting and impaired skeletal mineralization. Although conventional therapy with oral phosphate and active vitamin D analogues remains widely used, its long-term biochemical, auxological, and renal outcomes are variable. This study aimed to evaluate longitudinal biochemical changes, growth patterns, cumulative phosphate exposure, and nephrocalcinosis (NC) development in children with HR receiving conventional therapy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center case series included 20 children with HR followed for at least 1 year. Clinical, biochemical, and auxological parameters were recorded at baseline and annually. Longitudinal analyses were performed in patients with complete 3-year follow-up (n = 10) using the Friedman test, and cumulative phosphate exposure was compared according to NC status.
RESULTS: Alkaline phosphatase levels decreased significantly during follow-up (P = .021), whereas serum phosphate levels did not show sustained normalization (P = 0.627). Height standard deviation score did not significantly change over 3 years (P = .644). Nephrocalcinosis developed in 25% (n = 5/20) of the overall cohort and in 40% (n = 4/10) of patients with complete follow-up. Patients with NC had significantly higher cumulative phosphate exposure (P = .010), without significant differences in height standard deviation score (SDS) or other biochemical parameters.
CONCLUSION: Conventional therapy was associated with partial biochemical improvement but limited auxological benefit. Higher cumulative phosphate exposure was associated with NC development without evident growth advantage, underscoring the importance of balancing biochemical targets with renal safety in pediatric HR.

articles.title: Validity and Reliability of a Thai Version of the Paediatric Haemophilia Activities List.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Paediatric Haemophilia Activities List (PedHAL) is a self-administered instrument for assessing activity limitations in children with haemophilia, yet no Thai version has previously undergone psychometric evaluation.
AIM: To evaluate the validity and reliability of a Thai version of the PedHAL.
METHODS: Following permission from the original developer, the PedHAL was translated into Thai using forward-backwards translation. Content validity was examined via the content validity index (CVI). Construct validity was determined by correlating PedHAL scores with the Functional Independence Score in Haemophilia (FISH) and the Haemophilia Joint Health Score (HJHS). Internal consistency and test-retest reliability were assessed with Cronbach's alpha and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), respectively. The participants were nineteen children with haemophilia who attended the Departments of Rehabilitation Medicine and Paediatrics, Faculty of Medicine Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University, between June 2021 and September 2022.
RESULTS: The Thai PedHAL demonstrated excellent content validity (CVI  =  0.99; threshold  ≥ 0.90) and good construct validity, as evidenced by a strong positive correlation with FISH (r  =  0.703; range 0.70‒0.89) and a moderate negative correlation with HJHS (r  =  -0.475; range 0.40‒0.69). Reliability testing revealed excellent test-retest reliability (ICC  =  0.955; threshold ≥ 0.90) and excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha  =  0.944; threshold ≥ 0.90).
CONCLUSION: The Thai version of the PedHAL has acceptable-to-excellent psychometric properties for measuring activity limitations in Thai children with haemophilia. It may serve as a valuable instrument for both clinical and research applications.

articles.title: Imagery ability in children with Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy and associations with clinical characteristics: a cross-sectional pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Movement Imagery Questionnaire for Children (MIQ-C) assesses children's imagery ability through three subcomponents: internal visual imagery (IVI), external visual imagery (EVI), and kinesthetic imagery (KI).
OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to evaluate the imagery ability and its associations with clinical characteristics in children with Obstetric Brachial Plexus Palsy (OBPP).
METHODS: Fifteen children with OBPP (mean age 10.67 ± 1.18 years; 8 males and 7 females) and 15 healthy children frequency‑matched for age and sex were included. Motor imagery was assessed using the MIQ-C. Motor and sensory functions in participants with OBPP were evaluated using the Active Movement Scale (AMS) and the Narakas Sensory Grading System (NSG), respectively. Mann-Whitney U tests assessed between-group differences in MIQ-C subscores; intraclass correlation coefficients (95% confidence intervals) evaluated test-retest reliability in both groups; and Spearman rank correlations examined associations with clinical characteristics in the OBPP group.
RESULTS: Children with OBPP had significantly lower scores than the control group across all MIQ-C subscores (after Bonferroni adjustment to 0.0167; p ≤ .005). In the OBPP group, clinical type was strongly negatively correlated with all MIQ-C subscores. Higher imagery scores were observed in children classified as NSG = 3 than in those classified as NSG = 2. Positive correlations also were found between MIQ-C subscores and AMS scores.
CONCLUSION: Compared to controls, children with OBPP demonstrated lower imagery scores, suggesting potential differences in imagery ability between the groups. Exploratory findings also indicated possible relationships between imagery scores and clinical characteristics; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size. Motor imagery assessment may offer complementary information about imagery ability alongside routine motor and sensory evaluations in OBPP rehabilitation.

articles.title: Two-dimensional speckle-tracking imaging for assessing cardiac dysfunction in liver cirrhosis: correlation with Child-Pugh score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging (2D-STI) enables sensitive and quantitative assessment of myocardial deformation, its application in patients with liver cirrhosis (LC) has largely been limited to ventricular function. This study applied 2D-STI to evaluate both ventricular and atrial function in order to identify early myocardial dysfunction in this population.
METHODS: A total of 82 patients with LC were enrolled and stratified according to the Child-Pugh classification into Class A (n = 30), Class B (n = 29), and Class C (n = 23). Thirty healthy individuals served as controls. All 112 participants underwent conventional echocardiography and 2D-STI assessment.
RESULTS: Compared with controls, all LC groups showed reduced left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) and right ventricular free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS) (both P < 0.05), with a progressive decline from Class A to Class C. In contrast, right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RVGLS) was significantly decreased only in Classes B and C (P < 0.05). Left atrial conduit strain (LAScd) was significantly reduced across all LC groups (P < 0.05), whereas left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) and contractile strain (LASct) demonstrated a biphasic pattern -initially increased, then decreased- compared with controls. Overall, 2D-STI detected cardiac dysfunction earlier than conventional echocardiography. Significant negative correlations were observed between Child-Pugh score and LVGLS, RVFWLS, and RVGLS.
CONCLUSION: Cardiac function is impaired in patients with LC and deteriorates with increasing disease severity. Compared with conventional echocardiography, 2D-STI detects cardiac dysfunction at an earlier stage, providing valuable support for early clinical intervention.

articles.title: Bridging Inpatient and Community Care Following First Episode Psychosis: A Pilot Feasibility and Acceptability Study of a Brief Psychological Intervention.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study evaluated the implementation feasibility and acceptability of a brief CBT-informed psychological intervention designed to bridge inpatient and community care for young adults experiencing a first episode of psychosis (FEP).
METHODS: A six-session individual CBT-informed intervention was delivered to patients experiencing a FEP approaching discharge from a specialist early intervention inpatient unit. The intervention commenced on the ward (the initial session) and continued into the community. Feasibility was assessed from a service implementation perspective, including recruitment, uptake, retention, intervention completion, and outcome measure completion rates. Acceptability was evaluated using satisfaction ratings and qualitative interviews.
RESULTS: During a seven-month period, 43 patients were screened, and 38 were eligible to participate. Twenty-eight (74%) consented, six (15%) disengaged, and 17 (44%) completed all six sessions and study measures. Findings indicated that the intervention could be successfully delivered across inpatient and community settings within routine clinical care. Patients reported high satisfaction with therapy (mean satisfaction score = 4.76/5). Qualitative feedback highlighted the value of psychological continuity across care settings, development of coping strategies, and opportunities to make sense of admission and recovery experiences. Clinical outcome measures were successfully collected; however, the study was not designed to evaluate intervention effectiveness.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest that delivering a brief CBT-informed intervention across inpatient and community services is feasible within routine clinical practice and acceptable to young adults experiencing FEP. Further controlled research is required to evaluate clinical effectiveness and longer-term outcomes.

articles.title: Virtual Reality-Based Rehabilitation for Pediatric Acquired Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundVirtual reality and augmented reality (VR/AR) rehabilitation shows promise after adult brain injury, but its efficacy in pediatric acquired brain injury remains unclear.ObjectiveTo synthesize within-person changes in cognitive, motor, and functional outcomes following VR/AR rehabilitation in pediatric acquired brain injury and explore moderators.MethodsSix databases were searched through March 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. Of 373 records, ten studies (nine VR, one AR) were included: four randomized trials and six uncontrolled studies. Standardized mean changes were pooled using three-level random-effects meta-analysis.ResultsAcross 72 effect sizes, VR/AR rehabilitation was associated with significant pre-post improvement (g = 0.62, 95% CI [0.15, 1.09], p = .01). Improvements were significant for motor and functional outcomes, but not cognitive outcomes. Outcome domain, developmental stage, study design, immersion, assessment method, and treatment dose were not significant moderators. Longer pre-post intervals predicted larger changes (β = 0.01, p = .004), potentially reflecting natural recovery. Overall improvements remained significant across assumed correlations and when restricting analyses to VR, excluding mixed diagnostic samples, or clustering by research team. Funnel plot asymmetry suggested possible publication bias.ConclusionsVR-based rehabilitation was associated with within-person improvement, but comparative efficacy remains uncertain because evidence is limited, heterogeneous, and predominantly uncontrolled. Larger controlled studies should evaluate efficacy, safety, mechanisms, durability, and functional transfer.

articles.title: From Training to Practice in Public School Music Therapy: Clients, Service Delivery, and Professional Support.
articles.abstract: Many music therapists work in school settings with children and adolescents with disabilities, yet little is known about how they specifically deliver services. This study describes the results of a questionnaire asking music therapists working in school settings in the United States about their training, current service delivery models, collaboration with other professionals, and thoughts about music therapy in inclusive settings; a total of 360 responses were analyzed. Respondents were neutral about the adequacy of their undergraduate practica and coursework to prepare them to work with children with disabilities but felt that their internship was adequate preparation. During their training and professional work, respondents most often collaborated with special educators and paraprofessionals. Music therapy sessions were most often provided in self-contained groups, followed by individual sessions, and inclusive groups. The most common special education categories served were children with intellectual disability, speech language impairment, and autism. Findings are discussed considering recommendations for educators and suggestions for future research to grow the evidence base about music therapy with children with disabilities.

articles.title: Prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease among obese, overweight, and at-risk children and adolescents in Türkiye: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Among children, the overall prevalence of MASLD is estimated at around 7%, and early manifestation is associated with a more severe prognosis. Despite this growing burden, no systematic analysis of pediatric MASLD prevalence in Türkiye has yet been conducted. Here, we aimed to estimate the pediatric MASLD prevalence among children with specific conditions in Türkiye.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted for studies published in English and/or Turkish between 2005 and 2023 using the databases MEDLINE, PubMed, EMBASE, and ULAKBIM. The search strategy included the following terms: "Türkiye AND NAFLD AND Pediatric" and "Türkiye AND NAFLD AND Prevalence AND Children AND Adolescent." The studies identified through this literature review were incorporated into the meta-analysis, which included either obese/overweight or at-risk children or adolescents with specific conditions such as increased transaminases.
RESULTS: The pooled overall prevalence of MASLD was estimated as 44.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 39.5-49.7) among at-risk children and adolescents. Heterogeneity among studies was considerable, with an I2 value of 96%, indicating substantial variability. Subgroup analysis showed a pooled prevalence of 54.9% in boys (95% CI: 48.6-61.1) and 41.2% in girls (95% CI: 35.6-46.9). Regionally, the prevalence was 49.0% (95% CI: 41.2-57.1) in the Marmara and Aegean regions, and 42.2% (95% CI: 35.3-49.1) in the Black Sea, Mediterranean, and Central Anatolian regions.
CONCLUSION: The results of this study indicate a markedly high prevalence of MASLD among at-risk children and adolescents. These findings should serve as an alert for policymakers to adapt healthcare strategies aimed at preventing childhood obesity and MASLD.

articles.title: Predictors and prognostic stratification of bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome after pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
articles.abstract: Bronchiolitis Obliterans Syndrome (BOS) after pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) carries high mortality, partly due to diagnostic delays and static assessments. This brief report evaluates a dynamic monitoring strategy for early warning. This single-center, retrospective cohort study included 201 children who underwent allo-HSCT between January 2015 and December 2024, comprising 29 patients with BOS and 172 non-BOS controls.Independent risk factors for BOS were identified using multivariate Cox regression analysis. Diagnostic performance of a relative FEV1 decline ≥ 10% ("at-risk" signal) was assessed. The longitudinal trajectories of pulmonary function and high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) imaging scores were also compared. Cumulative BOS incidence was 6.9%. Multivariate analysis identified grade III-IV aGVHD (HR = 15.12), cGVHD (HR = 6.94), dry cough (HR = 11.77), and an early post-transplant FEV1/FVC decline of ≥ 10% (HR = 8.70) as independent risk factors for BOS development. The "at-risk" signal (BOS stage 0p) advanced diagnosis by a median of 176 days (NPV 85.0%). A significant "radio-functional discordance" (worsening HRCT scores despite stable FEV1) was observed (P < 0.001). Dynamic FEV1 monitoring suggests a sensitive early warning and prognostic signal in pediatric BOS, though its low PPV necessitates integration with comprehensive evaluation. The radio-functional discordance highlights the need for combined functional and imaging surveillance.Given the exploratory nature of this single‑center cohort with limited case numbers, all findings should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Age-Stratified Sirolimus Trough Concentrations in Pediatric Vascular Malformations: A Real-World Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus is increasingly being used off-label to treat pediatric vascular malformations. In this study, the age-stratified drug exposure, pharmacokinetic variability, and long-term treatment characteristics of sirolimus were evaluated in a real-world pediatric population.
METHODS: In this study, 144 patients (younger than 19 years) with vascular malformations who were treated with sirolimus at a single center (July 2018 and March 2025) were retrospectively analyzed. A total of 2054 therapeutic drug monitoring measurements were obtained. The patients were stratified into 6 age groups (1 month and younger to 12-18 years). The outcomes included trough concentration, interindividual variability (coefficient of variation), target range attainment, treatment duration, and MRI-based response.
RESULTS: The median follow-up was 18.3 months (range, 0.3-74.1 months). Neonates (1 month and younger) showed the highest interindividual variability (coefficient of variation = 61.6%), with lower variability observed in adolescents (40.0%, P < 0.001). Overall, 73.4% of the trough concentrations were within the target range (4-10 ng/mL), and the mean duration within the therapeutic range per patient was 70.9%. Supratherapeutic levels (>15 ng/mL) were most frequent in neonates (6.6%). Prolonged therapy (≥24 months) was observed in 31.9% of patients, with a median duration of 35.1 months. Among the 44 patients who underwent follow-up MRI, 84.1% showed disease improvement or stability.
CONCLUSIONS: Sustained long-term treatment continuity suggests that sirolimus was generally tolerated across pediatric age groups, although direct toxicity data were not systematically captured in this study. Younger patients exhibited greater pharmacokinetic variability, necessitating closer monitoring and cautious dose adjustment. Prospective PK-PD studies incorporating standardized clinical outcomes are needed to define optimal trough targets and individualized dosing strategies.

articles.title: Adjunct Low-Dose Dexmedetomidine for Sedation in Mechanically Ventilated Children: An Exploratory Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective sedation in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) is complicated by the adverse effects of benzodiazepines and opioids. Dexmedetomidine may provide a benzodiazepine-sparing alternative with distinct pharmacologic properties.
OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that adjunct, fixed low-dose, no-bolus dexmedetomidine would reduce midazolam and fentanyl exposure per ventilator-day in mechanically ventilated children.
METHODS: In a triple-blind randomized controlled trial, 60 mechanically ventilated patients aged 1 month to 12 years were randomized to standard sedation (continuous midazolam and fentanyl) plus low-dose dexmedetomidine (a fixed-rate continuous infusion at 0.2 µg/kg/h without a loading bolus) or matched placebo (0.9% normal saline). In both groups, midazolam and fentanyl were titrated per protocol to achieve the target Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) level.
RESULTS: Among 60 randomized children, adjunct fixed low-dose dexmedetomidine did not reduce the prespecified primary outcome of fentanyl or midazolam exposure per ventilator-day. Median fentanyl exposure per ventilator-day was 70.0 µg·kg-1·day-1 in the control group and 90.6 µg·kg-1·day-1 in the dexmedetomidine group; median midazolam exposure per ventilator-day was 7.0 mg·kg-1·day-1 and 9.1 mg·kg-1·day-1, respectively. Neither primary comparison remained statistically significant after Holm correction. In an unadjusted secondary analysis, the median time to first successful extubation was 6 days in the dexmedetomidine group and 15 days in the control group. This finding was exploratory and was not confirmed by the prespecified competing-risk or longitudinal ventilation analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Adjunct fixed low-dose dexmedetomidine without a loading bolus did not reduce fentanyl or midazolam exposure per ventilator-day. Early sedative-analgesic exposure was higher with dexmedetomidine, and the apparent early-extubation signal was exploratory and was not confirmed by competing-risk or longitudinal analyses of ventilation.

articles.title: Evaluation of clinical, immunological, genetic characteristics and follow-up results of patients presenting with common variable immunodeficiency phenotype.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID) is an antibody deficiency characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia, recurrent infections and non-infectious clinical features. Patients presenting with heterogeneous clinical findings lead to delayed diagnosis, various complications, and organ damage.
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the clinical, immunological, genetic features of CVID cases diagnosed in our clinic over a 20-year period.
METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 51 patients diagnosed with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) according to ESID criteria and followed at the Department of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology, Ankara University Faculty of Medicine, between 2002 and 2022.
RESULTS: The median age at diagnosis was 11.08 years (range: 4-27.91), with a median diagnostic delay of 4.79 years (range: 1-22.91). The most common clinical manifestation was sinopulmonary infections (96%). The most frequent non-infectious clinical manifestation was lymphoproliferation (41.1%). Splenomegaly was significantly more common in patients with autoimmune disease (53.3%). Patients with bronchiectasis had significantly lower proportions of class-switched memory B cells (p = 0.020). CD4+ naive T-cell counts were significantly lower in patients with malignancy compared to those without malignancy (p = 0.006). Genetic analysis performed in 40 patients revealed pathogenic variants in 35%, most frequently involving TACI, followed by ICOS and NFKB2. Following immunoglobulin replacement therapy, infection-related hospitalization rates markedly decreased (from 71.4% to 9.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: CVID patients can present with a wide variety of clinical features. Early diagnosis and treatment can improve quality of life. Identification of genetic defects will enhance understanding of immunopathogenesis opening new avenues for targeted therapies.

articles.title: Changes in the Number of Patients With Drug Overdose due to Deliberate Self-Harm Transported to the Hospital Emergency Department During the Past 12 Years.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Recently, over-the-counter (OTC) drug overdoses have increased. This study aimed to clarify the clinical characteristics and temporal trends of acute drug overdose and explore effective countermeasures in emergency medical settings.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients admitted to our hospital for acute drug overdose due to deliberate self-harm between January 2012 and December 2023. Data collected from medical records included sex, age, ingested substances, implementation of advanced interventions, and outcomes. Cases were categorized as prescription drugs only or OTC drugs present. Comparisons were made before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Severe cases were defined as those requiring advanced interventions; psychiatric care history was assessed in severe cases.
RESULTS: Of the 1676 included patients (mean age 37.8 years), 74.4% used only prescription drugs, 15.0% used only OTC drugs and 5.1% used both. OTC drug-involved cases increased significantly from 15.7% before to 29.7% after the COVID-19 pandemic (p < 0.001). The proportion of patients aged 10-29 years also increased significantly (p < 0.001), as did their OTC drug use (p < 0.001). Severe cases accounted for 8.2% (n = 137) and 12 deaths (0.7%). The proportion of severe cases did not differ significantly between groups. Among the severe cases, psychiatric care history was more frequent in the prescription-only group (90.9%) compared to the OTC-involved group (54.5%).
CONCLUSION: Since 2019, a marked increase in OTC drug overdoses among younger individuals has been observed. Emergency departments should play a key role in initiating multidisciplinary, community-based support systems to prevent recurrence.

articles.title: Assessing quality of life during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injuries.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to assess quality of life (QOL) outcomes during adolescence and adulthood following brachial plexus birth injury (BPBI) and to identify factors linked to poorer outcomes. Additionally, the authors aimed to determine the construct validity of the Impact of a Brachial Plexus Injury Questionnaire (Mancuso scale) for use in the birth injury population.
METHODS: This study utilized a cross-sectional, within-subject comparative survey design to assess the QOL outcomes of adolescents and adults with BPBI. Participants older than 13 years of age and with a history of BPBI were identified using the United Brachial Plexus Network Facebook group. QOL was assessed using the World Health Organization Quality of Life Scale-Brief Version (WHOQOL-BREF) in adults, Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) in adolescents, and a brachial plexus injury-specific tool (Mancuso scale). To determine construct validity, scores from each Mancuso subscale were compared to the participants' overall WHOQOL-BREF scores.
RESULTS: Adults (n = 59) who completed the WHOQOL-BREF had a mean overall score of 63.1 ± 22.2 (0- to 100-point scale). The scores of the Mancuso scale with regard to the symptoms, limitations, and emotion subscales were 45.8 ± 29.5, 35.2 ± 17.3, and 43.6 ± 25.3, respectively. These findings contrasted with the published values from subjects who had sustained a traumatic brachial plexus injury whose scores were 66 ± 18.7, 48.2 ± 22.3, and 39.5 ± 21.2, respectively. For adolescents (n = 4), the overall score on PedsQL was 63.7 ± 21.3. Adolescent scores on the Mancuso scale were 31.7 ± 26.9, 29.8 ± 20.7, and 39.7 ± 18.8, respectively. In adults, severe functional limitation and limited access to care were associated with poorer QOL (p < 0.05), whereas surgical history and occupational therapy attendance did not. Higher scores on the Mancuso subscales correlated with lower quality of life scores on the WHOQOL-BREF. Adolescent data analysis revealed similar, nonsignificant results.
CONCLUSIONS: BPBI plays a role in long-term QOL, notably by the severity of functional limitation and access to care. The Mancuso scale shows promising construct validity in the adult BPBI population, but a larger sample of adolescents is needed.

articles.title: Persistent bowel dysfunction and health-related quality of life after surgery for Hirschsprung disease: generic versus disease-specific outcomes and measurement heterogeneity in children and adolescents.
articles.abstract: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a condition that can implant intestinal continuity surgically although technical success does not necessarily correlate with its age-specific bowel functionality. This critical narrative review addresses the association of persistent postoperative bowel dysfunction and health-related quality-of-life (HRQoL) with specific emphasis on discordance between generic and disease-specific measures, and on heterogeneity in the outcome measures. The literature review was updated: June 20 to July 15, 2026(PubMed), Web of science, Google Scholar, and NCBI Bookshelf. Twenty-five records were filtered and 19 sources published since 1998 constituted the main evidence base of outcomes; all sources were categorized according to evidence level and population and mixed HD/anorectal-malformation (ARM) evidence was classified as indirect. Reported constipation and fecal incontinence/soiling do not represent consistent reliable prevalence studies and vary greatly among the studies because of age, follow-up, operative method, definitions, questionnaire, type of respondent and bowel-management practice. The chronic obstructive symptoms need an assessment of mechanical or histopathologic errors that can be corrected prior to the intensification of bowel management. No statistically significant difference in generic HRQoL at the group level was shown between healthy comparison and available evidence, though results indicated a great degree of heterogeneity, precluding a general interpretation; disease-specific instruments and symptom-stratified analyses showed evidence of statistically important impairment in a sub-group with chronic dysfunction. Parent- proxy and child self-reports are not interchangeable but rather give complementary views. A standardized follow-up ought to thus combine effective bowel-function evaluation, generic and disease-specific HRQoL questionnaires, in addition to child plus parent reports.

articles.title: Functional outcomes in pediatric colorectal surgery: a predictor-based analysis of Hirschsprung disease and anorectal malformation in a resource-limited setting.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Long-term fecal continence and bowel habit outcomes remain a significant challenge in pediatric colorectal surgery. This study evaluated long-term functional bowel outcomes in patients treated for Hirschsprung disease (HD) and Anorectal Malformations (ARM) using the standardized Rintala Bowel Function Score, identifying key clinical predictors of favorable outcomes.
METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted at St. Paul's Hospital Millennium Medical College, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, among children who underwent definitive surgical repair for HD and ARM between January 2018 and December 2022. Functional bowel outcomes were evaluated using the Rintala Bowel Function Score (0-20 scale), with a score ≥ 17 defined as a clinically favorable outcome. Multivariable logistic regression was utilized to assess predictive factors.
RESULTS: A total of 136 patients were included: 94 with HD and 42 with ARM. In the HD cohort, the presence of associated congenital anomalies and colonic excision proximal to the splenic flexure were major negative predictors of bowel function, reducing the probability of a favorable outcome from 66 to 22% (p = 0.007) and from 75 to 28% (p = 0.008), respectively. In the ARM cohort, 100% of patients with low-severity malformations achieved favorable outcomes compared with 54.5% of those with high/intermediate-severity malformations (p = 0.004).
CONCLUSION: While anatomical severity appears to be an important factor influencing bowel function outcomes in ARM, associated systemic anomalies and the extent of colonic excision were also associated with poorer bowel function in children with HD. These findings highlight the potential importance of structured, long-term postoperative follow-up, with particular attention to children at higher risk of functional bowel problems.

articles.title: Pediatric total thyroidectomy and lobectomy; an analysis of surgeon specialty and outcomes for same-day discharge.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Our study aimed to evaluate differences in patient outcomes overall and by specialty for same-day discharge (SDD) following pediatric total thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy.
METHODS: Data from the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-Pediatric (NSQIP-P) was used to evaluate thyroidectomy and thyroid lobectomy patients (2017-2021). For each operation, patients were categorized into SDD and those discharged 1-2 days post-operation (non-SDD).
