articles.title: The Effect of Care Team Composition on Healthcare Resource Use Among Rural Children Enrolled in Hospice.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aimed to examine the effect of care team composition on healthcare resource use among rural children enrolled in hospice during the last year of life.MethodsThe sample included 3131 children aged 20 years or younger who received concurrent hospice care, resided in rural communities in 28 Midwestern and Southern states, and were enrolled in Medicaid between 2011 and 2022. Analyses used multivariable logistic and Poisson regression models adjusted for demographic, health, and community characteristics and year of data collection.ResultsChildren had a mean age of 10.1 years (SD = 7.1); 42.1% received care from a medical subspecialist, 52.5% from a primary care provider, and the mean care team size was 9.1 providers (SD = 17.0). Multiple hospital admissions occurred in 80.3% of children, multiple ED visits in 40.4%, and children averaged 1.2 duplicate medications (SD = 0.90). Subspecialist involvement was associated with lower resource use: 69% lower odds of multiple admissions, 83% lower odds of multiple ED visits, and a 37% lower rate of duplicate medications. In contrast, primary care involvement and larger care team size were associated with significantly greater resource use, particularly ED visits and medication utilization.ConclusionCare team composition was significantly associated with healthcare use among rural children enrolled in hospice. Future research should examine the specific mechanisms through which care team composition influences healthcare use.

articles.title: Cigarette smoking in Canadian adolescents: A cross-sectional examination of psychosocial determinants.
articles.abstract: Tobacco cigarette smoking is often initiated during adolescence. Although rates of cigarette smoking have declined in the past decades, some Canadian adolescents still engage in this behaviour despite its widely known health risks. It is important to understand the predictors of cigarette smoking in a contemporary context. Psychosocial factors associated with cigarette smoking behaviours among Canadian adolescents are examined. # Methods This study used a population-based dataset of 23,732 Canadian adolescents in grades 6-10 who completed the 2022 cycle of the Health Behaviour in School-aged Children (HBSC) Survey. Bivariate analysis and sequential multiple logistic regression models were utilized to assess adolescents' odds of having ever smoked cigarettes in relation to a range of psychosocial predictor variables. # Results Among the participants, 7.5% reported having ever smoked cigarettes. The fully specified models showed significant associations between cigarette smoking and other substance use (vaping: Odds Ratio=26.3, alcohol: Odds Ratio = 4.7) and higher friend support (Odds Ratio = 1.1), indicating that these were predictors of cigarette smoking, when holding other factors constant. Higher relative family affluence (Odds Ratio = 0.6), having higher family support (Odds Ratio=0.9), and higher teacher support (Odds Ratio = 0.8) were significantly associated with reduced odds of cigarette smoking. # Conclusion Other substance use was a significant predictor for increased odds of smoking. Some factors that were associated with reduced odds were identified, including family and teacher support. These findings can inform future research that seeks to examine the mechanisms underlying these associations.

articles.title: Adolescent-responsive sexual and reproductive health services in Asia-Pacific settings: a systematic scoping review.
articles.abstract: In the Asia-Pacific region, adolescents face significant impacts from unintended pregnancy and are disproportionately affected by the growing HIV epidemic. Despite decades of policy commitments, adolescents have high unmet need for sexual and reproductive health services. The World Health Organization's 2015 global standards for quality adolescent health services provide a framework, but evidence of their implementation in the region remains limited. This systematic scoping review mapped approaches to adolescent-responsive sexual and reproductive health service delivery in Asia-Pacific low- and middle-income countries and factors influencing implementation. On 6 January 2026, three databases (Medline, Embase and Scopus) were searched for peer-reviewed literature published between January 2019 and December 2025. In line with scoping review methodology, methodological quality was not assessed. Twenty-five studies met the inclusion criteria, spanning nine South and Southeast Asian countries; none were from Pacific Island countries. The most evidence was available for Standards 1, 3 and 5. Where studies reported on equity and non-discrimination (Standard 6), and providers' competencies (Standard 4), they described shortfalls, although evidence on competencies was mixed. Few studies reported on community support, data and quality improvement, or adolescents' participation (Standards 2, 7 and 8), reflecting limited available evidence. These findings underscore priorities for investment in adolescent health. More comprehensive, adolescent-centred sexual and reproductive health services and action on stigma are needed, with adolescent engagement and co-leadership central to this shift. Self-care may complement formal health systems, although evidence of its effectiveness in the region remains limited.

articles.title: The impact of a co-designed PrEP referral directory on PrEP continuation among migrant female sex workers in Kisii County, Kenya.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Kenya, female sex workers (FSWs) are disproportionately burdened with HIV compared with the general population. Low continuation of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) among FSWs, driven by temporary or permanent migration from safe spaces, heightens their risk of HIV acquisition and transmission, as many do not know where to access PrEP in new locations. We evaluated the impact of a PrEP referral directory in enhancing PrEP continuation among young migrant FSWs.
METHODS: We adopted a pre-post study design, with PrEP continuation as the primary outcome. Health facilities offering PrEP in common migration destinations were mapped. FSWs aged 18-24 years were randomly selected from a safe space register, enrolled, and provided with a co-designed PrEP referral directory listing PrEP-offering facilities. Participants were encouraged to call, or text prior to migrating to facilitate early linkage to services. Phone-based follow-up interviews and facility records were used to assess continuation, comparing pre- and post-intervention periods.
RESULTS: We enrolled 299 participants: mean age was 22 years; 12 out of 299 had no formal education, 163 out of 299 had primary education and 239 out of 299 were single. Migration was the main barrier to continuation (48.1%), with 28.4% migrating twice and 23.7% three times monthly. Post-intervention, 68.2% obtained PrEP refills at linked facilities, with 96.0% citing the directory as the main facilitator. PrEP continuation increased from 17.6% pre-intervention to 41.3% post-intervention (P < 0.001). Monthly continuation rose significantly: 11% versus 40% (OR 5.1, 95% CI: 2.47-11.89) in Month 1; 20% versus 38% (OR 2.5, 95% CI: 1.36-4.96) in Month 2; 22% versus 43% (OR 2.4, 95% CI: 1.38-4.49) in Month 3; 19% versus 47% in Month 4 (OR 3.9, 95% CI: 2.04-8.11); 17% versus 43% in Month 5 (OR 3.9, 95% CI: 1.98-8.41); and 17% versus 37% in Month 6 (OR 2.8, 95% CI: 1.48-5.55). All comparisons were statistically significant (P < 0.001 for Months 1, 4 and 5; P = 0.002 for Month 2, P = 0.0013 for Month 3 and P = 0.0008 for Month 6).
CONCLUSION: The PrEP referral directory significantly improved PrEP continuation among migrating FSWs. Integrating such mobility-responsive tools into PrEP programming could strengthen PrEP continuation among mobile key populations.

articles.title: PREGNANCY OUTCOMES IN A CONTEMPORARY COHORT OF WOMEN WITH REPAIRED TETRALOGY OF FALLOT.
articles.abstract: Most women with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) now reach reproductive age, but pregnancy outcomes in contemporary cohorts, particularly after pulmonary valve replacement (PVR), remain uncertain. The aim of this study as to assess maternal cardiac, obstetric and neonatal outcomes in a contemporary cohort of women with rTOF. We retrospectively included all pregnancies in women with rTOF followed at a tertiary referral center for complex congenital heart disease (CHD) and high-risk pregnancy between 2013 and 2024. A total of 44 pregnancies in 32 women with rTOF were included, resulting in 45 live births. Severe PR was present in 43% of pregnancies, and 40% had undergone prior PVR. Maternal cardiac events occurred in 6.8%: 2 cases of supraventricular arrhythmias and 1 case of thrombosis on an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) lead. Among women with prior PVR, transvalvular gradients increased transiently during pregnancy and returned to baseline postpartum. Mean gestational age was 38 weeks, vaginal birth was preferred and cesarean section was performed in 18% of pregnancies. The most frequent adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes were low birth weight (22%) and preterm birth (11%), both associated with lower pre-pregnancy right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) possibly reflecting impaired uteroplacental perfusion related to right ventricular dysfunction. In conclusion, in this contemporary cohort, pregnancy in women with rTOF was associated with low risk of maternal cardiac events, mainly supraventricular arrhythmias. However, low birth weight and preterm birth remained frequent and were associated with lower pre-pregnancy RVEF, underscoring the importance of specialized cardio-obstetric follow-up.

articles.title: Epidemiologic profile of self-reported drug allergy in a sample of adolescent females suffering from dysmenorrhea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-reported drug allergy (SRDA) continues to be a major global public health problem, particularly among adult females.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to determine the epidemiologic profile of SRDA in adolescent females aged 13-19 years with dysmenorrhea.
MATERIAL AND METHOD: In this cross-sectional study, data of 821 participants were analyzed. The data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire. The diagnosis of allergic disease was established with self-reported information provided by participants, without performing laboratory tests or physical examination.
RESULTS: The mean age of adolescent females was 17.8 ± 0.7 years. The mean age at the onset of menarche was approximately 11.8 ± 1.4 years; moreover, 59.3% of the participants experienced regular menstruations, but 72.0% suffered from dysmenorrhea. A total of 83 (10.1%) adolescent females reported having SRDA; of these, 23 participants (27.7%) reported being allergic to more than two medications; moreover, the age at the onset of SRDA was 10.7 ± 6.6 years. Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that allergic rhinitis, consumption of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and recommended use of NSAIDs by mothers were associated with SRDA. Allergic rhinitis and consumption of NSAIDs without prescription were associated with SRDA in adolescent females suffering from dysmenorrhea.
CONCLUSION: It is important that parents understand the adverse effects that these medications generate if used without professional supervision. Healthcare professionals should be better trained to identify adolescent females with greater susceptibility to reporting SRDA.

articles.title: Laryngeal involvement in chronic spontaneous urticaria-associated angioedema: Is there a genuine risk?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) affects up to 1% of the population, and 40% of patients develop concomitant angioedema (CSU-AE). While clinically significant laryngeal involvement in mast cell-mediated CSU-AE is considered rare, and large cohorts report no fatal airway compromise, patients frequently present to emergency departments with symptoms perceived as potentially airway affecting.
OBJECTIVE: To describe retrospective clinical observations of CSU-AE patients presenting with symptoms suggestive of upper airway involvement and to contextualize these findings within the existing literature.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective descriptive review of consecutive CSU patients evaluated between October 2017 and July 2018 at two tertiary referral centers (Milan, Italy and Sofia, Bulgaria). Medical records were screened for angioedema localization, history of physician-documented laryngeal involvement during emergency evaluations, history of airway interventions, medication exposure, and acute treatment response.
RESULTS: Among 1,098 patients, 530 (48%) experienced angioedema and wheals in the context of CSU-AE. Thirteen patients (2%) had objectively documented laryngeal involvement prompting emergency assessment; three patients (all female) underwent endotracheal intubation. No fatalities or loss of consciousness occurred. None had concurrent wheals during the reported laryngeal episodes. History of NSAID exposure preceded some laryngeal exacerbations, though not in intubated cases. None of the patients was receiving ACE inhibitor treatment, all had normal C1 inhibitor (antigen and function) and normal C4. Laryngeal symptoms resolved within hours following standard acute therapy with corticosteroids and/or antihistamines (AHs). Due to the retrospective design, diagnostic work-up for alternative angioedema mechanisms (genetic testing) was incomplete.
CONCLUSIONS: These observations do not indicate an increased intrinsic airway risk in CSU-AE. Rather, they illustrate diagnostic and management challenges in emergency settings and highlight the importance of mechanism-aware clinical assessment to avoid unnecessary invasive airway interventions. Laryngeal angioedema in CSU-AE is rare and presents with a mild clinical phenotype that does not typically require airway intervention.

articles.title: Antibiotic allergy labels in children attending a tertiary paediatric allergy clinic: prevalence, clinical phenotypes and delabelling outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibiotic allergy labels are common in children, although many are assigned on the basis of clinical history and are not confirmed following specialist evaluation.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of suspected antibiotic allergy labels and to describe implicated antibiotics, reaction phenotypes, temporal trends, atopic comorbidities and oral drug provocation (ODP) outcomes among children attending a tertiary paediatric allergy clinic.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective observational study of children aged 0-17 years attending a tertiary paediatric allergy outpatient clinic in Athens, Greece, between January 2023 and December 2025. Data on reported antibiotic allergy, implicated agents, reaction phenotypes, atopic comorbidities and ODP outcomes were extracted from specialist clinical records.
RESULTS: Among 742 outpatient visits representing 569 unique children, 57 visits (7.7%; 95% CI 6.0-9.8) and 55 children (9.7%) carried a suspected antibiotic allergy label. Label prevalence declined from 10.7% in 2023 to 4.7% in 2025. Aminopenicillins accounted for 77.4% of implicated antibiotic entries, with amoxicillin-clavulanate being the most frequently implicated agent. Delayed cutaneous reactions predominated (81.0%), whereas immediate reactions were uncommon (10.3%). Among 56 completed ODP assessments, 52 (92.9%) demonstrated tolerance, including 44/47 delayed cutaneous reactions, 5/6 immediate reactions and all three challenged serum sickness-like reactions.
CONCLUSION: In this tertiary paediatric allergy cohort, reported antibiotic allergy predominantly reflected histories of non-severe beta-lactam reactions and was infrequently confirmed following specialist evaluation. These findings support careful clinical assessment and structured risk stratification, with ODP performed by experienced specialists in appropriately selected children as part of antibiotic allergy delabelling pathways.

articles.title: Association of sleep disturbances with poor asthma control in children: Unveiling a hidden burden.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a prevalent chronic condition in children and has been associated with sleep disturbances. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of sleep disturbances in children with asthma and to identify the clinical predictors of impaired sleep quality.
METHODS: The study included children aged 6-16 years with asthma who were followed at the Pediatric Allergy and Immunology Department of Ankara Bilkent City Hospital. A control group of participants with comparable age and demographic characteristics and without any history of chronic, allergic, or psychiatric conditions was also recruited. Sleep disturbances were assessed using the Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC), while asthma control was evaluated using the Childhood Asthma Control Test (C-ACT) or ACT. Asthma severity and treatment steps were categorized according to the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA).
RESULTS: A total of 210 children diagnosed with asthma (mean age: 11.2 ± 3.4 years; 54.3% male) were included in the study. According to the SDSC, 45.2% of children with asthma had clinically significant sleep disturbances. Compared to healthy controls (n = 199), asthmatic children had significantly higher total SDSC scores [63 (IQR: 50-74) vs. 53 (46-61); p < 0.001] and all subscale scores (p < 0.001). Among asthmatic children, poor asthma control, GINA Step ≥3 treatment, and asthma exacerbations within the last six months were significantly associated with sleep disturbances. In multivariate logistic regression analysis, ACT/C-ACT scores were identified as independent predictors of sleep disturbance, with higher scores associated with lower odds of sleep disturbance (OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.11-0.35; p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Poor asthma control was strongly associated with sleep impairment. Routine assessment of sleep quality could support asthma management in pediatric populations.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and treatment response of Eosinophilic Esophagitis in pediatric patients: A descriptive study in a tertiary care institution in Cali, Colombia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic immune-mediated esophageal disease with increasing incidence worldwide, although pediatric data from Latin America remain limited.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective longitudinal descriptive study including patients aged 0-18 years diagnosed with EoE between 2013 and 2023 at a tertiary referral center in Colombia. Diagnosis was based on compatible clinical manifestations and histologic confirmation on esophageal biopsy. Demographic, clinical, histologic, and allergen sensitization profiles, as well as treatment response and endoscopic follow-up, were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Seventy-five patients were included, with a median age of 10 years, and 65% were male. The most frequent symptoms were persistent gastroesophageal reflux (53%), recurrent abdominal pain (51%), and vomiting (32%). Allergic comorbidities were frequent, predominantly allergic rhinitis and asthma. Among patients who underwent follow-up endoscopy (68%), clinical and histologic remission were observed in 59% and 39%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: This pediatric cohort demonstrated a substantial atopic burden and a heterogeneous therapeutic response. The discordance between clinical and histologic remission underscores the importance of structured endoscopic follow-up. These findings provide region-specific data that may inform multidisciplinary management strategies in pediatric EoE.

articles.title: High prevalence of hypovitaminosis D in Mexican children with atopic dermatitis: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Vitamin D has been implicated in epidermal barrier function and immune regulation, but its clinical relevance in pediatric atopic dermatitis (AD) remains uncertain. This retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence of vitamin D insufficiency and deficiency in Mexican children with AD and to explore its association with disease severity in a tertiary-care setting. Patients aged 6 months to 17 years evaluated between January 2022 and January 2023 were included if they had a diagnosis of AD and an available serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D measurement. Disease severity was assessed using the SCORing Atopic Dermatitis index. A total of 423 patients were analyzed; 223 (52.7%) had mild disease, 178 (42.1%) had moderate disease, and 22 (5.2%) had severe disease. Only 23 patients (5.4%) had sufficient vitamin D levels, whereas 273 (64.5%) had insufficiency and 127 (30.0%) had deficiency. The distribution of categorical vitamin D status did not differ significantly across severity strata. Serum vitamin D levels differed modestly across severity groups, with the lowest mean concentration observed in severe disease. In the full cohort, serum vitamin D levels were not independently associated with SCORAD after age adjustment. In an exploratory analysis restricted to moderate-to-severe disease, lower vitamin D levels were associated with higher SCORAD values. Hypovitaminosis D was highly prevalent in this Mexican pediatric cohort with AD. Its relationship with disease severity appears nonuniform and should be interpreted cautiously in light of the cross-sectional design.

articles.title: Association of genotype-predicted thiopurine S-methyltransferase/nudix hydrolase 15 phenotypes with 6-mercaptopurine tolerability and hospitalization-related outcomes in Chinese pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia patients: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This multicenter retrospective study aimed to investigate the association of genotype-predicted thiopurine S-methyltransferase (TPMT) and nudix hydrolase 15 (NUDT15) phenotypes with 6-mercaptopurine (6-MP) treatment tolerance and hospitalization-related outcomes during high-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX) consolidation block in Chinese pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) patients.
METHODS: This study included 103 Chinese pediatric ALL patients. Genotypes were translated into Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium guideline-defined predicted metabolizer phenotypes, and patients were classified as predicted normal metabolizers (n = 80) or predicted intermediate metabolizers (n = 23). Data on 6-MP treatment tolerance and hospitalization-related outcomes were collected across four cycles of HD-MTX treatment. Longitudinal data were analyzed using linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models. To control the false discovery rate across the five prespecified primary outcomes in the mixed-effects modeling, multiple comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted P values (Padj) < 0.05 were considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable between the predicted normal metabolizers and intermediate metabolizer groups. The body surface area-adjusted 6-MP total dose was consistently lower in the intermediate metabolizer group across all four cycles. Longitudinal analysis confirmed that intermediate metabolizer patients experienced significantly longer inpatient stays (β = 0.98 days, Padj = 0.033), a higher risk of chemotherapy delay [odds ratio (OR) = 2.86, Padj = 0.02], and an increased likelihood of unplanned readmission (OR = 3.75, Padj = 0.018). Intermediate metabolizer status was not significantly associated with infection risk.
CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, genotype-predicted TPMT/NUDT15 intermediate metabolizer status was associated with lower prescribed 6-MP dose intensity and worse hospitalization-related outcomes during HD-MTX consolidation.

articles.title: National Trends and Demographic Disparities in Self-Reported Cognitive Difficulty Among U.S. High School Students, 2015-2023.
articles.abstract: The National Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS) asks students whether, because of a physical, mental, or emotional problem, they have serious difficulty concentrating, remembering, or making decisions. We analyzed nationally representative 2015-2023 YRBS data from 50,222 U.S. high school students using survey-weighted prevalence estimates and logistic regression. The prevalence of this self-reported cognitive difficulty increased from 29.9% (95% CI, 27.7%-32.1%) in 2015 to 45.0% (95% CI, 43.1%-47.0%) in 2023-approximately 3 in 10 students to nearly 1 in 2 (adjusted odds ratio per 2-year cycle, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.18-1.25)-while 2021 and 2023 estimates were similar. The increase was steeper among female than male students. In secondary models, insufficient sleep, excessive recreational screen use, frequent poor mental health, household basic needs not consistently met, and unstable housing were associated with cognitive difficulty. These findings identify a growing functional signal requiring surveillance, school-health assessment, referral pathways, and further study.

articles.title: Brief Report: Short-Term Outcomes of Child-Child Sexual Interactions.
articles.abstract: There is much controversy over the potential effects of sexual interactions between similar-aged children, although little empirical data relevant to the question has been offered. Exploratory, non-violent, and non-coercive play is at times conflated with abusive interactions, with both lay and professional authors fearing that sexual exploration of any kind may lead to adverse outcomes. Problems with conflation of these two experiences emerge frequently in legal contexts, where experts are requested to comment on the potential consequences of child-child sexual encounters based on very little empirical information. To investigate such interactions, 25 children seen in forensic or clinical settings were examined utilizing the Trauma Symptom Checklist for Children (TSCC). Results showed limited potential negative outcomes, with no child meeting criteria for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). One child did receive a borderline positive result and several were elevated on specific subscales, most commonly Sexual Concerns and Anxiety. In general, results suggest that child-child sexual interactions are not universally harmful, although specific reactions will vary due to family and cultural context.

articles.title: Inpatient Faecal Disimpaction in Children: A Multicentre Audit of Management Practices and Short-Term Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Faecal impaction is a common complication of paediatric functional constipation and frequently necessitates inpatient disimpaction. Despite this, there is no universally accepted protocol for inpatient management, and endpoints defining successful disimpaction remain unclear. This study aimed to audit inpatient management strategies for paediatric faecal impaction and assess whether stool output characteristics at discharge are associated with short-term clinical improvement.
METHODS: This multicentre retrospective audit included children aged 4-17 years admitted for inpatient faecal disimpaction across eight Queensland hospitals between January and December 2021. Data collected included demographics, disimpaction regimens, route of administration, adjunct enema use, length of stay (LOS), Bristol Stool Scale scores at admission and discharge, and Bowel Management Tool Scores (BMST) at admission and first follow-up.
RESULTS: Seventy-five inpatient episodes were included. Median LOS was 4 days (interquartile range, 3-5). BMST improved by a median of 3.5 points, with 73% of patients demonstrating categorical improvement at follow-up. Adjunct enemas were used in 24% of admissions and were not associated with reduced LOS compared with admissions without enemas (median 5.2 vs. 4.3 days; p=0.60). Nasogastric/gastrostomy administration was used in 71% of cases and oral administration in 29%, with no significant difference in LOS (p=0.44). Approximately 84% of patients were discharged with Bristol Stool Types 7-7+. Achieving Type 7+ stool output (clear and watery) did not confer greater improvement in BMST compared with Type 7 output [3 (1.5-7) vs. 4 (2-6.2), p=0.7].
CONCLUSION: Inpatient faecal disimpaction is associated with meaningful short-term symptom improvement in children. Treating to clear outputs does not appear to confer additional clinical benefit. These findings support a pragmatic approach to inpatient disimpaction and highlight the need for standardised, evidence-based protocols.

articles.title: Effects of Adjunctive Physiotherapy on Clinical Outcomes in Children with Functional Constipation: A Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Functional constipation (FC) is a common pediatric gastrointestinal disorder that has a substantial impact on affected children and their families. This study aimed to evaluate whether the addition of physiotherapy (PT) to standard medical treatment improves clinical outcomes in children with FC.
METHODS: In this randomized controlled study, 65 children aged 4-18 years diagnosed with FC according to the Rome IV criteria were allocated to receive standard medical treatment alone (n=35) or standard medical treatment plus PT (n=30). All patients received lactulose, toilet training, and dietary counseling. The PT program included abdominal isometric exercises, abdominal massage, pelvic floor exercises, and diaphragmatic breathing and was conducted for 3 months. The primary outcome was within-group improvement in constipation-related symptoms, and the secondary outcome was overall treatment success, defined as the absence of FC according to the Rome IV criteria at the end of follow-up.
RESULTS: All constipation-related symptoms significantly improved over time in both groups. A significant between-group difference was observed only for stool-withholding behavior, which improved more frequently in the PT group (adjusted odds ratio, 3.680; 95% confidence interval, 1.410-9.610; p=0.008). No significant intergroup differences were found in other symptoms. The overall treatment success rate was higher in the PT group than in the standard medical treatment group (100.0% vs. 85.7%, p=0.031).
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive PT may improve short-term overall treatment success in children with FC, particularly by reducing stool-withholding behavior. Larger studies with longer follow-up periods are required to confirm these findings.

articles.title: A Systematic Review and Decision Analysis of the Accuracy of Intestinal Lymphogram for Celiac Disease in Children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Celiac disease (CD) is characterized by an increased proportion of CD3+ T-cell receptor gamma/delta-positive (TCRγδ+) intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) and a reduced number of CD3-IELs. We aimed to summarize available evidence on the accuracy of intestinal flow cytometry for diagnosing CD in children.
METHODS: Electronic and manual searches were performed using keywords related to diagnostic validity. Two researchers independently extracted data from the selected studies. Pooled estimates of the accuracy measures were calculated using a random-effects model, and the risk of bias and threshold effect were further assessed. The clinical utility of intestinal lymphogram in diagnosing several serological and histological phenotypes (conventional, seronegative, and potential CD) was simulated using a Bayesian approach. Accordingly, the meta-analyzed indicators and several assumptions regarding CD prevalence were considered.
RESULTS: The search yielded 656 citations, of which seven were finally included, providing a population of 1,248 patients with CD. Pooled sensitivity and specificity of combined high TCRγδ+ and low CD3-IELs were 90% and 99%, respectively. Only two high-quality studies provided sensitivity data for children initially diagnosed with potential CD. Across both cohorts, 38% of children with potential CD progressed to CD, based on heterogeneous diagnostic criteria. Using pooled diagnostic accuracy measures for this pre-test probability, the resulting positive and negative predictive values were 98% and 95%, respectively. No specific data on seronegative CD were retrieved.
CONCLUSION: The intraepithelial lymphogram acts as a potentially useful adjunctive marker in children, though its prognostic value in potential CD remains uncertain.

articles.title: Clinical, Laboratory, and Genetic Evaluations of Cystic Fibrosis Patients with Gastrointestinal System Involvement.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal recessive genetic disease caused by a mutation in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator gene. This study provides a detailed evaluation of patients with CF and gastrointestinal (GI) involvement at our university, a reference center in southern Turkey, with respect to genetic, clinical, radiological, and anthropometric characteristics.
METHODS: The clinical, laboratory, and radiological findings, genetic results, and prognoses of 97 patients diagnosed with CF and followed at the Cukurova University Medical Faculty, Department of Pediatric Gastroenterology, between 2011 and 2022 were retrospectively reviewed.
RESULTS: Pancreatic insufficiency was detected in 75.3% of patients and was the most common GI manifestation. It was followed by growth retardation (64.9%; defined as a weight below the 5th percentile at any time during follow-up), constipation (30.9%), gastroesophageal reflux (GER; 14.4%), hepatic steatosis (4.1%), pancreatitis (4.1%), rectal prolapse (1.0%), and meconium ileus (1.0%). Genetic analysis showed that F508del was the most common mutation (14.4%). According to the Gomez and Waterlow classifications, malnutrition improved significantly over time (p<0.05).
CONCLUSION: In recent years, the inclusion of CF in newborn screening programs in many countries has enabled earlier diagnosis. Along with a better understanding of its pathophysiology, improved care, and advances in treatment, this has increased the number of patients followed into adulthood. Because CF is a multisystem disease, a multidisciplinary approach is required.

articles.title: Early Complications of Epicardial Permanent Pacemaker Implantation in Neonates and Infants Weighing 5 kg or Less.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: We evaluated the incidence and predictors of early complications following epicardial permanent pacemaker (ePPM) implantation in neonates and infants weighing 5 kg or less.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 40 patients weighing 5 kg or less who underwent ePPM implantation between 1999 and 2025. Early complications were defined as ePPM-related adverse events requiring medical or surgical intervention within 6 months post-implantation. Firth's penalized logistic regression was performed to identify predictors for early complications. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) determined the optimal cutoff value.
RESULTS: The median age and body weight at implantation were 58 days (interquartile range [IQR], 21.8-118.3 days) and 3.7 kg (IQR, 3.2-4.3 kg), respectively. Early complications occurred in 9 patients (22.5%), including wound dehiscence (n=5), pocket infection (n=3), and pericardial effusion (n=1). On multivariable analysis, body weight at implantation was an independent predictor of complications (odds ratio [OR], 0.77 per 100-g increase; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60-0.98; p=0.031). ROC analysis identified 3.5 kg as the optimal cutoff value for predicting early complications (area under the curve, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.87-1.00; p<0.001), with 100% sensitivity and 84% specificity. A staged ePPM implantation strategy using initial temporary epicardial pacing was performed without early complications in four high-risk patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Early complications remain a significant concern after ePPM implantation in neonates and infants weighing 5kg or less, with body weight identified as an independent predictor. Patients weighing below 3.5 kg represent a high-risk subgroup requiring tailored surgical strategies and vigilant postoperative surveillance.

articles.title: Survival after neonatal chest compressions at birth: Temporal trends and prognostic factors in a population-based cohort, Queensland, Australia.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine temporal trends and prognostic factors for 28-day survival among infants receiving chest compressions (CC) in Queensland, Australia.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using the Queensland Perinatal Data Collection (2008-2024), including all liveborn CC recipients at birth. Temporal trends in crude 28-day survival were examined overall and by gestational age (GA) groups. Multivariable generalised estimating equations were used to identify factors independently associated with survival while accounting for clustering within birthing locations.
RESULTS: Among 3,077 CC recipients, 70.5% established regular spontaneous breathing within 60 minutes of birth, and 89.0% survived to 28 days. Crude 28-day survival improved from 82% in 2008 to 89% in 2024 and was consistently higher in term (GA ≥37+0 weeks) than preterm infants. Compared with term infants, adjusted odds of survival declined with decreasing GA: 32+0 to 36+6 weeks (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40-0.77), 28+0 to 31+6 weeks (aOR 0.35, 95% CI 0.23-0.54), and <28+0 weeks (aOR 0.17, 95% CI 0.12-0.23). However, after adjusting for cord pH or epinephrine administration, survival in infants born at 32+0 to 36+6 weeks did not differ significantly from term infants.
CONCLUSION: Survival to 28 days among CC recipients was high and increased over time. Lower gestational age was the strongest independent prognostic factor for mortality, although the survival difference between term and moderate-to-late preterm infants was attenuated after adjustment for cord pH or epinephrine administration. Prospective studies assessing CC indications and measures of resuscitation quality are needed to optimise neonatal resuscitation and improve outcomes.

articles.title: Pediatric forensic cases during the COVID 19 lockdown and reopening periods: a retrospective cohort study from a tertiary care pediatric emergency department.
articles.abstract: The COVID‑19 lockdown disrupted daily life, altering children's exposure to risks and reshaping emergency department utilisation. Understanding how these changes influenced pediatric forensic epidemiology is essential for prevention and policy development. All forensic cases involving children aged 1 month-18 years were included. Two periods were analysed: the COVID-19 lockdown period (March 2020-June 2021) and the post-lockdown period (June 2021-March 2024). Data on demographics, causes, outcomes and costs were extracted from medical and forensic records. During the COVID‑19 lockdown period, the incidence of forensic cases was 25.8 per 1000 PED visits per month, whereas during the reopening period this rate decreased to 12.7 per 1000 PED visits per month (p < 0.001). Exposure to chemical substances and assault were more frequent during the lockdown period (p = 0.01 and p = 0.001, respectively), whereas food poisoning was more common during the reopening period (p = 0.004). Forensic cases were predominant among female adolescents (p = 0.004). Male sex was associated with a significantly higher likelihood of forensic cases (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.05-1.49, p = 0.011). Furthermore, the COVID-19 lockdown period was independently associated with an increased odds of forensic cases (OR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.65-2.56, p < 0.001). The median outpatient and total bills per PED visit were lower in forensic cases (48.7 vs. 68.1 TRY, p < 0.001 and 57.8 vs. 90.2 TRY, p < 0.001, respectively). Different COVID‑19 periods were associated with significant differences in the incidence, causes, and patterns of pediatric forensic cases. Male sex and the lockdown period were identified as independent risk factors for forensic presentations, highlighting the complex interaction between demographic and temporal factors in forensic epidemiology.

articles.title: Trends in United States Pediatric In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Incidence and Mortality in a Nationally Representative Sample, 2009-2022.
articles.abstract:
AIM: National estimates of pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) incidence in the United States rely on a voluntary registry that may underrepresent smaller and critical access hospitals. Administrative datasets offer a nationally representative alternative. We estimated nationally representative pediatric IHCA incidence and mortality trends from 2009 through 2022.
METHODS: Serial cross-sectional analysis of five triennial editions of the Kids' Inpatient Database (2009-2022), identifying IHCA in children <18 years by ICD-9 (99.60, 99.63) and ICD-10 (5A12012) cardiopulmonary resuscitation procedure codes. Two hospitals with implausible CPR rates were excluded. Survey-weighted incidence per 1,000 hospitalizations and in-hospital mortality among resuscitated children were estimated overall and by neonatal status, complex chronic condition (CCC) status, ZIP-code income quartile, and US Census region. Trends were tested with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression across the full period and, as exploratory analyses, within the ICD-10 era (2016-2022).
RESULTS: Observed IHCA incidence was 1.11/1,000 in 2009 and 1.22/1,000 in 2012, decreased to 1.11/1,000 at the ICD-10 transition and increased to 1.35/1,000 by 2022. IHCA incidence in children hospitalized with a CCC rose from 3.26 to 6.60/1,000 (6.2%/year, p<0.001), while incidence without CCC remained low. Incidence varied by socioeconomic status (lowest vs highest income quartile 1.78 vs 1.04/1,000 in 2022). In-hospital mortality ranged from 34.1% (2012) to 40.4% (2019), whereas IHCA deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased 1.7%/year (p<0.001), concentrated among children with a CCC.
CONCLUSION: The incidence of pediatric IHCA increased among hospitalizations involving children with CCC and was higher among children who live in lower income areas. In-hospital mortality after CPR was largely stable, whereas arrest-related deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased among children with CCC. A single hospital's coding practices can materially distort national administrative estimates. What is already known Pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest affects approximately 15,200 children annually in the United States, with this national estimate derived primarily from a voluntary registry that may underrepresent smaller and critical access hospitals. Administrative databases offer nationally representative coverage but rely on procedure codes that are susceptible to misclassification. What this study adds In this nationally representative administrative database sample spanning 2009-2022, this study demonstrated that: 1) the incidence of IHCA among children with complex chronic conditions (CCC) rose steadily and accounted for the substantial majority of events, 2) the overall IHCA incidence was higher among children who live in lower income areas with the gradient worsening over the period evaluated, and 3) in-hospital mortality after CPR increased only slightly (34-40%), whereas arrest-related deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased more, driven mainly by rising incidence among children with CCC, and 4) CPR coding at a single hospital can substantially distort national administrative estimates.

articles.title: Opioid Prescribing Calibration, Consumption, and Disposal After Posterior Spinal Fusion for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: A 7-year Institutional Stewardship Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) pathways have reduced inpatient opioid exposure after posterior spinal fusion (PSF) for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), yet the discharge prescription has received far less scrutiny. Temporal trends in prescription size, caregiver-reported consumption, and household disposal of unused medication remain poorly characterized.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 321 patients aged 10 to 20 years undergoing primary PSF for AIS from 2018 to 19 through 2024 to 25 at a single tertiary pediatric hospital. Prescribing among 275 patients discharged with tablets was modeled with multivariable linear regression. Caregiver-reported pill counts from a postoperative survey (consumption cohort, n=79; telephone era, n=36; text-message era, n=43) informed consumption and waste analyses; disposal and home pain-management items came from all respondents (n=91 to 115 per item). Sensitivity analyses addressed pathway timing, survey modality, response bias, and missing pill counts among families still taking opioids.
RESULTS: Median tablets prescribed declined 67%, from 55 to 18 (adjusted β=-4.91 tablets/year; 95% CI, -5.53 to -4.29; P<0.001), beginning before the most recent ERAS pathway. Reported consumption declined from a median of 30 to 7 tablets, but this decline could not be separated from the survey modality change (telephone era only, P=0.69). The median unused proportion rose from 10% to 40% (unadjusted β=+4.6 percentage points/year; P=0.004) but not significantly after adjustment (P=0.056) or when families still taking opioids were assumed to use their full prescription. Among families with leftover opioids, 22% reported disposal. Requests for additional pain medication (18%) and satisfaction (93%) did not differ between survey eras.
CONCLUSIONS: Discharge opioid prescribing after PSF for AIS declined substantially over 7 years without an apparent change in home pain-management outcomes. Consumption and waste estimates are less certain because they rest on a small, survey-dependent cohort. A default prescription near 15 tablets is a hypothesis for prospective testing, and routine disposal kits at discharge warrant evaluation.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV-therapeutic study.

articles.title: Navigating discharge information during early oral antibiotic switch in children: a qualitative comparison of caregiver and clinician experiences.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early switch from intravenous (IV) to oral antibiotic therapy is clinically safe for hospitalized children and supports earlier discharge. Responsibility for ongoing care then shifts to caregivers, increasing reliance on effective communication during the hospital-to-home transition.
OBJECTIVE: To explore the information needs and preferences of caregivers during children's transition home on oral antibiotic therapy and examine clinician perceptions of these needs.
METHODS: This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with caregivers of children discharged home on oral antibiotics following IV therapy and clinicians involved in their care. Participants were recruited through a hospital participating in the HOMEFREE program and consumer networks. Interviews explored information needs, timing, delivery, understanding, and discharge readiness. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, followed by interpretation through Longo's Extended Model of Health Information Seeking Behaviour.
RESULTS: Fifteen caregivers and eight clinicians participated. Four interrelated themes were identified. Information was frequently delivered at clinically appropriate but challenging time points, limiting families' ability to absorb key messages. Clinicians relied primarily on verbal communication, whereas caregivers preferred written information that could be revisited after discharge. Confidence in oral antibiotic therapy developed through observing recovery at home rather than clinical explanation alone. Caregivers often compensated for information gaps through vigilance and self-advocacy, and clinicians recognised that this dynamic could advantage more confident families.
CONCLUSIONS: Although oral antibiotic switch is clinically safe, family confidence and preparedness may be influenced by how information is delivered and used. Timely, multimodal communication may support safer and more equitable discharge.

articles.title: Increasing Emergency Department Burden of Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Injuries: A National 10-Year Analysis of Mechanisms and Severity Predictors, 2015-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ) is a rapidly growing grappling-based combat sport, but emergency department (ED) surveillance and sport-specific mechanism classification are limited.
HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that BJJ-related ED visits have grown disproportionately compared with overall martial arts ED presentations and that sport-specific mechanisms predict nonroutine disposition.
STUDY DESIGN: Descriptive epidemiology study.
METHODS: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS), 2015-2024. BJJ cases were identified from product code 3257, which corresponds to martial arts equipment and activity-related injuries, followed by a 2-reviewer narrative review. Trends were analyzed using survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression. An 11-category force vector mechanism taxonomy was developed from narratives. Pre- versus post-COVID eras were compared with false discovery rate correction. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of nonroutine disposition.
RESULTS: Of 7618 martial arts ED visits, 1448 (19.0%) were BJJ related (58,170 weighted national cases). Annual BJJ volume rose nearly 5-fold (incidence rate ratio, 1.148/year; 95% CI, 1.090-1.209; P < .001) while total martial arts volume remained stable; BJJ's share climbed from 7.3% to 27.7%. The cohort was 78.0% male (mean age 25.7 ± 12.3 years); pediatric patients (≤17 years) comprised 29.5%. Strain/sprain (23.2%), fracture (15.5%), and contusion/abrasion (9.3%) predominated. The taxonomy classified 69.8% of cases into 8 defined categories, led by direct impact (21.8%), joint torque (16.4%), and fall (11.2%), with the remaining 30.2% indeterminate; the era profile was stable after multiplicity correction. Four independent predictors of nonroutine disposition emerged: internal injury (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 20.62; 95% CI, 7.55-56.26), neck compression (aOR, 5.26; 95% CI, 1.84-14.98), fracture (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 1.30-10.90), and age (aOR, 1.50 per decade; 95% CI, 1.18-1.90); optimism-corrected C-statistic = 0.748.
CONCLUSION: Our study showed that BJJ-related ED presentations are rising rapidly while the injury profile remains stable; because denominators are unavailable, these are presentation counts rather than a measured change in per-capita injury risk. The injury taxonomy and disposition model further identified predictors of injury patterns and ED disposition. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective, exposure-denominated validation.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of ultrasound elastography for assessing liver stiffness in children with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and biliary atresia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of two-dimensional shear wave elastography (2D-SWE) in assessing liver stiffness in pediatric patients with NAFLD and in infants with biliary atresia (BA).
METHODS: In this retrospective study with case-control sampling, 129 children with NAFLD and 129 healthy controls, as well as 83 infants with BA and 83 age-matched infants with non-BA cholestasis, were enrolled. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) was performed using 2D-SWE. Demographic, anthropometric, biochemical, and conventional ultrasound data were collected at enrollment.
RESULTS: In the NAFLD cohort, LSM was significantly higher in the NAFLD group than in healthy controls (4.42 ± 0.92 vs. 3.74 ± 0.28 kPa; P < 0.001), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.865 (95% CI: 0.820-0.910). All other metabolic, inflammatory, and ultrasound measurements also showed significant differences between the two groups (all P < 0.05), except for age, sex, total bilirubin, and direct bilirubin (P > 0.05). In the BA cohort, LSM was significantly higher in BA infants than in non-BA cholestasis infants (13.58 ± 8.46 vs. 6.31 ± 1.02 kPa; P < 0.001; AUC = 0.890, 95% CI: 0.865-0.935). BA infants also showed significantly elevated liver enzymes, bilirubin, inflammatory markers, and rates of gallbladder abnormality, splenomegaly, and ascites, as well as lower lipid levels (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: 2D-SWE provides good diagnostic accuracy for detecting liver stiffness in pediatric NAFLD and BA, supporting its use as a non-invasive assessment tool for group discrimination in these two distinct pediatric liver diseases.

articles.title: Prevalence and associated factors of enuresis among primary school-aged children in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nocturnal enuresis (NE) is a common childhood condition that can cause psychological distress, social isolation, and impaired quality of life for affected children and their families. However, most previous studies have focused on children and adolescents as a whole, with limited evidence specifically for primary school-aged pupils.
PURPOSE: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the prevalence and associated factors of NE among primary school students (5-12 years) in China.
METHODS: We searched the China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, the China Science and Technology Journal Database, PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science for cross-sectional studies on the prevalence and associated factors of NE in Chinese primary school children from inception to May 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment. A random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool prevalence estimates and odds ratios (ORs). Descriptive subgroup analyses and random-effects meta-regression were performed to explore heterogeneity.
RESULTS: Twenty-two studies involving 161,662 participants (11,091 NE cases) were included. The pooled prevalence of NE was 10% (95% CI: 9%-11%), which should be interpreted as a descriptive summary of the available data rather than a precise population estimate, given the substantial heterogeneity across studies (I2 = 100%). Descriptively, the prevalence was higher in males (9%) than in females (6%) and showed a downward trend with age, decreasing from 16% at age 5 to 2% at age 12. Meta-regression analysis indicated that diagnostic criteria alone did not account for the observed between-study heterogeneity (R2 = 0%, I2 res = 99.16%). Significant associated factors included male sex (OR = 1.48), family history of NE (OR = 2.60), constipation (OR = 1.85), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (OR = 2.63), arousal dysfunction (OR = 2.76), bedtime fluid intake (OR = 1.95), daytime symptoms (OR = 1.88), and living in households with three or more children (OR = 2.32), while older age was associated with lower odds of NE (OR = 0.76).
CONCLUSION: NE prevalence among Chinese primary school children is relatively high and influenced by multiple demographic, genetic, physiological, and environmental factors. Enhanced screening and comprehensive management for this population are warranted. However, given the persistent, massive heterogeneity (I2 = 100%) that remains unexplained by diagnostic criteria, this pooled prevalence should be interpreted with caution as a contextual descriptive summary rather than a single standardized parameter.

articles.title: Pain Pathophysiology and Assessment in Pediatric Critical Care.
articles.abstract: Pain is pervasive and affects upwards of 59% of critically ill children. Consequences of severe pain include worsened health related quality of life and longer lengths of stay. Evaluating pain in non-verbal critically ill children is a unique challenge due to difficulties with communication and the wide variety of developmental stages. The purpose of our review is to examine the underlying pathophysiology of pain, the current landscape in pain assessment of non-verbal critically ill children and pain assessment tools for non-verbal critically ill children. We performed literature searches from April 25, 2023 to November 20, 2025; we performed literature searches using PubMed and EMBASE with a combination of keywords that included "pain", "pathophysiology", "pediatric", "comfort-behavioral", "FLACC", "P-CPOT", "ventilated", "PICU". The pathophysiology of pain starts with inflammatory reactions at the site of injury, which are transmitted via the dorsal horn to the ascending spinothalamic tract and converge onto the brain using two separate pathways. There are three behavioral pain scales that have been validated in both ventilated and non-ventilated critically ill children: the faces, legs, activity, crying, and consolability scale; the COMFORT-Behavior scale; and the pediatric critical care pain observation tool. While pain assessments are regularly performed in PICUs worldwide, there still exist sites in which validated scales are not used, or no scales are used to evaluate pain. Pain is frequent among critically ill children, and its prompt identification can be challenging. Understanding the pathophysiology of pain and the barriers that clinicians face in identifying pain, particularly in non-verbal critically ill children, will improve the care of these patients.

articles.title: Molecular epidemiology, virulence gene profiles, and clinical outcomes of bovine Cryptosporidium in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: Cryptosporidium spp. are major causes of neonatal calf diarrhea and represent a zoonotic concern. This study investigated Cryptosporidium occurrence, GP60 subtype distribution, and selected virulence-associated gene targets in bovine field samples from Türkiye. Fecal samples were collected from 83 diarrheic calves aged 5-30 days from 20 farms; after 16 of the sampled calves subsequently died, their respective asymptomatic dams were additionally sampled as an outcome-dependent, calf-associated group rather than as an independent control group. All 99 samples were screened by Kinyoun acid-fast staining, and the 76 microscopy-positive samples were subsequently subjected to SSU 18S rRNA nested PCR. Ten virulence-associated gene targets were screened by PCR, and GP60 subtyping was performed for all PCR-confirmed samples. Oocyst-like structures were detected in 76/99 samples (76.8%), and 74/76 (97.4%) microscopy-positive samples were confirmed by PCR. GP60 sequence analysis identified two C. parvum IIa subtype patterns: IIaA13G2R1 (58/74, 78.4%) and IIaA14G1R1 (16/74, 21.6%). In this dataset, IIaA13G2R1 was detected in all fatal calf cases and their asymptomatic dams, whereas IIaA14G1R1 was observed only among non-fatal diarrheic calves. GP60, COWP, Cp15, TRAP-C1, HSP70, HSP90, and aminopeptidase-like metalloprotease were detected in all 74 PCR-confirmed samples; cryptopain and cryptostatin were each detected in 65/74 samples (87.8%), and CDPK in 58/74 samples (78.4%). Among the variably detected targets, CDPK showed an exploratory association with calf outcome; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously. Apart from previous PCR-based work targeting COWP and Cp15, this study provides the first broader PCR-based profile of selected virulence-associated gene targets in bovine Cryptosporidium field samples from Türkiye. These findings represent preliminary molecular associations and should not be interpreted as evidence of gene expression, functional virulence, or causality.

articles.title: Return to School and Readmission Risk After Pain-Related Hospitalizations in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pain is the primary cause of inpatient admissions in sickle cell disease (SCD) and readmission is common. For school-aged youth, successful transition from the hospital necessitates school reentry. This study assessed rates of school return following a pain-related admission and the relationship between school return and readmission.
METHODS: Sixteen youth (7-17 years) admitted for SCD-related pain and caregivers completed daily surveys about school attendance and pain severity for 10 consecutive school days after discharge. Descriptive, independent samples t-test, and chi-square analyses were used to assess differences in pain, school attendance, and readmission.
RESULTS: On average, participants (age M = 13.75; 69% female; 75% HbSS) attended 6.13 out of 10 school days, with 25% returning the next school day after discharge and 13% attending all 10 days. Almost all (94%) reported ongoing pain throughout the monitoring period. Most youth (63%) exhibited variable school attendance after initial school return. Those with variable attendance attended fewer school days (M = 4.40, SD = 2.46) compared to "consistent school attenders" (M = 9, SD = 0.89), p < 0.001, and reported higher daily pain (MVariableAttenders = 3.78, SDVariableAttenders = 1.68; MConsistentAttenders = 1.47, SDConsistentAttenders = 0.81), p = 0.007. Half of "variable school attenders" were readmitted, compared to none of the consistent attenders, χ2 (df = 1) = 4.36, p = 0.037.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that school reentry after a pain-related hospitalization is difficult for many patients and essential to consider in discharge planning. Youth continue reporting pain following discharge, with some experiencing variable school attendance and readmission for pain. Promoting school attendance should be a core component of comprehensive SCD management plans, with implications for pain management and healthcare utilization.

articles.title: Transfer to adult care - experiences of young adults living with human immunodeficiency virus in Jamaica.
articles.abstract: Combination antiretroviral therapy has improved health outcomes for adolescents living with the human Immunodeficiency Virus (ALHIV). Long-term survival necessitates effective interventions for optimal continuity of care as they transition to adult healthcare. No National Transition Policy for adolescents with chronic illnesses exists in Jamaica, despite anecdotal reports of informal, site-specific processes for their transfer from pediatric to adult care settings. We present qualitative evaluative feedback from eleven young adults living with HIV (YALHIV) (18-34 years old) post-transfer from pediatric to adult care. Identified themes included: (1) perceptions of transfer - apprehension and uncertainty, (2) barriers to transfer - remorse about moving to adult clinics, stigma, loss of bond with providers, lack of communication, (3) facilitators - greater personal responsibility, shorter wait times with flexible scheduling at the adult clinic, (4) self-management (adherence to clinic visits and antiretroviral medication) and (5) recommendations - enhanced collaboration between pediatric and adult healthcare providers (HCP), pre-transfer exposure to the adult clinic, and increased psychoeducation pre- and post-transfer. These qualitative findings inform the transition process for YALHIV, which should be optimized through early, continual disclosure of diagnosis and enhanced psychoeducation for clients, while fostering a collaborative approach between pediatric and adult healthcare providers.

articles.title: Feasibility of implementing a digital peer-support intervention aimed at reducing HIV-related stigma among adolescents and young adults living with HIV in south Ethiopia.
articles.abstract: Adolescents and young adults living with HIV (AYLHIV) experience a high burden of HIV-related stigma, but there are limited data on the interventions needed to reduce stigma. We assessed the feasibility of a planned Telegram-based peer-support intervention to reduce HIV-related stigma among AYLHIV in south Ethiopia. Eighteen AYLHIV (15-22 years old) were recruited from three public hospitals. The nine-week intervention was delivered via Telegram Messenger following an initial digital skill orientation, irrespective of prior experience of using the mobile application. In a mixed-methods design, we collected data using semi-structured face-to-face interviews and focus group discussions and reported feasibility outcomes using Bowen et al.'s framework. Participants described the discussion platform as private, safe, and supportive, with a family-like atmosphere. Retention was high (94.4%) and the overall scheduled-session attendance rate was 67.6%. Participants exchanged 4,033 messages, with an average of 13 messages per participant per session. Contextual, operational, and technical barriers may have reduced engagement; participants also provided recommendations to improve future intervention. Overall, the Telegram Messenger-based digital peer-support intervention appears feasible and acceptable across key feasibility domains, supporting progression to an evaluation of intervention effectiveness.Abbreviations: AYLHIV: adolescents and young adults living with HIV; ART: antiretroviral therapy; ARV: antiretroviral; EAT: East Africa Time; GB: gigabyte(s); HIV: human immunodeficiency virus; IT: information technology; mHealth: mobile health; MRC: Medical Research Council; SD: standard deviation.

articles.title: A Pilot Study of Peer-Delivered Sun Safety Education: Impact on Elementary Students' Dermatologic Knowledge and Melanoma Identification Skills.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Skin cancer is the most common cancer affecting Americans, with sun exposure during childhood playing a major role in skin cancer development. Traditional adult-delivered sun safety programs face engagement limitations, while peer-delivered education may enhance learning through social modeling and relatability.
OBJECTIVES: To present the results of a pilot study evaluating the preliminary effectiveness of a peer-delivered sun safety education program in improving elementary students' comprehensive dermatologic knowledge, including skin anatomy, melanoma identification skills, and sun protection knowledge.
METHODS: In this single-site pilot study, forty-six elementary students (22 third-graders, 24 fifth-graders) completed a comprehensive 9-item knowledge assessment immediately before and after a peer-delivered skin and sun education presentation. Two trained student presenters delivered content covering skin anatomy, ultraviolet radiation, physical versus chemical sunscreens, sun protection strategies, and melanoma ABCs with visual examples. The assessment evaluated anatomical knowledge, sunscreen science, melanoma identification skills, and sun safety knowledge; two additional unscored behavioral questions (sunburn history and intention to protect the skin) were also asked.
RESULTS: In this pilot sample, both grades demonstrated statistically significant improvements with very large effect sizes. Third-graders improved from 5.73 to 8.41 out of 9 points (p<0.001, Cohen's dz=2.29). Fifth-graders improved from 6.42 to 8.75 points (p<0.001, dz=2.08). Overall, 93.5% of students showed improved knowledge.
CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary pilot study, peer-to-peer education was associated with significant immediate improvements in sun safety knowledge among elementary students. However, given the small sample size (n = 46) and single-site, uncontrolled design, these findings are hypothesis-generating. Further evaluation in larger, multi-site, controlled studies is needed before broader conclusions about the generalizability or superiority of this peer education model can be drawn. This pilot may inform the design of future school-based melanoma prevention research.

articles.title: Hyperkeratotic Halo Nevus in Childhood: Three Cases with Standard and UV Dermoscopic Documentation and Narrative Review of the Literature.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Halo nevus (HN) is a benign melanocytic lesion with a peripheral depigmented halo due to immune-mediated regression. A rare hyperkeratotic pediatric variant may precede halo development, posing a diagnostic challenge.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the clinical and dermoscopic features of hyperkeratotic halo nevus (HHN) in children.
METHODS: We performed a narrative literature review and reported a case series of three children evaluated with clinical examination, dermoscopy, and UV dermoscopy. Screening for autoimmune diseases included thyroid function, anti-thyroid antibodies, and celiac serology.
RESULTS: Three Caucasian children (mean age 9 years) presented with multiple asymptomatic hyperkeratotic halo nevi, mainly on the trunk (Fitzpatrick II). Diagnosis was based on clinical and dermoscopic findings; biopsy was not required. Thyroid function and celiac serology were unremarkable in all patients, while one patient showed positive anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies despite normal thyroid function. UV dermoscopy enhanced visualization of perilesional depigmentation and showed increased central reflectance, which we interpreted as a possible keratin-related optical phenomenon.
CONCLUSIONS: HHN is a rare but benign variant of HN that can be diagnosed clinically when dermoscopic features are reassuring. UV dermoscopy may provide complementary information by enhancing visualization of perilesional depigmentation; the observed increased central reflectance may represent a keratin-related optical phenomenon, although this interpretation requires further validation.

articles.title: Eruptive Melanocytic Nevi in a 11-Year-Old Girl Following Stevens-Johnson Syndrome: Case Report and Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Eruptive melanocytic nevi (EMN) are melanocytic nevi occurring in a short time interval. EMN may be idiopathic or triggered by dermatological conditions and/or systemic treatments.
OBJECTIVES: We report the case of an 11-year-old female patient developing EMN after a bullous eruption, and performed a systematic review of current literature, focusing on pediatric EMN both idiopathic and dermatologically triggered.
METHODS: A literature search, using PubMed database and following PRISMA guidelines, was carried out, including all records up to the 6th of June 2025. Inclusion criteria were: English language, human subjects, age </= 18 years, idiopathic or dermatologically triggered EMN, detailed clinical data.
RESULTS: 30 pediatric patients with EMN were included in the review. Idiopathic cases accounted for 7 patients, while a clear dermatological cause was reported in 22/30 patients. Of note one patient developed EMN after Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) without previous skin involvement. A complete clinical correspondence between previous lesions and EMN has been found in 6/11 patients with a history of previous bullous eruption, and only in 2/7 patients with LCH displaying skin involvement. Histological examination in 25/30 patients revealed compound or junctional nevi, with no cases of melanoma.
CONCLUSIONS: Even if patients undergoing severe bullous eruptions frequently receive systemic immunosuppressive treatments, the high level of anatomic correspondence between bullous lesions and subsequent EMN seems to suggest an etiological link between the disruption of the cutaneous basement membrane and the melanocytic proliferation. Conversely, in LCH, EMN may be triggered by both cutaneous lesions and systemic treatments. Melanoma occurs rarely among EMN, although follow-up is recommended.

articles.title: Pediatric Musculoskeletal Emergencies: A Primer for Practicing Radiologists.
articles.abstract: Acute musculoskeletal conditions are a frequent cause of pediatric emergency imaging. In children, skeletal immaturity and open physes influence injury patterns, predisposing to unique fracture types. Incomplete ossification and growth plate anatomy may obscure or mimic pathology, complicating interpretation. Beyond trauma, musculoskeletal infections are also common reasons for pediatric emergency visits. Radiographs remain the first-line imaging modality, while ultrasound, CT, and MR imaging are important problem solving modalities. Clear understanding of age-related patterns of musculoskeletal injury and infection, normal anatomic variants, and imaging pitfalls allows accurate assessment of various acute musculoskeletal conditions in the pediatric population.

articles.title: Abdominopelvic Imaging Emergency in Children: A Comprehensive Update and Review.
articles.abstract: Abdominopelvic emergencies are one of the most common causes of pediatric emergency department visits, frequently resulting in urgent surgical management. Because conditions such as midgut, volvulus and torsion are time-sensitive, accurate and timely diagnosis is essential and imaging evaluation plays a crucial role. Following abdominal radiograph, ultrasound remains the preferred next imaging modality in most conditions to avoid radiation, even more so with the introduction of contrast-enhanced ultrasound. Advancements in computed tomography and MRI continue to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient safety. This article provides an up-to-date review of current imaging protocols and imaging characteristics of pediatric abdominopelvic emergency conditions.

articles.title: Pediatric Thoracic Imaging Emergency: Practical Approach for Daily Practice.
articles.abstract: Imaging of thoracic emergencies in children is crucial for early diagnosis, guiding treatment, and avoiding severe complications. Radiography, ultrasound, and computed tomography are the most common modalities in emergency imaging. Radiologists should be familiar with the appropriate choice of imaging modality and the radiologic characteristics of serious conditions that can present acutely in the pediatric emergency room. This article discusses a practical overview of the major pediatric thoracic emergencies, including pulmonary infections, airway abnormalities, neoplasms, air leaks, traumatic injuries, and foreign bodies. An up-to-date review of key imaging findings is provided, with emphasis on features that are unique to children.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Emergency Radiology: Where Do We Stand Now?
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in pediatric emergency radiology, where timely and accurate image interpretation is critical. Current evidence highlights its strongest role in detection and localization tasks across neuroimaging, thoracic, abdominopelvic, and musculoskeletal studies. AI also shows promise for classification, severity assessment, and workflow prioritization, improving diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in some settings. However, existing research is limited by retrospective designs, small datasets, insufficient external validation, and poor transferability of adult-trained models. Pediatric-specific models, multicenter validation, prospective studies, and thoughtful clinical integration are needed before wider adoption beyond assistive use in routine pediatric emergency imaging practice today.

articles.title: Serum Renin As a Prognostic Biomarker in Children With Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) derangement contributes to acute kidney injury (AKI) and is associated with poor outcomes in critical illness. Serum renin, a clinically available biomarker of RAAS derangement, is associated with poor outcomes in critically ill adults and children. Renin has not been evaluated in children with sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI), either alone or in combination with other prognostic enrichment tools, including the recently derived pediatric sepsis-associated AKI (pSAKI) subphenotypes.
DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a multicenter, prospective, observational study of pediatric septic shock.
SETTING: Ten U.S. PICUs from January 2002 to February 2025.
PATIENTS: Patients 0-18 years old with early SA-AKI (serum creatinine-based Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 1-3 on days 1-2 of admission) with residual day 1 serum available for renin measurement.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Seven hundred eight patients were examined by renin tertiles. The highest renin tertile cohort (T3, > 247 pg/mL) had one fewer severe AKI-free day (4 [0-6] vs. 5 [1-7] T2 vs. 5 [2-7] T1; p < 0.001), higher day 7 severe AKI rates (47% vs. 32% vs. 27%; p < 0.001), fewer PICU-free days, and higher 28-day mortality rates. In multivariate analysis incorporating markers of illness severity, including age, T3 was independently associated with fewer severe AKI-free days (β = -0.5; se = 0.2; p = 0.01), fewer PICU-free days, and higher adjusted odds of day 7 severe AKI and 28-day mortality. Patients were assigned to either the pSAKI-1 or pSAKI-2 subphenotype to assess for additional enrichment. T3 patients had uniformly worse outcomes among the less severe pSAKI-1 subphenotype but not among pSAKI-2 patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Worsening RAAS derangement, as evidenced by increasing renin concentrations, is associated with worse outcomes in children with SA-AKI. Serum renin may provide clinically useful prognostic enrichment in this population, both alone and in combination with the pSAKI subphenotypes.

articles.title: Residents' Ventilator Management Performance in an Online Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Case Scenario: Secondary Analysis of the Game-Based Education in Residency Study, 2015-2017.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate resident performance in an online pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) case scenario of mild/moderate severity, with the provision of individualized feedback.
DESIGN: A secondary analysis of the Game-based Education in Residency study.
SETTING: The dataset comprised residents in their first clinical rotation in any of 28 international PICUs, recruited between October 2015 and December 2017.
SUBJECTS: Residents who used the online mechanical ventilation (MV) simulator and completed PARDS tasks were included in the analysis.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The simulated MV parameters analyzed among 125 residents were positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), Fio2, tidal volume (Vt), peak inspiratory pressure (PIP), Pao2, and pH. Residents' MV selections in relation to recommended scoring goals were: median (interquartile range [IQR]) PEEP, below or in the lower range (8 cm H2O [IQR, 7-8 cm H2O]); median Fio2, above or in the higher range (60% [IQR, 51-60%]); and median Vt, within range (5.36 mL/kg [IQR, 4.98-5.73 mL/kg]). Residents had higher than recommended median Pao2 (93 mm Hg [IQR, 83-99 mm Hg]), pH (7.37 [IQR, 7.33-7.40]), and median PIP (30 cm H2O [IQR, 28-31 cm H2O]). Progress through the case scenario was associated with greater odds (odds ratio [OR] and 95% CI) of adherence to goals in PEEP, Fio2, and Vt: PEEP (OR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.65-4.34; p < 0.001); Fio2 (OR, 2.48; 95% CI, 1.29-4.76; p = 0.007); and Vt (OR, 2.66; 95% CI, 1.11-6.38; p = 0.028).
CONCLUSIONS: In an international PICU residents' educational dataset from 2015 to 2017, we found that progression through the simulated PARDS case was associated with greater odds of adherence to PEEP, Fio2, and Vt goals, which suggests that repeated practice and individualized feedback were of benefit. However, residents did not wean Fio2 or MV parameters when Pao2 and pH were above goal. These results may help educators design contemporary MV teaching.

articles.title: Clinical Factors Associated With Physical Restraint Use in Critically Ill Children: A Secondary Analysis of the PICU Up! Pilot Trial, 2019-2020.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify clinical factors associated with physical restraint use in critically ill children.
