DESIGN: This is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected observational daily data from the baseline (preintervention) phase of the PICU Up! multicenter stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial (NCT03860168). The analytic dataset represents a shared subset of the larger parent study population.
SETTING: Six PICUs in the United States, from May 2019 to March 2020.
PATIENTS: A total of 1153 patients younger than 18 years admitted to a PICU for 3 or more days.
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Children younger than 18 years old admitted for 3 or more consecutive PICU days were included. Daily data on sedation level, medication exposure, device use, and restraint status were collected, and multivariable generalized estimating equation models were used to evaluate associated factors. Physical restraints were used in 216 patients (18.7%) and 1,043 of 11,491 patient-days (9.07%), with a median duration of 3 days (interquartile range, 2-5). In multivariable analysis, the strongest predictor of restraint use was previous-day restraint (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 22.79; 95% CI, 16.72-31.07). Other significant factors included age 3-17 years vs. 0-2 years (aOR, 2.46-2.69), mechanical ventilation (aOR, 2.98; 95% CI, 1.39-6.38), benzodiazepine use (aOR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.05-2.10), and opioid use (aOR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.42-2.78). Light sedation (State Behavioral Scale [SBS] -1) was associated with restraint use compared with calm/alert status (SBS 0; aOR, 1.72; 95% CI, 1.24-2.37), while agitation (SBS > 0) showed no association (SBS 1 [aOR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.52-1.80] and SBS 2 [aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.47-2.54]). Invasive devices were associated with increased restraint use (p < 0.001). Notably, 51 patients (12.5%) of 407 patients receiving neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA) remained restrained, and 30 patients were restrained on the day of ICU discharge.
CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to previous reports linking agitation to restraint use, agitation (SBS > 0) was not associated with restraint use; only light sedation (SBS -1) was associated with increased odds of being restrained. Previous-day restraint use was the strongest predictor of continued restraint, highlighting persistence of previous-day practices with limited reassessment. The presence of restraints during periods of NMBA administration and at discharge days further suggests the need for improved reevaluation practices.

articles.title: Physiological Impact of Chest Wall Closure in Infants Post-Cardiac Surgery. Implications for Mechanical Ventilation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effect of delayed sternal closure post-cardiac surgery on respiratory system mechanics and hemodynamics.
DESIGN: Prospective single-center physiologic study.
SETTING: Cardiac PICU.
PATIENTS: Infants (< 1 yr old) with delayed sternal closure post-cardiopulmonary bypass for correction or palliation of a congenital heart disease.
INTERVENTIONS: Four ventilation conditions were studied: 1) baseline: positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) 5 cm H2O and low tidal volume (Vt; 6-7 mL/kg); 2) PEEP 5, high Vt (9-10 mL/kg); 3) PEEP 3, low Vt; and 4) PEEP 8, low Vt. Respiratory rate was adjusted to end-tidal carbon dioxide. Measurements were repeated after sternal closure.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Esophageal pressure (Pes), transpulmonary pressure (PL), normalized respiratory system elastance (Ers) in cm H2O/(mL/kg), and hemodynamics, including transmural pressures, were obtained before and after sternal closure. The open-sternum model used assumes that the chest wall maintains a vertical pleural pressure gradient, with the most nondependent lung exposed to atmospheric pressure. A nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O was used as a marker of overdistention, and end-expiratory PL 0-2 cm H2O was considered to prevent collapse. Ten patients were included: median (interquartile range) age 32 days (18-50 d) and weight 3.1 kg (3.0-3.5 kg). Chest closure increased Pes in all conditions and Ers in most conditions, except for PEEP 8 low Vt. Chest closure reduced expiratory PL in all conditions, at baseline from -0.5 cm H2O (-1.2 to -0.1 cm H2O) to -2.5 cm H2O (-3.1 to -1.8 cm H2O). Sternal closure impacted nondependent inspiratory PL differently depending on the ventilator settings. High Vt was the condition more frequently associated with high nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O. Blood pressure was maintained with fluids or vasopressors. Central venous pressure increased after closure, but the transmural filling pressure remained unchanged.
CONCLUSIONS: Infants with delayed sternal closure exhibited elevated Pes and Ers after chest wall closure. Under the model assumptions, during the open-chest phase, high Vt was more frequently associated with high nondependent PL, suggesting overdistention. Sternal closure made expiratory PL more negative. These findings suggest that individualized PEEP and Vt adjustments guided by Pes could be considered to help preserve expiratory PL and minimize the risk of overdistension before and after chest closure.

articles.title: Imaging in young ischemic stroke: a pictorial review.
articles.abstract: Young ischemic stroke encompasses a group of cerebrovascular disorders occurring in patients younger than 45 years, with pediatric stroke generally defined as stroke occurring between 28 days and 18 years of age. The incidence of stroke in the pediatric and young adult population is increasing and is emerging as a major public health issue. Diagnosis of young stroke is often challenging because of non-specific clinical presentations, etiologies that differ from those in older adults, and the wide range of stroke mimics. Imaging plays a critical role in the prompt and accurate diagnosis of young stroke by characterizing stroke subtypes, identifying underlying causes, assessing vascular abnormalities, and guiding management decisions. This pictorial review highlights the current imaging workup for diagnosing young stroke describing the advantages and limitations of various imaging modalities. We present a pictorial review of stroke in the young based on their imaging features, differentiating them from common stroke mimics. Using a multimodality case-based approach, we illustrate the characteristic imaging findings and classic signs of a broad spectrum of young ischemic stroke etiologies. They range from common causes like cardioembolism and dissection to less common infectious, metabolic and genetic causes like Borrelia vasculitis, Fabry disease and Adenosine deaminase 2 deficiency (DADA2). This review aims to equip radiologists and trainees with a structured and practical approach to the diagnosis and management of young stroke through classic imaging patterns and illustrative cases, ultimately facilitating improved patient outcome.

articles.title: Taiwanese Dermatological Association consensus for the management of atopic dermatitis: A 2024 update.
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by eczematous lesions and intense itching. AD commonly arises in children, in some of whom the condition may persist into adulthood; and a significant proportion of patients experience adult-onset disease as well. Although the prevalence of AD in Taiwan has risen over the past decades, recent therapeutic advances have contributed greatly to disease management. The Taiwanese Dermatological Association (TDA) has therefore developed an evidence-based consensus for the management of AD in Taiwan, and established a consensus committee to provide regular updates. This paper presents the 2024 update, for which a literature search was conducted to include relevant papers published between January 2020- March 2023. Supplementary searches targeted to approvals of new AD medications were subsequently conducted, and information was updated to August 2026. The consensus committee included 17 dermatology experts, and a modified Delphi method was used to evaluate the recommendations, with an approval threshold of ≥ 75%. A total of 21 new recommendations were added, 4 recommendations were revised, and the treatment algorithm was updated. Special considerations for pregnant, lactating, pediatric, and geriatric patients, as well as patients with active infections or undergoing vaccination, were included. This update incorporates the latest evidence and approved therapies, and may help to enhance treatment outcomes for AD patients in Taiwan.

articles.title: Natural History of Prenatally Identified Children With 48,XXYY Syndrome in Infancy and Early Childhood.
articles.abstract: 48,XXYY syndrome is a rare sex chromosome aneuploidy (SCA) associated with a variable profile of neurodevelopmental and medical. The limited information available in the literature is almost exclusively limited to postnatally diagnosed cases. This study aims to describe the early medical and developmental features of prenatally identified 48,XXYY infants, The eXtraordinarY Babies Study prospectively follows children prenatally identified to be at high risk for SCA with annual medical and neurodevelopmental evaluations. Data presented herein include the prevalence of medical conditions, developmental milestones, developmental and adaptive functioning assessment scores, and therapy utilization in 15 participants confirmed to have 48,XXYY. Comparisons were made with 47,XYY and 47,XXY males also enrolled in the eXtraordinarY Babies Study, the general population and a 2008 cohort of individuals postnatally identified 48,XXYY. Infants and young chlidren with 48,XXYY exhibited a range of early medical features, including elevated rates of feeding and GI disorders (breastfeeding difficulties, gastroesophageal reflux, and eosinophilic esophagitis), allergic disorders (food allergies and environmental allergies), and hypotonia. Developmental and adaptive functioning scores identified variable delays in motor, communication, and social domains, with nearly all infants receiving speech therapy, physical and/or occupational therapy due to delays or proactive developmental care. Medical and developmental findings were more prevalent in 48,XXYY compared to the 47,XYY and 47,XXY cohorts, although considerable individual variability and overlap in developmental functioning were observed across groups. Compared to the 2008 postnatally identified 48,XXYY cohort, infants identified prenatally received earlier intervention services, and developmental outcomes in the first years of life were similar between the two groups. Prenatal identification of 48,XXYY provides opportunity for early developmental monitoring, anticipatory guidance, and proactive referrals for medical evaluations and intervention. These findings provide valuable insights for genetic counselors and healthcare providers, emphasizing the spectrum of medical and developmental findings and the importance of early and proactive care to support individual outcomes. Prospective study of this prenatally identified cohort will provide important data about the natural history and phenotypic variability in XXYY, as well as identification of predictors of health and developmental outcomes. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03396562.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Family Maltreatment After Military Parental Injury in a Matched Retrospective Cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pediatric nurse practitioners may provide care for military families experiencing parental health conditions associated with injury. Parental injury or illness may contribute to stress, leading to increased risks of child maltreatment or family violence.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 6,253 spouses and 13,298 children of 9,157 injured service members who returned to duty. Records were followed for two years for child maltreatment, family violence, and well-child care. Chi-square, Wilcoxon rank sum tests, and logistic regression compared and calculated odds of outcomes.
RESULTS: Families with parents who experienced co-occurring mental health and physical injury were at significantly increased risk of child maltreatment, family violence, and decreased well-child care. Having a non-injured parent with a mental health diagnosis was associated with significantly higher odds of maltreatment.
CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric nurse practitioners should be aware of risk factors for maltreatment during periods of parental injury and provide avenues for early identification.

articles.title: Bolus Volume and Mortality in Extremely Low Gestational Age Infants with Shock.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between clinical outcomes and the volume of fluid boluses administered during the first 24 hours of a shock episode in extremely low gestational age newborns (ELGANs) requiring vasoactive support.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included ELGANs (≤28 weeks) at a single Level IV NICU between 2013 and 2021 who received vasoactive medications for shock within the first seven days of life. The primary predictor was total fluid volume (cc/kg) administered in the first 24 hours of shock. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for gestational age, birth weight, 5-minute Apgar score, systemic corticosteroid use, and highest vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS).
RESULTS: Of 97 infants, 26 (27%) died within 14 days of the shock episode. Non-survivors received a higher median bolus volume compared to survivors (40 cc/kg vs. 20 cc/kg, p<0.001). Greater bolus volume was independently associated with increased odds of 14-day mortality (aOR 1.026, 95% CI 1.004-1.048, p=0.019). Each additional 10 cc/kg was associated with an approximately 29% increase in mortality odds. No significant associations were found between bolus volume and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or bronchopulmonary dysplasia after adjustment.
CONCLUSION: Greater cumulative fluid bolus volume was independently associated with higher 14-day mortality in ELGANs with shock requiring vasoactive support. Although residual confounding illness severity cannot be excluded, these findings support cautious, individualized use of volume expansion and highlight the need for prospective studies of hemodynamically targeted resuscitation in this population.

articles.title: Departure From Planned 39-Week Delivery for Fetal Congenital Heart Disease: Indications for Earlier Birth.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Delivery >39 weeks' gestation is recommended for fetuses with congenital heart disease (FCHD). However, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), maternal diabetes and fetal growth restriction (FGR) are more common in these pregnancies and often necessitate early delivery. We evaluated indications for delivery at <39 weeks and examined maternal covariates, cardiac diagnoses and placental pathology.
STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective observational study included maternal-fetal dyads with prenatally diagnosed, structurally isolated, genetically unremarkable FCHD delivered at a single center. Gestational age and delivery indication were obtained from medical record. Placental pathology was assessed using Amsterdam criteria. Regression models evaluated associations with gestational age and neonatal mortality.
RESULTS: 46.3% (99/214) delivered <39 weeks; 65.6% (65/99) were due to maternal or fetal compromise, and 34.3% (33/99) to obstetric indications. HDP (20.1%) was strongly associated with <39-week delivery (32.3% vs 9.6%, p<0.001) and the greatest reduction in gestational age (-2.31 weeks, p<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified preeclampsia, type 2 diabetes, lower birthweight Z-score, and race as independent predictors of earlier delivery (p<0.05). Neonatal mortality was higher with maternal/fetal indications (15.7%) versus obstetric (5.4%) or elective FCHD delivery (5.6%) (p=0.02).
CONCLUSION: Nearly half of FCHD infants delivered before 39 weeks, largely due to maternal and placental disease, underscoring the importance of placental health in this population.

articles.title: Healthcare Team Awareness, Knowledge, and Perceptions of Neonatal Delirium: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neonatal delirium is increasingly recognized as an important neuropsychiatric condition in critically ill infants, yet awareness and understanding among healthcare providers remain limited. Underdiagnosis may contribute to prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity, and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. This study assessed healthcare team members' awareness, perceptions, and knowledge of neonatal delirium across a large children's hospital and affiliated neonatal care locations.
STUDY DESIGN: A cross‑sectional electronic survey was distributed to multidisciplinary NICU team members within a quaternary academic children's health system and affiliated sites. The survey included demographic items, multiple‑choice questions, Likert‑scale statements, and open‑ended responses. Descriptive statistics summarized quantitative data, and content categorization was applied to open‑ended responses.
RESULTS: A total of 117 respondents completed the survey, representing nursing, advanced practice providers, physicians, respiratory therapists, rehabilitation therapists, and pharmacy. Nearly half of respondents had never heard the term neonatal delirium. Among those familiar with the condition, definitions most commonly referenced agitation, altered consciousness, and sleep-wake disturbance. Ninety percent of respondents agreed that newborn infants can experience delirium, while only 60% indicated that delirium can also occur in preterm infants. Sixty percent indicated that delirium is assessable in infants, and 73% reported previously caring for an infant with suspected delirium. Respondents identified multiple barriers to screening and management, including limited awareness, lack of content expertise, and concerns about medication safety.
CONCLUSIONS: Awareness and understanding of neonatal delirium vary considerably among NICU providers, with notable educational and structural barriers to consistent recognition and management. These findings support the need for foundational education, multidisciplinary training, and continued research to inform development of effective strategies for assessing and managing neonatal delirium in neonatal care settings.

articles.title: The Role of Droperidol in the Management of Acute Agitation: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute behavioral disturbance accounts for ~1.7 million emergency department visits in the USA annually, with 83% involving an underlying serious mental illness. A 2001 FDA black box warning regarding QT prolongation reduced use of droperidol, a butyrophenone antipsychotic, but recent data challenge these concerns.
METHODS: We reviewed randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and observational studies from 2000 to 2025 assessing droperidol's efficacy and safety.
RESULTS: Droperidol provides rapid, effective sedation, with onset within 3 to 10 minutes and median time to adequate sedation of 14 to 25 minutes. Sixty-four percent of patients achieved adequate sedation at 15 minutes with droperidol versus 25% to 35% with ziprasidone and 29% with lorazepam. QT prolongation occurred in 1.3% of 1009 patients, mostly those with pre-existing risk factors. Respiratory depression was less common with droperidol (12%) than with ziprasidone (36% to 39%) or lorazepam (48%). Droperidol-midazolam combinations achieved faster sedation and reduced need for rescue medications (41% vs. 62%). Droperidol-treated patients had shorter hospital stays. Large studies found negligible rates of torsades de pointes or extracardiac arrhythmias. Elderly and pediatric patients responded favorably to low-dose droperidol. The American College of Emergency Physicians now recommends droperidol as first-line treatment for severe agitation. Combined with benzodiazepines, droperidol shows synergistic effects and allows lower doses of both with fewer adverse effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Recent evidence contradicts earlier FDA concerns, supporting droperidol as a safe, effective treatment for acute agitation. Its rapid onset, efficacy, safety profile, and operational benefits, including shorter ED stay, support its return to routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Extravascular Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillators in Children: Real World Evidence.
articles.abstract: The extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (EV-ICD) is a novel substernal ICD with limited reports in children and adolescents. Single-centre review of EV-ICDs in children <18-years. Clinical, peri-procedural, and electrocardiographic data reviewed, including device performance in routine exercise stress testing. Median follow-up 10.9 (IQR 7.5 - 12.5) months. Between April 2025-April 2026, 15 EV-ICDs were successfully implanted by a single cardiothoracic surgeon: median age 13.8-years, IQR 10.2-16.4; 11 (73%) male; weight 52 kg, IQR 38.2-64.1; BSA 1.6 m2, IQR 1.2-1.8. Smallest child was 4-years, 17.3 kg (BSA 0.7 m2). Indications were primary (n = 10) and secondary (n = 5) prevention. Underlying diagnoses included cardiomyopathy (n = 9), channelopathy (n = 3). One child had a previous sternotomy and another severe chest-wall deformity. Median anaesthetic time was 148 min (IQR 130-161), surgical time 68 min (59-88), fluoroscopy time 2.6 min (2.2-3.8). Median 3 (IQR 2-4) day hospitalisation. Two children experienced early complications. In one child, defibrillator threshold testing terminated ventricular fibrillation (VF) into ventricular tachycardia (VT) requiring CPR and a decision to use external cardioversion. The child fully recovered. One adolescent experienced profound bradycardia and syncope early post anaesthesia. R-wave amplitude at implant (5mV, IQR 4.2 - 6.7), discharge (5, IQR 2.8 - 8.1) and latest follow-up (5.8, IQR 3.2 - 13.7) was stable. Device sensing during routine exercise stress testing has been appropriate. There has been one successful appropriate high voltage therapy and no inappropriate high voltage therapy. This is the largest single-centre series internationally, demonstrating reliable paediatric EV-ICD implantation and short-term device performance. Ongoing paediatric surveillance is necessary.

articles.title: From Competence to Expertise in Congenital Cardiology: The LENS Model for Learning to See Problems Differently.
articles.abstract: Competency-based medical education has improved how paediatric and congenital cardiology defines readiness for independent practice. Competencies and entrustable professional activities describe what trainees should be able to do, and the degree of supervision they require. Competence is an essential threshold rather than the endpoint of professional development. The mechanisms through which a competent congenital cardiologist subsequently develops expertise remain incompletely understood. Research in medical education and cognitive psychology suggests that experts do not simply accumulate more knowledge or more clinical experience. Expertise involves changes in knowledge organisation, clinical problem representation, information selection, recognition of discordance, management of uncertainty, decision-making and adaptation when familiar solutions are insufficient. These concepts are particularly relevant to congenital cardiology, where clinicians integrate complex anatomy, physiology, imaging, haemodynamics, previous interventions and longitudinal trajectories while frequently making decisions despite incomplete evidence. We propose that the expert congenital cardiologist may be distinguished not simply by knowing more answers, but by seeing problems differently. We introduce the LENS model as a conceptual framework for this process: Link information into a coherent clinical representation; Extract the discriminating signal from noise; Notice discordance, uncertainty and possible failure of the initial pattern; and Shift reasoning strategy, seek distributed expertise or learn when the existing model is insufficient. The framework integrates literature on medical expertise, deliberate practice, adaptive expertise, uncertainty and congenital cardiac decision-making. It offers a vocabulary for teaching, faculty development and future empirical study while deliberately preserving the distinction between career stage, reputation and demonstrated expertise.

articles.title: Patients with Congenital Heart Disease have Inferior Intent-to-Treat Outcomes When Listed for Pediatric Heart Transplantation.
articles.abstract: While the impact of patient characteristics on waitlist and post-transplant mortality in pediatric heart transplantation has been widely studied, these metrics are limited in their ability to provide a complete picture for patients and their families. In contrast, less prevalent in the literature is an intent-to-treat analysis approach, which provides a single data point that encompasses both of these measures. This retrospective study examines pediatric patients listed for heart transplantation in the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) database between 2016 and 2025, evaluating the impact of transplant indication on intent-to-treat outcomes following the implementation of the 2016 allocation policy, which prioritizes children with congenital heart disease (CHD) on inotropic support. Kaplan-Meier analysis by transplant indication was performed across all pediatric patients listed during the study period, followed by Cox regression analyses using clinical and demographic covariates. In this initial analysis, CHD patients had poorer intent-to-treat outcomes. Risk and protective factors in this particularly high-risk population were then identified using univariable Cox regression. Significant factors (p < 0.05) were entered into a multivariable Cox regression, which was used to generate a predictive score for one-year intent-to-treat mortality (c-statistic = 0.74). Risk factors significant in the multivariable analysis were age 0-1 years, geographic region, public (rather than private) insurance, need for life support and/or hemodialysis, and low serum albumin level. Following external validation and study of transplant timing on outcomes, these findings may serve as an additional tool to identify and prioritize high-risk patients and target modifiable risk factors.

articles.title: Outcome After Late Pulmonary Valve Replacement in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.abstract: The optimal timing of pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in adults with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and severe pulmonary regurgitation remains controversial. Current recommendations rely largely on right ventricular volumetric thresholds derived from cohorts undergoing intervention during adolescence or early adulthood, although their prognostic value remains debated. To identify predictors of postoperative morbidity and mortality after PVR in patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF, with a specific focus on invasive preoperative hemodynamic parameters. We conducted a retrospective single-center study including patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF who underwent surgical PVR between 2009 and 2018. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint including supraventricular arrhythmia, cardiovascular rehospitalization, or all-cause death during follow-up. Clinical, imaging, and hemodynamic variables were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Forty-eight patients (mean age at PVR 41 ± 9.8 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 52 months. The primary outcome occurred in 23 patients (48%). Preoperative signs of advanced disease, including right heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction, and a history of syncope or ventricular tachycardia, were associated with adverse outcomes. Although right ventricular end-diastolic volumes were markedly increased in both groups, they were not associated with the primary outcome. Conversely, right ventricular end-systolic volume and, particularly, right ventricular end-diastolic pressure (RVEDP) showed stronger prognostic value. In multivariable analysis, RVEDP remained the only independent predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.01-3.40; p = 0.04). In adults aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF undergoing PVR, elevated RVEDP is a key predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality, whereas right ventricular end diastolic volumes on MRI are not. Invasive hemodynamic assessment may help refine the timing of PVR in this "senior" population.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Short-Term Thromboprophylaxis with Direct Oral Anticoagulants in Children After Surgical Bioprosthetic Pulmonary Valve Replacement: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract: The impact of short-term thromboprophylaxis on short and mid-term outcomes in children undergoing surgical pulmonary valve placement (SPVR) is not well defined. Furthermore, the use of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) in this population is not well studied. In this single-center, retrospective study, aspirin (ASA) monotherapy was compared to short-term (3 months) ASA + DOAC in children ≤ 18 years of age undergoing SPVR. We aimed to evaluate pulmonary valve (PV) mean gradient, PV peak gradient, and PV dysfunction (defined as moderate or greater regurgitation or stenosis) on echocardiogram at three time points: post-operative discharge (T1), one-year follow-up (T2), and most recent follow-up (T3). Sixty-six patients were included, of whom 32 received ASA monotherapy and 34 received ASA + DOAC for 90 days, with a total median follow-up time of 851 days. Baseline demographics were similar between the groups. There was no difference between groups regarding PV mean and peak gradient, or PV dysfunction at T1, T2, or T3. There were 16 bleeding events with no difference between the ASA and ASA + DOAC groups (6 (19%) vs. 10 (29%); p = 0.31, respectively). There were no differences regarding clinically relevant non-major bleeding, readmission within 30-days for bleeding, or hospital length of stay. In children undergoing SPVR, short-term thromboprophylaxis with ASA + DOAC had a similar safety profile to ASA monotherapy. DOAC use did not show significant benefit in PV function in the short-term. The benefits of DOAC thromboprophylaxis in SPVR should be evaluated with long-term, prospective studies.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatrics.
articles.journal: Curr Probl Pediatr Adolesc Health Care
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is already part of pediatric practice, particularly for triage, early detection, documentation, and point-of-care decision support. Some currently available tools perform at an expert level, including bone age estimation and fracture detection. Ambient documentation is easing a persistent burden, and language models effectively draft notes and messages. However, the evidence for the technology in pediatrics lags behind adult medicine. Of the 876 AI and machine learning (ML) enabled devices currently authorized by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), only 149 carry labeling for patients younger than 18 years, and only 19% of those report validation in children. This review article examines where AI already exists in, or is approaching, everyday pediatric use. In each domain, the discussion pairs the strength of the technology with its present limitations. Notably, strong test set statistics do not always translate into better outcomes, and few pediatric tools have been validated externally or prospectively. The reasons for that gap are examined in depth: pediatric datasets are smaller and less representative, which leaves them more prone to bias, and a child's consent binds their data for longer than an adult's. In general, the argument is neither for swift adoption nor for resistance. Instead, it is for holding the technology to a high standard, which means keeping a human in the loop and training clinicians to be exacting judges of the currently available tools.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Bipolar Disorder.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Pediatric (bipolar disorder) BD carries substantial morbidity, including prolonged symptom burden, high rates of suicide attempts and substance use, and psychosocial impairment. Accurate diagnosis requires careful longitudinal assessment, as presentations in youth often differ from adults, with more rapid cycling, mixed features, and irritability over classic euphoric mania. Early diagnosis and treatment are critical to reduce potential impairment and to support early recovery of youth with BD. The purpose of this article is to discuss the use of antipsychotics in the treatment of pediatric BD.

articles.title: Clozapine in Children and Adolescents: Indications, Efficacy, and Safety.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic but it remains underutilized. This review synthesizes evidence for clozapine use in children and adolescents, including additional indications such as suicidality, aggression, autism, and catatonia. Children have differences in pharmacokinetics, dosing, and side effect profiles. Although side effects can include agranulocytosis, myocarditis, and metabolic effects, regular laboratory and vital sign monitoring and adjunctive treatments can mitigate these risks. Persistent barriers often delay initiation, but increased education and systems-level changes can reduce barriers to clozapine use. Recent regulatory changes and emerging evidence support earlier and more widespread use of clozapine in appropriately selected pediatric populations.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Use in Adolescents with Substance Use and Substance Use Disorders.
articles.journal: Child Adolesc Psychiatr Clin N Am
articles.abstract: Antipsychotic medications are frequently prescribed off label in adolescents, particularly to manage agitation, behavioral dysregulation, and sleep disturbances, often in the context of substance use. However, their use is not consistently supported by a strong evidence base and carries meaningful risks, including metabolic, neurologic, and long-term health consequences. This article examines the clinical complexity of adolescents with substance use and co-occurring psychiatric symptoms, highlighting the risk of diagnostic ambiguity during acute intoxication or withdrawal. We provide a practical, developmentally informed framework to guide clinicians in the thoughtful, time-limited, and indication-specific use of antipsychotics in this population.

articles.title: A quality improvement initiative to increase kangaroo mother care duration in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit in Northern India.
articles.abstract: Kangaroo mother care (KMC) reduces mortality and morbidity in preterm and low-birth-weight infants, but daily duration in Indian neonatal units often falls short of the World Health Organization minimum of 8 hours. In our Level III neonatal unit, a baseline audit found a mean KMC duration of 4 hours/day, and infants on non-invasive respiratory support rarely received KMC. Using the Point-of-Care Quality Improvement framework, three Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles over 12 weeks (December 2024-February 2025) addressed staff training for KMC during continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) or high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), family engagement and workflow, and behavioural reinforcement. A 12-week sustenance phase followed. Eligible infants weighed <2000 g, were haemodynamically stable, and were not on invasive ventilation or phototherapy. KMC hours were taken from shift-wise nursing records. The outcome was mean daily KMC duration per infant, analysed on a run chart. All 20 eligible infants received KMC, 12 (60%) while on CPAP or HFNC. Median per-infant KMC duration was 9.75 hours/day (interquartile range 8.8-10.6), compared with 4 hours/day at baseline; 17 infants (85%) averaged at least 8 hours/day. Duration was lower among infants who started KMC during the second and third cycles and returned to the median during the sustenance phase. No hypothermia or device dislodgement occurred; one infant had an apnoeic episode. A people-centred quality improvement initiative using existing unit resources was associated with longer daily KMC, including in infants on non-invasive respiratory support, and the gain was maintained over 12 weeks. The 12-hour target could not be reached.

articles.title: Neurological manifestations in pediatric COVID-19: a comparative single-center study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical characteristics, investigations, management, and outcomes of hospitalized children with SARS-CoV-2 infection with and without neurological involvement, and to determine whether neurological disease reflects systemic severity or a distinct clinical pattern.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of children aged 1 month-16 years with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a tertiary pediatric center between June 2022 and June 2023. Patients were divided into those with neurological manifestations (ND group, n = 24) and those without neurological involvement (non-ND group, n = 23). Demographic features, clinical presentation, laboratory and neuroimaging findings, treatment, and outcomes were compared.
RESULTS: Children with neurological involvement were significantly older (median 5.75 vs. 3.00 years, p = 0.022) and less likely to present with fever or systemic inflammatory features. They demonstrated lower inflammatory markers and significantly less cardiac involvement, including dilated cardiomyopathy. Common neurological presentations included encephalopathy (50%), headache (45.8%), and seizures (20.8%). 37% met MIS-C criteria. Neuroimaging revealed lacunar infarctions, demyelinating white matter lesions, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, and cauda equina nerve root enhancement. Despite similar mortality rates, children with neurological involvement had a significantly higher rate of incomplete recovery, with more than a quarter experiencing persistent neurological sequelae (29.2% vs. 4.3%, p = 0.048).
CONCLUSION: Neurological manifestations of pediatric COVID-19 represent a clinically distinct pattern characterized by limited systemic inflammation but an increased risk of persistent neurological sequelae. Early neurological evaluation, appropriate neuroimaging, and structured long-term follow-up are warranted even in the absence of severe systemic illness.

articles.title: Exploring outcomes and insights from joint agency response investigations for children with learning disabilities who die unexpectedly: an observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In England, sudden unexpected child deaths are investigated through a joint agency response (JAR). There is wide variation in practice concerning JAR, particularly for children with underlying health conditions, many of whom have learning disability (LD); potentially limiting identification of causes and contributory factors for deaths.
METHODS: All child deaths with LD (including those who died suddenly and unexpectedly), aged 4–17 years, dying between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022 were identified retrospectively by the National Child Mortality Database (NCMD). Data were extracted from NCMD records and information on life-limiting conditions (LLCs) obtained from Hospital Episode Statistics. Unexpected deaths investigated through a JAR were compared with those without for demographics, underlying conditions, causes of death and process of investigations.
RESULTS: There were 738 deaths of children with LD of which 309 (41.8%) were unexpected; 257/309 (83%) had LLCs; 215/309 (69.5%) were subject to JAR. Chromosomal, genetic and congenital anomalies were the most common cause of death accounting for 95/215 (44.2%) JAR cases and 49/94 (52.1%) non-JAR cases. Compliance with JAR processes overall was low. Postmortem examination (PM) took place for 166/215 (77.2%) JAR cases and 21/94 (22.3%) non-JAR cases (p<0.001). A new condition was identified as the cause of death rather than a pre-existing condition as cause of death in 112/215 (52.3%) JAR cases compared with 13/94 (13.8%) non-JAR cases (p<0.001). After adjustment for JAR components, only PM remained associated, with an increase in chance of identifying a new cause of death (72.1% (95% CI 61.6% to 72.7%)). JAR home visits provided little new information relevant to the cause of death.
CONCLUSIONS: Clearer guidance is required on when and how to undertake JAR investigations following sudden deaths of children with LD. Current guidance is largely based on deaths of previously healthy children.

articles.title: Evolution of the clinical profile and cardiac outcomes of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across three COVID-19 waves in Central Kerala: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical profile, laboratory findings, cardiac manifestations, treatment patterns and outcomes of children diagnosed with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across the Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves of the COVID-19 pandemic.
DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study.
SETTING: A tertiary care teaching hospital in Central Kerala, India.
PARTICIPANTS: 95 children fulfilling established diagnostic criteria for MIS-C admitted between November 2020 and December 2022 were included. Patients were categorised into three groups according to the predominant SARS-CoV-2 variant wave: Alpha (wave 1), Delta (wave 2) and Omicron (wave 3).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, echocardiographic findings, treatment modalities and markers of disease severity, including duration of hospitalisation, intensive care stay, oxygen requirement, inotropic support and ventilator support.
RESULTS: Gastrointestinal symptoms remained the predominant presentation across all three waves, whereas respiratory symptoms increased during the later waves. Mucocutaneous manifestations varied significantly across waves (p=0.02). The duration of hospital stay (p=0.004), duration of fever (p=0.009) and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (p=0.003) decreased significantly over successive waves, suggesting reduced overall disease severity. Pericardial effusion also decreased significantly (p=0.002), while the prevalence of left ventricular dysfunction showed a declining trend. In contrast, coronary artery dilatation increased significantly during the Omicron wave (p<0.0001). Oxygen requirement declined significantly in the third wave (p=0.02), whereas intensive care stay, inotropic support and ventilator support did not differ significantly between waves.
CONCLUSIONS: The clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across successive COVID-19 waves, with evidence of decreasing systemic disease severity but persistent changes in cardiac involvement. The marked increase in coronary artery dilatation during the Omicron wave highlights the importance of continued echocardiographic surveillance and long-term cardiac follow-up, even during clinically milder phases of the pandemic.

articles.title: Role of hyponatraemia in risk stratification of well-appearing febrile infants aged 28-90 days: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Distinguishing invasive and serious bacterial infections (IBI and SBI) remains challenging. We aimed to evaluate the role of hyponatraemia in identifying IBI and SBI and to assess its contribution to the Step-by-Step Approach in well-appearing febrile infants aged 28–90 days.
METHODS: This single-centre, 10-year retrospective study included well-appearing febrile infants aged 28–90 days without an apparent source of infection. Clinical characteristics were compared between infants with and without hyponatremia. In patients meeting the laboratory criteria of the Step-by-Step Approach, serum sodium was integrated into the final step and diagnostic performance was compared with the original algorithm.
RESULTS: Among 381 patients, 69 (18.1%) had hyponatremia. IBI was more frequent in the hyponatraemia group than in the normonatraemia group (11.6% vs 1.3%, p<0.001). Hyponatraemia was also associated with higher SBI rates, hospitalisation and longer length of stay (p<0.001). Of the 291 patients with procalcitonin measurements, 9 (3.1%) had IBI and 74 (25.4%) had SBI. Among 164 (56.3%) classified as low-risk, 1 (0.6%) had IBI and 18 (10.9%) had SBI. Integrating serum sodium into the algorithm identified 1 additional IBI and 6 additional SBI cases among low-risk infants and improved the negative predictive value for IBI (100% vs 99.4%). The sodium-integrated approach also showed a lower negative likelihood ratio (<0.01 vs 0.19) and lower post-test probability of IBI (<0.01% vs 0.6%); as this reflects a single reclassified IBI case, this estimate warrants cautious interpretation pending validation in larger cohorts. The SBI reclassification, based on a larger number of events, showed a more robust improvement in sensitivity (75.7% vs 83.8%).
CONCLUSION: Hyponatremia is associated with increased IBI and SBI rates in well-appearing febrile infants. Integrating serum sodium into the Step-by-Step Approach modestly improved risk stratification and may enhance identification of low-risk patients.

articles.title: Paediatric clinicians' knowledge and experiences of e-bike and e-scooter harms in children and young people: a UK national service evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: E-bike and e-scooter use is increasing, with growing concern about harms in children and young people (CYP). We assessed paediatric clinicians’ legislative knowledge, clinical experiences and prevention opportunities.
METHODS: This UK national service evaluation comprised a narrative literature review, clinician survey, structured local needs-assessment discussions and contextual mortality data from England. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively; free-text responses and discussion notes underwent descriptive thematic synthesis.
RESULTS: 484 clinicians contributed: 353 completed the survey, 217 participated in structured local discussions and 86 contributed to both components. Legislative knowledge was limited: 11% correctly identified the minimum age for rental e-bike use, 22% for private e-bike use and 25% knew that a driving licence is required for rental e-scooter use. Of 303 clinicians, 142 (47%) reported encountering e-bike or e-scooter-related injuries or discussing micromobility use with CYP in the past year. Reported harms included head injury, fractures and polytrauma, with dual riding, lack of helmet use and motor-vehicle collisions commonly reported. National mortality data identified 17 child deaths in England between April 2019 and December 2025 related to e-bike or e-scooter use; numbers were small, and 2025 data were incomplete, but the distribution over time raises concern that deaths may be increasing. Clinicians reported inconsistent advice provision, barriers to discussion and support for coordinated prevention strategies.
CONCLUSIONS: E-bike and e-scooter-related harm is an emerging paediatric public health concern. Improved education about additional risks, integration into routine risk assessment, improved injury surveillance and coordinated policy responses, including legislative review, are needed to reduce preventable harm.

articles.title: Opioid prescribing practices at discharge across common pediatric urologic surgery procedures.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In 2020, the American Pediatric Surgical Association released evidence-based guidelines for opioid prescribing after common urologic surgeries. Procedures were grouped into recommended opioid free recovery (OFR) and opioid free recovery possible (OFRP). The purpose of this study was to evaluate opioids prescribed at discharge across common procedures in pediatric urologic surgery.
METHODS: The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-Pediatric (2023) was queried for patients ≤18 years undergoing elective procedures, including one OFR procedure (hypospadias repair) and two OFRP procedures (orchiopexy and pyeloplasty). The primary outcome was the proportion of opioid prescriptions at discharge for OFR and OFRP procedures. Secondary outcomes were demographic and clinical variables associated with an opioid prescription at discharge.
RESULTS: A total of 4149 patients underwent hypospadias repair (OFR), while 2916 patients underwent OFRP procedures (1220 orchiopexy; 1696 pyeloplasty). For hypospadias repair, 28.2% were given an opioid prescription at discharge with associations of opioid prescriptions with age, race, ethnicity, postoperative length of stay and operation time. Within ORFP procedures, 21.1% of patients were prescribed an opioid at discharge. Factors associated with opioid prescriptions after orchiopexy were age, ethnicity, history of asthma and operative time, while after pyeloplasty, associated factors were age, ethnicity, procedure approach, and postoperative length of stay.
CONCLUSIONS: Despite published guidelines, hypospadias repair, orchiopexy and pyeloplasty procedures had >20% of patients prescribed opioid at discharge. Further research and quality improvement efforts on postoperative pain management protocols to improve opioid stewardship in pediatric urology are warranted.

articles.title: State of The Art of The da Silva's Cone Operation for Treatment of Ebstein's Anomaly.
articles.abstract: Ebstein's anomaly (EA) is a complex congenital heart disease caused by embryological failure of the tricuspid valve (TV) leaflet delamination, leading to displacement of the leaflets and right ventricular myopathy. In 1958, Hunter and Lillehei began developing surgical techniques for the repair of EA. Their technique was followed by many others. However, those techniques presented significant limitations due to the wide range of anatomical variations in the disease. The Da Silva Cone repair (CR) for EA emerged as the most anatomical repair technique for all forms of the disease, yielding the best results for most patients. Since CR can be performed with low mortality and morbidity, is effective and durable, and rarely requires TV replacement, it has been widely adopted. It allowed that surgical intervention can be indicated before the development of significant right ventricular dilatation or dysfunction. CR can be applied to any age, but it carries more risk in the neonate with critical EA. Therefore, neonates with critical EA may benefit from a staged approach, performing the Starnes procedure in the neonatal period and the CR later. The 2025 American Association for Thoracic Surgery expert consensus on managing EA covered preoperative evaluation, surgical indications, and contraindications in neonates, children, and adults. Additionally, the expert consensus discussed the approach to cardiac arrhythmias associated with EA and alternative procedures for select cases, including TV replacement and a bidirectional cavopulmonary shunt, depending on patient characteristics. They also agreed that the CR repair of the TV is beneficial when surgery is indicated.

articles.title: Focal Digital Clubbing as an Initial Symptom of Adolescent-Onset Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Digital clubbing is typically linked to pulmonary or cardiovascular diseases. There have been no reported cases of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) where the initial complaint was solely foca digital clubbing and a chilblain-like rash on the ngers. A 13-year-old girl experienced digital clubbing for 3 months. Physical examination revealed focal digital clubbing of the thumb, index nger, and middle nger on her right hand, along with slight blotchy erythema assessed as a chilblain-like rash. Laboratory data showed hypocomplementemia and a high anti-double-stranded DNA antibody titer. She was also positive for antiphospholipid antibodies, had prolonged prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time, and elevated anti-prothrombin antibody levels. She was diagnosed with SLE complicated by hypoprothrombinemia associated with lupus anticoagulant. Prednisolone treat ment resolved the digital clubbing and laboratory abnormalities. Digital clubbing may be an initial symptom of SLE. Screening for autoimmune diseases should be considered when a patient presents with digital clubbing not associated with pulmonary or cardiovascular diseases or malignant tumors.   Cite this article as: Sato M, Nagamori T, Kurisawa MJ, Tsuda J, Ishibazawa E, Takahashi S. Focal digital clubbing as an initial symptom of adolescent-onset systemic lupus erythematosus: a case report. Eur J Rheumatol. 2025, 12(4), 0075, doi:10.5152/eurjrheum.2025.24075.

articles.title: Diagnostic yield of genetic testing in heart transplant recipients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: A single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiomyopathy genetic testing is recommended for patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) but is inconsistently applied once a patient has reached end-stage disease and undergone heart transplantation. Whether a transplant program can systematically test its existing NICM cohort and what completion rate is achievable when testing is operationalized in the clinic rather than offered ad hoc is not well characterized.
METHODS: We studied all 73 adults followed in the Southern Alberta Transplant Program after transplantation for NICM: dilated (DCM), non-dilated left ventricular (NDLVC), restrictive, or hypertrophic (HCM). Cardiomyopathy genetic testing was offered as a program-wide initiative and performed in adulthood using clinically validated multigene panels. Variants were classified by ACMG/AMP criteria; pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants interpreted as explanatory for the recipient's cardiomyopathy were counted as diagnostic. Single heterozygous P/LP variants in autosomal recessive genes were interpreted as carrier findings and not counted toward yield. Yields are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs); the childhood- versus adult-transplant comparison was tested with Fisher's exact test.
RESULTS: Of 71 eligible patients, 27 (38.0%) had a genetic-testing result before the 12-month operational window; of the 44 offered testing during the window, 37 completed it (84.1%), raising cohort testing coverage to 90.1% (64/71). A diagnostic pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant was identified in 28 of 64 tested patients (43.8%; 95% CI 32.3%-55.9%); a sensitivity analysis restricted to the 36 patients tested with the comprehensive Invitae 121-gene panel yielded an indistinguishable 38.9% (14/36; 95% CI 24.8%-55.1%), with no evidence that variation in panel breadth materially biased the overall estimate. Two additional patients carried a single heterozygous P/LP variant in an autosomal recessive gene (carrier findings, not counted). Yield was higher in patients transplanted in childhood (10/14, 71.4%) than in adulthood (18/50, 36.0%; Fisher's exact P = 0.031). TTN was the most frequent gene (7 P/LP), followed by LMNA, PKP2, and MYH7 (3 each).
CONCLUSIONS: A 12-month program-wide initiative raised cardiomyopathy genetic testing coverage in an existing NICM heart transplant cohort from 38% to 90% by embedding testing in routine transplant clinic visits. The diagnostic yield among tested patients (43.8%) was consistent with published estimates and similar when restricted to the most comprehensive panel, with markedly higher yield in patients transplanted in childhood. These findings provide a reproducible operational template for transplant programs seeking to close the implementation gap in cardiomyopathy genetic evaluation and to enable cascade testing of at-risk relatives.

articles.title: Cranial Injuries due to Misuse of Infant Carriers.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Infant carriers (car seats, bouncy chairs) can cause injuries when used for other than their intended purpose.
METHODS: We studied children aged 0-24 months with carrier related injuries reported to the Pennsylvania Trauma Outcome Study (PTOS) dataset (2001-2022 inclusive).
RESULTS: There were 562 injured children, averaging 23 injuries per year. Mean age was 3.3 months; 54.3% were male. Most (82.7%) fell from an elevated surface; 88.7% fell an estimated 2-5 feet. Head injuries (intracranial injury/hemorrhage and/or skull fracture) were present in 85.6%. Admission Glasgow Coma Scores were most commonly 15 (79.1%); 7 had GCS <12. Average Injury Severity Score was 9.3 (range 1-30). Average length of stay was 1.4 days; 30% spent >1 day in the intensive care unit. Two children underwent cranial operations. There were no deaths, and 82.9% were discharged home.
CONCLUSION: Falls in, or from, infant carriers are a significant public health concern. Education, advocacy, and changes in carrier design may help reduce the frequency of these injuries.

articles.title: Transfusion practices among children admitted to a South African PICU following cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood products may be required in patients undergoing cardiac surgery; however, there is a paucity of data on blood transfusion guidelines in the perioperative and postoperative cardiac surgery period.
OBJECTIVES: To describe the prevalence of blood product transfusion, factors associated with transfusion and outcomes in patients who received blood products following cardiac surgery.
METHODS: This was a prospective, single-centre observational study that consecutively recruited 126 children aged <18 years admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) following cardiac surgery between July 2017 and January 2018. Demographic, intraoperative and postoperative blood product transfusion data were extracted from patient records, entered into a standardised case record form and analysed using Statistica version 13 (StatSoft Inc, USA). Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.
RESULTS: Of the recruited children, 53% received blood products, with 30.9% receiving cryoprecipitate, 22.2% receiving packed red blood cells, 18.3% receiving albumin, 15.9% receiving fresh frozen plasma and 15.1% receiving platelet concentrates. Factors associated with the use of blood products included previous cardiac surgery, younger age, lower weight and prolonged coagulation parameters (p<0.05). Receiving blood products was associated with worse outcomes: a standardised mortality ratio of 3.1 v. 0 (p<0.0001), median (IQR) PICU length of stay of 5 (3 - 11) v. 2 (2 - 5) days (p<0.0001), and duration of mechanical ventilation of 47 (22 - 132) v. 20 (6 - 27) hours (p<0.0001).
CONCLUSION: There is a high prevalence of blood product use in children in the PICU following cardiac surgery, and this is associated with worse outcomes.
CONTRIBUTION OF THE STUDY: This is the first South African study to describe the use of all major blood product types, not only red blood cells, and their indications in children following paediatric cardiac surgery. It demonstrates a markedly different transfusion pattern from that reported in North American PICUs, with cryoprecipitate, rather than red blood cells, being the most frequently used product. Blood product use was common and was independently associated with worse outcomes, including longer PICU stays, prolonged ventilation and higher standardised mortality. These findings highlight the need for locally developed, evidence-based transfusion protocols to support blood product stewardship, particularly in resource-constrained settings that depend on voluntary blood donation.

articles.title: Patient- and family-reported satisfaction in child and adolescent psychiatric inpatient care: An exploratory descriptive survey.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To describe and compare patient- and family-reported satisfaction with child and adolescent psychiatric inpatient care in a Japanese inpatient unit.
METHODS: Patients aged 8-15 years discharged from a single Japanese inpatient unit and their families completed an anonymous web questionnaire with separate patient and family versions. Overall satisfaction was rated on a 10-point scale, and respondents who reported interaction rated the usefulness of five professional groups. Because responses were unlinked, 10 probable patient-family pairs identified from submission times were used in sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: Invitations were handed to 61 patients and their families at discharge; 52 family members (85.2%) and 26 patients (42.6%) responded. Family members reported higher satisfaction than patients (mean 8.14 [SD 1.83] vs. 6.27 [SD 2.15]; medians 8 vs. 7; mean difference 1.87, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-2.86), and the lower 95% CI limit was at least 0.73 in all sensitivity analyses addressing dependence between the groups. The maximum score was given by 25.5% of family members and 3.8% of patients. Among respondents who rated each professional group, a higher proportion of family members than patients rated child and adolescent psychiatrists (98.1% vs. 69.2%) and nurses (92.3% vs. 73.1%) as useful, whereas proportions for psychiatric social workers, clinical psychologists, and teachers were similar or higher among patients. These profession-specific comparisons were descriptive only.
CONCLUSION: Patients rated inpatient care less favorably than family members. Family reports should complement, not replace, patients' own evaluations, and future multicenter studies should use matched patient-family dyads.

articles.title: REACH: A multidimensional index for measuring community concordance in US children's hospitals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Equitable access to pediatric healthcare is essential for improving health outcomes and assessing health system accountability. Existing metrics for measuring hospital concordance with surrounding communities are adult-centric or sensitive to hospital catchment area definition.
OBJECTIVE: Through REACH (Representation and Equity in Area-based Child Hospitalizations) index, we aimed to develop a multidimensional, robust, and standardized concordance measure that combines four sociodemographic dimensions, ethnicity, payor, race, and sex, into a composite score that is comparable across hospitals.
METHODS: Using 695,046 inpatient and observation encounters from 48 U.S. children's hospitals in the Pediatric Health Information System (PHIS) for 2023 and 2023 American Community Survey (ACS) five-year estimate, we defined hospital catchment areas and calculated dimension-specific concordance indexes using weighted Chi-square divergence between observed hospitalizations and expected pediatric population. The four indexes were aggregated into a composite REACH score with 95% confidence intervals. Robustness of REACH was assessed using Spearman correlation between unrestricted and two conservative catchment definitions across 48 hospitals.
RESULTS: REACH scores ranged from 0.89 to 0.98. All hospitals demonstrated high (≥0.80) to very high (≥0.90) concordance, with 60% of hospitals scoring ≥0.95. REACH was stable across catchment definitions, with strong correlations (ρ ≥ 0.7); all hospitals stayed in the high-to-very high range. Overall, 87.5% of hospitals retained their concordance category, while six showed modest downward shifts (from very high to high) under the most conservative definition.
CONCLUSION: REACH offers an effective framework to measure community concordance in pediatric hospitals, with potential future applications for benchmarking, quality improvement, and policy development to advance equitable healthcare access.

articles.title: Caregiving networks and children with neurologic impairment: A multicenter social network analysis protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with neurologic impairment (NI) often require care from multiple paid and unpaid caregivers-a "caregiving network"-yet little is known about how caregiving networks influence child health. Understanding how networks influence health could support innovative intervention designs targeting groups of caregivers.
OBJECTIVES: This multicenter prospective cohort study will evaluate whether caregiving network characteristics are associated with serious health events and quality of life among children with NI.
METHODS: THRIvE (Teamwork and Healthy Relationships Improving Engagement in Caregiving) is a multicenter prospective cohort study enrolling children ages 2-16 years with NI and at least one hospitalization or emergency department (ED) visit in the prior 12 months, along with primary caregivers (PCGs) and secondary caregivers (SCGs), at five academic medical centers. Caregiving networks will be assessed at enrollment using egocentric social network analysis administered to PCGs and validated with SCG surveys. Exposures include network density, centralization, triadic closure, network size, and composition. Primary outcomes at 12 months are serious health events (death or hospitalization) and child quality of life. Secondary outcomes include clinical symptoms, missed school days, and ED visits. Associations will be examined using mixed-effects regression models accounting for site clustering, confounding, and multiple comparisons.
RESULTS: This study will provide novel prospective evidence about how caregiving network configurations are associated with health outcomes in children with NI.
CONCLUSIONS: Findings may identify modifiable social network features that can inform future family-centered, network-based interventions to improve child health and quality of life.

articles.title: Design Thinking in Advance Care Planning for Emerging Adults: Enhancing Control and Customization to Support Engagement.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study examined how emerging adults with serious illness engage with advance care planning (ACP) through a design-informed lens.Background:ACP enables individuals to communicate their preferences and goals for medical care if they are unable to make decisions for themselves. Although ACP is widely recognized as critical for individuals with serious illness, engagement remains low among emerging adults (ages 18-29), a distinct developmental subgroup within the adolescent and young adult population. Traditional ACP approaches emphasize documentation and legal requirements, which may limit engagement among individuals navigating identity development, autonomy, and future-oriented life transitions.Methods: A secondary analysis was conducted using data from 39 emerging adults with oncology or hematology diagnoses who reviewed the ACP communication guide, Voicing My CHOiCES (VMC). Structured interviews assessed participant perspectives on usability, preferences, and emotional responses. Data were explored using thematic content analysis.Results:Two central themes emerged: (1) affording choice and control and (2) designing for customization and usability. Participants valued opportunities for personalization, structured guidance, and revisable formats. Design elements that supported autonomy, reduced cognitive burden, and facilitated reflection were associated with more positive experiences of engagement, while overly rigid features constrained expression.Discussion: Across themes, ACP engagement with emerging adults was closely tied to how the VMC tool structured interaction. Design features that enabled choice, reduced complexity, and allowed for iterative engagement were associated with more positive experiences. This suggests that designing ACP as a flexible, user-centered, developmentally tailored process may better support meaningful participation.

articles.title: The Radiographic Lung Edema Score in Pediatric Acute Respiratory Failure: Associations With Systemic Inflammatory Biomarkers and Multiple Organ Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although chest radiographs (CXR) are among the most used imaging modalities in critically ill patients, their interpretation and clinical significance remain incompletely leveraged. The Radiographic Lung Edema (RALE) score is a prognostic bedside tool widely applied in adults to quantify lung edema on CXR. However, this score has been infrequently studied in children, and its potential to reflect broader aspects of critical illness pathophysiology beyond the lungs is unknown. We sought to determine the reproducibility of the RALE score, and whether higher RALE scores were associated with circulating inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers, multi-organ dysfunction, and worse clinical outcomes in pediatric acute respiratory failure (ARF).
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.
SETTING: Multicenter PICUs.
PATIENTS: Critically ill children (2 wk to 17 yr old) receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for ARF, enrolled in the CAF-PINT (Coagulation and Fibrinolysis in Pediatric Insulin Titration) study (2012-2016).
INTERVENTIONS: None.
MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A baseline RALE score was calculated for each patient from a single CXR obtained within 72 hours of IMV initiation. Among 212 patients, RALE scores demonstrated good inter-rater reliability (intra-class coefficient 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.87). After adjustment for ARF etiology and illness severity, higher RALE scores were associated with fewer 28-day ventilator-free days (sub-distribution hazard ratio per 1-sd increase, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.69-0.95). Structural equation modeling demonstrated that this association was mediated through both pulmonary dysfunction, measured by the oxygenation index (β -0.14; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.22 to -0.06), and extrapulmonary organ dysfunction, measured by the Pediatric Logistic Organ Dysfunction score (β -0.05; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.10 to -0.002). Similar associations were observed for 28-day PICU-free days. Finally, penalized regression selected soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1, intercellular adhesion molecule-1, and tumor necrosis factor receptor-1 as biomarkers associated with higher RALE scores.
CONCLUSIONS: We provide evidence that the RALE score is not solely a lung injury marker but also reflects broader systemic pathophysiology. These findings have important implications for the interpretation and clinical application of this bedside tool in pediatric ARF.

articles.title: The relationship of physical activity and exercise to the initiation and use of nicotine and cocaine.
articles.abstract: Each year, the USA federal government spends hundreds of billions of dollars addressing the ramifications of substance use; however, limited and ineffective treatment strategies exist to mitigate these challenges. Continued targeting of the adolescent population contributes to the growing number of substance-dependent individuals because of an enhanced susceptibility to substance use. Many studies have suggested that exercise may be a suitable adjunct or nonpharmacological therapy because of its rewarding potential and ability to reduce stress and other drug-related risk factors. This review aims to assess the clinical associations of physical activity and preclinical evidence of exercise as protection against the development of nicotine and cocaine use disorders. This will build on previous work by using a substance-use-cycle-specific lens, focusing on substance initiation and use, while clarifying and addressing concerns about the timing of exercise exposure relative to the substance-use experience and its impact on exercise intervention efficacy. Together, this work identifies clinical observations associated with lower instances of nicotine initiation and use, in addition to preclinical behavioral and molecular interventions associated with reductions in cocaine initiation and use, providing support for the protective effect of physical activity and exercise.

articles.title: A Gap on Judgment of Fertility and the Need for Contraception Between Physicians and Patients With Rheumatic Diseases: A Multicenter Questionnaire Survey.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Effective contraception is essential for women of reproductive age with rheumatic disease (RD), specifically those receiving teratogenic drugs, and physicians should recognize that these women may wish to conceive or control their fertility. This study aimed to evaluate the status of preconception care and contraception use, awareness, and counseling among women with RD in Japan.
METHODS: This cross-sectional questionnaire survey included Japanese women with RD (age: 18-45 years) and their attending physicians, conducted between September 2023 and May 2024 at 14 medical institutions. Patient and physician responses were linked and analyzed.
RESULTS: In total, 157 patients completed the survey. Of these, 35% of patients wished to conceive in the future and 38% were aware of their current need for contraception. The results revealed a gap between physicians' and patients' judgment of fertility and the need for contraception. Most patients used less effective contraceptive methods (condoms: 67.1%; withdrawal: 20.5%). Although patients were aware of the need for contraception, only 12% had received specific contraception instructions from their healthcare providers, whereas 39% had never received contraception counseling. Most of the patients decided on contraceptive methods themselves or together with their partners. One patient who tested positive for antiphospholipid antibodies used contraindicated estrogen-containing contraceptives.
CONCLUSION: Significant deficiencies exist in contraception counseling and awareness among women with RD. Proactive and system-building approaches are urgently required to improve preconception care and reproductive safety in this population.

articles.title: Emerging Drugs.
articles.abstract: Therapeutic development in Sjögren's disease has accelerated after decades of largely negative clinical trials. Improved patient selection, refined outcome measures, and targeted modulation of key immune pathways have produced positive late-stage studies and the prospect of disease-modifying treatment. This article examines emerging B-cell-directed therapies, neonatal Fc receptor inhibitors, costimulatory blockade, intracellular signaling inhibitors, immune-restorative approaches, repurposed therapies, and cellular treatments. It also considers lessons from contemporary trials, including phenotype-based enrollment, multidimensional endpoints, and organ-specific responses, and discusses how these advances may enable increasingly precise therapeutic selection.

articles.title: Systemic Lupus and Other Autoimmune Disorders During Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Rheumatologic conditions occur in reproductive aged women, requiring a multidisciplinary approach to care. Patients require coordinated care with obstetrics, maternal fetal medicine, and rheumatology. Many drugs used for the care of rheumatologic conditions are safe in pregnancy, but detailed review should occur, ideally preconception, so the patient can be on the safest regimen while maintaining disease control. Anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies particularly pose unique risks of neonatal lupus syndrome, including cardiac manifestations. Medical management is unique to each disease and includes ultrasounds and antenatal testing to optimize both maternal and fetal well-being and minimize perinatal risks.

articles.title: Demographic, clinical and echocardiographic profile of adult patients with congenital heart disease at a leading cardiovascular healthcare facility of Pakistan: A descriptive cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the demographic, clinical, and echocardiographic characteristics of adults with congenital heart disease (CHD).
METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional study was performed at the department of pediatric cardiology, National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NICVD), Karachi, Pakistan, from November 2022 to October 2023. Inclusion criteria were adult patients (≥18 years of age) diagnosed with CHDs (both already diagnosed and newly diagnosed).
RESULTS: Of 184 patients, 100 (54.3%) were male. Mean age and BMI were 25.66 ± 9.19 years and 17.75 ± 4.32 kg/m2. Seventeen (9.2%) adult CHD patients were newly diagnosed. Shortness of breath, cyanosis, palpitation, and chest pain, were reported in 158 (85.9%), 65 (35.3%), 52 (28.3%), and 51 (27.7%) patients. Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF), atrial septal defect (ASD), ventricular septal defect (VSD), and patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) were the most common CHD types, noted in 46 (25.0%), 35 (19.0%), 32 (17.4%), and 12 (6.5%) patients respectively. ASD was significantly more prevalent in females than in males (82.9% vs. 17.1%, p < .001), and it was significantly more frequent in 18-30 age group (p < .001). TOF was more common in 18-30 age group (p = .013). VSD was significantly more prevalent in males (p = .028).
CONCLUSIONS: TOF, ASD, VSD, and PDA were the most frequent types of adult CHDs. Notably, 9.2% of patients were newly diagnosed, suggesting potential underdiagnosis or late detection. With a substantial portion of the population experiencing CHD-related symptoms with some diagnosed only in adulthood, demand for dedicated centers equipped with expertise in managing adult CHD becomes evident.

articles.title: Documenting Psychosocial Needs at the End of Life: Implementation of an Interdisciplinary Huddle to Foster Communication in Pediatric Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: - Psychosocial support is a core component of pediatric oncology palliative care (PPC), yet structured approaches for documenting and communicating psychosocial information across interdisciplinary teams remain inconsistent in pediatric cancer.
OBJECTIVE: - To describe the content documented within a structured interdisciplinary psychosocial huddle note and summarize lessons learned from its implementation within a hospital-based pediatric palliative care program for children with cancer.
METHODS: - This single-site retrospective decedent study included patients at a large pediatric cancer center with at least one documented end-of-life psychosocial huddle note between October 2023 and October 2025. The first huddle note for each patient was reviewed for documentation across nine psychosocial domains. Demographic, clinical, temporal, and interdisciplinary participation data were collected. For patients with multiple notes, changes in documentation over time were assessed.
RESULTS: - Forty-six patients with malignancy met inclusion criteria. The most frequently documented domains were social/spiritual support (84.8%), family/caregiver support (82.6%), and anticipatory grief (76.1%). Emotional distress (45.7%) and goals of care/decision-making (43.5%) were documented in nearly half. Notes reflected broad interdisciplinary participation, particularly from social work, child life, and spiritual care. Documentation patterns varied across demographic and clinical subgroups. Among 14 patients with multiple notes, all demonstrated changes in at least one psychosocial domain over time.
CONCLUSIONS: - Structured psychosocial huddle notes facilitated interdisciplinary communication and documentation of supportive care needs and revealed variability in documentation of decision-making processes. Standardized longitudinal documentation may strengthen communication, continuity, and goal-concordant end-of-life care in PPC for children with cancer.

articles.title: Predictors of Clinician Success, Quality, and Resilience in Outpatient Pediatric Palliative Care.
articles.abstract:
