CONTEXT: Many inpatient PPC programs are growing into the outpatient setting, heeding the call of national organizations to offer pediatric palliative care (PPC) across the care continuum. In this context, expanding PPC programs face high volumes with limited resources.
OBJECTIVES: To improve sustainability, we aimed to assess associations between outpatient pediatric palliative care (OPPC) clinic operationalization and clinician perception of programmatic success, quality of care and team resilience.
METHODS: In a national cross-sectional study, 48 freestanding children's hospitals with established inpatient PPC programs were surveyed about their OPPC program's success, quality of care, and team resilience in Spring 2021; participants were asked to base responses on pre- March 2020 experiences.
RESULTS: Of the 28 programs with OPPC, 89% (25/28) responded to items on programmatic success, quality of care, and team resilience. Most reported that OPPC program design and workflow allowed for high-quality care (76%). Half felt their design and workflow were successful (52%) and promoted team resilience (48%). Across different clinical care models, OPPC programs with a dedicated clinic space reported increased programmatic success. Use of a free-standing clinic model was significantly associated with increased perception of success and high-quality care compared to floating and embedded clinic models. Perception that OPPC design and workflow promoted team resilience was associated with perception of high-quality care.
CONCLUSION: OPPC program design and workflow impacts clinician perception of success, provision of high-quality care, and team resilience. Quality metrics specific to OPPC models are needed to guide programs in successful expansion of PPC into the outpatient clinic setting.

articles.title: Perceived Clinical Utility of a Routine Family Experience Feedback Loop in Pediatric Palliative Care.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Home is typically the preferred setting of care for children living with serious illness, yet children and families frequently experience unmet needs in the home. Pediatric palliative care (PPC) teams provide longitudinal support for these children and families but have limited insight into families' day-to-day experiences and needs while at home. Routinely collecting family-reported data about care experiences in the home and sharing these data with PPC teams may enable more timely, responsive, and family-centered care.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the perceived clinical utility of sharing routinely collected, digitally enabled, family-reported data between families and PPC teams.
METHODS: We used a modified experience-based co-design approach to evaluate acceptability, perceived feasibility, and perceived clinical actionability through 1) individual interviews with family participants, (2) "clinical action check-in" meetings with outpatient PPC clinicians, and (3) co-design sessions with PPC and hospice clinicians. We used a content analytic approach to identify codes, categories, and themes.
RESULTS: Twenty-four parents of children with serious illness and 11 PPC and hospice clinicians participated in this project. Sharing routinely collected care experience data was perceived as: (1) acceptable or valuable, although comfort and willingness varied for families, (2) feasible with attention to timing, frequency, recipients, and implementation, and (3) clinically actionable along a spectrum.
CONCLUSION: A routinely collected, digitally enabled feedback loop between home and hospital is perceived by families and clinicians as holding promise for helping teams identify unmet needs and tailor care. Facilitating routine, bidirectional communication between families and teams may improve alignment between the care provided and families' needs at home.

articles.title: Altitude and disease persistence in childhood immune thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract: Yin and colleagues reported childhood immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) lasting at least three months in 8.8% of children hospitalized in Xining and 27.3% in Ningbo. In Ningbo, 79 of 88 children achieved complete response within the first seven days, while only 64 recovered before three months. At least 15 of the 24 children with prolonged disease must therefore have achieved early complete response. Linking their platelet counts to intervening treatment would clarify how long those responses lasted. Because each altitude was represented by one hospital, referral practices and opportunities to detect secondary immune disease may also contribute to the observed difference. Parental consanguinity, family histories of immunodeficiency or autoimmunity, immunoglobulin levels before intravenous immunoglobulin, and diagnoses emerging during follow-up merit systematic documentation. Our clinical impression of more frequent persistence in Van than in Adana raises this question in Türkiye. Published series from Van, Adana, and Istanbul used different definitions of disease duration, limiting geographic comparisons. At three months, a child's platelet trajectory and the appearance of another cytopenia or lymphoproliferation can guide reassessment of presumed primary ITP. Prospective comparisons across residential altitudes should document bleeding, rescue treatment, sustained platelet recovery off therapy, and the timing and basis of any subsequent diagnosis.

articles.title: Early-Life Farm Exposure and Food Allergy.
articles.abstract: Food allergy has increased substantially, increasing interest in environmental exposures that may promote immune tolerance. The "farm effect," in which children raised in traditional farming environments have lower rates of allergic disease, may also extend to food allergy. This review summarizes epidemiologic and mechanistic evidence linking prenatal and early-life farm exposures with food allergy and related atopic outcomes. Protective associations likely reflect combined exposures to livestock, farm dust, environmental microbes, diet, and farm milk during critical developmental windows. Proposed mechanisms include altered gut microbiome maturation, microbial metabolites, reduced epithelial inflammation, innate immune programming, and enhanced regulatory T-cell responses. However, direct evidence for clinically confirmed food allergy remains limited compared with evidence for asthma and allergic sensitization. Future studies should identify specific microbial, metabolic, and immune pathways that mediate protection and determine whether safe, defined surrogates of farm exposure can be translated into food allergy prevention strategies.

articles.title: Genetic Risk Stratification for Pediatric Fever-Associated Seizures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort.
articles.abstract: Fever-associated seizures are a common pediatric emergency. Complex febrile seizures and fever-sensitive epilepsy show marked genetic heterogeneity, but real-world evidence linking genetic information to the prediction of short-term recurrence and readmission remains insufficient. This single-center real-world retrospective cohort included children with their first qualifying fever-associated seizure presentation at the center from 2019 to 2023 and at least 12 months of follow-up. Genetic variants were classified according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics criteria, and pathway-based genetic risk tiers were constructed. Multivariable Cox models were used to evaluate associations between pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants and 12-month recurrence and readmission. Prediction models based on clinical variables alone and models additionally incorporating genetic risk tiers were compared using the C-index, 12-month area under the curve, Brier score, net reclassification improvement, integrated discrimination improvement, bootstrap correction, and decision curve analysis. The overall pathogenic or likely pathogenic detection rate was 13.64%, with a higher rate in fever-sensitive epilepsy than in complex febrile seizures. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were independently associated with recurrence and readmission, and high-risk pathways showed stronger effects. Adding genetic risk tiers modestly improved internally validated predictive performance and showed greater decision-curve net benefit. These findings suggest that genetic information may have potential value for short-term risk stratification and post-discharge management in children with fever-associated seizures; however, independent external validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Asthma Blitz Days: An Innovative Approach to Asthma Management in Schools.
articles.abstract: Asthma is the most prevalent chronic condition among school-aged children in the United States, contributing to emergency department visits, school absences, and diminished well-being. Inadequate asthma control is driven by medication nonadherence, psychosocial stressors, and social determinants of health. School nurses are pivotal in coordinating care, supporting medication management, and fostering asthma-friendly environments. In Pitt County, North Carolina, Asthma Blitz Days were developed as a collaborative, school-based intervention between Pitt County School Health Program and ECU Health (formerly Vidant) Maynard Children's Hospital Pediatric Asthma Program. Targeting Pre-K to 5th grade students with documented asthma, this program assessed symptoms, delivered age-appropriate education using the teach-back method, and improved medication and documentation compliance. School nurse-led, multidisciplinary interventions like Asthma Blitz Days offer a scalable approach to improving asthma control and promoting health equity in school communities.

articles.title: Hypophosphatemia in Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Incidence, Determinants, and Clinical Impact in a Tertiary Emergency and Intensive Care Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Serum phosphate levels commonly decline during treatment of pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), but the determinants and clinical implications of hypophosphatemia remain incompletely defined. We aimed to determine its incidence, predictors, and clinical impact during pediatric DKA.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 116 DKA episodes managed in a tertiary pediatric emergency department and intensive care unit between January 2022 and June 2025 were analyzed. Demographic characteristics, admission biochemical parameters, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Hypophosphatemia was defined according to age-specific reference ranges. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of hypophosphatemia, while length of hospital stay was assessed using multivariable linear regression of log-transformed values.
RESULTS: Hypophosphatemia occurred in 72/116 episodes (62.1%). Compared with those without hypophosphatemia, affected patients had lower admission pH (7.03±0.13 vs. 7.12±0.17; P=0.002), bicarbonate (7.8±2.4 vs. 9.8±3.3 mEq/L; P<0.001), and potassium levels (4.43±0.96 vs. 4.81±0.66 mEq/L; P=0.024). Hyponatremia and hypokalemia were more frequent, whereas hyperkalemia was less common (all P<0.05). Lower admission pH (OR: 0.008, 95% CI: 0.000-0.219; P=0.004) and lower baseline phosphate concentration (OR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.47-0.97; P=0.031) independently predicted hypophosphatemia. Although hospitalization was longer in the hypophosphatemia group (85.3±75.2 vs. 56.2±36.4 h; P=0.018), hypophosphatemia was not independently associated with length of stay. Higher admission pH independently predicted shorter hospitalization (β=-0.957, P=0.026). Baseline phosphate positively correlated with nadir phosphate during treatment (r=0.303, P<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: Hypophosphatemia is common during pediatric DKA and is closely associated with the severity of metabolic acidosis at presentation. However, it does not independently affect hospitalization duration, suggesting that it primarily reflects disease severity rather than independently determining short-term outcomes.

articles.title: Balanced Crystalloids Versus Normal Saline for Fluid Resuscitation in Pediatric Septic Shock: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Septic shock is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the pediatric population worldwide, and evidence comparing balanced crystalloids with normal saline (NS) for resuscitation remains inconclusive.
OBJECTIVE: To compare balanced crystalloids with NS for fluid resuscitation in children with septic shock, incorporating recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Cochrane Central, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception to May 2026, without language restrictions.
STUDY SELECTION: RCTs comparing balanced crystalloids with NS in patients aged 0 to 18 years with sepsis or septic shock were eligible.
DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool). Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were pooled using random-effects models; heterogeneity was assessed with the I2 statistic; leave-one-out and post hoc sensitivity analyses excluding the largest trial were performed.
RESULTS: Six RCTs comprising 10,308 participants were included. RRs are reported with NS as the reference. Pooled mortality showed no statistical significance between groups (3.8% with balanced crystalloids vs. 4.0% with NS; RR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.67-1.27; P = 0.63). Acute kidney injury incidence also did not differ significantly between groups (19.7% vs. 29.6%; RR, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.46-1.27; P = 0.29). The need for renal replacement therapy (RRT) was lower with balanced crystalloids (1.3% vs. 1.9%; RR, 0.67; 95% CI, 0.48-0.92; P = 0.01). Hyperchloremia incidence was lower with balanced crystalloids (32.3% vs. 49.9%; RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.61-0.69; P < 0.00001). After excluding the largest trial (PRoMPT BOLUS), mortality remained nonsignificant (RR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.45-1.50), and the reductions in RRT (RR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39-0.87) and hyperchloremia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.59-0.82) persisted.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with NS, balanced crystalloids reduced the need for RRT and the incidence of hyperchloremia, without significantly affecting mortality or acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Revisiting the Risk of Bacteremia in Well-Appearing Infants With Fever Without a Source ≥40 °C: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fever without a source (FWS) in infants is a frequent reason for emergency consultation. Historically, very high fever (≥40 °C) has been associated with an increased risk of bacteremia, prompting extensive diagnostic testing and empiric antibiotic therapy. However, recent epidemiological changes, including expanded vaccination and post-pandemic shifts in pathogen circulation, may have modified this risk. We aim to address this in our study.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter observational study in 2 tertiary hospitals in Catalonia (2018 to 2025). Well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months presenting with FWS ≥40 °C were included. The primary outcome was bacteremia. Clinical, laboratory, and microbiological data were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: A total of 184 infants were included (median age 14.3 mo). Blood cultures were obtained in 168 (91.3%). Only one case of bacteremia (0.5%; 95% CI: 0.1-3.0) was identified, secondary to urinary tract infection (UTI), with no cases of occult bacteremia. UTI prevalence was 19.6%, and pneumonia 2.7%. Overall, 42.3% received antibiotics, and 16.3% were hospitalized, with all patients showing favorable outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: In well-appearing infants aged 2 to 24 months with FWS ≥40 °C, bacteremia appears uncommon, although the wide confidence interval precludes firm conclusions. These exploratory findings suggest that a more selective diagnostic approach may warrant consideration over routine blood cultures and empiric antibiotics, pending prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Can Pediatric Emergency Medicine Clinicians Identify Solid Organ Injuries Using Contrast-Enhanced FAST in Abdominal Trauma?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-enhanced FAST (cFAST) has demonstrated superior sensitivity to B-mode FAST for detecting solid organ injury in blunt abdominal trauma, yet no prior study has evaluated cFAST image interpretation by pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) clinicians. We evaluated the sensitivity and specificity of cFAST interpretation for solid organ injuries by PEM clinicians following a web-based didactic.
METHODS: In this prospective, single-center study (February-May 2026), PEM clinicians credentialed in B-mode FAST without prior cFAST training completed a web-based didactic. Participants interpreted 12 simulated cases (25 cine clips), evaluating 41 organs (15 injured, 26 non-injured), all reviewed by a cFAST expert or cFAST-trained pediatric radiologist with CT confirmation. Pooled organ-level sensitivity and specificity were calculated with clustering correction using robust standard errors.
RESULTS: Among 41 participants, 1681 organ-level decisions were analyzed. Pooled sensitivity was 87.97% (95% CI: 84.96%-91.09%), specificity was 89.12% (95% CI: 86.53%-91.78%), negative predictive value (NPV) was 92.77% (95% CI: 90.99%-94.59%), and positive predictive value was 82.34% (95% CI: 78.68%-86.17%). False-negative decisions occurred in 4.4% (n = 74/1681).
CONCLUSION: After a web-based curriculum, PEM clinicians achieved high sensitivity, specificity, and NPV with few missed injuries, supporting future investigation of cFAST as an adjunctive screening tool in pediatric blunt abdominal trauma risk-stratification assessments.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Echocardiographic Platform for Automated Measurements in Children.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study assessed the accuracy of a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted echocardiographic platform for automated measurements in children.
METHODS: In this prospective, blinded, comparative, single-center pilot study, transthoracic echocardiography was performed in pediatric subjects aged 5 to 18 years using the Siemens Acuson Origin cardiovascular ultrasound system. For spectral Doppler assessments, two echocardiographic acquisitions were required: one using the AI-assisted protocol with automatic spectral Doppler marker placement, and one with manual marker placement. For all other analyses, a single manual acquisition was required for subsequent AI and manual assessments. Images were initially analyzed with the AI-assisted protocol, followed immediately by manual evaluation by a pediatric cardiologist blinded to the AI-derived results. Indices included B-mode, M-mode, Doppler, speckle tracking, and four-dimensional (4D) parameters. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis.
RESULTS: Thirty subjects (23 males; age 12.2±3.8 years) were studied, including 23 with structurally normal heart, six with congenital heart diseases, and one with dilated cardiomyopathy. Feasibility exceeded 90% for 2D AI-assisted assessment and 80% for 4D ventricular volumetry, but was below 35% for 4D atrial volumetry. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was strong for all parameters except septal (ICC 0.2) and left ventricular posterior wall thickness (ICC 0.5). Bland-Altman analysis showed no significant systematic differences.
CONCLUSION: Our pilot findings suggest that a commercially available AI-assisted echocardiographic system may be feasible and reasonably accurate for conventional and advanced quantitative echocardiographic assessment for children in a real-world setting.

articles.title: Novel pathogenic variant in haploinsufficiency of A20 with severe gastrointestinal effects and fulminant hepatic failure: A pediatric case series.
articles.abstract: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a rare autoinflammatory disorder caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in tumor necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3), encoding a negative regulator of nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NFκB) signaling. We report two pediatric patients with a previously unreported novel pathogenic variant (p. Glu409*) in the zinc finger (ZnF) 1 domain, exhibiting markedly divergent phenotypes. Case 1 presented with very-early-onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEO-IBD) and autoimmune thyroiditis, requiring aggressive infliximab dose escalation. Case 2 developed fulminant hepatic failure requiring liver transplantation, followed by post-transplant complications including refractory rejection, recurrent infections, and post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder. This represents the first known case of HA20 in solid organ transplantation. These cases underscore the importance of early genetic diagnosis in unexplained pediatric inflammatory disease and transplant rejection, as HA20 recognition may alter immunosuppressive strategies and guide therapies including cytokine blockade or Janus kinase (JAK) inhibition.

articles.title: Social Determinants of Health in Infantile Hemangioma Care: A 10-Year Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The objective of this study was to determine how measures of social vulnerability correlate with timing and modality of treatment for infantile hemangioma (IH).
METHODS: Clinical informatics techniques were used to identify patients diagnosed with IH before 24 months of age over a 10-year period at a single academic institution. Outcomes included age at diagnosis, treatment received, and age at treatment initiation. Multivariable regression models were used to measure associations with race, home language, insurance payor, and neighborhood Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Changes in these outcomes after the 2019 publication of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) IH Clinical Practice Guideline (CPG) were also assessed.
RESULTS: The cohort included 1633 patients. Black infants received propranolol later than White infants (β = +4.82 months, p = 0.0224). Asian patients were diagnosed earlier than other races/ethnicities (β = -1.03 months, p = 0.0385) and had lower odds of receiving propranolol (OR = 0.61, p = 0.0339). Infants from non-English-speaking families had lower odds of receiving propranolol (OR = 0.37, p = 0.0005) and initiated timolol earlier than patients from English-speaking families. Government-insured patients had higher odds of receiving propranolol (OR = 1.66, p = 0.0097), lower odds of receiving timolol (OR = 0.65, p = 0.0093), and later timolol initiation (β = +3.23 months, p = 0.0079) than privately insured patients. Patients in the most disadvantaged quartile (Q4) started timolol later than other groups (p = 0.0055). Following publication of the 2019 CPG, age at diagnosis decreased from 6.30 to 5.04 months (p = 0.001) and timolol was started earlier (6.84-4.32 months, p = 0.0006).
CONCLUSIONS: Race, preferred language, insurance status, and neighborhood-level social vulnerability were associated with differences in the timing and modality of IH care. These findings underscore the need for focused study and intervention to ensure that all infants with IH receive timely and effective IH care, regardless of social circumstance.

articles.title: Enhancing Rural and Indigenous Pediatric Dermatology: A Scoping Review and Practical Algorithm for Primary Care.
articles.abstract: Children living in rural and remote Canadian communities, including many First Nations, Inuit, and Métis communities, face substantial barriers to timely dermatologic care. We conducted a scoping review of common pediatric skin conditions in these settings and used the findings, supplemented by established clinical guidance and expert input, to develop a practical diagnostic and management algorithm for front-line clinicians. The review focuses on inflammatory, infectious, and environmental conditions commonly encountered in primary care and highlights contextual factors that may influence presentation, treatment, and outcomes, including geographic isolation, limited specialist access, crowded housing, water insecurity, and extreme weather exposure. The proposed algorithm is intended to support initial assessment, treatment, and referral while identifying persistent evidence gaps and the need for culturally safe, community-informed models of care.

articles.title: Predictors of Parental Strain in Pediatric Atopic Dermatitis: Findings From the US National Survey of Children's Health.
articles.abstract: Caring for a child with atopic dermatitis (AD) places strain on parents, but it remains unclear whether additional atopic comorbidities or psychosocial context compounds this burden. Data from the 2007-2008 National Survey of Children's Health among 6913 children aged 6-17 years was analyzed using survey-weighted multivariable regression to examine associations between a 5-item parental strain scale and parent-reported AD severity, comorbid asthma, allergic rhinitis, and food allergy, along with family, social, and healthcare access factors. Increased parental strain was associated with AD severity and with delayed or forgone care. Decreased parental strain was associated with better maternal mental health and with the female sex of the child. Atopic comorbidities were not associated with strain. Parental strain was more strongly associated with psychosocial factors and the severity of AD than the presence of additional atopic comorbidities.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Integrating a Peer Education Program to Improve HIV Service Uptake Among University Students: Evidence from Malawi University of Business and Applied Sciences.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although peer education programs are crucial in Malawi, there is paucity of data on their effect on uptake of HIV services among students in colleges. This study assessed the effectiveness of integrating a peer educators' program in enhancing HIV services uptake among students at Malawi University of Business and Applied Sciences.
METHODS: This was a complementary mixed-methods study. The quantitative component employed a retrospective comparative pre-post design to assess changes in HIV service utilization before and after integration of the peer educator programme. Quantitative data on HIV service utilization provided by the MUBAS campus clinic were obtained for 12-month period before integration of the peer educator programme and 12-month period following its integration. Comparative analysis and Z-test were performed to compare the proportions of students accessing HIV service before and after integration of the program. An exploratory qualitative study used 12 key informant interviews [KIIs] to explore barriers and facilitators in the implementation of the program. Data were analysed using a framework method of analysis.
RESULTS: The study findings showed that in 2023, before the integration of the peer educator program, a total number of 1,875 clients accessed HIV services compared to 2,579 clients who accessed the services in 2024. This indicates a 37.55% percentage increase [Z-value of +12.418 and p = 2.09 × 10-35]. HIV self-test kit distribution increased by 241% following the integration of peer educators, with a Z-value of +20.544 and p = 8.68 × 10-94. Participants regarded the peer educator program as effective in improving students' knowledge, related to HIV and SRHR, facilitating access to sexual and reproductive health services and promoting health seeking behaviour among students at MUBAS.
CONCLUSIONS: The integration of peer educator programs in services distribution, demonstrated to be an effective model to improve access to HIV services among young people in higher education institutions.

articles.title: Improving Rates of Screening for Health-related Social Needs in a Pediatric Emergency Department.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In September 2024, our hospital implemented health-related social needs (HRSN) screening in the pediatric emergency department (PED). We aimed to increase rates of completed HRSN screens from a baseline of 18% in October 2024 to greater than 50% by December 2025.
METHODS: Using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, we implemented a new workflow that shifted from verbal to paper screening, posted screening posters in the PED, and provided stakeholders with education and weekly updates on screening rates. The primary outcome measure was the percentage of eligible patient encounters with a completed HRSN screen. The secondary outcome measure was the percentage of patients with a completed HRSN screen who requested to be connected with resources. We created statistical process control charts and performed chi-square tests or Fisher's exact tests to assess the associations between demographics and HRSN screen completion status.
RESULTS: The mean screening rate increased from 18% to 40% during the course of 14 months. The mean rate of patients/caregivers requesting connection to resources on HRSN screens increased from 16% to 29%. Patients aged younger than 18 years, Black non-Hispanic patients, Hispanic patients, patients with public insurance, and patients who preferred the Haitian Creole language were less likely to have a completed HRSN screen.
CONCLUSIONS: Through our quality improvement initiative, we improved HRSN screening rates in our PED. We observed an increase in the rate of patients/caregivers requesting connections to resources. We could increase these rates in future studies through targeted interventions to engage patient groups that were less likely to complete screening and by improving stakeholder buy-in.

articles.title: Increasing Resident Involvement in Medical Resuscitations in the Pediatric Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Project.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Primary care and general emergency providers must recognize critically ill children and initiate life-sustaining interventions, yet trainees report limited experience and low confidence in this domain. The pediatric emergency department (PED) offers an optimal setting to improve resident exposure to pediatric medical resuscitations (MRs). We aimed to increase resident involvement in PED MRs from 45% to 70% during a 6-month period and evaluate the effect on resident confidence in managing critically ill children.
METHODS: We implemented a disruptive alarm-based alert system and assigned 1 resident per shift to a defined MR-response role. The process measure was alert-system use per 25 MRs; the outcome measure was the percentage of MRs with resident involvement, defined by resident completion of the encounter note per 25 MRs. We assessed change over time using standard rules for special-cause variation. Residents voluntarily completed pre- and postintervention surveys.
RESULTS: Resident involvement in MRs in the PED increased from 45% to 64%. Use of the disruptive alarm increased from 0% to 33%. Residents initially indicated increased confidence in responding to MRs, but this confidence waned over time.
CONCLUSIONS: A standardized disruptive alert system paired with designated MR roles increased resident involvement in MRs in the PED and may influence resident confidence in managing critically ill children.

articles.title: X-Linked Agammaglobulinemia Diagnosed in Adolescence Complicated by Invasive Aspergillosis: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA) is a primary humoral immunodeficiency that is typically recognized in early childhood. We report a 16-year-old male with recurrent respiratory tract infections (RTIs) since childhood who presented with severe pulmonary infection and focal neurological deficits. Immunologic evaluation showed profound hypogammaglobulinemia, with serum IgG of 0.24 g/L and both IgA and IgM < 0.10 g/L, together with virtually absent peripheral CD19+ B cells (0.00%). Genetic testing identified a hemizygous Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) c.1039G > C (p.Ala347Pro) variant. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) detected the Aspergillus flavus/oryzae complex. Serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) galactomannan (GM) tests were positive, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed multiple ring-enhancing lesions. Taken together, these findings supported invasive pulmonary aspergillosis with possible central nervous system (CNS) Aspergillus involvement. This case illustrates the clinical heterogeneity of XLA, including delayed recognition until adolescence, and underscores the importance of integrating immunologic, microbiological, mycological, imaging, and longitudinal clinical evidence when interpreting multiple pathogen-detection results in complex infections.

articles.title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and management in nursing practice.
articles.abstract: Asthma is one of the most common chronic respiratory conditions in the UK, affecting both children and adults. It is characterised by airway inflammation, variable symptoms, and reversible airflow limitation. This article provides a nursing-focused overview of asthma, exploring the definition, altered pathophysiology, diagnosis, and both pharmacological and non-pharmacological management. It highlights the importance of accurate assessment, early differentiation from other respiratory conditions, and the use of structured diagnostic tools within national guidance. Education, adherence support, and awareness of excessive reliever use are identified as key nursing priorities. By following national and local guidelines, promoting the use of combination and anti-inflammatory therapies, and providing holistic, person-centred education, nurses can improve symptom control, reduce preventable hospital admissions, and enhance quality of life for individuals and families living with asthma.

articles.title: Functional Somatic Symptoms in Paediatric Patients With Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Aberrant stress-system activation or dysregulation affects the cardiovascular system through various pathways, including the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, autonomic nervous system, neuro-endocrine system, and a range of neurophysiological intermediaries. In children with congenital heart disease-who have high rates of adverse childhood experiences, comorbid medical conditions, and neurodevelopmental issues-this activation/dysregulation commonly results in functional cardiac symptoms such as orthostatic intolerance, (functional) chest pain, and syncope-like presentations. Despite the obvious need, research into stress-system responses in children with congenital heart disease is limited. This article reviews commonly encountered clinical scenarios with the goal of encouraging practitioners to recognise the interconnections between structural cardiac lesions in children, stress-system activation/dysregulation, and functional somatic symptoms. Children with congenital heart disease and comorbid functional symptoms require comprehensive management strategies. We propose a framework to help clinicians facilitate appropriate treatment.

articles.title: First-hand Alcohol-Related Harms in Hong Kong University Dormitories: A Serial Cross-sectional Study Comparing the Normative, Social Unrest, and COVID-19 Pandemic Periods.
articles.abstract: Between September 2018 and June 2021, we conducted serial cross-sectional surveys of university dormitory residents in Hong Kong (n = 2659). Drinking behaviors and first-hand harms were examined across a normative period, time of protests, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Drinking levels remained steady between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic, and the proportions reporting drinking-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5%, respectively. Binge drinking was associated with high first-hand harms across 3 periods (adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 3.46-5.76). Having a drinking roommate was also correlated with harms during the normative period (AOR = 1.66). During the protests, underage drinking history and university location were associated with high first-hand harms (AOR: 1.69 and 1.82). During the COVID-19 pandemic, weekend dormitory residence and low alcohol-related knowledge were significant factors (AOR: 2.78 and 2.85). The findings indicate the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance for the Diagnosis and Monitoring of Takayasu Arteritis in Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Imaging evidence of vasculitis is mandatory for classification of Takayasu arteritis (TA) in children, yet the ability of a negative study to exclude the diagnosis has not been evaluated. We aimed to determine the negative predictive value (NPV) of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for excluding TA in children, to describe the imaging phenotype at diagnosis, and to characterise interval change on serial imaging.
METHODS: This retrospective study included all children who underwent CMR for suspected or established large vessel vasculitis at a single tertiary centre between May 2018 and November 2025. The protocol comprised contrast-enhanced angiography, 3D balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) imaging, black-blood imaging and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of vessel walls. TA was classified by the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES paediatric criteria. A true negative was defined as a negative baseline CMR with no emergence of TA over at least 6 months of documented follow-up. Interval change on serial CMR was classified per scan pair as improved, unchanged or worsened, recording wall findings (thickening, LGE) and luminal findings (stenosis, dilation) separately, by two readers.
RESULTS: 161 children underwent 222 CMR studies. Of 156 initial diagnostic studies, 10 (6%) showed TA and 146 were negative. No child with a negative baseline CMR developed TA during a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR 2.1 to 4.7), corresponding to an observed NPV of 100% (95% CI 97.5 to 100). Positive initial studies were characterised by aortic wall thickening and LGE in 7 of 10 children (70%), these were concordant in every child; extra-aortic involvement was present in 7 (70%). Fifteen children with TA underwent serial CMR (51 interval comparisons; inter-reader agreement 90%, weighted κ 0.86, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.96): 11 intervals (22%) showed improvement, 20 (39%) no change and 20 (39%) worsening. Two children had a previously undescribed imaging finding of focal 3D bSSFP signal abnormalities at sites of disease, consistent with a local susceptibility effect that improved or resolved with treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: In a tertiary referral population, no child with a negative CMR developed TA during follow-up. Serial CMR detected interval change with high agreement between readers. These findings support CMR as a reliable investigation for both the exclusion and longitudinal monitoring of TA in children.

articles.title: Lichen sclerosus amongst Prepubertal Nepalese Boys with Phimosis: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lichen sclerosus (Ls), a chronic lymphocyte-mediated scarring dermatosis of possibly autoimmune origin typically affects the foreskin and glans penis in boys. With an elusive etiology and multifactorial causation, it has an incidence that is globally variable. Nevertheless, a resultant genital discoloration and recurrent balanoposthitis can seriously impact urinary functions in boys in addition to the risks of malignancy. Early identification is imperative for successful control and prevention of complications.
OBJECTIVE: To study the profile of Nepalese boys with phimosis, determine the prevalence of Lichen sclerosus and assess the outcomes of treatment modalities.
METHOD: A prospective observational study was performed in boys who underwent treatment for phimosis between 1st September 2024 to 28th February 2026. Demographical profile, clinical findings, surgical details and outcomes were studied.
RESULT: A total of 200 boys were evaluated for symptomatic non-retractable foreskins at a mean age of 8 years (range: 4-16 years) and a mean symptom duration of 17 months. Of them, 139 were clinically diagnosed to have Physiological Phimosis (PhP) with most of them categorized as Kikiro's Grade I-II. They underwent Foreskin Adhesiolysis (FA) as a conservative treatment along with local application of ultra potent steroid cream for 2 months and foreskin hygiene maintenance thereafter. At the end of 3 months, they all had complete resolution of symptoms and no recurrence. The remaining 61 were diagnosed to have Pathological Phimosis (PaP) with most of them categorized as Kikiro's Grade III-IV and underwent Sleeve circumcision. Of them, 33 had histological evidence of lichen sclerosus while the rest 28 had non-specific chronic inflammation (non-Ls). The overall prevalence of lichen sclerosus was found to be 16.5% (33/200). Boys with lichen sclerosus were also treated with steroid cream as an adjuvant therapy for 2 months and followed up for a median period of 10 months while the rest (non-Ls) were followed up without adjuvant treatment. No serious complications were noted.
CONCLUSION: A vast majority of Nepalese boys (69.5%) with symptomatic phimosis were responsive to conservative measures with only a third needing operative management. Of these, lichen sclerosus was the underlying pathological cause in 16.5%.

articles.title: Dermoscopic Findings in Alopecia Areata: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alopecia areata is an autoimmune condition characterized by non-scarring hair loss affecting the scalp and other hair-bearing regions. Dermoscopy, a non-invasive diagnostic method, significantly improves the ability to confirm diagnosis, evaluate disease progression, and monitor treatment outcomes.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical and dermoscopic patterns of alopecia areata among patients attending a tertiary dermatology centre in Nepal.
METHOD: A descriptive cross-sectional study was carried out over one year at Kathmandu Medical College Teaching Hospital's Dermatology Outpatient Department including 60 patients clinically diagnosed with alopecia areata. Scalp and affected areas were examined using a Heine Delta 20 contact dermoscope with 10-16× magnification. Demographic, clinical features, and dermoscopic findings were collected and analyzed.
RESULT: Sixty patients were evaluated. Male patients predominated (41/60), and the largest age group was 21-30 years (35/60). Disease duration was less than six months in 48/60 patients. Localized patchy alopecia was the predominant presentation (49/60), with the occipital scalp being the most frequently involved site (27/60). Dermoscopy most frequently demonstrated yellow dots (58/60), followed by short vellus hairs (42/60), black dots (37/60), broken hairs (35/60), exclamation mark hairs (32/60), and white regrowing hairs (14/60).
CONCLUSION: Dermoscopy is a rapid and non-invasive modality that demonstrates characteristic findings in alopecia areata. In this cohort, yellow dots, short vellus hairs, black dots, broken hairs, and exclamation mark hairs were frequently observed. Further analytical studies are required to determine their associations with disease duration and SALT severity. Dermoscopy also offers economic value by reducing the need for unnecessary laboratory investigations in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Conceptual and psychometric characteristics of instruments used in adults with CHD quality of life research: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improved survival among people with congenital heart disease (CHD) has increased the emphasis on quality of life as a long-term outcome. However, inconsistent distinctions between quality of life, health-related quality of life, health status and functioning complicate the interpretation of this evidence. Examining the conceptual basis and measurement properties of instruments used in contemporary CHD research is therefore necessary to establish which outcomes are being assessed.
AIM: To identify instruments used in studies reporting quality of life outcomes in adults with moderate or severe CHD, classify their intended constructs and summarise reported evidence of validity, reliability and suitability.
METHODS: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance. CINAHL, MEDLINE, PsycINFO and Scopus were searched for English-language quantitative and mixed-methods studies published from 2015 in high-income countries. Citation mining identified instrument development and validation literature. Instruments were classified by their primary intended purpose, and reported psychometric evidence and study definitions of quality of life were summarised descriptively.
RESULTS: Sixty-six records published between 2015 and 2026 identified 16 instruments. Five measured overall quality of life, eight assessed health-related quality of life, health status or functioning, and three were disease-specific. Studies using overall quality of life measures more commonly defined the construct, whereas those using short-form health surveys frequently reported quality of life without conceptual clarification. Validation evidence supported some instruments in adult CHD populations, although the suitability of measures developed for paediatric populations remained uncertain.
CONCLUSION: Contemporary CHD research reports conceptually distinct outcomes under the term quality of life, limiting comparability and interpretation. Explicit definitions and instrument selection informed by the intended construct and population are required to strengthen the assessment of patient-reported outcomes.

articles.title: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation in children and young adults with severe adrenergically mediated ventricular arrhythmias: a single-centre experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Left cardiac sympathetic denervation is established for selected high-risk inherited arrhythmia syndromes, but evidence for an intended bilateral strategy in children and young adults remains limited. We evaluated the rationale, feasibility, safety, follow-up ascertainment, and outcomes of intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation.
METHODS: Consecutive children and young adults undergoing intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation between January 2015 and November 2025 were reviewed. The operation targeted the lower stellate component and upper thoracic sympathetic chain bilaterally, usually through single-port thoracoscopic access. Outcomes were obtained from specialist cardiology follow-up, electrocardiography, Holter monitoring, exercise testing when available, inpatient telemetry, device interrogation, and medication records.
RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients were operated. Mean age was 12.4 years. Bilateral denervation was completed in 36 patients; 1 underwent left-sided denervation only owing to intraoperative haemodynamic instability. Single-port access was used in 30 patients. There were no intraoperative deaths, unplanned full thoracotomy conversions, intercostal injuries, reoperations for surgical complications, or denervation-related permanent pacing. Procedure-attributable morbidity comprised one mild Horner syndrome and one self-limited axillary wound complaint. Among 36 patients with post-discharge follow-up, 32 remained free from the primary malignant ventricular arrhythmic endpoint. Estimated malignant ventricular arrhythmia-free survival was 95.8 per cent at 1 year and 89.4 per cent at 3 years.
CONCLUSION: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation was feasible and had low procedure-attributable morbidity in selected young patients. It should be interpreted as an adjunct to multidisciplinary arrhythmia care, not as a replacement for medication, device surveillance, or follow-up.

articles.title: A Rare Case of Fulminant Guillain-Barre Syndrome as the Cardinal Presenting Feature of New Onset Pediatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Here we present a complex case of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) presenting initially as fulminant Guillain-Barre syndrome (GBS). This particular manifestation of neuropsychiatric lupus is uncommon but can be severe and even life threatening. Increasing providers' awareness of the overlap between lupus and GBS will improve diagnostic accuracy and timing as well as expedite appropriate therapies, which may differ from typical GBS treatment.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 12-year-old previously healthy Hispanic female presented with subacute onset vision changes and imbalance with ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and hyporeflexia. Given her classic clinical triad and suspicion for GBS variant Miller Fischer syndrome (MFS), neuroaxis imaging was obtained. MRI showed cranial nerve and ventral nerve root enhancement, and cytoalbuminologic dissociation seen on cerebrospinal fluid analysis also supported this diagnosis. Weakness including the facial and bulbar muscles and the extremities progressed rapidly and threatened respiratory functions, so the patient was intubated. Typical treatments for GBS including intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and plasma exchange (PLEX) were insufficient to manage symptoms, and additional evaluations supported a diagnosis of SLE with nephritis. Coordinated care between neuroimmunology and rheumatology enabled rapid escalation of therapy to include high-dose intravenous steroid pulses, cyclophosphamide, and rituximab. Together, these therapies eventually stabilized the patient, and with support from neuropsychology, psychiatry, and rehabilitation medicine, she was able to discharge from the hospital after 115 days of admission. She has remained in remission on maintenance immunosuppression including mycophenolate mofetil as well as hydroxychloroquine.
CONCLUSIONS: Neuropsychiatric lupus can be difficult to diagnose and manage, but its severity necessitates vigilance and aggressive management. In the current case, the isolated neurological symptoms at presentation consistent with GBS could have delayed diagnosis, but neuroimmunology and rheumatology were consulted early, and appropriate diagnostic testing was performed. The patient's multidisciplinary team worked closely together to appropriately escalate her treatment beyond what is typical for GBS, ultimately leading to remission of her neuropsychiatric symptoms and recovery of her baseline neurological status. This case highlights the complex nature of neuropsychiatric lupus, suggests that SLE should be on the differential in atypical or difficult-to-treat cases of GBS, and underscores the need for coordinated interdisciplinary care to achieve best outcomes for these patients.

articles.title: Patterns and Factors Associated With Coronary Artery Involvement in Kawasaki Disease: Experience From Southern Tunisia.
articles.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) is a paediatric vasculitis associated with coronary complications. We aimed to describe clinical and echocardiographic characteristics and factors associated with coronary involvement. This retrospective, single-centre study included 70 children over 18 years (2007-2024). Univariate analyses assessed clinical and laboratory associations. The mean age was 55.4 ± 32.8 months; 61.7% were younger than 5 years. Coronary involvement occurred in 32/70 (45.7%), including dilation in 25 (35.7%), wall thickening in 7 (10.0%) and aneurysms in 3 (4.3%). Lesions regressed in 27/32 (84.4%). Significant associations included cheilitis, rash, cervical lymphadenopathy, cough, rhinorrhoea, leucocytosis, lymphocytosis, lower mean corpuscular volume, higher mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration, thrombocytosis and elevated alanine aminotransferase. These unadjusted associations do not establish independent predictors. Early diagnosis, intravenous immunoglobulin and aspirin remain essential. Systematic echocardiographic assessment, structured follow-up and larger multicentre studies are needed to improve coronary risk stratification and long-term outcomes in children with KD.

articles.title: Clinical and Radiographic Characteristics of Pneumococcal Pneumonia in Children: A Case Series.
articles.abstract: Given the decline in pneumococcal infections related to widespread childhood vaccinations in the United States, we evaluate the rate of Streptococcus pneumoniae and also report the demographic and radiographic characteristics of children with pneumococcal pneumonia in the post-pneumococcal conjugate vaccine era. We studied the prevalence of medical comorbidities, clinical presentations and outcomes, antibiotic susceptibility results, and radiographic findings among children aged less than 18 years presenting to a pediatric Emergency Department between 2010 and 2023 with a diagnosis of pneumonia and detection of Streptococcus pneumoniae in blood and/or pleural fluid. Of the 31 cases of pneumococcal pneumonia, over 50% occurred among children less than 5 years of age, and 71% of children had medical comorbidities. Eighty percent of children had radiographic pneumonia; the most common radiographic findings included opacities (71.0%), consolidation (29.0%), and pleural effusion (25.8%). Given high rates of antibiotic overtreatment, these findings may help clinicians to judiciously use antibiotics for children with pneumonia.

articles.title: Treatment of vitiligo with narrowband ultraviolet B phototherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitiligo is an acquired immune depigmenting disorder. Narrowband 311 nm ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy is an important component of the standard treatment. Many questions arise about its safe use. The aim of the study was to clarify the use of NB-UVB in the management of vitiligo.
METHODS: A comprehensive review was coordinated by the French Society of Photodermatology, French vitiligo experts and the Centre of Evidence of the French Society of Dermatology to ascertain the efficacy and safety of NB-UVB used for vitiligo to draw up consensus guidelines.
RESULTS: The consulted experts defined NB-UVB phototherapy as a cornerstone treatment of vitiligo. They ensure its safety by establishing a dose protocol regarding treatment duration and subsequent monitoring. Given that most studies show that NB-UVB is not associated with an increased incidence of skin cancers, there is no ceiling on the maximum number of sessions allowed in adults with dark Fitzpatrick skin phototypes. In children and fair-skinned patients, additional data on the maximum number of sessions are needed before a recommendation can be made, even if the risk of cutaneous malignancy seems reduced in the population with vitiligo. For increased efficacy, NB-UVB combined with topical agents (calcineurin inhibitors, corticosteroids and ruxolitinib) and oral corticosteroids should be considered in localized vitiligo and active disease, respectively. A combination of NB-UVB with oral Janus kinase inhibitors seems promising.
CONCLUSION: There are now guidelines available to French dermatologists and practitioners for treating vitiligo with NB-UVB phototherapy.

articles.title: On the value of extending propranolol treatment for more than 6 months for infantile hemangioma: A retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infantile hemangiomas (IH) occur in approximately 4.5% of children, of whom 10% require treatment. The French and European guidelines recommend propranolol treatment for a minimum of 6 months; however, observational studies indicate that treatment is often extended beyond this duration in clinical practice.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the clinical relevance of continuing propranolol beyond 6 months.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study at Nancy Hospital, including infants treated with propranolol for ≥6 months between 2014 and April 2025. Patients were divided into a 6-month treatment group (6M group) and a prolonged treatment group (PT group, >6 months). IH regression was assessed by two blinded evaluators, with complete or near-complete regression defined as ≥80% reduction in IH volume.
RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients were included: 42 in the 6M group and 26 in the PT group (mean duration 9.7 ± 2.4 months). Deep or mixed IH were more frequent in the PT group (73% vs 43%). Complete or near-complete regression was observed in 34 patients (81%) in the 6M group and 20 patients (77%) in the PT group (p = 0.69). Severe adverse events were rare; one severe case of hypoglycemia occurred in the PT group. The relapse and re-treatment rates were not significantly different.
CONCLUSION: Extending propranolol beyond 6 months did not significantly improve IH regression, even in deeper lesions. Interpretation is limited by the retrospective design, small sample size, heterogeneous photographic assessment, and difficulty distinguishing treatment effects from natural involution. Prospective studies with larger cohorts are needed to identify IH subtypes that might benefit from longer therapy.

articles.title: Delayed Diagnosis of Coronary Sinus Ostial Atresia in a Single-Ventricle Patient.
articles.journal: World J Pediatr Congenit Heart Surg
articles.abstract: Coronary sinus ostial atresia is a rare congenital anomaly that is often clinically silent; however, hemodynamic compromise can occur if venous drainage is interrupted. We present a 4-month old infant with hypoplastic left heart syndrome who previously underwent palliation with a Norwood procedure. During bidirectional Glenn palliation, ligation of a 2-mm left superior vena cava resulted in coronary sinus dilation and myocardial edema, raising suspicion for coronary sinus ostial atresia. The coronary sinus was unroofed, and the child recovered well.

articles.title: Comparing 70 kV and 120 kV photon-counting CT protocols for pediatric cardiac imaging in children weighing 10-30 kg: Radiation dose and image quality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scanning at 70 kV on photon-counting CT (PCCT) reduces radiation dose by 50% compared to 120 kV in infants under 10 kg without loss of diagnostic quality. Whether scanning at a lower kV is of benefit in larger children, in whom greater attenuation increases image noise, has not been determined.
METHODS: We retrospectively compared ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT examinations in children weighing 10-30 kg acquired at 70 kV (n = 79) or 120 kV (n = 80), both at a CARE keV IQ level of 25. We measured signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in the ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery and compared radiation dose. Two pediatric cardiac radiologists rated image quality in five vascular structures on a 5-point Likert scale.
RESULTS: Groups were similar in age and size. Neither CNR nor SNR differed significantly. Median Likert scores were at least 4 for four of five structures in both groups. Median CTDIvol was 0.49 vs 0.63 mGy (P < 0.001), and effective dose 0.65 vs 0.75 mSv (P < 0.001) for 70 vs 120 kV.
CONCLUSION: In children weighing 10-30 kg, 70 kV ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT was associated with lower radiation dose than 120 kV, with no significant difference in CNR and median reader scores in the diagnostic range. A 120 kV protocol remains appropriate when metal-artifact reduction or advanced spectral reconstructions are needed.

articles.title: Precannulation Risk Factors Associated With Hemorrhagic Events During Respiratory Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Children: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: Hemorrhagic complications are frequent and clinically significant during pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), yet associated precannulation factors remain poorly defined. We evaluated these factors in a multicenter retrospective cohort of children receiving respiratory ECMO at four Colombian centers during 2018-2022. A total of 106 children were included; 53 (50.0%) developed at least one hemorrhagic complication during ECMO support, and 83% of events occurred within the first 7 days after cannulation. Cannulation-site bleeding was most frequent (41.5%), followed by intracranial hemorrhage (22.6%) and pulmonary hemorrhage (17.0%). In bias-reduced adjusted analyses, higher precannulation lactate concentrations, lower bicarbonate levels, previous severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, adenovirus infection at admission, and longer mechanical ventilation and vasoactive support before ECMO remained associated with bleeding. Patients who developed hemorrhagic complications had higher 28 day mortality than those without bleeding (39.6% vs. 13.2%; p = 0.002). When bleeding was modeled as a time-dependent exposure, hemorrhagic events were associated with a higher subsequent hazard of 28 day mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 4.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.09-11.64). Hemorrhagic complications affected half of children receiving respiratory ECMO, occurred predominantly during the first week, and were associated with increased mortality. Several precannulation characteristics remained associated with bleeding in bias-reduced adjusted analyses. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation.

articles.title: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Mortality in Pediatric Medical Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) using extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used in pediatric refractory cardiac arrest. This study investigated the association between ECPR and mortality in pediatric patients receiving venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO) for medical indications. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 28 days to <18 years who received VA-ECMO at a tertiary referral children's hospital between January 2010 and May 2025. The primary outcome was pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) mortality. Among 73 patients (non-ECPR, n = 58; ECPR, n = 15), ECPR was associated with increased mortality in unadjusted analysis (odds ratio [OR], 5.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.47-18.53; p = 0.010). After adjustment for pre-ECMO physiologic variables, the association between ECPR and mortality was no longer significant (adjusted OR, 1.74; 95% CI, 0.37-8.08; p = 0.483). Lower pre-ECMO arterial pH remained associated with higher mortality (adjusted OR, 1.87 per 0.1 decrease; 95% CI, 1.20-2.92; p = 0.006). In a sensitivity analysis, underlying cardiac disease was associated with lower mortality than noncardiac disease (adjusted OR, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.07-0.79; p = 0.020). These findings highlight the associations of pre-ECMO physiologic status and underlying disease category with PICU mortality.

articles.title: Clinically Suspected Fulminant Myocarditis Following PCR-Confirmed Pertussis in an Infant: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Cardiac involvement following pertussis infection is uncommon but may be associated with severe clinical deterioration in infants. We report the case of a 3-month-old girl who developed shock, ventricular arrhythmias, and severe biventricular systolic dysfunction approximately 2 weeks after PCR-confirmed Bordetella pertussis infection. Echocardiography demonstrated marked left ventricular dilatation, global hypokinesia, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%. Troponin I was markedly elevated. The clinical presentation was consistent with suspected fulminant myocarditis, although definitive myocardial confirmation was unavailable. The infant received intensive supportive care, inotropic treatment, heart failure medications, antiarrhythmic therapy, and intravenous immunoglobulin, with subsequent clinical and echocardiographic improvement. She was discharged in a stable condition but died unexpectedly approximately 2 months later. The immediate cause of death remained undetermined. This case emphasizes the importance of early cardiac assessment and structured post-discharge surveillance in infants with severe cardiac dysfunction following pertussis infection.

articles.title: Fournier's Gangrene Following Recent Varicella in an Immunocompetent Adult: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Varicella is a common, usually self-limiting viral illness in children; however, adult infection may be associated with severe systemic and secondary bacterial complications. Fournier's gangrene (FG) is a rare, rapidly progressive, and fatal necrotizing fasciitis involving the genital and perineal region, commonly seen in immunocompromised individuals. The occurrence of Fournier's gangrene in temporal association with recent varicella in an immunocompetent adult is exceedingly rare. We report the case of a 32-year-old previously healthy male who developed Fournier's gangrene 2 weeks after varicella infection. He presented with high-grade fever, malaise, and rapidly progressive scrotal pain, erythema, swelling, and necrosis. On examination, extensive scrotal edema, sloughed skin, exposed fascial planes, and foul-smelling purulent discharge extending to the perineum and left thigh were noted. Laboratory evaluation revealed marked leukocytosis, elevated inflammatory markers, and a high Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC) score. Ultrasonography demonstrated fascial thickening with gas within soft tissues, while wound and blood cultures revealed polymicrobial infection. He was managed with broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, hemodynamic support, and repeated surgical debridements followed by secondary wound closure, resulting in gradual clinical recovery. This case highlights a rare but life-threatening complication of adult varicella in an immunocompetent individual. The close temporal relationship between recent varicella and the subsequent development of FG suggests a temporal association, although a causal relationship cannot be established from a single case report. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for necrotizing soft tissue infections in patients presenting with perineal pain and swelling following varicella, as early diagnosis and prompt surgical intervention are critical for survival.

articles.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence-Based Dietary Advice: A Scoping Review of Nutritional Accuracy, Safety, and Eating-Related Risks.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This scoping review aimed to synthesize current evidence on generative artificial intelligence (AI)-based dietary advice, with particular attention to nutritional accuracy, safety, weight-management guidance, eating-related harm, and professional safeguards.
METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework, refined by Levac et al., and reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Embase were searched up to 30 June 2026. Original empirical studies evaluating generative AI or large language models for dietary advice, meal planning, nutritional information, weight management, or eating-disorder-related guidance were eligible. Study selection, data charting, and synthesis were performed independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by consensus or third-reviewer assessment.
RESULTS: Nine studies published between 2023 and 2026 were included. In this small and emerging evidence base, one study reported 84.38% accuracy on an objective nutrition-literacy assessment, and another found overall Diet Quality Index-International scores above 70 for chatbot-generated weight-loss plans. However, important limitations were identified in caloric accuracy, portion sizing, macronutrient and micronutrient balance, reproducibility, personalization, and management of food allergies and multimorbidity. Potential safety concerns were identified in adolescent and eating-disorder scenarios, where chatbot responses sometimes combined appropriate healthy-eating advice with restrictive or weight-focused recommendations; these studies did not establish resulting clinical or behavioral harm. Although some systems encouraged consultation with healthcare professionals, safety warnings and referral to regulated resources were inconsistent.
CONCLUSION: Evidence from the nine included studies remains preliminary, heterogeneous, and largely simulation-based. Generative AI may have a supplementary role in nutrition education and preliminary dietary guidance, but the available evidence is insufficient to support autonomous use in place of dietitians. Current findings indicate potential safety risks in high-risk or clinically complex scenarios rather than demonstrated long-term harm. Longitudinal and real-world studies are needed to establish the clinical and behavioral effects of AI-generated dietary advice.

articles.title: Exploring the potential therapeutic significance of secukinumab for annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.
articles.abstract: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis (AEI), also known as KRT1/KRT10-nEDD-annular, is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by recurrent annular erythema on the trunk and proximal extremities. Currently, the treatment of AEI is limited to the use of emollients, keratolytics, and oral retinoids, which remains insufficient. To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of secukinumab in patients with AEI. Two patients with AEI were enrolled for secukinumab therapy following a laboratory assessment that excluded contraindications. Disease severity was assessed using the Ichthyosis Area and Severity Index (IASI), the Children's Dermatology Life Quality Index (cDLQI) and the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI), and the 5-D itch scale. Immunological profiling was performed by measuring biomarker levels in both serum and lesional skin tissue. Significant differences in treatment efficacy were observed between the paediatric and adult patient receiving secukinumab, with the paediatric patient demonstrating marked outcomes and improvements in both subjective symptoms and skin lesions. Notably, despite showing no pre-treatment elevation in serum IL-17A levels, the paediatric patient exhibited increased IL-17A expression in lesional skin. Limitations: Small sample group. Although our findings are based on a small sample size, they provide novel therapeutic perspectives for the management of AEI and offer preliminary therapeutic clues for future clinical management.

articles.title: Recognition of Emergency Symptoms and Preparedness for Major Health Risks in Elementary Schools in Japan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elementary schools are settings in which children may experience unexpected health emergencies, and school staff play a central role in prevention and early response. While symptom recognition among staff is generally reported to be high, less attention has been paid to how initial responses and medical referrals are understood, shared, and operationalized within schools.
METHODS: We conducted a web-based survey of 505 elementary school staff members across Japan between July and August 2025 to assess recognition of key symptoms and respondents' awareness of school-based preparedness for concussion, heat stroke, food allergy, and choking. Background characteristics and preparedness measures were summarized using descriptive statistics. Associations between preparedness scores and respondent- and school-level factors were explored using multivariable linear regression models.
RESULTS: Recognition of key symptoms was generally high across conditions. In contrast, reported awareness of school-based preparedness measures varied widely, with first-aid procedures reported by 80%-90% of respondents, whereas recurrence prevention and return-to-activity protocols were less frequently reported, particularly for concussion (19.6%). Multivariable analyses showed higher preparedness scores among principals and vice principals across conditions (mean differences [MDs], 0.4-0.7), while lower scores were observed for food allergy in smaller schools (< 100 students, MD -0.49; 95% CI -0.87 to -0.11) and in the Hokkaido/Tohoku region (MD, -0.72; 95% CI -1.26 to -0.18).
CONCLUSIONS: Symptom recognition for major school health emergencies was generally high, whereas respondents' awareness of preparedness measures for recovery and emergency decision-making was less consistent. Awareness varied across staff roles, highlighting potential gaps in dissemination of school preparedness procedures.

articles.title: Association of vitamin therapy with acute encephalopathy with febrile convulsive status epilepticus and neurological outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute encephalopathy with febrile convulsive status epilepticus (AEFCSE) has a poor prognosis, but no definitive treatment. We aimed to evaluate whether early combination vitamin therapy (VT) (vitamin B1, B6, and l-carnitine) could prevent AEFCSE onset and improve neurological outcomes of pediatric febrile status epilepticus (FSE).
METHODS: The present, single-center, retrospective observational study enrolled patients admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit during 2017-2019 and 2022-2024 with FSE lasting ≥30 min. The patients were categorized into a VT group, who received vitamins within 72 h of the initial seizure onset, and a non-VT group. The primary outcome was the AEFCSE incidence. The secondary outcome was AEFCSE-related, poor neurological prognosis as defined by the Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category score. Inverse probability of treatment weighting based on propensity scores was used to adjust for confounding factors.
RESULTS: Of 109 included patients with FSE, 40 (37%) and 69 (63%) were in the VT and the non-VT group, respectively. AEFCSE occurred in eight (20%) and 11 (16%) patients in the respective group. After adjustment, VT was associated with lower but non-significant odds of AEFCSE (odds ratio [OR]: 0.60; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.21-1.73). AEFCSE-related, poor neurological outcomes occurred in five (13%) and eight (12%) patients in the respective group. After adjustment, the odds were lower but non-significant (OR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.16-1.90).
CONCLUSIONS: Early combination VT demonstrated an exploratory association with lower AEFCSE incidence and improved neurological outcomes in children with FSE albeit the findings were inconclusive.

articles.title: Pediatric Dermatologic Conditions.
articles.abstract: Pediatric skin conditions of the lower extremity present a diagnostic and management challenge, and this article offers the practitioner a systematic framework. It opens with practical guidance on performing cutaneous procedures in children-engaging the parent, minimizing pain and anxiety through topical anesthesia and distraction, and setting postoperative limits for optimal scar outcomes. It then surveys environmentally induced disorders, bites and stings, genodermatoses including the palmoplantar keratodermas, and bacterial, viral, and fungal infections. Eczematous conditions, psoriasis, nevi, pediatric melanoma, and nail disorders are each reviewed with attention to lower extremity presentation, common misdiagnoses, and current management strategies.

articles.title: Clinical spectrum and morbidity of ocular parasitic infections among rural children in central India.
articles.abstract: Ocular parasitic infections are an under-recognised cause of ocular morbidity in low- and middle-income countries. We found Taenia solium (26.5%) was the most common parasite, followed by Toxocara canis/cati (19.4%), Toxoplasma gondii (17.3%) and Acanthamoeba spp. (11.2%). Reduced visual acuity (66.3%), retinitis/chorioretinitis (38.8%), uveitis (32.7%) and vitreous involvement (28.6%) were the predominant clinical manifestations. Poor nutritional status was significantly associated with infection. Frequent open defaecation, barefoot outdoor play and inadequate handwashing before meals were identified as significant behavioural risk factors for ocular parasitic infection.

articles.title: Fulminant Early-Onset Sepsis Caused by Multidrug-Resistant Aeromonas hydrophila in a Preterm Neonate: A Case Report and Therapeutic Challenge.
articles.abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila is a rare but virulent pathogen in neonates, historically associated with aquatic environments. However, the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains presenting as early-onset sepsis (EOS) poses a severe diagnostic and therapeutic dilemma. We report a fatal case of a preterm neonate (33 weeks gestation) who developed fulminant septic shock at 20 hours of life. Despite the initiation of broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam), the clinical course rapidly progressed to pulmonary hemorrhage and death at 26 hours of life. Blood cultures subsequently confirmed Aeromonas hydrophila septicemia with high-level resistance to carbapenems (Meropenem MIC > 16 μg/mL) and piperacillin-tazobactam (MIC > 128 μg/mL). This case highlights the growing threat of nonfermenting MDR gram-negative organisms in EOS and underscores the limitations of standard empiric regimens against atypical pathogens.

articles.title: Pulmonary Artery Thrombosis in a Growth Faltering Infant With Acinetobacter Sepsis-A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary artery thrombosis is a rare finding in infant patients. Contributors to infant hypercoagulability include inherited thrombophilias, immature anticoagulation systems, and systemic insults such as septic shock and liver disease.
CASE PRESENTATION: We present the case of a 7-week-old girl with perinatal HIV exposure diagnosed with a pulmonary artery thrombus. The patient was admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) for sepsis due to Acinetobacter nosocomialis bacteremia. During a workup for growth faltering and an S3 gallop, echocardiogram revealed a mass in the main pulmonary artery. Days later, after failing to achieve therapeutic anticoagulation, infant developed hypoxia and echocardiogram demonstrated worsening luminal obstruction by the thrombus, prompting urgent treatment with thrombectomy. We hypothesize that septic shock, with associated coagulopathy and severe dehydration, predisposed to thrombus formation in this critically ill patient.
CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the rapid, multidisciplinary approach to diagnosing a pulmonary artery thrombus and the underlying factors contributing to hypercoagulability in an infant. This case is novel for the patient's risk factor of perinatal HIV exposure, which may have predisposed her to opportunistic infection as well as thrombosis. Hypoxia and hemodynamic instability presented later in her course, prompting invasive management. Early recognition and timely intervention are essential for optimizing patient outcomes.

articles.title: Transformations in play. Dyadic work inspired by psychoanalytic infant observation.
articles.abstract: The article explores the psychoanalytic foundations of Watch Me Play! (WMP), an applied approach first developed to promote understanding of the needs of babies and young children in care, now more widely used to support parent-child relationships and child development. Watch Me Play! is derived from psychoanalytic infant observation and underpinned by key concepts in child development research such as mind-mindedness, joint attention and contingent responsiveness.
